qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 - 4xy - 9x + 6y\)
qs.s: Group the terms into pairs as \(2x(3x - 2y) - 3(3x - 2y)\), then factor out \((3x - 2y)\) to get \((3x - 2y)(2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(10ax - 15ay - 4bx + 6by\)
qs.s: Group the polynomial into pairs as \(5a(2x - 3y) - 2b(2x - 3y)\), then factor out the common binomial to obtain \((2x - 3y)(5a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6ab + 14 - 21a - 4b\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms as \((6ab - 21a) - (4b - 14) = 3a(2b - 7) - 2(2b - 7)\), then factor out \((2b - 7)\) to obtain \((2b - 7)(3a - 2)\).
Group the terms into pairs as \(4x^2(2x - 3) + 5(2x - 3)\), then remove the common factor \((2x - 3)\) to get \((2x - 3)(4x^2 + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(xy + 4y - 3x - 12\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \((xy + 4y) - (3x + 12) = y(x + 4) - 3(x + 4)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x + 4)\) gives \((x + 4)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(ab - 2b - 7a + 14\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \((ab - 2b) - (7a - 14) = b(a - 2) - 7(a - 2)\). Factoring out \((a - 2)\) gives \((a - 2)(b - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(m^2 - mn + 3m - 3n\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \((m^2 - mn) + (3m - 3n) = m(m - n) + 3(m - n)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((m - n)\) gives \((m - n)(m + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(p^2 - pq - 4p + 4q\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \((p^2 - pq) - (4p - 4q) = p(p - q) - 4(p - q)\). Factoring out \((p - q)\) gives \((p - q)(p - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6ac - 9ad - 4bc + 6bd\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \((6ac - 9ad) - (4bc - 6bd) = 3a(2c - 3d) - 2b(2c - 3d)\). Factoring out \((2c - 3d)\) gives \((2c - 3d)(3a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2ax - 3by + 6ay - bx\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms to group common variables: \((2ax + 6ay) - (bx + 3by) = 2a(x + 3y) - b(x + 3y)\). Factoring out \((x + 3y)\) gives \((x + 3y)(2a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(mx - my + nx - ny - 4x + 4y\)
qs.s: Group into three pairs as \((mx - my) + (nx - ny) - (4x - 4y) = m(x - y) + n(x - y) - 4(x - y)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x - y)\) gives \((x - y)(m + n - 4)\).
Group into pairs as \(2m(2m + 3) - 5(2m + 3)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((2m + 3)\) gives \((2m - 5)(2m + 3)\).
Group into pairs as \(3y(y - 2) + 4(y - 2)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((y - 2)\) gives \((3y + 4)(y - 2)\).
Group into pairs as \(2x(x + 4) - 3(x + 4)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((x + 4)\) gives \((2x - 3)(x + 4)\).
Group into pairs as \(5a(a + 3) - 2(a + 3)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((a + 3)\) gives \((5a - 2)(a + 3)\).
Group into pairs as \(2b(b - 5) - 3(b - 5)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((b - 5)\) gives \((2b - 3)(b - 5)\).
Group into pairs as \(5x^2(3x - 5) - 2(3x - 5)\). Factoring out the common factor \((3x - 5)\) gives \((5x^2 - 2)(3x - 5)\).
Group terms into pairs as \(3x^2(2x - 3) + 2(2x - 3)\). Removing the common binomial factor \((2x - 3)\) gives \((3x^2 + 2)(2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6ab - 15a - 8b + 20\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs as \(3a(2b - 5) - 4(2b - 5)\). Removing the common factor \((2b - 5)\) yields \((3a - 4)(2b - 5)\).
First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(6x^2 + 9x - 4xy - 6y)\). Then group inside the parentheses as \(3x(2x + 3) - 2y(2x + 3)\), resulting in \(2(3x - 2y)(2x + 3)\).
Group terms into pairs as \(x^2(x + 2y) - 3y^2(x + 2y)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x + 2y)\) results in \((x^2 - 3y^2)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(p^2 + pq - 7p - 7q\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((p^2 + pq) - (7p + 7q) = p(p + q) - 7(p + q)\), which factors to \((p + q)(p - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(a^2 - 4a - ab + 4b\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((a^2 - 4a) - (ab - 4b) = a(a - 4) - b(a - 4)\), which factors to \((a - 4)(a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(y^2 + 2y - yz - 2z\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((y^2 + 2y) - (yz + 2z) = y(y + 2) - z(y + 2)\), which factors to \((y + 2)(y - z)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(m^2 + 6m + mn + 6n\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((m^2 + 6m) + (mn + 6n) = m(m + 6) + n(m + 6)\), which gives \((m + 6)(m + n)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(x^2 - 3x + xy - 3y\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((x^2 - 3x) + (xy - 3y) = x(x - 3) + y(x - 3)\), which factors to \((x - 3)(x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2x^2 - 6x + 9y - 3xy\)
qs.s: Rearrange as \((2x^2 - 3xy) - (6x - 9y) = x(2x - 3y) - 3(2x - 3y)\), which factors to \((2x - 3y)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(14ac - 21ad - 6bc + 9bd\)
qs.s: Group as \((14ac - 21ad) - (6bc - 9bd) = 7a(2c - 3d) - 3b(2c - 3d)\), which factors to \((2c - 3d)(7a - 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 - 9xy + 8x - 12y\)
qs.s: Group as \((6x^2 - 9xy) + (8x - 12y) = 3x(2x - 3y) + 4(2x - 3y)\), which factors to \((2x - 3y)(3x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(p^2 - 2pq - 3p + 6q\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs: \(p(p - 2q) - 3(p - 2q)\). Factor out the common binomial \((p - 2q)\) to get \((p - 2q)(p - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(y^2 + 6y - 6z - yz\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs: \(y(y + 6) - z(6 + y) = y(y + 6) - z(y + 6)\). Factor out the common factor \((y + 6)\) to get \((y + 6)(y - z)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(x^2 - 5x + 5y - xy\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs: \(x(x - 5) - y(x - 5)\). Factor out the common binomial \((x - 5)\) to get \((x - 5)(x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(a^2 + 3a - 3b - ab\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs: \(a(a + 3) - b(3 + a) = a(a + 3) - b(a + 3)\). Factor out the common binomial \((a + 3)\) to obtain \((a + 3)(a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 - 4xy + 15x - 10y\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs: \(2x(3x - 2y) + 5(3x - 2y)\). Factor out the common binomial \((3x - 2y)\) to obtain \((3x - 2y)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(ax + 2ay + bx + 2by - cx - 2cy\)
qs.s: Group terms into pairs by common monomial factors: \(a(x + 2y) + b(x + 2y) - c(x + 2y)\). Factor out the common binomial \((x + 2y)\) to obtain \((x + 2y)(a + b - c)\).
Group terms into pairs: \(4a(3a - 5b) - 3(3a - 5b)\). Factor out the common binomial \((3a - 5b)\) to get \((3a - 5b)(4a - 3)\).
Group terms into pairs: \(x^2(2x - 3y) + 5(2x - 3y)\). Factor out the common binomial \((2x - 3y)\) to obtain \((2x - 3y)(x^2 + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(a - ab + 1 - b\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \(a(1 - b) + 1(1 - b)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((1 - b)\) gives \((a + 1)(1 - b)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(3 - 3a + b - ab\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \(3(1 - a) + b(1 - a)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((1 - a)\) gives \((3 + b)(1 - a)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(1 - x - y + xy\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((1 - x) - y(1 - x)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((1 - x)\) gives \((1 - x)(1 - y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(m - 1 - mn + n\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((m - 1) - n(m - 1)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((m - 1)\) gives \((m - 1)(1 - n)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(x + 2 + xy + 2y\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((x + 2) + y(x + 2)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x + 2)\) gives \((x + 2)(y + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2a^2b - 6ab - 7a + 21\)
qs.s: Group as \((2a^2b - 6ab) - (7a - 21) = 2ab(a - 3) - 7(a - 3)\). Factoring out \((a - 3)\) gives \((2ab - 7)(a - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^3 - 4x^2y + 6x - 12y\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(x^3 - 2x^2y + 3x - 6y)\). Then group inside the brackets as \(x^2(x - 2y) + 3(x - 2y) = (x^2 + 3)(x - 2y)\), resulting in \(2(x^2 + 3)(x - 2y)\).
Group as \((6a^2b^2 - 4a^2) - (9b^2 - 6) = 2a^2(3b^2 - 2) - 3(3b^2 - 2)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((3b^2 - 2)\) yields \((2a^2 - 3)(3b^2 - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(ax - ay + az + 2bx - 2by + 2bz\)
qs.s: Group the six terms into two sets of three: \((ax - ay + az) + (2bx - 2by + 2bz) = a(x - y + z) + 2b(x - y + z)\). Factoring out \((x - y + z)\) gives \((a + 2b)(x - y + z)\).
Group the polynomial as \((6x^3 - 4x^2) + (9x - 6) = 2x^2(3x - 2) + 3(3x - 2)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((3x - 2)\) yields \((2x^2 + 3)(3x - 2)\).
Group the terms as \((2x^3 - 8x^2) - (3x - 12) = 2x^2(x - 4) - 3(x - 4)\). Factoring out \((x - 4)\) gives \((2x^2 - 3)(x - 4)\).
Group the terms as \((7x^3 + 14x^2) - (3x + 6) = 7x^2(x + 2) - 3(x + 2)\). Factoring out \((x + 2)\) gives \((7x^2 - 3)(x + 2)\).
Group the terms as \((4x^3 + 6x^2) - (10x + 15) = 2x^2(2x + 3) - 5(2x + 3)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((2x^2 - 5)(2x + 3)\).
Group the terms as \((3x^3 + 15x^2) - (4x + 20) = 3x^2(x + 5) - 4(x + 5)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x + 5)\) yields \((3x^2 - 4)(x + 5)\).
Group the terms as \((5x^3 - 10x^2) + (3x - 6) = 5x^2(x - 2) + 3(x - 2)\). Factoring out \((x - 2)\) yields \((5x^2 + 3)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 + 40x^3 - 28x^2 - 70x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(8x^3 + 20x^2 - 14x - 35)\). Grouping inside gives \(2x[4x^2(2x + 5) - 7(2x + 5)] = 2x(4x^2 - 7)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6xy - 15 + 10x - 9y\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms into pairs: \((6xy + 10x) - (9y + 15) = 2x(3y + 5) - 3(3y + 5)\). Factoring out the common binomial yields \((2x - 3)(3y + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(15a^2b + 25ab - 6ab^2 - 10b^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(b\) to get \(b(15a^2 + 25a - 6ab - 10b)\). Grouping inside yields \(b[5a(3a + 5) - 2b(3a + 5)] = b(5a - 2b)(3a + 5)\).
Rearrange the terms in descending order: \((3x^3 + 12x^2) - (7x + 28) = 3x^2(x + 4) - 7(x + 4)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((3x^2 - 7)(x + 4)\).
Group the terms as \((x^3 - 2x^2) + (7x - 14) = x^2(x - 2) + 7(x - 2)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((x - 2)(x^2 + 7)\).
Group the terms as \((x^3 + 4x^2) - (5x + 20) = x^2(x + 4) - 5(x + 4)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((x + 4)(x^2 - 5)\).
Group the terms as \((x^3 + 6x^2) - (2x + 12) = x^2(x + 6) - 2(x + 6)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((x + 6)(x^2 - 2)\).
Group the terms as \((x^3 - 7x^2) - (3x - 21) = x^2(x - 7) - 3(x - 7)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((x - 7)(x^2 - 3)\).
Group the terms as \((x^3 + 3x^2) + (5x + 15) = x^2(x + 3) + 5(x + 3)\). Factoring out the common binomial gives \((x + 3)(x^2 + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(12ax - 8bx + 15ay - 10by\)
qs.s: Group into pairs as \(4x(3a - 2b) + 5y(3a - 2b)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((3a - 2b)\) gives \((3a - 2b)(4x + 5y)\).
Group the terms as \((2x^3 - 4x^2y) - (3xy^2 - 6y^3) = 2x^2(x - 2y) - 3y^2(x - 2y)\). Factoring out \((x - 2y)\) results in \((x - 2y)(2x^2 - 3y^2)\).
Rearrange the polynomial in descending powers as \(3x^3 + 2x^2 - 15x - 10\), then group as \(x^2(3x + 2) - 5(3x + 2) = (3x + 2)(x^2 - 5)\).
Group in pairs to obtain \(4x^2(x - 3) - 5(x - 3)\). Factor out the common binomial \((x - 3)\) to get \((4x^2 - 5)(x - 3)\).
Group into pairs: \(3x^2(x - 2) - 5(x - 2)\). Factor out the common binomial \((x - 2)\) to get \((3x^2 - 5)(x - 2)\).
Group the terms as \(5x^2(x - 3) - 2(x - 3)\). Factoring out \((x - 3)\) yields \((5x^2 - 2)(x - 3)\).
Group terms in pairs: \(2x^2(x - 4) - 7(x - 4)\). Factoring out the common factor \((x - 4)\) gives \((2x^2 - 7)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2a^2b - 6ab^2 - 5a + 15b\)
qs.s: Group the first two and last two terms: \(2ab(a - 3b) - 5(a - 3b)\). Factoring out the common binomial factor \((a - 3b)\) yields \((2ab - 5)(a - 3b)\).
First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(3x^3 - 9x^2 - 5x + 15)\). Then group terms inside parentheses as \(3x^2(x - 3) - 5(x - 3)\) to get \(2x(3x^2 - 5)(x - 3)\).
Rearrange terms in descending powers of \(x\) as \(2x^3 + 5x^2 - 6x - 15\). Grouping in pairs gives \(x^2(2x + 5) - 3(2x + 5) = (x^2 - 3)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(ax + 2ay + bx + 2by - 3x - 6y\)
qs.s: Group into three pairs: \(a(x + 2y) + b(x + 2y) - 3(x + 2y)\). Factor out the common binomial \((x + 2y)\) to arrive at \((a + b - 3)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(4m^2 + mn^4 - 4n^3 - m^3n\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((4m^2 - 4n^3) - (m^3n - mn^4) = 4(m^2 - n^3) - mn(m^2 - n^3)\). Removing the common factor yields \((4 - mn)(m^2 - n^3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2x^3 + xy^2 - 2y - x^4y\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((2x^3 - 2y) - (x^4y - xy^2) = 2(x^3 - y) - xy(x^3 - y)\). Factor out the common binomial factor \((x^3 - y)\) to obtain \((2 - xy)(x^3 - y)\).
Group the terms as \((2x^2 - 6y) - (x^4y - 3x^2y^2) = 2(x^2 - 3y) - x^2y(x^2 - 3y)\). Factoring out \((x^2 - 3y)\) gives \((2 - x^2y)(x^2 - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6y - 3x^2 - 2xy^2 + x^3y\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((6y - 3x^2) - (2xy^2 - x^3y) = 3(2y - x^2) - xy(2y - x^2)\). Factor out the common binomial factor to get \((3 - xy)(2y - x^2)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(5a - a^2b + ab^3 - 5b^2\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((5a - 5b^2) - (a^2b - ab^3) = 5(a - b^2) - ab(a - b^2)\). Factor out \((a - b^2)\) to get \((5 - ab)(a - b^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2ax - 3bx + 4ay - 6by - 2az + 3bz\)
qs.s: Group the six terms into three pairs as \(x(2a - 3b) + 2y(2a - 3b) - z(2a - 3b)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((2a - 3b)\) gives \((2a - 3b)(x + 2y - z)\).

qs.q: The square has side \(4r\) and contains four circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Square \(16r^2\) minus four circles \(4\pi r^2\) gives \(4r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(4r\) by \(2r\) and contains two circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(8r^2\) minus two circles \(2\pi r^2\) gives \(8r^2-2\pi r^2=2r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(6r\) by \(4r\) and contains six circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(24r^2\) minus six circles \(6\pi r^2\) gives \(6r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The square has side \(2r\) and contains one circle of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Square \(4r^2\) minus circle \(\pi r^2\) gives \(r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(6r\) by \(2r\) and contains three circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(12r^2\) minus three circles \(3\pi r^2\) gives \(3r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(10r\) by \(2r\) and contains five circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(20r^2\) minus five circles \(5\pi r^2\) gives \(5r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(8r\) by \(4r\) and contains eight circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(32r^2\) minus eight circles \(8\pi r^2\) gives \(8r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(6r\) by \(4r\) and contains three circles, each of radius \(r\), spaced as shown. Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(24r^2\) minus three circles \(3\pi r^2\) gives \(3r^2(8-\pi)\).

qs.q: The rectangle is \(8r\) by \(6r\) and contains twelve circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Rectangle \(48r^2\) minus twelve circles \(12\pi r^2\) gives \(12r^2(4-\pi)\).

qs.q: The square has side \(6r\) and contains nine circles, each of radius \(r\). Find the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Square \(36r^2\) minus nine circles \(9\pi r^2\) gives \(9r^2(4-\pi)\).

exercises.name: Area word problem in factored form

qs.q: Determine the remaining area of a rectangular metal sheet in factored form, if the sheet is \(6x^2\text{ cm by } 3x\text{ cm}\), and a rectangular hole measuring \(4x\text{ cm by } 2x\text{ cm}\) is cut out of it.
qs.s: Subtract the hole area from the total sheet area: \((6x^2)(3x) - (4x)(2x) = 18x^3 - 8x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(2x^2\), gives \(2x^2(9x - 4)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the area of the walkway around a garden in factored form, if the outer boundary of the walkway is \(5x^2\text{ m by } 4x\text{ m}\), and the garden inside is \(6x\text{ m by } 2x\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The area of the walkway is \((5x^2)(4x) - (6x)(2x) = 20x^3 - 12x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(4x^2\), yields \(4x^2(5x - 3)\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the uncovered area of a poster board in factored form, if the poster board is \(2x^2\text{ cm by } 7x\text{ cm}\), and a photo placed on it is \(3x\text{ cm by } 2x\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The uncovered area is the total area minus the photo area: \((2x^2)(7x) - (3x)(2x) = 14x^3 - 6x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(2x^2\), gives \(2x^2(7x - 3)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the exposed area of a wooden plaque in factored form, if the plaque is \(4x^2\text{ cm by } 6x\text{ cm}\), and an engraved brass plate measuring \(5x\text{ cm by } 3x\text{ cm}\) is mounted on it.
qs.s: The exposed area is \((4x^2)(6x) - (5x)(3x) = 24x^3 - 15x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(3x^2\), results in \(3x^2(8x - 5)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the area of the picture frame border in factored form, if the picture frame is \(4x^2\text{ cm by } 3x\text{ cm}\), and the picture is \(5x\text{ cm by } 2x\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The border area is the outer area minus the picture area: \((4x^2)(3x) - (5x)(2x) = 12x^3 - 10x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(2x^2\), gives \(2x^2(6x - 5)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the remaining area of a rectangular metal plate in factored form, if the plate measures \(7x^2\text{ cm by } 4x\text{ cm}\), and two rectangular openings measuring \(3x\text{ cm by } 2x\text{ cm}\) and \(4x\text{ cm by } 2x\text{ cm}\) are removed.
qs.s: The combined area of the two openings is \((3x)(2x) + (4x)(2x) = 6x^2 + 8x^2 = 14x^2\). Subtracting this from the plate's area gives \((7x^2)(4x) - 14x^2 = 28x^3 - 14x^2 = 14x^2(2x - 1)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A rectangular patio measures \(5x^2\text{ m by } (3x + 2)\text{ m}\), and an inground swimming pool built inside it measures \(6x\text{ m by } (3x + 2)\text{ m}\). Determine the remaining area of the patio in factored form.
qs.s: The remaining area is \(5x^2(3x + 2) - 6x(3x + 2)\). Removing the common binomial factor \((3x + 2)\) gives \((5x^2 - 6x)(3x + 2)\), and factoring \(x\) from the first factor yields \(x(5x - 6)(3x + 2)\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the area of the mat surrounding an artwork in factored form, if the outer frame measures \(4x\text{ cm by } (2x^2 + 3x)\text{ cm}\), and the artwork measures \(2x\text{ cm by } (x^2 + 3x)\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The mat area is \([4x(2x^2 + 3x)] - [2x(x^2 + 3x)] = (8x^3 + 12x^2) - (2x^3 + 6x^2) = 6x^3 + 6x^2\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(6x^2\), gives \(6x^2(x + 1)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the area of the border of a rectangular billboard in factored form, if the outer billboard is \(8x^3y\text{ m by } 3xy^2\text{ m}\), and the central display screen is \(6x^2y\text{ m by } 2xy^2\text{ m}\).
qs.s: The border area is \((8x^3y)(3xy^2) - (6x^2y)(2xy^2) = 24x^4y^3 - 12x^3y^3\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(12x^3y^3\), yields \(12x^3y^3(2x - 1)\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: Determine the area of the border around a rectangular mirror in factored form, if the outer frame is \((4x^2 + 3x)\text{ cm by } 6x\text{ cm}\), and the mirror is \((2x + 1)\text{ cm by } 3x\text{ cm}\).
qs.s: The area of the border is \((6x)(4x^2 + 3x) - (3x)(2x + 1) = (24x^3 + 18x^2) - (6x^2 + 3x) = 24x^3 + 12x^2 - 3x\). Factoring out the greatest common factor, \(3x\), gives \(3x(8x^2 + 4x - 1)\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: A small equilateral triangle (white) is cut out of a large equilateral triangle. The area of an equilateral triangle with side s is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\). Use the figure to determine the shaded area in simplest factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\big((x+y)^2-(x-y)^2\big)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}(2x)(2y)=\sqrt3\,xy\).

qs.q: A small equilateral triangle (white) is cut out of a large equilateral triangle. The area of an equilateral triangle with side s is \(\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}s^2\). Use the figure to determine the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}\big((2x)^2-y^2\big)=\frac{\sqrt3}{4}(2x-y)(2x+y)\) (difference of squares).

qs.q: A square of side \(x+8\) has a smaller square of side \(x\) cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
A rectangle that is \(x+7\) long and \(2x\) wide has a square of side \(x\) cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
A large square has side \(2x+3\). A square of side 3 is cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
A square of side \(x\) has a smaller square of side 4 cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area = \(x^2-4^2=x^2-16=(x-4)(x+4)\) (difference of squares).

qs.q: A circle of radius \(5x\) has a circle of radius 3 with the same centre cut out of it (see the figure). Determine the shaded (ring) area in factored form.
A rectangle that is \(6x\) wide and \(4x+8\) tall has a smaller rectangle that is \(2x\) wide and \(x+2\) tall cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
A circle of radius \(x+6\) has a circle of radius \(x+2\) with the same centre cut out of it (see the figure). Determine the shaded (ring) area in factored form.
A large square has side \(3x+1\). A smaller square of side \(x-1\) is cut out of one corner (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area = \((3x+1)^2-(x-1)^2=\big(2x+2\big)\big(4x\big)=8x(x+1)\).

qs.q: A square of side \(5x+4\) has a square of side \(3x-1\) cut out of its middle (see the figure). Determine the shaded area in factored form.
A circle of radius \(2x\) just fits inside a square of side \(4x\) (see the figure). Determine the area of the region inside the square but outside the circle, in factored form.
Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 11x + 24 = (x + 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 24 by 3 to get 8, and check that \(3 + 8 = 11\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 12x + 35 = (x + 5)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 35 by 5 to get 7, and check that \(5 + 7 = 12\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 10x + 21 = (x + 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 21 by 7 to get 3, and check that \(7 + 3 = 10\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 9x + 20 = (x + 4)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 20 by 4 to get 5, and check that \(4 + 5 = 9\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 13x + 36 = (x + 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 36 by 9 to get 4, and check that \(9 + 4 = 13\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 4x - 77 = (x - 11)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(-77\) by \(-11\) to get \(+7\). Checking the sum, \(-11 + 7 = -4\), which confirms the missing factor is \(x + 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 72 - 6x = (x - 12)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Rewrite the trinomial in descending order of powers as \(x^2 - 6x - 72\). Dividing \(-72\) by \(-12\) gives \(+6\), and \(-12 + 6 = -6\), so the missing factor is \(x + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4x^2 - 8x - 60 = 4(x - 5)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor 4 gives \(4(x^2 - 2x - 15)\). Dividing \(-15\) by \(-5\) gives \(+3\), and \(-5 + 3 = -2\), so the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 5xy - 24y^2 = (x + 8y)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the last term \(-24y^2\) by \(8y\) to obtain \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \(8y + (-3y) = 5y\), so the missing factor is \(x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 19x + 84 = (x - 12)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term 84 by \(-12\) to get \(-7\). Checking the sum, \(-12 + (-7) = -19\), which confirms the missing factor is \(x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 2x - 24 = (x + 6)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: The two numbers must multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(2\). Since \(6 \times (-4) = -24\) and \(6 + (-4) = 2\), the missing factor is \(x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(y^2 - 11y + 28 = (y - 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: The two numbers must multiply to \(28\) and add to \(-11\). Since \((-7)(-4) = 28\) and \((-7) + (-4) = -11\), the missing factor is \(y - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 3x - 18 = (x - 6)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: The two numbers must multiply to \(-18\) and add to \(-3\). Since \((-6) \times 3 = -18\) and \(-6 + 3 = -3\), the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 7x + 10 = (x + 2)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: The two numbers must multiply to \(10\) and add to \(7\). Since \(2 \times 5 = 10\) and \(2 + 5 = 7\), the missing factor is \(x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 - 22a + 105 = (a - 15)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: The two numbers must multiply to \(105\) and add to \(-22\). Since \((-15)(-7) = 105\) and \((-15) + (-7) = -22\), the missing factor is \(a - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 54 - 3x = (x - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: First arrange the terms in descending order to get \(x^2 - 3x - 54\). Since \((-9) \times 6 = -54\) and \(-9 + 6 = -3\), the missing factor is \(x + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 + 9x - 84 = 3(x + 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3(x^2 + 3x - 28)\). Since \(7 \times (-4) = -28\) and \(7 + (-4) = 3\), the missing factor is \(x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 - 4ab - 96b^2 = (a - 12b)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Find the term that multiplies with \(-12b\) to give \(-96b^2\) and adds to \(-12b\) to give \(-4b\). Since \((-12b)(8b) = -96b^2\) and \(-12b + 8b = -4b\), the missing factor is \(a + 8b\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 16x + 63 = (x + 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(7\) to give \(63\) and adds to \(7\) to give \(16\). Since \(63 \div 7 = 9\) and \(7 + 9 = 16\), the missing factor is \(x + 9\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 12x + 35 = (x - 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(-7\) to give \(35\) and adds to \(-7\) to give \(-12\). Since \(35 \div (-7) = -5\) and \(-7 + (-5) = -12\), the missing factor is \(x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 3x - 40 = (x + 8)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(8\) to give \(-40\) and adds to \(8\) to give \(3\). Since \(-40 \div 8 = -5\) and \(8 + (-5) = 3\), the missing factor is \(x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 2x - 48 = (x - 8)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(-8\) to give \(-48\) and adds to \(-8\) to give \(-2\). Since \(-48 \div (-8) = 6\) and \(-8 + 6 = -2\), the missing factor is \(x + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 13x + 36 = (x + 4)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(4\) to give \(36\) and adds to \(4\) to give \(13\). Since \(36 \div 4 = 9\) and \(4 + 9 = 13\), the missing factor is \(x + 9\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 18x - 144 = (x + 24)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(-144\) by \(24\) yields \(-6\), and checking the sum gives \(24 + (-6) = 18\). Therefore, the missing factor is \(x - 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-x^2 + 2x + 63 = -(x - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) gives \(-(x^2 - 2x - 63)\). Since \(-63 \div (-9) = 7\) and \(-9 + 7 = -2\), the missing factor is \(x + 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 5xy - 66y^2 = (x - 11y)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the last term \(-66y^2\) by \(-11y\) yields \(6y\), and \(-11y + 6y = -5y\). Therefore, the missing binomial factor is \(x + 6y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 27x + 162 = (x - 18)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(162\) by \(-18\) gives \(-9\), and checking the sum gives \(-18 + (-9) = -27\). Therefore, the missing factor is \(x - 9\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 - 15x - 72 = 3(x - 8)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: First factor out the common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3(x^2 - 5x - 24)\). Then dividing \(-24\) by \(-8\) gives \(3\), so the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 4x - 21 = (x + 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(-21\) by \(3\) gives \(-7\), and \(3 + (-7) = -4\), so the missing factor is \(x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 8x + 15 = (x - 5)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(15\) by \(-5\) gives \(-3\), and \(-5 + (-3) = -8\), so the missing factor is \(x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(12\) by \(3\) gives \(4\), and \(3 + 4 = 7\), so the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 2x - 8 = (x - 2)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(-8\) by \(-2\) gives \(4\), and \(-2 + 4 = 2\), so the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 25x + 144 = (x - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing \(144\) by \(-9\) yields \(-16\), and checking the middle term gives \(-9 + (-16) = -25\), so the missing factor is \(x - 16\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 5x - 104 = (x + 13)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing \(-104\) by \(13\) yields \(-8\), and \(13 + (-8) = 5\), confirming the missing factor is \(x - 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 45y^2 - 4xy = (x - 9y)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form yields \(x^2 - 4xy - 45y^2\). Dividing \(-45y^2\) by \(-9y\) gives \(+5y\), and \(-9y + 5y = -4y\), so the missing factor is \(x + 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(k^2 + 15k + 56 = (k + 7)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(56\) by \(7\) to get \(8\), and verify that \(7 + 8 = 15\). Thus, the missing factor is \(k + 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(p^2 + 12p + 32 = (p + 8)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(32\) by \(8\) to get \(4\), and verify that \(8 + 4 = 12\). Thus, the missing factor is \(p + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 + 13a + 36 = (a + 4)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(36\) by \(4\) to get \(9\), and verify that \(4 + 9 = 13\). Thus, the missing factor is \(a + 9\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 + 10m + 21 = (m + 3)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(21\) by \(3\) to get \(7\), and verify that \(3 + 7 = 10\). Thus, the missing factor is \(m + 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 9x + 20 = (x + 5)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(20\) by \(5\) to get \(4\), and verify that \(5 + 4 = 9\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 4x - 96 = (x + 12)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(-96\) by \(12\) to get \(-8\), and verify that \(12 + (-8) = 4\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x - 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(u^2 + 3uv - 54v^2 = (u + 9v)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the last term \(-54v^2\) by \(9v\) to get \(-6v\), and verify that \(9v + (-6v) = 3v\). Thus, the missing factor is \(u - 6v\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 - 7m - 120 = (m - 15)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(-120\) by \(-15\) to get \(8\), and verify that \(-15 + 8 = -7\). Thus, the missing factor is \(m + 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(w^2 - 72 - 6w = (w - 12)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: First arrange the trinomial in descending powers as \(w^2 - 6w - 72\). Dividing \(-72\) by \(-12\) gives \(6\), and \(-12 + 6 = -6\), so the missing factor is \(w + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(y^2 - 23y + 132 = (y - 11)(\) _____ \()\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(132\) by \(-11\) to get \(-12\), and verify that \(-11 + (-12) = -23\). Thus, the missing factor is \(y - 12\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(p^2 - 3p - 28 = (p - 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need two numbers that multiply to \(-28\) and add to \(-3\). Since \((-7)(4) = -28\) and \(-7 + 4 = -3\), the missing factor is \(p + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 + 2m - 24 = (m + 6)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need two numbers that multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(2\). Since \(6 \times (-4) = -24\) and \(6 + (-4) = 2\), the missing factor is \(m - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(w^2 - 13w + 36 = (w - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need two numbers that multiply to \(36\) and add to \(-13\). Since \((-9)(-4) = 36\) and \(-9 + (-4) = -13\), the missing factor is \(w - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 - 8a + 12 = (a - 2)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: We need two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(-8\). Since \((-2)(-6) = 12\) and \(-2 + (-6) = -8\), the missing factor is \(a - 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(c^2 + 13cd - 48d^2 = (c + 16d)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Dividing the last term \(-48d^2\) by \(16d\) yields \(-3d\), and checking the sum gives \(16d + (-3d) = 13d\). Thus, the missing factor is \(c - 3d\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(k^2 - 45 - 4k = (k - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: First rearrange the trinomial in descending order as \(k^2 - 4k - 45\). Since \((-9)(5) = -45\) and \(-9 + 5 = -4\), the missing factor is \(k + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-t^2 - 3t + 40 = -(t + 8)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) yields \(-(t^2 + 3t - 40)\). Since \(8 \times (-5) = -40\) and \(8 + (-5) = 3\), the missing factor is \(t - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4y^2 - 24y - 108 = 4(y - 9)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(4\) leaves \(y^2 - 6y - 27\). Since \((-9)(3) = -27\) and \(-9 + 3 = -6\), the missing factor is \(y + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 - 2m - 24 = (m + 4)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(4\) to give \(-24\) and adds to \(4\) to give \(-2\). Since \((4)(-6) = -24\) and \(4 + (-6) = -2\), the missing factor is \(m - 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(w^2 - 5w - 14 = (w - 7)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(-7\) to give \(-14\) and adds to \(-7\) to give \(-5\). Since \((-7)(2) = -14\) and \(-7 + 2 = -5\), the missing factor is \(w + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(p^2 + 9p + 20 = (p + 5)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We need an integer that multiplies with \(5\) to give \(20\) and adds to \(5\) to give \(9\). Since \((5)(4) = 20\) and \(5 + 4 = 9\), the missing factor is \(p + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x - 3)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We find the number that multiplies with \(-3\) to give \(-15\) and adds to \(-3\) to give \(2\). Since \((-3)(5) = -15\) and \(-3 + 5 = 2\), the missing factor is \(x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 - 8a + 12 = (a - 6)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We find the number that multiplies with \(-6\) to give \(12\) and adds to \(-6\) to give \(-8\). Since \((-6)(-2) = 12\) and \(-6 + (-2) = -8\), the missing factor is \(a - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 + 5ab - 84b^2 = (a + 12b)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: We need a term that multiplies by \(12b\) to give \(-84b^2\) and adds to \(12b\) to give \(5b\). Since \((12b)(-7b) = -84b^2\) and \(12b + (-7b) = 5b\), the missing factor is \(a - 7b\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 3xy - 28y^2 = (x + 4y)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: The missing term must multiply by \(4y\) to give \(-28y^2\) and add to \(4y\) to give \(-3y\). Since \((4y)(-7y) = -28y^2\) and \(4y + (-7y) = -3y\), the missing factor is \(x - 7y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(z^2 - 72 - 6z = (z - 12)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: First rewrite the trinomial in descending order as \(z^2 - 6z - 72\). Since \((-12)(6) = -72\) and \(-12 + 6 = -6\), the missing factor is \(z + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4k^2 - 8k - 60 = 4(k + 3)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Factoring out the common factor \(4\) leaves \(k^2 - 2k - 15\). Since \(3 \times (-5) = -15\) and \(3 + (-5) = -2\), the missing factor is \(k - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-u^2 + 2u + 48 = -(u - 8)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) gives \(-(u^2 - 2u - 48)\). Since \((-8)(6) = -48\) and \(-8 + 6 = -2\), the missing factor is \(u + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(w^2 - 11w + 24 = (w - 8)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Find the number that multiplies by \(-8\) to give \(24\) and adds to \(-8\) to give \(-11\): \(24 \div (-8) = -3\). Thus, the missing factor is \(w - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(p^2 - 4p - 21 = (p + 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Find the number that multiplies by \(3\) to give \(-21\) and adds to \(3\) to give \(-4\): \(-21 \div 3 = -7\). Thus, the missing factor is \(p - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 + 9m + 20 = (m + 4)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Find the number that multiplies by \(4\) to give \(20\) and adds to \(4\) to give \(9\): \(20 \div 4 = 5\). Thus, the missing factor is \(m + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 2x - 15 = (x - 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Find the number that multiplies by \(-3\) to give \(-15\) and adds to \(-3\) to give \(2\): \(-15 \div (-3) = 5\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 5xy - 36y^2 = (x + 9y)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the last term \(-36y^2\) by \(9y\) to get \(-4y\), and verify that \(9y + (-4y) = 5y\). Thus, the missing factor is \(x - 4y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 - 12x - 36 = 3(x - 6)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3(x^2 - 4x - 12)\). Dividing \(-12\) by \(-6\) gives \(2\), so the missing factor is \(x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(y^2 - 8y - 105 = (y + 7)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the constant term \(-105\) by \(7\) to get \(-15\), and verify that \(7 + (-15) = -8\). Thus, the missing factor is \(y - 15\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-2x^2 + 8x + 42 = -2(x + 3)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(x^2 - 4x - 21)\). Dividing \(-21\) by \(3\) gives \(-7\), so the missing factor is \(x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 - 14mn + 48n^2 = (m - 6n)(\underline{\quad})\)
qs.s: Divide the last term \(48n^2\) by \(-6n\) to get \(-8n\), and verify that \(-6n + (-8n) = -14n\). Thus, the missing factor is \(m - 8n\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(y^2 - 8y + 15 = (y - 3)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15\) by \(-3\) gives \(-5\), and \((-3) + (-5) = -8\), so the missing factor is \(y - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(a^2 + 2a - 8 = (a + 4)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing \(-8\) by \(4\) gives \(-2\), and \(4 + (-2) = 2\), so the missing factor is \(a - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(p^2 - 9p + 14 = (p - 2)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing \(14\) by \(-2\) gives \(-7\), and \((-2) + (-7) = -9\), so the missing factor is \(p - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(m^2 - 3m - 10 = (m - 5)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing \(-10\) by \(-5\) gives \(2\), and \((-5) + 2 = -3\), so the missing factor is \(m + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 5x + 6 = (x + 2)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing the constant term \(6\) by \(2\) gives \(3\), and \(2 + 3 = 5\), so the missing factor is \(x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 - 2xy - 35y^2 = (x - 7y)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing the last term \(-35y^2\) by \(-7y\) gives \(5y\), and \((-7y) + 5y = -2y\), so the missing factor is \(x + 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2k^2 + 10k - 48 = 2(k + 8)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(2\) yields \(2(k^2 + 5k - 24)\), and dividing \(-24\) by \(8\) gives the missing factor \(k - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(u^2 + 5uv - 84v^2 = (u + 12v)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Dividing the final term \(-84v^2\) by \(12v\) yields \(-7v\), and \(12v + (-7v) = 5v\), so the missing factor is \(u - 7v\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-n^2 - 3n + 40 = -(n + 8)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) gives \(-(n^2 + 3n - 40)\). Dividing \(-40\) by \(8\) gives \(-5\), so the missing factor is \(n - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(x^2 + 72 - 17x = (x - 9)( \underline{\quad} )\)
qs.s: Rewrite the trinomial in descending order as \(x^2 - 17x + 72\). Dividing \(72\) by \(-9\) gives \(-8\), which satisfies \((-9) + (-8) = -17\), so the missing factor is \(x - 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: x² + 7x + 12 = (x + 3)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with 3 to give 12 and add to 3 to give 7. Since 12 ÷ 3 = 4 and 3 + 4 = 7, the missing factor is x + 4.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: w² − 8w + 12 = (w − 2)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with −2 to give 12 and add to −2 to give −8. Since 12 ÷ (−2) = −6 and −2 + (−6) = −8, the missing factor is w − 6.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: y² − 7y + 10 = (y − 5)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with −5 to give 10 and add to −5 to give −7. Since 10 ÷ (−5) = −2 and −5 + (−2) = −7, the missing factor is y − 2.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: m² − 3m − 18 = (m − 6)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with −6 to give −18 and add to −6 to give −3. Since −18 ÷ (−6) = 3 and −6 + 3 = −3, the missing factor is m + 3.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: a² + 2a − 15 = (a + 5)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with 5 to give −15 and add to 5 to give 2. Since −15 ÷ 5 = −3 and 5 + (−3) = 2, the missing factor is a − 3.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: p² − 23p + 120 = (p − 8)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing constant must multiply with −8 to give 120 and add to −8 to give −23. Since 120 ÷ (−8) = −15 and −8 + (−15) = −23, the missing factor is p − 15.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: −t² + 2t + 35 = −(t − 7)( _____ )
qs.s: Factoring out −1 gives −(t² − 2t − 35). Since −35 ÷ (−7) = 5 and −7 + 5 = −2, the missing factor is t + 5.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: u² − 3uv − 28v² = (u − 7v)( _____ )
qs.s: The missing term must multiply with −7v to give −28v² and add to −7v to give −3v. Since −28v² ÷ (−7v) = 4v and −7v + 4v = −3v, the missing factor is u + 4v.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: 3n² + 15n − 72 = 3(n + 8)( _____ )
qs.s: Factoring out the common factor 3 gives 3(n² + 5n − 24). Since −24 ÷ 8 = −3 and 8 + (−3) = 5, the missing factor is n − 3.

qs.q: Complete the factoring: k² − 40 − 3k = (k − 8)( _____ )

qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(x^2 + 7x - 60)\). The factors of \(-60\) that sum to \(7\) are \(12\) and \(-5\), which gives \(-2(x + 12)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2 + 6xy + 56y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(x^2 - 3xy - 28y^2)\). Finding factors of \(-28y^2\) that add to \(-3y\) gives \(-2(x - 7y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(48x - 4x^2 - 80\)
qs.s: First arrange in descending order as \(-4x^2 + 48x - 80\). Factoring out \(-4\) gives \(-4(x^2 - 12x + 20)\), which factors into \(-4(x - 10)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^2 - 35x + 150\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-5\) to obtain \(-5(x^2 + 7x - 30)\). Two integers that multiply to \(-30\) and add to \(7\) are \(10\) and \(-3\), giving \(-5(x + 10)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^2 + 4x - 4\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(x^2 - 4x + 4)\). Since \(-2\) and \(-2\) multiply to \(4\) and add to \(-4\), the expression factors as \(-(x - 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^2 - 10x - 25\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(x^2 + 10x + 25)\). Since \(5\) and \(5\) multiply to \(25\) and add to \(10\), the expression factors completely as \(-(x + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^2 + 8x - 16\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(x^2 - 8x + 16)\). Since \(-4\) and \(-4\) multiply to \(16\) and add to \(-8\), the expression factors completely as \(-(x - 4)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^2 + 24xy - 36y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-4\) to obtain \(-4(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)\). Recognizing the perfect square trinomial gives \(-4(x - 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36x - 2x^2 - 162\)
qs.s: Rearrange terms in descending order as \(-2x^2 + 36x - 162\) and factor out \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(x^2 - 18x + 81)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial yields \(-2(x - 9)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(105 + 20x - 5x^2\)
qs.s: Write the trinomial in descending order as \(-5x^2 + 20x + 105\) and factor out \(-5\) to get \(-5(x^2 - 4x - 21)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-5(x - 7)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2 - 10xy + 48y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(x^2 + 5xy - 24y^2)\). The two factors of \(-24\) that sum to \(5\) are \(8\) and \(-3\), giving \(-2(x + 8y)(x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^2 - 18x + 48\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(x^2 + 6x - 16)\). Finding two factors of \(-16\) that add to \(6\) gives \(8\) and \(-2\), resulting in \(-3(x + 8)(x - 2)\).

exercises.name: Factoring Trinomials with Monomial GCF or Two Variables

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 + 2x^2 - 15x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 + 2x - 15)\). Then find two numbers that multiply to \(-15\) and add to \(2\), which are \(5\) and \(-3\), giving \(x(x + 5)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^3 + 9m^2 + 14m\)
qs.s: First factor out the common factor \(m\) to get \(m(m^2 + 9m + 14)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(14\) and add to \(9\) are \(7\) and \(2\), resulting in \(m(m + 7)(m + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^3 - 3a^2 - 10a\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(a\) to obtain \(a(a^2 - 3a - 10)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-10\) and add to \(-3\) are \(-5\) and \(2\), yielding \(a(a - 5)(a + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 - 4x^2 - 12x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 - 4x - 12)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-12\) and add to \(-4\) are \(-6\) and \(2\), giving \(x(x - 6)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^3 - 7y^2 + 12y\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(y\) to get \(y(y^2 - 7y + 12)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(-7\) are \(-3\) and \(-4\), giving \(y(y - 3)(y - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 + 24x^3 - 28x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(4x^2\) to obtain \(4x^2(x^2 + 6x - 7)\). The factors of \(-7\) that add to \(6\) are \(7\) and \(-1\), producing \(4x^2(x + 7)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3y - 2x^2y^2 - 35xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(xy\) to get \(xy(x^2 - 2xy - 35y^2)\). Factoring the remaining two-variable trinomial gives \(xy(x - 7y)(x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^3 + 10x^2 + 48x\)
qs.s: Factor out the leading coefficient and common monomial factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(x^2 - 5x - 24)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2x(x - 8)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^3 - 15x^2 - 42x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(x^2 - 5x - 14)\). The factors of \(-14\) that sum to \(-5\) are \(-7\) and \(2\), giving \(3x(x - 7)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5a^3b - 15a^2b + 50ab\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5ab\) to get \(-5ab(a^2 + 3a - 10)\). The factors of \(-10\) that add to \(3\) are \(5\) and \(-2\), yielding \(-5ab(a + 5)(a - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: c^2 - 18cd + 81d^2
qs.s: Find two factors of 81 that add to -18, which are -9 and -9. Therefore, c^2 - 18cd + 81d^2 = (c - 9d)(c - 9d) = (c - 9d)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: p^2 + 8pq + 16q^2
qs.s: Find two factors of 16 that add to 8, which are 4 and 4. Therefore, p^2 + 8pq + 16q^2 = (p + 4q)(p + 4q) = (p + 4q)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: m^2 - 14mn + 49n^2
qs.s: Find two factors of 49 that add to -14, which are -7 and -7. Therefore, m^2 - 14mn + 49n^2 = (m - 7n)(m - 7n) = (m - 7n)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: a^2 - 10ab + 25b^2
qs.s: Find two factors of 25 that add to -10, which are -5 and -5. Therefore, a^2 - 10ab + 25b^2 = (a - 5b)(a - 5b) = (a - 5b)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: x^2 + 16xy + 64y^2
qs.s: Find two factors of 64 that add to 16, which are 8 and 8. Therefore, x^2 + 16xy + 64y^2 = (x + 8y)(x + 8y) = (x + 8y)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: 5u^4v - 30u^3v^2 + 45u^2v^3
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor 5u^2v to obtain 5u^2v(u^2 - 6uv + 9v^2). Factoring the trinomial gives 5u^2v(u - 3v)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: 3x^3 - 24x^2y + 48xy^2
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor 3x to get 3x(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields 3x(x - 4y)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: 2p^3q + 32p^2q^2 + 128pq^3
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor 2pq to obtain 2pq(p^2 + 16pq + 64q^2). Then, factor the trinomial to get 2pq(p + 8q)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: -2a^2b + 20ab^2 - 50b^3
qs.s: Factor out the common factor -2b to get -2b(a^2 - 10ab + 25b^2). Then, factor the trinomial to obtain -2b(a - 5b)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: -m^3n - 14m^2n^2 - 49mn^3
qs.s: Factor out the common factor -mn to get -mn(m^2 + 14mn + 49n^2). Factoring the trinomial produces -mn(m + 7n)^2.

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2z - 9xz - 36z\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(z\) to get \(z(x^2 - 9x - 36)\). Then find two factors of \(-36\) that add to \(-9\), which are \(-12\) and \(3\), giving \(z(x - 12)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^2k - 13mk + 42k\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(k\) to get \(k(m^2 - 13m + 42)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(42\) and add to \(-13\) are \(-6\) and \(-7\), so the factored form is \(k(m - 6)(m - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(p^2c - 4pc - 45c\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(c\) to get \(c(p^2 - 4p - 45)\). The factors of \(-45\) that add to \(-4\) are \(-9\) and \(5\), resulting in \(c(p - 9)(p + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^2w + 3yw - 40w\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(w\) to obtain \(w(y^2 + 3y - 40)\). Two factors of \(-40\) that add to \(3\) are \(8\) and \(-5\), giving \(w(y + 8)(y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2b + 5ab - 50b\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(b\) to get \(b(a^2 + 5a - 50)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-50\) and add to \(5\) are \(10\) and \(-5\), resulting in \(b(a + 10)(a - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^2y - 42xy - 360y\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(6y\) to get \(6y(x^2 - 7x - 60)\). Two factors of \(-60\) that add to \(-7\) are \(-12\) and \(5\), giving \(6y(x - 12)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2a^3b - 16a^2b^2 - 66ab^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2ab\) to get \(2ab(a^2 - 8ab - 33b^2)\). Factoring the two-variable trinomial gives \(2ab(a - 11b)(a + 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^4y - 25x^3y + 70x^2y\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-5x^2y\) to leave \(-5x^2y(x^2 + 5x - 14)\). Find factors of \(-14\) that sum to \(5\), which are \(7\) and \(-2\), yielding \(-5x^2y(x + 7)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^3y - 15x^2y - 108xy\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3xy\) to get \(3xy(x^2 - 5x - 36)\). Then factor the trinomial using numbers that multiply to \(-36\) and add to \(-5\), which are \(-9\) and \(4\), yielding \(3xy(x - 9)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2y + 10xy + 48y\)
qs.s: Factor out the negative common factor \(-2y\) so the leading coefficient inside the parentheses is \(1\): \(-2y(x^2 - 5x - 24)\). Then factor the trinomial into \(-2y(x - 8)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4 + 14x^3 - 24x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2x^2\), leaving \(-2x^2(x^2 - 7x + 12)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2x^2(x - 3)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^4 - 2x^3 + 24x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-x^2\), giving \(-x^2(x^2 + 2x - 24)\). Factoring the trinomial into binomial factors results in \(-x^2(x + 6)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^5 - 6x^4 + 20x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2x^3\), to obtain \(-2x^3(x^2 + 3x - 10)\). Then, factor the trinomial into \((x + 5)(x - 2)\) to get \(-2x^3(x + 5)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^4 + 9x^3 + 30x^2\)
qs.s: First, factor out the greatest common factor, \(-3x^2\), to get \(-3x^2(x^2 - 3x - 10)\). Then, factor the remaining trinomial into \((x - 5)(x + 2)\) to obtain \(-3x^2(x - 5)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^3 - 10x^2 + 40x\)
qs.s: First, factor out the greatest common factor, \(-5x\), giving \(-5x(x^2 + 2x - 8)\). Then, factor the quadratic trinomial into \((x + 4)(x - 2)\) to get \(-5x(x + 4)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^5 + 40x^4 + 240x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-5x^3\), to get \(-5x^3(x^2 - 8x - 48)\). Finding factors of \(-48\) that sum to \(-8\) gives \(-5x^3(x - 12)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4y^2 + 30x^3y^3 - 112x^2y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2x^2y^2\), leaving \(-2x^2y^2(x^2 - 15xy + 56y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial into binomials that multiply to \(56y^2\) and add to \(-15y\) yields \(-2x^2y^2(x - 8y)(x - 7y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^5 - 28x^4 + 120x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-4x^3\), to obtain \(-4x^3(x^2 + 7x - 30)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-4x^3(x + 10)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^4y + 9x^3y^2 + 84x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-3x^2y\), to obtain \(-3x^2y(x^2 - 3xy - 28y^2)\). Then, find two factors that multiply to \(-28y^2\) and add to \(-3y\), giving \(-3x^2y(x - 7y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2a^3b^3 - 10a^2b^4 + 72ab^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2ab^3\), to get \(-2ab^3(a^2 + 5ab - 36b^2)\). Factoring the resulting two-variable trinomial gives \(-2ab^3(a + 9b)(a - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^4 - 7x^3 - 12x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-x^2\) to obtain \(-x^2(x^2 + 7x + 12)\). Factoring the trinomial with two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(7\) yields \(-x^2(x + 3)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^4 + 8x^3 + 60x^2\)
qs.s: First factor out \(-4x^2\) to leave \(-4x^2(x^2 - 2x - 15)\). Then find two factors of \(-15\) that add to \(-2\), which are \(-5\) and \(3\), giving \(-4x^2(x - 5)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4 - 6x^3 + 20x^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x^2\) to get \(-2x^2(x^2 + 3x - 10)\). Then find two integers that multiply to \(-10\) and add to \(3\), which are \(5\) and \(-2\), giving \(-2x^2(x + 5)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^4 + 20x^3 + 60x^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the monomial GCF \(-5x^2\) to get \(-5x^2(x^2 - 4x - 12)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial using \(-6\) and \(2\), which multiply to \(-12\) and add to \(-4\), giving \(-5x^2(x - 6)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^4 - 15x^3 - 18x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3x^2\) to obtain \(-3x^2(x^2 + 5x + 6)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial by finding two numbers that multiply to \(6\) and add to \(5\) gives \(-3x^2(x + 2)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4y - 6x^3y^2 + 56x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the two-variable monomial factor \(-2x^2y\) to get \(-2x^2y(x^2 + 3xy - 28y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial into two binomials gives \(-2x^2y(x + 7y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^4y - 15x^3y^2 + 72x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-3x^2y\) to get \(-3x^2y(x^2 + 5xy - 24y^2)\). Then find two numbers that multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(5\), which are \(8\) and \(-3\), yielding \(-3x^2y(x + 8y)(x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^3y^2 + 42x^2y^3 - 72xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-6xy^2\) to obtain \(-6xy^2(x^2 - 7xy + 12y^2)\). Factoring the two-variable trinomial gives \(-6xy^2(x - 3y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^5 + 26x^4 - 72x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the degree-3 common factor \(-2x^3\) to obtain \(-2x^3(x^2 - 13x + 36)\). Finding two factors of \(36\) that add to \(-13\) gives \(-4\) and \(-9\), resulting in \(-2x^3(x - 4)(x - 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5a^3b^2 - 25a^2b^3 + 70ab^4\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-5ab^2\) to obtain \(-5ab^2(a^2 + 5ab - 14b^2)\). Then factor the quadratic in two variables using factors \(7\) and \(-2\) to get \(-5ab^2(a + 7b)(a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3u^3 + 24u^2v + 36uv^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3u\) to get \(3u(u^2 + 8uv + 12v^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \((u + 2v)(u + 6v)\) since \(2\) and \(6\) add to \(8\) and multiply to \(12\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^3 + 30x^2y + 36xy^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(6x\) to get \(6x(x^2 + 5xy + 6y^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \(6x(x + 2y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^3 - 4x^2y - 30xy^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(x^2 - 2xy - 15y^2)\), then find two numbers that multiply to \(-15\) and add to \(-2\), giving \(2x(x - 5y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^3 - 28a^2b + 40ab^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(4a\) to get \(4a(a^2 - 7ab + 10b^2)\), then factor the trinomial using factors \(-2\) and \(-5\) to obtain \(4a(a - 2b)(a - 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^3y^2 - 18x^2y^3 + 60xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-6xy^2\) to obtain \(-6xy^2(x^2 + 3xy - 10y^2)\), then factor the resulting trinomial into \(-6xy^2(x + 5y)(x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 + 24x^3y - 160x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(4x^2\) to get \(4x^2(x^2 + 6xy - 40y^2)\), then find two numbers that multiply to \(-40\) and add to \(6\), giving \(4x^2(x + 10y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-5x^3y + 15x^2y^2 + 140xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the negative monomial factor \(-5xy\) to obtain \(-5xy(x^2 - 3xy - 28y^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \(-5xy(x - 7y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^4y - 84x^3y^2 + 144x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(12x^2y\) to get \(12x^2y(x^2 - 7xy + 12y^2)\), then factor the trinomial into \((x - 3y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-8a^4 + 8a^3b + 48a^2b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the leading common monomial factor \(-8a^2\) to leave \(-8a^2(a^2 - ab - 6b^2)\), then factor the remaining trinomial into \(-8a^2(a - 3b)(a + 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-p^3q - 4p^2q^2 + 12pq^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-pq\) to obtain \(-pq(p^2 + 4pq - 12q^2)\). The integers multiplying to \(-12\) and adding to \(4\) are \(6\) and \(-2\), so the completely factored form is \(-pq(p + 6q)(p - 2q)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-m^3n + 3m^2n^2 + 10mn^3\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-mn\) gives \(-mn(m^2 - 3mn - 10n^2)\). Find two integers that multiply to \(-10\) and add to \(-3\), yielding \(-mn(m - 5n)(m + 2n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^3y + 2x^2y^2 + 8xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-xy\) to get \(-xy(x^2 - 2xy - 8y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(-8\) that add to \(-2\), which gives \(-xy(x - 4y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^3y + x^2y^2 + 12xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out \(-xy\) to get \(-xy(x^2 - xy - 12y^2)\). The integers that multiply to \(-12\) and add to \(-1\) are \(-4\) and \(3\), giving \(-xy(x - 4y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-a^3b - 5a^2b^2 - 6ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-ab\) to obtain \(-ab(a^2 + 5ab + 6b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-ab(a + 2b)(a + 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^5y^2 - 10x^4y^3 + 72x^3y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(-2x^3y^2\) to get \(-2x^3y^2(x^2 + 5xy - 36y^2)\). Then find two integers that multiply to \(-36\) and add to \(5\), yielding \(-2x^3y^2(x + 9y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(48x^2y^3 + 10x^3y^2 - 2x^4y\)
qs.s: First rewrite the terms in descending order of powers of \(x\) as \(-2x^4y + 10x^3y^2 + 48x^2y^3\), then factor out \(-2x^2y\) to get \(-2x^2y(x^2 - 5xy - 24y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2x^2y(x - 8y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3y^3 + 24x^2y^4 - 36xy^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-4xy^3\) to obtain \(-4xy^3(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)\). The remaining trinomial is a perfect square, giving \(-4xy^3(x - 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4y^2 + 8x^3y^3 + 42x^2y^4\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2x^2y^2\), to get \(-2x^2y^2(x^2 - 4xy - 21y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(-21\) that add to \(-4\), giving \(-2x^2y^2(x - 7y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3a^5b - 9a^4b^2 + 84a^3b^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3a^3b\), leaving \(-3a^3b(a^2 + 3ab - 28b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-3a^3b(a + 7b)(a - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3u^5 - 15u^4v + 18u^3v^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3u^3\) to get \(3u^3(u^2 - 5uv + 6v^2)\). Factoring the trinomial results in \(3u^3(u - 2v)(u - 3v)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^4y + 14x^3y^2 + 24x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x^2y\) to get \(2x^2y(x^2 + 7xy + 12y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(2x^2y(x + 3y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5x^3y - 20x^2y^2 - 60xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(5xy\) to get \(5xy(x^2 - 4xy - 12y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(5xy(x - 6y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3a^4 + 9a^3b - 30a^2b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3a^2\) to obtain \(3a^2(a^2 + 3ab - 10b^2)\). Then factor the remaining trinomial to get \(3a^2(a + 5b)(a - 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(96a^3b^3 - 4a^5b - 8a^4b^2\)
qs.s: Arrange terms in descending powers of \(a\) as \(-4a^5b - 8a^4b^2 + 96a^3b^3\), then factor out \(-4a^3b\) to get \(-4a^3b(a^2 + 2ab - 24b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-4a^3b(a + 6b)(a - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3a^5b^2 + 15a^4b^3 + 108a^3b^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3a^3b^2\) to obtain \(-3a^3b^2(a^2 - 5ab - 36b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields \(-3a^3b^2(a - 9b)(a + 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-8x^5y + 80x^4y^2 - 200x^3y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-8x^3y\) to get \(-8x^3y(x^2 - 10xy + 25y^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(-8x^3y(x - 5y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(15u^3v^3 - 5u^4v^2 + 140u^2v^4\)
qs.s: Arrange in descending powers of \(u\) as \(-5u^4v^2 + 15u^3v^3 + 140u^2v^4\) and factor out \(-5u^2v^2\) to get \(-5u^2v^2(u^2 - 3uv - 28v^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-5u^2v^2(u - 7v)(u + 4v)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5x^4y^3 - 85x^3y^4 + 360x^2y^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(5x^2y^3\) to get \(5x^2y^3(x^2 - 17xy + 72y^2)\). Finding two factors of \(72\) that add to \(-17\) gives \(5x^2y^3(x - 8y)(x - 9y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-u^4v^2 + 7u^3v^3 - 10u^2v^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-u^2v^2\) to get \(-u^2v^2(u^2 - 7uv + 10v^2)\). Then find two factors of \(10\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-2\) and \(-5\), giving \(-u^2v^2(u - 2v)(u - 5v)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^3y^3 + 8x^2y^4 - 12xy^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-xy^3\) to get \(-xy^3(x^2 - 8xy + 12y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(12\) that add to \(-8\), which are \(-2\) and \(-6\), giving \(-xy^3(x - 2y)(x - 6y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^3y^2 - 6x^2y^3 - 20xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(2xy^2\) to get \(2xy^2(x^2 - 3xy - 10y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(-10\) that add to \(-3\), which are \(-5\) and \(2\), giving \(2xy^2(x - 5y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^4y - 5x^3y^2 - 6x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-x^2y\) to get \(-x^2y(x^2 + 5xy + 6y^2)\). Then find two factors of \(6\) that add to \(5\), which are \(2\) and \(3\), giving \(-x^2y(x + 2y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-a^3b^2 + 2a^2b^3 + 8ab^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-ab^2\) to get \(-ab^2(a^2 - 2ab - 8b^2)\). Then find two factors of \(-8\) that add to \(-2\), which are \(-4\) and \(2\), giving \(-ab^2(a - 4b)(a + 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(44x^3y^4 + 240x^2y^5 - 4x^4y^3\)
qs.s: Rearrange in descending powers of \(x\) to get \(-4x^4y^3 + 44x^3y^4 + 240x^2y^5\), then factor out \(-4x^2y^3\) to obtain \(-4x^2y^3(x^2 - 11xy - 60y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial with factors \(-15\) and \(4\) gives \(-4x^2y^3(x - 15y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^4yz^2 + 10x^3y^2z^2 + 72x^2y^3z^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(-2x^2yz^2\) to get \(-2x^2yz^2(x^2 - 5xy - 36y^2)\). Find two factors of \(-36\) that sum to \(-5\), which are \(-9\) and \(4\), giving \(-2x^2yz^2(x - 9y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(140ab^4 - 15a^2b^3 - 5a^3b^2\)
qs.s: Arrange the terms in descending powers of \(a\) as \(-5a^3b^2 - 15a^2b^3 + 140ab^4\) and factor out the GCF \(-5ab^2\) to get \(-5ab^2(a^2 + 3ab - 28b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-5ab^2(a + 7b)(a - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^3y^2 + 34x^2y^3 - 144xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-2xy^2\) to get \(-2xy^2(x^2 - 17xy + 72y^2)\). Two factors of \(72\) that sum to \(-17\) are \(-8\) and \(-9\), which results in \(-2xy^2(x - 8y)(x - 9y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3x^5y^2 + 24x^4y^3 + 144x^3y^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-3x^3y^2\) to obtain \(-3x^3y^2(x^2 - 8xy - 48y^2)\). Two factors of \(-48\) that add to \(-8\) are \(-12\) and \(4\), yielding \(-3x^3y^2(x - 12y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: y^5 + 10y^4z + 21y^3z^2
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial y^3 to get y^3(y^2 + 10yz + 21z^2). Two numbers that multiply to 21 and add to 10 are 3 and 7, giving y^3(y + 3z)(y + 7z).

qs.q: Factor completely: u^8 - 12u^7v + 35u^6v^2
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor u^6 to get u^6(u^2 - 12uv + 35v^2). Find two integers that multiply to 35 and add to -12, which are -5 and -7, yielding u^6(u - 5v)(u - 7v).

qs.q: Factor completely: a^5 - 9a^4b + 20a^3b^2
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor, a^3, to obtain a^3(a^2 - 9ab + 20b^2). Then find two factors of 20 that add to -9, which are -4 and -5, giving a^3(a - 4b)(a - 5b).

qs.q: Factor completely: x^7 + 3x^6y - 18x^5y^2
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor x^5 to obtain x^5(x^2 + 3xy - 18y^2). Two factors of -18 that add to 3 are 6 and -3, resulting in x^5(x + 6y)(x - 3y).

qs.q: Factor completely: m^6 - 2m^5n - 24m^4n^2
qs.s: Factor out the common factor m^4 to get m^4(m^2 - 2mn - 24n^2). Find two numbers that multiply to -24 and add to -2, which are -6 and 4, yielding m^4(m - 6n)(m + 4n).

qs.q: Factor completely: x^4yz^2 - 15x^3y^2z^2 + 54x^2y^3z^2
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor x^2yz^2 to get x^2yz^2(x^2 - 15xy + 54y^2). Two numbers that multiply to 54 and add to -15 are -6 and -9, giving x^2yz^2(x - 6y)(x - 9y).

qs.q: Factor completely: 3x^5 - 15x^4y - 72x^3y^2
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor 3x^3 to get 3x^3(x^2 - 5xy - 24y^2). Two factors of -24 that add to -5 are -8 and 3, yielding 3x^3(x - 8y)(x + 3y).

qs.q: Factor completely: 2a^4b^2 - 28a^3b^3 + 96a^2b^4
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial 2a^2b^2 to obtain 2a^2b^2(a^2 - 14ab + 48b^2). Two factors of 48 that add to -14 are -6 and -8, resulting in 2a^2b^2(a - 6b)(a - 8b).

qs.q: Factor completely: -x^5y + 4x^4y^2 + 45x^3y^3
qs.s: Factor out the negative common factor -x^3y to get -x^3y(x^2 - 4xy - 45y^2). Two numbers that multiply to -45 and add to -4 are -9 and 5, giving -x^3y(x - 9y)(x + 5y).

exercises.name: Factoring Trinomials with Rational Coefficients or Variable Exponents

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{7}{6}x + \frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{1}{3}\) and add to \(\frac{7}{6}\). Since \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{7}{6}\), the trinomial factors as \((x + \frac{1}{2})(x + \frac{2}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{7}{12}x + \frac{1}{12}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{1}{12}\) and add to \(-\frac{7}{12}\). Since \((-\frac{1}{4})(-\frac{1}{3}) = \frac{1}{12}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{7}{12}\), the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{1}{4})(x - \frac{1}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{1}{10}x - \frac{1}{5}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{5}\) and add to \(-\frac{1}{10}\). Since \((-\frac{1}{2})(\frac{2}{5}) = -\frac{1}{5}\) and \(-\frac{1}{2} + \frac{2}{5} = -\frac{1}{10}\), the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{1}{2})(x + \frac{2}{5})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{1}{6}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{6}\) and add to \(\frac{1}{6}\). Since \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot (-\frac{1}{3}) = -\frac{1}{6}\) and \(\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{6}\), the trinomial factors as \((x + \frac{1}{2})(x - \frac{1}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{11}{15}x + \frac{2}{15}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{2}{15}\) and add to \(\frac{11}{15}\). Since \(\frac{1}{3} \cdot \frac{2}{5} = \frac{2}{15}\) and \(\frac{1}{3} + \frac{2}{5} = \frac{11}{15}\), the trinomial factors as \((x + \frac{1}{3})(x + \frac{2}{5})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{23}{24}x + \frac{5}{24}\)
qs.s: We look for two fractions that multiply to \(\frac{5}{24}\) and add to \(-\frac{23}{24}\). Since \((-\frac{1}{3})(-\frac{5}{8}) = \frac{5}{24}\) and \(-\frac{1}{3} - \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{8}{24} - \frac{15}{24} = -\frac{23}{24}\), the expression factors as \((x - \frac{1}{3})(x - \frac{5}{8})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} + \frac{7}{10}x^n + \frac{1}{10}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^n\) so the expression becomes \(u^2 + \frac{7}{10}u + \frac{1}{10}\). Since \(\frac{1}{2} \cdot \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{10}\) and \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{7}{10}\), it factors as \((x^n + \frac{1}{2})(x^n + \frac{1}{5})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - \frac{1}{6}x^n - \frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: Using the substitution \(u = x^n\), factor \(u^2 - \frac{1}{6}u - \frac{1}{3}\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{3}\) and add to \(-\frac{1}{6}\) are \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\), giving \((x^n - \frac{2}{3})(x^n + \frac{1}{2})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{1}{4}xy - \frac{3}{8}y^2\)
qs.s: Treating this as a trinomial in \(x\), find two terms with \(y\) that multiply to \(-\frac{3}{8}y^2\) and add to \(\frac{1}{4}y\). Since \((\frac{3}{4}y)(-\frac{1}{2}y) = -\frac{3}{8}y^2\) and \(\frac{3}{4}y - \frac{1}{2}y = \frac{1}{4}y\), the trinomial factors as \((x + \frac{3}{4}y)(x - \frac{1}{2}y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 - \frac{11}{12}x^2 + \frac{1}{6}x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to obtain \(x(x^2 - \frac{11}{12}x + \frac{1}{6})\). Then factor the trinomial using \(-\frac{1}{4}\) and \(-\frac{2}{3}\), which add to \(-\frac{11}{12}\) and multiply to \(\frac{1}{6}\), yielding \(x(x - \frac{1}{4})(x - \frac{2}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - x + \frac{5}{36}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{5}{36}\) and add to \(-1\). The numbers are \(-\frac{1}{6}\) and \(-\frac{5}{6}\), so the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{1}{6})(x - \frac{5}{6})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 2x + \frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{3}{4}\) and add to \(-2\). The numbers are \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-\frac{3}{2}\), giving \((x - \frac{1}{2})(x - \frac{3}{2})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + x + \frac{6}{25}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{6}{25}\) and add to \(1\). The numbers are \(\frac{2}{5}\) and \(\frac{3}{5}\), so the trinomial factors as \((x + \frac{2}{5})(x + \frac{3}{5})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - x + \frac{3}{16}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(\frac{3}{16}\) and add to \(-1\). The numbers are \(-\frac{1}{4}\) and \(-\frac{3}{4}\), so the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{1}{4})(x - \frac{3}{4})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - x - \frac{4}{9}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(-\frac{4}{9}\) and add to \(-1\). The numbers are \(-\frac{4}{3}\) and \(\frac{1}{3}\), so the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{4}{3})(x + \frac{1}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{7}{10}xy + \frac{1}{10}y^2\)
qs.s: Find two coefficients that multiply to \(\frac{1}{10}\) and add to \(-\frac{7}{10}\). Since \(-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{5} = -\frac{5}{10} - \frac{2}{10} = -\frac{7}{10}\) and \((-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{1}{5}) = \frac{1}{10}\), the trinomial factors as \((x - \frac{1}{2}y)(x - \frac{1}{5}y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - \frac{7}{6}x^n + \frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: Treat the trinomial as a quadratic in \(x^n\). The numbers that multiply to \(\frac{1}{3}\) and add to \(-\frac{7}{6}\) are \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(-\frac{1}{2}\), giving \((x^n - \frac{2}{3})(x^n - \frac{1}{2})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 - \frac{3}{4}x^2 + \frac{1}{8}x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 - \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{1}{8})\). The inner quadratic factors using \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4}\) since \(-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{4} = -\frac{3}{4}\) and \((-\frac{1}{2})(-\frac{1}{4}) = \frac{1}{8}\), giving \(x(x - \frac{1}{2})(x - \frac{1}{4})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{1}{12}x - \frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Find two fractions that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and add to \(\frac{1}{12}\). The values \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(-\frac{2}{3}\) satisfy \(\frac{3}{4} - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{9}{12} - \frac{8}{12} = \frac{1}{12}\) and \((\frac{3}{4})(-\frac{2}{3}) = -\frac{1}{2}\), yielding \((x + \frac{3}{4})(x - \frac{2}{3})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{1}{3}\)
qs.s: We find two fractions that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{3}\) and add to \(-\frac{1}{6}\), which are \(-\frac{2}{3}\) and \(\frac{1}{2}\). Thus, \(x^2 - \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{1}{3} = \left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{12}\)
qs.s: We look for two fractions that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{12}\) and add to \(\frac{1}{3}\); these are \(\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-\frac{1}{6}\). Thus, \(x^2 + \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{12} = \left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{6}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{3}{16}\)
qs.s: We find two fractions that multiply to \(-\frac{3}{16}\) and add to \(\frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{4}\), which are \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4}\). Thus, the factored form is \(\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{1}{8}\)
qs.s: We look for two fractions that multiply to \(\frac{1}{8}\) and add to \(-\frac{3}{4}\); these are \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4}\). Thus, \(x^2 - \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{1}{8} = \left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{1}{6}\)
qs.s: We look for two fractions that multiply to \(\frac{1}{6}\) and add to \(\frac{5}{6}\); since \(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{6} + \frac{2}{6} = \frac{5}{6}\), the factors are \(\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{5}{12}xy - \frac{1}{6}y^2\)
qs.s: Find two coefficients that multiply to \(-\frac{1}{6}\) and add to \(\frac{5}{12}\), which are \(\frac{2}{3}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4}\). Including the variable \(y\) in the second term gives \(\left(x + \frac{2}{3}y\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{4}y\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - \frac{1}{4} + \frac{5}{12}x\)
qs.s: First rearrange in descending powers of \(x\) as \(x^2 + \frac{5}{12}x - \frac{1}{4}\). Two numbers multiplying to \(-\frac{1}{4}\) and adding to \(\frac{5}{12}\) are \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(-\frac{1}{3}\), giving \(\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{3}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 - \frac{1}{10}x^2 - \frac{1}{5}x\)
qs.s: First remove the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x\left(x^2 - \frac{1}{10}x - \frac{1}{5}\right)\). Then factor the trinomial using \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and \(\frac{2}{5}\), which multiply to \(-\frac{1}{5}\) and add to \(-\frac{1}{10}\), giving \(x\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(x + \frac{2}{5}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + \frac{7}{12}x - \frac{5}{24}\)
qs.s: Find two fractions that multiply to \(-\frac{5}{24}\) and add to \(\frac{7}{12} = \frac{14}{24}\); these are \(\frac{5}{6} = \frac{20}{24}\) and \(-\frac{1}{4} = -\frac{6}{24}\). Thus, the factored form is \(\left(x + \frac{5}{6}\right)\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{4}x^3 + 2x^2 + 3x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{1}{4}x\) to get \(\frac{1}{4}x(x^2 + 8x + 12)\). Finding two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(8\) gives \(2\) and \(6\), resulting in \(\frac{1}{4}x(x + 2)(x + 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{2}x^3 - 3x^2 + 4x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{1}{2}x\) to get \(\frac{1}{2}x(x^2 - 6x + 8)\). The integers that multiply to \(8\) and add to \(-6\) are \(-2\) and \(-4\), giving \(\frac{1}{2}x(x - 2)(x - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{3}x^3 - x^2 - 6x\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(\frac{1}{3}x\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{3}x(x^2 - 3x - 18)\). The numbers that multiply to \(-18\) and add to \(-3\) are \(-6\) and \(3\), giving \(\frac{1}{3}x(x - 6)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{5}x^3 - x^2 - 10x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{1}{5}x\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{5}x(x^2 - 5x - 50)\). Two factors of \(-50\) that add to \(-5\) are \(-10\) and \(5\), giving \(\frac{1}{5}x(x - 10)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{2}x^3 + 2x^2 - 6x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(\frac{1}{2}x\) to get \(\frac{1}{2}x(x^2 + 4x - 12)\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-12\) and add to \(4\) are \(6\) and \(-2\), so the expression factors completely as \(\frac{1}{2}x(x + 6)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{2}x^3y - 3x^2y^2 - 20xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(\frac{1}{2}xy\) to get \(\frac{1}{2}xy(x^2 - 6xy - 40y^2)\). The two factors of \(-40\) that sum to \(-6\) are \(-10\) and \(4\), giving \(\frac{1}{2}xy(x - 10y)(x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{2}{5}x^3 - \frac{6}{5}x^2 - 16x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{2}{5}x\) from each term to yield \(\frac{2}{5}x(x^2 - 3x - 40)\). Factoring the quadratic gives two numbers multiplying to \(-40\) and adding to \(-3\), which are \(-8\) and \(5\), resulting in \(\frac{2}{5}x(x - 8)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-\frac{3}{4}x^3 + 6x^2 + 36x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-\frac{3}{4}x\) to get \(-\frac{3}{4}x(x^2 - 8x - 48)\). Factoring the trinomial using two numbers that multiply to \(-48\) and add to \(-8\) gives \(-12\) and \(4\), yielding \(-\frac{3}{4}x(x - 12)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{6}x^5 + x^4 - 12x^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{1}{6}x^3\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{6}x^3(x^2 + 6x - 72)\). Finding two numbers that multiply to \(-72\) and add to \(6\) gives \(12\) and \(-6\), so the complete factorization is \(\frac{1}{6}x^3(x + 12)(x - 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-\frac{1}{3}x^3 + \frac{4}{3}x^2 + 15x\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-\frac{1}{3}x\) first to get \(-\frac{1}{3}x(x^2 - 4x - 45)\). Then factor the quadratic using two numbers that multiply to \(-45\) and add to \(-4\), which are \(-9\) and \(5\), yielding \(-\frac{1}{3}x(x - 9)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(z^{2n} - 11z^n + 18\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(18\) and add to \(-11\), which are \(-9\) and \(-2\). Treating the expression as quadratic in \(z^n\), the factored form is \((z^n - 9)(z^n - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^{2k} + 9w^k + 20\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(20\) and add to \(9\), which are \(4\) and \(5\). Treating the expression as quadratic in \(w^k\), the factored form is \((w^k + 4)(w^k + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^{2n} + 2y^n - 24\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(2\), which are \(6\) and \(-4\). Treating the expression as quadratic in \(y^n\), the factored form is \((y^n + 6)(y^n - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{2m} - 5a^m - 14\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(-14\) and add to \(-5\), which are \(-7\) and \(2\). Treating the expression as quadratic in \(a^m\), the factored form is \((a^m - 7)(a^m + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - 8x^n + 15\)
