qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(15\) and add to \(-8\), which are \(-3\) and \(-5\). Treating the expression as quadratic in \(x^n\), the factored form is \((x^n - 3)(x^n - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n+1} + 13x^{n+1} + 42x\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^{2n} + 13x^n + 42)\). Then find two integers that multiply to \(42\) and add to \(13\), which are \(6\) and \(7\), yielding \(x(x^n + 6)(x^n + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - 3x^n y^n - 40y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Treat the expression as quadratic in \(x^n\) with end term \(-40y^{2n}\). The factors of \(-40\) that add to \(-3\) are \(-8\) and \(5\), giving \((x^n - 8y^n)(x^n + 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2a^{2n} - 10a^n + 48\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) first to get \(-2(a^{2n} + 5a^n - 24)\). Then find two numbers that multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(5\), which are \(8\) and \(-3\), yielding \(-2(a^n + 8)(a^n - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^{2n} - 21x^n + 36\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3(x^{2n} - 7x^n + 12)\). Then find two numbers that multiply to \(12\) and add to \(-7\), which are \(-3\) and \(-4\), giving \(3(x^n - 3)(x^n - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{3}b^{2n} + 2b^n - 9\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(\frac{1}{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{3}(b^{2n} + 6b^n - 27)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \(-27\) that add to \(6\), which are \(9\) and \(-3\), giving \(\frac{1}{3}(b^n + 9)(b^n - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{6n} - 8x^{3n} + 15\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^{3n}\). Factoring \(u^2 - 8u + 15\) gives \((u - 3)(u - 5)\), resulting in \((x^{3n} - 3)(x^{3n} - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{2n} - 9a^n + 14\)
qs.s: Let \(u = a^n\). Factoring \(u^2 - 9u + 14\) yields \((u - 2)(u - 7)\), which gives \((a^n - 2)(a^n - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^{6n} + 4y^{3n} - 12\)
qs.s: Let \(u = y^{3n}\). The expression \(u^2 + 4u - 12\) factors into \((u + 6)(u - 2)\), giving \((y^{3n} + 6)(y^{3n} - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{4n} - 7x^{2n} + 10\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^{2n}\). The trinomial becomes \(u^2 - 7u + 10\), which factors as \((u - 2)(u - 5)\), giving \((x^{2n} - 2)(x^{2n} - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^{8n} + 3m^{4n} - 10\)
qs.s: Let \(u = m^{4n}\). The quadratic \(u^2 + 3u - 10\) factors as \((u + 5)(u - 2)\), giving \((m^{4n} + 5)(m^{4n} - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{4n} - 8x^{2n}y^{2n} + 15y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Treat the expression as quadratic in \(x^{2n}\); the factors of \(15y^{4n}\) that add to \(-8y^{2n}\) are \(-3y^{2n}\) and \(-5y^{2n}\), giving \((x^{2n} - 3y^{2n})(x^{2n} - 5y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3a^{5n} - 15a^{3n} - 42a^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3a^n\) to get \(3a^n(a^{4n} - 5a^{2n} - 14)\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(3a^n(a^{2n} - 7)(a^{2n} + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{2}x^{4n} + \frac{3}{2}x^{2n} - 9\)
qs.s: Factor out \(\frac{1}{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{2}(x^{4n} + 3x^{2n} - 18)\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(\frac{1}{2}(x^{2n} + 6)(x^{2n} - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^{5n}y^n - 10x^{3n}y^{3n} - 28x^n y^{5n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x^n y^n\) to get \(2x^n y^n(x^{4n} - 5x^{2n}y^{2n} - 14y^{4n})\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(2x^n y^n(x^{2n} - 7y^{2n})(x^{2n} + 2y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^{6n} - 8x^{3n} + 42\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(x^{6n} + 4x^{3n} - 21)\). Then factor the resulting trinomial into \(-2(x^{3n} + 7)(x^{3n} - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{6n} + 2x^{3n} - 15\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^{3n}\) to rewrite the expression as \(u^2 + 2u - 15\). The integers that multiply to \(-15\) and add to \(2\) are \(5\) and \(-3\), so the factored form is \((x^{3n} + 5)(x^{3n} - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^{2n} - 11w^n + 18\)
qs.s: Let \(u = w^n\) to express the trinomial as \(u^2 - 11u + 18\). The integers that multiply to \(18\) and add to \(-11\) are \(-9\) and \(-2\), so the expression factors into \((w^n - 9)(w^n - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{8n} - 7a^{4n} + 10\)
qs.s: Let \(u = a^{4n}\) to rewrite the expression as \(u^2 - 7u + 10\). The integers that multiply to \(10\) and add to \(-7\) are \(-5\) and \(-2\), giving \((a^{4n} - 5)(a^{4n} - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(p^{12x} - 8p^{6x} - 20\)
qs.s: Let \(u = p^{6x}\) to write the trinomial as \(u^2 - 8u - 20\). Finding factors of \(-20\) that add to \(-8\) yields \(-10\) and \(2\), so the result is \((p^{6x} - 10)(p^{6x} + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^{4k} + 5m^{2k} - 24\)
qs.s: Let \(u = m^{2k}\) to write the trinomial as \(u^2 + 5u - 24\). Two numbers that multiply to \(-24\) and add to \(5\) are \(8\) and \(-3\), giving \((m^{2k} + 8)(m^{2k} - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{5}x^{8n} - \frac{3}{5}x^{4n} - 8\)
qs.s: Factor out the common fraction \(\frac{1}{5}\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{5}(x^{8n} - 3x^{4n} - 40)\). The integers that multiply to \(-40\) and add to \(-3\) are \(-8\) and \(5\), yielding \(\frac{1}{5}(x^{4n} - 8)(x^{4n} + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(60 + 8x^{3n} - 4x^{6n}\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms in descending order as \(-4x^{6n} + 8x^{3n} + 60\) and factor out \(-4\) to get \(-4(x^{6n} - 2x^{3n} - 15)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-4(x^{3n} - 5)(x^{3n} + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^{2n}y^{2n} - 18x^n y^{3n} + 40y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2y^{2n}\) to obtain \(2y^{2n}(x^{2n} - 9x^n y^n + 20y^{2n})\). Factoring the remaining trinomial with respect to \(x^n\) and \(y^n\) yields \(2y^{2n}(x^n - 4y^n)(x^n - 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{5n} - 8a^{4n} + 15a^{3n}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(a^{3n}\) to get \(a^{3n}(a^{2n} - 8a^n + 15)\). Then factor the trinomial into \((a^n - 3)(a^n - 5)\), giving \(a^{3n}(a^n - 3)(a^n - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{6n} - 5x^{3n}y^{2n} - 24y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Treating the expression as quadratic in \(x^{3n}\) with second variable \(y^{2n}\), find two factors of \(-24\) that add to \(-5\), which are \(-8\) and \(3\). Thus, the polynomial factors completely into \((x^{3n} - 8y^{2n})(x^{3n} + 3y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(p^{2n} - 9p^n + 14\)
qs.s: The two numbers that multiply to \(14\) and sum to \(-9\) are \(-2\) and \(-7\), so \(p^{2n} - 9p^n + 14 = (p^n - 2)(p^n - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{2m} + 8a^m + 12\)
qs.s: Let \(u = a^m\). The expression becomes \(u^2 + 8u + 12 = (u + 2)(u + 6)\), giving \((a^m + 2)(a^m + 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^{6k} - 5w^{3k} - 14\)
qs.s: Let \(u = w^{3k}\). Factoring \(u^2 - 5u - 14\) yields \((u - 7)(u + 2)\), which gives \((w^{3k} - 7)(w^{3k} + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(c^{4x} + 3c^{2x} - 18\)
Factor completely: \(2x^{5n} - 20x^{3n} + 42x^n\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x^n\) to get \(2x^n(x^{4n} - 10x^{2n} + 21)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial into \(2x^n(x^{2n} - 3)(x^{2n} - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{2}x^{6n} - \frac{9}{2}x^{3n} + 10\)
qs.s: Factor out the rational coefficient \(\frac{1}{2}\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{2}(x^{6n} - 9x^{3n} + 20)\), which factors into \(\frac{1}{2}(x^{3n} - 4)(x^{3n} - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{2n} - 8a^n b^{2m} - 33b^{4m}\)
qs.s: Treating the expression as quadratic in \(a^n\), find two factors of \(-33\) that sum to \(-8\), which are \(-11\) and \(3\), giving \((a^n - 11b^{2m})(a^n + 3b^{2m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4y^{6k} - 20y^{3k} + 200\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-4\) first to obtain \(-4(y^{6k} + 5y^{3k} - 50)\), then find two numbers that multiply to \(-50\) and add to \(5\), yielding \(-4(y^{3k} + 10)(y^{3k} - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5w^{4n} + 65w^{2n} + 180\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(5\) to get \(5(w^{4n} + 13w^{2n} + 36)\). Since two numbers that multiply to \(36\) and add to \(13\) are \(4\) and \(9\), the completely factored form is \(5(w^{2n} + 4)(w^{2n} + 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} + 4x^n y^m - 12y^{2m}\)
qs.s: We look for two integers with a product of \(-12\) and a sum of \(4\), which are \(6\) and \(-2\). Thus, \(x^{2n} + 4x^n y^m - 12y^{2m} = (x^n + 6y^m)(x^n - 2y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - 8x^n y^m + 15y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(15\) and add to \(-8\), which are \(-3\) and \(-5\). Thus, \(x^{2n} - 8x^n y^m + 15y^{2m} = (x^n - 3y^m)(x^n - 5y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{2n} + 9a^n b^m + 14b^{2m}\)
qs.s: The two integers that multiply to \(14\) and add to \(9\) are \(2\) and \(7\). Therefore, the trinomial factors as \((a^n + 2b^m)(a^n + 7b^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - 3x^n y^m - 10y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Find two integers that multiply to \(-10\) and add to \(-3\), which are \(-5\) and \(2\). Hence, the factored expression is \((x^n - 5y^m)(x^n + 2y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(u^{2n} - 10u^n v^m + 21v^{2m}\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(21\) that add to \(-10\), which are \(-3\) and \(-7\). Therefore, \(u^{2n} - 10u^n v^m + 21v^{2m} = (u^n - 3v^m)(u^n - 7v^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{3}x^{2n} - 4x^n y^m + 9y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common fraction \(\frac{1}{3}\) to obtain \(\frac{1}{3}(x^{2n} - 12x^n y^m + 27y^{2m})\). Finding factors of \(27\) that add to \(-12\) gives \(\frac{1}{3}(x^n - 3y^m)(x^n - 9y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(30y^{2m} + 4x^n y^m - 2x^{2n}\)
qs.s: First arrange in descending powers as \(-2x^{2n} + 4x^n y^m + 30y^{2m}\), then factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(x^{2n} - 2x^n y^m - 15y^{2m})\). Factoring the remaining trinomial yields \(-2(x^n - 5y^m)(x^n + 3y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5a^2 x^{2n} - 40a^2 x^n y^m + 75a^2 y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Factor out the monomial GCF \(5a^2\) to get \(5a^2(x^{2n} - 8x^n y^m + 15y^{2m})\). Then factor the trinomial into \((x^n - 3y^m)(x^n - 5y^m)\), giving \(5a^2(x^n - 3y^m)(x^n - 5y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^{2n} - 21x^n y^m - 54y^{2m}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3(x^{2n} - 7x^n y^m - 18y^{2m})\). Factoring the trinomial with numbers that multiply to \(-18\) and add to \(-7\) gives \(3(x^n - 9y^m)(x^n + 2y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{2n} - 25x^n y^m + 84y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(84\) that have a sum of \(-25\), which are \(-4\) and \(-21\). Thus, the trinomial factors as \((x^n - 4y^m)(x^n - 21y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^{8a} - 5w^{4a}z^{2b} - 24z^{4b}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = w^{4a}\) and \(v = z^{2b}\), giving \(u^2 - 5uv - 24v^2\). The factors of \(-24\) with a sum of \(-5\) are \(-8\) and \(3\), so the expression factors as \((w^{4a} - 8z^{2b})(w^{4a} + 3z^{2b})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{10n} - 3x^{5n}y^{4m} - 18y^{8m}\)
qs.s: Substitute \(u = x^{5n}\) and \(v = y^{4m}\) to obtain \(u^2 - 3uv - 18v^2\). Two integers with a product of \(-18\) and a sum of \(-3\) are \(-6\) and \(3\), giving \((x^{5n} - 6y^{4m})(x^{5n} + 3y^{4m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^{4x} + 9m^{2x}n^{3y} + 14n^{6y}\)
qs.s: Treat the trinomial as quadratic in \(m^{2x}\) and \(n^{3y}\). Finding two numbers that multiply to \(14\) and add to \(9\) yields \(2\) and \(7\), resulting in \((m^{2x} + 2n^{3y})(m^{2x} + 7n^{3y})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{6n} + 2x^{3n}y^{2m} - 15y^{4m}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^{3n}\) and \(v = y^{2m}\) to rewrite the expression as \(u^2 + 2uv - 15v^2\). Since \(5\) and \(-3\) multiply to \(-15\) and add to \(2\), the trinomial factors as \((x^{3n} + 5y^{2m})(x^{3n} - 3y^{2m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{4k} - 7a^{2k}b^{3n} + 10b^{6n}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = a^{2k}\) and \(v = b^{3n}\) so the expression becomes \(u^2 - 7uv + 10v^2\). The two factors of \(10\) that sum to \(-7\) are \(-2\) and \(-5\), giving \((a^{2k} - 2b^{3n})(a^{2k} - 5b^{3n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{4n+2} - 11x^{2n+1}y^{3m} + 28y^{6m}\)
qs.s: Recognizing that \(x^{4n+2} = (x^{2n+1})^2\) and \(y^{6m} = (y^{3m})^2\), the expression is quadratic in \(x^{2n+1}\) and \(y^{3m}\). Two integers that multiply to \(28\) and add to \(-11\) are \(-4\) and \(-7\), giving \((x^{2n+1} - 4y^{3m})(x^{2n+1} - 7y^{3m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(10a^{4n}b^{3m} - 2a^{8n} + 48b^{6m}\)
qs.s: Rearrange in descending powers of \(a\) to get \(-2a^{8n} + 10a^{4n}b^{3m} + 48b^{6m}\), then factor out the common factor \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(a^{8n} - 5a^{4n}b^{3m} - 24b^{6m})\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2(a^{4n} - 8b^{3m})(a^{4n} + 3b^{3m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(\frac{1}{4}x^{6n} - \frac{1}{2}x^{3n}y^{2m} - \frac{3}{4}y^{4m}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common fraction \(\frac{1}{4}\) to get \(\frac{1}{4}(x^{6n} - 2x^{3n}y^{2m} - 3y^{4m})\). Factoring the quadratic-form trinomial produces \(\frac{1}{4}(x^{3n} - 3y^{2m})(x^{3n} + y^{2m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{8n} + 7x^{4n}y^{5m} - 120y^{10m}\)
qs.s: Treating the expression as quadratic in \(x^{4n}\) and \(y^{5m}\), find two integers whose product is \(-120\) and whose sum is \(7\). The correct pair is \(15\) and \(-8\), giving \((x^{4n} + 15y^{5m})(x^{4n} - 8y^{5m})\).

exercises.name: Factoring by Grouping Binomials or Quadratic Form

qs.q: Factor completely: \((5u + 2)p^2 + 2(5u + 2)p - 24(5u + 2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((5u + 2)\) to obtain \((5u + 2)(p^2 + 2p - 24)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \((5u + 2)(p + 6)(p - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((a - 3b)w^2 - 8(a - 3b)w + 15(a - 3b)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((a - 3b)\) to get \((a - 3b)(w^2 - 8w + 15)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \((a - 3b)(w - 3)(w - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x - 2)m^2 - 5(3x - 2)m - 14(3x - 2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((3x - 2)\) to obtain \((3x - 2)(m^2 - 5m - 14)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \((3x - 2)(m - 7)(m + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4k + 1)x^2 + 7(4k + 1)x + 12(4k + 1)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((4k + 1)\) to get \((4k + 1)(x^2 + 7x + 12)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \((4k + 1)(x + 3)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x - 7)t^2 - (2x - 7)t - 20(2x - 7)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((2x - 7)\) to get \((2x - 7)(t^2 - t - 20)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \((2x - 7)(t - 5)(t + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x - 4)y^2 + 2(3x - 4)y + 35(4 - 3x)\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(35(4 - 3x)\) as \(-35(3x - 4)\) and factor out \((3x - 4)\) to obtain \((3x - 4)(y^2 + 2y - 35)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \((3x - 4)(y + 7)(y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-(2u + 7)x^2 + 5(2u + 7)x + 84(2u + 7)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-(2u + 7)\) to obtain \(-(2u + 7)(x^2 - 5x - 84)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-(2u + 7)(x - 12)(x + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x(a + 2b)y^2 - 18x(a + 2b)y - 48x(a + 2b)\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3x(a + 2b)\) to get \(3x(a + 2b)(y^2 - 6y - 16)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(3x(a + 2b)(y - 8)(y + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4a - 1)m^2 - 3(4a - 1)mn - 40(4a - 1)n^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((4a - 1)\) to get \((4a - 1)(m^2 - 3mn - 40n^2)\). Factoring the two-variable quadratic trinomial gives \((4a - 1)(m - 8n)(m + 5n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(30(3w + 5)y - 2(3w + 5)y^2 - 108(3w + 5)\)
qs.s: Arrange the terms in descending order of powers of \(y\) and factor out \(-2(3w + 5)\) to get \(-2(3w + 5)(y^2 - 15y + 54)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-2(3w + 5)(y - 6)(y - 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(z^3(2x - 1) - 9z^2(2x - 1) + 20z(2x - 1)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(z(2x - 1)\) to get \(z(2x - 1)(z^2 - 9z + 20)\), and then factor the remaining trinomial into \((z - 4)(z - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^3(x + y) - 7a^2(x + y) - 18a(x + y)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(a(x + y)\) to yield \(a(x + y)(a^2 - 7a - 18)\), then factor the trinomial into \((a - 9)(a + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3(m - n) - 5x^2(m - n) + 6x(m - n)\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x(m - n)\) to get \(x(m - n)(x^2 - 5x + 6)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((x - 2)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^3(a - 2) + 2y^2(a - 2) - 15y(a - 2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(y(a - 2)\) to obtain \(y(a - 2)(y^2 + 2y - 15)\), and then factor the trinomial into \((y + 5)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3(c + d) + 8x^2(c + d) + 12x(c + d)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x(c + d)\) to obtain \(x(c + d)(x^2 + 8x + 12)\), which then factors into \(x(c + d)(x + 2)(x + 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^3(a + 3b) + 16x^2(a + 3b) - 30x(a + 3b)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-2x(a + 3b)\) to leave \(-2x(a + 3b)(x^2 - 8x + 15)\), then factor the resulting trinomial into \((x - 3)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3(y - 5) - 3x^2(y - 5) + 28x(5 - y)\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(+28x(5 - y)\) as \(-28x(y - 5)\) and factor out \(x(y - 5)\) to get \(x(y - 5)(x^2 - 3x - 28)\), which factors into \(x(y - 5)(x - 7)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3y(m + 2n) + 2x^2y^2(m + 2n) - 24xy^3(m + 2n)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(xy(m + 2n)\) to get \(xy(m + 2n)(x^2 + 2xy - 24y^2)\), then factor the two-variable trinomial into \((x + 6y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x - 2)y^2 - 5(3x - 2)y + 14(2 - 3x)\)
qs.s: Rewrite \(+14(2 - 3x)\) as \(-14(3x - 2)\) and factor out \((3x - 2)\) to get \((3x - 2)(y^2 - 5y - 14)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \((3x - 2)(y - 7)(y + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2u + 3v)a^2 - 11(2u + 3v)ab - 60(2u + 3v)b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \((2u + 3v)\) to leave \((2u + 3v)(a^2 - 11ab - 60b^2)\). Find factors of \(-60b^2\) that sum to \(-11b\), which are \(-15b\) and \(4b\), giving \((2u + 3v)(a - 15b)(a + 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 + 5x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x^4 + 6x^2 + 9) - x^2 = (x^2 + 3)^2 - x^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x^2 + x + 3)(x^2 - x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 + 2x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x^4 + 6x^2 + 9) - 4x^2 = (x^2 + 3)^2 - (2x)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x^2 + 2x + 3)(x^2 - 2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 + 3x^2 + 4\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x^4 + 4x^2 + 4) - x^2 = (x^2 + 2)^2 - x^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x^2 + x + 2)(x^2 - x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 + 7x^2 + 16\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x^4 + 8x^2 + 16) - x^2 = (x^2 + 4)^2 - x^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x^2 + x + 4)(x^2 - x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 3x^2 + 1\)
qs.s: Rewrite as \((x^4 - 2x^2 + 1) - x^2 = (x^2 - 1)^2 - x^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x^2 + x - 1)(x^2 - x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 + 4x^2y^2 + 16y^4\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \((x^4 + 8x^2y^2 + 16y^4) - 4x^2y^2 = (x^2 + 4y^2)^2 - (2xy)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares yields \((x^2 + 2xy + 4y^2)(x^2 - 2xy + 4y^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 + x^4 + 1\)
Factor completely: \(a^4 - 7a^2b^2 + b^4\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \((a^4 + 2a^2b^2 + b^4) - 9a^2b^2 = (a^2 + b^2)^2 - (3ab)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((a^2 + 3ab + b^2)(a^2 - 3ab + b^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^5 + 6x^3 + 8x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(x^4 + 3x^2 + 4)\). Then complete the square on the quartic to factor it completely as \(2x(x^2 + x + 2)(x^2 - x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 + 8x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Complete the square to obtain \((4x^4 + 12x^2 + 9) - 4x^2 = (2x^2 + 3)^2 - (2x)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((2x^2 + 2x + 3)(2x^2 - 2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3a - 1)^2 + (3ab - b) - 30b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(b\) from the middle term to get \((3a - 1)^2 + b(3a - 1) - 30b^2\). Factoring \(u^2 + ub - 30b^2\) gives \((u + 6b)(u - 5b)\), resulting in \((3a + 6b - 1)(3a - 5b - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4x + 1)^2 - (4xz + z) - 12z^2\)
qs.s: Rewrite the middle term as \(-z(4x + 1)\) and substitute \(u = 4x + 1\) to obtain \(u^2 - uz - 12z^2\). Factoring gives \((u - 4z)(u + 3z)\), which simplifies to \((4x - 4z + 1)(4x + 3z + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x + 2)^2 + (3xy + 2y) - 6y^2\)
qs.s: Rewrite the middle term as \(y(3x + 2)\) and let \(u = 3x + 2\) to get \(u^2 + uy - 6y^2\). Factor into \((u + 3y)(u - 2y)\) and substitute \(u = 3x + 2\) to obtain \((3x + 3y + 2)(3x - 2y + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((5x + 2)^2 + (5xz + 2z) - 2z^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(z\) from \((5xz + 2z)\) and let \(u = 5x + 2\) to rewrite the expression as \(u^2 + uz - 2z^2\). Factoring gives \((u + 2z)(u - z)\), which yields \((5x + 2z + 2)(5x - z + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x - 5)^2 + (2xy - 5y) - 12y^2\)
qs.s: Factor \(y\) from the middle term to get \((2x - 5)^2 + y(2x - 5) - 12y^2\). Letting \(u = 2x - 5\), the expression factors as \((u + 4y)(u - 3y)\), giving \((2x + 4y - 5)(2x - 3y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((5x + 3)^2 - (35xz + 21z) - 60z^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-7z\) from \(-(35xz + 21z)\) to get \((5x + 3)^2 - 7z(5x + 3) - 60z^2\). Letting \(u = 5x + 3\), this factors into \((u - 12z)(u + 5z) = (5x - 12z + 3)(5x + 5z + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x - 2)^2 + (12xy - 8y) - 21y^2\)
qs.s: Factor \(4y\) from the middle term to obtain \((3x - 2)^2 + 4y(3x - 2) - 21y^2\). With \(u = 3x - 2\), this factors as \((u + 7y)(u - 3y) = (3x + 7y - 2)(3x - 3y - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-(2x + 5)^2 - (2xz + 5z) + 30z^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) first to write \(-[(2x + 5)^2 + z(2x + 5) - 30z^2]\). Setting \(u = 2x + 5\), factor the trinomial into \((u + 6z)(u - 5z)\) to arrive at \(-(2x + 6z + 5)(2x - 5z + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4x - 1)^2 - 18y^2 + (12xy - 3y)\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms into standard quadratic form: \((4x - 1)^2 + 3y(4x - 1) - 18y^2\). Factoring the quadratic in \((4x - 1)\) gives \((4x + 6y - 1)(4x - 3y - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x + 4y)^2 + 2w(x + 4y) - 24w^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x + 4y\). The expression becomes \(u^2 + 2wu - 24w^2 = (u + 6w)(u - 4w)\), which gives \((x + 4y + 6w)(x + 4y - 4w)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((p - 5q)^2 - 6r(p - 5q) - 16r^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = p - 5q\). The expression becomes \(u^2 - 6ru - 16r^2 = (u - 8r)(u + 2r)\), which produces \((p - 5q - 8r)(p - 5q + 2r)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x - y)^2 + 5z(2x - y) - 14z^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = 2x - y\). The expression becomes \(u^2 + 5zu - 14z^2 = (u + 7z)(u - 2z)\), which substitutes back to \((2x - y + 7z)(2x - y - 2z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((a + 3b)^2 - 7c(a + 3b) + 10c^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = a + 3b\). The expression becomes \(u^2 - 7cu + 10c^2 = (u - 2c)(u - 5c)\), which gives \((a + 3b - 2c)(a + 3b - 5c)\) after substituting back.

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3m + n)^2 - 9k(3m + n) + 20k^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = 3m + n\). The expression becomes \(u^2 - 9ku + 20k^2 = (u - 4k)(u - 5k)\), which yields \((3m + n - 4k)(3m + n - 5k)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x - y)^2 + 5a(y - 2x) - 24a^2\)
qs.s: Rewrite \((y - 2x)\) as \(-(2x - y)\) to obtain \((2x - y)^2 - 5a(2x - y) - 24a^2\), which factors into \((2x - y - 8a)(2x - y + 3a)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3(x - 2y)^2 - 36a(x - 2y) + 96a^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3[(x - 2y)^2 - 12a(x - 2y) + 32a^2]\), and then factor the quadratic form as \(3(x - 2y - 4a)(x - 2y - 8a)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(45z^2 - 4z(m - 3n) - (m - 3n)^2\)
qs.s: Rearrange in descending powers of \((m - 3n)\) and factor out \(-1\) to get \(-[(m - 3n)^2 + 4z(m - 3n) - 45z^2] = -(m - 3n + 9z)(m - 3n - 5z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2c(a + 2b)^2 - 6c^2(a + 2b) + 56c^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2c\) to get \(-2c[(a + 2b)^2 + 3c(a + 2b) - 28c^2]\), which factors into \(-2c(a + 2b + 7c)(a + 2b - 4c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x + y)^2 + (10xz + 5yz) - 14z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring \(5z\) from the middle terms gives \((2x + y)^2 + 5z(2x + y) - 14z^2\). Letting \(u = 2x + y\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 5zu - 14z^2\) factors into \((u + 7z)(u - 2z)\), yielding \((2x + y + 7z)(2x + y - 2z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4x + 3y)^2 - (8xz + 6yz) - 15z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring \(-2z\) from the middle terms gives \((4x + 3y)^2 - 2z(4x + 3y) - 15z^2\). Letting \(u = 4x + 3y\), the quadratic \(u^2 - 2zu - 15z^2\) factors into \((u - 5z)(u + 3z)\), giving \((4x + 3y - 5z)(4x + 3y + 3z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2a - 3b)^2 + (8ac - 12bc) - 21c^2\)
qs.s: Factoring \(4c\) from the middle terms gives \((2a - 3b)^2 + 4c(2a - 3b) - 21c^2\). Letting \(u = 2a - 3b\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 4cu - 21c^2\) factors into \((u + 7c)(u - 3c)\), giving \((2a - 3b + 7c)(2a - 3b - 3c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x + 4y)^2 - (5xz + 20yz) - 24z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring \(-5z\) from the middle terms gives \((x + 4y)^2 - 5z(x + 4y) - 24z^2\). Letting \(u = x + 4y\), the quadratic \(u^2 - 5zu - 24z^2\) factors into \((u - 8z)(u + 3z)\), giving \((x + 4y - 8z)(x + 4y + 3z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((3x - 2y)^2 + (9wx - 6wy) - 18w^2\)
qs.s: Factoring \(3w\) from the middle terms gives \((3x - 2y)^2 + 3w(3x - 2y) - 18w^2\). Letting \(u = 3x - 2y\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 3wu - 18w^2\) factors into \((u + 6w)(u - 3w)\), giving \((3x - 2y + 6w)(3x - 2y - 3w)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2(3x + 2y)^2 - (78xz + 52yz) + 72z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(2\) yields \(2[(3x + 2y)^2 - 13z(3x + 2y) + 36z^2]\). Letting \(u = 3x + 2y\), the quadratic \(u^2 - 13zu + 36z^2\) factors into \((u - 9z)(u - 4z)\), giving \(2(3x + 2y - 9z)(3x + 2y - 4z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-(3x - 4y)^2 - (6xz - 8yz) + 40z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out \(-1\) gives \(-[(3x - 4y)^2 + 2z(3x - 4y) - 40z^2]\). Letting \(u = 3x - 4y\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 2zu - 40z^2\) factors into \((u + 8z)(u - 5z)\), resulting in \(-(3x - 4y + 8z)(3x - 4y - 5z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5(2x - y)^2 + (30xz - 15yz) - 140z^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(5\) gives \(5[(2x - y)^2 + 3z(2x - y) - 28z^2]\). Letting \(u = 2x - y\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 3zu - 28z^2\) factors as \((u + 7z)(u - 4z)\), yielding \(5(2x - y + 7z)(2x - y - 4z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-60z^2 + (4x + 3y)^2 + (28xz + 21yz)\)
qs.s: Rearranging the terms in descending quadratic order gives \((4x + 3y)^2 + 7z(4x + 3y) - 60z^2\). Letting \(u = 4x + 3y\), the quadratic \(u^2 + 7zu - 60z^2\) factors into \((u + 12z)(u - 5z)\), giving \((4x + 3y + 12z)(4x + 3y - 5z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a(2x + 5y)^2 - (8axz + 20ayz) - 32az^2\)
qs.s: Factoring out the common factor \(a\) gives \(a[(2x + 5y)^2 - 4z(2x + 5y) - 32z^2]\). Letting \(u = 2x + 5y\), the quadratic \(u^2 - 4zu - 32z^2\) factors into \((u - 8z)(u + 4z)\), yielding \(a(2x + 5y - 8z)(2x + 5y + 4z)\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage box has a volume of \((x^3 + 9x^2 + 14x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 9x + 14) = x(x + 2)(x + 7)\). Comparing the three dimensions \(x\), \(x + 2\), and \(x + 7\) for \(x > 0\), the greatest dimension is \((x + 7)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular block is \((x^3 + 13x^2 + 30x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 13x + 30) = x(x + 3)(x + 10)\). Since \(x > 0\), the dimensions are \(x\), \(x + 3\), and \(x + 10\), making \((x + 10)\text{ cm}\) the greatest dimension.

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular solid is \((x^3 + 8x^2 + 15x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(x\) yields \(x(x^2 + 8x + 15) = x(x + 3)(x + 5)\). For \(x > 0\), the dimensions are \(x\), \(x + 3\), and \(x + 5\), so the greatest dimension is \((x + 5)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular prism is \((x^3 + 10x^2 + 24x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out the common factor \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 10x + 24) = x(x + 4)(x + 6)\). For \(x > 0\), the dimensions are \(x\), \(x + 4\), and \(x + 6\), so the greatest dimension is \((x + 6)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping container has a volume of \((x^3 + 11x^2 + 18x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) yields \(x(x^2 + 11x + 18) = x(x + 2)(x + 9)\). For \(x > 0\), comparing the dimensions shows that the greatest dimension is \((x + 9)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular solid is \((x^3 + 22x^2 + 96x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 22x + 96) = x(x + 6)(x + 16)\). For \(x > 0\), the three dimensions are \(x\), \(x + 6\), and \(x + 16\), so the greatest dimension is \((x + 16)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage container has a volume of \((x^3 + 5x^2 - 84x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 7\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 5x - 84) = x(x - 7)(x + 12)\). For \(x > 7\), the dimensions are positive values \(x - 7\), \(x\), and \(x + 12\), so the greatest dimension is \((x + 12)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular block is \((x^3 - 23x^2 + 120x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 15\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) yields \(x(x^2 - 23x + 120) = x(x - 8)(x - 15)\). For \(x > 15\), the three dimensions are \(x - 15\), \(x - 8\), and \(x\), so the greatest dimension is \(x\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular shipping crate has a volume of \((x^3 + 25x^2 + 144x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 0\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) yields \(x(x^2 + 25x + 144) = x(x + 9)(x + 16)\). For \(x > 0\), the dimensions are \(x\), \(x + 9\), and \(x + 16\), which means the greatest dimension is \((x + 16)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular prism is \((x^3 - 3x^2 - 70x)\text{ cm}^3\). For \(x > 10\), determine its greatest dimension in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \(x(x^2 - 3x - 70) = x(x - 10)(x + 7)\). For \(x > 10\), the dimensions are \(x - 10\), \(x\), and \(x + 7\), so the greatest dimension is \((x + 7)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A square-based pyramid has a volume of \(2x^3 + 16x^2 + 32x\). Determine the area of the base.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(x^2 + 8x + 16) = 2x(x + 4)^2\). Since the pyramid has a square base, the area of the base is \((x + 4)^2\).

qs.q: A storage box in the shape of a square-based prism has a volume of \(3x^3 + 30x^2 + 75x\). Determine the area of the base.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(x^2 + 10x + 25) = 3x(x + 5)^2\). Since the box has a square base, the area of the base is \((x + 5)^2\).

qs.q: A decorative candle in the shape of a square-based pyramid has a volume of \(2x^3 + 28x^2 + 98x\). Determine the area of the base.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(x^2 + 14x + 49) = 2x(x + 7)^2\). Since the base is square, its area is \((x + 7)^2\).

qs.q: A toy building block in the shape of a square-based pyramid has a volume of \(5x^3 + 20x^2 + 20x\). Determine the area of the base.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(5x\) to get \(5x(x^2 + 4x + 4) = 5x(x + 2)^2\). Since the base is square, its area is \((x + 2)^2\).

qs.q: A greenhouse in the shape of a square-based pyramid has a volume of \(2x^3 + 24x^2 + 72x\). Determine the area of the base.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(x^2 + 12x + 36) = 2x(x + 6)^2\). The area of the square base is \((x + 6)^2\).

qs.q: A square-based pyramid has a volume of \(2x^3 + 36x^2 + 162x\). Determine the height of the pyramid.
qs.s: Factoring gives \(2x(x^2 + 18x + 81) = 2x(x + 9)^2\), so the square base area is \(A = (x + 9)^2\). Since the volume of a pyramid is \(V = \frac{1}{3}Ah\), we have \(2x(x + 9)^2 = \frac{1}{3}(x + 9)^2 h\), which yields \(h = 6x\).

qs.q: A storage trunk in the shape of a square-based prism has a volume of \(5x^3 + 60x^2 + 180x\). Determine the perimeter of the base.
qs.s: Factor out \(5x\) to get \(5x(x^2 + 12x + 36) = 5x(x + 6)^2\), giving a base side length of \(x + 6\). The perimeter of the square base is \(4(x + 6) = 4x + 24\).

qs.q: A square-based pyramid has a volume of \(2x^3 + 32x^2 + 128x\). Determine the side length of the base.
qs.s: Factor out \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(x^2 + 16x + 64) = 2x(x + 8)^2\). The area of the square base is \((x + 8)^2\), so its side length is \(\sqrt{(x + 8)^2} = x + 8\).

qs.q: A monument in the shape of a square-based pyramid has a volume of \(6x^3 + 84x^2 + 294x\). Determine the perimeter of the base.
qs.s: Factor out \(6x\) to get \(6x(x^2 + 14x + 49) = 6x(x + 7)^2\), which gives a base side length of \(x + 7\). The perimeter of the base is \(4(x + 7) = 4x + 28\).

qs.q: A square-based pyramid has a volume of \(4x^3 + 80x^2 + 400x\). Determine the height of the pyramid.
qs.s: Factoring gives \(4x(x^2 + 20x + 100) = 4x(x + 10)^2\), showing the base area is \(A = (x + 10)^2\). Since \(V = \frac{1}{3}Ah\), \(4x(x + 10)^2 = \frac{1}{3}(x + 10)^2 h\), so \(h = 12x\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of \((2x^3 + 12x^2y + 18xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the side length of its square base in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor gives \(2x(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2) = 2x(x + 3y)^2\). Since the solid has a square base, the side length of the base is \((x + 3y)\text{ cm}\) and the height is \(2x\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of \((x^3 + 10x^2y + 25xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the side length of its square base in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2) = x(x + 5y)^2\). The side length of the square base is therefore \((x + 5y)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of \((7x^3 + 14x^2y + 7xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the height of the solid in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out \(7x\) yields \(7x(x^2 + 2xy + y^2) = 7x(x + y)^2\). Because the base is square with side length \((x + y)\text{ cm}\), the height is \(7x\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of \((5x^3 + 20x^2y + 20xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the height of the solid in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring the volume expression gives \(5x(x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2) = 5x(x + 2y)^2\). The square base has side length \((x + 2y)\text{ cm}\), so the height of the solid is \(5x\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a height of \(4x\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \((4x^3 + 36x^2 + 72x)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the perimeter of its base in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Dividing the volume by the height gives the base area \(x^2 + 9x + 18 = (x + 3)(x + 6)\). The perimeter of the base is \(2[(x + 3) + (x + 6)] = 2(2x + 9) = (4x + 18)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a height of \(2x\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \((2x^3 + 16x^2y + 32xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the sum of the lengths of all 12 edges of the solid in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Factoring the volume yields \(2x(x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2) = 2x(x + 4y)^2\), so the square base edges have length \((x + 4y)\text{ cm}\) and the 4 vertical edges have length \(2x\text{ cm}\). The sum of all 12 edges is \(8(x + 4y) + 4(2x) = 8x + 32y + 8x = (16x + 32y)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid has a volume of \((3x^3 + 15x^2 - 42x)\text{ cm}^3\). If its height is \(3x\text{ cm}\) and its length is \((x + 7)\text{ cm}\), determine its width in terms of \(x\).
qs.s: Factoring out the height \(3x\) gives \(3x(x^2 + 5x - 14) = 3x(x + 7)(x - 2)\). Since volume equals \(\text{height} \times \text{length} \times \text{width}\) and the length is \((x + 7)\text{ cm}\), the width must be \((x - 2)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a height of \(5x\text{ cm}\) and a volume of \((5x^3 - 30x^2y + 45xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\), where \(x > 3y\). Determine the difference between the height of the solid and the side length of its square base, in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Factoring the volume gives \(5x(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2) = 5x(x - 3y)^2\), so the base side length is \((x - 3y)\text{ cm}\). Subtracting this from the height gives \(5x - (x - 3y) = (4x + 3y)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular solid with a square base has a volume of \((6x^3 + 36x^2y + 54xy^2)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the perimeter of its square base in terms of \(x\) and \(y\).
qs.s: Factoring gives \(6x(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2) = 6x(x + 3y)^2\), so the square base has side length \((x + 3y)\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of the base is \(4(x + 3y) = (4x + 12y)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is \((6x^2 + 36xy + 54y^2)\text{ m}^2\). Determine the edge length of the cube.
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(6\) to get \(6(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2) = 6(x + 3y)^2\). Since the surface area of a cube is \(6s^2\), the edge length is \(s = (x + 3y)\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is \((6x^2 + 60x + 150)\text{ cm}^2\). Determine the perimeter of one of its faces.
qs.s: Factor out \(6\) to get \(6(x^2 + 10x + 25) = 6(x + 5)^2\), which gives an edge length of \(s = x + 5\text{ cm}\). The perimeter of a square face is \(4s = 4(x + 5) = (4x + 20)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \((4\pi x^2 + 48\pi x + 144\pi)\text{ mm}^2\). Determine the radius of the sphere.
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(4\pi\) to get \(4\pi(x^2 + 12x + 36) = 4\pi(x + 6)^2\). Since the surface area formula is \(4\pi r^2\), the radius is \(r = (x + 6)\text{ mm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \((4\pi x^2 + 16\pi xy + 16\pi y^2)\text{ cm}^2\). Determine the diameter of the sphere.
qs.s: Factor out \(4\pi\) to obtain \(4\pi(x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2) = 4\pi(x + 2y)^2\). Since the surface area of a sphere is \(4\pi r^2\), the radius is \(r = x + 2y\text{ cm}\), which gives a diameter of \(2r = (2x + 4y)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A cylinder with a height of \(3\text{ cm}\) has a volume of \((3\pi x^2 + 24\pi x + 48\pi)\text{ cm}^3\). Determine the diameter of the cylinder's base.
qs.s: Factor out \(3\pi\) to get \(3\pi(x^2 + 8x + 16) = 3\pi(x + 4)^2\). Comparing this to \(V = \pi r^2 h = 3\pi r^2\), the radius is \(r = x + 4\text{ cm}\), so the diameter is \(2r = (2x + 8)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: Two spheres have surface areas of \((4\pi x^2 + 40\pi xy + 100\pi y^2)\text{ cm}^2\) and \((4\pi x^2 + 16\pi xy + 16\pi y^2)\text{ cm}^2\), respectively. Determine the difference between the diameters of the two spheres.
qs.s: Factoring gives \(SA_1 = 4\pi(x + 5y)^2\) and \(SA_2 = 4\pi(x + 2y)^2\), so the diameters are \(2(x + 5y) = 2x + 10y\text{ cm}\) and \(2(x + 2y) = 2x + 4y\text{ cm}\). The difference between the diameters is \((2x + 10y) - (2x + 4y) = 6y\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cube is \((6x^2 + 84x + 294)\text{ cm}^2\). Determine the sum of the lengths of all \(12\) edges of the cube.
qs.s: Factor out \(6\) to get \(6(x^2 + 14x + 49) = 6(x + 7)^2\), meaning each edge length is \(s = x + 7\text{ cm}\). A cube has \(12\) edges, so their total length is \(12(x + 7) = (12x + 84)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of a rectangular prism is \((3x^3 + 39x^2 + 120x)\text{ cm}^3\). If the height of the prism is \(3x\text{ cm}\) and its width is \((x + 5)\text{ cm}\), determine its length.
qs.s: Factor out \(3x\) to get \(3x(x^2 + 13x + 40) = 3x(x + 5)(x + 8)\). Since \(V = \text{height} \times \text{width} \times \text{length} = 3x(x + 5)\cdot l\), the length is \(l = (x + 8)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The surface area of a sphere is \((4\pi x^4 + 32\pi x^3 y + 64\pi x^2 y^2)\text{ cm}^2\). Determine the diameter of the sphere.
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(4\pi x^2\) to obtain \(4\pi x^2(x + 4y)^2 = 4\pi(x^2 + 4xy)^2\). Comparing to \(4\pi r^2\) gives radius \(r = x^2 + 4xy\text{ cm}\), so the diameter is \(2r = (2x^2 + 8xy)\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rectangular box has a height of \(4\text{ m}\) and a volume of \((4x^2 + 60xy + 216y^2)\text{ m}^3\). Determine the perimeter of the base of the box.
qs.s: Dividing the volume by the height \(4\) gives the base area \(x^2 + 15xy + 54y^2 = (x + 6y)(x + 9y)\). The perimeter of the base is \(2[(x + 6y) + (x + 9y)] = 2(2x + 15y) = (4x + 30y)\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cylindrical can has a volume of \(\pi(x^3 + 4x^2 + 4x)\). Determine the diameter of the can.
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(\pi x(x^2 + 4x + 4) = \pi x(x + 2)^2\). The radius is \(r = x + 2\), so the diameter is \(2(x + 2) = 2x + 4\).

qs.q: A cylinder has a volume of \(\pi(x^3 + 6x^2 + 9x)\). Determine the diameter of the cylinder.
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives the volume as \(\pi x(x^2 + 6x + 9) = \pi x(x + 3)^2\). Comparing this to \(V = \pi r^2 h\) yields a radius of \(r = x + 3\), so the diameter is \(2(x + 3) = 2x + 6\).

qs.q: A cylindrical water tank has a volume of \(\pi(x^3 - 8x^2 + 16x)\). Determine the diameter of the tank.
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(\pi x(x^2 - 8x + 16) = \pi x(x - 4)^2\). Comparing to \(V = \pi r^2 h\), the radius is \(r = x - 4\), which means the diameter is \(2(x - 4) = 2x - 8\).

qs.q: A cylindrical storage silo has a volume of \(\pi(x^3 - 6x^2 + 9x)\). Determine the diameter of the silo.
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) yields \(\pi x(x^2 - 6x + 9) = \pi x(x - 3)^2\). The radius is \(r = x - 3\), so the diameter is \(2(x - 3) = 2x - 6\).

qs.q: A cylindrical container has a volume of \(\pi(x^3 + 10x^2 + 25x)\). Determine the diameter of the container.
qs.s: Factoring out \(x\) gives \(\pi x(x^2 + 10x + 25) = \pi x(x + 5)^2\). The radius is \(r = x + 5\), making the diameter \(2(x + 5) = 2x + 10\).

qs.q: A cylindrical water tower has a height of \(3x\) and a volume of \(\pi(3x^3 + 42x^2 + 147x)\). Determine the diameter of the tower.
qs.s: Factoring out the height \(3x\) gives \(\pi(3x)(x^2 + 14x + 49) = \pi(3x)(x + 7)^2\). Comparing to \(V = \pi r^2 h\), the radius is \(r = x + 7\), so the diameter is \(2(x + 7) = 2x + 14\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism has a height of \(x\) and a volume of \(x^3 + 3x^2 - 28x\). Determine the perimeter of the base of the prism.
qs.s: Factoring out the height \(x\) yields \(x(x^2 + 3x - 28) = x(x + 7)(x - 4)\), so the dimensions of the base are \(x + 7\) and \(x - 4\). The perimeter of the base is \(2((x + 7) + (x - 4)) = 2(2x + 3) = 4x + 6\).

qs.q: A rectangular prism with a square base has a height of \(4x\) and a volume of \(4x^3 - 48x^2 + 144x\). Determine the perimeter of the base.
qs.s: Factoring out the height \(4x\) gives \(4x(x^2 - 12x + 36) = 4x(x - 6)^2\). The side length of the square base is \(x - 6\), so its perimeter is \(4(x - 6) = 4x - 24\).

qs.q: A rectangular storage container has a height of \(x\) and a volume of \(x^3 + 15x^2 + 54x\). Determine the perimeter of the base of the container.
qs.s: Factoring out the height \(x\) gives \(x(x^2 + 15x + 54) = x(x + 6)(x + 9)\), meaning the base dimensions are \(x + 6\) and \(x + 9\). The perimeter of the base is \(2((x + 6) + (x + 9)) = 2(2x + 15) = 4x + 30\).

qs.q: A cylinder with a height of \(2x\) has a volume of \(\pi(2x^3 - 32x^2 + 128x)\). Determine the diameter of the cylinder.
qs.s: Factoring out the common factor \(2x\) gives the volume as \(\pi(2x)(x^2 - 16x + 64) = \pi(2x)(x - 8)^2\). Since \(h = 2x\), the radius is \(r = x - 8\), which makes the diameter \(2(x - 8) = 2x - 16\).

qs.q: The total surface area of a cylinder with radius \(x\text{ cm}\) is \((2\pi x^2 + 14\pi x y)\text{ cm}^2\). Determine the height of the cylinder.
qs.s: The total surface area of a cylinder is \(A = 2\pi r(r + h) = 2\pi x(x + h)\). Factoring the given area yields \(2\pi x(x + 7y)\), so \(x + h = x + 7y\), which gives \(h = 7y\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A sheet of cardboard measuring 9 inches by 11 inches has squares \(x\) inches wide cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: Cutting squares of side \(x\) removes \(2x\) from both the length and width, leaving base dimensions of \((9 - 2x)\) and \((11 - 2x)\) inches. With a folded height of \(x\) inches, the volume is \(V = x(9 - 2x)(11 - 2x)\).

qs.q: A craft paper sheet measuring 3 inches by 7 inches has squares \(x\) inches wide cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top tray. Express the volume of the tray in factored form.
qs.s: The base of the tray measures \((3 - 2x)\) inches by \((7 - 2x)\) inches, and folding the sides gives a height of \(x\) inches. Thus, the volume in factored form is \(V = x(3 - 2x)(7 - 2x)\).

qs.q: A piece of poster board measuring 11 inches by 15 inches has squares \(x\) inches wide cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: Removing corner squares of width \(x\) leaves a base measuring \((11 - 2x)\) inches by \((15 - 2x)\) inches. Multiplying the base area by the height \(x\) gives \(V = x(11 - 2x)(15 - 2x)\).

qs.q: A sheet of aluminum measuring 5 feet by 9 feet has squares \(x\) feet wide cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top bin. Express the volume of the bin in factored form.
qs.s: Cutting two corners from each dimension reduces the width to \((5 - 2x)\) feet and the length to \((9 - 2x)\) feet. The height is \(x\) feet, so the volume is \(V = x(5 - 2x)(9 - 2x)\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of tin measuring 7 cm by 13 cm has squares \(x\) cm wide cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: The base of the box has dimensions \((7 - 2x)\) cm and \((13 - 2x)\) cm, and the folded sides create a height of \(x\) cm. Therefore, the volume in factored form is \(V = x(7 - 2x)(13 - 2x)\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of plastic has a length that is 8 cm longer than its width, \(w\). Squares of side length 3 cm are cut from each corner, and the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in terms of \(w\) in factored form.
qs.s: The sheet has width \(w\) and length \(w + 8\). Cutting 3 cm squares from each corner reduces each dimension by \(2(3) = 6\) cm, giving base dimensions of \(w - 6\) and \((w + 8) - 6 = w + 2\), with height 3, so \(V = 3(w - 6)(w + 2)\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of cardboard has a length of \((4x + 9)\) cm and a width of \((3x + 5)\) cm. Squares with side length \(x\) cm are cut from each corner, and the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) from each dimension gives a length of \((4x + 9) - 2x = 2x + 9\) and a width of \((3x + 5) - 2x = x + 5\). With a height of \(x\), the volume is \(V = x(x + 5)(2x + 9)\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of cardboard measuring 19 inches by 23 inches has squares with side length \(2x\) inches cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: Cutting two corners of side \(2x\) subtracts \(2(2x) = 4x\) from each dimension, giving base dimensions of \((19 - 4x)\) and \((23 - 4x)\). Since the height is \(2x\), the volume is \(V = 2x(19 - 4x)(23 - 4x)\).

qs.q: A square sheet of metal measuring 21 cm by 21 cm has squares of side length \(x\) cm cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: The cut reduces both dimensions of the square base from 21 cm to \((21 - 2x)\) cm. With height \(x\) cm, the volume is \(V = x(21 - 2x)(21 - 2x) = x(21 - 2x)^2\).

qs.q: A sheet of metal measuring 25 cm by 35 cm has squares of side length \(3x\) cm cut from each corner. Then the sides are folded up to form an open-top box. Express the volume of the box in factored form.
qs.s: Each corner cut removes \(3x\) cm, so two cuts per side reduce dimensions by \(2(3x) = 6x\) cm to \((25 - 6x)\) and \((35 - 6x)\). With a height of \(3x\), the volume is \(V = 3x(25 - 6x)(35 - 6x)\).

qs.q: A town has an initial population of \(N\) residents. If the population grows at an annual rate \(k\), the population at the end of one year is \(N + Nk\). At the end of two years, the population is \(N + Nk + (N + Nk)k\). Factor the last expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((N + Nk)\) to get \((N + Nk)(1 + k)\). Then factor out \(N\) from the first factor to obtain \(N(1 + k)(1 + k) = N(1 + k)^2\).

qs.q: A company's annual revenue is \(R\) dollars and grows at a yearly rate \(g\). At the end of the first year, the revenue is \(R + Rg\). At the end of the second year, the revenue is \(R + Rg + (R + Rg)g\). Factor the last expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((R + Rg)\) to get \((R + Rg)(1 + g)\). Then factor out \(R\) from the first factor to obtain \(R(1 + g)(1 + g) = R(1 + g)^2\).

qs.q: If a vehicle is purchased for \(V\) dollars and depreciates at an annual rate \(d\), its value at the end of one year is \(V - Vd\). At the end of two years, its value is \(V - Vd - (V - Vd)d\). Factor the last expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((V - Vd)\) to get \((V - Vd)(1 - d)\). Then factor out \(V\) from the first factor to obtain \(V(1 - d)(1 - d) = V(1 - d)^2\).

qs.q: A computer system valued at $500 depreciates at an annual rate \(x\). At the end of one year, its value is \(500 - 500x\). At the end of two years, its value is \(500 - 500x - (500 - 500x)x\). Factor the last expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((500 - 500x)\) to get \((500 - 500x)(1 - x)\). Then factor out \(500\) from the first factor to get \(500(1 - x)(1 - x) = 500(1 - x)^2\).

qs.q: If $100 is invested at an annual interest rate \(r\), compounded yearly, the amount of money at the end of one year is \(100 + 100r\). At the end of two years, the amount of money is \(100 + 100r + (100 + 100r)r\). Factor the last expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((100 + 100r)\) to get \((100 + 100r)(1 + r)\). Then factor out \(100\) from the first factor to get \(100(1 + r)(1 + r) = 100(1 + r)^2\).

qs.q: An investment of $600 earns interest at an annual rate \(r\) in the first year, growing to \(600 + 600r\). In the second year, the interest rate increases to \(2r\), so the total amount at the end of the second year is \(600 + 600r + (600 + 600r)(2r)\). Factor this expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((600 + 600r)\) to get \((600 + 600r)(1 + 2r)\). Then factor out \(600\) from \((600 + 600r)\) to obtain \(600(1 + r)(2r + 1)\).

qs.q: A company vehicle purchased for $1200 depreciates at an annual rate \(d\). At the end of two years, its value is \(1200 - 2400d + 1200d^2\). At the end of three years, its value is \((1200 - 2400d + 1200d^2) - (1200 - 2400d + 1200d^2)d\). Factor this expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common polynomial \((1200 - 2400d + 1200d^2)\) to get \((1200 - 2400d + 1200d^2)(1 - d)\). Factoring the first term gives \(1200(1 - 2d + d^2) = 1200(1 - d)^2\), so the completely factored form is \(1200(1 - d)^3\).

qs.q: An investor deposits $100 at the beginning of Year 1 and another $100 at the beginning of Year 2, both earning interest at an annual rate \(r\) compounded yearly. At the end of Year 2, the total accumulated balance is \([100 + 100r + (100 + 100r)r] + (100 + 100r)\). Factor this expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((100 + 100r)\) from both terms to get \((100 + 100r)[(1 + r) + 1] = (100 + 100r)(r + 2)\). Then factor out \(100\) from the first factor to obtain \(100(1 + r)(r + 2)\).

qs.q: An investor has two accounts that both earn an annual interest rate \(r\). At the end of two years, Account A has grown to \(P + 2Pr + Pr^2\). At the end of one year, Account B with an initial deposit of \(5P\) dollars has grown to \(5P + 5Pr\). Write the total value of both accounts, \((P + 2Pr + Pr^2) + (5P + 5Pr)\), in completely factored form.
qs.s: Combine like terms to express the total as \(Pr^2 + 7Pr + 6P = P(r^2 + 7r + 6)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields two factors of 6 that add to 7, giving \(P(r + 1)(r + 6)\).

qs.q: If \(P\) dollars is invested at an annual interest rate \(r\) compounded yearly, the amount of money at the end of two years is \(P + 2Pr + Pr^2\). At the end of three years, the amount is \((P + 2Pr + Pr^2) + (P + 2Pr + Pr^2)r\). Factor this expression completely.
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((P + 2Pr + Pr^2)\) to obtain \((P + 2Pr + Pr^2)(1 + r)\). Then factor the first part as \(P(1 + 2r + r^2) = P(1 + r)^2\), which gives \(P(1 + r)^2(1 + r) = P(1 + r)^3\).

exercises.name: Complete factoring of a quadratic trinomial

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4x^2 + 16x + 15 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant \(15\) by \(3\) to get \(5\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(5) + (3)(2x) = 16x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 + 22x + 15 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(8x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(4x\), and \(15\) by \(3\) to get \(5\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(5) + (3)(4x) = 22x\), so the missing factor is \(4x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 17x + 5 = (2x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the last term \(5\) by \(5\) to get \(1\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(1) + (5)(3x) = 17x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 13x + 6 = (3x + 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(2x\), and \(6\) by \(2\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term, \((3x)(3) + (2)(2x) = 13x\), which confirms the factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 + 19x + 6 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(10x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(5x\), and the constant \(6\) by \(3\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(2) + (3)(5x) = 19x\), so the missing factor is \(5x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(28x^2 + 13x - 6 = (7x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(28x^2\) by \(7x\) to get \(4x\), and \(-6\) by \(-2\) to get \(+3\). Verifying the middle term gives \((7x)(3) + (-2)(4x) = 13x\), confirming the missing factor is \(4x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 - 23x - 21 = (4x - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to obtain \(5x\), and \(-21\) by \(-7\) to obtain \(+3\). Verifying the middle term gives \((4x)(3) + (-7)(5x) = -23x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(24x^2 - 41x + 12 = (8x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(24x^2\) by \(8x\) to get \(3x\), and \(12\) by \(-3\) to get \(-4\). Checking the middle term, \((8x)(-4) + (-3)(3x) = -32x - 9x = -41x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 - 11xy - 15y^2 = (4x + 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(3x\), and \(-15y^2\) by \(3y\) to get \(-5y\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x)(-5y) + (3y)(3x) = -11xy\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 - 38xy + 24y^2 = (5x - 6y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(3x\), and \(24y^2\) by \(-6y\) to get \(-4y\). Verifying the middle term gives \((5x)(-4y) + (-6y)(3x) = -38xy\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 4y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 19x + 10 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(10\) by \(-2\) to get \(-5\). Checking the middle term, \(3x(-5) + (-2)(2x) = -19x\), confirms the missing factor is \(2x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 + 10x - 3 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(8x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(4x\), and the constant term \(-3\) by \(3\) to get \(-1\). Checking the middle term, \(2x(-1) + 3(4x) = 10x\), confirms the missing factor is \(4x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 - 5x - 2 = (4x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(12x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant term \(-2\) by \(1\) to get \(-2\). Checking the middle term, \(4x(-2) + 1(3x) = -5x\), confirms the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 11x + 4 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant term \(4\) by \(1\) to get \(4\). Checking the middle term, \(2x(4) + 1(3x) = 11x\), confirms the missing factor is \(3x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 + 9x + 2 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(10x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(5x\), and the constant term \(2\) by \(1\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term, \(2x(2) + 1(5x) = 9x\), confirms the missing factor is \(5x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 - 37x + 15 = (4x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and the constant term \(15\) by \(-5\) to get \(-3\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \(4x(-3) + (-5)(5x) = -37x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^4 + 7x^2 - 20 = (2x^2 + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(6x^4\) by \(2x^2\) to obtain \(3x^2\), and the constant term \(-20\) by \(5\) to obtain \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x^2(-4) + 5(3x^2) = 7x^2\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x^2 - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^3 - 26x^2 + 8x = x(3x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factoring out the greatest common factor \(x\) leaves \(15x^2 - 26x + 8\). Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) yields \(5x\), and dividing \(8\) by \(-4\) yields \(-2\), which gives the missing factor \(5x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8a^2 - 14ab - 15b^2 = (2a - 5b)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(8a^2\) by \(2a\) to get \(4a\), and the last term \(-15b^2\) by \(-5b\) to get \(+3b\). Checking the middle term gives \(2a(3b) + (-5b)(4a) = -14ab\), confirming the missing factor is \(4a + 3b\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2p^2 - 3p - 5 = (2p - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(2p^2\) by \(2p\) gives \(p\), and dividing the constant \(-5\) by \(-5\) gives \(1\). Checking the middle term gives \(2p(1) + (-5)(p) = -3p\), so the missing factor is \(p + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3y^2 + 13y + 4 = (3y + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(3y^2\) by \(3y\) gives \(y\), and dividing the constant \(4\) by \(1\) gives \(4\). Checking the middle term gives \(3y(4) + 1(y) = 13y\), confirming the missing factor is \(y + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3m^2 + 5m - 2 = (3m - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(3m^2\) by \(3m\) gives \(m\), and dividing the constant \(-2\) by \(-1\) gives \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(3m(2) + (-1)(m) = 5m\), confirming the missing factor is \(m + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2a^2 - 9a + 7 = (2a - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(2a^2\) by \(2a\) gives \(a\), and dividing the constant \(7\) by \(-7\) gives \(-1\). Checking the middle term gives \(2a(-1) + (-7)(a) = -9a\), so the missing factor is \(a - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2x^2 + 9x + 10 = (2x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(2x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(x\), and dividing the constant \(10\) by \(5\) gives \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(2) + 5(x) = 9x\), so the missing factor is \(x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10a^2 - 19ab - 15b^2 = (2a - 5b)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(10a^2\) by \(2a\) gives \(5a\), and dividing \(-15b^2\) by \(-5b\) gives \(3b\). Checking the middle term gives \((2a)(3b) + (-5b)(5a) = -19ab\), so the missing factor is \(5a + 3b\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(24x^2 - 14x - 5 = (4x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(24x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(6x\), and dividing \(-5\) by \(1\) gives \(-5\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x)(-5) + 1(6x) = -14x\), confirming the missing factor is \(6x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2 = (3x - 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) gives \(4x\), and dividing \(6y^2\) by \(-2y\) gives \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \((3x)(-3y) + (-2y)(4x) = -17xy\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 + 34x - 16 = (5x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(-16\) by \(-2\) gives \(8\). Checking the middle term gives \((5x)(8) + (-2)(3x) = 34x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x + 8\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 7x - 20 = (2x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(-20\) by \(5\) gives \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(-4) + 5(3x) = 7x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 - 19x + 6 = (5x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(6\) by \(-2\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term gives \(5x(-3) + (-2)(2x) = -19x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 + 14x - 8 = (3x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(5x\), and divide the constant term \(-8\) by \(4\) to get \(-2\). Verifying the middle term gives \(3x(-2) + 4(5x) = 14x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 11x - 10 = (2x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide the constant term \(-10\) by \(5\) to get \(-2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(-2) + 5(3x) = 11x\), confirming the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 17x + 12 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to obtain \(3x\), and divide \(12\) by \(-3\) to obtain \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(-4) + (-3)(3x) = -17x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 + 7x - 12 = (3x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to obtain \(4x\), and divide \(-12\) by \(4\) to obtain \(-3\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \(3x(-3) + 4(4x) = 7x\), which confirms the factor is \(4x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(28x^2 - 27xy - 10y^2 = (7x + 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(28x^2\) by \(7x\) to get \(4x\), and the last term \(-10y^2\) by \(2y\) to get \(-5y\). Checking the middle term gives \(7x(-5y) + 2y(4x) = -35xy + 8xy = -27xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(4x - 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(24x^2 - 41x - 35 = (3x - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(24x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(8x\), and the constant \(-35\) by \(-7\) to get \(+5\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(5) + (-7)(8x) = 15x - 56x = -41x\), so the missing factor is \(8x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(36x^2 - 43xy + 12y^2 = (9x - 4y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(36x^2\) by \(9x\) to obtain \(4x\), and divide \(12y^2\) by \(-4y\) to obtain \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \(9x(-3y) + (-4y)(4x) = -27xy - 16xy = -43xy\), which confirms the factor is \(4x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(40x^2 - 59x + 21 = (5x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(40x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(8x\), and divide the constant \(21\) by \(-3\) to get \(-7\). Verifying the middle term gives \(5x(-7) + (-3)(8x) = -35x - 24x = -59x\), confirming the missing factor is \(8x - 7\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(42x^2 + 71x + 30 = (6x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(42x^2\) by \(6x\) to get \(7x\), and the constant term \(30\) by \(5\) to get \(6\). Verifying the middle term gives \(6x(6) + 5(7x) = 36x + 35x = 71x\), so the missing factor is \(7x + 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 + 7x - 5 = (2x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-5\) by \(-1\) to get \(+5\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \(2x(5) + (-1)(3x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 - 7x - 2 = (3x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(-2\) by \(-2\) to get \(+1\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(1) + (-2)(5x) = -7x\), so the missing factor is \(5x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 - 14x + 3 = (4x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(8x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(3\) by \(-1\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term gives \(4x(-3) + (-1)(2x) = -14x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 - 17xy - 5y^2 = (3x - 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(4x\), and divide \(-5y^2\) by \(-5y\) to get \(+y\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(y) + (-5y)(4x) = -17xy\), so the missing factor is \(4x + y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 + 23xy - 21y^2 = (4x + 7y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(-21y^2\) by \(7y\) to get \(-3y\). Checking the middle term gives \(4x(-3y) + 7y(5x) = 23xy\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(28x^2 - 41x + 15 = (7x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(28x^2\) by \(7x\) to get \(4x\), and divide \(15\) by \(-5\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term gives \(7x(-3) + (-5)(4x) = -41x\), confirming the missing factor is \(4x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-18x^3 + 33x^2 - 12x = -3x(2x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Removing the common factor \(-3x\) leaves \(6x^2 - 11x + 4\). Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(+4\) by \(-1\) gives \(-4\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 + 10x + 3 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(8x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(3\) by \(3\) to get \(1\). Checking the middle term gives \(4x(1) + 3(2x) = 10x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4a^2 - 8a + 3 = (2a - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(4a^2\) by \(2a\) to get \(2a\), and the constant term \(3\) by \(-1\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term gives \(2a(-3) + (-1)(2a) = -8a\), so the missing factor is \(2a - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6y^2 + 7y + 2 = (2y + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6y^2\) by \(2y\) to get \(3y\), and the last term \(2\) by \(1\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(2y(2) + 1(3y) = 7y\), so the missing factor is \(3y + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4x^2 + 12x + 9 = (2x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(9\) by \(3\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(3) + 3(2x) = 12x\), so the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 7x - 3 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant term \(-3\) by \(-3\) to get \(1\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(1) + (-3)(3x) = -7x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(14x^2 + 13xy - 12y^2 = (2x + 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(14x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(7x\), and \(-12y^2\) by \(3y\) to get \(-4y\). Checking the middle term gives \(2x(-4y) + 3y(7x) = 13xy\), so the missing factor is \(7x - 4y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 - 34x - 16 = (3x - 8)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to obtain \(5x\), and divide \(-16\) by \(-8\) to obtain \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \(3x(2) + (-8)(5x) = -34x\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 11x + 4 = (3x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(6x^2\) by \(3x\) yields \(2x\), and dividing \(4\) by \(-4\) yields \(-1\). Checking the sum of outer and inner products gives \((3x)(-1) + (-4)(2x) = -11x\), confirming \(2x - 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(4x^2 - 4x - 3 = (2x + 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(4x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing the constant term \(-3\) by \(1\) gives \(-3\). Checking the middle term, \((2x)(-3) + (1)(2x) = -4x\), which confirms \((2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 + 11x - 6 = (5x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the first term \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(2x\), and dividing the constant \(-6\) by \(-2\) gives \(3\). Verifying the middle term, \((5x)(3) + (-2)(2x) = 11x\), confirming \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 - 2x - 15 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(8x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(4x\), and dividing \(-15\) by \(-3\) gives \(5\). Checking the outer and inner products confirms \((2x)(5) + (-3)(4x) = 10x - 12x = -2x\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(24x^2 - 38xy + 15y^2 = (4x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(24x^2\) by \(4x\) yields \(6x\), and dividing \(15y^2\) by \(-3y\) yields \(-5y\). Checking the middle term confirms \((4x)(-5y) + (-3y)(6x) = -20xy - 18xy = -38xy\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(18x^2 - 27x - 35 = (3x - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(18x^2\) by \(3x\) yields \(6x\), and dividing \(-35\) by \(-7\) yields \(5\). Checking the outer and inner products gives \((3x)(5) + (-7)(6x) = 15x - 42x = -27x\), confirming \(6x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 - 19xy + 6y^2 = (5x - 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(15x^2\) by \(5x\) gives \(3x\), and dividing \(6y^2\) by \(-3y\) gives \(-2y\). Verifying the middle term, \((5x)(-2y) + (-3y)(3x) = -10xy - 9xy = -19xy\), confirming \(3x - 2y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(-12x^2 + 11x + 15 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing the leading term \(-12x^2\) by \(4x\) gives \(-3x\), and dividing \(15\) by \(3\) gives \(5\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x)(5) + (3)(-3x) = 20x - 9x = 11x\), confirming \(-3x + 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2x^2 - 9x + 10 = (x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(2x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(10\) by \(-2\) to get \(-5\). Checking the middle term gives \((x)(-5) + (-2)(2x) = -9x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 - 2x - 8 = (x - 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(3x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(-8\) by \(-2\) to get \(4\). Checking the middle term gives \((x)(4) + (-2)(3x) = -2x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(2x^2 + 5x - 12 = (x + 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(2x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(2x\), and divide \(-12\) by \(4\) to get \(-3\). Checking the middle term gives \((x)(-3) + (4)(2x) = 5x\), so the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 + 7x + 2 = (x + 2)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(3x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(2\) by \(2\) to get \(1\). Checking the middle term gives \((x)(1) + (2)(3x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(3x + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(3x^2 - 8x + 5 = (x - 1)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(3x^2\) by \(x\) to get \(3x\), and divide \(5\) by \(-1\) to get \(-5\). Checking the middle term gives \((x)(-5) + (-1)(3x) = -8x\), so the missing factor is \(3x - 5\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(8x^2 + 2xy - 15y^2 = (2x + 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(8x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(4x\), and divide \(-15y^2\) by \(3y\) to get \(-5y\). Verifying the middle term, \((2x)(-5y) + (3y)(4x) = 2xy\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 + 11x - 15 = (3x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(12x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(4x\), and divide \(-15\) by \(5\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term, \((3x)(-3) + (5)(4x) = 11x\), so the missing factor is \(4x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^4 - 13x^2 - 5 = (2x^2 - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(6x^4\) by \(2x^2\) to get \(3x^2\), and divide \(-5\) by \(-5\) to get \(1\). Verifying the middle term, \((2x^2)(1) + (-5)(3x^2) = -13x^2\), so the missing factor is \(3x^2 + 1\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(15x^2 - 19xy + 6y^2 = (3x - 2y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(15x^2\) by \(3x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(6y^2\) by \(-2y\) to get \(-3y\). Verifying the middle term, \((3x)(-3y) + (-2y)(5x) = -19xy\), so the missing factor is \(5x - 3y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 - 27x - 14 = (4x - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(5x\), and divide \(-14\) by \(-7\) to get \(2\). Verifying the middle term, \((4x)(2) + (-7)(5x) = -27x\), so the missing factor is \(5x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(12x^2 + 17x + 6 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(12x^2\) by \(4x\) to get \(3x\), and divide the constant term \(6\) by \(3\) to get \(2\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x)(2) + 3(3x) = 17x\), confirming the factor is \(3x + 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(14x^2 - 27x - 20 = (2x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(14x^2\) by \(2x\) to obtain \(7x\), and the constant term \(-20\) by \(-5\) to obtain \(4\). Since \((2x)(4) + (-5)(7x) = -27x\), the missing factor is \(7x + 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 - 23x + 12 = (2x - 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(10x^2\) by \(2x\) gives \(5x\), and dividing \(12\) by \(-3\) gives \(-4\). Checking the middle term gives \((2x)(-4) + (-3)(5x) = -23x\), which confirms the factor is \(5x - 4\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 + 7x - 6 = (4x + 3)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Dividing \(20x^2\) by \(4x\) yields \(5x\), and dividing \(-6\) by \(3\) yields \(-2\). Checking the middle term confirms \((4x)(-2) + 3(5x) = 7x\), so the missing factor is \(5x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(48x^2 + 22x - 15 = (6x + 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(48x^2\) by \(6x\) to get \(8x\), and divide \(-15\) by \(5\) to get \(-3\). Verifying the middle term gives \((6x)(-3) + 5(8x) = 22x\), confirming the factor is \(8x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(35x^2 - 58x + 24 = (5x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(35x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(7x\), and divide the constant \(24\) by \(-4\) to get \(-6\). Checking the outer and inner products confirms \((5x)(-6) + (-4)(7x) = -58x\), so the missing factor is \(7x - 6\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(36x^2 - 25xy - 25y^2 = (4x - 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide \(36x^2\) by \(4x\) to obtain \(9x\), and divide \(-25y^2\) by \(-5y\) to obtain \(5y\). Verifying the middle term gives \((4x)(5y) + (-5y)(9x) = -25xy\), confirming the factor is \(9x + 5y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^4 - 23x^2 - 21 = (4x^2 - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the leading term \(20x^4\) by \(4x^2\) to get \(5x^2\), and divide the constant \(-21\) by \(-7\) to get \(3\). Checking the middle term gives \((4x^2)(3) + (-7)(5x^2) = -23x^2\), confirming the missing factor is \(5x^2 + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(28x^2 + 13xy - 6y^2 = (4x + 3y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(28x^2\) by \(4x\) to obtain \(7x\), and the last term \(-6y^2\) by \(3y\) to obtain \(-2y\). Checking the cross products gives \((4x)(-2y) + (3y)(7x) = 13xy\), so the missing factor is \(7x - 2y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(14x^2 + 13x - 12 = (7x - 4)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(14x^2\) by \(7x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(-12\) by \(-4\) to get \(3\). Thus, the missing factor is \(2x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(10x^2 - 29x + 21 = (5x - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(10x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(2x\), and the constant term \(21\) by \(-7\) to get \(-3\). Thus, the missing factor is \(2x - 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(6x^2 - 19x + 10 = (2x - 5)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(6x^2\) by \(2x\) to get \(3x\), and the constant term \(10\) by \(-5\) to get \(-2\). Thus, the missing factor is \(3x - 2\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(28x^2 + 27xy - 10y^2 = (4x + 5y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(28x^2\) by \(4x\) to obtain \(7x\), and the last term \(-10y^2\) by \(5y\) to obtain \(-2y\). Thus, the missing factor is \(7x - 2y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(35x^2 - 27x - 18 = (5x - 6)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(35x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(7x\), and the constant term \(-18\) by \(-6\) to get \(3\). Thus, the missing factor is \(7x + 3\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(20x^2 - 31xy - 9y^2 = (5x - 9y)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(20x^2\) by \(5x\) to get \(4x\), and the last term \(-9y^2\) by \(-9y\) to get \(y\). Thus, the missing factor is \(4x + y\).

qs.q: Complete the factoring: \(18x^4 - 27x^2 - 35 = (3x^2 - 7)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Divide the first term \(18x^4\) by \(3x^2\) to get \(6x^2\), and the constant term \(-35\) by \(-7\) to get \(5\). Thus, the missing factor is \(6x^2 + 5\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(3 \times 8 = 24\) and add to \(14\), which are \(2\) and \(12\). Rewrite the middle term as \(12x + 2x\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x + 2)(x + 4)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 12 = 24\) and add to \(11\), which are \(3\) and \(8\). Rewrite the middle term as \(8x + 3x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x + 3)(x + 4)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 10 = 20\) and add to \(9\), which are \(4\) and \(5\). Rewrite the middle term as \(4x + 5x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x + 5)(x + 2)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(3 \times 6 = 18\) and add to \(11\), which are \(9\) and \(2\). Rewrite the middle term as \(9x + 2x\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x + 2)(x + 3)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(5 \times 8 = 40\) and add to \(14\), which are \(10\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(10x + 4x\) and factor by grouping to get \((5x + 4)(x + 2)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times (-24) = -288\) and add to \(23\), which are \(32\) and \(-9\). Group as \(4x(3x + 8) - 3(3x + 8) = (4x - 3)(3x + 8)\).
Find two factors of \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(4x(2x - 5y) + 3y(2x - 5y) = (4x + 3y)(2x - 5y)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times (-10) = -60\) and add to \(-11\), which are \(-15\) and \(4\). Factor by grouping: \(3x(2x - 5) + 2(2x - 5) = (3x + 2)(2x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3 + 22x^2 - 6x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(6x^2 - 11x + 3)\). Then factor the quadratic using \(-9\) and \(-2\) to get \(-2x(3x - 1)(2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^3 + 26x^2 + 24x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(3x^2 + 13x + 12)\). Factor the remaining quadratic using factors \(9\) and \(4\) (since \(9 \times 4 = 36\) and \(9 + 4 = 13\)) to obtain \(2x(3x + 4)(x + 3)\).
Find two factors of \(3 \times 3 = 9\) that add to \(10\), which are \(9\) and \(1\). Rewrite as \(3x^2 + 9x + x + 3 = 3x(x + 3) + 1(x + 3) = (3x + 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2x^2 + 7x + 3\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(2 \times 3 = 6\) that add to \(7\), which are \(1\) and \(6\). Factor by grouping: \(2x^2 + x + 6x + 3 = x(2x + 1) + 3(2x + 1) = (2x + 1)(x + 3)\).
Find two factors of \(5 \times 4 = 20\) that add to \(12\), which are \(10\) and \(2\). Group terms to get \(5x(x + 2) + 2(x + 2) = (5x + 2)(x + 2)\).
Find two factors of \(8 \times (-15) = -120\) that add to \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Factor by grouping: \(8x^2 - 20x + 6x - 15 = 4x(2x - 5) + 3(2x - 5) = (4x + 3)(2x - 5)\).

Find two factors of \(6 \times 20 = 120\) that sum to \(23\), which are \(15\) and \(8\). Split the middle term and factor by grouping: \(6x^2 + 15x + 8x + 20 = 3x(2x + 5) + 4(2x + 5) = (3x + 4)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^3 + 22x^2 + 24x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(2x^2 + 11x + 12)\). Then find factors of \(2 \times 12 = 24\) that add to \(11\) (\(8\) and \(3\)) to obtain \(2x(2x + 3)(x + 4)\).
Find two factors of \(6 \times 10 = 60\) that sum to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Rewrite as \(6x^2 + 15xy + 4xy + 10y^2 = 3x(2x + 5y) + 2y(2x + 5y) = (3x + 2y)(2x + 5y)\).
Find two factors of \(12 \times 10 = 120\) that sum to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Factor by grouping: \(12x^2 - 15x - 8x + 10 = 3x(4x - 5) - 2(4x - 5) = (4x - 5)(3x - 2)\).
