Find two numbers that multiply to \(14 \times 3 = 42\) and add to \(13\), which are \(7\) and \(6\). Rewrite the middle term as \(7x + 6x\) and factor by grouping to get \((7x + 3)(2x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(8 \times 3 = 24\) and add to \(10\), which are \(6\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(6x + 4x\) and factor by grouping to get \((4x + 3)(2x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(12 \times 5 = 60\) and add to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(15x + 4x\) and factor by grouping to get \((4x + 5)(3x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times 3 = 45\) and add to \(14\), which are \(9\) and \(5\). Rewrite the middle term as \(9x + 5x\) and factor by grouping to get \((5x + 3)(3x + 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times 10 = 60\) and add to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Rewrite the middle term as \(15x + 4x\) and factor by grouping to get \((3x + 2)(2x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^3 + 33x^2 - 12x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(6x^2 - 11x + 4)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial with factors of \(24\) that sum to \(-11\) (\(-8\) and \(-3\)) gives \(-3x(3x - 4)(2x - 1)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(15 \times (-14) = -210\) and add to \(11\), which are \(21\) and \(-10\). Rewrite the middle term as \(21x - 10x\) and factor by grouping to get \((5x + 7)(3x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 + 34x^2 + 14x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(6x^2 + 17x + 7)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(2x(3x + 7)(2x + 1)\).

Find two numbers that multiply to \(8 \times 15 = 120\) and add to \(-22\), which are \(-12\) and \(-10\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-12xy - 10xy\) and factor by grouping to get \((4x - 5y)(2x - 3y)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(10 \times 6 = 60\) and whose sum is \(-19\), which are \(-15\) and \(-4\). Rewrite as \(10x^2 - 15x - 4x + 6 = 5x(2x - 3) - 2(2x - 3) = (2x - 3)(5x - 2)\).

Find two numbers whose product is \(6 \times 12 = 72\) and whose sum is \(-17\), which are \(-9\) and \(-8\). Rewrite the trinomial as \(6x^2 - 9x - 8x + 12\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x - 3)(3x - 4)\).

Find two numbers whose product is \(4 \times 15 = 60\) and whose sum is \(-16\), which are \(-10\) and \(-6\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(4x^2 - 10x - 6x + 15 = 2x(2x - 5) - 3(2x - 5) = (2x - 3)(2x - 5)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \(8 \times 3 = 24\) and whose sum is \(-14\), which are \(-12\) and \(-2\). Rewrite as \(8m^2 - 12m - 2m + 3 = 4m(2m - 3) - 1(2m - 3) = (2m - 3)(4m - 1)\).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(6 \times 10 = 60\) and add to \(19\), which are \(15\) and \(4\). Rewrite as \(6y^2 + 15y + 4y + 10 = 3y(2y + 5) + 2(2y + 5) = (2y + 5)(3y + 2)\).

Find two numbers whose product is \(12 \times 15 = 180\) and sum is \(-28\), which are \(-18\) and \(-10\). Rewrite the middle term as \(12x^2 - 18xy - 10xy + 15y^2 = 6x(2x - 3y) - 5y(2x - 3y) = (2x - 3y)(6x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18a^3b + 33a^2b^2 - 12ab^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-3ab\) to get \(-3ab(6a^2 - 11ab + 4b^2)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \(6 \times 4 = 24\) that add to \(-11\) (which are \(-8\) and \(-3\)) to get \(-3ab(2a - b)(3a - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 - 38x^2 + 30x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(6x^2 - 19x + 15)\). Then find two factors of \(6 \times 15 = 90\) that sum to \(-19\) (which are \(-10\) and \(-9\)) to factor the quadratic into \(2x(2x - 3)(3x - 5)\).
Find two integers whose product is \(15 \times 15 = 225\) and sum is \(-34\), which are \(-25\) and \(-9\). Group terms: \(15x^2 - 25x - 9x + 15 = 5x(3x - 5) - 3(3x - 5) = (3x - 5)(5x - 3)\).

Find two integers that multiply to \(20 \times 24 = 480\) and add to \(-47\), which are \(-32\) and \(-15\). Rewrite the expression as \(20y^2 - 32y - 15y + 24 = 4y(5y - 8) - 3(5y - 8) = (4y - 3)(5y - 8)\).
Find two factors of (10)(-15) = -150 that add to 19, which are 25 and -6. Rewrite as 10t^2 + 25t - 6t - 15 = 5t(2t + 5) - 3(2t + 5) = (2t + 5)(5t - 3).
Find two factors of (15)(8) = 120 that add to -26, which are -20 and -6. Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: 15x^2 - 20x - 6x + 8 = 5x(3x - 4) - 2(3x - 4) = (3x - 4)(5x - 2).
Find two factors of (12)(12) = 144 that add to -25, which are -16 and -9. Rewrite as 12a^2 - 16a - 9a + 12 = 4a(3a - 4) - 3(3a - 4) = (3a - 4)(4a - 3).
Find two factors of (18)(10) = 180 that sum to -27, which are -15 and -12. Rewrite as 18w^2 - 15w - 12w + 10 = 3w(6w - 5) - 2(6w - 5) = (3w - 2)(6w - 5).
Find two factors of (20)(6) = 120 that sum to -23, which are -15 and -8. Factor by grouping: 20z^2 - 15z - 8z + 6 = 5z(4z - 3) - 2(4z - 3) = (4z - 3)(5z - 2).
Find two factors of (24)(-35) = -840 that add to -41, which are -56 and 15. Rewrite the expression as 24x^2 - 56x + 15x - 35 and group terms to get (3x - 7)(8x + 5).
Find two factors of (36)(24) = 864 that add to -59, which are -32 and -27. Rewrite as 36x^2 - 32x - 27x + 24 and factor by grouping to get 4x(9x - 8) - 3(9x - 8) = (4x - 3)(9x - 8).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^3 + 33x^2 + 30x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor -3x to obtain -3x(6x^2 - 11x - 10). Then find factors of (6)(-10) = -60 that add to -11 (-15 and 4) to factor the trinomial into -3x(2x - 5)(3x + 2).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(30a^3b - 49a^2b^2 + 20ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor ab to get ab(30a^2 - 49ab + 20b^2). Two factors of (30)(20) = 600 that add to -49 are -25 and -24, which factors the expression into ab(5a - 4b)(6a - 5b).
Find two factors of (24)(15) = 360 that add to -38, which are -20 and -18. Rewrite as 24x^2 - 20xy - 18xy + 15y^2 and factor by grouping to get (4x - 3y)(6x - 5y).
Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 5 = 10\) and add to \(-11\), which are \(-10\) and \(-1\). Grouping gives \(2a(a - 5) - 1(a - 5) = (2a - 1)(a - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(3x^2 - 8x + 5\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(3 \times 5 = 15\) and add to \(-8\), which are \(-3\) and \(-5\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping to get \((3x - 5)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2w^2 + 5w - 3\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times (-3) = -6\) and add to \(5\), which are \(6\) and \(-1\). Factoring by grouping yields \((2w - 1)(w + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(2x^2 + 9x + 7\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(2 \times 7 = 14\) and add to \(9\), which are \(2\) and \(7\). Factoring by grouping yields \((2x + 7)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(3m^2 - 7m + 2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers that multiply to \(3 \times 2 = 6\) and add to \(-7\), which are \(-6\) and \(-1\). Splitting the middle term gives \(3m(m - 2) - 1(m - 2) = (3m - 1)(m - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 - 11xy + 4y^2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers multiplying to \(6 \times 4 = 24\) and adding to \(-11\), which are \(-8\) and \(-3\). Splitting the middle term as \(-8xy - 3xy\) and factoring by grouping yields \((2x - y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^3 - 21x^2 - 9x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to obtain \(3x(6x^2 - 7x - 3)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial by grouping to get \(3x(3x + 1)(2x - 3)\).
Find two factors of \(18(10) = 180\) that add to \(-27\), which are \(-15\) and \(-12\). Split the middle term as \(-15m - 12m\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((6m - 5)(3m - 2)\).
Find two factors of \(15(-10) = -150\) that add to \(-19\), which are \(-25\) and \(6\). Split the middle term as \(-25x + 6x\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((3x - 5)(5x + 2)\).
Find two factors of \(14(-25) = -350\) that add to \(-25\), which are \(-35\) and \(10\). Split the middle term as \(-35p + 10p\) and factor by grouping to get \((2p - 5)(7p + 5)\).
Find two factors of \(12(-15) = -180\) that add to \(11\), which are \(20\) and \(-9\). Split the middle term as \(20y - 9y\) and factor by grouping to get \((3y + 5)(4y - 3)\).
Find two factors of \(21(-8) = -168\) that add to \(-22\), which are \(-28\) and \(6\). Split the middle term as \(-28k + 6k\) and factor by grouping to get \((3k - 4)(7k + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(30y^2 - 2y - 56\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to obtain \(2(15y^2 - y - 28)\). Then find factors of \(15(-28) = -420\) that add to \(-1\), which are \(-21\) and \(20\), yielding \(2(5y - 7)(3y + 4)\).
Find two factors of \(28(-18) = -504\) that add to \(-3\), which are \(-24\) and \(21\). Rewrite \(-3ab\) as \(-24ab + 21ab\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((7a - 6b)(4a + 3b)\).
Find two factors of \(15(8) = 120\) that add to \(-26\), which are \(-20\) and \(-6\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-20xy - 6xy\) and factor by grouping to obtain \((3x - 4y)(5x - 2y)\).
Find two factors of \(40(-36) = -1440\) that sum to \(81\), which are \(96\) and \(-15\). Rewrite \(81z\) as \(96z - 15z\) and factor by grouping to get \((5z + 12)(8z - 3)\).
Find factors of \(3(-80) = -240\) that add up to \(-14\), which are \(-24\) and \(10\). Grouping gives \(3y(y - 8) + 10(y - 8) = (3y + 10)(y - 8)\).

Find two numbers whose product is \(2(-70) = -140\) and whose sum is \(-13\), which are \(-20\) and \(7\). Rewrite the middle term and factor by grouping: \(2x^2 - 20x + 7x - 70 = 2x(x - 10) + 7(x - 10) = (2x + 7)(x - 10)\).
Find two integers whose product is \(3(-72) = -216\) and sum is \(19\), which are \(27\) and \(-8\). Factoring by grouping gives \(3w(w + 9) - 8(w + 9) = (3w - 8)(w + 9)\).
Find factors of \(2(-55) = -110\) that sum to \(-17\), which are \(-22\) and \(5\). Grouping gives \(2k(k - 11) + 5(k - 11) = (2k + 5)(k - 11)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^2 - 19x - 36\)
qs.s: The product \(ac = 6(-36) = -216\), and the factors that sum to \(-19\) are \(-27\) and \(8\). Rewrite and factor by grouping: \(6x^2 - 27x + 8x - 36 = 3x(2x - 9) + 4(2x - 9) = (2x - 9)(3x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-15a^4 + 35a^3 + 30a^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-5a^2\) to obtain \(-5a^2(3a^2 - 7a - 6)\). The trinomial factors using numbers that multiply to \(3(-6) = -18\) and add to \(-7\) (\(-9\) and \(2\)), giving \(-5a^2(3a + 2)(a - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 - 26x^2 - 16x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(6x^2 - 13x - 8)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \(6(-8) = -48\) that add to \(-13\) (\(-16\) and \(3\)) to obtain \(2x(2x + 1)(3x - 8)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^2 - 11xy - 15y^2\)
qs.s: Find factors of \(12(-15) = -180\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-20\) and \(9\). Rewrite the middle term to factor by grouping: \(12x^2 - 20xy + 9xy - 15y^2 = 4x(3x - 5y) + 3y(3x - 5y) = (4x + 3y)(3x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(15x^2 - 34x - 16\)
qs.s: The product \(ac = 15(-16) = -240\), and the factors that add to \(-34\) are \(-40\) and \(6\). Factoring by grouping yields \(15x^2 - 40x + 6x - 16 = 5x(3x - 8) + 2(3x - 8) = (5x + 2)(3x - 8)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6x^2 + x - 12\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(ac = 6(-12) = -72\) that sum to \(1\), which are \(9\) and \(-8\). Rewrite as \(6x^2 + 9x - 8x - 12 = 3x(2x + 3) - 4(2x + 3) = (2x + 3)(3x - 4)\).
Find two factors of \(ac = 4(-15) = -60\) that sum to \(-7\), which are \(-12\) and \(5\). Rewrite as \(4y^2 - 12y + 5y - 15 = 4y(y - 3) + 5(y - 3) = (4y + 5)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(9w^2 + 5w - 4\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(ac = 9(-4) = -36\) that sum to \(5\), which are \(9\) and \(-4\). Rewrite as \(9w^2 + 9w - 4w - 4 = 9w(w + 1) - 4(w + 1) = (9w - 4)(w + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(8x^2 + 6x - 9\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(ac = 8(-9) = -72\) that sum to \(6\), which are \(12\) and \(-6\). Rewrite as \(8x^2 + 12x - 6x - 9 = 4x(2x + 3) - 3(2x + 3) = (4x - 3)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(6t^2 + 7t - 5\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(ac = 6(-5) = -30\) that sum to \(7\), which are \(10\) and \(-3\). Rewrite as \(6t^2 + 10t - 3t - 5 = 2t(3t + 5) - 1(3t + 5) = (2t - 1)(3t + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^3 - 26x^2 + 10x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(6x^2 - 13x + 5)\). Factoring the trinomial by finding factors of \(30\) that add to \(-13\) (\(-10\) and \(-3\)) gives \(2x(2x - 1)(3x - 5)\).
Find two factors of \(ac = 12(12) = 144\) that add to \(-25\), which are \(-16\) and \(-9\). Rewrite as \(12x^2 - 16x - 9x + 12 = 4x(3x - 4) - 3(3x - 4) = (4x - 3)(3x - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6x^4 + 11x^2 - 10\)
qs.s: Treat the polynomial as quadratic in \(x^2\). Factors of \(ac = 6(-10) = -60\) that sum to \(11\) are \(15\) and \(-4\), giving \(6x^4 + 15x^2 - 4x^2 - 10 = 3x^2(2x^2 + 5) - 2(2x^2 + 5) = (3x^2 - 2)(2x^2 + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(15x^2 - 11xy - 12y^2\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(ac = 15(-12) = -180\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-20\) and \(9\). Rewrite as \(15x^2 - 20xy + 9xy - 12y^2 = 5x(3x - 4y) + 3y(3x - 4y) = (5x + 3y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^3 + 15x^2 + 18x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to get \(-3x(6x^2 - 5x - 6)\). Then factor \(6x^2 - 5x - 6\) using factors of \(-36\) that sum to \(-5\) (\(-9\) and \(4\)) to reach \(-3x(3x + 2)(2x - 3)\).
Find two numbers whose product is \((8)(-15) = -120\) and whose sum is \(-14\), which are \(-20\) and \(6\). Factor by grouping: \(8m^2 - 20m + 6m - 15 = 4m(2m - 5) + 3(2m - 5) = (2m - 5)(4m + 3)\).
Find two factors of \((6)(-20) = -120\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\). Rewrite the middle term as \(-15x + 8x\) and factor by grouping to get \((2x - 5)(3x + 4)\).
Find two factors of \((6)(12) = 72\) that sum to \(-17\), which are \(-9\) and \(-8\). Factor by grouping: \(6w^2 - 9w - 8w + 12 = 3w(2w - 3) - 4(2w - 3) = (2w - 3)(3w - 4)\).
Find two factors of \((14)(-12) = -168\) that sum to \(-13\), which are \(-21\) and \(8\). Factor by grouping: \(14t^2 - 21t + 8t - 12 = 7t(2t - 3) + 4(2t - 3) = (2t - 3)(7t + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10a^3b - 5a^2b^2 + 30ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5ab\) to get \(-5ab(2a^2 + ab - 6b^2)\). Then factor the trinomial using factors of \((2)(-6) = -12\) that add to \(1\) (\(4\) and \(-3\)) to arrive at \(-5ab(a + 2b)(2a - 3b)\).
Find two factors of \((24)(-35) = -840\) that add to \(-2\), which are \(-30\) and \(28\). Rewrite the trinomial as \(24x^2 - 30x + 28x - 35 = 6x(4x - 5) + 7(4x - 5) = (4x - 5)(6x + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^2 - 23xy + 10y^2\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \((12)(10) = 120\) that sum to \(-23\), which are \(-15\) and \(-8\). Split the middle term and factor by grouping: \(12x^2 - 15xy - 8xy + 10y^2 = 3x(4x - 5y) - 2y(4x - 5y) = (4x - 5y)(3x - 2y)\).

exercises.name: Factor trinomials with negative leading coefficients or common factors

qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(5x^2 - 7x - 6)\). Find two factors of \(5(-6) = -30\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-10\) and \(3\), giving \(-(5x + 3)(x - 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 5x - 2)\). Find two factors of \(3(-2) = -6\) that add to \(-5\), which are \(-6\) and \(1\), yielding \(-(3x + 1)(x - 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 7x + 2)\). Find two factors of \(3(2) = 6\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-6\) and \(-1\), giving \(-(3x - 1)(x - 2)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 - 3x - 5)\). Then find two factors of \(2(-5) = -10\) that add to \(-3\), which are \(-5\) and \(2\), giving \(-(2x - 5)(x + 1)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 + 5x - 3)\). Find two factors of \(2(-3) = -6\) that add to \(5\), which are \(6\) and \(-1\), yielding \(-(2x - 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-10x^2 - 19x + 15\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(10x^2 + 19x - 15)\). Factoring by grouping using \(25\) and \(-6\) (which multiply to \(-150\) and add to \(19\)) gives \(-(2x + 5)(5x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^2 + 16xy - 15y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(4x^2 - 16xy + 15y^2)\). Find factors of \(4(15) = 60\) that sum to \(-16\), which are \(-10\) and \(-6\), giving \(-(2x - 3y)(2x - 5y)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(5x^2 + 13xy + 6y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-(5x + 3y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-2x^2 + 7xy - 3y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 - 7xy + 3y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-(2x - y)(x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-2x^2 + xy + 6y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 - xy - 6y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-(2x + 3y)(x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-3x^2 - 7xy - 2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 + 7xy + 2y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-(3x + y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-3x^2 - 5xy + 2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(3x^2 + 5xy - 2y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-(3x - y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-20x^2y + 18xy^2 + 18y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2y\) to get \(-2y(10x^2 - 9xy - 9y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2y(5x + 3y)(2x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^2 + 23xy - 10y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(12x^2 - 23xy + 10y^2)\). Finding factors of \(120\) that sum to \(-23\) yields \(-(3x - 2y)(4x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^3 + 9x^2y + 15xy^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x\) to obtain \(-3x(2x^2 - 3xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-3x(2x - 5y)(x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3y + 22x^2y^2 - 24xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2xy\) to get \(-2xy(2x^2 - 11xy + 12y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-2xy(2x - 3y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-8x^4y - 14x^3y^2 + 15x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-x^2y\) to get \(-x^2y(8x^2 + 14xy - 15y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial yields \(-x^2y(4x - 3y)(2x + 5y)\).

Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(3x^2 - 10x - 8)\), then find two numbers whose product is \(3(-8) = -24\) and whose sum is \(-10\), which are \(-12\) and \(2\). Factoring by grouping yields \(-(3x + 2)(x - 4)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(4x^2 + 7x - 15)\). Two factors of \(4(-15) = -60\) that sum to \(7\) are \(12\) and \(-5\), giving the factored form \(-(4x - 5)(x + 3)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to rewrite the trinomial as \(-(3x^2 + 11x - 20)\). Find factors of \(3(-20) = -60\) that sum to \(11\), which are \(15\) and \(-4\), yielding \(-(3x - 4)(x + 5)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(2x^2 + 7x - 15)\), then find two factors of \(2(-15) = -30\) that add to \(7\), which are \(10\) and \(-3\). Grouping gives \(-(2x - 3)(x + 5)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(6x^2 - 7x - 5)\). Find factors of \(6(-5) = -30\) that sum to \(-7\), which are \(-10\) and \(3\), giving \(-(2x + 1)(3x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-20x^2 + 34x - 6\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(10x^2 - 17x + 3)\). Then find two factors of \(10(3) = 30\) that add to \(-17\) (\(-15\) and \(-2\)), factoring the quadratic into \(-2(5x - 1)(2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-15x^2 - 19xy + 10y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(15x^2 + 19xy - 10y^2)\). Find two factors of \(15(-10) = -150\) that sum to \(19\), which are \(25\) and \(-6\), factoring by grouping into \(-(5x - 2y)(3x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^4 - 9x^3 + 42x^2\)
qs.s: Remove the common factor \(-3x^2\) to leave \(-3x^2(2x^2 + 3x - 14)\). Then find two factors of \(2(-14) = -28\) that add to \(3\) (\(7\) and \(-4\)), producing the completely factored form \(-3x^2(2x + 7)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^3y + 14x^2y^2 + 8xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2xy\) to get \(-2xy(2x^2 - 7xy - 4y^2)\). Find two numbers whose product is \(2(-4) = -8\) and sum is \(-7\) (\(-8\) and \(1\)), giving \(-2xy(2x + y)(x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3 + 26x^2 - 10x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(6x^2 - 13x + 5)\). Two factors of \(6(5) = 30\) that sum to \(-13\) are \(-10\) and \(-3\), which factors the trinomial into \(-2x(2x - 1)(3x - 5)\).
Factor out -1 to get -(3a^2 + 11ab + 6b^2). Find factors of 3(6) = 18 that add to 11 (9 and 2), giving -(3a + 2b)(a + 3b).
Factor out -1 to get -(2x^2 + 5xy - 12y^2). Find factors of 2(-12) = -24 that add to 5 (8 and -3), resulting in -(2x - 3y)(x + 4y).

qs.q: Factor: \(-4x^2 + 8xy - 3y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out -1 to get -(4x^2 - 8xy + 3y^2). Find factors of 4(3) = 12 that add to -8 (-6 and -2), giving -(2x - y)(2x - 3y).

qs.q: Factor: \(-5x^2 - 8xy + 4y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out -1 to obtain -(5x^2 + 8xy - 4y^2). Find two numbers whose product is 5(-4) = -20 and sum is 8 (10 and -2), which yields -(5x - 2y)(x + 2y).
Factor out -1 to get -(10x^2 - 29xy + 10y^2). Find factors of 10(10) = 100 that add to -29 (-25 and -4), giving -(5x - 2y)(2x - 5y).
Factor out the greatest common factor -2xy^2 to get -2xy^2(2x^2 - xy - 6y^2). Factoring the resulting trinomial yields -2xy^2(2x + 3y)(x - 2y).
Factor out the greatest common factor -3x to obtain -3x(2x^2 - 5xy - 3y^2). Factoring the trinomial inside gives -3x(2x + y)(x - 3y).
Factor out the common factor -2a to get -2a(6a^2 - 11ab - 10b^2). Then factor the quadratic expression to get -2a(3a + 2b)(2a - 5b).
Factor out the greatest common factor -4x^2 to get -4x^2(3x^2 - 7xy - 6y^2). Factoring the trinomial gives -4x^2(3x + 2y)(x - 3y).
Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(12x^2 - 17xy + 6y^2)\). Finding two numbers that multiply to \((12)(6) = 72\) and add to \(-17\) gives \(-9\) and \(-8\), which factors into \(-3(3x - 2y)(4x - 3y)\).
Factor out the common factor \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(12x^2 - 32xy + 5y^2)\). Find factors of \((12)(5) = 60\) that add to \(-32\), which are \(-30\) and \(-2\), giving \(-2(2x - 5y)(6x - y)\).
Factor out \(-4\) to obtain \(-4(6x^2 - 7xy - 20y^2)\). Find factors of \((6)(-20) = -120\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\), leading to \(-4(2x - 5y)(3x + 4y)\).
Factor out \(-6\) to get \(-6(10x^2 - 11xy - 6y^2)\). Find factors of \((10)(-6) = -60\) that sum to \(-11\), which are \(-15\) and \(4\), yielding \(-6(2x - 3y)(5x + 2y)\).
Factor out \(-5\) to get \(-5(6x^2 - 5xy - 6y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial by finding factors of \((6)(-6) = -36\) that sum to \(-5\) gives \(-9\) and \(4\), yielding \(-5(2x - 3y)(3x + 2y)\).
Factor out \(-6\) to obtain \(-6(21x^2 - 47xy + 20y^2)\). Find factors of \((21)(20) = 420\) that add to \(-47\), which are \(-35\) and \(-12\), giving \(-6(3x - 5y)(7x - 4y)\).

Factor out the common monomial \(-6xy\) to obtain \(-6xy(12x^2 - 23xy + 10y^2)\). Factoring the remaining trinomial with factors of \((12)(10) = 120\) that add to \(-23\) (\(-15\) and \(-8\)) yields \(-6xy(3x - 2y)(4x - 5y)\).
Factor out \(-5x^3\) to get \(-5x^3(12x^2 - x - 20)\). Find factors of \((12)(-20) = -240\) that add to \(-1\), which are \(-16\) and \(15\), yielding \(-5x^3(3x - 4)(4x + 5)\).

Factor out the common factor \(-4x^2y\) to leave \(-4x^2y(6x^2 + xy - 35y^2)\). Find factors of \((6)(-35) = -210\) that add to \(1\), which are \(15\) and \(-14\), giving \(-4x^2y(2x + 5y)(3x - 7y)\).

Factor out the greatest common factor \(-8\) to get \(-8(20x^2 + 11xy - 42y^2)\). Find factors of \((20)(-42) = -840\) that sum to \(11\), which are \(35\) and \(-24\), yielding \(-8(4x + 7y)(5x - 6y)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2\), giving \(-2(16x^2 - 24xy + 9y^2)\). Since \(16x^2 - 24xy + 9y^2\) is a perfect square trinomial, the complete factorization is \(-2(4x - 3y)^2\).
Factor out the common factor of \(-2\) to get \(-2(6x^2 + 17xy + 12y^2)\). Finding factors of \(6 \times 12 = 72\) that sum to \(17\) gives \(8\) and \(9\), yielding \(-2(2x + 3y)(3x + 4y)\).

Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-5\), to get \(-5(6x^2 + 5xy - 4y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping with factors of \(-24\) that sum to \(5\) (\(8\) and \(-3\)) produces \(-5(2x - y)(3x + 4y)\).
Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(25x^2 + 20xy + 4y^2)\). Recognizing the remaining trinomial as a perfect square yields \(-3(5x + 2y)^2\).
Factor out the greatest common factor, \(-2\), to obtain \(-2(9x^2 + 30xy + 25y^2)\). The trinomial is a perfect square, factoring into \(-2(3x + 5y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-30x^4 - 25x^3y + 30x^2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor of \(-5x^2\) to obtain \(-5x^2(6x^2 + 5xy - 6y^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-5x^2(2x + 3y)(3x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18a^3b^2 + 33a^2b^3 + 30ab^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3ab^2\) to yield \(-3ab^2(6a^2 - 11ab - 10b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping gives \(-3ab^2(2a - 5b)(3a + 2b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24x^3y - 28x^2y^2 + 80xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the monomial greatest common factor, \(-4xy\), leaving \(-4xy(6x^2 + 7xy - 20y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial using factors of \(6 \times (-20) = -120\) that add to \(7\) (\(15\) and \(-8\)) yields \(-4xy(2x + 5y)(3x - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-144x^2 - 132xy + 210y^2\)
qs.s: Remove the common factor of \(-6\) to get \(-6(24x^2 + 22xy - 35y^2)\). Finding factors of \(24 \times (-35) = -840\) that sum to \(22\) (\(42\) and \(-20\)) allows factoring by grouping into \(-6(4x + 7y)(6x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-60x^2 + 117xy - 54y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(20x^2 - 39xy + 18y^2)\). Two negative factors of \(20 \times 18 = 360\) that sum to \(-39\) are \(-24\) and \(-15\), giving the factorization \(-3(4x - 3y)(5x - 6y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-4x^2 - 7xy + 2y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(4x^2 + 7xy - 2y^2)\), then factor the trinomial by finding factors of \((4)(-2) = -8\) that add to \(7\), giving \(-(4x - y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-15u^2 - uv + 2v^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(15u^2 + uv - 2v^2)\), then factor the trinomial using factors of \(-30\) that add to \(1\) (\(6\) and \(-5\)) to get \(-(3u - v)(5u + 2v)\).
Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(10x^2 - 11xy - 6y^2)\), then split the middle term using factors of \(-60\) that sum to \(-11\) (\(-15\) and \(4\)) to get \(-(5x + 2y)(2x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-6m^2 - 7mn + 5n^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6m^2 + 7mn - 5n^2)\), and then factor the trinomial into \(-(2m - n)(3m + 5n)\) using factors of \(-30\) that add to \(7\) (\(10\) and \(-3\)).
Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(8p^2 - 14pq + 3q^2)\), then find two numbers whose product is \(24\) and sum is \(-14\) (\(-12\) and \(-2\)) to obtain \(-(4p - q)(2p - 3q)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-16a^3b + 28a^2b^2 + 30ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2ab\) to get \(-2ab(8a^2 - 14ab - 15b^2)\), then find factors of \((8)(-15) = -120\) that add to \(-14\) (\(-20\) and \(6\)) to obtain \(-2ab(4a + 3b)(2a - 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^2 + 25xy - 12y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(12x^2 - 25xy + 12y^2)\), then use factors of \((12)(12) = 144\) that add to \(-25\) (\(-16\) and \(-9\)) to factor by grouping into \(-(3x - 4y)(4x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3 - 26x^2y + 10xy^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(6x^2 + 13xy - 5y^2)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((3x - y)(2x + 5y)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-a\) to obtain \(-a(3a^2 + 10ab - 8b^2)\). Factoring the resulting trinomial gives \(-a(a + 4b)(3a - 2b)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2y\) to get \(-2y(2x^2 + 5xy - 3y^2)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-2y(x + 3y)(2x - y)\).
Remove the common factor \(-n\) to yield \(-n(4m^2 - 8mn - 5n^2)\). Factoring the trinomial produces \(-n(2m + n)(2m - 5n)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(-6u^2v - uv^2 + 2v^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-v\) to get \(-v(6u^2 + uv - 2v^2)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-v(2u - v)(3u + 2v)\).
Factor out \(-y\) to get \(-y(6x^2 - 7xy - 3y^2)\). Then find factors of \(6 \times (-3) = -18\) that add to \(-7\), which gives \(-y(2x - 3y)(3x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-15x^3y + 34x^2y^2 - 16xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-xy\) to get \(-xy(15x^2 - 34xy + 16y^2)\). Since \((-24) \times (-10) = 240\) and \((-24) + (-10) = -34\), the trinomial factors as \((3x - 2y)(5x - 8y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^4y - 26x^3y^2 + 10x^2y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-2x^2y\) to leave \(-2x^2y(6x^2 + 13xy - 5y^2)\). Factoring by grouping with \(15xy - 2xy\) produces \(-2x^2y(2x + 5y)(3x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-36x^3y^2 + 42x^2y^3 + 120xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(-6xy^2\) to get \(-6xy^2(6x^2 - 7xy - 20y^2)\). Factoring the trinomial using factors of \(-120\) that add to \(-7\) yields \(-6xy^2(2x - 5y)(3x + 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-8a^4b^2 - 22a^3b^3 + 21a^2b^4\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-a^2b^2\) to get \(-a^2b^2(8a^2 + 22ab - 21b^2)\). Factoring the trinomial using factors of \(8 \times (-21) = -168\) that sum to \(22\) (\(28\) and \(-6\)) gives \(-a^2b^2(2a + 7b)(4a - 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^2(y + 2)^3 + 3x(y + 2)^3 - 2(y + 2)^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((y + 2)^3\) to get \((y + 2)^3(9x^2 + 3x - 2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial to obtain \((y + 2)^3(3x + 2)(3x - 1)\).
Factor out \((k + 5)^3\) to obtain \((k + 5)^3(10x^2 + 11x - 6)\). Then factor the quadratic into \((2x + 3)(5x - 2)\) to give \((k + 5)^3(2x + 3)(5x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6y^2(b + 1)^4 + 7y(b + 1)^4 - 3(b + 1)^4\)
qs.s: Factor out \((b + 1)^4\) to get \((b + 1)^4(6y^2 + 7y - 3)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \((b + 1)^4(2y + 3)(3y - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12m^2(p - 2)^3 - 5m(p - 2)^3 - 2(p - 2)^3\)
qs.s: Factor out \((p - 2)^3\) to get \((p - 2)^3(12m^2 - 5m - 2)\). Factor the remaining quadratic trinomial into \((3m - 2)(4m + 1)\) for a complete factorization of \((p - 2)^3(3m - 2)(4m + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^2(x - 3)^2 - 8a(x - 3)^2 - 5(x - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((x - 3)^2\) to obtain \((x - 3)^2(4a^2 - 8a - 5)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial results in \((x - 3)^2(2a + 1)(2a - 5)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x(2y - 1)^2\) to obtain \(2x(2y - 1)^2(6x^2 - 13x + 5)\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(2x(2y - 1)^2(2x - 1)(3x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(20x^2 y(2a - b)^3 - 23xy^2(2a - b)^3 + 6y^3(2a - b)^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(y(2a - b)^3\) to leave \(20x^2 - 23xy + 6y^2\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping produces \(y(2a - b)^3(4x - 3y)(5x - 2y)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-6x(w + 1)^3\) to leave \(8x^2 - 14x - 15\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial yields \(-6x(w + 1)^3(2x - 5)(4x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-6x^2 y(a + 2b)^3 + 21xy^2(a + 2b)^3 - 15y^3(a + 2b)^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3y(a + 2b)^3\) to leave \(2x^2 - 7xy + 5y^2\). Factoring this two-variable trinomial results in \(-3y(a + 2b)^3(x - y)(2x - 5y)\).

Factor out \((c - 2)^5\) to leave the quadratic-form polynomial \(9x^4 - 37x^2 + 4\), which factors into \((x^2 - 4)(9x^2 - 1)\). Factoring both differences of squares gives \((c - 2)^5(x - 2)(x + 2)(3x - 1)(3x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2(a - 3)^2 + 7x(a - 3)^2 - 3(a - 3)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-(a - 3)^2\) to obtain \(-(a - 3)^2(2x^2 - 7x + 3)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((2x - 1)(x - 3)\) to get \(-(a - 3)^2(2x - 1)(x - 3)\).
Factor out \(-(p - 5)^2\) to leave \(-(p - 5)^2(2t^2 + 5t - 12)\). Factor the trinomial to obtain \(-(p - 5)^2(2t - 3)(t + 4)\).
Factor out \(-(k + 2)^2\) to leave \(-(k + 2)^2(5m^2 + 13m - 6)\). Factoring the trinomial by finding factors of \(-30\) that add to \(13\) gives \(-(k + 2)^2(5m - 2)(m + 3)\).
Factor out \(-(w + 4)^2\) to get \(-(w + 4)^2(3a^2 - 11a + 6)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((3a - 2)(a - 3)\), resulting in \(-(w + 4)^2(3a - 2)(a - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^2(y - 1)^2 - 4x(y - 1)^2 + 3(y - 1)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-(y - 1)^2\) to yield \(-(y - 1)^2(4x^2 + 4x - 3)\). Factoring the quadratic expression gives \(-(y - 1)^2(2x - 1)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-2x^2(y + 3)^2 - 7xy(y + 3)^2 + 15y^2(y + 3)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-(y + 3)^2\) to yield \(-(y + 3)^2(2x^2 + 7xy - 15y^2)\), then factor the two-variable trinomial into \((2x - 3y)(x + 5y)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x(y - 2)^2\) to obtain \(-3x(y - 2)^2(2x^2 - 5x - 3)\). Factoring \(2x^2 - 5x - 3\) completely gives \(-3x(y - 2)^2(2x + 1)(x - 3)\).

Factor out \(-(a + 1)^2\) to obtain \(-(a + 1)^2(3x^4 - 11x^2 - 4)\), factor in quadratic form as \(-(a + 1)^2(3x^2 + 1)(x^2 - 4)\), and finally factor the difference of squares into \((x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^5(m - 4)^2 + 10x^3(m - 4)^2 - 9x(m - 4)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-x(m - 4)^2\) to obtain \(-x(m - 4)^2(x^4 - 10x^2 + 9) = -x(m - 4)^2(x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 9)\), then apply the difference of squares to both factors to reach \(-x(m - 4)^2(x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).
Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x(2y - 1)^3\) to get \(-2x(2y - 1)^3(4x^2 + 7x - 2)\), then factor the trinomial into \((4x - 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor: \(1 + x - 72x^2\)
qs.s: Find two factors of \(-72\) that add to \(1\), which are \(9\) and \(-8\). Thus, \(1 + x - 72x^2 = (1 + 9x)(1 - 8x)\).
Find two factors of \(-42\) that add to \(-11\), which are \(-14\) and \(3\). Thus, \(1 - 11x - 42x^2 = (1 - 14x)(1 + 3x)\).
Find two factors of \(-36\) that add to \(-5\), which are \(-9\) and \(4\). Thus, \(1 - 5x - 36x^2 = (1 - 9x)(1 + 4x)\).
Find two factors of \(-45\) that add to \(4\), which are \(9\) and \(-5\). Thus, \(1 + 4x - 45x^2 = (1 + 9x)(1 - 5x)\).
Find two factors of \(-48\) that add to \(-2\), which are \(-8\) and \(6\). Thus, \(1 - 2x - 48x^2 = (1 - 8x)(1 + 6x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - 9x^3 - 90x^6\)
qs.s: Treat the expression in quadratic form with variable \(x^3\), and find two factors of \(-90\) that add to \(-9\), which are \(-15\) and \(6\). This factors directly into \((1 - 15x^3)(1 + 6x^3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - 3(x + 2y) - 28(x + 2y)^2\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x + 2y\) so the expression becomes \(1 - 3u - 28u^2 = (1 - 7u)(1 + 4u)\). Substituting \(x + 2y\) back for \(u\) and expanding gives \((1 - 7x - 14y)(1 + 4x + 8y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2a - 3) - 5x(2a - 3) - 24x^2(2a - 3)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((2a - 3)\) to get \((2a - 3)(1 - 5x - 24x^2)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial into \((1 - 8x)(1 + 3x)\), resulting in \((2a - 3)(1 - 8x)(1 + 3x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6 - 7x - 20x^2\)
qs.s: Find two numbers whose product is \(6(-20) = -120\) and whose sum is \(-7\), which are \(-15\) and \(8\). Rewrite the expression as \(6 - 15x + 8x - 20x^2 = 3(2 - 5x) + 4x(2 - 5x) = (2 - 5x)(3 + 4x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3y - 21xy - 90x^2y\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3y\) to get \(3y(1 - 7x - 30x^2)\). Then find two factors of \(-30\) that add to \(-7\), which are \(-10\) and \(3\), giving \(3y(1 - 10x)(1 + 3x)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 20x^2 + 64\)
qs.s: Factoring the trinomial in quadratic form gives \((x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 16)\). Applying the difference of squares to both factors completely yields \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 13x^2 + 36\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\) to write the expression as \(u^2 - 13u + 36 = (u - 4)(u - 9)\). Substituting \(x^2\) back in gives \((x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 9)\), which factors by difference of squares into \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25 - 26x^2 + x^4\)
qs.s: Rearranging the polynomial as \(x^4 - 26x^2 + 25\) allows it to factor into \((x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 25)\), which then factors by difference of squares into \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x - 5)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16 - 17y^2 + y^4\)
qs.s: Rewriting in descending powers gives \(y^4 - 17y^2 + 16 = (y^2 - 1)(y^2 - 16)\). Factoring each difference of squares yields \((y - 1)(y + 1)(y - 4)(y + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 29x^2 + 100\)
qs.s: In quadratic form, the expression factors into \((x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 25)\). Factoring each difference of squares results in \((x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 5)(x + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 29x^2y^2 + 100y^4\)
qs.s: Factoring the homogeneous trinomial in quadratic form gives \((x^2 - 4y^2)(x^2 - 25y^2)\). Each factor is a difference of squares, giving \((x - 2y)(x + 2y)(x - 5y)(x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 17x^2 + 4\)
qs.s: Using the \(ac\)-method on the quadratic form gives \((4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring both differences of squares yields \((2x - 1)(2x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 37x^2y^2 + 9y^4\)
qs.s: Using the \(ac\)-method on \(4(x^2)^2 - 37(x^2)(y^2) + 9(y^2)^2\) yields \((4x^2 - y^2)(x^2 - 9y^2)\), which factors by difference of squares into \((2x - y)(2x + y)(x - 3y)(x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^5 - 39x^3 + 108x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(x^4 - 13x^2 + 36)\), which factors as \(3x(x^2 - 4)(x^2 - 9)\) and completely as \(3x(x - 2)(x + 2)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9 - 13x^2 + 4x^4\)
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(4x^4 - 13x^2 + 9 = (x^2 - 1)(4x^2 - 9)\). Applying the difference of squares to both factors yields \((x - 1)(x + 1)(2x - 3)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^4 - 5x^2 - 4\)
qs.s: Factoring the quadratic form gives \((9x^2 + 4)(x^2 - 1)\). Then, factoring the difference of squares \(x^2 - 1\) results in \((9x^2 + 4)(x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5x^4 - 11x^2 - 36\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\) to rewrite the trinomial as \(5u^2 - 11u - 36 = (5u + 9)(u - 4)\). Substituting \(x^2\) back in yields \((5x^2 + 9)(x^2 - 4)\), and factoring the difference of squares gives \((5x^2 + 9)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^4 + 5x^2 - 7\)
qs.s: Treat the polynomial as a quadratic in \(x^2\) to factor it as \((2x^2 + 7)(x^2 - 1)\). Factoring the difference of squares \(x^2 - 1\) gives \((2x^2 + 7)(x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 + 11x^2 - 45\)
qs.s: Factoring in quadratic form gives \((x^2 + 5)(4x^2 - 9)\). Factoring the second binomial as a difference of squares yields \((x^2 + 5)(2x - 3)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 31x^2 - 45\)
qs.s: Using quadratic form with \(u = x^2\), factor \(4u^2 - 31u - 45\) into \((4u + 5)(u - 9)\). Replacing \(u\) with \(x^2\) and factoring the difference of squares \(x^2 - 9\) produces \((4x^2 + 5)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 37x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Factoring in quadratic form produces \((4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 9)\). Since both factors are differences of squares, factoring each completely yields \((2x - 1)(2x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^5 - 68x^3 + 16x\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(4x\) to obtain \(4x(4x^4 - 17x^2 + 4) = 4x(4x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring both differences of squares gives \(4x(2x - 1)(2x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^4 - 11x^2 - 36\)
qs.s: Factor the quadratic form trinomial into \((3x^2 + 4)(4x^2 - 9)\) using factors of \(12 \times (-36) = -432\) that add to \(-11\). Then factor the difference of squares \(4x^2 - 9\) to obtain \((3x^2 + 4)(2x - 3)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5x^4 - 19x^2 y^2 - 4y^4\)
qs.s: Treat the expression as quadratic in \(x^2\) and \(y^2\) to factor it as \((5x^2 + y^2)(x^2 - 4y^2)\). Factoring the difference of squares \(x^2 - 4y^2\) gives \((5x^2 + y^2)(x - 2y)(x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(24x^5 + 54x^3 - 15x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(8x^4 + 18x^2 - 5) = 3x(2x^2 + 5)(4x^2 - 1)\). Then factor the difference of squares \(4x^2 - 1\) to get \(3x(2x^2 + 5)(2x - 1)(2x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^4 - 82x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(u = x^2\) to write the expression as \(9u^2 - 82u + 9 = (9u - 1)(u - 9) = (9x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 9)\). Applying the difference of squares to each factor gives \((3x - 1)(3x + 1)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^4 - 37x^2 + 4\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^2\); then \(9u^2 - 37u + 4 = (9u - 1)(u - 4) = (9x^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring both factors via difference of squares gives \((3x - 1)(3x + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 - 25x^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(u = x^2\) to get \(16u^2 - 25u + 9 = (16u - 9)(u - 1) = (16x^2 - 9)(x^2 - 1)\). Factoring completely using differences of squares gives \((4x - 3)(4x + 3)(x - 1)(x + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 25x^2 + 36\)
qs.s: Using \(u = x^2\), factor \(4u^2 - 25u + 36\) as \((4u - 9)(u - 4) = (4x^2 - 9)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring each factor as a difference of squares yields \((2x - 3)(2x + 3)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 - 40x^2 y^2 + 9y^4\)
qs.s: Factoring the quadratic form in two variables gives \((4x^2 - 9y^2)(4x^2 - y^2)\). Each factor is a difference of squares, resulting in \((2x - 3y)(2x + 3y)(2x - y)(2x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^5 y - 26x^3 y^3 + 8x y^5\)
qs.s: Factor out the GCF \(2xy\) to get \(2xy(9x^4 - 13x^2 y^2 + 4y^4) = 2xy(9x^2 - 4y^2)(x^2 - y^2)\). Factoring each difference of squares yields \(2xy(3x - 2y)(3x + 2y)(x - y)(x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 - 17x^4 + 16\)
qs.s: Factoring as a quadratic in \(x^4\) gives \((x^4 - 16)(x^4 - 1) = (x^2 - 4)(x^2 + 4)(x^2 - 1)(x^2 + 1)\). Factoring the remaining differences of squares completely yields \((x - 1)(x + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)(x^2 + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^5 - 75x^3 + 108x\)
qs.s: First factor out the GCF \(3x\) to obtain \(3x(4x^4 - 25x^2 + 36)\). Then factor the quadratic form into \(3x(4x^2 - 9)(x^2 - 4)\) and apply difference of squares to both binomials to get \(3x(2x - 3)(2x + 3)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36x^4 - 97x^2 + 36\)
qs.s: Using the ac-method on \(36u^2 - 97u + 36\) with \(ac = 1296 = (-81)(-16)\) gives \((9u - 4)(4u - 9) = (9x^2 - 4)(4x^2 - 9)\). Both factors are differences of squares, giving \((3x - 2)(3x + 2)(2x - 3)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((u^2 - v^2)w^2 - 4(u^2 - v^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((u^2 - v^2)\) to obtain \((u^2 - v^2)(w^2 - 4)\). Then factor each difference of squares completely to arrive at \((u - v)(u + v)(w - 2)(w + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((m^2 - 25)c^2 - 16(m^2 - 25)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((m^2 - 25)\) to get \((m^2 - 25)(c^2 - 16)\). Factoring each difference of squares yields \((m - 5)(m + 5)(c - 4)(c + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((p^2 - 1)k^2 - 36(p^2 - 1)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((p^2 - 1)\) to get \((p^2 - 1)(k^2 - 36)\). Then factor each difference of squares to obtain \((p - 1)(p + 1)(k - 6)(k + 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 4)y^2 - (x^2 - 4)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((x^2 - 4)\) to obtain \((x^2 - 4)(y^2 - 1)\). Then factor both differences of squares to get \((x - 2)(x + 2)(y - 1)(y + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((a^2 - b^2)x^2 - 9(a^2 - b^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial factor \((a^2 - b^2)\) to obtain \((a^2 - b^2)(x^2 - 9)\). Then factor each difference of squares completely to get \((a - b)(a + b)(x - 3)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^2 x^2 - n^2 x^2 - 16m^2 + 16n^2\)
qs.s: Group terms to get \(x^2(m^2 - n^2) - 16(m^2 - n^2) = (m^2 - n^2)(x^2 - 16)\). Factoring both differences of squares gives \((m - n)(m + n)(x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 9)y^2 - 5(x^2 - 9)y + 6(x^2 - 9)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common binomial \((x^2 - 9)\) to get \((x^2 - 9)(y^2 - 5y + 6)\). Then factor \((x^2 - 9)\) into \((x - 3)(x + 3)\) and \((y^2 - 5y + 6)\) into \((y - 2)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^4 - y^4)a^2 - (x^4 - y^4)\)

qs.s: Factor out \((a^2 - 25)\) to get \((a^2 - 25)(2x^2 + 5x - 3)\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((a - 5)(a + 5)\) and factoring the trinomial gives \((2x - 1)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^3(y^2 - 1) - 8x(y^2 - 1)\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x(y^2 - 1)\) to obtain \(2x(y^2 - 1)(x^2 - 4)\). Factoring both differences of squares yields \(2x(y - 1)(y + 1)(x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)x^2 - 16(a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)\) to get \((a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)(x^2 - 16)\). Then factor \((a^2 + 10ab + 25b^2)\) into \((a + 5b)^2\) and \((x^2 - 16)\) into \((x - 4)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 12xy + 36y^2)z^2 - 25(x^2 - 12xy + 36y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common polynomial \((x^2 - 12xy + 36y^2)\) to leave \((x^2 - 12xy + 36y^2)(z^2 - 25)\). Factor the trinomial to \((x - 6y)^2\) and the difference of squares to \((z - 5)(z + 5)\), giving \((x - 6y)^2(z - 5)(z + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2)b^2 - 9(x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2)\) to obtain \((x^2 - 4xy + 4y^2)(b^2 - 9)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \((x - 2y)^2\) and factoring the difference of squares gives \((b - 3)(b + 3)\), resulting in \((x - 2y)^2(b - 3)(b + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((m^2 - 8mn + 16n^2)y^2 - (m^2 - 8mn + 16n^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out \((m^2 - 8mn + 16n^2)\) to leave \((m^2 - 8mn + 16n^2)(y^2 - 1)\). Factor the trinomial as \((m - 4n)^2\) and the difference of squares as \((y - 1)(y + 1)\), yielding \((m - 4n)^2(y - 1)(y + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((u^2 + 2uv + v^2)c^2 - 49(u^2 + 2uv + v^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((u^2 + 2uv + v^2)\) to obtain \((u^2 + 2uv + v^2)(c^2 - 49)\). Then factor \((u^2 + 2uv + v^2)\) as \((u + v)^2\) and \((c^2 - 49)\) as \((c - 7)(c + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2)a^2 - 16(2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out \((2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2)\) to get \((2x^2 + 7xy + 3y^2)(a^2 - 16)\). Factoring the non-monic trinomial yields \((2x + y)(x + 3y)\) and factoring the difference of squares yields \((a - 4)(a + 4)\), giving \((2x + y)(x + 3y)(a - 4)(a + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2a^3(x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2) - 32a(x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2a(x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2)\) to get \(2a(x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2)(a^2 - 16)\). Then factor \((x^2 + 10xy + 25y^2)\) as \((x + 5y)^2\) and \((a^2 - 16)\) as \((a - 4)(a + 4)\), giving \(2a(x + 5y)^2(a - 4)(a + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^2(4x^2 - 20xy + 25y^2) - 9(4x^2 - 20xy + 25y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((4x^2 - 20xy + 25y^2)\) to obtain \((4x^2 - 20xy + 25y^2)(4a^2 - 9)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial as \((2x - 5y)^2\) and the difference of squares as \((2a - 3)(2a + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)a^2 - 5(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)a - 14(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)\) from all three terms to get \((x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2)(a^2 - 5a - 14)\). Factoring both trinomials completely gives \((x - 3y)^2(a - 7)(a + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)m^4 - 81(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)\) to obtain \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)(m^4 - 81)\). The trinomial factors as \((x - 4y)^2\), and factoring \(m^4 - 81\) completely requires factoring the difference of squares twice: \((m^2 + 9)(m^2 - 9) = (m^2 + 9)(m - 3)(m + 3)\).

qs.q: Find the positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(7x^2 + kx + 1\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors if \(k\) is the sum of two factors of \(ac = 7(1) = 7\). The only positive sum from the factor pairs of \(7\) is \(7 + 1 = 8\).

qs.q: Find the positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kx - 1\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors if \(k\) is the sum of two factors of \(ac = 2(-1) = -2\). The only positive sum from the factor pairs of \(-2\) is \(2 + (-1) = 1\).

qs.q: Find the positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(5x^2 + kx - 1\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors if \(k\) is the sum of two factors of \(ac = 5(-1) = -5\). The only positive sum from the factor pairs of \(-5\) is \(5 + (-1) = 4\).

qs.q: Find the sum of all positive integer values of \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(3x^2 + kx - 4\)
qs.s: The factor pairs of \(ac = -12\) that yield positive sums are \((12, -1)\), \((6, -2)\), and \((4, -3)\), giving \(k = 11, 4,\) and \(1\). Their sum is \(11 + 4 + 1 = 16\).

qs.q: How many positive integer values of \(k\) allow the trinomial \(2x^2 + kx - 15\) to be factored?
qs.s: Each positive integer \(k\) corresponds to the positive difference of a factor pair of \(|ac| = 30\). Since \(30\) has four distinct factor pairs (\((1, 30), (2, 15), (3, 10), (5, 6)\)), there are \(4\) positive integer values of \(k\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(3x^2 + kx - 8\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors if \(k\) is the sum of two integer factors of \(ac = 3(-8) = -24\). The factor pair with the greatest sum is \(24\) and \(-1\), which gives \(k = 24 + (-1) = 23\).

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(5x^2 + kx - 12\)
qs.s: The value of \(k\) must be the sum of two factors of \(ac = 5(-12) = -60\). The factor pair of \(-60\) with the smallest positive sum is \(10\) and \(-6\), which gives \(k = 10 + (-6) = 4\).

qs.q: Find the greatest negative integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kx - 9\)
qs.s: The negative values of \(k\) are the sums of the factor pairs of \(ac = -18\): \(1 - 18 = -17\), \(2 - 9 = -7\), and \(3 - 6 = -3\). The greatest among these negative values is \(-3\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kx - 11\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -11\). The factor pairs give \(k = 2q + p \in \{-21, -9, 9, 21\}\), so the greatest integer is \(21\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(3x^2 + kx - 2\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((3x + p)(x + q)\) with integers satisfying \(pq = -2\). Testing the factor pairs \((-1, 2)\), \((1, -2)\), \((-2, 1)\), and \((2, -1)\) yields \(k = 3q + p \in \{-5, -1, 1, 5\}\), so the greatest integer is \(5\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kx - 7\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2x + p)(x + q)\) where \(pq = -7\). Testing the factor pairs \((-1, 7)\), \((1, -7)\), \((-7, 1)\), and \((7, -1)\) gives \(k = 2q + p \in \{-13, -5, 5, 13\}\), so the greatest integer is \(13\).

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(5x^2 + kx - 3\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((5x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -3\). The factor pairs give possible values \(k = 5q + p \in \{-14, -2, 2, 14\}\), of which the smallest positive value is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(4x^2 + kx - 15\)
qs.s: Factoring as \((4x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -15\) yields positive odd values \(k \in \{7, 11, 17, 59\}\), while factoring as \((2x + p)(2x + q)\) yields positive even values \(k \in \{4, 28\}\). The smallest positive integer is therefore \(4\).

qs.q: Find the sum of all positive integers \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kxy - 15y^2\)
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2x + py)(x + qy)\) with \(pq = -15\), which yields positive values \(k = 2(15) - 1 = 29\), \(k = 2(-1) + 15 = 13\), \(k = 2(5) - 3 = 7\), and \(k = 2(3) - 5 = 1\). The sum of these values is \(29 + 13 + 7 + 1 = 50\).

qs.q: Find the sum of all positive integers \(k\) so that the trinomial can be factored: \(2x^2 + kx - 9\)
qs.s: Factoring as \((2x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -9\) yields the positive values \(k = 2(9) - 1 = 17\), \(k = 2(-1) + 9 = 7\), and \(k = 2(3) - 3 = 3\). Their sum is \(17 + 7 + 3 = 27\).

qs.q: How many positive integer values of \(k\) are there so that the trinomial can be factored: \(4x^2 + kx - 5\)?
qs.s: Factoring as \((4x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = -5\) gives positive values \(k = 19\) and \(k = 1\), while factoring as \((2x + p)(2x + q)\) gives \(k = 8\). Thus, there are exactly \(3\) positive integer values of \(k\).

qs.q: How many integer values of \(k\) are there so that the trinomial can be factored: \(3x^2 + kx - 8\)?
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((3x + p)(x + q)\) where \(pq = -8\). The four factor pairs \((\pm 1, \mp 8)\), \((\pm 8, \mp 1)\), \((\pm 2, \mp 4)\), and \((\pm 4, \mp 2)\) produce \(8\) distinct integer values: \(k \in \{\pm 2, \pm 5, \pm 10, \pm 23\}\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2m^2 + km - 3\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((2m + a)(m + b)\) requires \(ab = -3\), giving \(k = 2b + a\). Choosing \(b = 3\) and \(a = -1\) maximizes the middle coefficient to \(2(3) + (-1) = 5\).

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(3p^2 + kp - 5\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((3p + a)(p + b)\) requires \(ab = -5\), giving \(k = 3b + a\). The possible integer values of \(k\) are \(-14, -2, 2,\) and \(14\), of which the smallest positive value is 2.

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(3y^2 + ky + 7\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((3y + m)(y + n)\) with \(mn = 7\) gives \(k = 3n + m\). The positive factor pairs \((1, 7)\) and \((7, 1)\) yield \(k = 3(7) + 1 = 22\) and \(k = 3(1) + 7 = 10\), so the smallest positive integer is 10.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2x^2 + kx + 5\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2x + m)(x + n)\) where \(mn = 5\), giving \(k = 2n + m\). Testing the positive factor pairs \((m, n) = (1, 5)\) and \((5, 1)\) gives \(k = 11\) and \(k = 7\), so the greatest integer is 11.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2t^2 + kt + 7\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((2t + m)(t + n)\) requires \(mn = 7\), giving \(k = 2n + m\). Testing the positive pairs \((1, 7)\) and \((7, 1)\) gives \(k = 2(7) + 1 = 15\) and \(k = 2(1) + 7 = 9\), so the greatest integer is 15.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(8x^2 + kxy - 3y^2\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((rx + py)(sx + qy)\) with \(rs = 8\) and \(pq = -3\), \(k = rq + sp\) is maximized by choosing \(s = 8, r = 1, p = 3\), and \(q = -1\). This gives \(k = 8(3) + 1(-1) = 23\).

qs.q: How many positive integer values of \(k\) are there so that the trinomial \(6x^2 + kx + 5\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients?
qs.s: Factoring as \((rx + p)(sx + q)\) with positive integers, the factor pairs of 6 are \((1, 6)\) and \((2, 3)\), and the only pair for 5 is \((1, 5)\). This yields four distinct positive values: \(1(5)+6(1)=11\), \(1(1)+6(5)=31\), \(2(5)+3(1)=13\), and \(2(1)+3(5)=17\).

qs.q: What is the sum of all positive integer values of \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2x^2 + kx + 9\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients?
qs.s: Factoring as \((2x + p)(x + q)\) with \(pq = 9\) gives \(k = 2q + p\). The positive pairs \((p, q) = (1, 9), (9, 1),\) and \((3, 3)\) give \(k = 19, 11,\) and \(9\), whose sum is \(19 + 11 + 9 = 39\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(6x^2 + kx - 5\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((rx + p)(sx + q)\) with \(rs = 6\) and \(pq = -5\), the maximum value of \(k = rq + sp\) occurs when \(\{r, s\} = \{1, 6\}\) with \(s = 6, p = 5\), and \(q = -1\). This gives \(k = 6(5) + 1(-1) = 29\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(4x^2 + kx - 9\) can be factored into binomials with integer coefficients.
qs.s: Factoring as \((rx + p)(sx + q)\) with \(rs = 4\) and \(pq = -9\), the maximum occurs with \(s = 4, r = 1, p = 9\), and \(q = -1\). This gives \(k = 4(9) + 1(-1) = 35\).

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(3w^2 + kw + 2\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((3w + p)(w + q)\) where \(pq = 2\). The possible positive values of \(k\) are \(3(2) + 1 = 7\) and \(3(1) + 2 = 5\), giving a maximum integer value of 7.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2x^2 + kx + 9\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2x + p)(x + q)\) where \(pq = 9\). The pairs of positive factors of 9 give \(k = 2(9) + 1 = 19\), \(k = 2(1) + 9 = 11\), and \(k = 2(3) + 3 = 9\), so the greatest value is 19.

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(2n^2 + kn + 11\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((2n + p)(n + q)\) where \(pq = 11\). The positive values of \(k\) are \(2(11) + 1 = 23\) and \(2(1) + 11 = 13\), so the smallest positive value is 13.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(3x^2 + kx - 5\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((3x + p)(x + q)\) where \(pq = -5\). Testing the factor pairs \((-1, 5)\) and \((5, -1)\) yields \(k = 3(5) - 1 = 14\) and \(k = 3(-1) + 5 = 2\), so the greatest integer is 14.

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(5y^2 + ky + 4\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial factors as \((5y + p)(y + q)\) where \(pq = 4\). The possible positive values for \(k\) are \(5(4) + 1 = 21\), \(5(1) + 4 = 9\), and \(5(2) + 2 = 12\), making 9 the smallest positive integer.

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(6x^2 + kxy - 7y^2\) can be factored.
qs.s: The factorization can take the form \((6x + py)(x + qy)\) or \((3x + py)(2x + qy)\) where \(pq = -7\). The possible positive values for \(k\) are \(6(7) - 1 = 41\), \(6(1) - 7 = -1\) (giving \(k = 1\) when signs reverse), \(3(7) - 2(1) = 19\), and \(2(7) - 3(1) = 11\), so the smallest positive integer is 1.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(6x^2 + kx + 5\) can be factored.
qs.s: Factoring \(6x^2 + kx + 5\) requires checking \((6x + p)(x + q)\) and \((3x + p)(2x + q)\) with \(pq = 5\). The possible positive values of \(k\) are \(6(5) + 1 = 31\), \(6(1) + 5 = 11\), \(3(5) + 2(1) = 17\), and \(3(1) + 2(5) = 13\), so the greatest integer is 31.

qs.q: Find the greatest integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(8x^2 + kxy + 3y^2\) can be factored.
qs.s: The possible forms are \((8x + py)(x + qy)\) and \((4x + py)(2x + qy)\) with \(pq = 3\). The resulting positive values of \(k\) are \(8(3) + 1 = 25\), \(8(1) + 3 = 11\), \(4(3) + 2(1) = 14\), and \(4(1) + 2(3) = 10\), so the greatest value is 25.

qs.q: Find the smallest positive integer \(k\) so that the trinomial \(4x^2 + kx + 9\) can be factored.
qs.s: The trinomial can factor as \((4x + p)(x + q)\) or \((2x + p)(2x + q)\) with \(pq = 9\). Testing all positive factor pairs yields \(k \in \{12, 13, 15, 20, 37\}\), so the smallest positive value is \(2(3) + 2(3) = 12\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(25a^{2m} + 30a^m b^n + 9b^{2n}\)
qs.s: This is a perfect square trinomial with first term \((5a^m)^2\), last term \((3b^n)^2\), and middle term \(2(5a^m)(3b^n) = 30a^m b^n\). Factoring yields \((5a^m + 3b^n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(9x^{2m} - 24x^m y^n + 16y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Recognize the polynomial as a perfect square trinomial of the form \(a^2 - 2ab + b^2 = (a - b)^2\), where \(a = 3x^m\) and \(b = 4y^n\). Since \(-2(3x^m)(4y^n) = -24x^m y^n\), it factors as \((3x^m - 4y^n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(4x^{2m} + 28x^m y^n + 49y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Recognize this as a perfect square trinomial of the form \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2\), where \(a = 2x^m\) and \(b = 7y^n\). Because \(2(2x^m)(7y^n) = 28x^m y^n\), the factored form is \((2x^m + 7y^n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(15x^{2m} - 26x^m y^n + 8y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^m\) and \(v = y^n\). To factor \(15u^2 - 26uv + 8v^2\), find two factors of \(15 \times 8 = 120\) that add to \(-26\), which are \(-20\) and \(-6\), giving \((3x^m - 4y^n)(5x^m - 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(6x^{2m} - 11x^m y^n - 10y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Treat \(x^m\) and \(y^n\) as the variables in the quadratic form \(6u^2 - 11uv - 10v^2\). Finding two factors of \(6(-10) = -60\) that sum to \(-11\) gives \(-15\) and \(4\), which factors by grouping into \((2x^m - 5y^n)(3x^m + 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m, n,\) and \(k\) are natural numbers: \(8x^{2m} y^{2n} - 22x^m y^n z^k - 21z^{2k}\)
qs.s: Let \(u = x^m y^n\) and \(v = z^k\) to write the expression as \(8u^2 - 22uv - 21v^2\). Finding factors of \(8(-21) = -168\) that sum to \(-22\) yields \(-28\) and \(6\), which gives \((2x^m y^n - 7z^k)(4x^m y^n + 3z^k)\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(6x^{6m} - 19x^{3m} y^{2n} + 10y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Recognize this as a quadratic form in \(u = x^{3m}\) and \(v = y^{2n}\), giving \(6u^2 - 19uv + 10v^2\). Finding factors of \(60\) that sum to \(-19\) gives \(-15\) and \(-4\), factoring into \((2x^{3m} - 5y^{2n})(3x^{3m} - 2y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(12x^{2m} - 2x^m y^n - 4y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2\) to get \(2(6x^{2m} - x^m y^n - 2y^{2n})\). Then factor the quadratic form trinomial into \(2(2x^m + y^n)(3x^m - 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(9x^{2m} - 21x^m y^n + 6y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3(3x^{2m} - 7x^m y^n + 2y^{2n})\). Factoring the remaining quadratic trinomial gives \(3(3x^m - y^n)(x^m - 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(6x^{2m} + 26x^m y^n + 8y^{2n}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(3x^{2m} + 13x^m y^n + 4y^{2n})\). Factoring the quadratic form trinomial gives \(2(3x^m + y^n)(x^m + 4y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(14x^{2m} - 4x^m y^n - 18y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(7x^{2m} - 2x^m y^n - 9y^{2n})\). Then, factor the trinomial in quadratic form to obtain \(2(7x^m - 9y^n)(x^m + y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(12x^{2m} + 14x^m y^n - 10y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2\) to obtain \(2(6x^{2m} + 7x^m y^n - 5y^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial inside yields \(2(2x^m - y^n)(3x^m + 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(12x^{3m}y^n - 26x^{2m}y^{2n} + 12x^m y^{3n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(2x^m y^n\) to get \(2x^m y^n(6x^{2m} - 13x^m y^n + 6y^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial using the ac-method gives \(2x^m y^n(2x^m - 3y^n)(3x^m - 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-18x^{2m} + 33x^m y^n + 30y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the negative common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(6x^{2m} - 11x^m y^n - 10y^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial by grouping produces \(-3(3x^m + 2y^n)(2x^m - 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(15x^{4m} - 5x^{2m}y^{3n} - 50y^{6n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the numerical common factor \(5\) to obtain \(5(3x^{4m} - x^{2m}y^{3n} - 10y^{6n})\). Recognizing the quadratic form in terms of \(x^{2m}\) and \(y^{3n}\) gives \(5(3x^{2m} + 5y^{3n})(x^{2m} - 2y^{3n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-12x^{3m}y^n - 14x^{2m}y^{2n} + 10x^m y^{3n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2x^m y^n\) to get \(-2x^m y^n(6x^{2m} + 7x^m y^n - 5y^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(-2x^m y^n(2x^m - y^n)(3x^m + 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) is a natural number: \(-9x^{4m} + 3x^{2m}y^{2m} + 12y^{4m}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-3\) to get \(-3(3x^{4m} - x^{2m}y^{2m} - 4y^{4m})\). Factoring the resulting quadratic expression gives \(-3(3x^{2m} - 4y^{2m})(x^{2m} + y^{2m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-10x^{4m} - 25x^{2m}y^{2n} + 15y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5\) to obtain \(-5(2x^{4m} + 5x^{2m}y^{2n} - 3y^{4n})\). Factoring the trinomial produces \(-5(2x^{2m} - y^{2n})(x^{2m} + 3y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(-6x^{4n} + 15x^{2n}y^{2n} + 9y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(2x^{4n} - 5x^{2n}y^{2n} - 3y^{4n})\). Factoring the trinomial in quadratic form yields \(-3(2x^{2n} + y^{2n})(x^{2n} - 3y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-6x^{2m} + 9x^m y^n + 42y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3\) to obtain \(-3(2x^{2m} - 3x^m y^n - 14y^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial in terms of \(x^m\) and \(y^n\) yields \(-3(2x^m - 7y^n)(x^m + 2y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-8x^{4n} + 14x^{2n}y^{2m} + 4y^{4m}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(4x^{4n} - 7x^{2n}y^{2m} - 2y^{4m})\). Factoring the quadratic trinomial gives \(-2(4x^{2n} + y^{2m})(x^{2n} - 2y^{2m})\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-18a^{4m+1}b^{2n} - 15a^{2m+1}b^{3n} + 12a b^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3ab^{2n}\) to leave \(-3ab^{2n}(6a^{4m} + 5a^{2m}b^n - 4b^{2n})\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(-3ab^{2n}(2a^{2m} - b^n)(3a^{2m} + 4b^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-12x^{5m}y^n + 14x^{3m}y^{2n} + 10x^m y^{3n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(-2x^m y^n\) to get \(-2x^m y^n(6x^{4m} - 7x^{2m}y^n - 5y^{2n})\). Factoring the quadratic form inside yields \(-2x^m y^n(2x^{2m} + y^n)(3x^{2m} - 5y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-6x^{6m} - 7x^{3m}y^{2n} + 20y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(6x^{6m} + 7x^{3m}y^{2n} - 20y^{4n})\). In quadratic form with \(u = x^{3m}\) and \(v = y^{2n}\), \(6u^2 + 7uv - 20v^2\) factors into \((2u + 5v)(3u - 4v)\), giving \(-(2x^{3m} + 5y^{2n})(3x^{3m} - 4y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-8x^{4m} + 14x^{2m}y^{3n} + 15y^{6n}\)
Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-12x^{6m} + 23x^{3m}y^{4n} - 10y^{8n}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(12x^{6m} - 23x^{3m}y^{4n} + 10y^{8n})\). Letting \(u = x^{3m}\) and \(v = y^{4n}\), the quadratic form \(12u^2 - 23uv + 10v^2\) factors into \((3u - 2v)(4u - 5v)\), giving \(-(3x^{3m} - 2y^{4n})(4x^{3m} - 5y^{4n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-4x^{8m} - 7x^{4m}y^{5n} + 15y^{10n}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(4x^{8m} + 7x^{4m}y^{5n} - 15y^{10n})\). In quadratic form with \(u = x^{4m}\) and \(v = y^{5n}\), \(4u^2 + 7uv - 15v^2\) factors into \((u + 3v)(4u - 5v)\), which gives \(-(x^{4m} + 3y^{5n})(4x^{4m} - 5y^{5n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-10a^{4m} + 19a^{2m}b^{3n} - 6b^{6n}\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(10a^{4m} - 19a^{2m}b^{3n} + 6b^{6n})\). Letting \(u = a^{2m}\) and \(v = b^{3n}\), the trinomial factors as \((2u - 3v)(5u - 2v)\), yielding \(-(2a^{2m} - 3b^{3n})(5a^{2m} - 2b^{3n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-24x^{9m} + 38x^{5m}y^{3n} - 8x^m y^{6n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x^m\) to get \(-2x^m(12x^{8m} - 19x^{4m}y^{3n} + 4y^{6n})\). Letting \(u = x^{4m}\) and \(v = y^{3n}\), factor \(12u^2 - 19uv + 4v^2 = (3u - 4v)(4u - v)\), yielding \(-2x^m(3x^{4m} - 4y^{3n})(4x^{4m} - y^{3n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-30x^{8m}y^n - 25x^{5m}y^{3n} + 30x^{2m}y^{5n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5x^{2m}y^n\) to get \(-5x^{2m}y^n(6x^{6m} + 5x^{3m}y^{2n} - 6y^{4n})\). Factoring the trinomial inside gives \(-5x^{2m}y^n(2x^{3m} + 3y^{2n})(3x^{3m} - 2y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-20x^{7m}y^{2n} + 37x^{4m}y^{4n} - 15x^m y^{6n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-x^m y^{2n}\) to obtain \(-x^m y^{2n}(20x^{6m} - 37x^{3m}y^{2n} + 15y^{4n})\). Using \(ac = 300\) and factors \(-25, -12\), the trinomial factors into \((4x^{3m} - 5y^{2n})(5x^{3m} - 3y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-18x^{5m} + 33x^{3m}y^{2n} + 30x^m y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x^m\) to get \(-3x^m(6x^{4m} - 11x^{2m}y^{2n} - 10y^{4n})\). Factoring the trinomial in quadratic form gives \(-3x^m(2x^{2m} - 5y^{2n})(3x^{2m} + 2y^{2n})\).

qs.q: Factor the polynomial completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(-12x^{7m}y^{2n} + 26x^{4m}y^{5n} - 12x^m y^{8n}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x^m y^{2n}\) to obtain \(-2x^m y^{2n}(6x^{6m} - 13x^{3m}y^{3n} + 6y^{6n})\). Then factor the quadratic form \(6(x^{3m})^2 - 13(x^{3m})(y^{3n}) + 6(y^{3n})^2\) into \((2x^{3m} - 3y^{3n})(3x^{3m} - 2y^{3n})\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(2x^{n+2} + 7x^{n+1} - 4x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(2x^2 + 7x - 4)\). Then factor the quadratic trinomial to obtain \(x^n(2x - 1)(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(4x^{n+2} + 8x^{n+1} + 3x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(x^n\) to obtain \(x^n(4x^2 + 8x + 3)\), which factors as \(x^n(2x + 1)(2x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(2x^{n+2} - 5x^{n+1} - 3x^n\)
qs.s: First factor out \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(2x^2 - 5x - 3)\), then factor the remaining quadratic into \(x^n(2x + 1)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(3x^{n+2} - 7x^{n+1} + 2x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x^n\) to obtain \(x^n(3x^2 - 7x + 2)\), which factors into \(x^n(3x - 1)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(5x^{n+2} + 13x^{n+1} - 6x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(5x^2 + 13x - 6)\). Factoring the trinomial gives \(x^n(5x - 2)(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(3x^{n+2}y^m - 10x^{n+1}y^{m+1} + 8x^n y^{m+2}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x^n y^m\) to get \(x^n y^m(3x^2 - 10xy + 8y^2)\), which factors into \(x^n y^m(3x - 4y)(x - 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(6x^{n+3} - 7x^{n+2} - 20x^{n+1}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x^{n+1}\) to get \(x^{n+1}(6x^2 - 7x - 20)\), and factor the quadratic expression to get \(x^{n+1}(2x - 5)(3x + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(2x^{2n} + 7x^n y^m - 15y^{2m}\)
qs.s: Recognize the expression as a quadratic form in terms of \(x^n\) and \(y^m\). Factoring gives \((2x^n - 3y^m)(x^n + 5y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(6x^{2n} - 11x^n - 10\)
qs.s: Treat this expression as quadratic in \(x^n\). Factoring \(6(x^n)^2 - 11(x^n) - 10\) directly yields \((3x^n + 2)(2x^n - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(-6x^{n+2} + 21x^{n+1} + 45x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3x^n\) to leave \(-3x^n(2x^2 - 7x - 15)\), which factors into \(-3x^n(2x + 3)(x - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(3x^{n+2} + 5x^{n+1} - 2x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(3x^2 + 5x - 2)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial to obtain \(x^n(3x - 1)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(6x^{n+2} + 7x^{n+1} + 2x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(6x^2 + 7x + 2)\), then factor the remaining quadratic to obtain \(x^n(2x + 1)(3x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(2x^{n+2} + x^{n+1} - 6x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(2x^2 + x - 6)\), then factor the trinomial to obtain \(x^n(2x - 3)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(2x^{n+2} - 7x^{n+1} + 3x^n\)
qs.s: Factor out the common term \(x^n\) to get \(x^n(2x^2 - 7x + 3)\), then factor the quadratic expression to obtain \(x^n(2x - 1)(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(8x^{2n} - 10x^n - 3\)
qs.s: Recognize the expression as a quadratic form in \(x^n\) as \(8(x^n)^2 - 10(x^n) - 3\), which factors into \((4x^n + 1)(2x^n - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(3x^{2n+2} + 5x^{n+2} - 2x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x^2\) to get \(x^2(3x^{2n} + 5x^n - 2)\), then factor the quadratic form in \(x^n\) to obtain \(x^2(3x^n - 1)(x^n + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(-18x^{n+2} + 15x^{n+1} + 12x^n\)

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(n\) is a natural number: \(12x^{n+3} - 26x^{n+2} + 12x^{n+1}\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2x^{n+1}\) to obtain \(2x^{n+1}(6x^2 - 13x + 6)\), then factor the quadratic trinomial to get \(2x^{n+1}(3x - 2)(2x - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming that \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(6x^{n+2}y^m - 7x^{n+1}y^{m+1} - 5x^n y^{m+2}\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial \(x^n y^m\) to get \(x^n y^m(6x^2 - 7xy - 5y^2)\), then factor the two-variable quadratic expression to obtain \(x^n y^m(2x + y)(3x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(y > 0\): \(y^4\)
qs.s: The principal square root of \(y^4\) is \(\sqrt{y^4} = y^{4/2} = y^2\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(b > 0\): \(b^8\)
qs.s: The principal square root of \(b^8\) is \(\sqrt{b^8} = b^{8/2} = b^4\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(a > 0\): \(a^6\)
qs.s: The principal square root of \(a^6\) is \(\sqrt{a^6} = a^{6/2} = a^3\).

qs.s: The principal square root of \(t^2\) is \(\sqrt{t^2} = t^{2/2} = t\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\): \(a^4 b^{16}\)
qs.s: Divide each variable's exponent by 2: \(\sqrt{a^4 b^{16}} = a^{4/2} b^{16/2} = a^2 b^8\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(y > 0\): \(49y^6\)
qs.s: Take the square root of the coefficient and divide the exponent by 2: \(\sqrt{49y^6} = \sqrt{49} \cdot \sqrt{y^6} = 7y^3\).

qs.s: The principal square root is found by dividing the exponent by 2: \(\sqrt{x^{36}} = x^{36/2} = x^{18}\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root. Assume \(x > 0\): \((2x^3)(8x^7)\)
qs.s: First multiply the monomials: \((2x^3)(8x^7) = 16x^{10}\). Then find the principal square root: \(\sqrt{16x^{10}} = 4x^5\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root, assuming \(c > 0\): \(c^{12}\)

qs.q: Find the principal square root, assuming \(m > 0\) and \(n > 0\): \(m^{16} n^6\)
qs.s: Find the principal square root of each variable factor by halving its exponent: \(\sqrt{m^{16} n^6} = m^{16/2} n^{6/2} = m^8 n^3\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root, assuming \(x > 0\), \(y > 0\), and \(z > 0\): \(144 x^{18} y^4 z^2\)
qs.s: Take the square root of 144 and divide each variable's exponent by 2: \(\sqrt{144 x^{18} y^4 z^2} = 12 x^{18/2} y^{4/2} z^{2/2} = 12 x^9 y^2 z\).

qs.q: Find the principal square root, assuming \(a > 0\) and \(b > 0\): \(25 a^{12} b^8\)
