qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^2 - 60x + 50\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to obtain \(2(9x^2 - 30x + 25)\). The expression inside is a perfect square trinomial with leading coefficient greater than \(1\), giving \(2(3x - 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(5y^2 - 40y + 80\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(5\) to get \(5(y^2 - 8y + 16)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(5(y - 4)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^2 + 24x + 72\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(x^2 + 12x + 36)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(2(x + 6)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(6t^2 - 36t + 54\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(6\) to get \(6(t^2 - 6t + 9)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(6(t - 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2m^2 - 36m + 162\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2(m^2 - 18m + 81)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(2(m - 9)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3w^2 + 42w + 147\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3(w^2 + 14w + 49)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(3(w + 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-50x^3 + 140x^2 - 98x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x\) to obtain \(-2x(25x^2 - 70x + 49)\). Factoring the remaining perfect square trinomial yields \(-2x(5x - 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12y^3 + 36y^2 + 27y\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(3y\) to get \(3y(4y^2 + 12y + 9)\). Recognizing \(4y^2 + 12y + 9\) as a perfect square trinomial gives \(3y(2y + 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-32a^2 + 48ab - 18b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the negative common factor \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(16a^2 - 24ab + 9b^2)\). Factoring the two-variable perfect square trinomial gives \(-2(4a - 3b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(20x^3y - 60x^2y^2 + 45xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(5xy\) to obtain \(5xy(4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(5xy(2x - 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^3 + 14a^2 + 49a\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(a\) to obtain \(a(a^2 + 14a + 49)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(a(a + 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(n^3 + 20n^2 + 100n\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(n\) to get \(n(n^2 + 20n + 100)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(n(n + 10)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^3 - 18m^2 + 81m\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(m\) to get \(m(m^2 - 18m + 81)\). Since \(m^2 - 18m + 81 = (m - 9)^2\), the completely factored form is \(m(m - 9)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^3 + 10x^2 + 25x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(x\) to get \(x(x^2 + 10x + 25)\). Then recognize \(x^2 + 10x + 25\) as the perfect square trinomial \((x + 5)^2\), giving \(x(x + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^3 - 12y^2 + 36y\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(y\) to obtain \(y(y^2 - 12y + 36)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial yields \(y(y - 6)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-32x^4 - 48x^3 - 18x^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2x^2\) to obtain \(-2x^2(16x^2 + 24x + 9)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to obtain \(-2x^2(4x + 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12y^5 + 84y^4 + 147y^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3y^3\) to obtain \(3y^3(4y^2 + 28y + 49)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial \(4y^2 + 28y + 49\) yields \(3y^3(2y + 7)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-3a^3b + 24a^2b^2 - 48ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3ab\) to get \(-3ab(a^2 - 8ab + 16b^2)\). The remaining trinomial is a perfect square, giving \(-3ab(a - 4b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^3 - 60x^2 + 50x\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(9x^2 - 30x + 25)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial \(9x^2 - 30x + 25\) as \((3x - 5)^2\) to obtain \(2x(3x - 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(50x^3y - 120x^2y^2 + 72xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(2xy\) to get \(2xy(25x^2 - 60xy + 36y^2)\). Since \(25x^2 - 60xy + 36y^2 = (5x - 6y)^2\), the completely factored expression is \(2xy(5x - 6y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the perfect square trinomial completely: \(16x^2 - 56xy + 49y^2\)
qs.s: Identify \(a = 4x\) and \(b = 7y\), and check that the middle term is \(2(4x)(7y) = 56xy\). Using \(a^2 - 2ab + b^2 = (a - b)^2\) yields \((4x - 7y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the perfect square trinomial completely: \(49u^2 + 42uv + 9v^2\)
qs.s: Recognize that \(49u^2 = (7u)^2\), \(9v^2 = (3v)^2\), and the middle term is \(2(7u)(3v) = 42uv\). Applying \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2\) gives \((7u + 3v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the perfect square trinomial completely: \(36m^2 - 60mn + 25n^2\)
qs.s: Recognize that \(\sqrt{36m^2} = 6m\), \(\sqrt{25n^2} = 5n\), and the middle term is \(2(6m)(5n) = 60mn\). Factoring gives \((6m - 5n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the perfect square trinomial completely: \(25a^2 - 70ab + 49b^2\)
qs.s: This matches the pattern \(a^2 - 2ab + b^2 = (a - b)^2\) with \(a = 5a\) and \(b = 7b\), since \(2(5a)(7b) = 70ab\). Factoring gives \((5a - 7b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor the perfect square trinomial completely: \(4x^2 + 20xy + 25y^2\)
qs.s: Recognize the form \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 = (a + b)^2\) with \(a = 2x\) and \(b = 5y\), since \(2(2x)(5y) = 20xy\). Factoring gives \((2x + 5y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 - 40x^2y^2 + 25y^4\)
Factor completely: \(2x^3 - 28x^2y + 98xy^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(x^2 - 14xy + 49y^2)\). Then factor the perfect square trinomial to get \(2x(x - 7y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^5 - 36x^3y^2 + 27xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3x\) to get \(3x(4x^4 - 12x^2y^2 + 9y^4)\). Factoring the resulting perfect square trinomial gives \(3x(2x^2 - 3y^2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(50a^3b - 120a^2b^2 + 72ab^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2ab\) to get \(2ab(25a^2 - 60ab + 36b^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial in parentheses gives \(2ab(5a - 6b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^2 + 36xy - 27y^2\)
qs.s: First factor out the common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2)\). The remaining trinomial is a perfect square, factoring to \(-3(2x - 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12p^2 + 36pq - 27q^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to obtain \(-3(4p^2 - 12pq + 9q^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(-3(2p - 3q)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-45c^2 + 60cd - 20d^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-5\) to obtain \(-5(9c^2 - 12cd + 4d^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(-5(3c - 2d)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-75m^2 - 90mn - 27n^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-3\) to get \(-3(25m^2 + 30mn + 9n^2)\). Recognizing the trinomial as a perfect square yields \(-3(5m + 3n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^2 + 48xy - 32y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to get \(-2(9x^2 - 24xy + 16y^2)\). Since \(9x^2 - 24xy + 16y^2\) is a perfect square trinomial, it factors completely as \(-2(3x - 4y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-32u^2 - 80uv - 50v^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(-2\) to obtain \(-2(16u^2 + 40uv + 25v^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial yields \(-2(4u + 5v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-147a^2 + 336ab - 192b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(-3\) to obtain \(-3(49a^2 - 112ab + 64b^2)\). The trinomial is a perfect square with square roots \(7a\) and \(8b\), giving \(-3(7a - 8b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-50r^4 - 140r^2s^2 - 98s^4\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-2\) to get \(-2(25r^4 + 70r^2s^2 + 49s^4)\). Since \(25(r^2)^2 + 70(r^2)(s^2) + 49(s^2)^2\) is a perfect square trinomial, it factors completely as \(-2(5r^2 + 7s^2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-72m^3n^2 + 120m^2n^3 - 50mn^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-2mn^2\) to get \(-2mn^2(36m^2 - 60mn + 25n^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial gives \(-2mn^2(6m - 5n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-36u^3v - 120u^2v^2 - 100uv^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-4uv\) to get \(-4uv(9u^2 + 30uv + 25v^2)\). Factoring the resulting perfect square trinomial yields \(-4uv(3u + 5v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-24x^3y + 72x^2y^2 - 54xy^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common monomial factor \(-6xy\) to get \(-6xy(4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2)\). The remaining perfect square trinomial factors as \(-6xy(2x - 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-4x^2 - 20xy - 25y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(4x^2 + 20xy + 25y^2)\). Since the trinomial is a perfect square \((2x)^2 + 2(2x)(5y) + (5y)^2\), it factors completely as \(-(2x + 5y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-25a^2 + 30ab - 9b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(25a^2 - 30ab + 9b^2)\). Recognizing the perfect square trinomial \((5a)^2 - 2(5a)(3b) + (3b)^2\) gives \(-(5a - 3b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-x^2 + 14xy - 49y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to get \(-(x^2 - 14xy + 49y^2)\). This factors as the square of a binomial, yielding \(-(x - 7y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-49m^2 - 28mn - 4n^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to rewrite the expression as \(-(49m^2 + 28mn + 4n^2)\). Factoring the perfect square trinomial produces \(-(7m + 2n)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-16u^2 + 56uv - 49v^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) to obtain \(-(16u^2 - 56uv + 49v^2)\). Because \((4u)^2 - 2(4u)(7v) + (7v)^2 = (4u - 7v)^2\), the completely factored form is \(-(4u - 7v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-18x^5 - 60x^3y^2 - 50xy^4\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2x\) to get \(-2x(9x^4 + 30x^2y^2 + 25y^4)\). Recognizing \((3x^2)^2 + 2(3x^2)(5y^2) + (5y^2)^2\) gives the complete factorization \(-2x(3x^2 + 5y^2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-75a^4 + 90a^3b - 27a^2b^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the monomial GCF \(-3a^2\) to obtain \(-3a^2(25a^2 - 30ab + 9b^2)\). Since the trinomial is a perfect square, it factors completely as \(-3a^2(5a - 3b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-12x^3y - 36x^2y^2 - 27xy^3\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(-3xy\) to get \(-3xy(4x^2 + 12xy + 9y^2)\). Factoring the resulting perfect square trinomial yields \(-3xy(2x + 3y)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-50a^2b - 140ab^2 - 98b^3\)
qs.s: Factor out the common monomial factor \(-2b\) to get \(-2b(25a^2 + 70ab + 49b^2)\). The trinomial inside the parentheses is a perfect square, giving \(-2b(5a + 7b)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(-48x^2 + 144xy - 108y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor of \(-12\) to get \(-12(4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2)\). Then factor the remaining perfect square trinomial as \(-12(2x - 3y)^2\).

exercises.name: Finding shaded area in factored form

qs.q: A square of side 3x has a square hole of side 2y (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The shaded region is a ring between two circles with the same centre. The big radius is 5 and the small radius is y. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Ring area \(=\pi\cdot5^2-\pi y^2=\pi(25-y^2)=\pi(5-y)(5+y)\).

qs.q: The whole rectangle has width x+7 and height x. The white part has width 3. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=x(x+7)-3x=x^2+4x=x(x+4)\).

qs.q: A square of side 2x has a square hole of side 3 in the middle (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side x has a square of side 4 removed from one corner (dashed outline, not shaded). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=x^2-4^2=x^2-16=(x-4)(x+4)\) (difference of squares).

qs.q: A square of side x+3 has a square hole of side 2 in the middle (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 2x+3 has a square hole of side x-1 (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 4x+1 has a square hole of side 2x-3 (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The shaded region is a ring between two circles with the same centre. The small radius is x and the big radius is x+4. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 4x has a circular hole of radius x (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The figure shows four shaded rectangles that fit together to form one big rectangle. Write the total shaded area in factored form.
A square of side \(x+7\) has a square of side 3 cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side \(x+6\) has a square of side 2 cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side \(x+3\) has a square of side 1 cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side \(x+8\) has a square of side \(x-2\) cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
A square of side \(2x+7\) has a square of side 3 cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
A square of side \(3x+4\) has a square of side \(x+2\) cut out of its centre (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
The shaded region is a square of side \(x\) with a square of side \(5\) cut out of its middle. Write the shaded area in factored form.
qs.s: Area \(=x^2-5^2=(x-5)(x+5)\) (difference of squares).

qs.q: The shaded region is made of two rectangles, each of width \(x+7\). The upper one has height \(5\) and the lower one has height \(x\) (see the figure). Write the total shaded area in factored form.
The shaded ring lies between a circle of radius \(R\) and a circle of radius \(r\). Write its area in factored form.
qs.s: Area \(=\pi R^2-\pi r^2=\pi(R^2-r^2)=\pi(R-r)(R+r)\).

qs.q: The shaded region is a square of side \(2x\) with a square of side \(y\) cut out of its middle. Write the shaded area in factored form.
The shaded region is a square of side \(7\) with a square of side \(2x\) cut out of its middle. Write the shaded area in factored form.
The shaded region is a square of side \(3x\) with a square of side \(2y\) cut out of its middle. Write the shaded area in factored form.
The shaded region is a rectangle of length \(8x\) and height \(4x\) with two circles, each of radius \(x\), cut out. Write the shaded area in factored form.

The shaded region is made of three rectangles stacked on top of each other, each of width \(2x+1\). Their heights are \(3\), \(x\) and \(5\) (see the figure). Write the total shaded area in factored form.
The shaded region is the part of a square of side \(x+4\) that lies outside a smaller square of side \(x-1\) placed inside it. Write the shaded area in factored form.
The shaded ring lies between a circle of radius \(3x\) and a circle of radius \(2y\). Write its area in factored form.
A circle of radius x + 3 contains a smaller circle of radius x with the same centre. The ring between them is shaded. Use the figure to write the shaded area in factored form.
A square of side x + 3 has a square hole of side 2 (white) in the middle. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side x has a smaller square (white) cut from one corner. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=x^2-3^2=(x-3)(x+3)\) (difference of squares).

qs.q: A square of side 6x has a square of side y (white) cut from each of its four corners. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 2x has a smaller square (white) of side y cut from one corner. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 3x + 9 has a square hole of side x + 3 (white) in the middle. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
A square of side 4x + 1 has a square hole of side 2x - 3 (white) in the middle. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
A circle of radius 4x + y contains a smaller circle of radius 2x - y with the same centre. The ring between them is shaded. Use the figure to write the shaded area in fully factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=\pi\big((4x+y)^2-(2x-y)^2\big)=\pi(2x+2y)(6x)=12\pi x(x+y)\).

qs.q: A square of side 2x + 5y has a square (white) of side x - y cut from one corner. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=(2x+5y)^2-(x-y)^2=\big((2x+5y)-(x-y)\big)\big((2x+5y)+(x-y)\big)=(x+6y)(3x+4y)\).

qs.q: A square of side 7x has a square of side 2y (white) cut from each of its four corners. Use the figure to write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side y has a square of side 6 removed from one corner (dashed outline, not shaded). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 3x has a circular hole of radius x (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=(3x)^2-\pi x^2=9x^2-\pi x^2=x^2(9-\pi)\).

qs.q: A square of side 4y has a square hole of side 3 (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The shaded region is a ring between two circles with the same centre. The big radius is 6 and the small radius is x. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Ring area \(=\pi\cdot6^2-\pi x^2=\pi(36-x^2)=\pi(6-x)(6+x)\).

qs.q: The whole rectangle has height 3x and width x+9. The white part has width 2. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A rectangle of length 10x and width 4x has two identical circular holes of radius x (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
qs.s: Shaded area \(=10x\cdot4x-2\pi x^2=40x^2-2\pi x^2=2x^2(20-\pi)\).

qs.q: A square of side 5x+2 has a square hole of side 3x (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side 8x has a square hole of side 2x+1 (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A square of side x+5 has a square hole of side x-2 (white). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The shaded region is a ring between two circles with the same centre. The small radius is x+1 and the big radius is 2x+3. Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
A circle of radius \(3x\) has a circle of radius \(y\) with the same centre cut out of it (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded ring in factored form.

A rectangular frame has an outer rectangle that is \(x+7\) wide and \(x+4\) tall. The inner (white) rectangle is \(x+3\) wide and \(x\) tall (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded frame in factored form.
A rectangle is \(x+4\) wide and \(2x+6\) tall. A diagonal cuts it into two triangles and one triangle is shaded (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded triangle in factored form.
A square of side \(x+9\) has a square of side 9 cut out of one corner (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in factored form.
The figure is a trapezoid with parallel sides \(x+8\) and \(x+2\) and height \(x+3\). It is shaded. Write its area in factored form.
The shaded figure is a trapezoid with parallel sides \(3x+5\) and \(x+3\) and height \(2x+1\). Write its area in fully factored form.
A square of side \(3x+2\) has a square of side 2 cut out of one corner (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded region in fully factored form.
A circle of radius \(2x+5\) has a circle of radius \(2x+1\) with the same centre cut out of it (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded ring in fully factored form.

A rectangular frame of width 3 has an inner (white) rectangle that is \(2x\) wide and \(x+5\) tall, so its outer rectangle is \(2x+6\) wide and \(x+11\) tall (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded frame in fully factored form.
A circle of radius \(3x+y\) has a circle of radius \(x+y\) with the same centre cut out of it (see the figure). Write the area of the shaded ring in fully factored form.
Factor completely: \((a^2 - 10a + 25) - 16b^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((a - 5)^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula \((a - 5)^2 - (4b)^2 = (a - 5 + 4b)(a - 5 - 4b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 8x + 16) - 9y^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((x + 4)^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula \((x + 4)^2 - (3y)^2 = (x + 4 + 3y)(x + 4 - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((m^2 + 12m + 36) - 25n^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((m + 6)^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula \((m + 6)^2 - (5n)^2 = (m + 6 + 5n)(m + 6 - 5n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((y^2 + 14y + 49) - 64z^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((y + 7)^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula \((y + 7)^2 - (8z)^2 = (y + 7 + 8z)(y + 7 - 8z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((p^2 - 4p + 4) - 49q^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((p - 2)^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula \((p - 2)^2 - (7q)^2 = (p - 2 + 7q)(p - 2 - 7q)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36a^2 - (b^2 + 10b + 25)\)
qs.s: Factor the trinomial as \((b + 5)^2\), then use the difference of squares \([6a + (b + 5)][6a - (b + 5)]\) and distribute the negative sign to get \((6a + b + 5)(6a - b - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3(x^2 - 6x + 9) - 48y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3[(x^2 - 6x + 9) - 16y^2]\), then factor \((x - 3)^2 - (4y)^2\) to obtain \(3(x - 3 + 4y)(x - 3 - 4y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2) - 25z^2\)
qs.s: Factor the non-monic trinomial as \((2x - 3y)^2\), then apply the difference of squares \((2x - 3y)^2 - (5z)^2 = (2x - 3y + 5z)(2x - 3y - 5z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2)a^2 - 9(x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common trinomial factor to get \((x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2)(a^2 - 9)\), then factor the perfect square trinomial and the difference of squares to get \((x + 4y)^2(a + 3)(a - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 6x + 9) - (y^2 - 8y + 16)\)
qs.s: Factor each trinomial to obtain \((x + 3)^2 - (y - 4)^2\), apply the difference of squares \([(x + 3) + (y - 4)][(x + 3) - (y - 4)]\), and simplify to \((x + y - 1)(x - y + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((m^2 - 10mn + 25n^2) - 64p^2\)
qs.s: Recognize the first three terms as \((m - 5n)^2\), resulting in \((m - 5n)^2 - (8p)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula yields \((m - 5n + 8p)(m - 5n - 8p)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2) - 25z^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((x + 3y)^2\), giving \((x + 3y)^2 - (5z)^2\). Then apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \((x + 3y + 5z)(x + 3y - 5z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((16u^2 + 24uv + 9v^2) - w^2\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((4u + 3v)^2\) to get \((4u + 3v)^2 - w^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \((4u + 3v + w)(4u + 3v - w)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((25x^2 - 30xy + 9y^2) - 16z^2\)
qs.s: Write the trinomial as \((5x - 3y)^2\) to obtain \((5x - 3y)^2 - (4z)^2\). Applying the difference of squares produces \((5x - 3y + 4z)(5x - 3y - 4z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((9a^2 - 12ab + 4b^2) - 49c^2\)
qs.s: Factor the trinomial as \((3a - 2b)^2\), which gives \((3a - 2b)^2 - (7c)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula gives \((3a - 2b + 7c)(3a - 2b - 7c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^2 - 81z^2 + 40xy + 25y^2\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms into \((16x^2 + 40xy + 25y^2) - 81z^2\), which factors as \((4x + 5y)^2 - (9z)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula yields \((4x + 5y + 9z)(4x + 5y - 9z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)m^2 - 36(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)\) to obtain \((x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2)(m^2 - 36)\). Factoring the trinomial as \((x - 4y)^2\) and the difference of squares as \((m + 6)(m - 6)\) gives \((x - 4y)^2(m + 6)(m - 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49x^2 - y^2 + 12yz - 36z^2\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms with a negative sign to get \((7x)^2 - (y^2 - 12yz + 36z^2) = (7x)^2 - (y - 6z)^2\). Applying the difference of squares and distributing the negative sign gives \((7x + y - 6z)(7x - y + 6z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12a^3 - 36a^2b + 27ab^2 - 48ac^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3a\) to get \(3a[(4a^2 - 12ab + 9b^2) - 16c^2]\). Then factor the trinomial as \((2a - 3b)^2\) and apply the difference of squares to obtain \(3a(2a - 3b + 4c)(2a - 3b - 4c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2) - (4a^2 - 20ab + 25b^2)\)
qs.s: Factor both trinomials into perfect squares to get \((x + 3y)^2 - (2a - 5b)^2\). Factoring as a difference of squares and distributing the negative sign yields \((x + 3y + 2a - 5b)(x + 3y - 2a + 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - m^8\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula successively: \(1 - m^8 = (1 + m^4)(1 - m^4) = (1 + m^4)(1 + m^2)(1 - m^2) = (1 + m^4)(1 + m^2)(1 + m)(1 - m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^8 - 256\)
qs.s: Factor repeatedly using the difference of squares: \(y^8 - 256 = (y^4 + 16)(y^4 - 16) = (y^4 + 16)(y^2 + 4)(y^2 - 4) = (y^4 + 16)(y^2 + 4)(y + 2)(y - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^8 - b^8\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula three times: \(a^8 - b^8 = (a^4 + b^4)(a^4 - b^4) = (a^4 + b^4)(a^2 + b^2)(a^2 - b^2) = (a^4 + b^4)(a^2 + b^2)(a + b)(a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(256x^8 - 1\)
Factor completely: \(x^8 y^8 - 1\)
qs.s: Factor as a difference of squares three times: \(x^8 y^8 - 1 = (x^4 y^4 + 1)(x^4 y^4 - 1) = (x^4 y^4 + 1)(x^2 y^2 + 1)(x^2 y^2 - 1) = (x^4 y^4 + 1)(x^2 y^2 + 1)(xy + 1)(xy - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 - 17x^4 + 16\)
qs.s: Factor the quadratic in \(x^4\) into \((x^4 - 16)(x^4 - 1)\), then factor each resulting binomial completely using difference of squares to obtain \((x^2 + 4)(x^2 + 1)(x + 2)(x - 2)(x + 1)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 - 2x^4 + 1\)
qs.s: Recognize the polynomial as a perfect square trinomial \((x^4 - 1)^2\), then factor the base \(x^4 - 1\) completely into \((x^2 + 1)(x + 1)(x - 1)\) and square each factor to get \((x^2 + 1)^2(x + 1)^2(x - 1)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^9 - 512x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(x^8 - 256)\), then factor the remaining binomial three times using difference of squares to get \(2x(x^4 + 16)(x^2 + 4)(x + 2)(x - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{16} - 1\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula four times in succession: \(x^{16} - 1 = (x^8 + 1)(x^8 - 1) = (x^8 + 1)(x^4 + 1)(x^4 - 1) = (x^8 + 1)(x^4 + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x + 1)(x - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^9 - x^8 - x + 1\)
qs.s: Group by pairs to get \(x^8(x - 1) - 1(x - 1) = (x^8 - 1)(x - 1)\), then completely factor \(x^8 - 1\) to obtain \((x^4 + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x + 1)(x - 1)(x - 1) = (x^4 + 1)(x^2 + 1)(x + 1)(x - 1)^2\).
Express each trinomial as a perfect square: \((5x^3 - 3y^2)^2 - (4u^2 + 3v^4)^2\). Then apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \((5x^3 - 3y^2 + 4u^2 + 3v^4)(5x^3 - 3y^2 - 4u^2 - 3v^4)\).

Recognize each part as a squared binomial: \((4a^3 + 5b^2)^2 - (2c^2 - 5d^3)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares and distributing the negative sign yields \((4a^3 + 5b^2 + 2c^2 - 5d^3)(4a^3 + 5b^2 - 2c^2 + 5d^3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((4u^4 + 12u^2v^2 + 9v^4) - (9p^6 - 6p^3q^3 + q^6)\)
qs.s: Factor each trinomial into a binomial square to obtain \((2u^2 + 3v^2)^2 - (3p^3 - q^3)^2\). Factoring as a difference of squares yields \((2u^2 + 3v^2 + 3p^3 - q^3)(2u^2 + 3v^2 - 3p^3 + q^3)\).
Rewrite the expression as a difference of squares: \((3m^2 - 4n^2)^2 - (x^3 + 5y^3)^2\). Factoring gives \((3m^2 - 4n^2 + x^3 + 5y^3)(3m^2 - 4n^2 - x^3 - 5y^3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^4 - 6x^2y^2 + 9y^4) - (a^6 + 4a^3b^3 + 4b^6)\)
qs.s: Each group is a perfect square trinomial: \((x^2 - 3y^2)^2 - (a^3 + 2b^3)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula gives \((x^2 - 3y^2 + a^3 + 2b^3)(x^2 - 3y^2 - a^3 - 2b^3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^6 - 12x^3y^2 + 9y^4 - 9a^4 - 12a^2b^3 - 4b^6\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((4x^6 - 12x^3y^2 + 9y^4) - (9a^4 + 12a^2b^3 + 4b^6) = (2x^3 - 3y^2)^2 - (3a^2 + 2b^3)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares produces \((2x^3 - 3y^2 + 3a^2 + 2b^3)(2x^3 - 3y^2 - 3a^2 - 2b^3)\).

Factor out the common factor \(3\) to obtain \(3[(4x^6 - 16x^3y^3 + 16y^6) - (a^4 + 6a^2b^2 + 9b^4)] = 3[(2x^3 - 4y^3)^2 - (a^2 + 3b^2)^2]\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \(3(2x^3 - 4y^3 + a^2 + 3b^2)(2x^3 - 4y^3 - a^2 - 3b^2)\).

Factor out the common factor \(3\) first: \(3[(x^6 - 8x^3y^3 + 16y^6) - (a^4 + 12a^2b^2 + 36b^4)] = 3[(x^3 - 4y^3)^2 - (a^2 + 6b^2)^2]\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \(3(x^3 - 4y^3 + a^2 + 6b^2)(x^3 - 4y^3 - a^2 - 6b^2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely assuming \(m, n\) are natural numbers: \((9x^{4n} - 12x^{2n}y^{2m} + 4y^{4m}) - (25a^{2n} + 30a^n b^m + 9b^{2m})\)
qs.s: Write each trinomial as a binomial square: \((3x^{2n} - 2y^{2m})^2 - (5a^n + 3b^m)^2\). Applying the difference of squares gives \((3x^{2n} - 2y^{2m} + 5a^n + 3b^m)(3x^{2n} - 2y^{2m} - 5a^n - 3b^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(p\) and \(q\) are natural numbers: \(81^{2p}x^{2p} - 100^{2q}y^{2q}\)
qs.s: Rewrite the binomial as \((81^p x^p)^2 - (100^q y^q)^2\) and apply the difference of squares identity to yield \((81^p x^p + 100^q y^q)(81^p x^p - 100^q y^q)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(16^{2m}a^{2m} - 49^{2n}b^{2n}\)
qs.s: Express the expression as \((16^m a^m)^2 - (49^n b^n)^2\) and factor using the difference of squares formula to obtain \((16^m a^m + 49^n b^n)(16^m a^m - 49^n b^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(9^{2m}u^{2m} - 64^{2n}v^{2n}\)
qs.s: Recognize the expression as a difference of squares \((9^m u^m)^2 - (64^n v^n)^2\), which factors into \((9^m u^m + 64^n v^n)(9^m u^m - 64^n v^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(25^{2m}x^{2m} - 36^{2n}y^{2n}\)
qs.s: Write each term as a square, \((25^m x^m)^2 - (36^n y^n)^2\), and apply the difference of squares identity \(A^2 - B^2 = (A + B)(A - B)\) to get \((25^m x^m + 36^n y^n)(25^m x^m - 36^n y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(a\) and \(b\) are natural numbers: \(4^{2a}c^{2a} - 121^{2b}d^{2b}\)
qs.s: Express each term as a square, \((4^a c^a)^2 - (121^b d^b)^2\), and factor as a difference of squares to get \((4^a c^a + 121^b d^b)(4^a c^a - 121^b d^b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\), \(n\), and \(k\) are natural numbers: \(64^{2k}w^{2k} - a^{2m} + 6a^m b^n - 9b^{2n}\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms by factoring out \(-1\) to get \((64^k w^k)^2 - (a^m - 3b^n)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares and carefully distributing the negative sign gives \((64^k w^k + a^m - 3b^n)(64^k w^k - a^m + 3b^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\), \(n\), and \(k\) are natural numbers: \(x^{2m} + 2x^m y^n + y^{2n} - 36^{2k}z^{2k}\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as a perfect square trinomial \((x^m + y^n)^2 - (36^k z^k)^2\), then factor using the difference of squares formula to obtain \((x^m + y^n + 36^k z^k)(x^m + y^n - 36^k z^k)\).

qs.q: Factor completely, assuming \(m\) and \(n\) are natural numbers: \(25^{2m}x^{2m+2} - 49^{2n}x^2 y^{2n}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(x^2\) to get \(x^2(25^{2m}x^{2m} - 49^{2n}y^{2n})\), then factor the remaining difference of squares into \(x^2(25^m x^m + 49^n y^n)(25^m x^m - 49^n y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - 16^{4n}z^{4n}\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula to get \((1 + 16^{2n}z^{2n})(1 - 16^{2n}z^{2n})\), then factor the difference factor again to yield \((1 + 16^{2n}z^{2n})(1 + 16^n z^n)(1 - 16^n z^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25^{4k}x^{4k} - 1\)
qs.s: Write the binomial as \((25^{2k}x^{2k})^2 - 1^2 = (25^{2k}x^{2k} + 1)(25^{2k}x^{2k} - 1)\), then factor the difference of squares factor again to obtain \((25^{2k}x^{2k} + 1)(25^k x^k + 1)(25^k x^k - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(u^{4m}v^{4m} - w^{4m}\)
qs.s: Factor as a difference of squares to get \((u^{2m}v^{2m} + w^{2m})(u^{2m}v^{2m} - w^{2m})\), then factor the second binomial again to obtain \((u^{2m}v^{2m} + w^{2m})(u^m v^m + w^m)(u^m v^m - w^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4^{4n}y^{4n} - 1\)
qs.s: Express the expression as a difference of squares \((4^{2n}y^{2n} + 1)(4^{2n}y^{2n} - 1)\), then factor the second binomial again to obtain \((4^{2n}y^{2n} + 1)(4^n y^n + 1)(4^n y^n - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{4m}b^{4m} - 1\)
qs.s: Factor \(a^{4m}b^{4m} - 1\) as \((a^{2m}b^{2m} + 1)(a^{2m}b^{2m} - 1)\), and factor the difference term once more as a difference of squares to get \((a^{2m}b^{2m} + 1)(a^m b^m + 1)(a^m b^m - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 b^{4m} - 9b^{4m} - a^2 + 9\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \(b^{4m}(a^2 - 9) - (a^2 - 9) = (a^2 - 9)(b^{4m} - 1)\), then factor \(a^2 - 9\) as \((a + 3)(a - 3)\) and factor \(b^{4m} - 1\) twice to obtain \((a + 3)(a - 3)(b^{2m} + 1)(b^m + 1)(b^m - 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^{4m+1}y - 2xy^{4m+1}\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2xy\) to get \(2xy(x^{4m} - y^{4m})\), then apply the difference of squares formula twice on \(x^{4m} - y^{4m}\) to obtain \(2xy(x^{2m} + y^{2m})(x^m + y^m)(x^m - y^m)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{8m} - 256\)
qs.s: Factor repeatedly using the difference of squares by taking the square root of both the variable power and the numerical term at each step, yielding \((x^{4m} + 16)(x^{2m} + 4)(x^m + 2)(x^m - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^{8m}b^{8n} - c^{8k}\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula three times successively to completely factor the expression into four factors: \((a^{4m}b^{4n} + c^{4k})(a^{2m}b^{2n} + c^{2k})(a^m b^n + c^k)(a^m b^n - c^k)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^{4m} - 5x^{2m}y^{2n} + 4y^{4n}\)
qs.s: Factor the trinomial as a quadratic in form to get \((x^{2m} - 4y^{2n})(x^{2m} - y^{2n})\), then factor each difference of squares completely to obtain \((x^m + 2y^n)(x^m - 2y^n)(x^m + y^n)(x^m - y^n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^8 - y^8\)
qs.s: Apply the difference of squares formula three times successively to get \((x^4 + y^4)(x^2 + y^2)(x + y)(x - y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16b^8 - 81\)
qs.s: Factor as a difference of squares twice to obtain \((4b^4 + 9)(2b^2 + 3)(2b^2 - 3)\), which cannot be factored further over the integers.

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16m^4 - 81n^4\)
qs.s: Factor the difference of squares to get \((4m^2 + 9n^2)(4m^2 - 9n^2)\), then factor the second binomial again to obtain \((4m^2 + 9n^2)(2m + 3n)(2m - 3n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(81 - a^8\)
qs.s: Factor as a difference of squares twice to get \((9 + a^4)(3 + a^2)(3 - a^2)\), noting that \(3 - a^2\) cannot be factored further over the integers.

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 y^2 - 9x^4 - 16y^2 + 144\)
qs.s: Factor by grouping as \((x^4 - 16)(y^2 - 9)\), then apply the difference of squares formula to factor \(x^4 - 16\) as \((x^2 + 4)(x + 2)(x - 2)\) and \(y^2 - 9\) as \((y + 3)(y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((y^2 - 16)^2 - (y + 4)^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \((y + 4)^2\) to get \((y + 4)^2[(y - 4)^2 - 1]\), then use the difference of squares on the bracketed term to arrive at \((y + 4)^2(y - 3)(y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^9 b - a b^9\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(ab\) to get \(ab(a^8 - b^8)\), then apply the difference of squares formula three times to obtain \(ab(a^4 + b^4)(a^2 + b^2)(a + b)(a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(u^8 - 2u^4 v^4 + v^8\)
qs.s: Recognize the expression as a perfect square trinomial \((u^4 - v^4)^2\), then factor the interior difference of squares completely to get \([(u^2 + v^2)(u + v)(u - v)]^2 = (u^2 + v^2)^2(u + v)^2(u - v)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(y^2 - 9 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Applying the difference of squares formula \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\) with \(a = y\) and \(b = 3\), we get \(y^2 - 9 = (y - 3)(y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(m^2 - 36 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Since \(36 = 6^2\), using the difference of squares identity \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\) gives \((m - 6)(m + 6)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 - 25 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Recognizing \(a^2 - 25\) as \(a^2 - 5^2\), apply the difference of squares formula to factor it as \((a - 5)(a + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^2 - 49 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula with \(a = w\) and \(b = 7\), we obtain \(w^2 - 49 = (w - 7)(w + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 4 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Using the difference of squares formula \(a^2 - b^2 = (a - b)(a + b)\) with \(a = x\) and \(b = 2\), we factor \(x^2 - 4\) as \((x - 2)(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(c^2 - d^2 + 5c + 5d = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Group as \((c^2 - d^2) + 5(c + d) = (c - d)(c + d) + 5(c + d)\), then factor out the common binomial factor \((c + d)\) to get \((c + d)(c - d + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4p^2 - 12pq + 9q^2 - 25 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first three terms as the square of a binomial \((2p - 3q)^2\), then factor the difference of squares \((2p - 3q)^2 - 5^2\) to obtain \((2p - 3q - 5)(2p - 3q + 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 6x + 9 - y^2 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as the perfect square trinomial \((x + 3)^2\), giving \((x + 3)^2 - y^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula to get \((x + 3 - y)(x + 3 + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 - 2ab + b^2 - 16 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Recognize the first three terms as the perfect square \((a - b)^2\), which gives \((a - b)^2 - 4^2\); factoring this difference of squares yields \((a - b - 4)(a - b + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49 - m^2 - 2mn - n^2 = (\quad)(\quad)\)
qs.s: Factor \(-1\) from the last three terms to rewrite the expression as \(7^2 - (m + n)^2\), then use the difference of squares formula to obtain \([7 - (m + n)][7 + (m + n)] = (7 - m - n)(7 + m + n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9m^2 - 30mn + 25n^2 - 6m + 10n\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as \((3m - 5n)^2\) and factor \(-2\) from the last two terms: \((3m - 5n)^2 - 2(3m - 5n)\). Factoring out \((3m - 5n)\) gives \((3m - 5n)(3m - 5n - 2)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 + 12xy + 9y^2 + 2x + 3y\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first three terms as \((2x + 3y)^2\), giving \((2x + 3y)^2 + 1(2x + 3y)\). Factoring out \((2x + 3y)\) yields \((2x + 3y)(2x + 3y + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2 + 4x - 12y\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as a perfect square trinomial and factor 4 from the remaining two terms: \((x - 3y)^2 + 4(x - 3y)\). Factoring out the common binomial \((x - 3y)\) gives \((x - 3y)(x - 3y + 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 - 7a - 7b\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as \((a + b)^2\) and factor \(-7\) from the last two terms to get \((a + b)^2 - 7(a + b)\). Factoring out \((a + b)\) gives \((a + b)(a + b - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2 + 3x + 12y\)
qs.s: Recognize the first three terms as \((x + 4y)^2\) and factor 3 from the last two terms to get \((x + 4y)^2 + 3(x + 4y)\). Factoring out \((x + 4y)\) results in \((x + 4y)(x + 4y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2 - a^2 + 6ab - 9b^2\)
qs.s: Group the expression into two perfect square trinomials: \((x^2 + 4xy + 4y^2) - (a^2 - 6ab + 9b^2) = (x + 2y)^2 - (a - 3b)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula gives \((x + 2y + a - 3b)(x + 2y - a + 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^3 - 16x^2y + 32xy^2 - 6x^2 + 24xy\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to get \(2x(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2 - 3x + 12y)\). Group within the brackets as \((x - 4y)^2 - 3(x - 4y)\), then factor out \((x - 4y)\) to arrive at \(2x(x - 4y)(x - 4y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3a^2 + 12ab + 12b^2 - 27c^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor 3 to obtain \(3[(a^2 + 4ab + 4b^2) - 9c^2]\). Group the perfect square trinomial to write \(3[(a + 2b)^2 - (3c)^2]\), then factor the difference of squares to get \(3(a + 2b - 3c)(a + 2b + 3c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2 + 5x + 15y + 6\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((x + 3y)^2 + 5(x + 3y) + 6\). Treating \((x + 3y)\) as a single variable, factor this quadratic trinomial into \((x + 3y + 2)(x + 3y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 - 4xy + y^2 - 2x + y - 12\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as \((2x - y)^2\) and factor \(-1\) from the next two terms: \((2x - y)^2 - (2x - y) - 12\). Factoring this quadratic in terms of \((2x - y)\) gives \((2x - y - 4)(2x - y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 + 12xy + 9y^2 - 4x - 6y + 1\)
Factor completely: \(x^2 - 8xy + 16y^2 + 10x - 40y + 25\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((x - 4y)^2 + 10(x - 4y) + 25\). With \(u = x - 4y\), this factors as \(u^2 + 10u + 25 = (u + 5)^2\), giving \((x - 4y + 5)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9x^2 - 6xy + y^2 - 12x + 4y + 4\)
qs.s: Group the expression as \((3x - y)^2 - 4(3x - y) + 4\). Substituting \(u = 3x - y\) yields \(u^2 - 4u + 4 = (u - 2)^2 = (3x - y - 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 - 4ab + 4b^2 - 6a + 12b + 9\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((a - 2b)^2 - 6(a - 2b) + 9\). Letting \(u = a - 2b\), this becomes \(u^2 - 6u + 9 = (u - 3)^2\), so the factored form is \((a - 2b - 3)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2 + 4x + 12y + 4\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((x + 3y)^2 + 4(x + 3y) + 4\). Substituting \(u = x + 3y\) gives \(u^2 + 4u + 4 = (u + 2)^2\), which results in \((x + 3y + 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2 - z^2 - 8z - 16\)
qs.s: Group as \((x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2) - (z^2 + 8z + 16) = (x - 3y)^2 - (z + 4)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \([(x - 3y) + (z + 4)][(x - 3y) - (z + 4)] = (x - 3y + z + 4)(x - 3y - z - 4)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3x^2 - 12xy + 12y^2 - 3z^2 - 18z - 27\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3\) to get \(3[(x - 2y)^2 - (z + 3)^2]\), then apply the difference of squares to get \(3(x - 2y + z + 3)(x - 2y - z - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12x^2 - 36xy + 27y^2 + 24x - 36y + 12\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3\) to get \(3[(2x - 3y)^2 + 4(2x - 3y) + 4]\). Letting \(u = 2x - 3y\), this simplifies to \(3(u + 2)^2 = 3(2x - 3y + 2)^2\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^2 + 12ab + 9b^2 - 16c^2 + 8c - 1\)
qs.s: Group the terms as \((2a + 3b)^2 - (4c - 1)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula gives \([(2a + 3b) + (4c - 1)][(2a + 3b) - (4c - 1)] = (2a + 3b + 4c - 1)(2a + 3b - 4c + 1)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2x^2 - 4xy + 2y^2 + 7x - 7y + 3\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \(2(x - y)^2 + 7(x - y) + 3\). Letting \(u = x - y\), factor the trinomial \(2u^2 + 7u + 3 = (2u + 1)(u + 3)\), then substitute back to obtain \((2x - 2y + 1)(x - y + 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - 6xy + 9y^2 - 49\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as \((x - 3y)^2 - 7^2\), then factor as a difference of squares to get \((x - 3y + 7)(x - 3y - 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49a^2 - 28ab + 4b^2 - 81\)
qs.s: Write the first three terms as \((7a - 2b)^2\), giving \((7a - 2b)^2 - 9^2 = (7a - 2b + 9)(7a - 2b - 9)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 + 20xy + 25y^2 - 9\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as a perfect square trinomial, \((2x + 5y)^2 - 3^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \((2x + 5y + 3)(2x + 5y - 3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25a^2 - 30ab + 9b^2 - 64\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as \((5a - 3b)^2 - 8^2\), then apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \((5a - 3b + 8)(5a - 3b - 8)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^2 + 24xy + 9y^2 - 25\)
qs.s: Recognize that the first three terms form the square of a binomial, \((4x + 3y)^2 - 5^2\), which factors as \((4x + 3y + 5)(4x + 3y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(18x^3 - 48x^2y + 32xy^2 - 50x\)
qs.s: First factor out the greatest common factor \(2x\) to obtain \(2x(9x^2 - 24xy + 16y^2 - 25)\), then write the trinomial as \((3x - 4y)^2\) and apply the difference of squares to reach \(2x(3x - 4y + 5)(3x - 4y - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2 - a^2 + 6ab - 9b^2\)
qs.s: Group the terms into two perfect square trinomials: \((x^2 + 8xy + 16y^2) - (a^2 - 6ab + 9b^2) = (x + 4y)^2 - (a - 3b)^2\), then apply the difference of squares and distribute signs to get \((x + 4y + a - 3b)(x + 4y - a + 3b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(12a^3b - 60a^2b^2 + 75ab^3 - 27abc^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(3ab\) to get \(3ab(4a^2 - 20ab + 25b^2 - 9c^2) = 3ab[(2a - 5b)^2 - (3c)^2]\), then apply the difference of squares to reach \(3ab(2a - 5b + 3c)(2a - 5b - 3c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25a^2 - 36c^2 - 70ab + 49b^2\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms to group the perfect square trinomial as \((25a^2 - 70ab + 49b^2) - 36c^2 = (5a - 7b)^2 - (6c)^2\), which factors as \((5a - 7b + 6c)(5a - 7b - 6c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49 - 16x^2 - 24xy - 9y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) from the variable terms to get \(49 - (16x^2 + 24xy + 9y^2) = 7^2 - (4x + 3y)^2\), then factor as a difference of squares and distribute the negative sign to get \((7 + 4x + 3y)(7 - 4x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16m^2 - (x^2 + 6xy + 9y^2)\)
qs.s: Rewrite the trinomial as \((x + 3y)^2\) to express the polynomial as the difference of squares \((4m)^2 - (x + 3y)^2\). Factoring gives \((4m + (x + 3y))(4m - (x + 3y)) = (4m + x + 3y)(4m - x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(64k^2 - (m^2 - 14mn + 49n^2)\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \((8k)^2 - (m - 7n)^2\). Using the difference of squares formula and distributing the negative sign gives \((8k + m - 7n)(8k - m + 7n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36z^2 - (x^2 - 10xy + 25y^2)\)
qs.s: Recognize the trinomial as \((x - 5y)^2\) to write the expression as \((6z)^2 - (x - 5y)^2\). Applying the difference of squares formula yields \((6z + x - 5y)(6z - x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(9p^2 - (16a^2 + 8ab + b^2)\)
qs.s: Factor the trinomial as \((4a + b)^2\) to obtain the difference of squares \((3p)^2 - (4a + b)^2\). Factoring gives \((3p + 4a + b)(3p - 4a - b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49c^2 - (9u^2 - 12uv + 4v^2)\)
qs.s: Factor the perfect square trinomial as \((3u - 2v)^2\), then factor the difference of squares \((7c)^2 - (3u - 2v)^2\) to obtain \((7c + 3u - 2v)(7c - 3u + 2v)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36m^2 - 4n^2 - 20n - 25\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms as \(36m^2 - (4n^2 + 20n + 25) = (6m)^2 - (2n + 5)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((6m + 2n + 5)(6m - 2n - 5)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \((x^2 + 8x + 16) - (y^2 - 6y + 9)\)
qs.s: Factor each trinomial to get \((x + 4)^2 - (y - 3)^2\). Apply the difference of squares to get \([(x + 4) + (y - 3)][(x + 4) - (y - 3)] = (x + y + 1)(x - y + 7)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(3a^3 - 12a^2b + 12ab^2 - 27ac^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the common factor \(3a\) to leave \((a^2 - 4ab + 4b^2) - 9c^2 = (a - 2b)^2 - (3c)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \(3a(a - 2b + 3c)(a - 2b - 3c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^2 - 12ab + 9b^2 - 16c^2 + 8cd - d^2\)
qs.s: Group into two perfect square trinomials: \((4a^2 - 12ab + 9b^2) - (16c^2 - 8cd + d^2) = (2a - 3b)^2 - (4c - d)^2\). Factoring as a difference of squares yields \((2a - 3b + 4c - d)(2a - 3b - 4c + d)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(50x^2 - 2(4y^2 - 28yz + 49z^2)\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2\) to get \(2[25x^2 - (2y - 7z)^2]\). Then apply the difference of squares formula to obtain \(2(5x + 2y - 7z)(5x - 2y + 7z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^4 - 4x^2 - 12xy - 9y^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) from the last three terms to form a perfect square: \(x^4 - (4x^2 + 12xy + 9y^2) = (x^2)^2 - (2x + 3y)^2\). Using the difference of squares formula yields \((x^2 + 2x + 3y)(x^2 - 2x - 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(16x^4 - 25x^2 + 20xy - 4y^2\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression by grouping the last three terms: \(16x^4 - (25x^2 - 20xy + 4y^2) = (4x^2)^2 - (5x - 2y)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \((4x^2 + 5x - 2y)(4x^2 - 5x + 2y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(25a^4 - 9a^2 + 30ab - 25b^2\)
qs.s: Group the expression as \((5a^2)^2 - (9a^2 - 30ab + 25b^2) = (5a^2)^2 - (3a - 5b)^2\). Applying difference of squares results in \((5a^2 + 3a - 5b)(5a^2 - 3a + 5b)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(36m^4 - 16m^2 - 24mn - 9n^2\)
qs.s: Rewrite the expression as \((6m^2)^2 - (16m^2 + 24mn + 9n^2) = (6m^2)^2 - (4m + 3n)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \((6m^2 + 4m + 3n)(6m^2 - 4m - 3n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^4 - 4x^2 + 4xy - y^2\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms as a perfect square trinomial: \(4x^4 - (4x^2 - 4xy + y^2) = (2x^2)^2 - (2x - y)^2\). Then apply the difference of squares formula to get \((2x^2 + 2x - y)(2x^2 - 2x + y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4a^2 - 12ab + 9b^2 - 16x^2 - 40xy - 25y^2\)
qs.s: Group the six terms into two perfect square trinomials: \((4a^2 - 12ab + 9b^2) - (16x^2 + 40xy + 25y^2) = (2a - 3b)^2 - (4x + 5y)^2\). Applying difference of squares gives \((2a - 3b + 4x + 5y)(2a - 3b - 4x - 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49x^6 - 4x^4 + 20x^2 y^3 - 25y^6\)
qs.s: Group the expression as \((7x^3)^2 - (4x^4 - 20x^2 y^3 + 25y^6) = (7x^3)^2 - (2x^2 - 5y^3)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((7x^3 + 2x^2 - 5y^3)(7x^3 - 2x^2 + 5y^3)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(w^2 - u^2 + 2uv - v^2\)
qs.s: Factor out \(-1\) from the last three terms to get \(w^2 - (u^2 - 2uv + v^2) = w^2 - (u - v)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares yields \((w + u - v)(w - (u - v)) = (w + u - v)(w - u + v)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(a^2 + 2ab + b^2 - c^2\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as a perfect square trinomial: \((a^2 + 2ab + b^2) - c^2 = (a + b)^2 - c^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((a + b + c)(a + b - c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(x^2 - y^2 - 2yz - z^2\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms with a negative sign factored out: \(x^2 - (y^2 + 2yz + z^2) = x^2 - (y + z)^2\). Factoring this difference of squares gives \((x + y + z)(x - y - z)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(1 - m^2 + 2mn - n^2\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms by factoring out \(-1\): \(1 - (m^2 - 2mn + n^2) = 1^2 - (m - n)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((1 + (m - n))(1 - (m - n)) = (1 + m - n)(1 - m + n)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(p^2 - 2pq + q^2 - r^2\)
qs.s: Group the first three terms as a perfect square trinomial: \((p^2 - 2pq + q^2) - r^2 = (p - q)^2 - r^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((p - q + r)(p - q - r)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(20xy - 4x^2 - 25y^2 + 9z^2\)
qs.s: Rearrange the terms to isolate the positive square: \(9z^2 - (4x^2 - 20xy + 25y^2) = (3z)^2 - (2x - 5y)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares yields \((3z + 2x - 5y)(3z - 2x + 5y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(2a^3 - 8ab^2 - 24abc - 18ac^2\)
qs.s: Factor out the greatest common factor \(2a\) to obtain \(2a[a^2 - (4b^2 + 12bc + 9c^2)] = 2a[a^2 - (2b + 3c)^2]\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \(2a(a + 2b + 3c)(a - 2b - 3c)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(49w^2 - 4x^2 + 12xy - 9y^2\)
qs.s: Group the last three terms by factoring out \(-1\): \(49w^2 - (4x^2 - 12xy + 9y^2) = (7w)^2 - (2x - 3y)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \((7w + 2x - 3y)(7w - 2x + 3y)\).

qs.q: Factor completely: \(4x^2 - 9y^2 - 12x + 9\)
qs.s: Group the \(x\)-terms with the constant to form a perfect square trinomial: \((4x^2 - 12x + 9) - 9y^2 = (2x - 3)^2 - (3y)^2\). Factoring the difference of squares gives \((2x - 3 + 3y)(2x - 3 - 3y) = (2x + 3y - 3)(2x - 3y - 3)\).
