qs.q: Determine whether the given ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \((-5, -4)\); \(y = -4\).
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because \(-4 = -4\).
d: No, it is not a solution because \(-5 \neq -4\).

qs.s: Substitute \(y = -4\) into the equation to get \(-4 = -4\), which is true. Therefore, \((-5, -4)\) is a solution to the equation.

qs.q: Determine whether the given ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \((-8, 8)\); \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x + 2\).
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because \(-\frac{3}{4}(-8) + 2 = 8\).

qs.q: Determine whether the given ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \((-2, 3)\); \(5x + 3y = -1\).

qs.q: Determine whether the given ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \((3, -2)\); \(2x + 5y = -4\).

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.7x + 0.06y = -2.5\).
qs.s: Substitute \((-4, 5)\) into the equation: \(0.7(-4) + 0.06(5) = -2.8 + 0.30 = -2.5\). Since both sides are equal, \((-4, 5)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(-0.5x + 0.08y = 1.82\).
qs.s: Substitute \((-3, 4)\) into the equation: \(-0.5(-3) + 0.08(4) = 1.5 + 0.32 = 1.82\). Since both sides equal \(1.82\), \((-3, 4)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.05x - 1.4y = 3.1\).
qs.s: Substitute \((6, -2)\) into the equation: \(0.05(6) - 1.4(-2) = 0.30 + 2.8 = 3.1\). Since the left side equals the right side, \((6, -2)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.25x - 1.2y = 5.6\).
qs.s: Substitute \((8, -3)\) into the equation: \(0.25(8) - 1.2(-3) = 2.0 + 3.6 = 5.6\). Since the statement is true, \((8, -3)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.06x - 1.3y = 5.5\).
qs.s: Substitute \((5, -4)\) into the equation: \(0.06(5) - 1.3(-4) = 0.30 + 5.2 = 5.5\). Since the left side equals \(5.5\), \((5, -4)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(1.5(2x - 1) - 0.4(y + 5) = 2.2x - 1.5\).
qs.s: Substitute \((1, -3)\) into both sides: the left side evaluates to \(1.5(1) - 0.4(2) = 0.7\), and the right side evaluates to \(2.2(1) - 1.5 = 0.7\). Since both sides are equal, \((1, -3)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.025x - 0.15y = 14.5\).
qs.s: Substitute \((400, -30)\) into the equation: \(0.025(400) - 0.15(-30) = 10 + 4.5 = 14.5\). Since both sides equal \(14.5\), \((400, -30)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(\frac{2}{3}x - 1.5y = 8.5\).
qs.s: Substitute \((6, -3)\) into the equation: \(\frac{2}{3}(6) - 1.5(-3) = 4 + 4.5 = 8.5\). Since the left side equals the right side, \((6, -3)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.4x - 0.7y + 1.2 = 0.1x + 0.8y - 3.3\).
qs.s: Substitute \((-10, 1)\) into both sides: the left side evaluates to \(0.4(-10) - 0.7(1) + 1.2 = -3.5\), and the right side evaluates to \(0.1(-10) + 0.8(1) - 3.3 = -3.5\). Since both sides are equal, \((-10, 1)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Determine which ordered pair is a solution to the equation: \(0.5(x - 4) - 1.2(y + 3) = 5.4\).
qs.s: Substitute \((10, -5)\) into the left side: \(0.5(10 - 4) - 1.2(-5 + 3) = 0.5(6) - 1.2(-2) = 3.0 + 2.4 = 5.4\). Since the left side equals the right side, \((10, -5)\) is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(44x - 54y = 64\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, -\frac{1}{6}\right)\) into the equation: \(44\left(\frac{5}{4}\right) - 54\left(-\frac{1}{6}\right) = 55 - (-9) = 55 + 9 = 64\). The left side matches the right side, so it is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(45x - 32y = 42\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(\frac{2}{5}, -\frac{3}{4}\right)\) into the equation: \(45\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) - 32\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = 18 - (-24) = 18 + 24 = 42\). Since the equality holds, this ordered pair satisfies the equation.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(28x - 24y = 37\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) into the equation: \(28\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) - 24\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = 21 - (-16) = 21 + 16 = 37\). Since both sides are equal, this ordered pair is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(56x + 33y = 1\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(-\frac{3}{8}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) into the equation: \(56\left(-\frac{3}{8}\right) + 33\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -21 + 22 = 1\). Both sides are equal, so the ordered pair is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(42x - 35y = -49\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{4}{5}\right)\) into the equation: \(42\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) - 35\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) = -21 - 28 = -49\). Since the left side equals the right side, it is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(4(3x + 2) - 3(5y - 1) + 6x = 36\)?
qs.s: Simplifying the equation gives \(18x - 15y + 11 = 36\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) yields \(18\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) - 15\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) + 11 = 15 - (-10) + 11 = 36\), so the ordered pair satisfies the equation.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(12(2x - 1) - 15(3y + 2) = -17\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(y = -\frac{1}{5}\) to get \(12\left(2\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 1\right) - 15\left(3\left(-\frac{1}{5}\right) + 2\right) = 12\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) - 15\left(\frac{7}{5}\right) = 4 - 21 = -17\). This matches the right-hand side, so the ordered pair is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(15x - 8y + 5 = 3x + 16y - 17\)?
qs.s: Substituting \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}\right)\) gives \(15\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) - 8\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) + 5 = -5 - 6 + 5 = -6\) on the left side, and \(3\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) + 16\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) - 17 = -1 + 12 - 17 = -6\) on the right side. Since both sides equal \(-6\), it is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(\frac{4x + 1}{3} - \frac{6y - 1}{5} = 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) into the expression: \(\frac{4(1/2) + 1}{3} - \frac{6(-2/3) - 1}{5} = \frac{3}{3} - \frac{-5}{5} = 1 - (-1) = 2\). The left side equals 2, confirming it is a solution.

qs.q: Which of the following ordered pairs is a solution to the equation \(144x - 112y = 109\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(\left(\frac{5}{12}, -\frac{7}{16}\right)\) into the equation: \(144\left(\frac{5}{12}\right) - 112\left(-\frac{7}{16}\right) = 12(5) - 7(-7) = 60 + 49 = 109\). Since the left side equals \(109\), this ordered pair satisfies the equation.

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(4x + 3y = 24\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) into the equation: \(4x + 3(0) = 24\), which gives \(4x = 24\). Dividing both sides by 4 yields \(x = 6\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(2x + 7y = 14\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) into the equation: \(2x + 7(0) = 14\), which gives \(2x = 14\). Dividing both sides by 2 yields \(x = 7\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(2x + 5y = 10\).
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(2(0) + 5y = 10\), which gives \(5y = 10\). Dividing both sides by 5 yields \(y = 2\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3x + 4y = 12\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) into the equation: \(3x + 4(0) = 12\), which gives \(3x = 12\). Dividing both sides by 3 yields \(x = 4\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(5x + 3y = 15\).
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(5(0) + 3y = 15\), which gives \(3y = 15\). Dividing both sides by 3 yields \(y = 5\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3(x - 4) + 2y = 18\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) to get \(3(x - 4) = 18\). Dividing both sides by 3 gives \(x - 4 = 6\), so \(x = 10\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 3y - 45 = 0\).
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(5(0) - 3y - 45 = 0\), which simplifies to \(-3y = 45\). Dividing both sides by \(-3\) yields \(y = -15\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(7x - 4y + 5x + 10y = 72\).
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(-4y + 10y = 72\), which simplifies to \(6y = 72\). Dividing both sides by 6 yields \(y = 12\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(14x - 9y = 252\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) to get \(14x = 252\). Dividing both sides by 14 yields \(x = 18\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(8x + 3y = 48 - 4x\).
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, substitute \(y = 0\) to get \(8x = 48 - 4x\). Adding \(4x\) to both sides gives \(12x = 48\), which yields \(x = 4\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3x - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(3(0) - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{1}{2}y = 3\). Multiplying both sides by \(-2\) gives \(y = -6\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(4x + \frac{1}{2}y = 4\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(4(0) + \frac{1}{2}y = 4\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{2}y = 4\). Multiplying both sides by \(2\) gives \(y = 8\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3x + \frac{1}{2}y = 6\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(3(0) - \frac{1}{2}y = 6\), which simplifies to \(\frac{1}{2}y = 6\). Multiplying both sides by \(2\) gives \(y = 12\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3x - \frac{1}{5}y = 3\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(3(0) - \frac{1}{5}y = 3\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{1}{5}y = 3\). Multiplying both sides by \(-5\) gives \(y = -15\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(2x - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation: \(2(0) - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{1}{3}y = 1\). Multiplying both sides by \(-3\) gives \(y = -3\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(5x - \frac{2}{3}y + 4 = 2x + 16\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation to get \(-\frac{2}{3}y + 4 = 16\). Subtract \(4\) to get \(-\frac{2}{3}y = 12\), then multiply by \(-\frac{3}{2}\) to obtain \(y = -18\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(6x - \frac{1}{3}y + 8 = 2x + \frac{1}{6}y - 2\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(-\frac{1}{3}y + 8 = \frac{1}{6}y - 2\). Subtracting \(\frac{1}{6}y\) and \(8\) gives \(-\frac{1}{2}y = -10\), and multiplying by \(-2\) yields \(y = 20\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{8}y - 5 = \frac{1}{4}x + 5\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(-\frac{5}{8}y - 5 = 5\). Add \(5\) to both sides to obtain \(-\frac{5}{8}y = 10\), then multiply by \(-\frac{8}{5}\) to find \(y = -16\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(3(2x - 5) - \frac{3}{4}y = 6\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(3(-5) - \frac{3}{4}y = 6\), which simplifies to \(-15 - \frac{3}{4}y = 6\). Adding \(15\) gives \(-\frac{3}{4}y = 21\), and multiplying by \(-\frac{4}{3}\) yields \(y = -28\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(2(3x - 4) - \frac{2}{5}y = 4 - 2x\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, substitute \(x = 0\) to get \(2(-4) - \frac{2}{5}y = 4\), which simplifies to \(-8 - \frac{2}{5}y = 4\). Adding \(8\) gives \(-\frac{2}{5}y = 12\), and multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{2}\) yields \(y = -30\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3x + 5y = 14\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) and \(y = 1\) into \(3x + 5y = 14\) to get \(3(3) + 5(1) = 9 + 5 = 14\). Thus, \((3, 1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(2x + 3y = 7\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2\) and \(y = 1\) into \(2x + 3y = 7\) to get \(2(2) + 3(1) = 4 + 3 = 7\), which is true. Therefore, \((2, 1)\) is a point on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(4x + 3y = 10\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 1\) and \(y = 2\) into \(4x + 3y = 10\) to get \(4(1) + 3(2) = 4 + 6 = 10\), so \((1, 2)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 3y = 4\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -1\) and \(y = -3\) into \(5x - 3y = 4\) to get \(5(-1) - 3(-3) = -5 + 9 = 4\), which verifies that \((-1, -3)\) is on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3x - 2y = 8\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2\) and \(y = -1\) into \(3x - 2y = 8\) to get \(3(2) - 2(-1) = 6 + 2 = 8\), confirming that \((2, -1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(8x + 5y = 59\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) and \(y = 7\) into \(8x + 5y = 59\) to get \(8(3) + 5(7) = 24 + 35 = 59\), which verifies that \((3, 7)\) is on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3(x + 2) - 5y = 31\)?
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying gives \(3x - 5y = 25\). Substituting \((5, -2)\) gives \(3(5) - 5(-2) = 15 + 10 = 25\), confirming it lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 2y = 2x + 4y + 18\)?
qs.s: Combine like terms to get \(3x - 6y = 18\), or \(x - 2y = 6\). Substituting \((4, -1)\) yields \(4 - 2(-1) = 4 + 2 = 6\), so \((4, -1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(4(x - 3) + 3(y + 1) = 7\)?
qs.s: Expand to get \(4x - 12 + 3y + 3 = 7\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = 16\). Substituting \((1, 4)\) gives \(4(1) + 3(4) = 4 + 12 = 16\), so \((1, 4)\) is on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(7x - 4y = 47\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5\) and \(y = -3\) into \(7x - 4y = 47\) to obtain \(7(5) - 4(-3) = 35 + 12 = 47\), showing that \((5, -3)\) is on the graph.

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{1}{3}x - 0.5y = 2\)
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(-0.5y = 2\), then divide by \(-0.5\) to find \(y = -4\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{1}{5}x - 0.5y = 1\)
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(-0.5y = 1\), then divide by \(-0.5\) to find \(y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{1}{4}x + 0.6y = 3\)
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(0.6y = 3\), then divide by \(0.6\) to find \(y = 5\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{1}{2}x - 0.4y = 4\)
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(-0.4y = 4\), then divide by \(-0.4\) to find \(y = -10\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{4}{5}x - 0.5y = 4\)
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(-0.5y = 4\), then divide by \(-0.5\) to find \(y = -8\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{2}{3}x - 0.6y + 9 = 0.2y + 1\)
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) yields \(-0.6y + 9 = 0.2y + 1\). Subtracting \(0.2y\) and \(9\) gives \(-0.8y = -8\), so \(y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{1}{2}(4x - 6) - 1.5y = 0.5(y + 8) + 1\)
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(-3 - 1.5y = 0.5y + 5\). Collecting like terms yields \(-2y = 8\), so \(y = -4\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{3}{4}(x - 8) - 0.5(y + 2) = 1\)
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(\frac{3}{4}(-8) - 0.5(y + 2) = 1\), which simplifies to \(-6 - 0.5y - 1 = 1\). Solving \(-0.5y - 7 = 1\) gives \(-0.5y = 8\), so \(y = -16\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(\frac{5}{6}x - 0.7y + 15 = \frac{1}{3}x + 0.5y - 9\)
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) gives \(-0.7y + 15 = 0.5y - 9\). Rearranging terms results in \(-1.2y = -24\), so \(y = 20\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation: \(0.4(2y - 5) - \frac{3}{5}(x + 10) = 4\)
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) simplifies to \(0.8y - 2 - 6 = 4\), which gives \(0.8y - 8 = 4\). Adding \(8\) and dividing by \(0.8\) yields \(y = 15\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = 3x + 1\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the equation: \(y = 3(-2) + 1 = -6 + 1 = -5\). Thus, \((-2, -5)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -3x + 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2\) into the equation: \(y = -3(2) + 2 = -6 + 2 = -4\). Thus, \((2, -4)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -x + 4\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2\) into the equation: \(y = -(-2) + 4 = 2 + 4 = 6\). Thus, \((-2, 6)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = 2x - 5\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) into the equation: \(y = 2(3) - 5 = 6 - 5 = 1\). Thus, \((3, 1)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -4x - 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 1\) into the equation: \(y = -4(1) - 3 = -4 - 3 = -7\). Thus, \((1, -7)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(3x + 2y = 12\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2\) and \(y = 3\) into the equation: \(3(2) + 2(3) = 6 + 6 = 12\). Since the equation is satisfied, \((2, 3)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(4x - 3y = 9\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) and \(y = 1\) into the equation: \(4(3) - 3(1) = 12 - 3 = 9\). Since the equation is satisfied, \((3, 1)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 5\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 6\) into the equation: \(y = -\frac{2}{3}(6) + 5 = -4 + 5 = 1\). Thus, \((6, 1)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -4\) into the equation: \(y = \frac{3}{4}(-4) - 2 = -3 - 2 = -5\). Thus, \((-4, -5)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair is a point on the graph of the linear equation \(2x + 5y = -10\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5\) and \(y = -4\) into the equation: \(2(5) + 5(-4) = 10 - 20 = -10\). Since the equation is satisfied, \((5, -4)\) lies on the graph of the linear equation.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{3}{5}x + 1\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5\) into \(y = -\frac{3}{5}x + 1\) to get \(y = -\frac{3}{5}(5) + 1 = -3 + 1 = -2\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((5, -2)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4\) into \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\) to get \(y = -\frac{1}{2}(4) + 3 = -2 + 3 = 1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((4, 1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + 4\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 6\) into \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + 4\) to get \(y = -\frac{5}{6}(6) + 4 = -5 + 4 = -1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((6, -1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4\) into \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 2\) to get \(y = -\frac{1}{4}(4) - 2 = -1 - 2 = -3\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((4, -3)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) into \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\) to get \(y = -\frac{2}{3}(3) + 2 = -2 + 2 = 0\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((3, 0)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 6y = 30\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -6\) into \(5x - 6y = 30\) to get \(5(-6) - 6y = 30\), which gives \(-30 - 6y = 30\). Adding \(30\) gives \(-6y = 60\), and dividing by \(-6\) yields \(y = -10\), giving the ordered pair \((-6, -10)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{5}{8}x + 15\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 16\) into \(y = -\frac{5}{8}x + 15\) to get \(y = -\frac{5}{8}(16) + 15 = -10 + 15 = 5\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((16, 5)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3x + 4y = 12\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -4\) into \(3x + 4y = 12\) to get \(3(-4) + 4y = 12\), which simplifies to \(-12 + 4y = 12\). Adding \(12\) gives \(4y = 24\), so \(y = 6\), giving the ordered pair \((-4, 6)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(2x - 5y = 20\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -5\) into \(2x - 5y = 20\) to get \(2(-5) - 5y = 20\), which simplifies to \(-10 - 5y = 20\). Adding \(10\) gives \(-5y = 30\), and dividing by \(-5\) yields \(y = -6\), so the ordered pair is \((-5, -6)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(4x + 3y = -24\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3\) into \(4x + 3y = -24\) to get \(4(-3) + 3y = -24\), so \(-12 + 3y = -24\). Adding \(12\) gives \(3y = -12\), and dividing by \(3\) gives \(y = -4\), so the ordered pair is \((-3, -4)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = \frac{2}{5}x + 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -5\) into the equation to get \(y = \frac{2}{5}(-5) + 3 = -2 + 3 = 1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((-5, 1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = \frac{3}{5}x - 2\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5\) into the equation to get \(y = \frac{3}{5}(5) - 2 = 3 - 2 = 1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((5, 1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 1\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) into the equation to get \(y = -\frac{2}{3}(3) + 1 = -2 + 1 = -1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((3, -1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) into the equation to get \(y = \frac{4}{3}(3) - 3 = 4 - 3 = 1\). Therefore, the ordered pair \((3, 1)\) lies on the graph.

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 3y = 30\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) into the equation to get \(5(3) - 3y = 30\), which gives \(15 - 3y = 30\). Subtracting 15 yields \(-3y = 15\), and dividing by \(-3\) gives \(y = -5\), giving the point \((3, -5)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3x - 4y = 24\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4\) into the equation to get \(3(4) - 4y = 24\), which simplifies to \(12 - 4y = 24\). Subtracting 12 and dividing by \(-4\) yields \(y = -3\), giving the point \((4, -3)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(3x - 8y = -24\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 8\) into the equation to get \(3(8) - 8y = -24\), which simplifies to \(24 - 8y = -24\). Subtracting 24 yields \(-8y = -48\), and dividing by \(-8\) gives \(y = 6\), giving the point \((8, 6)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(4x + 7y = -28\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 7\) into the equation to get \(4(7) + 7y = -28\), which gives \(28 + 7y = -28\). Subtracting 28 yields \(7y = -56\), and dividing by 7 gives \(y = -8\), giving the point \((7, -8)\).

qs.q: Which ordered pair lies on the graph of the linear equation \(2x + 5y = -15\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -5\) into the equation to get \(2(-5) + 5y = -15\), which simplifies to \(-10 + 5y = -15\). Adding 10 gives \(5y = -5\), so \(y = -1\), giving the point \((-5, -1)\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{2}{3}x + 0.5y = 4\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to obtain \(0.5y = 4\). Dividing both sides by \(0.5\) gives \(y = 8\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(0.25x + \frac{2}{3}y = 2\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(\frac{2}{3}y = 2\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{3}{2}\) gives \(y = 3\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{2}{5}x - 0.8y = 4\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 0\) into the equation to get \(-0.8y = 4\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.8\) yields \(y = -5\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(0.5x + \frac{3}{4}y = 3\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\), giving \(\frac{3}{4}y = 3\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{4}{3}\) yields \(y = 4\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{1}{3}x + 0.4y = 2\)?
qs.s: To find the \(y\)-intercept, set \(x = 0\) to get \(0.4y = 2\). Dividing both sides by \(0.4\) gives \(y = 5\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation -\frac{3}{4}(x + 8) + 0.6y = 3$?
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) yields \(-\frac{3}{4}(8) + 0.6y = 3\), which simplifies to \(-6 + 0.6y = 3\). Adding \(6\) gives \(0.6y = 9\), so \(y = 15\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{3}{5}x + 0.5(y - 4) = 4\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(0.5(y - 4) = 4\), which expands to \(0.5y - 2 = 4\). Adding \(2\) gives \(0.5y = 6\), so \(y = 12\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{1}{2}(4x - 6) + 1.4y = 0.2y + 21\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(\frac{1}{2}(-6) + 1.4y = 0.2y + 21\), which simplifies to \(-3 + 1.4y = 0.2y + 21\). Collecting like terms yields \(1.2y = 24\), so \(y = 20\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{4}{5}x - 1.2y + 14 = 2 + 0.8y\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to get \(-1.2y + 14 = 2 + 0.8y\). Rearranging gives \(2y = 12\), which simplifies to \(y = 6\).

qs.q: What is the \(y\)-intercept of the graph of the linear equation \(\frac{2}{3}x + 0.7y = 12 - 0.5y\)?
qs.s: Set \(x = 0\) to obtain \(0.7y = 12 - 0.5y\). Adding \(0.5y\) to both sides gives \(1.2y = 12\), so dividing by \(1.2\) yields \(y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.8x + \frac{1}{2}y = 1\)
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(-0.8x + \frac{1}{2}(0) = 1\), which gives \(-0.8x = 1\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.8\) yields \(x = -1.25\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.5x + \frac{1}{3}y = 1\)
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(-0.5x + \frac{1}{3}(0) = 1\), which gives \(-0.5x = 1\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.5\) yields \(x = -2\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.1x + \frac{1}{6}y = 1\)
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(-0.1x + \frac{1}{6}(0) = 1\), which simplifies to \(-0.1x = 1\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.1\) yields \(x = -10\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.25x + \frac{1}{5}y = 1\)
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(-0.25x + \frac{1}{5}(0) = 1\), which gives \(-0.25x = 1\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.25\) yields \(x = -4\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.2x + \frac{1}{4}y = 1\)
qs.s: To find the \(x\)-intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(-0.2x + \frac{1}{4}(0) = 1\), which gives \(-0.2x = 1\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.2\) yields \(x = -5\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.8x - 14 = -\frac{2}{5}y - 2\)
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-0.8x - 14 = -2\), and add \(14\) to both sides to obtain \(-0.8x = 12\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.8\) yields \(x = -15\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-1.2x + \frac{3}{4}y + 9 = 3\)
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-1.2x + 9 = 3\), so \(-1.2x = -6\). Dividing both sides by \(-1.2\) yields \(x = 5\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.75x + 8 = -\frac{1}{3}y + 20\)
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-0.75x + 8 = 20\), and subtract \(8\) from both sides to get \(-0.75x = 12\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.75\) yields \(x = -16\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.4x + \frac{3}{5}y - 7 = 5\)
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-0.4x - 7 = 5\), and add \(7\) to both sides to obtain \(-0.4x = 12\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.4\) yields \(x = -30\).

qs.q: Find the \(x\)-intercept of the linear equation: \(-0.6x + \frac{2}{3}y = 6\)
qs.s: Set \(y = 0\) to get \(-0.6x = 6\). Dividing both sides by \(-0.6\) yields \(x = -10\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(x = 2\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: The equation \(x = 2\) indicates that the \(x\)-value is constant at \(2\) for all values of \(y\), representing a vertical line passing through \((2, 0)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(y = 1\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: The equation \(y = 1\) defines a line where every point has a \(y\)-coordinate of \(1\), resulting in a horizontal line through \((0, 1)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(y = -5\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: The equation \(y = -5\) indicates that the \(y\)-value is constant at \(-5\) for all values of \(x\), representing a horizontal line passing through \((0, -5)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(x = -3\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: The equation \(x = -3\) means that every point on the line has an \(x\)-coordinate of \(-3\), which forms a vertical line passing through \((-3, 0)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(y = 4\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: The equation \(y = 4\) means that every point on the line has a \(y\)-coordinate of \(4\), which forms a horizontal line passing through \((0, 4)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(3x - 15 = 0\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: Adding \(15\) to both sides gives \(3x = 15\), and dividing by \(3\) yields \(x = 5\). The graph of \(x = 5\) is a vertical line passing through \((5, 0)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(3(y + 1) = y + 7\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: Expanding gives \(3y + 3 = y + 7\), and solving for \(y\) yields \(2y = 4\), or \(y = 2\). The graph of \(y = 2\) is a horizontal line passing through \((0, 2)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(-4y + 7 = 19\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(7\) from both sides gives \(-4y = 12\), and dividing by \(-4\) yields \(y = -3\). The graph of \(y = -3\) is a horizontal line passing through \((0, -3)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(5x - 4 = 2x + 14\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(2x\) and adding \(4\) to both sides gives \(3x = 18\), so \(x = 6\). The graph of \(x = 6\) is a vertical line passing through \((6, 0)\).

qs.q: Which statement correctly describes the graph of the linear equation \(2y + 8 = 0\) on a Cartesian plane?
qs.s: Subtracting \(8\) from both sides gives \(2y = -8\), and dividing by \(2\) yields \(y = -4\). The graph of \(y = -4\) is a horizontal line passing through \((0, -4)\).

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a laptop, in hundreds of dollars, is modeled by \(V = -\frac{2}{3}t + 8\), where \(t\) is the number of years since it was purchased. Use the equation to determine what the laptop is worth, in dollars, after 6 years.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 6\) into the equation to get \(V = -\frac{2}{3}(6) + 8 = -4 + 8 = 4\). Since \(V\) is in hundreds of dollars, the laptop is worth \(4 \times 100 = \$400\).

qs.q: The amount of fuel \(A\), in litres, remaining in a vehicle's tank is modeled by \(A = -\frac{4}{3}t + 52\), where \(t\) is the driving time in hours. What is the amount of fuel remaining, in litres, after 9 hours of driving?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 9\) into the equation to calculate \(A = -\frac{4}{3}(9) + 52 = -12 + 52 = 40\text{ L}\).

qs.q: The height \(h\), in centimetres, of a burning candle is given by \(h = -\frac{3}{2}t + 24\), where \(t\) is the time in hours since it was lit. What is the height of the candle, in centimetres, after 6 hours?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 6\) into the formula to find \(h = -\frac{3}{2}(6) + 24 = -9 + 24 = 15\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The water level \(h\), in metres, in a storage reservoir is given by \(h = -\frac{1}{2}t + 7\), where \(t\) is the time in days since draining began. Use the equation to find the water level, in metres, after 6 days.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 6\) into the equation to obtain \(h = -\frac{1}{2}(6) + 7 = -3 + 7 = 4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The balance \(B\), in hundreds of dollars, in a student's savings account is modeled by \(B = -\frac{1}{4}w + 5\), where \(w\) is the number of weeks since the start of the semester. What is the account balance, in dollars, after 12 weeks?
qs.s: Substitute \(w = 12\) into the model to find \(B = -\frac{1}{4}(12) + 5 = -3 + 5 = 2\). Since \(B\) represents hundreds of dollars, the balance is \(2 \times 100 = \$200\).

qs.q: A company models its weekly profit \(P\), in dollars, using the equation \(P = 48n - (18n + 750)\), where \(n\) is the number of items manufactured and sold. Use this model to determine the profit, in dollars, when 60 items are sold.
qs.s: Simplify the expression to \(P = 30n - 750\). Substituting \(n = 60\) gives \(P = 30(60) - 750 = 1800 - 750 = \$1050\).

qs.q: The resale value \(V\) of a tractor, in thousands of dollars, is modeled by \(V = -\frac{7}{4}t + 70\), where \(t\) is the age of the tractor in years. According to this model, after how many years will the tractor's resale value reach $28 000?
qs.s: Set \(V = 28\) to obtain \(28 = -\frac{7}{4}t + 70\), which rearranges to \(\frac{7}{4}t = 42\). Solving for \(t\) gives \(t = 42 \times \frac{4}{7} = 24\) years.

qs.q: A community pool is being drained. The relationship between the draining time \(t\), in hours, and the volume of water \(W\), in hundreds of cubic metres, is given by the linear equation \(5t + 8W = 120\). What is the remaining volume of water, in cubic metres, after 8 hours of draining?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 8\) to get \(5(8) + 8W = 120\), giving \(8W = 80\), or \(W = 10\). Since \(W\) is measured in hundreds of cubic metres, the remaining volume is \(10 \times 100 = 1000\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: The market value \(V\) of an industrial machine, in hundreds of dollars, is modeled by \(V = -\frac{5}{3}t + 150\), where \(t\) is the time in years since it was purchased. How much value, in dollars, does the machine lose between year 3 and year 12?

The temperature \(T\), in degrees Celsius, of a cooling metal alloy inside a chamber is modeled by \(T = -\frac{5}{6}m + 85\), where \(m\) is the cooling time in minutes. What is the temperature of the alloy, in degrees Celsius, after 1 hour and 18 minutes?
qs.s: Convert the time to minutes: \(1\text{ h } 18\text{ min} = 78\text{ min}\). Substituting \(m = 78\) gives \(T = -\frac{5}{6}(78) + 85 = -65 + 85 = 20^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The annual consumption of bottled water per person in a certain country, \(W\) (in litres), can be approximated by \(W = 1.5t + 35\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2010. Estimate the annual bottled water consumption per person in 2018.
qs.s: The year 2018 corresponds to \(t = 2018 - 2010 = 8\). Substituting into the equation gives \(W = 1.5(8) + 35 = 12 + 35 = 47\text{ litres}\).

qs.q: The average cost of a cinema ticket, \(C\) (in dollars), in a metropolitan area can be approximated by \(C = 0.35t + 8.50\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2000. Estimate the average cost of a cinema ticket in 2020.

The average monthly mobile data usage per subscriber, \(D\) (in gigabytes), can be approximated by \(D = 0.8t + 3.2\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2012. Estimate the average monthly data usage in 2017.
qs.s: The year 2017 corresponds to \(t = 2017 - 2012 = 5\). Substituting \(t = 5\) into the model gives \(D = 0.8(5) + 3.2 = 4.0 + 3.2 = 7.2\text{ GB}\).

qs.q: The average height, \(H\) (in metres), of a stand of young trees can be approximated by \(H = 0.75t + 4.5\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2010. Estimate the average height of the trees in 2016.
qs.s: The year 2016 corresponds to \(t = 2016 - 2010 = 6\). Substituting \(t = 6\) yields \(H = 0.75(6) + 4.5 = 4.5 + 4.5 = 9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The mass of recyclable materials, \(M\) (in kilograms), collected annually per household in a city can be approximated by \(M = 2.4t + 150\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2005. Estimate the mass of recyclable materials collected per household in 2015.
qs.s: The year 2015 corresponds to \(t = 2015 - 2005 = 10\). Substituting \(t = 10\) into the equation gives \(M = 2.4(10) + 150 = 24 + 150 = 174\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: The temperature, \(T\) (in degrees Celsius), at an altitude of \(h\) hundreds of metres above sea level is modeled by \(T = -\frac{3}{5}h + 22\). Estimate the temperature at an altitude of \(2500\text{ metres}\).
qs.s: Since \(h\) is in hundreds of metres, \(2500\text{ metres}\) corresponds to \(h = 25\). Evaluating the model gives \(T = -\frac{3}{5}(25) + 22 = -15 + 22 = 7^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The average price of a solar panel, \(P\) (in dollars), can be approximated by \(P = -18.5t + 450\), where \(t\) is the number of years since 2010. According to this model, in which year will the average price drop to \(\$117\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(P = 117\) into the equation to get \(117 = -18.5t + 450\), which simplifies to \(18.5t = 333\), giving \(t = 18\). Adding 18 years to the base year 2010 gives 2028.

qs.q: A town's water reservoir drains during an inspection. The relationship between the remaining water volume, \(W\) (in thousands of litres), and the time elapsed, \(t\) (in hours), is modeled by the linear equation \(5t + 6W = 2100\). Estimate the volume of water remaining after 48 hours.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 48\) into the equation to get \(5(48) + 6W = 2100\), so \(240 + 6W = 2100\). Subtracting 240 gives \(6W = 1860\), which simplifies to \(W = 310\text{ thousand litres}\).

qs.q: The total operating cost, \(C\) (in dollars), of a commercial delivery van is given by \(C = 0.45k + 3200\), where \(k\) is the total distance driven in kilometres. If a courier company retires a van when its total operating cost reaches \(\$14\,000\), how many kilometres will the van have been driven?
qs.s: Substitute \(C = 14\,000\) to obtain \(14\,000 = 0.45k + 3200\), so \(0.45k = 10\,800\). Dividing both sides by 0.45 yields \(k = 24\,000\text{ km}\).

qs.q: The depth of water, \(d\) (in metres), in a reservoir during a dry season is modeled by \(d = 85 - \frac{3}{5}w\), where \(w\) is the number of weeks since the beginning of summer. How many weeks will it take for the water depth to drop from \(70\text{ metres}\) to \(52\text{ metres}\)?
qs.s: Find the time for each depth: \(70 = 85 - \frac{3}{5}w\) gives \(w = 25\), and \(52 = 85 - \frac{3}{5}w\) gives \(w = 55\). The time elapsed for this drop is \(55 - 25 = 30\text{ weeks}\).

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a delivery van, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(V + 35t = 420\), where \(t\) is the age of the van in years. If the van was bought new 3 years ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 5 years from now?
qs.s: The age of the van 5 years from now will be \(t = 3 + 5 = 8\) years. Substituting \(t = 8\) gives \(V + 35(8) = 420\), which simplifies to \(V = 140\) hundred dollars, or $14,000.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a commercial lawnmower, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(V + 15t = 180\), where \(t\) is the age of the mower in years. If the mower was bought new 4 years ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 2 years from now?
qs.s: The mower's age 2 years from now will be \(t = 4 + 2 = 6\) years. Substituting into the equation gives \(V + 15(6) = 180\), so \(V = 90\) hundred dollars, which is $9,000.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of office computer equipment, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(V + 40t = 500\), where \(t\) is the age of the equipment in years. If the equipment was bought new 1 year ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 4 years from now?
qs.s: Four years from now, the equipment will be \(t = 1 + 4 = 5\) years old. Substituting \(t = 5\) into the equation yields \(V + 40(5) = 500\), so \(V = 300\) hundred dollars, or $30,000.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a boat, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(V + 20t = 260\), where \(t\) is the age of the boat in years. If the boat was bought new 5 years ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 3 years from now?
qs.s: The age of the boat 3 years from now will be \(t = 5 + 3 = 8\) years. Solving \(V + 20(8) = 260\) gives \(V = 100\) hundred dollars, which equals $10,000.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a motorcycle, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(V + 12t = 160\), where \(t\) is the age of the motorcycle in years. If the motorcycle was bought new 2 years ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 3 years from now?
qs.s: The age of the motorcycle 3 years from now will be \(t = 2 + 3 = 5\) years. Substituting \(t = 5\) gives \(V + 12(5) = 160\), so \(V = 100\) hundred dollars, which equals $10,000.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a factory machine, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(2V + 75t = 950\), where \(t\) is the age of the machine in years. If the machine was purchased new 4 years ago, in how many years from now will its value be $25,000?
qs.s: A value of $25,000 corresponds to \(V = 250\), so \(2(250) + 75t = 950\) gives \(75t = 450\), or \(t = 6\) years total age. Since the machine is already 4 years old, it will reach this value in \(6 - 4 = 2\) years.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a school bus, in hundreds of dollars, satisfies the equation \(2V + 35t = 880\), where \(t\) is the age of the bus in years. A school district bought the bus when it was already 2 years old, and has owned it for 4 years. What will the value of the bus be, in dollars, 6 years from now?
qs.s: The current age of the bus is \(2 + 4 = 6\) years, so 6 years from now its age will be \(t = 6 + 6 = 12\) years. Substituting \(t = 12\) gives \(2V + 35(12) = 880\), so \(2V = 460\) and \(V = 230\) hundred dollars, or $23,000.

qs.q: A company owns two machines whose values, in hundreds of dollars, decrease over time according to \(V_1 + 30t = 400\) and \(V_2 + 45t = 550\), where \(t\) is the age in years. Both machines were bought new 3 years ago. What will be the difference in their values, in dollars, 2 years from now?
qs.s: Two years from now, the machines are \(t = 3 + 2 = 5\) years old. Evaluating at \(t = 5\) gives \(V_1 = 400 - 150 = 250\) ($25,000) and \(V_2 = 550 - 225 = 325\) ($32,500), so the difference is $32,500 - $25,000 = $7,500.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of a commercial printing press, in hundreds of dollars, is given by \(5V + 120t = 3000\), where \(t\) is the age of the press in years. If the press was purchased new 5 years ago, in how many years from now will its value reach a scrap value of $12,000?
qs.s: A scrap value of $12,000 corresponds to \(V = 120\), so \(5(120) + 120t = 3000\) yields \(120t = 2400\), meaning \(t = 20\) years total age. Since the press is already 5 years old, it will reach scrap value in \(20 - 5 = 15\) years.

qs.q: The value \(V\) of an industrial generator, in hundreds of dollars, is modeled by the equation \(4V + 45t = 1440\), where \(t\) is the age of the generator in years. If the generator was purchased new 6 years ago, what will its value be, in dollars, 10 years from now?
qs.s: Ten years from now, the generator will be \(t = 6 + 10 = 16\) years old. Substituting \(t = 16\) gives \(4V + 45(16) = 1440\), so \(4V = 720\), yielding \(V = 180\) hundred dollars, or $18,000.

qs.q: On a cold morning, the outdoor temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) \(t\) hours after 6:00 am is modeled by \(T - 2t = -11\). What is the estimated temperature at 10:00 am?
qs.s: At 10:00 am, \(t = 4\) hours after 6:00 am. Substituting \(t = 4\) into \(T - 2(4) = -11\) gives \(T - 8 = -11\), so \(T = -3^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The height of a burning candle, \(h\) (in centimetres), after burning for \(t\) hours is given by \(2t + h = 18\). What is the estimated height of the candle after 5 hours?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 5\) into \(2(5) + h = 18\) to get \(10 + h = 18\), which gives \(h = 8\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) on a winter afternoon is related to the number of hours after 1:00 pm, \(h\), by the linear equation \(T + 3h = 5\). What is the estimated temperature at 4:00 pm that day?
qs.s: At 4:00 pm, \(h = 3\) hours after 1:00 pm. Substituting \(h = 3\) into \(T + 3(3) = 5\) gives \(T + 9 = 5\), so \(T = -4^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A hiker's elevation \(E\) (in metres) \(t\) hours after starting a descent from a mountain pass is modeled by \(E + 50t = 650\). What is the hiker's estimated elevation after 3 hours?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 3\) into \(E + 50(3) = 650\) to get \(E + 150 = 650\), so \(E = 500\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The water depth \(d\) (in centimetres) in a draining pool is related to the number of minutes after opening the drain, \(m\), by the equation \(d + 4m = 80\). What is the estimated water depth after 15 minutes?
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 15\) into the equation to get \(d + 4(15) = 80\), which simplifies to \(d + 60 = 80\), so \(d = 20\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) on a mountain summit is modeled by \(2T + 3h = -10\), where \(h\) is the number of hours after 12:00 noon. By how many degrees Celsius does the estimated temperature drop between 2:00 pm and 6:00 pm?
qs.s: At 2:00 pm (\(h = 2\)), \(2T + 6 = -10\) gives \(T = -8^\circ\text{C}\), and at 6:00 pm (\(h = 6\)), \(2T + 18 = -10\) gives \(T = -14^\circ\text{C}\). The temperature drops by \(-8^\circ\text{C} - (-14^\circ\text{C}) = 6^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) in a cold storage unit \(t\) hours after a setting adjustment is modeled by \(3T + 4t = -10\). If the adjustment was made at 6:00 pm, what is the estimated temperature at 9:30 pm?
qs.s: From 6:00 pm to 9:30 pm is \(t = 3.5\) hours. Substituting into \(3T + 4(3.5) = -10\) gives \(3T + 14 = -10\), so \(3T = -24\) and \(T = -8^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A deep-sea research probe's depth \(D\) (in metres below sea level) \(t\) minutes after release is modeled by the equation \(3D - 40t = 450\). What is the probe's estimated depth after 15 minutes?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 15\) into \(3D - 40(15) = 450\) to get \(3D - 600 = 450\). Adding 600 gives \(3D = 1050\), so \(D = 350\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) in a mountain valley is modeled by \(2T + 5h = 8\), where \(h\) is the number of hours after 11:00 am. At what time is the temperature estimated to reach \(-6^\circ\text{C}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(T = -6\) into \(2(-6) + 5h = 8\) to get \(-12 + 5h = 8\), which gives \(5h = 20\), or \(h = 4\). Adding 4 hours to 11:00 am gives 3:00 pm.

qs.q: An airplane descends towards an airport. Its altitude \(A\) (in metres) is related to the descent time \(t\) (in minutes) by the equation \(A + 150t = 10\,500\). What is the airplane's estimated altitude after \(1\) hour of descent?
qs.s: Convert 1 hour to 60 minutes, then substitute \(t = 60\) into \(A + 150(60) = 10\,500\) to get \(A + 9000 = 10\,500\), so \(A = 1500\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The depth of snow \(S\) (in cm) on a mountain road \(h\) hours after 8:00 am is modeled by the equation \(S - 3h = 14\). Use this equation to estimate the snow depth at 1:00 pm that day.
qs.s: From 8:00 am to 1:00 pm is \(h = 5\) hours. Substituting \(h = 5\) gives \(S - 3(5) = 14\), so \(S - 15 = 14\), which yields \(S = 29\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The volume of water \(V\) (in liters) remaining in a reservoir \(t\) hours after 9:00 am is modeled by \(V + 4t = 60\). What is the estimated volume of water remaining at 3:00 pm that day?
qs.s: From 9:00 am to 3:00 pm is \(t = 6\) hours. Substituting \(t = 6\) into \(V + 4t = 60\) gives \(V + 24 = 60\), so \(V = 36\text{ L}\).

qs.q: The overnight temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) in a valley \(h\) hours after 6:00 pm is given by the linear equation \(T + 2h = 5\). Estimate the temperature at 11:00 pm that night.
qs.s: From 6:00 pm to 11:00 pm, \(h = 5\) hours have passed. Substituting \(h = 5\) into \(T + 2h = 5\) gives \(T + 10 = 5\), so \(T = -5^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: On a winter day, the temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) \(t\) hours after 12:00 pm is modeled by the linear equation \(T + 3t = -1\). What is the estimated temperature at 4:00 pm that day?
qs.s: At 4:00 pm, \(t = 4\) hours after 12:00 pm. Substituting \(t = 4\) into \(T + 3t = -1\) gives \(T + 12 = -1\), which simplifies to \(T = -13^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A hot-air balloon's altitude \(A\) (in meters) \(t\) minutes after beginning its descent is modeled by the linear equation \(A + 15t = 450\). What is the estimated altitude of the balloon after \(8\text{ minutes}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 8\) into the equation to get \(A + 15(8) = 450\), which simplifies to \(A + 120 = 450\), giving \(A = 330\text{ m}\).

qs.q: During an arctic expedition, the temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) \(t\) hours after 6:00 am is modeled by \(5(T + 4) + 6t = -10\). Estimate the temperature at 1:30 pm on the same day.
qs.s: From 6:00 am to 1:30 pm is \(t = 7.5\) hours. Substituting gives \(5(T + 4) + 6(7.5) = -10\), so \(5(T + 4) + 45 = -10\), which simplifies to \(5(T + 4) = -55\), \(T + 4 = -11\), and \(T = -15^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) inside an industrial freezer \(m\) minutes after a cooling cycle starts is modeled by \(4T + 3m = 80\). If the cycle begins at 1:15 pm, estimate the temperature at 2:35 pm that afternoon.
qs.s: The elapsed time between 1:15 pm and 2:35 pm is \(m = 80\) minutes. Substituting gives \(4T + 3(80) = 80\), so \(4T + 240 = 80\), which leads to \(4T = -160\) and \(T = -40^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The outdoor temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) at a research station \(h\) hours after 9:30 am is approximated by the linear equation \(2T + 6h = -5\). Estimate the temperature at 2:00 pm on the same day.
qs.s: From 9:30 am to 2:00 pm is \(h = 4.5\) hours. Substituting \(h = 4.5\) gives \(2T + 6(4.5) = -5\), so \(2T + 27 = -5\), which leads to \(2T = -32\) and \(T = -16^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A submarine's depth \(D\) (in meters below sea level) \(m\) minutes after beginning a descent is modeled by \(4D - 15m = 180\). If the dive starts at 2:00 pm, what is the estimated depth of the submarine at 2:24 pm?
qs.s: The time elapsed is \(m = 24\) minutes. Substituting gives \(4D - 15(24) = 180\), so \(4D - 360 = 180\), which gives \(4D = 540\) and \(D = 135\text{ m}\).

qs.q: On a cold evening, the temperature \(T\) (in \({}^\circ\text{C}\)) \(h\) hours after 12:00 pm (noon) is modeled by \(3T + 8h = 24\). At what time is the temperature estimated to reach \(-16^\circ\text{C}\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(T = -16\) into the equation to get \(3(-16) + 8h = 24\), giving \(-48 + 8h = 24\). Adding \(48\) gives \(8h = 72\), so \(h = 9\), which corresponds to 9:00 pm.

qs.q: Elena earns money by walking dogs (\(d\)) for $8 per hour and babysitting (\(b\)) for $10 per hour. Last weekend, she earned a total of $74. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(b\) when \(d = 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 3\) into \(8d + 10b = 74\) to get \(24 + 10b = 74\). Subtracting 24 yields \(10b = 50\), so \(b = 5\).

qs.q: Tickets for a school play cost $4 for students (\(s\)) and $6 for adults (\(a\)). The drama club collected a total of $48. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(a\) when \(s = 6\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 6\) into the equation \(4s + 6a = 48\) to get \(24 + 6a = 48\). Subtracting 24 yields \(6a = 24\), so \(a = 4\).

qs.q: In a basketball game, a team scored 38 points entirely from 2-point field goals (\(x\)) and 3-point field goals (\(y\)). If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(y\) when \(x = 7\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 7\) into \(2x + 3y = 38\) to get \(14 + 3y = 38\). Subtracting 14 yields \(3y = 24\), so \(y = 8\).

qs.q: A student buys notebooks (\(n\)) for $3 each and binders (\(b\)) for $5 each, spending exactly $36. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(b\) when \(n = 7\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(n = 7\) into \(3n + 5b = 36\) to get \(21 + 5b = 36\). Subtracting 21 gives \(5b = 15\), so \(b = 3\).

qs.q: A student has a collection of quarters (\(q\)) and dimes (\(d\)) totaling 95¢. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(d\) when \(q = 3\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(q = 3\) into the equation \(25q + 10d = 95\) to get \(75 + 10d = 95\). Subtracting 75 yields \(10d = 20\), so \(d = 2\).

qs.q: A catering service charges a $75 setup fee plus $14 per child plate (\(c\)) and $22 per adult plate (\(a\)). A family spent a total of $595 on a catered dinner. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(a\) when \(c = 12\)?

A shopper buys peaches (\(p\)) for $1.25 per pound and blueberries (\(b\)) for $3.50 per pound, spending a total of $27.50. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(b\) when \(p = 8\)?

A community theater charges a $50 booking fee plus $12 per student ticket (\(s\)) and $20 per adult ticket (\(a\)). A school group spent a total of $530 for a private performance. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(a\) when \(s = 25\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 25\) into \(12s + 20a + 50 = 530\) to get \(300 + 50 + 20a = 530\), which simplifies to \(350 + 20a = 530\). Subtracting 350 gives \(20a = 180\), so \(a = 9\).

qs.q: A print shop charges a $35 setup fee plus $0.20 per black-and-white flyer (\(b\)) and $0.75 per color flyer (\(c\)). A customer's total bill was $160.00. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(c\) when \(b = 250\)?

A cargo truck carries small crates (\(s\)) weighing 25 kg each and large crates (\(L\)) weighing 40 kg each. The truck also carries 150 kg of standard equipment, and the total load is 1350 kg. If the linear equation modeling this relationship is graphed, what is the value of \(L\) when \(s = 32\)?
The points \((3, -4), (3, 2),\) and \((-2, -1)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has the smallest \(y\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The vertical segment between \((3, -4)\) and \((3, 2)\) has a length of \(2 - (-4) = 6\) units. Shifting the vertex \((-2, -1)\) downward by \(6\) units gives the fourth vertex with the smallest \(y\)-coordinate: \((-2, -1 - 6) = (-2, -7)\).

qs.q: The points \((-4, 2), (1, 2),\) and \((2, -2)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that lies in the second quadrant?
qs.s: A vertex lies in the second quadrant when \(x < 0\) and \(y > 0\), which occurs when the segment between \((-4, 2)\) and \((1, 2)\) is a diagonal. The opposite vertex is \((-4 + 1 - 2, 2 + 2 - (-2)) = (-5, 6)\).

qs.q: The points \((-1, -4), (-1, 3),\) and \((3, 1)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has the smallest \(x\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The smallest \(x\)-coordinate occurs when the vertical segment from \((-1, -4)\) to \((-1, 3)\) is a diagonal. The opposite vertex is found by \((-1 + (-1) - 3, -4 + 3 - 1) = (-5, -2)\).

qs.q: The points \((-3, 1), (4, 1),\) and \((1, -3)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has a positive \(y\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The parallelogram with a positive \(y\)-coordinate occurs when the segment between \((-3, 1)\) and \((4, 1)\) is a diagonal. The fourth vertex opposite \((1, -3)\) is \((-3 + 4 - 1, 1 + 1 - (-3)) = (0, 5)\).

qs.q: The points \((-5, -2), (1, -2),\) and \((-2, 3)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has the largest \(x\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The horizontal segment between \((-5, -2)\) and \((1, -2)\) has a length of \(1 - (-5) = 6\) units. Shifting the vertex \((-2, 3)\) to the right by \(6\) units gives the fourth vertex with the largest \(x\)-coordinate: \((-2 + 6, 3) = (4, 3)\).

qs.q: The points \((-6, 8), (9, 14),\) and \((3, -5)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has the largest \(x\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The three possible fourth vertices are \((-12, -11)\), \((0, 27)\), and \((18, 1)\). The vertex with the largest \(x\)-coordinate is \((9 + 3 - (-6), 14 + (-5) - 8) = (18, 1)\).

qs.q: The points \((-14, -6), (-2, 10),\) and \((8, -4)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that lies in the third quadrant?
qs.s: The three possible fourth vertices are \((-4, -20)\), \((-24, 8)\), and \((20, 12)\). The only vertex in the third quadrant (where both coordinates are negative) is \((-14 + 8 - (-2), -6 + (-4) - 10) = (-4, -20)\).

qs.q: The points \((-7, -4), (5, -8),\) and \((11, 6)\) can serve as three vertices for three different parallelograms. What are the coordinates of the fourth vertex that has the smallest \(y\)-coordinate?
qs.s: The three possible fourth vertices are \((-13, -18)\), \((-1, 10)\), and \((23, 2)\). The one with the smallest \(y\)-coordinate is \((-7 + 5 - 11, -4 + (-8) - 6) = (-13, -18)\).

qs.q: Parallelogram $ABCD$ has vertices \(A(-8, 3)\), \(B(-2, 11)\), and \(C(7, 5)\). What are the coordinates of vertex \(D\)?
qs.s: In parallelogram $ABCD$, the opposite sides satisfy \(\vec{AD} = \vec{BC}\), so \(D = A + C - B\). Therefore, \(D = (-8 + 7 - (-2), 3 + 5 - 11) = (1, -3)\).

qs.q: Parallelogram $ABCD$ has vertices \(A(-15, 8)\), \(B(-3, -7)\), and \(C(12, -2)\). What are the coordinates of vertex \(D\)?
qs.s: Because diagonals \(AC\) and \(BD\) bisect each other, \(D = A + C - B\). Calculating the coordinates gives \(D = (-15 + 12 - (-3), 8 + (-2) - (-7)) = (0, 13)\).

qs.q: A laboratory technician burns a candle and models its height, \(H\) (in centimetres), after burning for \(t\) hours with the equation \(H = 36 - \frac{4}{3}t\). When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(H\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Set \(H = 0\) to find the horizontal intercept: \(0 = 36 - \frac{4}{3}t\). Solving for \(t\) gives \(\frac{4}{3}t = 36\), so \(t = 36 \times \frac{3}{4} = 27\).

qs.q: A landscaper models the volume of fuel remaining, \(V\) (in litres), in a commercial lawnmower after \(t\) hours of operation using the equation \(V = 24 - \frac{2}{3}t\). When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(V\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Set \(V = 0\) to find the horizontal intercept: \(0 = 24 - \frac{2}{3}t\), which gives \(\frac{2}{3}t = 24\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{3}{2}\) yields \(t = 36\).

qs.q: A pilot monitors a glider's descent, where the altitude, \(h\) (in metres), after \(t\) seconds is given by the equation \(h = 90 - \frac{5}{3}t\). When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(h\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Set \(h = 0\) to determine where the graph crosses the horizontal axis: \(0 = 90 - \frac{5}{3}t\). Solving for \(t\) gives \(\frac{5}{3}t = 90\), so \(t = 90 \times \frac{3}{5} = 54\).

qs.q: A maintenance crew is draining a community pool. The depth of the water, \(d\) (in centimetres), after draining for \(m\) minutes is modeled by the equation \(d = 60 - \frac{3}{4}m\). When graphing this relationship with \(m\) on the horizontal axis and \(d\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(m\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: To find the horizontal intercept, substitute \(d = 0\) into the equation: \(0 = 60 - \frac{3}{4}m\). Solving for \(m\) gives \(\frac{3}{4}m = 60\), so \(m = 60 \times \frac{4}{3} = 80\).

qs.q: A student tracks the remaining balance, \(B\) (in dollars), on a prepaid transit card after taking \(n\) bus rides using the equation \(B = 70 - \frac{7}{2}n\). When graphing this relationship with \(n\) on the horizontal axis and \(B\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(n\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Set \(B = 0\) to find the \(n\)-intercept: \(0 = 70 - \frac{7}{2}n\). Rearranging gives \(\frac{7}{2}n = 70\), and multiplying by \(\frac{2}{7}\) yields \(n = 20\).

qs.q: A municipal reservoir releases water through two spillways during maintenance. The volume of water remaining, \(V\) (in megalitres), is modeled by the equation \(V = 720 - \frac{5}{6}t - \frac{2}{3}t\), where \(t\) is the time in hours. When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(V\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Combine like terms to simplify the rate: \(-\frac{5}{6}t - \frac{4}{6}t = -\frac{9}{6}t = -\frac{3}{2}t\), so \(V = 720 - \frac{3}{2}t\). Setting \(V = 0\) gives \(\frac{3}{2}t = 720\), which yields \(t = 720 \times \frac{2}{3} = 480\).

qs.q: A logistics company tracks the remaining balance, \(B\) (in thousands of dollars), on an equipment loan using the equation \(B - 150 = 600 - \frac{5}{3}m\), where \(m\) is the number of months since the start of the year. When graphing this relationship with \(m\) on the horizontal axis and \(B\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(m\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: Set \(B = 0\) to find the intercept: \(0 - 150 = 600 - \frac{5}{3}m\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{5}{3}m = -750\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{3}{5}\) gives \(m = 750 \times \frac{3}{5} = 450\).

qs.q: A landscape architect designs a park and models the constraints on path lengths with the equation \(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{3}{4}y = 360\), where \(x\) is the length of paved paths (in metres) and \(y\) is the length of gravel paths (in metres). When graphing this relationship with \(x\) on the horizontal axis and \(y\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(x\)-intercept) of the graph?
qs.s: To find the horizontal intercept, set \(y = 0\): \(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{3}{4}(0) = 360\), so \(\frac{2}{5}x = 360\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{5}{2}\) gives \(x = 360 \times \frac{5}{2} = 900\).

qs.q: An industrial cooling system lowers the temperature, \(T\) (in degrees Celsius), of a chemical solution according to the equation \(T = 600 - \frac{3}{8}(2t + 40)\), where \(t\) is the cooling time in minutes. When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(T\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?

A cargo plane's flight computer models the remaining fuel, \(F\) (in kilograms), using the equation \(F = 840 - \frac{7}{4}(t + 40)\), where \(t\) is the elapsed flight time in minutes beyond the initial climb. When graphing this relationship with \(t\) on the horizontal axis and \(F\) on the vertical axis, what is the horizontal intercept (\(t\)-intercept) of the graph?

The amount of water, \(W\) (in liters), remaining in a leaking tank after \(t\) minutes is modeled by the equation \(W = 50 - \frac{3}{5}t\). Use the equation to estimate the amount of water remaining after 25 minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 25\) into the equation: \(W = 50 - \frac{3}{5}(25) = 50 - 15 = 35\text{ liters}\).

qs.q: Liam's total savings, \(S\) (in dollars), after working \(h\) hours is modeled by the equation \(S = 25 + \frac{5}{2}h\). Use the equation to estimate his total savings after working 14 hours.
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 14\) into the equation: \(S = 25 + \frac{5}{2}(14) = 25 + 35 = 60\text{ dollars}\).

qs.q: A student finds that the temperature, \(T\) (in degrees Celsius), of a cooling liquid over time \(m\) (in minutes) is modeled by the equation \(T = 80 - \frac{4}{3}m\). Estimate the temperature of the liquid after 15 minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 15\) into the equation: \(T = 80 - \frac{4}{3}(15) = 80 - 20 = 60^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A hiker starts at an elevation of 120 meters and walks up a mountain trail. Her elevation, \(E\) (in meters), after \(t\) minutes is modeled by the equation \(E = 120 + \frac{4}{5}t\). Use the equation to estimate her elevation after 40 minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 40\) into the equation: \(E = 120 + \frac{4}{5}(40) = 120 + 32 = 152\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: A candle's height, \(h\) (in centimeters), after burning for \(t\) hours is modeled by the equation \(h = 30 - \frac{3}{4}t\). Estimate the height of the candle after burning for 16 hours.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 16\) into the equation: \(h = 30 - \frac{3}{4}(16) = 30 - 12 = 18\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A storage tank initially contains 1500 gallons of liquid fertilizer. A pump empties the tank at a rate modeled by the equation \(V = 1500 - \frac{35}{2}t\), where \(V\) is the volume in gallons and \(t\) is the pumping time in minutes. Estimate the remaining volume after 1 hour and 10 minutes of pumping.
qs.s: Convert 1 hour and 10 minutes to \(t = 70\text{ minutes}\). Substitute \(t = 70\) into the equation: \(V = 1500 - \frac{35}{2}(70) = 1500 - 1225 = 275\text{ gallons}\).

qs.q: The total revenue \(R\) (in dollars) from selling \(a\) adult tickets and \(s\) student tickets for a school play is modeled by the linear equation \(12a + 7s = 840\). If the club sells 35 adult tickets, estimate the number of student tickets they must sell to reach their revenue goal of $840.
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 35\) into the equation to get \(12(35) + 7s = 840\), which simplifies to \(420 + 7s = 840\). Subtract 420 from both sides to get \(7s = 420\), so \(s = 60\).

qs.q: A drone begins descending from an altitude of 450 meters. Its altitude \(h\) (in meters) after \(t\) seconds is modeled by the equation \(h = 450 - \frac{5}{3}t\). Estimate the time \(t\) (in seconds) it takes for the drone to reach an altitude of 150 meters.
qs.s: Set \(h = 150\) to get \(150 = 450 - \frac{5}{3}t\), which rearranges to \(\frac{5}{3}t = 300\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{3}{5}\) to find \(t = 180\text{ seconds}\).

qs.q: The depth of water, \(d\) (in centimeters), in a reservoir during a dry season is modeled by the equation \(d = 850 - \frac{7}{4}t\), where \(t\) is the number of days since the start of summer. Estimate the decrease in water depth from day 20 to day 60.

A commercial airplane descends toward an airport. Its altitude, \(A\) (in feet), is modeled by the equation \(A = 32{,}000 - 1250m\), where \(m\) is the time in minutes after beginning its descent. Estimate the airplane's altitude 18 minutes after beginning its descent.

A baker has baking pans that can hold at most 16 muffins each. In each batch, he bakes blueberry muffins and bran muffins so that the total number of blueberry muffins (\(x\)) and bran muffins (\(y\)) is always 24. Which equation represents the different pairs of muffins \((x, y)\) the baker can make?
qs.s: The total number of blueberry muffins (\(x\)) and bran muffins (\(y\)) must equal 24, so the relationship is represented by the linear equation \(x + y = 24\).

qs.q: A board game uses two 10-sided dice, each numbered 1 through 10. On a special turn, the sum of the number rolled on the red die (\(x\)) and the number rolled on the blue die (\(y\)) must always equal 14. Which equation represents the different pairs of rolls \((x, y)\) that satisfy this condition?
qs.s: The sum of the roll on the red die (\(x\)) and the roll on the blue die (\(y\)) must equal 14, which is modeled by the linear equation \(x + y = 14\).

qs.q: A student works two part-time jobs and can work at most 12 hours at each job per week. The total number of hours he works at the library (\(x\)) and at the community center (\(y\)) is always 20 hours each week. Which equation represents the different pairs of hours \((x, y)\) the student can work?
qs.s: The total hours worked between the library (\(x\)) and the community center (\(y\)) is always 20, which is represented by the linear equation \(x + y = 20\).

qs.q: A gardener has containers that hold at most 10 litres each of liquid fertilizer. She mixes brand A (\(x\) litres) and brand B (\(y\) litres) so that the total volume of fertilizer is always 15 litres. Which equation represents the different pairs of volumes \((x, y)\) that the gardener can mix?
qs.s: The combined volume of brand A (\(x\)) and brand B (\(y\)) must equal 15 litres, which is modeled by the linear equation \(x + y = 15\).

qs.q: A music streaming app limits a custom playlist to a maximum of 20 songs per genre. A user creates a playlist with a total of 30 songs consisting of rock songs (\(x\)) and jazz songs (\(y\)). Which equation represents the different pairs of songs \((x, y)\) that can be on the playlist?
qs.s: The sum of the rock songs (\(x\)) and jazz songs (\(y\)) is always 30, which is represented by the linear equation \(x + y = 30\).

qs.q: A fitness club charges a one-time registration fee of $45 plus a monthly membership fee of $28. If \(x\) represents the number of months a person has been a member and \(y\) represents the total cost in dollars, which equation models the relationship between \(x\) and \(y\)?
qs.s: The monthly fee of $28 contributes \(28x\) for \(x\) months. Adding the one-time registration fee of $45 gives the total cost equation \(y = 28x + 45\).

qs.q: A school theater sells student tickets for $6 each and adult tickets for $10 each. The theater needs to collect a total of $450 from ticket sales for one performance. If \(x\) represents the number of student tickets sold and \(y\) represents the number of adult tickets sold, which equation represents the different pairs of ticket sales \((x, y)\) that reach this total?
qs.s: Multiplying the cost per ticket by the number of tickets gives \(6x\) for student tickets and \(10y\) for adult tickets. Setting their sum equal to the total revenue yields \(6x + 10y = 450\).

qs.q: A landscaper has a budget of $600 to purchase two types of trees: maple trees costing $50 each and oak trees costing $75 each. If \(x\) is the number of maple trees and \(y\) is the number of oak trees, which equation represents the different combinations of trees \((x, y)\) that use the entire budget?
qs.s: The cost of \(x\) maple trees at $50 each is \(50x\) and the cost of \(y\) oak trees at $75 each is \(75y\). Setting their combined cost equal to the $600 budget gives \(50x + 75y = 600\).

qs.q: A water reservoir initially holds 1500 litres of water and is drained at a constant rate of 25 litres per minute. If \(x\) represents the draining time in minutes and \(y\) represents the remaining volume of water in litres, which equation models the relationship between \(x\) and \(y\)?
qs.s: The water level starts at 1500 litres and decreases at a rate of 25 litres per minute, giving a slope of \(-25\). Therefore, the remaining volume is modeled by \(y = -25x + 1500\).

qs.q: A shipping company packs a cargo container with small boxes that weigh 4 kg each and large boxes that weigh 9 kg each. The total weight of the boxes in the container must be exactly 360 kg. If \(x\) is the number of small boxes and \(y\) is the number of large boxes, which equation represents the different pairs of boxes \((x, y)\) that can be loaded?
qs.s: The weight of \(x\) small boxes is \(4x\) kg and the weight of \(y\) large boxes is \(9y\) kg. Setting the sum of the weights equal to 360 kg gives the linear equation \(4x + 9y = 360\).

qs.q: Determine whether the slope of the line shown in the graph is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: As you move from left to right, the line rises (the values of \(y\) increase), which means the slope is positive.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine whether the slope of the graphed line is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: The line goes upward from left to right through the origin, which indicates a positive rate of change and thus a positive slope.

qs.q: The graph shows three connected line segments: \(AB\), \(BC\), and \(CD\). Which segment has a slope of zero?
qs.s: Segment \(BC\) is horizontal along \(y = 3\), so there is no vertical change, meaning its slope is zero.

qs.q: The graph displays two intersecting lines, labeled Line \(m\) and Line \(n\). Which statement correctly describes the signs of their slopes?
qs.a: Line \(m\) has a positive slope and Line \(n\) has a negative slope.
d: Line \(m\) has a negative slope and Line \(n\) has a positive slope.
qs.s: Line \(m\) slants upward from left to right (positive slope), while Line \(n\) slants downward from left to right (negative slope).

qs.q: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is plotted on the coordinate plane. Which side of the quadrilateral has a positive slope?
qs.s: Moving from left to right from \(A(-4, -2)\) to \(D(5, -1)\), side \(DA\) rises, so its slope is positive. (Side \(AB\) is vertical/undefined, \(BC\) is horizontal/zero, and \(CD\) falls/negative.)

qs.q: In the right triangle \(JKL\) shown on the coordinate plane, which side has a negative slope?
d: No side has a negative slope
qs.s: Side \(KL\) slants downward from \(L(-4, 4)\) to \(K(3, -3)\), so its slope is negative. (Side \(JK\) has a slope of zero, and side \(JL\) has an undefined slope.)

qs.q: Four lines labeled \(L_1\), \(L_2\), \(L_3\), and \(L_4\) are shown on the coordinate plane. Which line has an undefined slope?
qs.s: A line has an undefined slope if it is vertical. Line \(L_2\) is the vertical line (\(x = 3\)), so its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine whether the slope of the line is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: As you move from left to right along the line, the values of \(y\) increase (the line rises). Therefore, the slope is positive.

qs.q: The graph shows a path consisting of segments \(AB\), \(BC\), and \(CD\). Which segment has a slope of zero?
qs.s: Segment \(BC\) is completely horizontal because both \(B\) and \(C\) share the same \(y\)-coordinate (\(y = 3\)). A horizontal line has a slope of zero.

qs.q: The graph shows four lines labeled \(k\), \(l\), \(m\), and \(n\). Which line has an undefined slope?
qs.s: A line has an undefined slope if and only if it is vertical (\(\Delta x = 0\)). Line \(l\) is the vertical line, so its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Triangle \(ABC\) is plotted on the coordinate plane. Which side of the triangle has a negative slope?
qs.s: Side \(BC\) slants downward from \((1, 3)\) to \((5, -1)\) as you move left to right, meaning its slope is negative. Sides \(AB\) and \(AC\) both rise from left to right, so their slopes are positive.

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Which statement correctly describes the signs of their slopes?
qs.a: The slope of L_1 is positive, and the slope of L_2 is negative.
d: The slope of L_1 is negative, and the slope of L_2 is positive.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) goes upward from left to right, so its slope is positive. Line \(L_2\) goes downward from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Trapezoid $JKLM$ is shown on the coordinate plane. Which side of the trapezoid has a positive slope?
qs.s: Side \(JK\) rises from \((-4, -3)\) to \((-2, 3)\) as \(x\) increases, so its slope is positive. Sides \(KL\) and \(MJ\) are horizontal (slope 0), and side \(LM\) falls (negative slope).

qs.q: Determine whether the slope of the line shown in the graph is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: As you move from left to right, the line rises, which means the vertical change is positive as the horizontal change increases. Therefore, the slope is positive.

qs.q: The coordinate grid shows three lines labeled \(u\), \(v\), and \(w\). Which option correctly describes the slope of each line?
qs.a: \(u\) has zero slope, \(v\) has undefined slope, and \(w\) has positive slope
d: \(u\) has undefined slope, \(v\) has zero slope, and \(w\) has positive slope
\(u\) has zero slope, \(v\) has undefined slope, and \(w\) has negative slope
\(u\) has negative slope, \(v\) has undefined slope, and \(w\) has zero slope
qs.s: Line \(u\) is horizontal, so its slope is zero; line \(v\) is vertical, so its slope is undefined; and line \(w\) rises from left to right, so its slope is positive.

qs.q: The graph shows a path composed of segments \(AB\), \(BC\), \(CD\), and \(DE\). Which segment has a slope of zero?
qs.s: Segment \(BC\) is completely horizontal, meaning there is no vertical change as \(x\) increases from \(-2\) to \(2\). Thus, its slope is zero.

qs.q: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is plotted on the coordinate plane. What is the sign of the slope of the dashed diagonal connecting vertex \(A\) to vertex \(C\)?
qs.s: Connecting \(A(-4, 3)\) to \(C(4, -2)\) creates a segment that falls from left to right with a vertical change of \(-5\) over a horizontal change of \(8\), so its slope is negative.

qs.q: The lines \(k\) and \(m\) are graphed below. What are the signs of the slopes of line \(k\) and line \(m\)?
qs.a: Slope of \(k\) is positive; slope of \(m\) is negative
d: Slope of \(k\) is negative; slope of \(m\) is positive
qs.s: Line \(k\) rises from left to right, giving it a positive slope, while line \(m\) falls from left to right, giving it a negative slope.

qs.q: The graph shows four lines labeled \(L_1\), \(L_2\), \(L_3\), and \(L_4\). Which line has a negative slope?
qs.s: Line \(L_2\) slants downward from left to right, meaning \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine whether the slope of the line is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: As you trace the line from left to right, the graph rises (y-values increase as x-values increase). Therefore, the slope is positive.

qs.q: Lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are shown on the coordinate plane. Determine the signs of the slopes of line \(L_1\) and line \(L_2\), respectively.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) falls from left to right, so its slope is negative. Line \(L_2\) rises from left to right, so its slope is positive.

qs.q: Four lines labeled \(L_1\), \(L_2\), \(L_3\), and \(L_4\) are shown on the coordinate plane. Which line has an undefined slope?
qs.s: An undefined slope occurs when a line is completely vertical because \(\Delta x = 0\). Line \(L_4\) is vertical, so its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ is shown on the coordinate plane. Which side of the quadrilateral has a slope equal to zero?
