qs.s: A line segment with a slope of zero is horizontal. Side \(BC\) connects \((-1, 4)\) and \((4, 4)\), which have the same \(y\)-coordinate, so its slope is zero.

qs.q: Lines \(r\) and \(s\) are shown on the coordinate plane, with slopes \(m_r\) and \(m_s\), respectively. What is the sign of their product, \(m_r \cdot m_s\)?
qs.s: Line \(r\) rises from left to right, so \(m_r > 0\). Line \(s\) falls from left to right, so \(m_s < 0\). The product of a positive number and a negative number is always negative.

qs.q: Line \(k\) is graphed on the coordinate plane. Determine whether the slope of any line perpendicular to line \(k\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(k\) rises from left to right, so its slope is positive. Since perpendicular lines have slopes that are negative reciprocals of each other, any line perpendicular to line \(k\) must have a negative slope.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the horizontal line.
qs.s: For any two points on a horizontal line, such as \((-3, 3)\) and \((3, 3)\), the vertical change (rise) is \(0\). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{0}{6} = 0\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Identify the marked points \((-3, -1)\) and \((1, 2)\) on the line. Using the slope formula, \(\text{slope} = \frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{2 - (-1)}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: The graph shows four lines labeled \(L_1, L_2, L_3,\) and \(L_4\). Which line has a slope of \(-\frac{2}{3}\)?
qs.s: Lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) have positive slopes, while \(L_3\) and \(L_4\) have negative slopes. Line \(L_4\) passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((3, -3)\), giving a slope of \(\frac{-3 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Use the graph to calculate the slope of \(L_1\) minus the slope of \(L_2\).
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has slope \(m_1 = \frac{5 - 1}{2 - 0} = 2\), and line \(L_2\) has slope \(m_2 = \frac{-1 - 2}{3 - (-3)} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Subtracting the slopes gives \(m_1 - m_2 = 2 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: The graph shows triangle \(ABC\). Use the graph to determine the slope of side \(BC\).
qs.s: Side \(BC\) connects vertex \(B(-1, 5)\) to vertex \(C(5, 1)\). The slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{1 - 5}{5 - (-1)} = \frac{-4}{6} = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through the marked points.
qs.s: Using the coordinates of the marked points \((-8, -6)\) and \((7, 4)\), the slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{4 - (-6)}{7 - (-8)} = \frac{10}{15} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: The graph shows quadrilateral $PQRS$ with dashed diagonal \(PR\). Use the graph to determine the slope of diagonal \(PR\).
qs.s: Diagonal \(PR\) connects points \(P(-5, 4)\) and \(R(5, -4)\). The slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{-4 - 4}{5 - (-5)} = \frac{-8}{10} = -\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Determine the slope of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, such as \((0, -1)\) and \((3, 1)\). The vertical change is \(1 - (-1) = 2\) and the horizontal change is \(3 - 0 = 3\), giving a slope of \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to find the slope of the line.
qs.s: From \((0, 1)\) to \((1, 4)\), the line rises \(3\) units vertically for every \(1\) unit it moves horizontally to the right, so the slope is \(\frac{3}{1} = 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Choose two points on the line, \((-1, 3)\) and \((1, -1)\). Moving from left to right, the rise is \(-1 - 3 = -4\) and the run is \(1 - (-1) = 2\), so the slope is \(\frac{-4}{2} = -2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to calculate the slope of the line.
qs.s: Using the marked points \((0, -2)\) and \((3, -1)\), the rise is \(-1 - (-2) = 1\) and the run is \(3 - 0 = 3\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph of triangle \(ABC\) to find the numerical slope of side \(AB\).
qs.s: The coordinates of vertices \(A\) and \(B\) are \((-4, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\). The slope of side \(AB\) is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Determine the difference between the slope of \(L_1\) and the slope of \(L_2\) (\(m_1 - m_2\)).
qs.s: From the points on the graph, the slope of \(L_1\) is \(m_1 = \frac{3 - (-1)}{1 - (-1)} = 2\) and the slope of \(L_2\) is \(m_2 = \frac{0 - 2}{2 - (-2)} = -\frac{1}{2}\). The difference is \(2 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Using the marked points \((-3, -1)\) and \((1, 2)\), the vertical change (rise) is \(2 - (-1) = 3\) and the horizontal change (run) is \(1 - (-3) = 4\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the vertical line.
qs.s: For any vertical line, the horizontal change (run) is \(0\) (\(-3 - (-3) = 0\)). Since division by zero is undefined, the slope of a vertical line is undefined.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of line segment \(AB\).
qs.s: Point \(A\) is at \((-5, 5)\) and point \(B\) is at \((4, -1)\). The slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{-1 - 5}{4 - (-5)} = \frac{-6}{9} = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of line \(L_1\).
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) passes through the origin \((0, 0)\) and the point \((2, 1)\). The rise is \(1\) and the run is \(2\), so its slope is \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the horizontal line.
qs.s: For any horizontal line, the vertical change is \(0\) while the horizontal change is non-zero (\(3 - 3 = 0\) over \(4 - (-3) = 7\)). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{0}{7} = 0\).

qs.q: Determine the slope of the line shown in the graph by identifying points where it crosses grid intersections.
qs.s: Locating clear grid intersections along the line gives the points \((1, 1)\) and \((4, 5)\). The rise is \(5 - 1 = 4\) and the run is \(4 - 1 = 3\), giving a slope of \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Identify the two marked points on the line, (-1, -1) and (2, 1). The rise is 1 - (-1) = 2 and the run is 2 - (-1) = 3, so the slope is rise/run = 2/3.

qs.q: Determine the slope of the line passing through points A and B shown in the graph.
qs.s: Point A is at (-6, 7) and point B is at (6, -2). The slope is (-2 - 7) / (6 - (-6)) = -9/12, which simplifies to -3/4.

qs.q: Determine the slope of line k shown in the graph.
qs.s: Line k passes through points (-2, 0) and (2, 2). The slope is (2 - 0) / (2 - (-2)) = 2/4 = 1/2.

qs.q: Triangle PQR is shown on the coordinate plane. Determine the slope of the line containing side PR.
qs.s: Side PR connects vertices P(-4, -3) and R(5, 0). The slope is (0 - (-3)) / (5 - (-4)) = 3/9 = 1/3.

qs.q: Determine the slope of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: The line is vertical, passing through points such as (3, -2) and (3, 3). The horizontal run is 3 - 3 = 0, and division by zero is undefined, so the slope is undefined.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, such as (0, -1) and (3, 1). Using rise over run, the slope is (1 - (-1)) / (3 - 0) = 2/3.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of line L2.
qs.s: Locate line L2 and identify two integer points on it, such as (0, 2) and (4, -1). The slope is (-1 - 2) / (4 - 0) = -3/4.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of side AB of triangle ABC.
qs.s: Vertices A and B have coordinates A(-3, -2) and B(3, 2). The slope of side AB is (2 - (-2)) / (3 - (-3)) = 4/6 = 2/3.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Choose two points on the line, such as \((-3, -1)\) and \((3, 3)\). The slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{3 - (-3)} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Determine the difference between their slopes, calculated as \(m_1 - m_2\), where \(m_1\) is the slope of line \(L_1\) and \(m_2\) is the slope of line \(L_2\).
Determine the slope of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: For any two points on a vertical line, the change in \(x\) (run) is \(0\). Since slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}}\) and division by zero is undefined, the slope of a vertical line is undefined.

qs.q: Four lines are graphed on the coordinate plane. Which line has a slope of \(-\frac{2}{3}\)?
qs.s: Line \(L_3\) goes downward from left to right and passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((3, -1)\). Its slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{-1 - 1}{3 - 0} = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(A\) and \(B\).
qs.s: From point \(A(-3, 2)\) to point \(B(1, -1)\), the rise is \(-1 - 2 = -3\) and the run is \(1 - (-3) = 4\). Thus, the slope is \(-\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(C\) and \(D\).
qs.s: From point \(C(-1, -3)\) to point \(D(1, 1)\), the rise is \(1 - (-3) = 4\) and the run is \(1 - (-1) = 2\). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(P\) and \(Q\).
qs.s: Using points \(P(0, -1)\) and \(Q(3, 1)\), the rise is \(1 - (-1) = 2\) and the run is \(3 - 0 = 3\). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(J\) and \(K\).
qs.s: From point \(J(-4, -1)\) to point \(K(1, 1)\), the rise is \(1 - (-1) = 2\) and the run is \(1 - (-4) = 5\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(E\) and \(F\).
qs.s: From point \(E(-1, 2)\) to point \(F(1, -4)\), the rise is \(-4 - 2 = -6\) and the run is \(1 - (-1) = 2\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{-6}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(R\) and \(S\).
qs.s: The line is horizontal, so the vertical change (rise) between \(R(-4, 2)\) and \(S(3, 2)\) is \(2 - 2 = 0\), while the run is \(3 - (-4) = 7\). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{0}{7} = 0\).

qs.q: Use the graph to find the slope \(m_1\) of line \(L_1\) and the slope \(m_2\) of line \(L_2\). What is the value of \(m_1 - m_2\)?
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has slope \(m_1 = \frac{3 - (-1)}{1 - (-1)} = 2\), and line \(L_2\) has slope \(m_2 = \frac{0 - (-2)}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{1}{2}\). Their difference is \(m_1 - m_2 = 2 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: The figure shows triangle \(ABC\) on the coordinate plane. Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through side \(AB\).
qs.s: From vertex \(A(-4, -2)\) to vertex \(B(2, 6)\), the rise is \(6 - (-2) = 8\) and the run is \(2 - (-4) = 6\). Simplifying gives a slope of \(\frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the slope of the line passing through points \(M\) and \(N\).
qs.s: The line is vertical, so the horizontal change (run) between \(M(-3, -4)\) and \(N(-3, 3)\) is \(-3 - (-3) = 0\). Since division by zero is undefined, the slope is undefined.

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the slope of the line.
qs.s: Using the marked points \((-3, -2)\) and \((1, 1)\), the rise is \(1 - (-2) = 3\) and the run is \(1 - (-3) = 4\). Therefore, the slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: The graph shows a circle centered at the origin and a tangent line touching the circle at point \(P(3, 4)\) and passing through point \(Q(7, 1)\). Determine the slope of the tangent line.
qs.s: Using points \(P(3, 4)\) and \(Q(7, 1)\) on the tangent line, the rise is \(1 - 4 = -3\) and the run is \(7 - 3 = 4\), yielding a slope of \(\frac{-3}{4} = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: The graph shows the curve \(y = 4 - x^2\) intersected by a secant line at points \(A\) and \(B\). Determine the slope of the secant line.
qs.s: Reading the coordinates of intersection points \(A(-1, 3)\) and \(B(3, -5)\), the slope is \(\frac{-5 - 3}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\).

qs.q: The figure shows \(\triangle ABC\) plotted on a coordinate grid. Determine the slope of the line containing side \(AB\).
qs.s: From the grid, vertex \(A\) is at \((-4, -3)\) and vertex \(B\) is at \((2, 5)\). The slope of side \(AB\) is \(\frac{5 - (-3)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{8}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), are plotted on the coordinate plane. What is the value of \(m_1 - m_2\), where \(m_1\) is the slope of \(L_1\) and \(m_2\) is the slope of \(L_2\)?
qs.s: From the marked points, the slope of \(L_1\) is \(m_1 = \frac{5 - (-3)}{2 - (-2)} = 2\) and the slope of \(L_2\) is \(m_2 = \frac{-1 - 3}{4 - (-4)} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Subtracting gives \(m_1 - m_2 = 2 - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: The figure shows parallelogram $ABCD$ on a coordinate plane with dashed diagonal \(AC\). Determine the slope of diagonal \(AC\).
qs.s: Diagonal \(AC\) connects vertex \(A(-5, -2)\) to vertex \(C(5, 4)\). Its slope is \(\frac{4 - (-2)}{5 - (-5)} = \frac{6}{10} = \frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-18, 35)\) and \((27, -25)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-13, -8)\) and \((17, -8)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-54, 82)\) and \((18, -38)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-36, 19)\) and \((24, -31)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Calculate the changes: \(y_2 - y_1 = \frac{2}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = 1\) and \(x_2 - x_1 = \frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{1}{2}\). Thus, \(m = \frac{1}{1/2} = 2\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Calculate the changes: \(y_2 - y_1 = -\frac{5}{6} - \frac{4}{6} = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x_2 - x_1 = \frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 2\). Thus, \(m = \frac{-3/2}{2} = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-15, 42)\) and \((25, -18)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((0, -3)\) and \((0, 4)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4})\) and \((\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{5}{6})\).
qs.s: Calculating the changes in coordinates gives \(y_2 - y_1 = -\frac{5}{6} - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{19}{12}\) and \(x_2 - x_1 = \frac{1}{2} - (-\frac{1}{3}) = \frac{5}{6}\). Dividing the two values gives \(m = -\frac{19}{12} \times \frac{6}{5} = -\frac{19}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-25, 68)\) and \((15, -52)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-4, 5)\) and \((2, 1)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-125, -84)\) and \((75, 76)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-2.8, 7.3)\) and \((1.2, -4.7)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-42, 65)\) and \((38, -55)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-28, 65)\) and \((44, -25)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(1, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, 2\right)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{6}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-27, -58)\) and \((33, 42)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-2, 3)\) and \((4, -1)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-125, 84)\) and \((175, -96)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{3}{5}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{4}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Find the changes: \(\Delta y = \frac{4}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{11}{6}\) and \(\Delta x = \frac{1}{2} - \left(-\frac{3}{5}\right) = \frac{11}{10}\). The slope is \(m = \frac{11/6}{11/10} = \frac{11}{6} \cdot \frac{10}{11} = \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-39, 75)\) and \((45, -65)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{-65 - 75}{45 - (-39)} = \frac{-140}{84}\). Dividing both numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, \(28\), gives \(m = -\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{5}{6}, \frac{7}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: Calculate the changes: \(\Delta y = \frac{7}{8} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{9}{8}\) and \(\Delta x = -\frac{5}{6} - \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Then divide to find the slope: \(m = \frac{9/8}{-3/2} = \frac{9}{8} \cdot \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Calculate \(\Delta y = \frac{1}{6} - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{7}{12}\) and \(\Delta x = \frac{1}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{5}{6}\). The slope is \(m = \frac{-7/12}{5/6} = -\frac{7}{12} \cdot \frac{6}{5} = -\frac{7}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-3, 1)\) and \((2, -3)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-4, 3)\) and \((-4, -5)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{-5 - 3}{-4 - (-4)} = \frac{-8}{0}\), which is undefined because division by zero is undefined.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-3, 4)\) and \((5, 4)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{4 - 4}{5 - (-3)} = \frac{0}{8} = 0\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((5, -2)\) and \((1, 6)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{6 - (-2)}{1 - 5} = \frac{8}{-4} = -2\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-35, -48)\) and \((-15, 32)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{32 - (-48)}{-15 - (-35)} = \frac{80}{20} = 4\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{4}}{\frac{5}{6} - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{5}{4}}{\frac{7}{6}} = -\frac{5}{4} \cdot \frac{6}{7} = -\frac{15}{14}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-28, 43)\) and \((36, -53)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{-53 - 43}{36 - (-28)} = \frac{-96}{64} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-24, 51)\) and \((36, -19)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{-19 - 51}{36 - (-24)} = \frac{-70}{60} = -\frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{5}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{\frac{5}{8} - \left(-\frac{1}{6}\right)}{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{\frac{19}{24}}{-\frac{7}{6}} = \frac{19}{24} \cdot \left(-\frac{6}{7}\right) = -\frac{19}{28}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-5, 1)\) and \((-5, 4)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we get \(m = \frac{4 - 1}{-5 - (-5)} = \frac{3}{0}\). Because division by zero is undefined, the slope of the line is undefined.

qs.s: Applying the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we have \(m = \frac{3 - (-5)}{-1 - (-1)} = \frac{8}{0}\). Division by zero is undefined, so the slope of the line is undefined.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((150, -85)\) and \((150, 165)\).

qs.s: Applying the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we have \(m = \frac{\frac{7}{10} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)}{\frac{2}{5} - \frac{2}{5}} = \frac{\frac{19}{20}}{0}\). Because division by zero is undefined, the slope is undefined.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we compute \(m = \frac{-\frac{5}{6} - \frac{2}{3}}{-\frac{3}{4} - \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{3}{2}}{0}\). Since division by zero is undefined, the slope is undefined.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((0, -6)\) and \((4, 0)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we have \(m = \frac{0 - (-6)}{4 - 0} = \frac{6}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((5, -1)\) and \((2, 8)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we have \(m = \frac{8 - (-1)}{2 - 5} = \frac{9}{-3} = -3\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((-6, 2)\) and \((2, -2)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we have \(m = \frac{-2 - 2}{2 - (-6)} = \frac{-4}{8} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((28, -35)\) and \((-17, 40)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{40 - (-35)}{-17 - 28} = \frac{75}{-45} = -\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{5}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{\frac{5}{8} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)}{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{\frac{7}{8}}{-\frac{7}{6}} = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((3x + 2, 7x - 6)\) and \((3x + 8, 7x + 9)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{(7x + 9) - (7x - 6)}{(3x + 8) - (3x + 2)} = \frac{15}{6} = \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we obtain \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{1}{3}}{\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{\frac{1}{6}}{\frac{5}{12}} = \frac{1}{6} \cdot \frac{12}{5} = \frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{5}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we get \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{3}} = \frac{-\frac{3}{10}}{-\frac{1}{12}} = -\frac{3}{10} \cdot (-12) = \frac{18}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{5}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we calculate \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{2}}{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{-\frac{3}{10}}{-\frac{1}{6}} = -\frac{3}{10} \cdot (-6) = \frac{9}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{5}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we find \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{5} - \frac{1}{4}}{\frac{1}{3} - \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{-\frac{1}{20}}{-\frac{1}{6}} = -\frac{1}{20} \cdot \left(-\frac{6}{1}\right) = \frac{3}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{5}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), we find \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{2} - \frac{2}{5}}{\frac{1}{4} - \frac{1}{3}} = \frac{\frac{1}{10}}{-\frac{1}{12}} = \frac{1}{10} \cdot (-12) = -\frac{6}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{3}{8}, -\frac{5}{12}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{7}{12}, \frac{1}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: Using a common denominator of 24 for both differences, \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{8} - \left(-\frac{5}{12}\right)}{\frac{7}{12} - \left(-\frac{3}{8}\right)} = \frac{\frac{3}{24} + \frac{10}{24}}{\frac{14}{24} + \frac{9}{24}} = \frac{\frac{13}{24}}{\frac{23}{24}} = \frac{13}{23}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{5}{14}, -\frac{3}{7}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{2}{21}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the LCD of 42, the vertical change is \(\frac{5}{6} - \left(-\frac{3}{7}\right) = \frac{35+18}{42} = \frac{53}{42}\) and the horizontal change is \(-\frac{2}{21} - \frac{5}{14} = \frac{-4-15}{42} = -\frac{19}{42}\). Dividing gives \(m = \frac{53/42}{-19/42} = -\frac{53}{19}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-2\frac{1}{4}, 1\frac{1}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(1\frac{1}{2}, -3\frac{2}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to get \(\left(-\frac{9}{4}, \frac{7}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{11}{3}\right)\). Then \(m = \frac{-\frac{11}{3} - \frac{7}{6}}{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{9}{4}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{29}{6}}{\frac{15}{4}} = -\frac{29}{6} \cdot \frac{4}{15} = -\frac{58}{45}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-3\frac{3}{4}, -1\frac{5}{8}\right)\) and \(\left(2\frac{1}{2}, 3\frac{7}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: In improper fraction form, the points are \(\left(-\frac{15}{4}, -\frac{13}{8}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{31}{8}\right)\). Thus, \(m = \frac{\frac{31}{8} - \left(-\frac{13}{8}\right)}{\frac{5}{2} - \left(-\frac{15}{4}\right)} = \frac{\frac{44}{8}}{\frac{25}{4}} = \frac{11}{2} \cdot \frac{4}{25} = \frac{22}{25}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-1\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(2\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Rewriting the mixed numbers as improper fractions gives \(\left(-\frac{3}{2}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{9}{4}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{-\frac{5}{6} - \frac{2}{3}}{\frac{9}{4} - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{3}{2}}{\frac{15}{4}} = -\frac{3}{2} \cdot \frac{4}{15} = -\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \((0.12, 0.35)\) and \((0.48, 0.83)\).

qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{6} - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)}{\frac{3}{4} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} = \frac{\frac{5}{6}}{\frac{5}{4}} = \frac{5}{6} \cdot \frac{4}{5} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)}{-\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{2}} = \frac{\frac{7}{12}}{-\frac{7}{6}} = \frac{7}{12} \cdot \left(-\frac{6}{7}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{3}{8}, \frac{1}{3}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{5}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{1}{6}, \frac{3}{5}\right)\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{7}{12}, -\frac{5}{8}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, \frac{7}{16}\right)\).
qs.s: Using the slope formula, \(m = \frac{\frac{7}{16} - \left(-\frac{5}{8}\right)}{\frac{5}{6} - \left(-\frac{7}{12}\right)} = \frac{\frac{17}{16}}{\frac{17}{12}} = \frac{17}{16} \cdot \frac{12}{17} = \frac{12}{16} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(3\frac{1}{5}, -2\frac{3}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-1\frac{2}{5}, 1\frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Converting to improper fractions gives \(\left(\frac{16}{5}, -\frac{11}{4}\right)\) and \(\left(-\frac{7}{5}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\), so \(m = \frac{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{11}{4}\right)}{-\frac{7}{5} - \frac{16}{5}} = \frac{\frac{17}{4}}{-\frac{23}{5}} = \frac{17}{4} \cdot \left(-\frac{5}{23}\right) = -\frac{85}{92}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-1\frac{1}{3}, 2\frac{1}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(2\frac{1}{4}, -1\frac{1}{6}\right)\).
qs.s: Converting to improper fractions gives \(\left(-\frac{4}{3}, \frac{5}{2}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{9}{4}, -\frac{7}{6}\right)\), so \(m = \frac{-\frac{7}{6} - \frac{5}{2}}{\frac{9}{4} - \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{11}{3}}{\frac{43}{12}} = -\frac{11}{3} \cdot \frac{12}{43} = -\frac{44}{43}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-2\frac{2}{3}, -1\frac{5}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(1\frac{1}{4}, 3\frac{1}{8}\right)\).
qs.s: Converting to improper fractions gives \(\left(-\frac{8}{3}, -\frac{11}{6}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{5}{4}, \frac{25}{8}\right)\), so \(m = \frac{\frac{25}{8} - \left(-\frac{11}{6}\right)}{\frac{5}{4} - \left(-\frac{8}{3}\right)} = \frac{\frac{119}{24}}{\frac{47}{12}} = \frac{119}{24} \cdot \frac{12}{47} = \frac{119}{94}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line containing the pair of points: \(\left(-\frac{5}{7}, \frac{3}{14}\right)\) and \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\).

When the slopes \(-\frac{1}{5}, 1, -\frac{2}{3}\), and \frac{5}{6} are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the second position?
qs.s: Steepness is determined by absolute value: \(|-\frac{1}{5}| = 0.2\), \(|-\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67\), \(|\frac{5}{6}| \approx 0.83\), and \(|1| = 1\). The slopes from flattest to steepest are \(-\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{6}, 1\), which places \(-\frac{2}{3}\) in the second position.

qs.q: When the slopes \(-3, \frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\), and \frac{2}{3} are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the third position?
qs.s: Comparing the absolute values of the slopes gives \(|\frac{1}{4}| = 0.25\), \(|-\frac{1}{2}| = 0.5\), \(|\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67\), and \(|-3| = 3\). Ordering from flattest to steepest yields \(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{3}, -3\), so the slope in the third position is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: When the slopes \(2, -\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{5}\), and \(-\frac{4}{5}\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the second position?
qs.s: The steepness of a line depends on the absolute value of its slope: \(|-\frac{1}{3}| \approx 0.33\), \(|\frac{3}{5}| = 0.6\), \(|-\frac{4}{5}| = 0.8\), and \(|2| = 2\). Arranged from smallest to largest absolute value, the order is \(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{5}, -\frac{4}{5}, 2\), so the slope in the second position is \(\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: When the slopes \(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{2}{5}, -\frac{7}{10}\), and \(3\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the second position?
qs.s: Finding the absolute values yields \(|\frac{2}{5}| = 0.4\), \(|-\frac{1}{2}| = 0.5\), \(|-\frac{7}{10}| = 0.7\), and \(|3| = 3\). Ordering from smallest absolute value to largest gives \(\frac{2}{5}, -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{7}{10}, 3\), so \(-\frac{1}{2}\) is second.

qs.q: When the slopes \(\frac{1}{3}, -\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{8}\), and \(-2\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the third position?
qs.s: Evaluating the absolute values gives \(|\frac{1}{3}| \approx 0.33\), \(|\frac{5}{8}| = 0.625\), \(|-\frac{3}{4}| = 0.75\), and \(|-2| = 2\). Arranged from flattest to steepest, the order is \(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{3}{4}, -2\), meaning \(-\frac{3}{4}\) is third in the list.

qs.q: When the slopes \(0, -\frac{4}{11}, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{6}{7}\), and \frac{7}{4} are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the fourth position?
qs.s: Evaluating the absolute values gives \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{4}{11}| \approx 0.364\), \(|\frac{5}{8}| = 0.625\), \(|-\frac{6}{7}| \approx 0.857\), and \(|\frac{7}{4}| = 1.75\). Arranging from flattest to steepest gives \(0, -\frac{4}{11}, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{6}{7}, \frac{7}{4}\), so the slope in the fourth position is \(-\frac{6}{7}\).

qs.q: When the slopes \(-\frac{1}{6}, \frac{7}{12}, -\frac{3}{4}, \frac{4}{5}\), and \(-2\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the fourth position?
qs.s: Comparing absolute values with a common denominator of \(60\) shows \(|-\frac{1}{6}| = \frac{10}{60}\), \(|\frac{7}{12}| = \frac{35}{60}\), \(|-\frac{3}{4}| = \frac{45}{60} = 0.75\), \(|\frac{4}{5}| = \frac{48}{60} = 0.8\), and \(|-2| = 2\). The order from flattest to steepest is \(-\frac{1}{6}, \frac{7}{12}, -\frac{3}{4}, \frac{4}{5}, -2\), so \(\frac{4}{5}\) is in the fourth position.

qs.q: When the slopes \(0, -\frac{3}{8}, \frac{5}{6}, -\frac{7}{5}\), and \frac{11}{10} are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the fourth position?
qs.s: A slope of \(0\) is horizontal (the flattest), and comparing the absolute values gives \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{3}{8}| = 0.375\), \(|\frac{5}{6}| \approx 0.83\), \(|\frac{11}{10}| = 1.1\), and \(|-\frac{7}{5}| = 1.4\). The order from flattest to steepest is \(0, -\frac{3}{8}, \frac{5}{6}, \frac{11}{10}, -\frac{7}{5}\), making \(\frac{11}{10}\) fourth.

qs.q: When the slopes \(-\frac{2}{7}, \frac{4}{9}, -\frac{5}{6}, \frac{4}{3}\), and \(-\frac{9}{4}\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the second position?
qs.s: Calculating the absolute values gives \(|-\frac{2}{7}| \approx 0.29\), \(|\frac{4}{9}| \approx 0.44\), \(|-\frac{5}{6}| \approx 0.83\), \(|\frac{4}{3}| \approx 1.33\), and \(|-\frac{9}{4}| = 2.25\). Arranging from flattest to steepest gives \(-\frac{2}{7}, \frac{4}{9}, -\frac{5}{6}, \frac{4}{3}, -\frac{9}{4}\), so \(\frac{4}{9}\) is in the second position.

qs.q: When the slopes \(-\frac{3}{10}, \frac{5}{12}, -\frac{7}{15}, \frac{8}{9}\), and \(-\frac{5}{3}\) are arranged in order from flattest to steepest, which slope is in the second position?
qs.s: Using a common denominator of \(60\) to compare the closest values, \(|-\frac{3}{10}| = \frac{18}{60}\), \(|\frac{5}{12}| = \frac{25}{60}\), and \(|-\frac{7}{15}| = \frac{28}{60}\), while \(|\frac{8}{9}| \approx 0.89\) and \(|-\frac{5}{3}| \approx 1.67\). The order from flattest to steepest is \(-\frac{3}{10}, \frac{5}{12}, -\frac{7}{15}, \frac{8}{9}, -\frac{5}{3}\), placing \(\frac{5}{12}\) second.

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{2}{3}, \frac{7}{6}, -1\).
qs.s: Steepness is determined by the absolute value of the slope. Comparing the absolute values \(|-\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67\), \(|\frac{3}{4}| = 0.75\), \(|-1| = 1\), and \(|\frac{7}{6}| \approx 1.17\), the order from flattest to steepest is \(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{3}{4}, -1, \frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -2, \frac{4}{3}, \frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{5}.
qs.s: Comparing the absolute values \(|\frac{1}{2}| = 0.5\), \(|-\frac{3}{5}| = 0.6\), \(|\frac{4}{3}| \approx 1.33\), and \(|-2| = 2\) gives the order from flattest to steepest as \(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{3}, -2\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{7}{8}, -\frac{4}{3}, \frac{5}{7}, -1.
qs.s: Steepness corresponds to the magnitude of the slope: \(|\frac{5}{7}| \approx 0.71\), \(|\frac{7}{8}| = 0.875\), \(|-1| = 1\), and \(|-\frac{4}{3}| \approx 1.33\). Ordering from least to greatest absolute value gives \(\frac{5}{7}, \frac{7}{8}, -1, -\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{2}{3}, 1, -\frac{3}{5}, \frac{5}{4}.
qs.s: Steepness depends on the absolute value of each slope: \(|-\frac{3}{5}| = 0.6\), \(|-\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67\), \(|1| = 1\), and \(|\frac{5}{4}| = 1.25\). Arranging from smallest to largest absolute value gives \(-\frac{3}{5}, -\frac{2}{3}, 1, \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{2}{5}, \frac{3}{2}, 0, -1.
qs.s: A slope of \(0\) is horizontal (completely flat). Ordering by absolute values \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{2}{5}| = 0.4\), \(|-1| = 1\), and \(|\frac{3}{2}| = 1.5\) yields \(0, -\frac{2}{5}, -1, \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{7}{6}, 0, -\frac{9}{7}, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{4}{9}.
qs.s: A slope of \(0\) is horizontal (flattest); comparing the remaining absolute values gives \(|-\frac{4}{9}| \approx 0.44\), \(|\frac{5}{8}| = 0.625\), \(|\frac{7}{6}| \approx 1.17\), and \(|-\frac{9}{7}| \approx 1.29\), yielding the order \(0, -\frac{4}{9}, \frac{5}{8}, \frac{7}{6}, -\frac{9}{7}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{11}{16}, -\frac{5}{7}, -\frac{3}{5}, \frac{13}{18}, -\frac{9}{14}.
qs.s: Comparing absolute values gives \(|-\frac{3}{5}| = 0.60\), \(|-\frac{9}{14}| \approx 0.643\), \(|\frac{11}{16}| = 0.6875\), \(|-\frac{5}{7}| = \frac{90}{126} \approx 0.714\), and \(|\frac{13}{18}| = \frac{91}{126} \approx 0.722\). The order from flattest to steepest is \(-\frac{3}{5}, -\frac{9}{14}, \frac{11}{16}, -\frac{5}{7}, \frac{13}{18}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{5}{6}, \frac{7}{8}, -1, \frac{3}{4}, -\frac{11}{12}.
qs.s: Using the common denominator \(24\), the absolute values are \(|\frac{3}{4}| = \frac{18}{24}\), \(|-\frac{5}{6}| = \frac{20}{24}\), \(|\frac{7}{8}| = \frac{21}{24}\), \(|-\frac{11}{12}| = \frac{22}{24}\), and \(|-1| = \frac{24}{24}\). Ordering from smallest to largest absolute value gives \(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{5}{6}, \frac{7}{8}, -\frac{11}{12}, -1\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{13}{15}, \frac{7}{8}, -\frac{9}{10}, \frac{17}{20}.
qs.s: Expressing each absolute value with the common denominator \(120\) gives \(|\frac{17}{20}| = \frac{102}{120}\), \(|-\frac{13}{15}| = \frac{104}{120}\), \(|\frac{7}{8}| = \frac{105}{120}\), and \(|-\frac{9}{10}| = \frac{108}{120}\). Arranging by increasing absolute value gives \(\frac{17}{20}, -\frac{13}{15}, \frac{7}{8}, -\frac{9}{10}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{7}{5}, \frac{11}{8}, -\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{4}{3}, \frac{17}{12}.
qs.s: Expressed over the common denominator \(120\), the absolute values are \(|-\frac{4}{3}| = \frac{160}{120}\), \(|\frac{11}{8}| = \frac{165}{120}\), \(|-\frac{7}{5}| = \frac{168}{120}\), \(|\frac{17}{12}| = \frac{170}{120}\), and \(|-\frac{3}{2}| = \frac{180}{120}\). Arranging from least to greatest absolute value yields \(-\frac{4}{3}, \frac{11}{8}, -\frac{7}{5}, \frac{17}{12}, -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \(3, -\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}, -\frac{4}{3}\).
qs.s: Steepness is determined by the absolute value of the slope. Comparing the absolute values, \(|-\frac{1}{3}| \approx 0.33 < |\frac{3}{4}| = 0.75 < |-\frac{4}{3}| \approx 1.33 < |3| = 3\), so the order from flattest to steepest is \(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}, -\frac{4}{3}, 3\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \(-2, \frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}\).
qs.s: Steepness depends on the absolute value of each slope: \(|-\frac{1}{4}| = 0.25\), \(|\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67\), \(|-2| = 2\), and \(|\frac{5}{2}| = 2.5\). Ordering these from least to greatest gives \(-\frac{1}{4}, \frac{2}{3}, -2, \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{3}{5}, -4, \frac{1}{5}, \frac{7}{4}.
qs.s: Take the absolute values to determine steepness: \(|\frac{1}{5}| = 0.2\), \(|-\frac{3}{5}| = 0.6\), \(|\frac{7}{4}| = 1.75\), and \(|-4| = 4\). Arranging from smallest to largest absolute value yields \(\frac{1}{5}, -\frac{3}{5}, \frac{7}{4}, -4\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{7}{2}, \frac{1}{3}, 2, -\frac{5}{6}.
qs.s: Find the absolute value of each slope: \(|\frac{1}{3}| \approx 0.33\), \(|-\frac{5}{6}| \approx 0.83\), \(|2| = 2\), and \(|-\frac{7}{2}| = 3.5\). Arranging from flattest to steepest yields \(\frac{1}{3}, -\frac{5}{6}, 2, -\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \(3, -\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{5}{3}, \frac{4}{5}\).
qs.s: Comparing absolute values gives \(|-\frac{1}{2}| = 0.5 < |\frac{4}{5}| = 0.8 < |-\frac{5}{3}| \approx 1.67 < |3| = 3\). Therefore, the slopes from flattest to steepest are \(-\frac{1}{2}, \frac{4}{5}, -\frac{5}{3}, 3\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{4}{7}, 4, \frac{1}{8}, -\frac{8}{3}, \frac{3}{5}.
qs.s: Compare absolute values using common denominators where needed: \(|\frac{1}{8}| = 0.125 < |-\frac{4}{7}| = \frac{20}{35} < |\frac{3}{5}| = \frac{21}{35} < |-\frac{8}{3}| \approx 2.67 < |4| = 4\). The ordered slopes are \(\frac{1}{8}, -\frac{4}{7}, \frac{3}{5}, -\frac{8}{3}, 4\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{7}{4}, \frac{2}{5}, 0, 3, -\frac{3}{8}.
qs.s: A slope of 0 represents a horizontal line, which is the flattest. Comparing absolute values with common denominators, \(|0| = 0 < |-\frac{3}{8}| = \frac{15}{40} < |\frac{2}{5}| = \frac{16}{40} < |-\frac{7}{4}| = 1.75 < |3| = 3\), giving \(0, -\frac{3}{8}, \frac{2}{5}, -\frac{7}{4}, 3\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{7}{2}, -\frac{1}{9}, -5, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{2}{3}.
qs.s: Order by absolute value: \(|-\frac{1}{9}| \approx 0.11 < |\frac{5}{8}| = \frac{15}{24} < |-\frac{2}{3}| = \frac{16}{24} < |\frac{7}{2}| = 3.5 < |-5| = 5\). Thus, the slopes from flattest to steepest are \(-\frac{1}{9}, \frac{5}{8}, -\frac{2}{3}, \frac{7}{2}, -5\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -3, \frac{3}{10}, 0, \frac{13}{4}, -\frac{2}{7}.
qs.s: Horizontal lines with slope \(0\) are flattest. Since \(|-\frac{2}{7}| = \frac{20}{70} < |\frac{3}{10}| = \frac{21}{70} < |-3| = 3 < |\frac{13}{4}| = 3.25\), the slopes arranged from flattest to steepest are \(0, -\frac{2}{7}, \frac{3}{10}, -3, \frac{13}{4}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{5}{6}, -\frac{11}{5}, -\frac{1}{6}, \frac{9}{4}, -\frac{7}{9}.
qs.s: Compare absolute values: \(|-\frac{1}{6}| \approx 0.17\), \(|-\frac{7}{9}| = \frac{14}{18} \approx 0.78\), \(|\frac{5}{6}| = \frac{15}{18} \approx 0.83\), \(|-\frac{11}{5}| = 2.20\), and \(|\frac{9}{4}| = 2.25\). In order of increasing steepness, the slopes are \(-\frac{1}{6}, -\frac{7}{9}, \frac{5}{6}, -\frac{11}{5}, \frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{7}{2}, -\frac{8}{3}, \text{undefined}, 0.
qs.s: Steepness increases with the absolute value of the slope, with \(0\) being the flattest and undefined being the steepest. Since \(|-\frac{8}{3}| \approx 2.67 < |\frac{7}{2}| = 3.5\), the order is \(0, -\frac{8}{3}, \frac{7}{2}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \(-\frac{5}{4}, \frac{6}{5}, 0, \text{undefined}\).
qs.s: Steepness is determined by the absolute value of the slope, where \(0\) is horizontal (flattest) and undefined is vertical (steepest). Since \(|0| < |\frac{6}{5}| = 1.2 < |-\frac{5}{4}| = 1.25 < \text{undefined}\), the order from flattest to steepest is \(0, \frac{6}{5}, -\frac{5}{4}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{3}{5}, \frac{4}{7}, 0, \text{undefined}.
qs.s: Comparing the absolute values of the slopes gives \(|0| = 0 < |\frac{4}{7}| \approx 0.57 < |-\frac{3}{5}| = 0.60 < \text{undefined}\). Therefore, the order from flattest to steepest is \(0, \frac{4}{7}, -\frac{3}{5}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: \frac{2}{3}, -\frac{7}{4}, \text{undefined}, 0.
qs.s: The flattest line has a slope of \(0\) and the steepest line has an undefined slope. Comparing the non-zero slopes by absolute value gives \(|\frac{2}{3}| \approx 0.67 < |-\frac{7}{4}| = 1.75\), so the order from flattest to steepest is \(0, \frac{2}{3}, -\frac{7}{4}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{1}{4}, 0, \frac{5}{3}, \text{undefined}.
qs.s: Comparing the slopes by absolute value gives \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{1}{4}| = 0.25\), \(|\frac{5}{3}| \approx 1.67\), and undefined represents a vertical line. Arranged from flattest to steepest, the slopes are \(0, -\frac{1}{4}, \frac{5}{3}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q:
Four lines have slopes determined by the given pairs of points:
Line A: \((1, 4)\) and \((7, 4)\)
Line B: \((-2, 3)\) and \((1, -3)\)
Line C: \((4, -2)\) and \((4, 5)\)
Line D: \((0, -1)\) and \((6, 3)\)
Arrange the lines from flattest to steepest.
qs.a: Line A, Line D, Line B, Line C
d: Line B, Line A, Line D, Line C
Line C, Line B, Line D, Line A
Line A, Line B, Line D, Line C
qs.s: Calculating the slope \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\) for each line gives \(m_A = 0\), \(m_B = -2\), \(m_C = \text{undefined}\), and \(m_D = \frac{2}{3}\). Ordering by absolute value yields \(|m_A| = 0 < |m_D| = \frac{2}{3} < |m_B| = 2 < \text{undefined}\), so the order is Line A, Line D, Line B, Line C.

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{11}{4}, \frac{8}{3}, 0, -\frac{2}{5}, \text{undefined}.
qs.s: Ordering by absolute value gives \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{2}{5}| = 0.4\), \(|\frac{8}{3}| \approx 2.67\), \(|-\frac{11}{4}| = 2.75\), with undefined representing the vertical (steepest) line. The slopes from flattest to steepest are \(0, -\frac{2}{5}, \frac{8}{3}, -\frac{11}{4}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{13}{6}, \frac{9}{4}, -\frac{3}{7}, \frac{1}{2}, 0.
qs.s: Compare the slopes by their absolute values: \(|0| = 0\), \(|-\frac{3}{7}| \approx 0.43\), \(|\frac{1}{2}| = 0.5\), \(|-\frac{13}{6}| \approx 2.17\), and \(|\frac{9}{4}| = 2.25\). Arranged from flattest to steepest, the order is \(0, -\frac{3}{7}, \frac{1}{2}, -\frac{13}{6}, \frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q:
Four lines \(L_1, L_2, L_3, L_4\) pass through the following pairs of points:
\(L_1\): \((-3, 2)\) and \((5, -4)\)
\(L_2\): \((2, -1)\) and \((2, 6)\)
\(L_3\): \((-4, -3)\) and \((4, -3)\)
\(L_4\): \((-1, -2)\) and \((2, 7)\)
Arrange the lines from flattest to steepest.
qs.s: Using \(m = \frac{y_2 - y_1}{x_2 - x_1}\), the slopes are \(m_1 = -\frac{3}{4}\), \(m_2 = \text{undefined}\), \(m_3 = 0\), and \(m_4 = 3\). Ordering by absolute value gives \(|m_3| = 0 < |m_1| = 0.75 < |m_4| = 3 < \text{undefined}\), so the order is \(L_3, L_1, L_4, L_2\).

qs.q: Arrange the slopes from flattest to steepest: -\frac{17}{5}, 0, \frac{7}{2}, -\frac{5}{8}, \text{undefined}.
qs.s: Comparing absolute values gives \(|0| = 0 < |-\frac{5}{8}| = 0.625 < |-\frac{17}{5}| = 3.4 < |\frac{7}{2}| = 3.5 < \text{undefined}\). Therefore, the order from flattest to steepest is \(0, -\frac{5}{8}, -\frac{17}{5}, \frac{7}{2}, \text{undefined}\).

qs.q: If Line \(m\) has a slope of \(4\) and Line \(n\) has a slope of \(-8\), which line is steeper, and why?
d: Line \(m\), because positive slopes are always steeper than negative slopes
qs.s: A line's steepness depends on the absolute value of its slope regardless of direction. Since \(|-8| = 8\) is greater than \(|4| = 4\), Line \(n\) is steeper.

qs.q: If Line 1 has a slope of \(-3\) and Line 2 has a slope of \(7\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Steepness depends on the absolute value of the slope. Since \(|7| = 7\) and \(|-3| = 3\), Line 2 is steeper because \(7 > 3\).

qs.q: If Line \(j\) has a slope of \(-6\) and Line \(k\) has a slope of \(-2\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: The steepness of a line is determined by the magnitude of its slope, \(|m|\). Since \(|-6| = 6\) is greater than \(|-2| = 2\), Line \(j\) is steeper.

qs.q: If Line \(p\) has a slope of \(-1\) and Line \(q\) has a slope of \(3\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Comparing the absolute values of the slopes gives \(|3| = 3\) and \(|-1| = 1\). Since \(3 > 1\), Line \(q\) is steeper.

qs.q: If Line A has a slope of \(-5\) and Line B has a slope of \(2\), which line is steeper, and why?
d: Line B, because positive slopes are always steeper than negative slopes
qs.s: Steepness is determined by the absolute value of the slope. Since \(|-5| = 5\) and \(|2| = 2\), Line A is steeper because \(5 > 2\).

qs.q: If Line 1 has a slope of \(-\frac{5}{6}\) and Line 2 has a slope of \(-\frac{7}{8}\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Comparing absolute values with a common denominator of 24 gives \(\left|-\frac{7}{8}\right| = \frac{21}{24}\) and \(\left|-\frac{5}{6}\right| = \frac{20}{24}\). Since \(\frac{21}{24} > \frac{20}{24}\), Line 2 is steeper.

qs.q: If Line A has a slope of \(-\frac{7}{3}\) and Line B has a slope of \(\frac{9}{4}\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Find the absolute value of each slope: \(\left|-\frac{7}{3}\right| = \frac{28}{12}\) and \(\left|\frac{9}{4}\right| = \frac{27}{12}\). Since \(\frac{28}{12} > \frac{27}{12}\), Line A is steeper.

qs.q: If Line \(p\) has a slope of \(-\frac{17}{6}\) and Line \(q\) has a slope of \(\frac{23}{8}\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Find a common denominator to compare the absolute values: \(\left|\frac{23}{8}\right| = \frac{69}{24}\) and \(\left|-\frac{17}{6}\right| = \frac{68}{24}\). Since \(\frac{69}{24} > \frac{68}{24}\), Line \(q\) is steeper.

qs.q: If Line \(m\) has a slope of \(-\frac{13}{4}\) and Line \(n\) has a slope of \(3.2\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Convert \(-\frac{13}{4}\) to decimal form to get \(-3.25\). Since \(|-3.25| = 3.25\) is greater than \(|3.2| = 3.20\), Line \(m\) is steeper.

qs.q: If Line \(j\) has a slope of \(-4.35\) and Line \(k\) has a slope of \(4.308\), which line is steeper, and why?
qs.s: Take the absolute value of each slope: \(|-4.35| = 4.350\) and \(|4.308| = 4.308\). Since \(4.350 > 4.308\), Line \(j\) is steeper.

exercises.name: Analyze slope formula order of points

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((1, 4)\) and \((5, 12)\), one student calculated \(\frac{12 - 4}{5 - 1}\) and another student calculated \(\frac{4 - 12}{1 - 5}\). Are they both correct? Why?
qs.a: Yes, because \(\frac{8}{4}\) and \(\frac{-8}{-4}\) both simplify to \(2\).
d: No, because the first expression simplifies to \(2\) while the second simplifies to \(-2\).
No, because the first expression simplifies to \(\frac{1}{2}\) while the second simplifies to \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
Yes, because both expressions simplify to \(\frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: Evaluating the expressions gives \(\frac{8}{4} = 2\) and \(\frac{-8}{-4} = 2\). Dividing a negative by a negative yields a positive, so reversing the points does not change the resulting slope.

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((8, 2)\) and \((2, 5)\), one student calculated \(\frac{5 - 2}{2 - 8}\) and another student calculated \(\frac{2 - 5}{8 - 2}\). Are they both correct? Why?
qs.a: Yes, because \(\frac{3}{-6}\) and \(\frac{-3}{6}\) both simplify to \(-\frac{1}{2}\).
d: No, because the first expression simplifies to \(-\frac{1}{2}\) while the second simplifies to \(\frac{1}{2}\).
No, because the first expression simplifies to \(-2\) while the second simplifies to \(2\).
Yes, because both expressions simplify to \(-2\).
qs.s: The first calculation yields \(\frac{3}{-6} = -\frac{1}{2}\) and the second yields \(\frac{-3}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\). Since both students maintained consistent order between the numerator and denominator, both obtain the correct slope of \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((9, 5)\) and \((3, 1)\), one student calculated \(\frac{5 - 1}{9 - 3}\) and another student calculated \(\frac{1 - 5}{3 - 9}\). Are they both correct? Why?

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((6, 7)\) and \((2, 1)\), one student calculated \(\frac{7 - 1}{6 - 2}\) and another student calculated \(\frac{1 - 7}{2 - 6}\). Are they both correct? Why?

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((2, 9)\) and \((7, 4)\), one student calculated \(\frac{4 - 9}{7 - 2}\) and another student calculated \(\frac{9 - 4}{2 - 7}\). Are they both correct? Why?

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((-18, 55)\) and \((42, -25)\), Student A calculated \(\frac{-25 - 55}{42 - (-18)}\) and Student B calculated \(\frac{55 - (-25)}{-18 - 42}\). Are they both correct? Why?

qs.q:

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((-12, 18)\) and \((8, -22)\), Student A calculated \(\frac{-22 - 18}{8 - (-12)}\), Student B calculated \(\frac{18 - (-22)}{-12 - 8}\), and Student C calculated \(\frac{-22 - 18}{-12 - 8}\). Which students are correct? Why?

qs.s: Student A calculates \(\frac{-40}{20} = -2\) and Student B calculates \(\frac{40}{-20} = -2\), both maintaining consistent subtraction order. Student C mixed the subtraction order between the numerator and denominator, incorrectly arriving at \(\frac{-40}{-20} = 2\).

qs.q: In calculating the slope between \((-15, 7)\) and \((25, 7)\), Student A calculated \(\frac{7 - 7}{25 - (-15)}\) and Student B calculated \(\frac{7 - 7}{-15 - 25}\). Are they both correct? Why?

qs.q: The points \(T(3, -5)\), \(U(-2, 2)\), and \(V(-2, -5)\) are vertices of a triangle. By determining the slopes of the sides, which vertex forms a right angle?
qs.s: The slope of \(TV\) is \(\frac{-5 - (-5)}{-2 - 3} = 0\) (horizontal line), and the slope of \(UV\) is \(\frac{2 - (-5)}{-2 - (-2)}\), which is undefined (vertical line). Since horizontal and vertical lines are perpendicular, the right angle is at vertex \(V(-2, -5)\).

qs.q: The points \(J(-5, -4)\), \(K(-5, 3)\), and \(L(0, 3)\) are vertices of a triangle. By determining the slopes of the sides, which vertex forms a right angle?
qs.s: The slope of \(JK\) is \(\frac{3 - (-4)}{-5 - (-5)}\), which is undefined (vertical line), and the slope of \(KL\) is \(\frac{3 - 3}{0 - (-5)} = 0\) (horizontal line). Since vertical and horizontal lines are perpendicular, the right angle is at vertex \(K(-5, 3)\).

qs.q: The points \(P(1, -2)\), \(Q(6, 4)\), and \(R(6, -2)\) are vertices of a triangle. By determining the slopes of the sides, which vertex forms a right angle?
qs.s: The slope of \(PR\) is \(\frac{-2 - (-2)}{6 - 1} = 0\) (horizontal line), and the slope of \(QR\) is \(\frac{4 - (-2)}{6 - 6}\), which is undefined (vertical line). Since horizontal and vertical lines are perpendicular, the right angle is at vertex \(R(6, -2)\).

qs.q: The points \(A(2, 5)\), \(B(2, -3)\), and \(C(7, -3)\) are vertices of a triangle. By determining the slopes of the sides, which vertex forms a right angle?
qs.s: The slope of \(AB\) is \(\frac{-3 - 5}{2 - 2}\), which is undefined (vertical line), and the slope of \(BC\) is \(\frac{-3 - (-3)}{7 - 2} = 0\) (horizontal line). Since a vertical line and a horizontal line are perpendicular, the right angle is at vertex \(B(2, -3)\).

qs.q: The points \(D(-4, 1)\), \(E(3, 1)\), and \(F(-4, -6)\) are vertices of a triangle. By determining the slopes of the sides, which vertex forms a right angle?
qs.s: The slope of \(DE\) is \(\frac{1 - 1}{3 - (-4)} = 0\) (horizontal line), and the slope of \(DF\) is \(\frac{-6 - 1}{-4 - (-4)}\), which is undefined (vertical line). Since horizontal and vertical lines are perpendicular, the right angle is at vertex \(D(-4, 1)\).

qs.q: The points \(P(-3, 2)\), \(Q(-3, 14)\), and \(R(k, 2)\) form a right triangle with perpendicular legs \(PQ\) and \(PR\). If the hypotenuse \(QR\) has a slope of \(-\frac{3}{2}\), what is the value of \(k\)?
qs.s: Since \(PQ\) is vertical and \(PR\) is horizontal, the right angle is at \(P(-3, 2)\) and \(QR\) is the hypotenuse. Setting the slope \(\frac{2 - 14}{k - (-3)} = -\frac{3}{2}\) gives \(\frac{-12}{k + 3} = -\frac{3}{2}\), which simplifies to \(k + 3 = 8\), so \(k = 5\).

qs.q: The points \(A(-6, -5)\), \(B(-6, 7)\), and \(C(10, -5)\) form a right triangle because side \(AB\) is vertical and side \(AC\) is horizontal. What is the slope of the hypotenuse \(BC\)?
qs.s: Since \(AB\) is vertical (undefined slope) and \(AC\) is horizontal (slope \(0\)), the right angle is at \(A\), so \(BC\) is the hypotenuse. The slope of \(BC\) is \(\frac{-5 - 7}{10 - (-6)} = \frac{-12}{16} = -\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: The points \(U(x, 6)\), \(V(-5, 6)\), and \(W(-5, -9)\) form a right triangle with perpendicular legs \(UV\) and \(VW\). If the hypotenuse \(UW\) has a slope of \(\frac{5}{3}\), what is the value of \(x\)?
qs.s: Since \(UV\) is horizontal and \(VW\) is vertical, the right angle is at \(V(-5, 6)\) and \(UW\) is the hypotenuse. Setting the slope \(\frac{-9 - 6}{-5 - x} = \frac{5}{3}\) gives \(\frac{15}{x + 5} = \frac{5}{3}\), which simplifies to \(x + 5 = 9\), so \(x = 4\).

qs.q: The points \(J(4, -3)\), \(K(-8, -3)\), and \(L(-8, y)\) form a right triangle where side \(JK\) is horizontal and side \(KL\) is vertical. If the slope of the hypotenuse \(JL\) is \(-\frac{5}{6}\), what is the value of \(y\)?
qs.s: Since \(JK\) is horizontal (slope \(0\)) and \(KL\) is vertical (undefined slope), the right angle is at \(K(-8, -3)\) and \(JL\) is the hypotenuse. Setting the slope \(\frac{y - (-3)}{-8 - 4} = -\frac{5}{6}\) gives \(\frac{y + 3}{-12} = -\frac{5}{6}\), so \(y + 3 = 10\), which yields \(y = 7\).

qs.q: The points \(D(-8, -9)\), \(E(7, -9)\), and \(F(7, 11)\) form a right triangle because side \(DE\) is horizontal and side \(EF\) is vertical. What is the slope of the hypotenuse \(DF\)?
qs.s: Since \(DE\) is horizontal (slope \(0\)) and \(EF\) is vertical (undefined slope), the right angle is at \(E\), so \(DF\) is the hypotenuse. The slope of \(DF\) is \(\frac{11 - (-9)}{7 - (-8)} = \frac{20}{15} = \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(A(-3, -5)\), \(B(0, 1)\), and \(C(3, 7)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: Yes; the slope of both \(AB\) and \(BC\) is \(2\)
d: No; the slope of \(AB\) is \(2\) and the slope of \(BC\) is \(3\)
Yes; the slope of both \(AB\) and \(BC\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\)
No; the slope of \(AB\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\) and the slope of \(BC\) is \(2\)
qs.s: \(m_{AB} = \frac{1 - (-5)}{0 - (-3)} = \frac{6}{3} = 2\) and \(m_{BC} = \frac{7 - 1}{3 - 0} = \frac{6}{3} = 2\). Since both slopes are equal, the three points lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(D(-3, 4)\), \(E(0, 2)\), and \(F(3, 0)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: Yes; the slope of both \(DE\) and \(EF\) is \(-\frac{2}{3}\)

qs.s: \(m_{DE} = \frac{2 - 4}{0 - (-3)} = -\frac{2}{3}\) and \(m_{EF} = \frac{0 - 2}{3 - 0} = -\frac{2}{3}\). Because both slopes are equal to \(-\frac{2}{3}\), the points lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(P(-2, 3)\), \(Q(1, -3)\), and \(R(3, -6)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: No; the slope of \(PQ\) is \(-2\) and the slope of \(QR\) is \(-\frac{3}{2}\)

No; the slope of \(PQ\) is \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and the slope of \(QR\) is \(-\frac{2}{3}\)
Yes; the slope of both \(PQ\) and \(QR\) is \(-\frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: \(m_{PQ} = \frac{-3 - 3}{1 - (-2)} = -2\) and \(m_{QR} = \frac{-6 - (-3)}{3 - 1} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Since the slopes are not equal, the points do not lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(R(-5, -2)\), \(S(-1, 1)\), and \(T(3, 4)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: Yes; the slope of both \(RS\) and \(ST\) is \(\frac{3}{4}\)
d: No; the slope of \(RS\) is \(\frac{3}{4}\) and the slope of \(ST\) is \(1\)
Yes; the slope of both \(RS\) and \(ST\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\)
No; the slope of \(RS\) is \(\frac{4}{3}\) and the slope of \(ST\) is \(\frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: \(m_{RS} = \frac{1 - (-2)}{-1 - (-5)} = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(m_{ST} = \frac{4 - 1}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{3}{4}\). Since the slopes are equal, the three points lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(K(-1, -4)\), \(L(2, 2)\), and \(M(4, 7)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: No; the slope of \(KL\) is \(2\) and the slope of \(LM\) is \(\frac{5}{2}\)
d: Yes; the slope of both \(KL\) and \(LM\) is \(2\)
Yes; the slope of both \(KL\) and \(LM\) is motiv\(\frac{5}{2}\)
No; the slope of \(KL\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\) and the slope of \(LM\) is \(\frac{2}{5}\)
qs.s: \(m_{KL} = \frac{2 - (-4)}{2 - (-1)} = 2\) and \(m_{LM} = \frac{7 - 2}{4 - 2} = \frac{5}{2}\). Because \(2 \neq \frac{5}{2}\), the points do not lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(U\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\), \(V\left(1, -\frac{7}{12}\right)\), and \(W\left(3, -\frac{7}{4}\right)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: No; the slope of \(UV\) is \(-\frac{1}{2}\) and the slope of \(VW\) is \(-\frac{7}{12}\)
d: Yes; the slope of both \(UV\) and \(VW\) is \(-\frac{1}{2}\)
No; the slope of \(UV\) is \(-2\) and the slope of \(VW\) is \(-\frac{12}{7}\)
Yes; the slope of both \(UV\) and \(VW\) is \(-\frac{7}{12}\)

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(D(4, -5)\), \(E(4, 3)\), and \(F(5, 11)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: No; the slope of \(DE\) is undefined and the slope of \(EF\) is \(8\)
d: Yes; the slope of both \(DE\) and \(EF\) is \(8\)
No; the slope of \(DE\) is \(0\) and the slope of \(EF\) is \(8\)
Yes; the slope of both \(DE\) and \(EF\) is \(0\)
qs.s: \(m_{DE} = \frac{3 - (-5)}{4 - 4} = \frac{8}{0}\), which is undefined, while \(m_{EF} = \frac{11 - 3}{5 - 4} = 8\). Since a vertical line segment cannot connect to a segment of slope \(8\), the points do not lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(A(-11, 23)\), \(B(-3, 9)\), and \(C(9, -12)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: Yes; the slope of both \(AB\) and \(BC\) is \(-\frac{7}{4}\)
d: No; the slope of \(AB\) is \(-\frac{7}{4}\) and the slope of \(BC\) is \(-\frac{5}{3}\)
Yes; the slope of both \(AB\) and \(BC\) is \(-\frac{4}{7}\)
No; the slope of \(AB\) is \(-\frac{4}{7}\) and the slope of \(BC\) is \(-\frac{7}{4}\)
qs.s: \(m_{AB} = \frac{9 - 23}{-3 - (-11)} = -\frac{14}{8} = -\frac{7}{4}\) and \(m_{BC} = \frac{-12 - 9}{9 - (-3)} = -\frac{21}{12} = -\frac{7}{4}\). Since both simplified slopes are equal, the points lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(P\left(-\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\), \(Q\left(1, \frac{1}{2}\right)\), and \(R\left(\frac{5}{2}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: Yes; the slope of both \(PQ\) and \(QR\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\)
d: No; the slope of \(PQ\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\) and the slope of \(QR\) is \(1\)
Yes; the slope of both \(PQ\) and \(QR\) is \(\frac{3}{2}\)
No; the slope of \(PQ\) is \(\frac{3}{2}\) and the slope of \(QR\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\)
qs.s: \(m_{PQ} = \frac{1/2 - (-1/2)}{1 - (-1/2)} = \frac{1}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(m_{QR} = \frac{3/2 - 1/2}{5/2 - 1} = \frac{1}{3/2} = \frac{2}{3}\). Because both slopes are equal, the points all lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine whether the three points \(J(-15, -28)\), \(K(5, 12)\), and \(L(20, 41)\) all lie on the same line.
qs.a: No; the slope of \(JK\) is \(2\) and the slope of \(KL\) is \(\frac{29}{15}\)
d: Yes; the slope of both \(JK\) and \(KL\) is \(2\)
No; the slope of \(JK\) is \(\frac{1}{2}\) and the slope of \(KL\) is \(\frac{15}{29}\)
Yes; the slope of both \(JK\) and \(KL\) is \(\frac{29}{15}\)
qs.s: \(m_{JK} = \frac{12 - (-28)}{5 - (-15)} = \frac{40}{20} = 2\) and \(m_{KL} = \frac{41 - 12}{20 - 5} = \frac{29}{15}\). Since \(2 \neq \frac{29}{15}\), the three points do not lie on the same line.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I and II.
qs.s: A line that only goes through quadrants I and II is horizontal and parallel to the x-axis, so its slope is zero.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I, II, and IV.
qs.s: A line passing only through quadrants I, II, and IV has positive x- and y-intercepts and falls from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I and IV.
qs.s: A line that only goes through quadrants I and IV is vertical and parallel to the y-axis, so its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants II, III, and IV.
qs.s: A line passing only through quadrants II, III, and IV has negative x- and y-intercepts and falls from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I, III, and IV.
qs.s: A line passing only through quadrants I, III, and IV has a positive x-intercept and a negative y-intercept and rises from left to right, so its slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the product of the slopes, \(m_1 \cdot m_2\), is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: Line \(L_1\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and III, and Line \(L_2\) only passes through quadrants II and III.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has a positive slope (\(m_1 > 0\)), but Line \(L_2\) is a vertical line whose slope is undefined. Multiplying by an undefined slope results in an undefined product.

qs.q: Determine if the product of the slopes, \(m_1 \cdot m_2\), is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: Line \(L_1\) only passes through quadrants II, III, and IV, and Line \(L_2\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV.
qs.s: Both lines fall from left to right, so \(m_1 < 0\) and \(m_2 < 0\). The product of two negative numbers is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the product of the slopes, \(m_1 \cdot m_2\), is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: Line \(L_1\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and III, and Line \(L_2\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) rises from left to right so \(m_1 > 0\), while Line \(L_2\) falls from left to right so \(m_2 < 0\). The product of a positive number and a negative number is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the product of the slopes, \(m_1 \cdot m_2\), is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: Line \(L_1\) only passes through quadrants I, III, and IV, and Line \(L_2\) only passes through quadrants III and IV.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has a positive slope (\(m_1 > 0\)), while Line \(L_2\) is a horizontal line with a slope of zero (\(m_2 = 0\)). Therefore, the product \(m_1 \cdot m_2 = 0\).

qs.q: Determine if the product of the slopes, \(m_1 \cdot m_2 \cdot m_3\), is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: Line \(L_1\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and III; Line \(L_2\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV; and Line \(L_3\) only passes through quadrants II, III, and IV.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has a positive slope (\(m_1 > 0\)), while Line \(L_2\) and Line \(L_3\) both have negative slopes (\(m_2 < 0, m_3 < 0\)). The product of one positive number and two negative numbers is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I, II, and III.
qs.s: A line passing only through quadrants I, II, and III crosses the negative x-axis and positive y-axis, rising from left to right. Therefore, the slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((-4, 7)\) and only passes through three quadrants, avoiding quadrant III.
qs.s: Since the line passes through \((-4, 7)\) in quadrant II and avoids quadrant III, it must pass through quadrants I, II, and IV. A line passing through these three quadrants falls from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through quadrant II and quadrant IV, but does not pass through the origin and does not enter quadrant III.
qs.s: To connect quadrants II and IV without passing through the origin or quadrant III, the line must cross the positive axes through quadrant I. A line passing through quadrants I, II, and IV falls from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((-7, -15)\) and does not enter quadrants I or II.
qs.s: Because the line contains \((-7, -15)\) and never enters quadrants I or II, its y-coordinates cannot be positive. This requires the line to be horizontal (\(y = -15\)), so its slope is zero.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((12, -8)\) and does not enter quadrants II or III.
qs.s: Because the line contains \((12, -8)\) and never enters quadrants II or III, its x-coordinates cannot be negative. This requires the line to be vertical (\(x = 12\)), so its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through quadrant I and quadrant III, but does not pass through the origin and does not enter quadrant IV.
qs.s: To connect quadrants I and III without entering quadrant IV or passing through the origin, the line must cross the negative x-axis and positive y-axis through quadrant II. A line passing through quadrants I, II, and III rises from left to right, so its slope is positive.

qs.q: Line \(A\) only passes through quadrants I, III, and IV, while Line \(B\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV. Determine if the product of the slopes of Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(A\) rises from left to right and has a positive slope, whereas Line \(B\) falls from left to right and has a negative slope. The product of a positive slope and a negative slope is negative.

qs.q: Line \(A\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and III, while Line \(B\) only passes through quadrants III and IV. Determine if the quotient of the slope of Line \(A\) divided by the slope of Line \(B\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(A\) has a positive slope, and Line \(B\) is a horizontal line with a slope of zero. Dividing any non-zero value by zero results in an undefined quantity.

qs.q: Line \(A\) only passes through quadrants I and II, while Line \(B\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and III. Determine if the product of the slopes of Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(A\) is a horizontal line because it is confined to quadrants I and II, giving it a slope of zero. Multiplying zero by the positive slope of Line \(B\) yields zero.

qs.q: Line \(A\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV, while Line \(B\) only passes through quadrants II, III, and IV. Determine if the product of the slopes of Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Both Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) fall from left to right through their respective quadrants, so each has a negative slope. The product of two negative slopes is positive.

qs.q: Line \(A\) only passes through quadrants II, III, and IV, while Line \(B\) only passes through quadrants I, II, and IV. Determine if the sum of the slopes of Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Both Line \(A\) and Line \(B\) have negative slopes based on the quadrants they pass through. The sum of two negative numbers is always negative.

qs.q: Line \(L_1\) passes only through Quadrants I and II, and Line \(L_2\) passes only through Quadrants I, III, and IV. If Line \(L_3\) has a slope equal to the product of the slopes of \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), determine if the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) is horizontal, so its slope is \(0\), while Line \(L_2\) has a positive real slope. The product of zero and any real number is \(0\), so the slope of Line \(L_3\) is zero.

qs.q: Line \(L_1\) passes only through Quadrants I, II, and IV, and Line \(L_2\) passes only through Quadrants III and IV. If Line \(L_3\) has a slope equal to the slope of \(L_1\) divided by the slope of \(L_2\), determine if the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has a non-zero negative slope, while Line \(L_2\) is a horizontal line with a slope of zero. Because division by zero is undefined, the slope of Line \(L_3\) is undefined.

qs.q: Line \(L_1\) passes through the points \((-3, 8)\) and \((5, -8)\). Line \(L_2\) passes only through Quadrants I, II, and IV. If Line \(L_3\) has a slope equal to the slope of \(L_1\) divided by the slope of \(L_2\), determine if the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) has a slope of \(\frac{-8 - 8}{5 - (-3)} = -2\), which is negative, and Line \(L_2\) avoids Quadrant III, meaning its slope is also negative. Dividing a negative number by a negative number yields a positive result, so the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive.

qs.q: Line \(L_1\) passes only through Quadrants I, III, and IV, and Line \(L_2\) passes only through Quadrants I, II, and IV. If Line \(L_3\) has a slope equal to the product of the slopes of \(L_1\) and \(L_2\), determine if the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) avoids Quadrant II, so its slope is positive, while Line \(L_2\) avoids Quadrant III, so its slope is negative. The product of a positive number and a negative number is always negative, so Line \(L_3\) has a negative slope.

qs.q: Line \(L_1\) passes only through Quadrants I, II, and III, and Line \(L_2\) passes only through Quadrants II, III, and IV. If Line \(L_3\) has a slope equal to the slope of \(L_1\) minus the slope of \(L_2\), determine if the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive, negative, zero, or undefined.
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) avoids Quadrant IV, giving it a positive slope (\(m_1 > 0\)), while Line \(L_2\) avoids Quadrant I, giving it a negative slope (\(m_2 < 0\)). Subtracting a negative number from a positive number (\(m_1 - m_2\)) always results in a positive value, so the slope of Line \(L_3\) is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants II and III.
qs.s: A line that only goes through quadrants II and III lies entirely to the left of the \(y\)-axis and is vertical. The slope of any vertical line is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through quadrants I and III.
qs.s: A line passing only through quadrants I and III must pass through the origin and rise from left to right. Since \(y\) increases as \(x\) increases, the slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((3, 0)\) and passes through quadrant III.
qs.s: Any point in quadrant III has \(x < 0\) and \(y < 0\), so the slope between \((3, 0)\) and \((x, y)\) is \(m = \frac{y - 0}{x - 3} = \frac{\text{negative}}{\text{negative}}\), which is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through quadrants I, II, and III, but does not pass through quadrant IV.
qs.s: A line passing through quadrants I, II, and III has a positive \(y\)-intercept and a negative \(x\)-intercept. Because \(y\) increases as \(x\) increases, the slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((-4, 7)\) and does not pass through quadrant III or quadrant IV.
qs.s: Since the line never enters quadrants III or IV, the \(y\)-coordinates cannot be negative, meaning the line must be horizontal (\(y = 7\)). The slope of any horizontal line is zero.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((6, -3)\) and does not pass through quadrant II or quadrant III.
qs.s: Since the line never enters quadrants II or III, the \(x\)-coordinates cannot be negative, meaning the line must be vertical (\(x = 6\)). The slope of any vertical line is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through quadrants I, II, and IV, but does not pass through quadrant III.
qs.s: A line passing through quadrants I, II, and IV has a positive \(y\)-intercept and a positive \(x\)-intercept. Because \(y\) decreases as \(x\) increases, the slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line only going through Quadrants II and IV.
qs.s: A line that passes only through Quadrants II and IV must pass through the origin and fall from left to right, so its slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((0, -5)\) and passes through Quadrant II.
qs.s: Any point in Quadrant II has a negative x-coordinate and a positive y-coordinate, so moving from that point to \((0, -5)\) means y decreases as x increases. Therefore, the slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through Quadrants I and II, but never intersects the x-axis.
qs.s: A line that never intersects the x-axis must be parallel to the x-axis, which means it is a horizontal line. Therefore, its slope is zero.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through Quadrants I and IV, but never intersects the y-axis.
qs.s: A line that never intersects the y-axis must be parallel to the y-axis, which means it is a vertical line. Therefore, its slope is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line that passes through every quadrant except quadrant III.
qs.s: Passing through every quadrant except quadrant III means the line passes through quadrants I, II, and IV. Moving from quadrant II (\(x < 0, y > 0\)) to quadrant IV (\(x > 0, y < 0\)), \(\Delta x > 0\) while \(\Delta y < 0\), which means the slope is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line that passes through quadrants I, II, and III only.
qs.s: A line passing through quadrant III (\(x < 0, y < 0\)) and quadrant I (\(x > 0, y > 0\)) without entering quadrant IV has both \(x\) and \(y\) increasing from left to right. Because \(\Delta x > 0\) and \(\Delta y > 0\), the slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line with a negative y-intercept that passes through quadrants I, III, and IV only.
qs.s: The line crosses the negative y-axis at \((0, -b)\) with \(b > 0\) and enters quadrant I (\(x > 0, y > 0\)). As \(x\) increases from \(0\) to positive values, \(y\) must increase from \(-b\) to positive values (\(\Delta y > 0\) when \(\Delta x > 0\)), so the slope is positive.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((25, -38)\) and only goes through quadrants I and IV.
qs.s: To avoid entering quadrants II and III where \(x < 0\), the line must never cross the y-axis, meaning it is vertical with equation \(x = 25\). The slope of any vertical line is undefined.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line passes through the point \((-16, -45)\) and only goes through quadrants III and IV.
qs.s: To avoid entering quadrants I and II where \(y > 0\), the line must never cross the x-axis, meaning it is horizontal with equation \(y = -45\). The slope of any horizontal line is zero.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line going through quadrants II, III, and IV.
qs.s: To pass through quadrants II, III, and IV, the line must cross the negative y-axis and the negative x-axis, falling from left to right. Therefore, the slope of the line is negative.

qs.q: Determine if the slope is positive, negative, zero, or undefined: A line going through quadrants I, II, and III.
qs.s: To pass through quadrants I, II, and III, the line must cross the positive y-axis and the negative x-axis, rising from left to right. Therefore, the slope of the line is positive.
