qs.s: The speeds are given by the magnitude of each slope: from \(t = 0\) to \(2\), \((8-0)/2 = 4\text{ km/h}\); from \(t = 2\) to \(3\), slope is \(0\text{ km/h}\) (rests); from \(t = 3\) to \(4\), \((16-8)/1 = 8\text{ km/h}\); and from \(t = 4\) to \(5\), \(|(0-16)/1| = 16\text{ km/h}\) returning home.

qs.q: An athlete trains in three consecutive stages: Stage 1, Stage 2, and Stage 3. Their cycling speed is three times their swimming speed, and their running speed is twice their swimming speed. The distance-time graph shows these three stages. Which sequence correctly matches the stages to the activities?
qs.a: Stage 1: swimming; Stage 2: cycling; Stage 3: running
d: Stage 1: running; Stage 2: cycling; Stage 3: swimming
Stage 1: swimming; Stage 2: running; Stage 3: cycling
Stage 1: cycling; Stage 2: running; Stage 3: swimming
qs.s: From the slopes, the speeds are \((4-0)/2 = 2\text{ km/h}\) for Stage 1, \((10-4)/1 = 6\text{ km/h}\) for Stage 2, and \((18-10)/2 = 4\text{ km/h}\) for Stage 3. Since \(6 = 3 \times 2\) and \(4 = 2 \times 2\), Stage 1 is swimming, Stage 2 is cycling, and Stage 3 is running.

exercises.name: Rate of change from a graph

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: Choose two points on the line, \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, such as \((0, 1)\) and \((3, 3)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{3 - 1}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the linear relation shown in the graph.
qs.s: Select two points on the line, \((-1, 4)\) and \((1, -2)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-2 - 4}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to find the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 2)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{2 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the quadratic function \(f(x)\) to determine the average rate of change over the interval \([0, 4]\).
qs.s: Find the values of the function at the endpoints of the interval: \(f(0) = 5\) and \(f(4) = -3\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{-3 - 5}{4 - 0} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise function \(y = g(x)\). Determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([-4, 4]\).
qs.s: Find the function values at the endpoints: \(g(-4) = 1\) and \(g(4) = 3\). The average rate of change over \([-4, 4]\) is \(\frac{g(4) - g(-4)}{4 - (-4)} = \frac{3 - 1}{8} = \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the function \(f(x)\) to determine the average rate of change over the interval \([0, 6]\).
qs.s: Read the coordinates at the endpoints: \((0, -3)\) and \((6, 6)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{6 - (-3)}{6 - 0} = \frac{9}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Use the graph of the function \(f(x)\) to determine the average rate of change over the interval \([0, 3]\).
qs.s: From the graph, \(f(0) = 3\) and \(f(3) = 0\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{0 - 3}{3 - 0} = \frac{-3}{3} = -1\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function. Determine the rate of change of the function on the interval \([1, 5]\).
qs.s: On the interval \([1, 5]\), the graph is a line segment connecting \((1, 4)\) and \((5, -2)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-2 - 4}{5 - 1} = -\frac{6}{4} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the linear relation shown in the graph.
qs.s: Choose two points on the line, such as \((-1, -1)\) and \((2, 5)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{5 - (-1)}{2 - (-1)} = \frac{6}{3} = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([0, 4]\).
qs.s: The endpoints of the interval correspond to the points \((0, -2)\) and \((4, 6)\) on the graph. The average rate of change is \(\frac{6 - (-2)}{4 - 0} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([0, 6]\).
qs.s: Identify the values on the curve at the endpoints: \((0, 3)\) and \((6, 0)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{0 - 3}{6 - 0} = -\frac{3}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function. Determine the rate of change of the function over the interval \([3, 5]\).
qs.s: On the interval \([3, 5]\), the function is the line segment connecting \((3, 2)\) and \((5, -4)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-4 - 2}{5 - 3} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([0, 3]\).
qs.s: Find the coordinates on the curve at the endpoints of the interval: \((0, 3)\) and \((3, 0)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{0 - 3}{3 - 0} = \frac{-3}{3} = -1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([-4, 5]\).
qs.s: Read the points on the curve at \(x = -4\) and \(x = 5\), which are \((-4, -3)\) and \((5, 0)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{0 - (-3)}{5 - (-4)} = \frac{3}{9} = \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Choose the marked points \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\) on the line. The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([1, 3]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the curve passes through \((1, -1)\) and \((3, 5)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{5 - (-1)}{3 - 1} = \frac{6}{2} = 3\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([1, 5]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the points corresponding to the interval endpoints are \((1, 4)\) and \((5, -4)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{-4 - 4}{5 - 1} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([-4, 4]\).
qs.s: The coordinates at the interval boundaries are \((-4, -2)\) and \((4, 2)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{2 - (-2)}{4 - (-4)} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([0, 4]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the endpoints of the interval are \((0, -3)\) and \((4, 5)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{5 - (-3)}{4 - 0} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([-3, 3]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the points at the ends of the interval are \((-3, 2)\) and \((3, 0)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{0 - 2}{3 - (-3)} = \frac{-2}{6} = -\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, (-3, -1) and (3, 3). The rate of change is (3 - (-1)) / (3 - (-3)) = 4 / 6 = 2/3.

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the linear relation shown in the graph.
qs.s: Using the marked points (-1, 3) and (2, -3), calculate the slope: m = (-3 - 3) / (2 - (-1)) = -6 / 3 = -2.

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the linear function shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify the two points plotted on the line: (-2, 4) and (6, -2). The rate of change is (-2 - 4) / (6 - (-2)) = -6 / 8 = -3/4.

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function h(x). Determine the rate of change of h(x) on the interval [2, 6].
qs.s: On the interval [2, 6], the line segment connects (2, 5) and (6, -1). The rate of change is (-1 - 5) / (6 - 2) = -6 / 4 = -3/2.

qs.q: Use the graph of the parabola to determine the average rate of change over the interval [0, 4].
qs.s: Read the points from the graph at the interval endpoints: (0, -2) and (4, 6). The average rate of change is (6 - (-2)) / (4 - 0) = 8 / 4 = 2.

qs.q: Use the graph of the function to determine the average rate of change on the interval [-3, 1].
qs.s: At x = -3, y = -5, and at x = 1, y = 3. The average rate of change is (3 - (-5)) / (1 - (-3)) = 8 / 4 = 2.

qs.q: The graph shows the altitude y (in meters) of a drone over time x (in seconds). Determine the rate of change of altitude between x = 4 and x = 8.
qs.s: Find the coordinates at x = 4 and x = 8, which are (4, 12) and (8, 4). The rate of change is (4 - 12) / (8 - 4) = -8 / 4 = -2 m/s.

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: Using the marked points (-1, 4) and (1, -2), the rate of change is (-2 - 4) / (1 - (-1)) = -6 / 2 = -3.

qs.q: Determine the rate of change of the linear relation shown in the graph.
qs.s: Choose two points on the line, (0, -1) and (2, 3). The rate of change is the slope: (3 - (-1)) / (2 - 0) = 4 / 2 = 2.

qs.q: Find the rate of change of the graphed line.
qs.s: Using the marked points (-3, -1) and (3, 3), the rate of change is (3 - (-1)) / (3 - (-3)) = 4 / 6 = 2/3.

qs.q: Determine the rate of change shown in the graph.
qs.s: Using the marked points (-2, 3) and (2, 0), the rate of change is (0 - 3) / (2 - (-2)) = -3 / 4 = -3/4.

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Using the marked points (-2, 3) and (3, -2), the rate of change is (-2 - 3) / (3 - (-2)) = -5 / 5 = -1.

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function. What is the rate of change of the function on the interval [3, 7]?
qs.s: On the interval [3, 7], the line passes through (3, 6) and (7, 0). The rate of change is (0 - 6) / (7 - 3) = -6 / 4 = -3/2.

qs.q: Find the average rate of change of the function over the interval [0, 4] using the graph.
qs.s: From the graph, f(0) = -2 and f(4) = 6. The average rate of change is (6 - (-2)) / (4 - 0) = 8 / 4 = 2.

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the graphed function over the interval [-2, 4].
qs.s: Reading the graph at the interval endpoints gives (-2, 0) and (4, 3). The average rate of change is (3 - 0) / (4 - (-2)) = 3 / 6 = 1/2.

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, Line A and Line B. How much greater is the rate of change of Line A than the rate of change of Line B?
qs.s: Line A passes through (0, 0) and (2, 6), giving a rate of change of 6 / 2 = 3. Line B passes through (0, 1) and (4, 3), giving a rate of change of (3 - 1) / (4 - 0) = 0.5. The difference is 3 - 0.5 = 2.5.

qs.q: Use the graph of the function to find its average rate of change over the interval [1, 4].
qs.s: From the graph, the endpoints for the interval are (1, 4) and (4, -5). The average rate of change is (-5 - 4) / (4 - 1) = -9 / 3 = -3.

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, such as \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise function \(f(x)\). Determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([-6, 6]\).
qs.s: Read the function values at the endpoints: \(f(-6) = -4\) and \(f(6) = 5\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{5 - (-4)}{6 - (-6)} = \frac{9}{12} = \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Use the graph of \(f(x)\) to determine the average rate of change over the interval \([-2, 1]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the coordinates at the endpoints of the interval are \((-2, -5)\) and \((1, 4)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{4 - (-5)}{1 - (-2)} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph of \(g(x)\) to determine the average rate of change over the interval \([-1, 3]\).
qs.s: Reading the points from the graph gives \((-1, -4)\) and \((3, 4)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{4 - (-4)}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function \(h(x)\). Determine the rate of change of the function on the interval \([1, 5]\).
qs.s: On the interval \([1, 5]\), the segment connects the points \((1, 5)\) and \((5, -5)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-5 - 5}{5 - 1} = \frac{-10}{4} = -\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to calculate the rate of change.
qs.s: Select the marked points \((-1, 2)\) and \((1, -4)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{-4 - 2}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the rate of change of the relation.
qs.s: For any two points on this horizontal line, such as \((-3, 2)\) and \((3, 2)\), the vertical change is \(\Delta y = 2 - 2 = 0\). Hence, the rate of change is \(\frac{0}{3 - (-3)} = 0\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the rate of change of the linear relation.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, such as \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x} = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise function \(f(x)\). Determine the average rate of change of \(f(x)\) over the interval \([-6, 2]\).
qs.s: From the graph, the values at the interval endpoints are \(f(-6) = -3\) and \(f(2) = 1\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{f(2) - f(-6)}{2 - (-6)} = \frac{1 - (-3)}{2 - (-6)} = \frac{4}{8} = \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: The graph shows the quadratic function \(f(x) = \frac{1}{4}x^2 - 4\). Determine the average rate of change of \(f(x)\) over the interval \([-4, 2]\).
qs.s: From the graph, \(f(-4) = 0\) and \(f(2) = -3\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{f(2) - f(-4)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{-3 - 0}{2 - (-4)} = -\frac{3}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise linear function. Determine the rate of change of the function over the interval \([5, 9]\).
qs.s: Over \([5, 9]\), the segment connects the points \((5, 7)\) and \((9, -1)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-1 - 7}{9 - 5} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\).

qs.q: The graph shows the quadratic function \(f(x) = x^2 - 2x - 3\). Determine the average rate of change of \(f(x)\) over the interval \([1, 4]\).
qs.s: From the graph, \(f(1) = -4\) and \(f(4) = 5\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{f(4) - f(1)}{4 - 1} = \frac{5 - (-4)}{3} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\).

qs.q: Use the given graph to determine the rate of change of the line.
qs.s: Using the marked points \((-6, 9)\) and \((6, -7)\), the rate of change is \(\frac{-7 - 9}{6 - (-6)} = \frac{-16}{12} = -\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change for the linear function shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, \((-1, 4)\) and \((1, -2)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-2 - 4}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change for the line shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, \((-2, 4)\) and \((2, -2)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{-2 - 4}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{-6}{4} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the rate of change for the linear relation shown in the graph.
qs.s: Identify two points on the line, \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\). The rate of change is \(\frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{4}{2} = 2\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the quadratic function shown in the graph over the interval \([1, 4]\).
qs.s: Locate the points on the parabola at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 4\), which are \((1, 4)\) and \((4, -5)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{-5 - 4}{4 - 1} = \frac{-9}{3} = -3\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([0, 6]\).
qs.s: Find the endpoints of the interval on the graph, which are \((0, 4)\) and \((6, -5)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{-5 - 4}{6 - 0} = \frac{-9}{6} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function \(f(x)\) shown in the graph over the interval \([1, 3]\).
qs.s: Find the coordinates on the graph at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 3\), which are \((1, -3)\) and \((3, 5)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{5 - (-3)}{3 - 1} = \frac{8}{2} = 4\).

qs.q: Determine the average rate of change of the function shown in the graph over the interval \([1, 2]\).
qs.s: Locate the points on the graph at \(x = 1\) and \(x = 2\), which are \((1, -2)\) and \((2, 2)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{2 - (-2)}{2 - 1} = \frac{4}{1} = 4\).

qs.q: The graph shows a piecewise function. Determine the average rate of change of the function over the interval \([-1, 5]\).
qs.s: Find the values of the function at the endpoints of the interval: \((-1, 4)\) and \((5, -2)\). The average rate of change is \(\frac{-2 - 4}{5 - (-1)} = \frac{-6}{6} = -1\).

exercises.name: Multi-step rate of change word problems

qs.q: Water is pumped into a storage tank at a constant rate. At 10 minutes, the tank contains 180 liters of water, and at 25 minutes, it contains 390 liters. How many liters of water will be in the tank at 40 minutes?
qs.s: The filling rate is \(\frac{390 - 180}{25 - 10} = 14\) liters per minute. In the next \(40 - 25 = 15\) minutes, an additional \(15 \times 14 = 210\) liters are added, giving \(390 + 210 = 600\) liters.

qs.q: A motorist drives along a highway at a steady speed. At the 40 km marker, the elapsed driving time is 25 minutes, and at the 100 km marker, the elapsed time is 65 minutes. At this steady speed, what will the driving time be at the 160 km marker?
qs.s: The rate of travel is \(\frac{65 - 25}{100 - 40} = \frac{2}{3}\) minutes per km. The time at the 160 km marker is \(65 + (160 - 100) \times \frac{2}{3} = 65 + 40 = 105\) minutes.

qs.q: A candle burns down at a constant rate after being lit. At 15 minutes, its height is 22 cm, and at 45 minutes, its height is 16 cm. If it continues to burn at this rate, what will its height be at 75 minutes?
qs.s: The rate of change of height is \(\frac{16 - 22}{45 - 15} = -0.2\) cm per minute. At 75 minutes, the candle's height is \(16 + (75 - 45)(-0.2) = 16 - 6 = 10\) cm.

qs.q: Elena cycled at a steady rate from the 5 km mark to the end of a 25 km ride. At the 5 km mark, her elapsed time was 14 minutes, and at the 17 km mark, her elapsed time was 50 minutes. Determine the total time it took Elena to complete the 25 km ride.
qs.s: Elena's rate of change is \(\frac{50 - 14}{17 - 5} = 3\) minutes per km. Her total time to finish at 25 km is \(50 + (25 - 17) \times 3 = 74\) minutes.

qs.q: Marcus hiked up a mountain trail at a steady pace from the 2 km marker to the summit at the 9 km marker. At the 2 km marker, his elapsed time was 35 minutes, and at the 6 km marker, his elapsed time was 95 minutes. What was his elapsed time when he reached the summit?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{95 - 35}{6 - 2} = 15\) minutes per km. Reaching the 9 km summit takes an additional \((9 - 6) \times 15 = 45\) minutes, giving a total time of \(95 + 45 = 140\) minutes.

qs.q: A passenger train travels at a steady speed between two cities. At a station 140 km from the start, the elapsed travel time is 1 hour and 15 minutes. At a station 320 km from the start, the elapsed travel time is 2 hours and 45 minutes. If the train maintains this steady speed to the final terminal at 460 km, what is the total travel time?
qs.s: Converting times to 75 and 165 minutes gives a rate of \(\frac{165 - 75}{320 - 140} = 0.5\) minutes per km. Traveling from 320 km to 460 km takes \((460 - 320) \times 0.5 = 70\) more minutes, for a total of \(165 + 70 = 235\) minutes, or 3 hours 55 minutes.

qs.q: An airplane climbs at a steady rate after takeoff. At an altitude of 4200 m, the flight timer reads 8 minutes. At an altitude of 7800 m, the flight timer reads 17 minutes. The pilot is instructed to level off exactly when the flight timer reaches 23 minutes. What altitude will the airplane reach at that moment?
qs.s: The rate of climb is \(\frac{7800 - 4200}{17 - 8} = 400\) m per minute. At 23 minutes, the altitude is \(7800 + (23 - 17) \times 400 = 7800 + 2400 = 10\ 200\) m.

qs.q: A print shop starts a large production run with an ink reservoir. After printing 1200 posters, 840 mL of ink remains in the reservoir. After printing 2800 posters, 520 mL of ink remains. If ink is consumed at this constant rate, what is the total number of posters that can be printed from the start before the reservoir is completely empty?
qs.s: The consumption rate is \(\frac{520 - 840}{2800 - 1200} = -0.2\) mL per poster. Depleting the remaining 520 mL requires \(\frac{520}{0.2} = 2600\) additional posters, giving a total of \(2800 + 2600 = 5400\) posters.

qs.q: A research balloon ascends into the atmosphere where the temperature drops at a constant rate with altitude. At an altitude of 1200 m, the temperature is \(8^\circ\text{C}\), and at 3200 m, the temperature is \(-4^\circ\text{C}\). What temperature will the balloon record at an altitude of 5700 m?
qs.s: The rate of temperature change is \(\frac{-4 - 8}{3200 - 1200} = -0.006^\circ\text{C}\) per meter. At 5700 m, the temperature is \(-4 + (5700 - 3200)(-0.006) = -4 - 15 = -19^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: In a 42 km marathon, Maya ran at a steady pace after the 6 km checkpoint. At the 6 km checkpoint, her time was 31 minutes, and at the 26 km checkpoint, her time was 131 minutes. If her goal was to finish the marathon in under 4 hours (240 minutes), by how many minutes did her actual finish time beat her goal?
qs.s: Maya's pace is \(\frac{131 - 31}{26 - 6} = 5\) minutes per km, making her finish time \(131 + (42 - 26) \times 5 = 211\) minutes. She beats the 240-minute goal by \(240 - 211 = 29\) minutes.

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: A canoeist paddling down a river passes the 12 km checkpoint in 1 hr 12 min, and passes the 22 km checkpoint 1 hour later. Assuming a constant rate, find the speed of the canoeist in km/h.
qs.s: The canoeist covers 22 km - 12 km = 10 km in 1 hour, giving a speed of 10 km / 1 h = 10 km/h.

qs.q: A driver on a highway passes the 45 km marker in 30 minutes, and passes the 135 km marker 1 hour later. Assuming a constant speed, find the speed of the driver in km/h.
qs.s: The change in distance is 135 km - 45 km = 90 km over 1 hour, giving a speed of 90 km / 1 h = 90 km/h.

qs.q: A marathon runner passes the 10 km mark in 50 minutes, and passes the 22 km mark 1 hour later. Assuming a constant rate, find the speed of the runner in km/h.
qs.s: The runner covers 22 km - 10 km = 12 km in 1 hour, which gives a speed of 12 km / 1 h = 12 km/h.

qs.q: A cyclist passes the 15 km mark of a trail in 45 minutes, and passes the 35 km mark 1 hour later. Assuming a constant rate, find the speed of the cyclist in km/h.
qs.s: The cyclist travels 35 km - 15 km = 20 km in the 1 hour between checkpoints, so the speed is 20 km / 1 h = 20 km/h.

qs.q: A hiker passes the 8 km mark of a mountain trail in 2 hours, and passes the 14 km mark 1 hr 30 min later. Assuming a constant rate, find the walking speed of the hiker in km/h.
qs.s: The hiker covers 14 km - 8 km = 6 km in 1.5 hours, so the speed is 6 km / 1.5 h = 4 km/h.

qs.q: A marathon runner passes the 18 km mark in 1 hour 15 minutes, and passes the 30 km mark 50 minutes later. Assuming a constant rate, find the speed of the runner in km/h.
qs.s: The runner covers 30 km - 18 km = 12 km in 50 minutes, which is 5/6 of an hour. The speed is 12 / (5/6) = 14.4 km/h.

qs.q: A long-distance runner passes the 9 km mark in 45 minutes, and passes the 27 km mark 1 hour and 12 minutes later. By how many km/h did the runner's speed increase in the second interval compared to the first?
qs.s: The first speed is 9 km / 0.75 h = 12 km/h, and the second speed is (27 - 9) km / 1.2 h = 18 / 1.2 = 15 km/h. The increase is 15 - 12 = 3 km/h.

qs.q: A descending airplane passes an altitude of 9600 m at 4:10 p.m. and reaches an altitude of 3200 m at 4:26 p.m. What is the average rate of descent of the airplane in metres per minute?
qs.s: The altitude drops by 9600 m - 3200 m = 6400 m over 4:26 - 4:10 = 16 minutes, giving a rate of descent of 6400 m / 16 min = 400 m/min.

qs.q: A driver passes the 65 km marker on an interstate at 1:15 p.m. and passes the 245 km marker at 3:30 p.m. Assuming a constant speed, find the driver's speed in km/h.
qs.s: The elapsed time from 1:15 p.m. to 3:30 p.m. is 2 hours 15 minutes, or 2.25 hours. The speed is (245 - 65) km / 2.25 h = 180 / 2.25 = 80 km/h.

qs.q: A cyclist passes the 18 km mark of a ride in 45 minutes, and passes the 58 km mark 1 hour and 15 minutes later. Find the cyclist's average speed over the entire 58 km ride in km/h.
qs.s: The total time for the entire ride is 45 min + 1 hr 15 min = 2 hours. The average speed over the entire ride is 58 km / 2 h = 29 km/h.

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: A plane cruising at an altitude of 24 000 feet begins its descent for landing after flying for 4 hours. The entire flight time was 4 hours 30 minutes. Determine the average rate of descent of the plane in feet per minute.
qs.s: The descent took \(4\text{ h } 30\text{ min} - 4\text{ h} = 30\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{24\,000\text{ ft}}{30\text{ min}} = 800\text{ ft/min}\).

qs.q: A delivery drone cruising at an altitude of 1500 feet begins its descent after flying for 50 minutes. The drone touches down safely after a total flight time of 1 hour 15 minutes. Determine the average rate of descent of the drone in feet per minute.
qs.s: The descent took \(75\text{ min} - 50\text{ min} = 25\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{1500\text{ ft}}{25\text{ min}} = 60\text{ ft/min}\).

qs.q: A storage reservoir containing 36 000 litres of water begins draining after remaining full for 5 hours. The reservoir is completely emptied when the total elapsed time reaches 5 hours 45 minutes. Determine the average drainage rate in litres per minute.
qs.s: The drainage took \(5\text{ h } 45\text{ min} - 5\text{ h} = 45\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of drainage was \(\frac{36\,000\text{ L}}{45\text{ min}} = 800\text{ L/min}\).

qs.q: A hot air balloon flying at an altitude of 1800 metres begins to descend after cruising for 2 hours. The balloon touches down when the total flight time reaches 2 hours 20 minutes. Determine the balloon's average rate of descent in metres per minute.
qs.s: The descent took \(2\text{ h } 20\text{ min} - 2\text{ h} = 20\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{1800\text{ m}}{20\text{ min}} = 90\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q: A research submarine at a depth of 450 metres begins ascending to the surface after 3 hours of an underwater survey. The total mission time when it surfaces is 3 hours 15 minutes. Determine the submarine's average rate of ascent in metres per minute.
qs.s: The ascent took \(3\text{ h } 15\text{ min} - 3\text{ h} = 15\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of ascent was \(\frac{450\text{ m}}{15\text{ min}} = 30\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q: A high-altitude weather balloon at an altitude of 28.8 kilometres begins its descent after collecting atmospheric data for 3 hours. The entire flight from launch to touchdown at sea level lasts 3 hours 48 minutes. Determine the balloon's average rate of descent in metres per second.
qs.s: The balloon descended \(28.8\text{ km} = 28\,800\text{ m}\) in \(48\text{ minutes} = 48 \times 60 = 2880\text{ seconds}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{28\,800\text{ m}}{2880\text{ s}} = 10\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: A commercial airliner cruising at an altitude of 37 000 feet begins descending at 2 hours 15 minutes into the flight. It levels off at an assigned holding altitude of 12 000 feet at 2 hours 40 minutes. Determine the airplane's average rate of descent in feet per minute.
qs.s: The change in altitude was \(37\,000 - 12\,000 = 25\,000\text{ ft}\) over \(2\text{ h } 40\text{ min} - 2\text{ h } 15\text{ min} = 25\text{ minutes}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{25\,000\text{ ft}}{25\text{ min}} = 1000\text{ ft/min}\).

qs.q: A spacecraft begins re-entering the atmosphere at an altitude of 140 kilometres at 08:35 and descends to an altitude of 35 kilometres at 08:56. Determine its average rate of descent in kilometres per hour.
qs.s: The altitude dropped \(140 - 35 = 105\text{ km}\) in \(21\text{ minutes} = \frac{21}{60}\text{ hours} = 0.35\text{ hours}\). The average rate of descent was \(\frac{105\text{ km}}{0.35\text{ h}} = 300\text{ km/h}\).

qs.q: Flight A begins descending from an altitude of 31 500 feet after flying for 3 hours 15 minutes, landing at 4 hours 00 minutes. Flight B begins descending from an altitude of 26 000 feet after flying for 2 hours 50 minutes, landing at 3 hours 30 minutes. Determine the difference between the average rates of descent of the two flights in feet per minute.
qs.s: Flight A descended in \(45\text{ min}\) at \(\frac{31\,500\text{ ft}}{45\text{ min}} = 700\text{ ft/min}\), and Flight B descended in \(40\text{ min}\) at \(\frac{26\,000\text{ ft}}{40\text{ min}} = 650\text{ ft/min}\). The difference in their rates of descent is \(700 - 650 = 50\text{ ft/min}\).

qs.q: A cargo plane at an altitude of 34 000 feet begins its descent. For the first 30 minutes, it descends at an average rate of 700 feet per minute. It then enters its final approach and lands 20 minutes later. Determine the average rate of descent during the final 20-minute approach.
qs.s: In the first phase the plane descended \(700 \times 30 = 21\,000\text{ ft}\), leaving \(34\,000 - 21\,000 = 13\,000\text{ ft}\) to descend in the final 20 minutes. The average rate was \(\frac{13\,000\text{ ft}}{20\text{ min}} = 650\text{ ft/min}\).

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: A student is reading an assigned novel. When she starts reading on Saturday, she has already completed \(\frac{1}{8}\) of the book. Six hours later, she has completed \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the book. Calculate her reading rate per hour.
qs.s: The fraction of the book read is \(\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{13}{24}\). Dividing by 6 hours gives an average reading rate of \(\frac{13}{24} \div 6 = \frac{13}{144}\) of the book per hour.

qs.q: A storage tank is being filled with water. When the pump is turned on, the tank is \(\frac{1}{4}\) full. Six hours later, the tank is \(\frac{5}{6}\) full. Calculate the filling rate per hour.
qs.s: The fraction filled during this period is \(\frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{7}{12}\). Dividing by 6 hours gives the filling rate of \(\frac{7}{12} \div 6 = \frac{7}{72}\) of the tank per hour.

qs.q: A tablet battery was at \(\frac{1}{6}\) of full charge when plugged into a charger. Three hours later, the battery is at \(\frac{4}{5}\) of full charge. Calculate the charging rate per hour.
qs.s: The battery gained \(\frac{4}{5} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{19}{30}\) of full charge. Dividing by 3 hours yields a charging rate of \(\frac{19}{30} \div 3 = \frac{19}{90}\) of full charge per hour.

qs.q: A painter begins painting a fence where \(\frac{1}{5}\) was already painted. Four hours later, \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the fence is painted. Calculate the painter's painting rate per hour.
qs.s: The change in the fraction painted is \(\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{5} = \frac{7}{15}\). Dividing this by the 4 hours worked gives a rate of \(\frac{7}{15} \div 4 = \frac{7}{60}\) of the fence per hour.

qs.q: A road crew is paving a stretch of highway. Before starting their shift, \(\frac{2}{5}\) of the highway was already paved. Five hours later, \(\frac{7}{8}\) of the highway is paved. Calculate the paving rate per hour.
qs.s: The change in the paved portion is \(\frac{7}{8} - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{19}{40}\). Dividing by 5 hours gives a paving rate of \(\frac{19}{40} \div 5 = \frac{19}{200}\) of the highway per hour.

qs.q: At 9:00 AM, a swimming pool was \(\frac{5}{6}\) full. Due to a drain leak, by 5:00 PM that same day, the pool was only \(\frac{3}{8}\) full. Calculate the average rate of change of the pool's water level per hour.
qs.s: The change in water level is \(\frac{3}{8} - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{11}{24}\) over an 8-hour period. The average rate of change is \(-\frac{11}{24} \div 8 = -\frac{11}{192}\) of the pool per hour.

qs.q: A 3D printer creates a sculpture. After 2 hours of printing, it is \(\frac{1}{8}\) complete; after 5 hours, it is \(\frac{3}{8}\) complete; and after 9 hours, it is \(\frac{5}{6}\) complete. How much greater was the printer's average hourly rate between hour 5 and hour 9 than between hour 2 and hour 5?
qs.s: The rate between hours 2 and 5 is \(\left(\frac{3}{8} - \frac{1}{8}\right) \div 3 = \frac{1}{12}\), and between hours 5 and 9 it is \(\left(\frac{5}{6} - \frac{3}{8}\right) \div 4 = \frac{11}{96}\). The difference between the rates is \(\frac{11}{96} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{3}{96} = \frac{1}{32}\) of the sculpture per hour.

qs.q: Worker A starts a task with \(\frac{1}{5}\) completed and reaches \(\frac{3}{4}\) after 5 hours. Worker B starts the same task with \(\frac{1}{4}\) completed and reaches \(\frac{5}{6}\) after 7 hours. By how much does Worker A's hourly rate exceed Worker B's hourly rate?
qs.s: Worker A's rate is \(\left(\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{5}\right) \div 5 = \frac{11}{100}\) and Worker B's rate is \(\left(\frac{5}{6} - \frac{1}{4}\right) \div 7 = \frac{1}{12}\). The difference between the rates is \(\frac{11}{100} - \frac{1}{12} = \frac{33 - 25}{300} = \frac{2}{75}\) of the task per hour.

qs.q: A high-speed train travels along a route. At 20 minutes into the journey, it has covered \(\frac{1}{6}\) of the total distance. At 1 hour and 40 minutes, it has covered \(\frac{7}{9}\) of the total distance. What is the train's average rate of progress per hour?
qs.s: The elapsed time is 1 hour and 20 minutes, or \(\frac{4}{3}\) hours, and the distance covered is \(\frac{7}{9} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{11}{18}\). Dividing gives a rate of \(\frac{11}{18} \div \frac{4}{3} = \frac{11}{18} \times \frac{3}{4} = \frac{11}{24}\) of the distance per hour.

qs.q: A groundskeeper starts mowing a large lawn at 8:30 AM, when \(\frac{1}{6}\) of it was already cut. By 11:00 AM, \(\frac{7}{10}\) of the lawn is cut. Calculate the groundskeeper's mowing rate per hour.
qs.s: The time elapsed is \(2.5 = \frac{5}{2}\) hours, and the fraction mowed is \(\frac{7}{10} - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{8}{15}\). Dividing gives the mowing rate: \(\frac{8}{15} \div \frac{5}{2} = \frac{8}{15} \times \frac{2}{5} = \frac{16}{75}\) of the lawn per hour.

exercises.name: Slope, rise, run, and grade applications

qs.q: A symmetrical gable roof spans a total width of 16 feet. The ridge at the center rises 36 inches above the base. What is the slope of the roof?
qs.s: Because the roof is symmetrical, the horizontal run to the center ridge is \(\frac{16}{2} = 8\text{ ft} = 96\text{ in.}\) The slope is \(\frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{36}{96} = \frac{3}{8}\).

qs.q: A ramp currently has a horizontal run of 15 feet and rises 18 inches. By how many feet must the horizontal run be extended so that the ramp has a slope of \(\frac{1}{12}\)?
qs.s: For a slope of \(\frac{1}{12}\), a rise of 18 inches requires a run of \(18 \times 12 = 216\text{ in.} = 18\text{ ft}\). Extending the 15-foot run to 18 feet requires an additional \(18 - 15 = 3\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A mountain road climbs from an elevation of 4500 feet to 7140 feet over a horizontal distance of 5 miles. Given that \(1\text{ mile} = 5280\text{ feet}\), what is the slope of the road?
qs.s: The rise is \(7140 - 4500 = 2640\text{ ft}\) and the run is \(5 \times 5280 = 26400\text{ ft}\). The slope is \(\frac{2640}{26400} = \frac{1}{10}\).

qs.q: A drainage pipe must be installed with a downward slope of magnitude \(\frac{1}{50}\). If the pipe drops a vertical distance of 18 inches, what is the horizontal distance it covers, in feet?
qs.s: The horizontal run in inches is \(\frac{18}{1/50} = 900\text{ in.}\) Converting to feet gives \(\frac{900}{12} = 75\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A hiking trail has a constant slope of \(\frac{3}{25}\). If a hiker walks along a section of the trail that covers a horizontal distance of 600 yards, what is the elevation change, in feet? (\(1\text{ yard} = 3\text{ feet}\))
qs.s: The horizontal run is \(600\text{ yd} \times 3 = 1800\text{ ft}\). The elevation change is \(\frac{3}{25} \times 1800 = 216\text{ ft}\).

exercises.name: Slope, rise, run, and grade applications

qs.q: A railway track is designed with a constant 2% grade. How much elevation does a train gain along a 3200 m horizontal stretch of track?
qs.s: The elevation gained is calculated as \(\text{rise} = 0.02 \times 3200\text{ m} = 64\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A hiking trail climbs at an average grade of 12%. What is the change in elevation over a horizontal distance of 450 m?
qs.s: The elevation change is \(\text{rise} = 0.12 \times 450\text{ m} = 54\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A mountain road has a maximum grade of 6%. How much change in elevation occurs over a horizontal distance of 1500 m?
qs.s: The change in elevation is found by multiplying the grade by the horizontal distance: \(0.06 \times 1500\text{ m} = 90\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A scenic highway has a continuous 5% grade. How much change in elevation occurs along a 1400 m stretch of horizontal road?
qs.s: The change in elevation is \(\text{rise} = 0.05 \times 1400\text{ m} = 70\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Building regulations state that an access ramp cannot exceed an 8% grade. What is the maximum allowable change in elevation for a ramp with a horizontal run of 25 m?
qs.s: The maximum allowable rise is \(\text{rise} = \text{grade} \times \text{run} = 0.08 \times 25\text{ m} = 2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A railway line must climb to a mountain station that is 105 m higher than the valley station. If safety standards restrict the track to a maximum grade of 3.5%, what is the minimum horizontal run required?
qs.s: Using \(\text{run} = \text{rise} / \text{grade}\), the minimum run is \(105 / 0.035 = 3000\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A highway begins at an elevation of 350 m above sea level and climbs at a steady 4.5% grade over a horizontal distance of 6000 m. What is the final elevation of the highway?
qs.s: The elevation gain is \(0.045 \times 6000\text{ m} = 270\text{ m}\). Adding this to the starting elevation gives a final elevation of \(350 + 270 = 620\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An access ramp with a horizontal run of 40 m was initially constructed with a 10% grade. To meet new accessibility regulations, the vertical rise must be reduced by 1.6 m while keeping the 40 m horizontal run unchanged. What is the new percent grade of the ramp?
qs.s: The initial rise was \(0.10 \times 40 = 4\text{ m}\), so the adjusted rise is \(4 - 1.6 = 2.4\text{ m}\). The new grade is \((2.4 / 40) \times 100\% = 6\%\).

qs.q: A mountain pass road climbs from an initial elevation of 420 m to a peak elevation of 1140 m over a horizontal distance of 12 km. What is the average percent grade of the road?
qs.s: The total vertical rise is \(1140 - 420 = 720\text{ m}\) and the horizontal run is \(12\text{ km} = 12\,000\text{ m}\). The percent grade is \((720 / 12\,000) \times 100\% = 6\%\).

qs.q: A road consists of two consecutive sections. The first section has a 5% grade over a horizontal run of 1200 m, and the second section has an 8% grade over a horizontal run of 1500 m. What is the total change in elevation over the entire road?
qs.s: The first section rises \(0.05 \times 1200 = 60\text{ m}\) and the second rises \(0.08 \times 1500 = 120\text{ m}\). Adding both gives a total elevation change of \(60 + 120 = 180\text{ m}\).

exercises.name: Slope, rise, run, and grade applications

qs.q: A wheelchair ramp rises 3 ft over a horizontal run of 36 ft. Determine the height of a vertical support post placed 24 ft from the bottom of the ramp.
qs.s: The slope of the ramp is \(\frac{3\text{ ft}}{36\text{ ft}} = \frac{1}{12}\). Multiplying this slope by the run of \(24\text{ ft}\) gives a height of \(\frac{1}{12} \times 24 = 2\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: The roof of a garage rises 12 ft over a horizontal run of 20 ft. Determine the height of a vertical support placed 15 ft from the low end of the roof.
qs.s: The slope of the roof is \(\frac{12\text{ ft}}{20\text{ ft}} = \frac{3}{5}\). At \(15\text{ ft}\) from the low end, the height of the support is \(\frac{3}{5} \times 15 = 9\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A conveyor belt rises 10 m over a horizontal distance of 25 m. Determine the vertical height of the belt at a point 15 m from its lower end.
qs.s: The slope of the conveyor belt is \(\frac{10\text{ m}}{25\text{ m}} = 0.4\). The height at \(15\text{ m}\) from the lower end is \(0.4 \times 15 = 6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A skateboard ramp rises 5 ft over a horizontal run of 15 ft. Determine the height of a vertical brace placed 9 ft from the base of the ramp.
qs.s: The slope of the ramp is \(\frac{5\text{ ft}}{15\text{ ft}} = \frac{1}{3}\). At a horizontal distance of \(9\text{ ft}\) from the base, the height is \(\frac{1}{3} \times 9 = 3\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A hiking trail rises 140 m over a horizontal run of 350 m. Determine the elevation gain at a point 200 m along the run from the start of the trail.
qs.s: The slope of the trail is \(\frac{140\text{ m}}{350\text{ m}} = 0.4\). At \(200\text{ m}\) along the run, the elevation gain is \(0.4 \times 200 = 80\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A covered walkway roof rises 9 ft over a horizontal run of 24 ft. Two vertical support columns are installed under the roof, one at 6 ft and the other at 18 ft from the low end. How much taller is the second column than the first?
qs.s: The slope of the roof is \(\frac{9}{24} = \frac{3}{8}\). Since the horizontal distance between the columns is \(18 - 6 = 12\text{ ft}\), the difference in height is \(\frac{3}{8} \times 12 = 4.5\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A highway ramp rises 18 ft over a total horizontal run of 240 ft. A sign is placed where the ramp has risen 12 ft above its starting elevation. What is the horizontal distance from the sign to the high end of the ramp?
qs.s: The ramp has a slope of \(\frac{18}{240} = \frac{3}{40}\), leaving \(18 - 12 = 6\text{ ft}\) of vertical rise to the top. The horizontal distance remaining is \(6 \div \frac{3}{40} = 6 \times \frac{40}{3} = 80\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A lean-to shed is built so that the low end of its roof rests on a 6 ft wall. The roof rises an additional 8 ft over a horizontal run of 12 ft. Determine the total height from the ground to the roof at a point 9 ft from the wall.
qs.s: The roof slope is \(\frac{8\text{ ft}}{12\text{ ft}} = \frac{2}{3}\), so it rises \(\frac{2}{3} \times 9 = 6\text{ ft}\) above the wall. Adding the \(6\text{ ft}\) wall gives a total height of \(6 + 6 = 12\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: The roof of a barn rises 15 ft over a horizontal run of 24 ft. Determine the height of a vertical brace placed 8 ft from the high end of the roof.
qs.s: Since the brace is \(8\text{ ft}\) from the high end, it is \(24 - 8 = 16\text{ ft}\) from the low end. With a slope of \(\frac{15}{24} = \frac{5}{8}\), the height is \(\frac{5}{8} \times 16 = 10\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A wheelchair access ramp rises 32 inches over a horizontal run of 40 feet. Determine the height, in inches, of a vertical support placed 15 feet from the lower end of the ramp.
qs.s: The slope is \(\frac{32\text{ inches}}{40\text{ ft}} = 0.8\text{ inches per foot}\). Multiplying this rate by \(15\text{ ft}\) gives a height of \(0.8 \times 15 = 12\text{ inches}\).

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: A hot air balloon is at an altitude of \(1500\) metres. The pilot begins a controlled descent, reaching an altitude of \(1320\) metres after \(3\) minutes, and \(1140\) metres after \(6\) minutes. The balloon continues to descend at the same rate. Determine the rate of change of altitude with respect to time.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta t} = \frac{1320 - 1500}{3 - 0} = \frac{-180}{3} = -60\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q: A swimming pool holds \(48\,000\) litres of water. When a drainage pump is started, the pool has \(45\,600\) litres after \(20\) minutes, and \(43\,200\) litres after \(40\) minutes. The water continues to drain at the same rate until the pool is empty. Determine the rate of change of volume with respect to time.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta t} = \frac{45\,600 - 48\,000}{20 - 0} = \frac{-2400}{20} = -120\text{ L/min}\).

qs.q: An airplane cruises at an altitude of \(9000\) metres. When preparing to land, its altitude is \(8450\) metres after \(2\) minutes, and \(7900\) metres after \(4\) minutes. The airplane continues to descend at the same rate. Determine the rate of change of altitude with respect to time.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta t} = \frac{8450 - 9000}{2 - 0} = \frac{-550}{2} = -275\text{ m/min}\).

qs.q: A fuel tank contains \(1200\) litres of heating oil. When the furnace is turned on, the tank has \(1140\) litres after \(5\) hours, and \(1080\) litres after \(10\) hours. Oil continues to be consumed at the same rate. Determine the rate of change of volume with respect to time.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta t} = \frac{1140 - 1200}{5 - 0} = \frac{-60}{5} = -12\text{ L/h}\).

qs.q: A grain silo holds \(6000\text{ kg}\) of wheat. When the discharge chute is opened, the silo has \(5650\text{ kg}\) after \(5\) minutes, and \(5300\text{ kg}\) after \(10\) minutes. The wheat continues to empty at the same rate until the silo is empty. Determine the rate of change of mass with respect to time.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta m}{\Delta t} = \frac{5650 - 6000}{5 - 0} = \frac{-350}{5} = -70\text{ kg/min}\).

qs.q:
An engineer records the temperature of a cooling chemical solution at various times in the table below:
\(\displaystyle \begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}
\hline
\text{Time (min)} & 4 & 10 & 19 & 25 \\
\hline
\text{Temperature }(^{\circ}\text{C}) & 138 & 114 & 78 & 54 \\
\hline
\end{array}\)
Determine the rate of change of temperature with respect to time.
qs.s: Using points \((4, 138)\) and \((10, 114)\), the rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta T}{\Delta t} = \frac{114 - 138}{10 - 4} = \frac{-24}{6} = -4^{\circ}\text{C/min}\).

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir contained \(240\,000\text{ m}^3\) of water at 7:30 a.m. Due to high demand during a heat wave, the reservoir contained \(226\,500\text{ m}^3\) at 10:00 a.m., and \(213\,000\text{ m}^3\) at 12:30 p.m. If the water level continues to fall at this constant rate, determine the rate of change of volume with respect to time in cubic metres per hour.
qs.s: The elapsed time between 7:30 a.m. and 10:00 a.m. is \(2.5\text{ hours}\). The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta V}{\Delta t} = \frac{226\,500 - 240\,000}{2.5} = \frac{-13\,500}{2.5} = -5400\text{ m}^3/\text{h}\).

qs.q: A storage tank contains \(60\,000\text{ litres}\) of water. When two identical drain valves are opened simultaneously, the tank has \(56\,700\text{ litres}\) after \(15\text{ minutes}\) and \(53\,400\text{ litres}\) after \(30\text{ minutes}\). Determine the rate of change of volume with respect to time caused by a single valve.
qs.s: The combined rate of change is \(\frac{56\,700 - 60\,000}{15 - 0} = -220\text{ L/min}\), so the rate of change for a single valve is \(\frac{-220}{2} = -110\text{ L/min}\).

qs.q: A commercial jet begins its descent from an altitude of \(11\,200\text{ metres}\). After \(3\text{ minutes and } 45\text{ seconds}\), its altitude is \(9400\text{ metres}\), and after \(7\text{ minutes and } 30\text{ seconds}\), its altitude is \(7600\text{ metres}\). The jet continues to descend at the same constant rate. Determine the rate of change of altitude with respect to time in metres per second.
qs.s: Convert \(3\text{ minutes and } 45\text{ seconds}\) to \(225\text{ seconds}\). The rate of change is \(\frac{\Delta h}{\Delta t} = \frac{9400 - 11\,200}{225 - 0} = \frac{-1800}{225} = -8\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: Two identical storage tanks, Tank A and Tank B, each drain water at a constant rate. Tank A empties from \(18\,000\text{ litres}\) to \(11\,700\text{ litres}\) in \(35\text{ minutes}\). Tank B empties from \(15\,000\text{ litres}\) to \(5400\text{ litres}\) in \(40\text{ minutes}\). By how many litres per minute does the draining rate of Tank B exceed the draining rate of Tank A?
qs.s: Tank A drains at \(\frac{18\,000 - 11\,700}{35} = 180\text{ L/min}\) and Tank B drains at \(\frac{15\,000 - 5400}{40} = 240\text{ L/min}\), so the rate of Tank B exceeds Tank A by \(240 - 180 = 60\text{ L/min}\).

qs.q: A fuel tank on a cargo ship holds 25 000 gallons of fuel. After 15 minutes of travel, the tank has 24 550 gallons, and after 30 minutes, it has 24 100 gallons. The fuel continues to be consumed at the same constant rate. How much fuel remains after 2 hours?
qs.s: The rate of consumption is (25 000 - 24 550) / 15 = 30 gallons per minute. After 2 hours (120 minutes), the remaining fuel is 25 000 - 30(120) = 21 400 gallons.

qs.q: A hot air balloon begins descending from an altitude of 1800 metres. After 20 seconds, its altitude is 1740 metres, and after 40 seconds, its altitude is 1680 metres. If it continues to descend at the same constant rate, what is its altitude after 5 minutes?
qs.s: The descent rate is (1800 - 1740) / 20 = 3 metres per second. After 5 minutes (300 seconds), the altitude is 1800 - 3(300) = 900 metres.

qs.q: An oil storage tank contains 12 000 litres of heating oil. When a pump starts running, the tank has 11 550 litres after 15 seconds, and 11 100 litres after 30 seconds. The oil continues to pump out at the same constant rate. How much oil remains after 3 minutes?
qs.s: The pump removes oil at a rate of (12 000 - 11 550) / 15 = 30 litres per second. After 3 minutes (180 seconds), the volume remaining is 12 000 - 30(180) = 6600 litres.

qs.q: A grain silo holds 8000 kg of wheat. When the discharge chute is opened, the silo contains 7730 kg after 45 seconds, and 7460 kg after 90 seconds. The grain continues to empty at the same constant rate. How much wheat remains in the silo after 6 minutes?
qs.s: The silo empties at a rate of (8000 - 7730) / 45 = 6 kg per second. After 6 minutes (360 seconds), the wheat remaining is 8000 - 6(360) = 5840 kg.

qs.q: A swimming pool holds 48 000 litres of water. When draining begins, the pool has 46 400 litres after 20 minutes, and 44 800 litres after 40 minutes. The water continues to drain at the same constant rate. How much water remains after 3 hours?
qs.s: The pool drains at a rate of (48 000 - 46 400) / 20 = 80 litres per minute. After 3 hours (180 minutes), the volume remaining is 48 000 - 80(180) = 33 600 litres.

qs.q: A municipal swimming pool is being drained at a constant rate. After 2 hours, the pool contains 222 000 litres of water, and after 6 hours, it contains 166 000 litres. Drain pumps automatically shut off when 12 000 litres remain. How many hours in total will the draining process take from the start?
qs.s: The rate of drainage is (222 000 - 166 000) / 4 = 14 000 litres per hour, so the initial volume was 222 000 + 14 000(2) = 250 000 litres. To reach 12 000 litres, 238 000 litres must drain, taking 238 000 / 14 000 = 17 hours.

qs.q: A water reservoir is being drained at a constant rate. After 4 minutes, the reservoir holds 54 200 litres, and after 9 minutes, it holds 46 700 litres. If the water continues to drain at this same rate, how much water will remain in the reservoir after 25 minutes?
qs.s: The rate of drainage is (46 700 - 54 200) / (9 - 4) = -1500 litres per minute. From the 9-minute mark, 16 more minutes elapse, leaving 46 700 - 1500(16) = 22 700 litres.

qs.q: A 75 000-litre water cistern contains 12 000 litres when a refill pump is activated. After 40 minutes, the cistern contains 22 000 litres, and after 80 minutes, it contains 32 000 litres. Water continues to enter at the same constant rate. How many more litres of water are needed to completely fill the cistern after 3.5 hours of pumping?
qs.s: The cistern fills at a rate of (22 000 - 12 000) / 40 = 250 litres per minute. In 3.5 hours (210 minutes), the cistern reaches 12 000 + 250(210) = 64 500 litres, so 75 000 - 64 500 = 10 500 litres are still needed.

qs.q: A commercial fuel storage depot has 150 000 litres of fuel. During peak hours, fuel is drawn at a constant rate. After 45 minutes, 143 250 litres remain, and after 90 minutes, 136 500 litres remain. At this rate, how many hours after the start will the depot reach its reserve threshold of 15 000 litres?
qs.s: The depot drains at (150 000 - 143 250) / 45 = 150 litres per minute, which is 9000 litres per hour. To reach 15 000 litres, 135 000 litres must be drawn, taking 135 000 / 9000 = 15 hours.

qs.q: A water tank holds 18 000 litres. For the first 30 minutes, it drains through a single valve at a constant rate, holding 17 250 litres after 10 minutes and 16 500 litres after 20 minutes. After 30 minutes, a second valve is opened, draining an additional 50 litres per minute. How much water remains in the tank 50 minutes after the first valve was opened?
qs.s: The first valve drains at 75 litres per minute, leaving 18 000 - 75(30) = 15 750 litres at 30 minutes. Both valves then drain at 75 + 50 = 125 litres per minute for the remaining 20 minutes, leaving 15 750 - 125(20) = 13 250 litres.

qs.q: A municipal reservoir holds 40 000 cubic metres of water. During a controlled release, the volume is 37 600 cubic metres after 6 hours, and 35 200 cubic metres after 12 hours. If water continues to be released at this constant rate, how much time, in hours, is needed to release \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the water in the reservoir?
qs.s: The release rate is \(\frac{40\,000 - 37\,600}{6} = 400\text{ m}^3\text{ per hour}\). To release \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the reservoir's capacity (\(30\,000\text{ m}^3\)), it takes \(\frac{30\,000}{400} = 75\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A fuel storage tank contains 6000 gallons of oil. When pumped out at a constant rate, 5760 gallons remain after 15 minutes, and 5520 gallons remain after 30 minutes. How much time, in minutes, is required to pump out \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the oil from the tank?
qs.s: The pumping rate is \(\frac{6000 - 5760}{15} = 16\text{ gallons per minute}\). To pump out \(\frac{4}{5}\) of the tank (\(4800\text{ gallons}\)), it takes \(\frac{4800}{16} = 300\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A grain silo contains 18 000 kg of wheat. When an unloading chute is opened, the silo holds 17 400 kg after 10 minutes, and 16 800 kg after 20 minutes. If the wheat continues to unload at this constant rate, how much time, in minutes, is needed to empty \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the wheat in the silo?
qs.s: The unloading rate is \(\frac{18\,000 - 17\,400}{10} = 60\text{ kg per minute}\). To empty \(\frac{1}{2}\) of the wheat (\(9000\text{ kg}\)), it takes \(\frac{9000}{60} = 150\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A swimming pool holds 24 000 litres of water. When drained, it contains 23 200 litres after 20 minutes, and 22 400 litres after 40 minutes. The water continues to drain at the same constant rate until the pool is empty. How much time, in minutes, is needed to drain \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the water from the pool?
qs.s: The drainage rate is \(\frac{24\,000 - 23\,200}{20} = 40\text{ litres per minute}\). To drain \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the pool (\(16\,000\text{ litres}\)), it takes \(\frac{16\,000}{40} = 400\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A hot air balloon descends toward the ground from an altitude of 3600 metres. Its altitude is 3360 metres after 4 minutes, and 3120 metres after 8 minutes. If it continues to descend at the same constant rate, how much time, in minutes from the start, is needed to complete \(\frac{3}{5}\) of its descent?
qs.s: The descent rate is \(\frac{3600 - 3360}{4} = 60\text{ metres per minute}\). To descend \(\frac{3}{5}\) of the total altitude (\(2160\text{ metres}\)), it takes \(\frac{2160}{60} = 36\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A transport plane takes off with 60 000 kg of fuel. After cruising for 2 hours, 51 000 kg of fuel remains, and after 4.5 hours, 39 750 kg remains. Safety regulations require the plane to land with a reserve of at least \(\frac{1}{4}\) of its initial fuel. If fuel continues to be consumed at this constant rate, how many additional hours can the plane fly after the 4.5-hour mark before reaching this minimum reserve?
qs.s: The burn rate is \(\frac{51\,000 - 39\,750}{2.5} = 4500\text{ kg/h}\). To leave the required reserve of \(\frac{1}{4} \times 60\,000 = 15\,000\text{ kg}\), the plane can burn \(39\,750 - 15\,000 = 24\,750\text{ kg}\) after the 4.5-hour mark, allowing \(\frac{24\,750}{4500} = 5.5\text{ additional hours}\) of flight.

qs.q: A chemical storage tank contains 90 000 litres of solution. When a drain valve is opened, the tank holds 87 750 litres after 15 minutes, and 85 500 litres after 30 minutes. If the solution continues to drain at the same constant rate, how many additional hours will it take after the 30-minute mark until only \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the original solution remains in the tank?
qs.s: The drainage rate is \(\frac{90\,000 - 87\750}{15} = 150\text{ L/min}\). To leave \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the original volume (\(18\,000\text{ L}\)), the tank must lose \(85\,500 - 18\,000 = 67\,500\text{ L}\) after the 30-minute mark, which takes \(\frac{67\,500}{150} = 450\text{ minutes} = 7.5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: Two identical industrial tanks, Tank A and Tank B, each initially hold 15 000 litres of liquid and begin draining simultaneously. Tank A contains 14 000 litres after 20 minutes and 13 000 litres after 40 minutes. Tank B drains at a constant rate that is \(1.5\) times the drainage rate of Tank A. How many litres of liquid remain in Tank A at the moment Tank B has emptied \(\frac{2}{5}\) of its initial capacity?
qs.s: Tank A drains at \(\frac{15\,000 - 14\,000}{20} = 50\text{ L/min}\), making Tank B's rate \(1.5 \times 50 = 75\text{ L/min}\). Tank B empties \(\frac{2}{5} \times 15\,000 = 6000\text{ L}\) in \(\frac{6000}{75} = 80\text{ minutes}\), during which Tank A drains \(80 \times 50 = 4000\text{ L}\), leaving \(15\,000 - 4000 = 11\,000\text{ litres}\).

qs.q: A tank holding 20 000 litres of water begins draining through a single valve. It contains 18 500 litres after 25 minutes, and 17 000 litres after 50 minutes. At the 50-minute mark, an identical second valve is also opened, doubling the drainage rate. How much total time, in minutes from the beginning, is required to empty \(\frac{3}{4}\) of the initial volume of water from the tank?
qs.s: One valve drains at \(\frac{20\,000 - 18\,500}{25} = 60\text{ L/min}\), draining \(3000\text{ L}\) in the first 50 minutes. To reach \(\frac{3}{4}\) emptied (\(15\,000\text{ L}\)), both valves combined at \(120\text{ L/min}\) must drain the remaining \(12\,000\text{ L}\), which takes \(\frac{12\,000}{120} = 100\text{ minutes}\), giving a total of \(50 + 100 = 150\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A water reservoir contains 45 000 litres of water. Water is pumped in at a constant rate of 800 litres per hour while simultaneously draining out to supply a town. The reservoir holds 42 600 litres after 2 hours and 39 000 litres after 5 hours. At the 5-hour mark, the pump is shut off, but the water continues to drain out at the same consumption rate. How many additional hours will it take to drain \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the water that remained at the 5-hour mark?
qs.s: The net loss rate is \(\frac{42\,600 - 39\,000}{3} = 1200\text{ L/h}\), so the consumption rate is \(800 + 1200 = 2000\text{ L/h}\). Draining \(\frac{2}{3}\) of the remaining \(39\,000\text{ L}\) (\(26\,000\text{ L}\)) with the pump off takes \(\frac{26\,000}{2000} = 13\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A swimming pool contains 48 000 litres of water. When draining begins, it contains 45 600 litres after 20 minutes, and 43 200 litres after 40 minutes. If the water continues to drain at the same constant rate until the pool is empty, how long does it take to empty the pool?
qs.s: The drainage rate is \((45 600 - 43 200) / (40 - 20) = 120\) litres per minute. Draining the entire 48 000 litres takes \(48 000 / 120 = 400\) minutes.

qs.q: A high-capacity printer paper tray holds 6000 sheets. During a large print job, 5400 sheets remain after 20 minutes, and 4800 sheets remain after 40 minutes. If the printer continues to feed paper at this constant rate, how many minutes will it take from the start to use all the paper?
qs.s: The paper usage rate is \((5400 - 4800) / (40 - 20) = 30\) sheets per minute. Using all 6000 sheets takes \(6000 / 30 = 200\) minutes.

qs.q: A tablet battery is fully charged at 100%. During continuous video playback, the battery level is 92% after 40 minutes, and 84% after 80 minutes. If the battery continues to discharge at the same constant rate, how many total minutes will it take for the battery to reach 0%?
qs.s: The battery discharge rate is \((92 - 84) / (80 - 40) = 0.2\%\) per minute. To fully discharge from 100%, it will take \(100 / 0.2 = 500\) minutes.

qs.q: A compressed gas cylinder starts with 3600 psi of pressure. While in use, the cylinder has 3450 psi after 15 minutes, and 3300 psi after 30 minutes. If the gas continues to be used at the same constant rate, how many minutes will it take from the start for the cylinder to be completely empty (0 psi)?
qs.s: The rate of pressure decrease is \((3450 - 3300) / (30 - 15) = 10\) psi per minute. To drop from 3600 psi to 0 psi takes \(3600 / 10 = 360\) minutes.

qs.q: A fuel tank on an emergency generator holds 600 litres of fuel. When the generator is running, the tank has 570 litres after 2 hours, and 540 litres after 4 hours. The fuel continues to be consumed at the same constant rate until the tank is empty. How long can the generator run before the tank is completely empty?
qs.s: The rate of fuel consumption is \((570 - 540) / (4 - 2) = 15\) litres per hour. To consume the full 600 litres, it takes \(600 / 15 = 40\) hours.

qs.q: An industrial chemical vat holds 24 000 litres of liquid. A drain is opened, leaving 22 800 litres after 15 minutes and 20 400 litres after 45 minutes. After 100 minutes of draining at this constant rate, a second identical drain is opened, doubling the drainage rate. From the very beginning, how many total minutes will it take to completely empty the vat?
qs.s: The initial drain rate is \((22 800 - 20 400) / 30 = 80\) litres per minute, leaving \(24 000 - 80(100) = 16 000\) litres after 100 minutes. With the rate doubled to 160 litres per minute, draining the remaining liquid takes \(16 000 / 160 = 100\) minutes, for a total of \(100 + 100 = 200\) minutes.

qs.q: A storage reservoir currently contains 850 000 litres of water. Water flows into the reservoir from an intake canal at a constant rate of 1200 litres per minute, while water is continuously pumped out for irrigation at a constant rate. Technicians observe that the reservoir has 830 000 litres after 50 minutes, and 810 000 litres after 100 minutes. At what rate, in litres per minute, is water being pumped out?
qs.s: The net rate of change is \((810 000 - 830 000) / 50 = -400\) litres per minute, indicating a net loss of 400 L/min. Since water enters at 1200 L/min, the pumping rate must be \(1200 - (-400) = 1600\) litres per minute.

qs.q: Tank A holds 15 000 litres of water and has 14 400 litres after 20 minutes, and 13 500 litres after 50 minutes. Tank B holds 11 000 litres of water and has 10 700 litres after 30 minutes, and 10 400 litres after 60 minutes. If both tanks drain simultaneously at their constant rates, after how many minutes will both tanks contain the exact same volume of water?
qs.s: Tank A drains at \((14 400 - 13 500) / 30 = 30\) L/min, and Tank B drains at \((10 700 - 10 400) / 30 = 10\) L/min. Setting their remaining volumes equal, \(15 000 - 30t = 11 000 - 10t\), yields \(20t = 4000\), so \(t = 200\) minutes.

qs.q: A water reservoir was filled to capacity. Due to an undetected leak, 5 hours after filling, the reservoir contained 140 000 litres, and 12 hours after filling, it contained 112 000 litres. If water continues to leak at the same constant rate, how many total hours from the time it was full will it take for the reservoir to become completely empty?
qs.s: The rate of water loss is \((140 000 - 112 000) / (12 - 5) = 4000\) litres per hour, meaning the initial capacity was \(140 000 + 5(4000) = 160 000\) litres. Thus, it takes \(160 000 / 4000 = 40\) hours from when it was full to completely empty.

qs.q: An aircraft begins cruising with 43 400 kg of fuel in its tanks. After 30 minutes of flight, 41 000 kg remains, and after 75 minutes, 37 400 kg remains. The fuel continues to be consumed at this constant rate. Regulations require the aircraft to land with a reserve of at least 5000 kg of fuel. What is the maximum total flight time, in hours, before reaching this minimum reserve?
qs.s: The rate of fuel consumption is \((41 000 - 37 400) / 45 = 80\) kg/min, which equals \(80 \times 60 = 4800\) kg/h. The usable fuel above the reserve is \(43 400 - 5000 = 38 400\) kg, allowing a maximum flight time of \(38 400 / 4800 = 8\) hours.

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: Elena organizes a family reunion at a park. She pays $300 to reserve a picnic pavilion, plus $18 per person for barbecue catering. Cans of soda cost $1.50 each, and each person drinks an average of 2 sodas. Determine the cost per person if 40 people attend the reunion.
qs.s: The pavilion rental is $300 / 40 = $7.50 per person, catering is $18, and sodas cost 2 × $1.50 = $3. The total cost per person is $7.50 + $18 + $3 = $28.50.

qs.q: A company organizes an awards banquet. The company pays $800 to hire a keynote speaker, plus $35 per attendee for dinner. Dessert tickets cost $4 each, and each attendee consumes an average of 2 desserts. Determine the cost per person if 80 attendees go to the banquet.
qs.s: The speaker costs $800 / 80 = $10 per attendee, dinner is $35, and desserts cost 2 × $4 = $8. The total cost per person is $10 + $35 + $8 = $53.

qs.q: Marcus hosts a graduation party. He pays a flat fee of $600 to rent a venue, plus $15 per guest for dinner. Soft drinks cost $3 each, and each guest has an average of 2 soft drinks. Determine the cost per person if 50 guests attend the party.
qs.s: The venue costs $600 / 50 = $12 per guest, dinner is $15, and drinks cost 2 × $3 = $6. The total cost per person is $12 + $15 + $6 = $33.

qs.q: A sports club hosts an annual banquet. The club pays $500 for a DJ, plus $22 per guest for a buffet dinner. Raffle tickets cost $2 each, and guests purchase an average of 4 raffle tickets each. Determine the cost per person if 100 guests attend the banquet.
qs.s: The DJ costs $500 / 100 = $5 per guest, dinner is $22, and raffle tickets cost 4 × $2 = $8. The total cost per person is $5 + $22 + $8 = $35.

qs.q: A school organizes a field trip to an amusement park. The school pays $450 to charter a bus, plus $25 per student for admission. Ride vouchers cost $3 each, and each student uses an average of 3 vouchers. Determine the cost per student if 60 students attend the trip.
qs.s: The bus costs $450 / 60 = $7.50 per student, admission is $25, and ride vouchers cost 3 × $3 = $9. The total cost per student is $7.50 + $25 + $9 = $41.50.

qs.q: A community centre organizes a summer festival. The fixed costs are $3600 for staging and sound, plus $1400 for permits and security. Food costs $16.50 per person, beverages cost $2.25 each, and game tickets cost $1.50 each. On average, each attendee consumes 2 beverages and uses 4 game tickets. Determine the total cost per attendee if 400 attendees participate.
qs.s: Fixed costs total $3600 + $1400 = $5000, which is $5000 / 400 = $12.50 per attendee. Adding food ($16.50), beverages (2 × $2.25 = $4.50), and game tickets (4 × $1.50 = $6.00) yields $12.50 + $16.50 + $4.50 + $6.00 = $39.50 per attendee.

qs.q: An organization hosts a charity gala. The fixed costs include $1850 to rent the ballroom and $650 for audio equipment. Dinner costs $42 per guest. In addition, beverages cost $3.50 each and dessert tokens cost $4.00 each. If each guest averages 2 beverages and 1.5 dessert tokens, determine the total cost per guest when 250 guests attend.
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $1850 + $650 = $2500, or $2500 / 250 = $10 per guest. Adding dinner ($42), beverages (2 × $3.50 = $7), and desserts (1.5 × $4.00 = $6) gives a total of $10 + $42 + $7 + $6 = $65.00 per guest.

qs.q: A club plans a formal dinner. The venue charges a flat rental fee of $2400. Catering is $32 per person, and drinks cost $3 each, with each guest averaging 2 drinks. Determine how much the cost per person decreases if attendance increases from 80 guests to 120 guests.
qs.s: At 80 guests, the cost is $2400 / 80 + \(32 + 2(\)3) = $68 per person. At 120 guests, the cost is $2400 / 120 + \(32 + 2(\)3) = $58 per person, which is a decrease of $68 − $58 = $10 per person.

qs.q: A company organizes a weekend retreat. A bus is chartered for $1500, and lodge rental costs $2100. Meals cost $45 per employee for the weekend. Each employee also receives 3 tour passes at $12 each and 2 workshop supply sets at $8 each. Determine the total cost per employee if 75 employees attend.
qs.s: Fixed costs are $1500 + $2100 = $3600, or $3600 / 75 = $48 per employee. Adding meals ($45), tour passes (3 × $12 = $36), and workshop sets (2 × $8 = $16) gives $48 + $45 + $36 + $16 = $145 per employee.

qs.q: A conference center charges a fixed room fee of $1200 plus a $450 cleaning fee. Catered lunch costs $28.50 per attendee. Each attendee also receives a welcome kit costing $8.50 and drinks an average of 3 specialty coffees at $2.50 each. Determine the total cost per attendee if 150 attendees participate.
qs.s: Fixed costs total $1200 + $450 = $1650, which is $1650 / 150 = $11.00 per attendee. Adding lunch (\(28.50), the kit (\)8.50), and coffees (3 × $2.50 = $7.50) gives $11.00 + $28.50 + $8.50 + $7.50 = $55.50 per attendee.

qs.q: A committee books a banquet hall for an awards night. The hall costs $600, plus $25 per attendee for dinner. Specialty mocktails cost $4 each. Determine the cost per attendee if 120 attendees were present and averaged two mocktails each.
qs.s: The hall fee per person is $600 / 120 = $5, dinner is $25, and mocktails cost 2 * $4 = $8 per person. The total cost per attendee is $5 + $25 + $8 = $38.

qs.q: A company rents a park pavilion for an annual picnic. The rental fee is $600, plus $15 per employee for lunch. Canned beverages cost $1.50 each. Determine the cost per employee if 150 employees attended the picnic and averaged four beverages each.
qs.s: The pavilion fee is $600 / 150 = $4 per employee, lunch is $15, and drinks cost 4 * $1.50 = $6 per employee. The total cost is $4 + $15 + $6 = $25 per employee.

qs.q: Marco hires a DJ for a graduation party. The cost for the party was $400 for the DJ, plus $25 per guest for the buffet. Desserts cost $3 extra each. Determine the cost per person if 100 guests attended the party and averaged two desserts per person.
qs.s: The DJ cost per guest is $400 / 100 = $4, the buffet is $25, and desserts cost 2 * $3 = $6 per guest. Adding these gives a total cost of $4 + $25 + $6 = $35 per person.

qs.q: A school charters a bus for a class field trip. The bus rental is $450, plus $18 per student for park admission. Activity passes cost $2.50 each. Determine the cost per student if 50 students went on the trip and averaged four activity passes each.
qs.s: The bus cost per student is $450 / 50 = $9, admission is $18, and activity passes cost 4 * $2.50 = $10 per student. The total cost per student is $9 + $18 + $10 = $37.

qs.q: Nora hires a photographer for a family reunion. The cost was $500 for the photographer, plus $24 per person for barbecue catering. Drinks cost $2.50 extra each. Determine the cost per person if 80 people attended the reunion and averaged three drinks per person.
qs.s: The photographer cost per person is $500 / 80 = $6.25, catering is $24, and drinks cost 3 * $2.50 = $7.50 per person. Adding these gives a total cost of $6.25 + $24 + $7.50 = $37.75 per person.

qs.q: A company organizes an executive retreat. The conference center charges a fixed equipment fee of $1200. Meals cost $50 per person, and beverages cost $4 each, with participants averaging five beverages each. A 15% service fee is added to the total cost of meals and beverages only. If 80 participants attend, determine the total cost per person.
qs.s: The fixed fee is $1200 / 80 = $15 per person. Meals and drinks cost $50 + 5 * $4 = $70 per person, and adding the 15% service fee gives $70 * 1.15 = $80.50, for a total of $15 + $80.50 = $95.50 per person.

qs.q: A youth sports club hosts a banquet. The venue charges a flat maintenance fee of $480. The dinner costs $18 per person, and slices of cake cost $2.50 each. If 120 people attended and the total cost per person was $27, determine the average number of slices of cake consumed per person.
qs.s: The fixed cost per person is $480 / 120 = $4. Subtracting this and the $18 dinner from the $27 total leaves $27 - $4 - $18 = $5 spent on cake per person, which means an average of $5 / $2.50 = 2 slices.

qs.q: A conference hall charges a flat setup fee of $1500 plus $40 per attendee for lunch and materials. Refreshments cost $3 each, with attendees averaging four refreshments each. By how much does the total cost per attendee decrease if attendance increases from 100 to 150 attendees?
qs.s: Variable costs per person remain constant at $40 + 4 * $3 = $52, while the fixed cost per person drops from $1500 / 100 = $15 to $1500 / 150 = $10, resulting in a decrease of $15 - $10 = $5 per attendee.

qs.q: A foundation hosts a fundraising gala. The fixed costs include $2400 for venue rental and $1200 for a live band. The catered dinner costs $45 per guest, appetizers cost $4 each, and beverages cost $5 each. If 300 guests attend and average three appetizers and two beverages each, determine the total cost per guest.
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $2400 + $1200 = $3600, which is $3600 / 300 = $12 per guest. Adding the variable costs of $45 for dinner, 3 * $4 = $12 for appetizers, and 2 * $5 = $10 for drinks gives $12 + $45 + $12 + $10 = $79 per guest.

qs.q: A community dinner is attended by 150 adults and 50 children. The hall charges a flat rental fee of $1600. The meal costs $30 per adult and $16 per child. Beverages cost $2 each, with adults averaging three beverages and children averaging two beverages. Determine the overall average cost per person across all 200 attendees.
qs.s: Total variable costs are 150 * ($30 + 3 * $2) = $5400 for adults and 50 * ($16 + 2 * $2) = $1000 for children. Adding the $1600 flat fee gives $8000 total, so the average cost across all 200 attendees is $8000 / 200 = $40 per person.

exercises.name: Unit rates and rates of change in context

qs.q: At 8:00 am, Liam left home on a road trip. He arrived at his destination at 1:00 pm the same day after driving 325 km. He spent $45 on fuel during the trip. Determine Liam's average speed in km/h.
qs.s: The elapsed time between 8:00 am and 1:00 pm is 5 hours. Liam's average speed is 325 km / 5 h = 65 km/h.

qs.q: At 11:00 am, a city worker began draining a municipal pool. By 5:00 pm the same day, a total of 1500 L of water had been drained. The pool holds a maximum of 8000 L. Determine the average rate of drainage in L/h.
qs.s: The drainage took place over 6 hours (from 11:00 am to 5:00 pm). The average rate of drainage is 1500 L / 6 h = 250 L/h.

qs.q: At 10:00 am, Marcus rented a kayak to explore the coastline. He returned the kayak at 1:00 pm the same day after paddling 18 km. It cost $35 to rent the kayak. Determine Marcus's average speed in km/h.
qs.s: The elapsed time from 10:00 am to 1:00 pm is 3 hours. Marcus's average speed is 18 km / 3 h = 6 km/h (the rental cost of $35 is extraneous information).

qs.q: At 9:00 am, Brenda started hiking a trail in Garibaldi Park. She reached the scenic viewpoint at 1:00 pm the same day after travelling 16 km. Her backpack weighed 8 kg. Determine Brenda's average speed in km/h.
qs.s: The time taken from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm is 4 hours. Brenda's average speed is 16 km / 4 h = 4 km/h.

qs.q: At 7:00 am, Chloe rented a road bicycle. She returned the bicycle at 11:00 am the same day after cycling 68 km. The rental fee was $30. Determine Chloe's average speed in km/h.
qs.s: The elapsed time from 7:00 am to 11:00 am is 4 hours. Chloe's average speed is 68 km / 4 h = 17 km/h.

qs.q: A company rented a passenger van from 8:00 am to 6:00 pm on the same day. During this period, the van was driven 360 km. The rental fee was a base rate of $75 plus $0.25 per kilometre driven, and the driver spent $45 on fuel. Determine the total cost per hour of operating the van during the rental period.
qs.s: The total operating cost is $75 + (360 * $0.25) + $45 = $75 + $90 + $45 = $210. Over the 10-hour rental period, the rate of cost is $210 / 10 h = $21/h.

qs.q: On Saturday, Maya drove 180 km between 9:00 am and 11:30 am. On Sunday, she drove 234 km between 1:00 pm and 4:00 pm. By how many kilometres per hour was her average speed greater on Sunday than on Saturday?
qs.s: Saturday's average speed was 180 / 2.5 = 72 km/h, and Sunday's average speed was 234 / 3 = 78 km/h. The difference is 78 - 72 = 6 km/h.

qs.q: A hiking group started ascending a mountain trail at 6:45 am from an elevation of 390 m. They reached the summit at an elevation of 2190 m at 11:15 am the same day. The total trail distance was 12 km. Determine the group's average rate of elevation gain in metres per hour.
qs.s: The total elevation change is 2190 - 390 = 1800 m, and the elapsed time from 6:45 am to 11:15 am is 4.5 hours. The average rate of elevation gain is 1800 / 4.5 = 400 m/h.

qs.q: A courier rented a delivery van. When he picked up the van at 8:30 am, the odometer read 45 210 km. When he returned the van at 1:00 pm the same day, the odometer read 45 453 km. The rental cost was $85 plus $0.20 per kilometre. Determine the courier's average speed in km/h.
qs.s: The elapsed time from 8:30 am to 1:00 pm is 4.5 hours, and the distance travelled is 45 453 - 45 210 = 243 km. The average speed is 243 / 4.5 = 54 km/h.

qs.q: A delivery driver completed two routes in one morning. On the first route, from 7:30 am to 10:00 am, she drove 125 km. She took a 30-minute break, then drove the second route from 10:30 am to 1:30 pm, covering 145 km. Determine her average speed, in km/h, for the entire 6-hour period (including the break).
qs.s: The total distance is 125 + 145 = 270 km over a total elapsed time of 6 hours. Her overall average speed is 270 / 6 = 45 km/h.

qs.q: At 9:00 am, Priya rented an electric scooter. She returned it at 1:00 pm the same day after riding a distance of 36 km. The total rental cost was $30. Determine the rental rate in dollars per hour.
qs.s: The rental period is \(1:00\text{ pm} - 9:00\text{ am} = 4\text{ hours}\). The rate is \(\frac{\$30}{4\text{ h}} = \$7.50\text{ per hour}\).

qs.q: At noon, Elena rented a paddleboard at the beach. She returned it at 5:00 pm the same day after paddling 15 km. The rental cost was $45. Determine the rental rate in dollars per hour.
qs.s: The paddleboard was rented for 5 hours (from 12:00 pm to 5:00 pm). The rental rate is \(\frac{\$45}{5\text{ h}} = \$9.00\text{ per hour}\).

qs.q: At 9:00 am, Carlos rented a power washer to clean his patio. He returned the machine at 1:00 pm the same day after washing an area of 150 m\(^2\). The rental fee was $26. Determine the rental rate in dollars per hour.
qs.s: The duration of the rental is 4 hours (from 9:00 am to 1:00 pm). The rate is \(\frac{\$26}{4\text{ h}} = \$6.50\text{ per hour}\).

qs.q: At 1:00 pm, Marcus rented a kayak at the lake. He returned the kayak at 5:00 pm the same day after paddling 14 km. The total cost to rent the kayak was $38. Determine the rental rate in dollars per hour.
qs.s: The time elapsed from 1:00 pm to 5:00 pm is 4 hours. Dividing the rental cost by the time gives \(\frac{\$38}{4\text{ h}} = \$9.50\text{ per hour}\).

qs.q: At 9:00 am, David rented a lawn mower from an equipment shop. He returned it at 3:00 pm the same day after mowing 1200 m\(^2\) of grass. The rental cost was $51. Determine the rental rate in dollars per hour.
