qs.q: A collector's item is valued at $50 000 today and is expected to double in value over the next five years. What was its value four years ago, assuming the rate of increase remains constant?
qs.s: The annual rate of increase is \(\frac{50\,000}{5} = \$10\,000\). Four years ago, the item was worth \(50\,000 - 4(10\,000) = \$10\,000\).

qs.q: A piece of heavy industrial machinery is currently valued at $480 000. Due to depreciation, it is expected to lose two-thirds of its current value over the next eight years at a constant rate. How many years ago was the machine worth $680 000?
qs.s: The machine loses \(\frac{2}{3}(480\,000) = \$320\,000\) over 8 years, giving a depreciation rate of \(\frac{320\,000}{8} = \$40\,000\) per year. Solving \(480\,000 + 40\,000t = 680\,000\) gives \(t = 5\) years ago.

qs.q: An office complex is currently worth $2 400 000. Its value is projected to increase at a constant annual rate such that in eight years it will be worth 1.6 times its current value. If this linear trend has been consistent, how many years ago was the complex worth $1 500 000?

A commercial warehouse was worth $720 000 four years ago and is worth $960 000 today. If its value continues to grow at this constant annual rate, in how many years from today will the property be worth $1 500 000?
qs.s: The annual rate of increase is \(\frac{960\,000 - 720\,000}{4} = \$60\,000\) per year. Setting \(960\,000 + 60\,000t = 1\,500\,000\) gives \(60\,000t = 540\,000\), which solves to \(t = 9\) years from today.

qs.q: Property A is currently valued at $750 000 and is increasing at a constant rate of $40 000 per year. Property B was purchased three years ago for $450 000 and is currently worth $630 000. Assuming Property B continues to increase at this constant rate, in how many years from now will both properties have the same value?
qs.s: Property B's annual rate of increase is \(\frac{630\,000 - 450\,000}{3} = \$60\,000\) per year. Equating both values, \(750\,000 + 40\,000t = 630\,000 + 60\,000t\), gives \(20\,000t = 120\,000\), so \(t = 6\) years.

qs.q: A historic hotel was purchased six years ago and its value has been increasing at a constant annual rate. Today, the hotel is worth $1 800 000, and it is projected to be worth 50% more than its current value in five years. What was the purchase price of the hotel six years ago?
qs.s: The hotel will increase by \(0.50 \times 1\,800\,000 = \$900\,000\) over 5 years, giving an annual rate of \(\frac{900\,000}{5} = \$180\,000\). Six years ago, its value was \(1\,800\,000 - 6(180\,000) = \$720\,000\).

qs.q: A townhouse is currently worth $420 000. The owner expects the property to double in value linearly over the next 5 years. If \(V\) represents the value of the townhouse in dollars, determine the range of this relation over this period.
qs.s: At \(t = 0\), the initial value is \(420\,000\), and after doubling over 5 years, the value at \(t = 5\) is \(2 \times 420\,000 = 840\,000\). Therefore, the range is \(420\,000 \le V \le 840\,000\).

qs.q: A storefront is worth $620 000. The owner anticipates the property will double its value linearly over the next 8 years. If \(t\) represents time in years from now, determine the domain of this relation.
qs.s: The time \(t\) starts at the present (\(t = 0\)) and covers the projected 8-year span (\(t = 8\)). Hence, the domain is \(0 \le t \le 8\).

qs.q: An office condominium is worth $480 000. The owner expects the property to double in value linearly over the next 10 years. If \(V\) represents the value of the office condominium in dollars, determine the range of this relation over this 10-year period.
qs.s: The minimum value at \(t = 0\) is \(480\,000\), and the maximum value at \(t = 10\) after doubling is \(2 \times 480\,000 = 960\,000\). Therefore, the range is \(480\,000 \le V \le 960\,000\).

qs.q: A commercial warehouse is valued at $750 000. The owner projects that the property will double in value linearly over the next 6 years. If \(t\) represents time in years from now, determine the domain of this relation.
qs.s: The relation begins at the current time (\(t = 0\)) and extends over the next 6 years (\(t = 6\)). Therefore, the domain is \(0 \le t \le 6\).

qs.q: An investor purchases a parcel of land for $350 000. She expects the land to double in value linearly over the next 4 years. If \(V\) represents the value of the land in dollars, determine the range of this relation over this period.
qs.s: The value starts at \(350\,000\) and doubles to \(2 \times 350\,000 = 700\,000\) at the end of 4 years. Thus, the range of values is \(350\,000 \le V \le 700\,000\).

qs.q: A construction company buys an excavator for $300 000. It depreciates linearly at a constant rate of $30 000 per year until it reaches its salvage value of $60 000, at which point it is retired. If \(t\) represents time in years since purchase, determine the domain of this relation.
qs.s: The excavator loses \(300\,000 - 60\,000 = 240\,000\) in value at a rate of \(30\,000\) per year, taking \(240\,000 / 30\,000 = 8\) years. Therefore, the domain of time is \(0 \le t \le 8\).

qs.q: A delivery van's total maintenance cost is a linear relation of the total distance driven. The maintenance cost is $1400 after 5000 km and $2600 after 15 000 km. The company plans to retire the van at 25 000 km. If \(C\) represents the total maintenance cost in dollars, determine the range of this relation for distances from 0 km to 25 000 km.
qs.s: The rate of maintenance cost is \((2600 - 1400) / (15\,000 - 5000) = 0.12\) dollars/km, giving a base cost \(C(0) = 1400 - 0.12(5000) = 800\). At 25 000 km, the cost is \(800 + 0.12(25\,000) = 3800\), so the range is \(800 \le C \le 3800\).

qs.q: A printing company purchases an industrial press for $180 000. The press depreciates linearly at a constant rate of $15 000 per year until its value reaches $0. If \(t\) represents the time in years since purchase, determine the domain of this depreciation relation.
qs.s: Setting the value equation \(V(t) = 180\,000 - 15\,000t = 0\) gives \(t = 180\,000 / 15\,000 = 12\) years. Since time starts at \(t = 0\) and ends when the value reaches zero, the domain is \(0 \le t \le 12\).

qs.q: An apartment complex is worth $920 000 today (\(t = 0\)). Over the past 4 years (\(t = -4\)), its value increased linearly by a total of $200 000. Assuming this same annual rate of appreciation continues for the next 6 years (\(t = 6\)), determine the range of the property's value, \(V\), over this entire 10-year period.
qs.s: Four years ago, the value was \(920\,000 - 200\,000 = 720\,000\), giving an annual appreciation rate of \(200\,000 / 4 = 50\,000\) per year. In 6 years, the value will be \(920\,000 + 6(50\,000) = 1\,220\,000\), resulting in a range of \(720\,000 \le V \le 1\,220\,000\).

qs.q: A rental cottage was purchased 3 years ago and is worth $520 000 today (\(t = 0\)). Its value has increased, and is projected to continue increasing, linearly by $40 000 each year until 5 years from now (\(t = 5\)). If \(V\) represents the cottage's value in dollars, determine the range of this relation from purchase to 5 years from now.
qs.s: Three years ago (\(t = -3\)), the cottage was worth \(520\,000 - 3(40\,000) = 400\,000\), and in 5 years (\(t = 5\)), it will be worth \(520\,000 + 5(40\,000) = 720\,000\). Thus, the range of the property value is \(400\,000 \le V \le 720\,000\).

qs.q: A bicycle rental shop charges a fixed maintenance fee plus an hourly rental rate. Renting a bicycle for 3 hours costs $22.50, and renting it for 8 hours costs $40.00. Find the hourly rate.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((40.00 - 22.50) / (8 - 3) = 17.50 / 5 = 3.50\), so the hourly rate is $3.50 per hour.

qs.q: A municipal water department charges a fixed monthly service fee plus a rate per cubic meter of water used. A customer who uses 18 cubic meters pays $47.20, while a customer who uses 30 cubic meters pays $66.40. Find the cost per cubic meter.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((66.40 - 47.20) / (30 - 18) = 19.20 / 12 = 1.60\), so the charge is $1.60 per cubic meter.

qs.q: A roadside assistance company charges a flat dispatch fee plus a fee per kilometer towed. Towing a vehicle 11 km costs $62.25, and towing a vehicle 24 km costs $94.75. Find the towing cost per kilometer.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((94.75 - 62.25) / (24 - 11) = 32.50 / 13 = 2.50\), so the cost is $2.50 per kilometer.

qs.q: A truck rental company charges a daily base fee plus a fee per kilometer driven. Renting a truck and driving 24 km costs $58.80, while driving 40 km costs $81.20. Find the cost per kilometer.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((81.20 - 58.80) / (40 - 24) = 22.40 / 16 = 1.40\), so the cost is $1.40 per kilometer.

qs.q: A custom t-shirt printing company charges a setup fee plus an amount per shirt printed. An order of 15 shirts costs $162.50, and an order of 35 shirts costs $332.50. Find the printing cost per shirt.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((332.50 - 162.50) / (35 - 15) = 170.00 / 20 = 8.50\), so the cost is $8.50 per shirt.

qs.q: At 8:00 AM, a municipal water reservoir holds 1,425,000 liters of water. By 2:00 PM on the same day, due to high demand, the volume decreases to 1,173,000 liters. Find the rate of change of the water volume in liters per hour.
qs.s: The time elapsed from 8:00 AM to 2:00 PM is 6 hours, so the rate of change is \((1,173,000 - 1,425,000) / 6 = -252,000 / 6 = -42,000\) liters per hour.

qs.q: Freight Service A charges $148.50 to transport a 45 kg crate and $236.50 to transport an 85 kg crate. Freight Service B charges $132.00 to transport a 40 kg crate and $237.00 to transport a 75 kg crate. What is the difference between their rates per kilogram?
qs.s: Service A charges $(236.50 - 148.50)/(85 - 45) = 88.00/40 = \(2.20\) per kg, and Service B charges $(237.00 - 132.00)/(75 - 40) = 105.00/35 = \(3.00\) per kg. The difference in their rates is $3.00 - 2.20 = \(0.80\) per kg.

qs.q: A high-speed train travels at a constant speed along a track. At 15 minutes past noon, it has traveled 42.5 km from the station, and at 45 minutes past noon, it has traveled 117.5 km from the station. Find the rate of change of distance with respect to time in kilometers per hour.
qs.s: The distance traveled is \(117.5 - 42.5 = 75\) km over \(45 - 15 = 30\) minutes, which is \(0.5\) hours. The rate of change is \(75 / 0.5 = 150\) km/h.

qs.q: A telecommunications company charges a monthly base fee plus an overage charge per gigabyte (GB) of data. A customer who used 14.5 GB of data was billed $68.25, while a customer who used 22.0 GB was billed $94.50. Find the overage cost per gigabyte.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((94.50 - 68.25) / (22.0 - 14.5) = 26.25 / 7.5 = 3.50\), so the overage charge is $3.50 per gigabyte.

qs.q: An airplane begins its descent from cruising altitude. At 14 minutes into the descent, its altitude is 28,400 feet, and at 26 minutes, its altitude is 17,600 feet. Find the rate of change of the airplane's altitude in feet per minute.
qs.s: The rate of change is \((17,600 - 28,400) / (26 - 14) = -10,800 / 12 = -900\) feet per minute.

qs.q: A cell phone company charges a monthly base fee plus an overage charge per gigabyte (GB) of data. A customer who used 3 GB of data was charged $47.50, and a customer who used 7 GB was charged $81.50. Write the equation that shows how the total monthly bill, B, depends on the number of gigabytes used, g.
qs.s: The cost per gigabyte is m = (81.50 - 47.50)/(7 - 3) = 34/4 = 8.5. Using (3, 47.50) gives b = 47.50 - 8.5(3) = 22, so the equation is B = 8.5g + 22.

qs.q: An electrician charges a service call fee plus an hourly labor rate. A 3-hour job costs $205, and a 6-hour job costs $370. Write the equation that shows how the total cost, T, depends on the number of hours worked, h.
qs.s: The hourly rate is m = (370 - 205)/(6 - 3) = 165/3 = 55. Substituting (3, 205) gives b = 205 - 55(3) = 40, so the equation is T = 55h + 40.

qs.q: A moving truck company charges a daily base fee plus an amount per kilometre driven. Renting the truck and driving 40 km costs $62.00, while driving 90 km costs $107.00. Write the equation that shows how the total cost, C, depends on the number of kilometres driven, k.
qs.s: The rate per kilometre is m = (107 - 62)/(90 - 40) = 45/50 = 0.9. Substituting (40, 62) gives b = 62 - 0.9(40) = 26, so the equation is C = 0.9k + 26.

qs.q: A caterer charges a flat delivery fee plus a cost per guest. An event for 25 guests costs $437.50, and an event for 40 guests costs $670.00. Write the equation that shows how the total cost, C, depends on the number of guests, g.

A printing shop charges a setup fee plus a fixed cost per t-shirt. An order of 20 t-shirts costs $230, and an order of 50 t-shirts costs $515. Write the equation that shows how the total cost, C, depends on the number of t-shirts printed, n.
qs.s: The cost per t-shirt is m = (515 - 230)/(50 - 20) = 285/30 = 9.5. Substituting (20, 230) gives b = 230 - 9.5(20) = 40, so the equation is C = 9.5n + 40.

qs.q: A municipal swimming pool is being drained at a constant rate. After 4 hours, there are 18,200 litres of water remaining in the pool, and after 9 hours, there are 14,450 litres remaining. Write the linear equation that models the volume of water remaining, V, in terms of the number of hours of draining, t.
qs.s: The rate of drainage is m = (14450 - 18200)/(9 - 4) = -750 litres per hour. Finding the initial volume gives b = 18200 - (-750)(4) = 21200, so the equation is V = -750t + 21200.

qs.q: A commercial delivery van depreciates in value at a constant rate each year. When the van is 3 years old, its value is $23,600. When it is 7 years old, its value is $14,400. Write the linear equation that models the value of the van, V, in terms of its age, t, in years.
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is m = (14400 - 23600)/(7 - 3) = -2300 dollars per year. Solving 23600 = -2300(3) + b yields the initial value b = 30500, giving V = -2300t + 30500.

qs.q: A water delivery service charges a fixed monthly equipment fee plus a rate per cubic metre of water delivered. A customer's bill includes a $15 discount for early payment. With the discount applied, the customer paid $187.00 for 35 cubic metres in May, and $263.50 for 52 cubic metres in June. Write the linear equation that models the regular bill before any discount, B, in terms of the volume of water delivered, v.
qs.s: Adding the $15 discount gives undiscounted bills of $202 for 35 m³ and $278.50 for 52 m³, yielding a rate of m = (278.50 - 202)/(52 - 35) = 4.5. Solving 202 = 4.5(35) + b gives b = 44.5, so B = 4.5v + 44.5.

qs.q: A drone's battery depletes at a constant rate while flying. After 18 minutes of flight, the battery shows 71.5% remaining. After 42 minutes of flight, it shows 35.5% remaining. Write the linear equation that models the remaining battery percentage, B, in terms of the flight time, t, in minutes.
qs.s: The battery depletion rate is m = (35.5 - 71.5)/(42 - 18) = -1.5% per minute. Finding the initial percentage gives b = 71.5 - (-1.5)(18) = 98.5, so the linear equation is B = -1.5t + 98.5.

qs.q: A banquet hall charges a fixed rental fee plus a meal cost per person. For an event with 60 guests, the customer paid a $200 deposit and a remaining balance of $2,380. For an event with 95 guests, the customer paid a $200 deposit and a remaining balance of $3,640. Write the equation that shows how the total cost, C, depends on the number of guests, g.
qs.s: The total costs are $2,580 for 60 guests and $3,840 for 95 guests, giving a rate of m = (3840 - 2580)/(95 - 60) = 36 per guest. Solving 2580 = 36(60) + b yields the fixed fee b = 420, so C = 36g + 420.

qs.q: An electrician charges a flat service call fee plus an hourly labor rate. A 3-hour job costs $170, and a 5-hour job costs $260. How many hours did the electrician work if the total bill was $395?
qs.s: The hourly rate is \(\frac{260 - 170}{5 - 3} = \$45\) per hour, so the flat fee is \(170 - 45(3) = \$35\). Solving \(45h + 35 = 395\) gives \(45h = 360\), so \(h = 8\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A print shop charges a one-time setup fee plus a fixed price per custom t-shirt. An order of 12 t-shirts costs $132, and an order of 20 t-shirts costs $200. How many t-shirts can be purchased for $285?
qs.s: The price per shirt is \(\frac{200 - 132}{20 - 12} = \$8.50\), and the setup fee is \(132 - 8.50(12) = \$30\). Setting \(8.50n + 30 = 285\) gives \(8.50n = 255\), which solves to \(n = 30\text{ t-shirts}\).

qs.q: A mobile phone plan charges a monthly base fee plus a fixed rate per gigabyte of data used. A bill for 6 GB of data is $49.00, and a bill for 14 GB of data is $85.00. How many gigabytes of data were used if the monthly bill is $112.00?
qs.s: The rate per gigabyte is \(\frac{85 - 49}{14 - 6} = \$4.50\), so the monthly base fee is \(49 - 4.50(6) = \$22.00\). Solving \(4.50g + 22 = 112\) yields \(4.50g = 90\), so \(g = 20\text{ GB}\).

qs.q: A banquet hall charges a fixed room rental fee plus a meal fee per guest. An event with 25 guests costs $750, and an event with 40 guests costs $1110. How many guests can attend if the total budget is $1470?
qs.s: The cost per guest is \(\frac{1110 - 750}{40 - 25} = \$24\), and the room rental fee is \(750 - 24(25) = \$150\). Solving \(24n + 150 = 1470\) gives \(24n = 1320\), so \(n = 55\text{ guests}\).

qs.q: A moving truck rental company charges a daily base fee plus a fee per kilometer driven. Driving 40 km costs $49.00, and driving 90 km costs $79.00. How far can a customer drive on a budget of $109.00?
qs.s: The rate per kilometer is \(\frac{79 - 49}{90 - 40} = \$0.60\), giving a base fee of \(49 - 0.60(40) = \$25\). Solving \(0.60d + 25 = 109\) yields \(0.60d = 84\), so \(d = 140\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A catering service charges a fixed equipment fee plus a cost per guest. Catering an event for 45 guests costs $1182.50, and catering for 80 guests costs $1970.00. An event organizer has an overall budget of $3120.00, but must reserve $250.00 for decorations. How many guests can be catered with the remaining budget?
qs.s: The rate per guest is \(\frac{1970 - 1182.50}{80 - 45} = \$22.50\) and the equipment fee is \(1182.50 - 22.50(45) = \$170.00\). After subtracting the \(\$250.00\) decoration fee from the budget, solving \(22.50n + 170 = 2870\) yields \(n = 120\text{ guests}\).

qs.q: A manufacturer produces custom metal brackets with a fixed machine setup cost plus a constant cost per bracket. An order of 250 brackets costs $1425, and an order of 600 brackets costs $3175. A client pays $4825 for a production run, but 15 brackets from this run must be set aside for quality testing. How many brackets from this run are left to be sold?
qs.s: The cost per bracket is \(\frac{3175 - 1425}{600 - 250} = \$5.00\) and the setup fee is \(1425 - 5(250) = \$175\). Solving \(5n + 175 = 4825\) gives \(n = 930\) brackets produced, leaving \(930 - 15 = 915\text{ brackets}\) to be sold.

qs.q: A large industrial water tank is being drained at a constant rate. After 15 minutes of draining, the tank holds 4350 liters of water, and after 40 minutes, it holds 2850 liters. At this rate, how many minutes from the start of draining will it take for the volume to reach 450 liters?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{2850 - 4350}{40 - 15} = -60\text{ L/min}\), giving an initial volume of \(4350 - (-60)(15) = 5250\text{ L}\). Setting \(5250 - 60t = 450\) gives \(60t = 4800\), so \(t = 80\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A car rental agency charges a flat daily insurance fee plus a rate per kilometer driven. A 1-day rental with 180 km driven costs $151.00, and a 1-day rental with 320 km driven costs $228.00. A customer rents a car for 2 days, drives the exact same distance each day, and pays a total bill of $346.00. How many kilometers did the customer drive each day?
qs.s: The rate is \(\frac{228 - 151}{320 - 180} = \$0.55\) per km, and the daily fee is \(151 - 0.55(180) = \$52.00\). Since the total bill for 2 days is \(\$346.00\), each day costs \(\$173.00\); solving \(0.55x + 52 = 173\) gives \(x = 220\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A freight shipping service charges a flat booking fee plus a rate per kilometer. Transporting a shipment 240 km costs $414.00, and transporting it 580 km costs $890.00. If a company increases its shipping budget from $624.00 to $1100.00, how many additional kilometers can the shipment be transported?
qs.s: The rate is \(\frac{890 - 414}{580 - 240} = \$1.40\) per km and the booking fee is \(414 - 1.40(240) = \$78.00\). Solving \(1.40d + 78 = C\) gives \(d_1 = 390\text{ km}\) for \(\$624.00\) and \(d_2 = 730\text{ km}\) for \(\$1100.00\), so the additional distance is \(730 - 390 = 340\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A car rental company charges a daily base fee plus a fee per kilometer driven. A customer paid $54.50 for driving 35 km in a day, and another customer paid $77.00 for driving 60 km in a day. For a daily distance \(d \ge 0\), what is the minimum value in the range of the daily rental cost, in dollars?
qs.s: The rate per kilometer is \(m = \frac{77.00 - 54.50}{60 - 35} = \$0.90/\text{km}\), so the base fee is \(b = 54.50 - 0.90(35) = \$23\). For \(d \ge 0\), the range is \(C \ge 23\), so the minimum value is 23.

qs.q: An appliance repair technician charges a fixed service call fee plus an hourly labor rate. The technician charged $95 for a 2-hour job and $170 for a 5-hour job. For any job requiring \(h \ge 0\) hours, what is the minimum value in the range of the total charge, in dollars?
qs.s: The hourly rate is \(m = \frac{170 - 95}{5 - 2} = \$25/\text{h}\), so the fixed fee is \(b = 95 - 25(2) = \$45\). Since \(h \ge 0\), the range of the total charge is \(C \ge 45\), making the minimum value 45.

qs.q: A ride-share service charges a base pickup fare plus a constant rate per kilometer. A passenger paid $18.50 for a 9 km ride, and another passenger paid $30.50 for a 17 km ride. For any trip of distance \(d \ge 0\), what is the minimum value in the range of the total fare, in dollars?
qs.s: The rate per kilometer is \(m = \frac{30.50 - 18.50}{17 - 9} = \$1.50/\text{km}\), giving a base fare of \(b = 18.50 - 1.50(9) = \$5\). Since \(d \ge 0\), the range is \(C \ge 5\), so the minimum value is 5.

qs.q: A mobile phone company charges a monthly base fee plus a constant rate per gigabyte of data used. A customer was charged $38 for using 4 GB of data, and another customer was charged $59 for using 11 GB of data. For data usage \(g \ge 0\), what is the minimum value in the range of the monthly bill, in dollars?
qs.s: The rate per gigabyte is \(m = \frac{59 - 38}{11 - 4} = \$3/\text{GB}\), so the base fee is \(b = 38 - 3(4) = \$26\). Since \(g \ge 0\), the range is \(C \ge 26\), giving a minimum value of 26.

qs.q: A banquet hall charges a fixed room rental fee plus a set charge per guest. An event with 20 guests cost $430, and an event with 50 guests cost $790. For any event with \(n \ge 0\) guests, what is the minimum value in the range of the total event cost, in dollars?
qs.s: The cost per guest is \(m = \frac{790 - 430}{50 - 20} = \$12\), which gives a fixed room fee of \(b = 430 - 12(20) = \$190\). Since \(n \ge 0\), the range is \(C \ge 190\), so the minimum value is 190.

qs.q: A water reservoir drains at a constant rate. After 8 hours of draining, 700 liters of water remain, and after 20 hours, 400 liters remain. If draining stops when the reservoir is completely empty, what is the maximum value in the domain of hours that the reservoir can drain?
qs.s: The draining rate is \(m = \frac{400 - 700}{20 - 8} = -25\text{ L/h}\), giving an initial volume of \(b = 700 - (-25)(8) = 900\text{ L}\). Setting \(900 - 25t = 0\) yields \(t = 36\), so the maximum value in the domain is 36.

qs.q: A shipping courier charges a base processing fee plus a rate per kilogram. A 45 kg package costs $122 to ship, and a 75 kg package costs $182. If the company sets a strict maximum package weight of 160 kg, what is the maximum value in the range of the shipping cost, in dollars?
qs.s: The rate is \(m = \frac{182 - 122}{75 - 45} = \$2/\text{kg}\), giving a base fee of \(b = 122 - 2(45) = \$32\). For the domain \(0 \le w \le 160\), the maximum cost is \(C(160) = 2(160) + 32 = \$352\), which is the maximum value in the range.

qs.q: A print shop charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant rate per printed booklet. An order of 80 booklets costs $194, and an order of 140 booklets costs $296. If a customer has a maximum budget of $500, what is the maximum value in the domain of booklets they can order?
qs.s: The cost per booklet is \(m = \frac{296 - 194}{140 - 80} = \$1.70\), giving a setup fee of \(b = 194 - 1.70(80) = \$58\). Solving \(1.70n + 58 \le 500\) gives \(n \le 260\), so the maximum value in the domain is 260.

qs.q: An equipment rental company charges a flat delivery fee plus an hourly operating fee. A contractor paid $410 for 6 hours of use and $650 for 14 hours of use. If the contractor has an operating budget of $950, what is the maximum value in the domain of hours they can rent the equipment?
qs.s: The hourly rate is \(m = \frac{650 - 410}{14 - 6} = \$30/\text{h}\), giving a flat delivery fee of \(b = 410 - 30(6) = \$230\). Solving \(30h + 230 \le 950\) yields \(h \le 24\), so the maximum value in the domain is 24.

qs.q: A decorative candle burns down at a constant rate. After burning for 3 hours, its height is 19.5 cm, and after burning for 7 hours, its height is 13.5 cm. If the candle is allowed to burn until it is completely consumed (height = 0 cm), what is the maximum value in the domain of burning time, in hours?
qs.s: The burning rate is \(m = \frac{13.5 - 19.5}{7 - 3} = -1.5\text{ cm/h}\), giving an initial height of \(b = 19.5 - (-1.5)(3) = 24\text{ cm}\). Setting \(24 - 1.5t = 0\) yields \(t = 16\), so the maximum value in the domain is 16.

qs.q: A toy store finds that demand for a popular board game is 1200 units when the price is $25 per game, and 800 units when the price is $35 per game. Determine a linear equation expressing the demand, \(D\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A concert promoter finds that ticket demand is 2400 tickets when the price is $50 per ticket, and 1800 tickets when the price is $70 per ticket. Determine a linear equation expressing the demand, \(D\), in terms of the ticket price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A manufacturer determines that the weekly supply of running shoes is 1500 pairs when the price is $80 per pair, and 2100 pairs when the price is $100 per pair. Determine a linear equation expressing the weekly supply, \(S\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{2100 - 1500}{100 - 80} = 30\). Using \((80, 1500)\), the equation is \(S - 1500 = 30(p - 80)\), which simplifies to \(S = 30p - 900\).

qs.q: A fitness club discovers that it sells 450 memberships per month when the fee is $40 per month, and 350 memberships per month when the fee is $60 per month. Determine a linear equation expressing the number of monthly memberships sold, \(M\), in terms of the fee, \(f\) (in dollars).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{350 - 450}{60 - 40} = -5\). Using \((40, 450)\), we write \(M - 450 = -5(f - 40)\), which simplifies to \(M = -5f + 650\).

qs.q: A retailer finds that monthly sales of a smartwatch are 3200 units when priced at $120 each, and 2600 units when priced at $150 each. Determine a linear equation expressing monthly sales, \(N\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A farmer's market vendor finds that when honey is priced at $8 per jar, daily sales are 110 jars. When the price is raised to $12 per jar, daily sales drop to 65 jars. Determine a linear equation expressing the daily sales, \(S\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A department store finds that annual sales of a television set are 4800 units when the price is $600 per unit, and 3600 units when the price is $750 per unit. Determine a linear equation expressing the price, \(p\) (in dollars), in terms of the number of units sold, \(q\).
qs.s: The slope relating price to units sold is \(m = \frac{750 - 600}{3600 - 4800} = -\frac{1}{8}\). Using \((4800, 600)\), \(p - 600 = -\frac{1}{8}(q - 4800)\), which simplifies to \(p = -\frac{1}{8}q + 1200\).

qs.q: A software company sells 40,000 licenses of an app per year at a price of $50 each. When the price is increased by $20, annual sales decrease by 15,000 licenses. Determine a linear equation expressing the annual sales, \(N\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A manufacturer observes that the demand for a new tablet is 920 units when the price is $40 per unit, and 570 units when the price is $60 per unit. Determine a linear equation expressing the demand, \(D\), in terms of the price, \(p\) (in dollars).

A manufacturer supplies 1500 solar panels per month when the price is $220 each, and 2500 solar panels per month when the price is $300 each. Determine a linear equation expressing the price, \(p\) (in dollars), in terms of the number of solar panels supplied, \(s\).

Demand for tickets to a school concert is 1200 tickets when the price is $50 per ticket, and 800 tickets when the price is $70 per ticket. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the demand if the price drops to $40 per ticket.
qs.s: The rate of change is (800 - 1200) / (70 - 50) = -20 tickets per dollar. When the price drops to $40, the demand is 1200 + (-20)(40 - 50) = 1400 tickets.

qs.q: A decorative candle burns at a constant linear rate. After burning for 2 hours, its height is 22 cm, and after burning for 6 hours, its height is 14 cm. Determine the height of the candle after burning for 9 hours.
qs.s: The burning rate is (14 - 22) / (6 - 2) = -2 cm/h. After 9 hours, the height is 14 + (-2)(9 - 6) = 8 cm.

qs.q: A bakery finds that the weekly demand for its artisan bread is 500 loaves when the price is $4 per loaf, and 350 loaves when the price is $7 per loaf. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the demand if the price drops to $3 per loaf.
qs.s: The rate of change of demand is (350 - 500) / (7 - 4) = -50 loaves per dollar. At a price of $3, the demand is 500 + (-50)(3 - 4) = 550 loaves.

qs.q: A computer technician charges a fixed diagnostic fee plus an hourly rate. A 2-hour service call costs $140, and a 5-hour service call costs $290. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the cost of a 4-hour service call.
qs.s: The hourly rate is (290 - 140) / (5 - 2) = $50 per hour. Thus, the cost for 4 hours is 140 + 50(4 - 2) = $240.

qs.q: The air temperature on a mountain is 15°C at an elevation of 600 m, and 9°C at an elevation of 1600 m. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the temperature at an elevation of 2100 m.
qs.s: The temperature rate of change is (9 - 15) / (1600 - 600) = -0.006°C/m. At 2100 m, the temperature is 9 + (-0.006)(2100 - 1600) = 6°C.

qs.q: A manufacturer determines that demand for a smart thermostat is 14,000 units when priced at $120, and 11,600 units when priced at $150. Assuming a linear relationship, what price per unit should they set to achieve a demand of 16,400 units?
qs.s: The rate of change of demand is (11600 - 14000) / (150 - 120) = -80 units per dollar. Solving 16400 = 14000 - 80(P - 120) yields P - 120 = -30, so P = $90.

qs.q: A commercial printing service charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant rate per brochure. Printing 850 brochures costs $380, while printing 1450 brochures costs $590. If an organization has a budget of $800, how many brochures can they print?
qs.s: The unit cost is (590 - 380) / (1450 - 850) = $0.35 per brochure, giving a fixed fee of 380 - 0.35(850) = $82.50. Setting total cost to 800 gives 0.35n + 82.50 = 800, so n = 2050 brochures.

qs.q: A delivery truck's fuel consumption is linearly related to its cargo load. With a load of 1.5 tonnes, the truck consumes 14.2 L per 100 km. With a load of 3.5 tonnes, it consumes 17.8 L per 100 km. Determine the cargo load if the fuel consumption is 20.5 L per 100 km.
qs.s: The rate of consumption increase is (17.8 - 14.2) / (3.5 - 1.5) = 1.8 L per 100 km per tonne. Solving 20.5 = 17.8 + 1.8(L - 3.5) gives L - 3.5 = 1.5, so L = 5 tonnes.

qs.q: A deep-sea research probe measures water temperature at various depths. At a depth of 140 m, the temperature is 18.2°C, and at a depth of 380 m, the temperature is 11.0°C. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the water temperature at a depth of 550 m.
A stadium vendor finds that the demand for hot dogs is 1800 when the price is $4.50, and 1350 when the price is $6.00. Assuming the relationship is linear, at what price will the demand drop to zero?
qs.s: The rate of change is (1350 - 1800) / (6.00 - 4.50) = -300 hot dogs per dollar. Setting demand to zero in 0 = 1800 - 300(P - 4.50) gives P - 4.50 = 6.00, so P = $10.50.

qs.q: A research balloon records an air temperature of \(14^\circ\text{C}\) at an altitude of \(1000\text{ m}\), and \(2^\circ\text{C}\) at an altitude of \(3000\text{ m}\). Assuming temperature decreases linearly with altitude, determine the altitude at which the temperature is \(-10^\circ\text{C}\).
qs.s: The rate of temperature decrease is \(\frac{2 - 14}{3000 - 1000} = -0.006^\circ\text{C/m}\). To reach \(-10^\circ\text{C}\) from \(2^\circ\text{C}\) (a change of \(-12^\circ\text{C}\)), the altitude must increase by \(\frac{-12}{-0.006} = 2000\text{ m}\), resulting in an altitude of \(3000 + 2000 = 5000\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A company manufactures custom hoodies. The total production cost is $1500 for 50 hoodies and $2700 for 100 hoodies. Assuming the cost is linearly related to the number of hoodies produced, determine how many hoodies were produced if the total cost is $3900.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{2700 - 1500}{100 - 50} = \$24\text{ per hoodie}\). From \(\$2700\) to \(\$3900\) is an increase of \(\$1200\), which corresponds to \(\frac{1200}{24} = 50\) additional hoodies, so \(100 + 50 = 150\) hoodies were produced.

qs.q: Suppose demand for concert tickets is 1200 tickets when the price is $50 per ticket, and 900 tickets when the price is $65 per ticket. Assuming a linear relationship between price and demand, determine the price per ticket if 1400 tickets are sold.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{900 - 1200}{65 - 50} = -20\text{ tickets/\$}\). To sell 1400 tickets (an increase of 200 tickets from 1200), the price must change by \(\frac{200}{-20} = -\$10\), giving a price of \(50 - 10 = \$40\).

qs.q: A car's fuel tank has \(48\text{ L}\) of gasoline remaining after driving \(100\text{ km}\), and \(36\text{ L}\) remaining after driving \(250\text{ km}\). Assuming fuel is consumed linearly with distance, determine the distance driven when \(20\text{ L}\) remain in the tank.
qs.s: The consumption rate is \(\frac{36 - 48}{250 - 100} = -0.08\text{ L/km}\). To drop from \(36\text{ L}\) to \(20\text{ L}\) (a change of \(-16\text{ L}\)), the additional distance is \(\frac{-16}{-0.08} = 200\text{ km}\), so the total distance is \(250 + 200 = 450\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A bakery finds that the weekly demand for a specialty cake is 160 cakes when the price is $20 per cake, and 100 cakes when the price is $35 per cake. Assuming a linear relationship between price and demand, determine the price per cake if 180 cakes are sold.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{100 - 160}{35 - 20} = -4\text{ cakes/\$}\). Selling 180 cakes is an increase of 20 cakes from 160, requiring a price change of \(\frac{20}{-4} = -\$5\), so the price is \(20 - 5 = \$15\).

qs.q: A commercial delivery van depreciates in value at a constant linear rate. After 2.5 years of use, the van is valued at $31,500, and after 6 years, its value is $19,250. How many years after its initial purchase will the van reach a scrap value of $1,750?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \(\frac{19250 - 31500}{6 - 2.5} = -\$3500\text{/year}\). The initial value is \(31500 + 2.5(3500) = \$40,250\), so solving \(40250 - 3500t = 1750\) gives \(3500t = 38500\), which yields \(t = 11\text{ years}\).

qs.q: Suppose the demand for a smart speaker is 3000 units when the price is $90 per unit, and 2100 units when the price is $120 per unit. Assuming demand is linearly related to price, determine the price per unit needed to achieve a 20% increase in demand compared to the demand at $90.
qs.s: A 20% increase from 3000 units gives a target demand of \(3000 \times 1.20 = 3600\text{ units}\). The rate of change is \(\frac{2100 - 3000}{120 - 90} = -30\text{ units/\$}\), so the price change required is \(\frac{3600 - 3000}{-30} = -\$20\), giving a price of \(90 - 20 = \$70\).

qs.q: A theater company finds that attendance for its musical is 540 people when tickets are priced at $24, and 420 people when tickets are priced at $32. Assuming attendance is linearly related to ticket price, determine the total revenue generated if ticket prices are set such that 600 people attend.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{420 - 540}{32 - 24} = -15\text{ attendees/\$}\). For attendance to increase from 540 to 600 (\(\Delta q = +60\)), the price must change by \(\frac{60}{-15} = -\$4\), making the ticket price \(24 - 4 = \$20\). Total revenue is \(600 \times \$20 = \$12,000\).

qs.q: A manufacturer tracks the sales of a portable charger. The monthly demand is 18,000 units when the price is $12.50, and 14,000 units when the price is $15.00. Assuming demand is linearly related to price, determine the price per unit at which demand would drop to zero.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{14000 - 18000}{15.00 - 12.50} = -1600\text{ units/\$}\). To drop demand from 14,000 to 0 (\(\Delta q = -14000\)), the price must increase by \(\frac{-14000}{-1600} = \$8.75\), giving a price of \(15.00 + 8.75 = \$23.75\).

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir is being drained at a constant rate. After 6 hours of draining, the reservoir contains 360,000 litres of water, and after 15 hours, it contains 252,000 litres. Assuming a linear relationship, determine the total number of hours from the start of draining until the reservoir is completely empty.
qs.s: The draining rate is \(\frac{252000 - 360000}{15 - 6} = -12,000\text{ L/h}\). The initial volume at \(t = 0\) is \(360,000 + 6(12,000) = 432,000\text{ L}\), so the total time to drain completely is \(\frac{432000}{12000} = 36\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A freight company determines that the relationship between the shipping cost, S, and the distance traveled, d, in kilometers is linear. Suppose the cost is $320 for 30 km and $670 for 80 km. Find the shipping cost per kilometer.
qs.s: The cost per kilometer is the slope: (670 - 320) / (80 - 30) = 350 / 50 = $7 per km.

qs.q: An electrician determines that the relationship between the total fee charged, F, and the number of hours worked, h, is linear. Suppose the fee is $190 for 3 hours and $440 for 8 hours. Find the fee per hour.
qs.s: The hourly rate is the slope: (440 - 190) / (8 - 3) = 250 / 5 = $50 per hour.

qs.q: A fitness club determines that the relationship between the total amount paid, A, and the number of months of membership, m, is linear. Suppose the total amount paid is $210 after 4 months and $410 after 9 months. Find the cost per month.
qs.s: The monthly rate is the rate of change: (410 - 210) / (9 - 4) = 200 / 5 = $40 per month.

qs.q: A caterer determines that the relationship between the total cost, C, and the number of guests, g, is linear. Suppose the cost is $450 for 20 guests and $750 for 35 guests. Find the cost per guest.
qs.s: The rate of change is the change in cost divided by the change in the number of guests: (750 - 450) / (35 - 20) = 300 / 15 = $20 per guest.

qs.q: A print shop determines that the relationship between the production cost, C, and the number of t-shirts printed, n, is linear. Suppose the cost is $520 for 40 t-shirts and $870 for 75 t-shirts. Find the cost per t-shirt.
qs.s: The cost per t-shirt is given by the change in cost over the change in quantity: (870 - 520) / (75 - 40) = 350 / 35 = $10.

qs.q: A transport company finds that the relationship between the fuel remaining in a cargo truck's tank, F, in liters, and the distance traveled, d, in kilometers, is linear. The tank has 315 liters remaining after traveling 140 km, and 231 liters remaining after traveling 420 km. Find the rate of change of fuel remaining per kilometer.
qs.s: The rate of change is (231 - 315) / (420 - 140) = -84 / 280 = -0.3 liters per km.

qs.q: A deep-sea research submarine descends at a constant linear rate. At 1:15 p.m., its depth is 420 meters below the surface. At 2:45 p.m., its depth is 1,230 meters below the surface. Find the submarine's rate of descent in meters per minute.
qs.s: The elapsed time between 1:15 p.m. and 2:45 p.m. is 1 hour and 30 minutes, or 90 minutes. The rate of descent is (1,230 - 420) / 90 = 810 / 90 = 9 meters per minute.

qs.q: An aerospace manufacturer determines that the relationship between the total production cost, C, and the number of components produced, n, is linear. The total cost is $184,500 for 150 components and $247,000 for 275 components. Find the production cost per component.
qs.s: The unit cost is the slope of the relation: (247,000 - 184,500) / (275 - 150) = 62,500 / 125 = $500 per component.

qs.q: A laboratory technician records the temperature, T, of a chemical solution cooling at a linear rate. At t = 3.5 minutes, the temperature is 84.5°C, and at t = 11.5 minutes, the temperature is 56.5°C. Find the rate of change of the temperature per minute.
qs.s: The rate of change is (56.5 - 84.5) / (11.5 - 3.5) = -28 / 8 = -3.5°C per minute.

qs.q: A city's water reservoir volume, V, in megaliters, decreases linearly during a drought. On day 12, the reservoir holds 54,600 megaliters, and on day 44, it holds 43,400 megaliters. Find the rate of change of the water volume per day.
qs.s: The rate of change is the change in volume divided by elapsed days: (43,400 - 54,600) / (44 - 12) = -11,200 / 32 = -350 megaliters per day.

qs.q: A catering company determines that the relationship between the total cost of an event, \(C\), and the number of guests, \(g\), is linear. The cost is $850 for \(30\) guests and $1250 for \(50\) guests. Determine the fixed base fee.
qs.s: The rate per guest is \((1250 - 850) / (50 - 30) = 400 / 20 = \$20\). Thus, the fixed base fee is \(850 - 20(30) = \$250\).

qs.q: A manufacturer determines that the relationship between the weekly operating cost, \(C\), and the number of items manufactured, \(p\), is linear. The cost is $2900 for \(60\) items and $3900 for \(85\) items. Determine the fixed cost.

A truck rental agency determines that the total rental cost, \(C\), is linearly related to the distance driven, \(d\), in miles. The rental cost is $140 for driving \(40\) miles and $210 for driving \(75\) miles. Determine the fixed base charge.
qs.s: The rate per mile is \((210 - 140) / (75 - 40) = 70 / 35 = \$2\). Thus, the fixed base charge is \(140 - 2(40) = \$60\).

qs.q: A plumber determines that the total charge, \(C\), is linearly related to the number of hours worked, \(h\). A service call lasting \(3\) hours costs $190, and a service call lasting \(6\) hours costs $340. Determine the fixed service fee.
qs.s: The hourly rate is \((340 - 190) / (6 - 3) = 150 / 3 = \$50\). Thus, the fixed service fee is \(190 - 50(3) = \$40\).

qs.q: A printing company determines that the relationship between the total production cost, \(C\), and the number of booklets printed, \(n\), is linear. The total cost is $170 for \(40\) booklets and $260 for \(70\) booklets. Determine the fixed cost.
qs.s: The rate per booklet is \((260 - 170) / (70 - 40) = 90 / 30 = \$3\). Thus, the fixed cost is \(170 - 3(40) = \$50\).

qs.q: An engineering firm determines that the value, \(V\), of a piece of heavy equipment depreciates linearly over time, \(t\), in years. After \(3\) years, the equipment is valued at $38,500. After \(8\) years, its value is $24,750. Determine the original purchase price of the equipment.
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \((24750 - 38500) / (8 - 3) = -13750 / 5 = -\$2750\text{ per year}\). Thus, the original purchase price was \(38500 - (-2750)(3) = \$46,750\).

qs.q: A factory determines that the monthly operating cost, \(C\), is linearly related to the number of units produced, \(n\). Producing \(1200\) units in a month costs $41,000, and producing \(1750\) units costs $54,750. Determine the factory's fixed monthly operating cost.
qs.s: The variable cost per unit is \((54750 - 41000) / (1750 - 1200) = 13750 / 550 = \$25\). Thus, the fixed monthly operating cost is \(41000 - 25(1200) = \$11,000\).

qs.q: A freight company determines that the shipping cost, \(C\), is linearly related to the weight of the shipment, \(w\). Shipping a crate weighing \(45\text{ kg}\) costs $157. When the weight is increased by \(35\text{ kg}\), the total cost increases to $248. Determine the fixed handling fee.
qs.s: The second shipment weighs \(45 + 35 = 80\text{ kg}\), giving a rate of \((248 - 157) / (80 - 45) = 91 / 35 = \$2.60\text{ per kg}\). Thus, the fixed handling fee is \(157 - 2.60(45) = \$40\).

qs.q: A mobile phone company charges a monthly base fee plus a constant rate per gigabyte of data used beyond the monthly allowance. A customer who used \(16\text{ GB}\) of extra data was billed $68, while a customer who used \(28\text{ GB}\) of extra data was billed $101. Determine the monthly base fee.
qs.s: The rate per gigabyte is \((101 - 68) / (28 - 16) = 33 / 12 = \$2.75\). Thus, the monthly base fee is \(68 - 2.75(16) = \$24\).

qs.q: A water reservoir is being drained at a constant rate, so that the volume of water remaining, \(V\), is a linear function of time, \(t\), in hours. After \(14\) hours of draining, the reservoir contains \(5320\text{ L}\) of water. After \(22\) hours of draining, it contains \(4120\text{ L}\) of water. Determine the initial volume of water in the reservoir.
qs.s: The draining rate is \((4120 - 5320) / (22 - 14) = -1200 / 8 = -150\text{ L/h}\). Thus, the initial volume was \(5320 - (-150)(14) = 7420\text{ L}\).

qs.q: A pottery studio determines that the relationship between the income earned, \(I\), and the number of ceramic mugs crafted, \(m\), is linear. Suppose the income is $1300 on 40 mugs, and $2050 on 65 mugs. If the expense to craft 100 mugs is $1900, find the profit on 100 mugs. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The rate of income is $(2050 - 1300) / (65 - 40) = $30 per mug. Total income for 100 mugs is $1300 + 30(100 - 40) = $3100, giving a profit of $3100 - $1900 = $1200.

qs.q: An apparel manufacturer determines that the relationship between the income earned, \(I\), and the number of jackets produced, \(j\), is linear. Suppose the income is $1400 on 30 jackets, and $2300 on 50 jackets. If the expense to produce 70 jackets is $2100, find the profit on 70 jackets. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The rate of income is $(2300 - 1400) / (50 - 30) = $45 per jacket. Total income for 70 jackets is $1400 + 45(70 - 30) = $3200, so the profit is $3200 - $2100 = $1100.

qs.q: An electronics repair shop determines that the relationship between the income earned, \(I\), and the number of monitors rebuilt, \(n\), is linear. Suppose the income is $1700 on 30 monitors, and $2600 on 48 monitors. If the expense to rebuild 75 monitors is $2400, find the profit on 75 monitors. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The rate of income is $(2600 - 1700) / (48 - 30) = $50 per monitor. Total income on 75 monitors is $1700 + 50(75 - 30) = $3950, giving a profit of $3950 - $2400 = $1550.

qs.q: A bakery determines that the relationship between the income earned, \(I\), and the number of specialty cakes baked, \(c\), is linear. Suppose the income is $1250 on 25 cakes, and $2150 on 45 cakes. If the expense to bake 60 cakes is $1750, find the profit on 60 cakes. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The rate of income per cake is $(2150 - 1250) / (45 - 25) = $45. Total income for 60 cakes is $1250 + 45(60 - 25) = $2825, so the profit is $2825 - $1750 = $1075.

qs.q: A furniture manufacturer determines that the relationship between the income earned, \(I\), and the number of chairs produced, \(c\), is linear. Suppose the income is $1500 on 30 chairs, and $2300 on 50 chairs. If the expense to produce 80 chairs is $2200, find the profit on 80 chairs. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The rate of income per chair is $(2300 - 1500) / (50 - 30) = $40. The income on 80 chairs is $1500 + 40(80 - 30) = $3500, giving a profit of $3500 - $2200 = $1300.

qs.q: A tech company determines that the income earned, \(I\), is linearly related to the number of gadgets sold, \(g\). The income is $2300 on 30 gadgets and $3700 on 50 gadgets. The total expense to produce \(g\) gadgets is given by the equation \(E = 30g + 500\). How many gadgets must be sold to earn a profit of $2500? \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The income model is \(I = 70g + 200\), giving a profit model of \(P = I - E = 40g - 300\). Setting \(40g - 300 = 2500\) gives \(40g = 2800\), so \(g = 70\).

qs.q: A manufacturing company determines that both income, \(I\), and expense, \(E\), are linear functions of the number of items produced, \(p\). Income is $2400 on 40 items and $3900 on 65 items. Expense is $1900 on 40 items and $2650 on 65 items. Find the profit on 90 items. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: Income for 90 items is $2400 + 60(50) = $5400, and expense is $1900 + 30(50) = $3400. The profit is $5400 - $3400 = $2000.

qs.q: A manufacturer determines that total revenue, \(R\), is linearly related to the number of components produced, \(n\). Revenue is $4800 on 150 components and $7200 on 250 components. The expense consists of a fixed setup cost of $1500 plus $14 per component produced. Find the profit when 400 components are produced. \((\text{Profit} = \text{Revenue} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: Revenue for 400 components is $4800 + 24(250) = $10800, and expense is $1500 + 14(400) = $7100. Thus, profit is $10800 - $7100 = $3700.

qs.q: A publisher determines that the income, \(I\), from selling an art book is linearly related to the number of copies printed, \(b\). The income is $900 for 40 copies and $1950 for 70 copies. The expense is given by the equation \(E = 15b + 1500\). Find the break-even quantity (the number of copies that must be sold so that profit is \(0\)). \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The income relation is \(I = 35b - 500\), yielding profit \(P = I - E = 20b - 2000\). Setting profit to 0 gives \(20b = 2000\), which solves to \(b = 100\) copies.

qs.q: A workshop determines that both monthly income, \(I\), and monthly expense, \(E\), are linear functions of the number of units produced, \(x\). The income is $3400 on 40 units and $5800 on 70 units. The expense is $2500 on 40 units and $3700 on 70 units. How many units must the workshop produce to earn a monthly profit of $3300? \((\text{Profit} = \text{Income} - \text{Expense})\)
qs.s: The models are \(I = 80x + 200\) and \(E = 40x + 900\), giving \(P = 40x - 700\). Setting \(40x - 700 = 3300\) yields \(40x = 4000\), so \(x = 100\) units.

qs.q: A tutor found that the total earnings, E, from a tutoring package is linearly related to the number of sessions, s. She earned $110 for 4 sessions and $230 for 10 sessions. Find her earnings per session.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (230 - 110) / (10 - 4) = 120 / 6 = 20. Thus, her earnings are $20 per session.

qs.q: A potter found that the relationship between the total production cost, C, and the number of ceramic mugs made, m, is linear. It costs $35 to make 6 mugs and $75 to make 14 mugs. Find the production cost per mug.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (75 - 35) / (14 - 6) = 40 / 8 = 5. Thus, the production cost per mug is $5.

qs.q: Julian found that the total cost, C, of renting a bicycle is linearly related to the number of hours, h, it is rented. He paid $22 for 3 hours and $38 for 7 hours. Find the hourly rental rate.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (38 - 22) / (7 - 3) = 16 / 4 = 4. Thus, the hourly rental rate is $4.

qs.q: An electrician found that the total fee, F, charged for a repair job is linearly related to the number of hours worked, h. The fee is $95 for 2 hours of work and $185 for 5 hours of work. Find the hourly rate.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (185 - 95) / (5 - 2) = 90 / 3 = 30. Thus, the hourly rate is $30.

qs.q: Elena found that the relationship between the total cost, C, of catering an event and the number of guests, n, is linear. The cost is $120 for 10 guests and $270 for 25 guests. Find the cost per guest.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (270 - 120) / (25 - 10) = 150 / 15 = 10. Thus, the cost per guest is $10.

qs.q: A chemist cools a liquid solution at a constant linear rate. At 4 minutes, the temperature of the solution is \(62^\circ\text{C}\), and at 16 minutes, the temperature is \(-10^\circ\text{C}\). Find the rate of change of the temperature per minute.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (-10 - 62) / (16 - 4) = -72 / 12 = -6. Thus, the temperature changes at a rate of -6°C per minute.

qs.q: A water reservoir drains at a constant linear rate. After 8 hours of draining, the reservoir contains \(14{,}200\text{ m}^3\) of water. After 20 hours, it contains \(8{,}800\text{ m}^3\) of water. Find the rate of change of the volume of water per hour.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (8800 - 14200) / (20 - 8) = -5400 / 12 = -450. Thus, the volume changes at a rate of -450 m³ per hour.

qs.q: A commercial printer determines that the cost, C, of printing books is a linear function of the number of copies, n. It costs $14,100 to print 2,400 copies and $30,300 to print 6,000 copies. Find the printing cost per copy.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (30300 - 14100) / (6000 - 2400) = 16200 / 3600 = 4.5. Thus, the cost per copy is $4.50.

qs.q: A startup found that its cumulative profit, P, is linearly related to the number of months, m, it has been operating. In month 3, the startup had a net loss of $1,400 (a profit of -$1,400). In month 11, the startup reached a net profit of $5,000. Find the rate of change of profit per month.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (5000 - (-1400)) / (11 - 3) = 6400 / 8 = 800. Thus, the profit increases by $800 per month.

qs.q: A logistics company found that the fee, F, to ship cargo is linearly related to the cargo's weight, w. It costs $1,540 to ship 450 kilograms of cargo and $2,520 to ship 800 kilograms of cargo. Find the shipping fee per kilogram.
qs.s: The rate of change is m = (2520 - 1540) / (800 - 450) = 980 / 350 = 2.8. Thus, the shipping fee is $2.80 per kilogram.

qs.q: Devon found that the relationship between the profit, P, which he made selling n ceramic bowls is linear. Suppose he made a profit of $18 on 6 bowls, and $82 on 14 bowls. Find the fixed cost of his clay and glaze.
qs.s: The rate of profit per bowl is \(m = \frac{82 - 18}{14 - 6} = \frac{64}{8} = 8\). Using \((6, 18)\) in \(P = 8n - F\) gives \(18 = 8(6) - F = 48 - F\), so the fixed cost is \(F = 48 - 18 = \$30\).

qs.q: Elena found that the relationship between the profit, P, which she made selling n scented candles is linear. Suppose she made a profit of $14 on 6 candles, and $70 on 14 candles. Find the fixed cost of her supplies.
qs.s: The rate of profit per candle is \(m = \frac{70 - 14}{14 - 6} = \frac{56}{8} = 7\). Substituting \((6, 14)\) into \(P = 7n - F\) gives \(14 = 7(6) - F = 42 - F\), so the fixed cost is \(F = 42 - 14 = \$28\).

qs.q: Chloe found that the relationship between the profit, P, which she made selling n jars of jam is linear. Suppose she made a profit of $11 on 8 jars, and $59 on 16 jars. Find the fixed cost of her equipment.
qs.s: The rate of profit per jar is \(m = \frac{59 - 11}{16 - 8} = \frac{48}{8} = 6\). Substituting \((8, 11)\) into \(P = 6n - F\) gives \(11 = 6(8) - F = 48 - F\), resulting in a fixed cost of \(F = 48 - 11 = \$37\).

qs.q: Liam found that the relationship between the profit, P, which he made selling n custom T-shirts is linear. Suppose he made a profit of $25 on 5 T-shirts, and $115 on 15 T-shirts. Find the fixed startup cost.
qs.s: The rate of profit per T-shirt is \(m = \frac{115 - 25}{15 - 5} = \frac{90}{10} = 9\). Substituting \((5, 25)\) into \(P = 9n - F\) gives \(25 = 9(5) - F = 45 - F\), so the fixed startup cost is \(F = 45 - 25 = \$20\).

qs.q: Marcus found that the relationship between the profit, P, which he made selling n birdhouses is linear. Suppose he made a profit of $10 on 4 birdhouses, and $58 on 10 birdhouses. Find the fixed cost of his materials.
qs.s: The rate of profit per birdhouse is \(m = \frac{58 - 10}{10 - 4} = \frac{48}{6} = 8\). Using \((4, 10)\) in \(P = 8n - F\), we get \(10 = 8(4) - F = 32 - F\), which gives a fixed cost of \(F = 32 - 10 = \$22\).

qs.q: A furniture maker found that the relationship between the profit, P, which he made selling n dining tables is linear. Suppose he made a profit of -$600 on 8 tables, and $2900 on 22 tables. Find the fixed cost of his workshop.

Samantha found that the relationship between the profit, P, which she made selling n enamel pins is linear. Suppose she made a profit of $34 on 24 pins, and $151 on 60 pins. Find the fixed cost of the mold.

A food truck owner found that the relationship between the weekly profit, P, and the number of burgers sold, n, is linear. Suppose the profit was $310 on 120 burgers, and $750 on 200 burgers. Find the weekly fixed operating cost.

A bicycle workshop found that the relationship between the profit, P, which it made selling n custom bicycles is linear. Suppose the workshop made a profit of $1200 on 15 bicycles, and $4600 on 35 bicycles. Find the fixed cost of the workshop tools.

A tech startup found that the relationship between the monthly profit, P, and the number of software subscriptions sold, n, is linear. The company had a profit of -$800 on 50 subscriptions, and a profit of $5200 on 150 subscriptions. Find the monthly fixed operating cost.
A caterer found that the relationship between the total cost, C, and the number of guests, n, is linear. The cost is $350 for 20 guests, and $800 for 50 guests. Find the cost for 80 guests.
qs.s: The rate per guest is (800 - 350) / (50 - 20) = $15, giving the linear relation C = 15n + 50. For 80 guests, the cost is 15(80) + 50 = $1250.

qs.q: A water tank is draining at a constant rate, so the volume of water remaining is linearly related to time. After 4 minutes, there are 260 liters left, and after 9 minutes, there are 185 liters left. Find the volume of water remaining after 15 minutes.
qs.s: The draining rate is (185 - 260) / (9 - 4) = -15 L/min, so the volume is V = 320 - 15t. At t = 15 minutes, the volume remaining is 320 - 15(15) = 95 liters.

qs.q: The total cost of printing custom shirts is linearly related to the number of shirts ordered. An order of 10 shirts costs $110, while an order of 25 shirts costs $215. Find the cost of ordering 40 shirts.
qs.s: The cost per shirt is (215 - 110) / (25 - 10) = $7, yielding the linear model C = 7n + 40. For 40 shirts, the cost is 7(40) + 40 = $320.

qs.q: A plumber charges a fixed fee plus an hourly rate, so the total bill is a linear function of time. A job taking 3 hours costs $175, and a job taking 6 hours costs $310. Find the cost for a job that takes 10 hours.
qs.s: The hourly rate is (310 - 175) / (6 - 3) = $45/h, so the linear equation is C = 45h + 40. For 10 hours, the cost is 45(10) + 40 = $490.

qs.q: A salesperson's weekly pay is linearly related to the number of items sold. Selling 8 items results in a weekly pay of $540, and selling 14 items results in a weekly pay of $690. Find the weekly pay for selling 20 items.
qs.s: The commission per sale is (690 - 540) / (14 - 8) = $25, giving weekly pay P = 25n + 340. For 20 sales, the pay is 25(20) + 340 = $840.

qs.q: A shipping company charges a base pickup fee plus a rate per kilogram, creating a linear cost model. Shipping a 45 kg crate costs $119, while shipping an 85 kg crate costs $199. What is the total cost to ship two separate crates weighing 60 kg and 90 kg?

The temperature inside a cooling chamber decreases linearly over time. At 6 minutes, the temperature is 47°C, and at 16 minutes, the temperature is 12°C. At what time will the temperature reach -23°C?
qs.s: The rate of temperature change is (12 - 47) / (16 - 6) = -3.5°C/min, giving T = -3.5t + 68. Setting T = -23 gives -3.5t = -91, which yields t = 26 minutes.

qs.q: A company's total profit, P, is linearly related to the number of units, x, sold. Selling 80 units results in a loss of $600 (a profit of -$600), and selling 200 units results in a profit of $3000. How many units must be sold to earn a profit of $7500?
qs.s: The slope is (3000 - (-600)) / (200 - 80) = 30, giving the profit equation P = 30x - 3000. Setting P = 7500 gives 30x = 10500, so x = 350 units.

qs.q: An event hall charges a rental fee that is linearly related to the number of attendees. For 40 attendees, the total charge is $1450, and for 75 attendees, the total charge is $2325. If an organization was billed a total of $3700, how many attendees were at their event?
qs.s: The rate is (2325 - 1450) / (75 - 40) = $25 per attendee, giving C = 25n + 450. Setting C = 3700 gives 25n + 450 = 3700, which solves to n = 130 attendees.

qs.q: An airplane cruises at a constant altitude, and its total weight decreases linearly as fuel burns. At 1.5 hours of flight, the aircraft weighs 38,200 kg, and at 4 hours, it weighs 34,700 kg. What is the total flight time when the aircraft reaches its minimum safe weight of 30,500 kg?
qs.s: The burn rate is (34700 - 38200) / (4 - 1.5) = -1400 kg/h, giving W = 40300 - 1400t. Setting W = 30500 gives 1400t = 9800, so the total flight time is t = 7 hours.

qs.q: Maya found that the relationship between the profit, \(P\) (in dollars), which she made selling \(n\) printed t-shirts is linear. Suppose she made a profit of $20 on 6 t-shirts, and $80 on 18 t-shirts. Find the range of the profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{80 - 20}{18 - 6} = 5\), and the fixed cost gives an intercept of \(P(0) = 20 - 5(6) = -10\). With domain \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\), the range is \(\{-10, -5, 0, 5, \dots\}\).

qs.q: Liam found that the relationship between the profit, \(P\) (in dollars), which he made selling \(n\) ceramic mugs is linear. Suppose he made a profit of $12 on 4 mugs, and $66 on 10 mugs. Find the range of the profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{66 - 12}{10 - 4} = 9\), and the intercept is \(P(0) = 12 - 9(4) = -24\). For \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\), the profit values are \(-24, -15, -6, 3, \dots\), so the range is \(\{-24, -15, -6, 3, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A community center finds that the total cost, \(C\) (in dollars), to host an event for \(n\) attendees is linear. Suppose the cost is $74 for 8 attendees, and $116 for 14 attendees. Find the range of the cost, \(C\).
qs.s: The rate per attendee is \(m = \frac{116 - 74}{14 - 8} = 7\), and the base fee is \(C(0) = 74 - 7(8) = 18\). For whole numbers of attendees \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\), the range is \(\{18, 25, 32, 39, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A food truck vendor found that the relationship between the daily profit, \(P\) (in dollars), and the number of combo meals sold, \(n\), is linear. Suppose the vendor made a profit of $25 on 5 meals, and $145 on 20 meals. Find the range of the profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{145 - 25}{20 - 5} = 8\), so the initial value is \(P(0) = 25 - 8(5) = -15\). Since \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\), the range is \(\{-15, -7, 1, 9, \dots\}\).

qs.q: Carlos found that the relationship between the profit, \(P\) (in dollars), which he made selling \(n\) wooden birdhouses is linear. Suppose he made a profit of $16 on 4 birdhouses, and $76 on 14 birdhouses. Find the range of the profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{76 - 16}{14 - 4} = 6\), giving an intercept of \(P(0) = 16 - 6(4) = -8\). Evaluating \(P(n) = 6n - 8\) for \(n = 0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\) gives the range \(\{-8, -2, 4, 10, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A student council sells notebooks for a school fundraiser. The relationship between the profit, \(P\) (in dollars), and the number of notebooks sold, \(n\), is linear. Selling 20 notebooks results in a loss of $30 (a profit of \(-\$30\)), and selling 60 notebooks results in a profit of $70. Find the range of the profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{70 - (-30)}{60 - 20} = \frac{100}{40} = 2.5\), so the intercept is \(P(0) = -30 - 2.5(20) = -80\). Evaluating \(P(n) = 2.5n - 80\) for whole numbers \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\) gives the range \(\{-80, -77.5, -75, -72.5, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A catering company's total fee, \(C\) (in dollars), depends linearly on the number of guests, \(g\). An event with 15 guests costs $425, and an event with 35 guests costs $825. If a host has a maximum budget of $1225, what is the domain of the number of guests, \(g\)?
qs.s: The cost per guest is \(m = \frac{825 - 425}{35 - 15} = 20\), and the fixed fee is \(C(0) = 425 - 20(15) = 125\), giving \(C(g) = 20g + 125\). Setting \(20g + 125 \le 1225\) yields \(20g \le 1100\), so \(g \le 55\), meaning the domain is \(\{0, 1, 2, \dots, 55\}\).

qs.q: A vintage watch was purchased 5 years ago, and its value, \(V\) (in dollars), has been increasing linearly with time, \(t\), where \(t\) is the number of years from today (\(t = 0\) represents today). Two years ago (\(t = -2\)), the watch was valued at $520. In 3 years (\(t = 3\)), it will be valued at $720. Find the range of the watch's value, \(V\).
qs.s: The annual increase is \(m = \frac{720 - 520}{3 - (-2)} = 40\), giving a current value of \(V(0) = 520 - 40(-2) = 600\). Because the watch was purchased at \(t = -5\), the domain begins at \(-5\) with initial value \(V(-5) = 600 + 40(-5) = 400\), producing the range \(\{400, 440, 480, 520, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A community theatre's profit, \(P\) (in dollars), is a linear function of the number of tickets sold, \(t\). Selling 25 tickets results in a profit of $50, and selling 60 tickets results in a profit of $470. If the theatre has a maximum seating capacity of 100 tickets, what is the range of the profit, \(P\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{470 - 50}{60 - 25} = 12\), and \(P(0) = 50 - 12(25) = -250\). The domain is restricted to \(t \in \{0, 1, 2, \dots, 100\}\), so the maximum profit is \(P(100) = 12(100) - 250 = 950\), giving the finite range \(\{-250, -238, -226, \dots, 950\}\).

qs.q: A small business finds that the relationship between its weekly profit, \(P\) (in dollars), and the number of items sold, \(n\), is linear. The business operated at a loss of $120 (a profit of \(-\$120\)) when selling 8 items, and made a profit of $360 when selling 24 items. Find the range of the weekly profit, \(P\).
qs.s: The rate of profit is \(m = \frac{360 - (-120)}{24 - 8} = \frac{480}{16} = 30\), which gives \(P(0) = -120 - 30(8) = -360\). For \(n \in \{0, 1, 2, 3, \dots\}\), the profit starts at \(-360\) and increases by \(30\), yielding the range \(\{-360, -330, -300, -270, \dots\}\).

qs.q: A catering service charges a flat setup fee plus a fixed cost per guest. For 20 guests, the total cost is $260, and for 30 guests, the total cost is $360. If the cost is linearly related to the number of guests, what is the total cost for 50 guests?
qs.s: The cost per guest is \((360 - 260) / (30 - 20) = \$10\). For 20 additional guests beyond 30, the cost increases by \(20 \times \$10 = \$200\), making the total cost \(360 + 200 = \$560\).

qs.q: A water tank is draining at a constant rate. After 3 hours, 450 L of water remain in the tank, and after 7 hours, 250 L remain. Assuming a linear relationship, how many liters will remain in the tank after 9 hours?
qs.s: The rate of drainage is \((250 - 450) / (7 - 3) = -50\text{ L/h}\). In the 2 hours between hour 7 and hour 9, another \(100\text{ L}\) drains out, leaving \(250 - 100 = 150\text{ L}\).

qs.q: After burning for 2 hours, a candle is 14 cm tall. After burning for 5 hours, it is 8 cm tall. Assuming the candle burns at a constant rate, what will its height be after burning for 7 hours?
qs.s: The burn rate is \((8 - 14) / (5 - 2) = -2\text{ cm/h}\). After 2 more hours of burning (from 5 to 7 hours), the candle burns another \(4\text{ cm}\), leaving a height of \(8 - 4 = 4\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: At a price of $3 per cup, a lemonade stand sells 15 cups per day. When the price is lowered to $2 per cup, it sells 25 cups per day. Assuming a linear relationship between price and sales, how many cups will the stand sell per day if the price is lowered to $1 per cup?
qs.s: The rate of change is \((25 - 15) / (2 - 3) = -10\) cups per dollar. Lowering the price by another $1 (from $2 to $1) increases daily sales by \(10\) cups, giving \(25 + 10 = 35\) cups.

qs.q: When a bakery prices a specialty loaf of bread at $5, it sells 30 loaves each morning. When it raises the price to $7, it sells 18 loaves. Assuming sales depend linearly on price, how many loaves will the bakery sell if the price is set at $8?
qs.s: The rate of change is \((18 - 30) / (7 - 5) = -6\) loaves per dollar. Increasing the price by $1 (from $7 to $8) reduces sales by \(6\) loaves, giving \(18 - 6 = 12\) loaves.

qs.q: When a community theater charges $15 per ticket, an average of 220 people attend a show. When the ticket price is increased to $20, average attendance drops to 170 people. Assuming a linear relationship between price and attendance, at what ticket price would attendance drop to zero?
qs.s: The rate of change is \((170 - 220) / (20 - 15) = -10\) attendees per dollar. Dropping attendance from 170 to 0 requires losing 170 attendees, which corresponds to a price increase of \(170 / 10 = \$17\), giving a ticket price of \(20 + 17 = \$37\).

qs.q: The water level in a municipal reservoir drops at a constant rate during peak usage. At 1:00 p.m., the water level is 42.5 m, and at 4:00 p.m., it is 33.5 m. If the water level continues to decrease at this rate, at what time will it reach 12.5 m?
qs.s: The rate of drop is \((33.5 - 42.5) / 3 = -3\text{ m/h}\). Dropping from \(33.5\text{ m}\) to \(12.5\text{ m}\) is a decrease of \(21\text{ m}\), which takes \(21 / 3 = 7\text{ hours}\), making the time \(4{:}00\text{ p.m.} + 7\text{ hours} = 11{:}00\text{ p.m.}\)

qs.q: A sales representative earns a base monthly salary plus a constant commission percentage on all sales. In March, her sales were $12,000 and her total earnings were $3,100. In April, her sales were $18,000 and her total earnings were $3,700. How much must her sales be in May if she wants to earn $4,500?

A custom print shop charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant price per brochure. An order of 400 brochures costs $190, and an order of 750 brochures costs $295. What is the total cost for an order of 1,200 brochures?

An airplane consumes fuel at a constant rate during flight. After 2 hours of flight, 26,400 L of fuel remain in its tanks, and after 5 hours, 19,200 L remain. At this rate, after how many total hours from takeoff will the fuel tanks be completely empty?
qs.s: The fuel consumption rate is \((19{,}200 - 26{,}400) / (5 - 2) = -2{,}400\text{ L/h}\), so the initial fuel was \(26{,}400 + 2(2{,}400) = 31{,}200\text{ L}\). Dividing total capacity by the hourly burn rate gives \(31{,}200 / 2{,}400 = 13\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: When tickets to a school play were priced at $9, 30 tickets were sold. When the price was reduced to $6, 42 tickets were sold. Assuming a linear relationship, what would the ticket price have been if only 20 tickets were sold?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{6 - 9}{42 - 30} = -0.25\) dollars per ticket. Using \((30, 9)\), the price for 20 tickets is \(p = 9 + (-0.25)(20 - 30) = 9 + 2.50 = \$11.50\).

qs.q: When the price of a cup of lemonade was $3, a stand sold 8 cups per hour. When the price was reduced to $2, the stand sold 12 cups per hour. Assuming a linear relationship, what would the price have been if the stand sold only 6 cups in an hour?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{2 - 3}{12 - 8} = -0.25\) dollars per cup. Using \((8, 3)\), the price for 6 cups is \(p = 3 + (-0.25)(6 - 8) = 3 + 0.50 = \$3.50\).

qs.q: When a farmer sold baskets of strawberries for $10 each, 14 baskets were sold per day. When the price was reduced to $7 each, 20 baskets were sold per day. Assuming a linear relationship, what would the price per basket have been if only 9 baskets were sold in a day?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{7 - 10}{20 - 14} = -0.50\) dollars per basket. Using \((14, 10)\), the price for 9 baskets is \(p = 10 + (-0.50)(9 - 14) = 10 + 2.50 = \$12.50\).

qs.q: When the admission to a community pool was $8, there were 10 swimmers. When the admission was reduced to $5, there were 22 swimmers. Assuming a linear relationship, what would the admission have been if there were only 4 swimmers?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{5 - 8}{22 - 10} = -0.25\) dollars per swimmer. Using \((10, 8)\), the admission for 4 swimmers is \(p = 8 + (-0.25)(4 - 10) = 8 + 1.50 = \$9.50\).

qs.q: When a bakery priced a muffin at $5, it sold 10 muffins each morning. When the price was lowered to $3, it sold 18 muffins each morning. Assuming a linear relationship, what was the price of a muffin if the bakery sold only 8 muffins in a morning?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{3 - 5}{18 - 10} = -0.25\) dollars per muffin. Using \((10, 5)\), the price for 8 muffins is \(p = 5 + (-0.25)(8 - 10) = 5 + 0.50 = \$5.50\).

qs.q: A commercial printing press decreases in value at a constant linear rate. Four years after purchase, its value was appraised at $38,000. Seven years after purchase, its appraised value was $27,500. How many years after purchase will the printing press have a value of $6,500?
qs.s: The rate of depreciation is \(m = \frac{27,500 - 38,000}{7 - 4} = -3,500\) dollars per year, so \(V = 38,000 - 3,500(t - 4) = 52,000 - 3,500t\). Setting \(V = 6,500\) gives \(3,500t = 45,500\), which yields \(t = 13\) years.

qs.q: An online retailer sells custom phone cases. When the price is set at $16.50, weekly sales are 420 cases. When the price is raised to $19.00, sales fall to 320 cases. Assuming a linear relationship, what price should the retailer charge to sell 550 cases in a week?

A software company notices that when a subscription is priced at $36 per year, 1,400 users subscribe. When the price is raised to $48 per year, the number of subscribers drops to 1,100. Assuming a linear relationship, at what annual subscription price would the number of subscribers drop to zero?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{1100 - 1400}{48 - 36} = -25\) subscribers per dollar, giving the equation \(n = -25(p - 36) + 1400 = -25p + 2300\). Setting \(n = 0\) gives \(25p = 2300\), so \(p = \$92\).

qs.q: A concert venue charges $45 per ticket and sells 600 tickets. When the ticket price is increased to $55, ticket sales drop to 440 tickets. Assuming a linear relationship between ticket price and attendance, what ticket price would result in an attendance of 300 people?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{55 - 45}{440 - 600} = -0.0625\) dollars per ticket. For an attendance of 300, the price is \(p = 45 + (-0.0625)(300 - 600) = 45 + 18.75 = \$63.75\).

qs.q: A freight shipping company charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per pound. Shipping a 120-pound crate costs $185, while shipping a 280-pound crate costs $329. If a customer is billed $455 for a single shipment, what was the weight of the crate?
qs.s: The rate per pound is \(m = \frac{329 - 185}{280 - 120} = 0.90\) dollars per pound, and the flat fee is \(185 - 0.90(120) = \$77\). Solving \(455 = 0.90w + 77\) gives \(0.90w = 378\), so \(w = 420\) pounds.

qs.q: A student council sells hoodies for a fundraiser. When hoodies are priced at $45 each, they sell 30 hoodies. When the price is reduced to $35 each, they sell 55 hoodies. Assuming the relationship is linear, what should the price be to sell 45 hoodies?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{35 - 45}{55 - 30} = -0.40\) dollars per hoodie. For 45 hoodies, the price is \(45 + (-0.40)(45 - 30) = 45 - 6 = \$39\).

qs.q: A bookstore sells a popular novel. When the novel is priced at $28, they sell 15 copies per day. When the price is lowered to $16, they sell 35 copies per day. Assuming a linear relationship, what should the price be to sell 20 copies per day?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{16 - 28}{35 - 15} = -0.60\) dollars per copy. To sell 20 copies, the price should be \(28 + (-0.60)(20 - 15) = 28 - 3 = \$25\).

qs.q: When tickets to a community play are priced at $60 each, 20 people attend. When the ticket price is reduced to $40 each, 60 people attend. Assuming a linear relationship, what should the ticket price be for 45 people to attend?
qs.s: The rate of price change is \(\frac{40 - 60}{60 - 20} = -0.50\) dollars per person. For 45 people, the price should be \(60 + (-0.50)(45 - 20) = 60 - 12.50 = \$47.50\).

qs.q: When running shoes are priced at $120, a sports shop sells 14 pairs per week. When the price is reduced to $90, the shop sells 26 pairs per week. Assuming a linear relationship, what should the price be to sell 22 pairs in a week?
qs.s: The slope is \(\frac{90 - 120}{26 - 14} = -2.50\) dollars per pair. For 22 pairs, the price is \(120 + (-2.50)(22 - 14) = 120 - 20 = \$100\).

qs.q: A bakery finds that when a specialty cake is priced at $32, they sell 6 cakes per day. When the price is lowered to $20, they sell 10 cakes per day. Assuming a linear relationship, what should the price be to sell 9 cakes per day?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{20 - 32}{10 - 6} = -3\) dollars per cake. For 9 cakes, the price should be \(32 + (-3)(9 - 6) = 32 - 9 = \$23\).

qs.q: A fitness club charges a monthly membership fee. When the monthly fee is $48, the club maintains 620 active members. When the fee is raised to $60, membership decreases to 500 active members. Assuming the relationship is linear, how many active members will the club have if the fee is set to $66 per month?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{60 - 48}{500 - 620} = -0.10\) dollars per member. Increasing the price from $60 to $66 requires a change of \(\Delta n = \frac{66 - 60}{-0.10} = -60\) members, resulting in \(500 - 60 = 440\) members.

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir is being drained at a constant rate. After 6 hours of draining, the reservoir holds 45,000 liters. After 14 hours, it holds 29,000 liters. Assuming the relationship between time and remaining volume is linear, after how many total hours of draining will the reservoir be completely empty?
qs.s: The drainage rate is \(\frac{29\,000 - 45\,000}{14 - 6} = -2000\text{ L/h}\), so the initial volume at \(t = 0\) is \(45\,000 + 2000(6) = 57\,000\text{ L}\). Setting the volume to 0 yields \(t = \frac{57\,000}{2000} = 28.5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A distributor of solar panels finds that when panels are priced at $420 each, contractors buy 150 panels per week. When the price is reduced to $360 each, contractors buy 225 panels per week. Assuming a linear relationship, what price per panel should be set to sell 310 panels per week?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(\frac{360 - 420}{225 - 150} = -0.80\) dollars per panel. For 310 panels, the price should be \(360 + (-0.80)(310 - 225) = 360 - 68 = \$292\).

qs.q: A courier service determines that shipping a 12 kg parcel costs $54.40, while shipping a 20 kg parcel costs $78.40. Assuming the cost is a linear function of the parcel's weight, what is the weight of a parcel that costs exactly $100 to ship?
