qs.s: The cost per kilogram is \(\frac{78.40 - 54.40}{20 - 12} = \$3.00/\text{kg}\). For a total cost of $100, the weight is \(20 + \frac{100 - 78.40}{3.00} = 20 + 7.2 = 27.2\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: An electronics retailer sells a 55-inch television. When priced at $680, the store sells 25 units per month. When the price is discounted to $560, monthly sales increase to 55 units. Assuming a linear relationship between price and sales, how many units will the store sell in a month if the price is set to $480?
qs.s: The slope is \(\frac{560 - 680}{55 - 25} = -4\) dollars per unit. Setting the price to $480 gives \(480 - 560 = -4(n - 55)\), which simplifies to \(-80 = -4(n - 55)\), so \(n = 55 + 20 = 75\) units.

qs.q: When loaves of bread sell for $12 each, a bakery sells 15 loaves per day. When the price is reduced to $6 each, 33 loaves are sold per day. Assuming a linear relationship, how many loaves would the bakery expect to sell in a day if the price were $8 each?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{33 - 15}{6 - 12} = -3\) loaves per dollar. At a price of $8, the expected sales are \(n = 33 - 3(8 - 6) = 27\) loaves.

qs.q: When ceramic mugs are priced at $16 each, an artisan sells 9 mugs per day. When they are priced at $10 each, 18 mugs are sold per day. Assuming a linear relationship, how many mugs would the artisan expect to sell per day if the price were $12 each?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{18 - 9}{10 - 16} = -1.5\) mugs per dollar. At a price of $12, the expected daily sales are \(n = 18 - 1.5(12 - 10) = 15\) mugs.

qs.q: When a paperback novel sells for $20, a bookstore sells 12 copies each week. When the price is discounted to $14, 21 copies are sold each week. Assuming a linear relationship, how many copies would the bookstore expect to sell in a week if the price were set at $16?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{21 - 12}{14 - 20} = -1.5\) copies per dollar. At a price of $16, the expected sales are \(n = 21 - 1.5(16 - 14) = 18\) copies.

qs.q: When hats sell for $25 each, 10 of them are sold each day. When the hats are on sale for $15 each, 30 hats are sold each day. Assuming a linear relationship, how many hats would the store expect to sell in a day if the price were $18 each?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{30 - 10}{15 - 25} = -2\) hats per dollar, giving the relation \(n - 10 = -2(p - 25)\). For \(p = 18\), the expected sales are \(n = 10 - 2(18 - 25) = 24\) hats.

qs.q: When phone cases are sold for $24 each, a kiosk sells 7 cases per day. When the cases are discounted to $12 each, 15 cases are sold per day. Assuming a linear relationship, how many phone cases would the kiosk expect to sell per day if the price were $15 each?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{15 - 7}{12 - 24} = -\frac{2}{3}\) cases per dollar. For a price of $15, the expected sales are \(n = 15 - \frac{2}{3}(15 - 12) = 13\) cases.

qs.q: A food truck sells 140 gourmet burgers per day when priced at $8.50 each. When the price is raised to $11.00 each, daily sales drop to 90 burgers. Assuming a linear relationship between price and sales, what price should the food truck set to sell exactly 116 burgers per day?

A concert venue charges $45 per ticket and sells 1800 tickets. When the ticket price is increased to $60, sales drop to 1200 tickets. Assuming attendance is linearly related to ticket price, how many tickets would the venue expect to sell if the ticket price were set at $72?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{1200 - 1800}{60 - 45} = -40\) tickets per dollar. Evaluating at \(p = 72\) gives \(n = 1200 - 40(72 - 60) = 720\) tickets.

qs.q: At a price of $120 each, a manufacturer sells 350 bicycles per month. When the price is raised to $160 each, monthly sales drop to 270 bicycles. Assuming a linear relationship, at what price would monthly sales be expected to drop to zero?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{270 - 350}{160 - 120} = -2\) bicycles per dollar, giving the linear relation \(n - 350 = -2(p - 120)\). Setting \(n = 0\) gives \(0 = -2p + 590\), so \(p = \$295\).

qs.q: When an annual software subscription is priced at $180, a company sells 520 subscriptions per week. When the price is increased to $220, sales decrease to 440 subscriptions per week. Assuming a linear relationship, how many more subscriptions per week would the company sell if the price were set at $150 compared to if it were set at $200?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{440 - 520}{220 - 180} = -2\) subscriptions per dollar. The difference in sales for a price difference of \(200 - 150 = 50\) dollars is \(|-2 \times (-50)| = 100\) subscriptions.

qs.q: At an electronics store, when a tablet is priced at $350, the store sells 40 units per month. When the price is reduced to $275, monthly sales increase to 70 units. Assuming a linear relationship between price and sales, at what price should the store sell the tablet to achieve monthly sales of 90 units?
qs.s: The rate of change of price with respect to sales is \(m = \frac{275 - 350}{70 - 40} = -2.5\) dollars per unit. For \(n = 90\) units, the price must be \(p = 275 - 2.5(90 - 70) = \$225\).

exercises.name: Finding slope and y-intercept from standard form

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line: \(3x + 4y = -24\)
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) yields \(4y = -3x - 24\), or \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x - 6\). Therefore, the y-intercept is \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(5x - 6y = 18\)
qs.s: Rewriting the equation gives \(-6y = -5x + 18\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - 3\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(4x - 3y = 12\)
qs.s: Rewriting the equation in slope-intercept form gives \(-3y = -4x + 12\), or \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 4\). Thus, the slope is \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(2x + 5y = 15\)
qs.s: Rewriting in slope-intercept form gives \(5y = -2x + 15\), or \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 3\). Thus, the slope is \(-\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line: \(5x - 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) gives \(-2y = -5x + 10\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - 5\). Therefore, the y-intercept is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line: \(5(x + 1) - 3(y - 4) = 8\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(5x + 5 - 3y + 12 = 8\), which simplifies to \(5x - 3y = -9\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{5}{3}x + 3\), so the y-intercept is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line: \(7x - 5y + 11 = 3x + 3y - 21\)
qs.s: Combining like terms gives \(4x - 8y = -32\), which rearranges to \(-8y = -4x - 32\). Dividing by \(-8\) gives \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 4\), so the y-intercept is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(18x - 42y = 63\)
qs.s: Rewriting the equation gives \(-42y = -18x + 63\), so \(y = \frac{-18}{-42}x - \frac{63}{42}\). Simplifying the fraction \(\frac{18}{42}\) by dividing numerator and denominator by 6 yields a slope of \(\frac{3}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{2}{5}y = 6\)
qs.s: Multiplying the entire equation by \(20\) clears the fractions to give \(15x - 8y = 120\). Solving for \(y\) yields \(y = \frac{15}{8}x - 15\), so the slope is \(\frac{15}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{5}{12}y = 2\)
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD of \(24\) yields \(9x + 10y = 48\), which rearranges to \(10y = -9x + 48\). Dividing by \(10\) gives \(y = -\frac{9}{10}x + \frac{24}{5}\), so the slope is \(-\frac{9}{10}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(5x - 3y = 9\).
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(-3y = -5x + 9\), then divide by \(-3\) to obtain \(y = \frac{5}{3}x - 3\). The slope of the line is \(\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2x + 7y = 14\).
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to get \(7y = -2x + 14\), then divide by \(7\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{2}{7}x + 2\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{2}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(5x + 2y = 10\).
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(2y = -5x + 10\), then divide by \(2\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 5\). The slope is the coefficient of \(x\), which is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(6x + 5y = 15\).
qs.s: Subtract \(6x\) from both sides to get \(5y = -6x + 15\), then divide by \(5\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{6}{5}x + 3\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{6}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(3x - 4y = 12\).
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) from both sides to get \(-4y = -3x + 12\), then divide by \(-4\) to obtain \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\). The slope of the line is \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(7x - 2y + 9 = 3x + 4y - 3\).
qs.s: Rearrange the terms by subtracting \(4y\), \(7x\), and \(9\) from both sides to obtain \(-6y = -4x - 12\). Dividing by \(-6\) gives \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + 2\), so the slope is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(28x - 16y = 45\).
qs.s: Subtract \(28x\) from both sides to get \(-16y = -28x + 45\). Divide by \(-16\) to obtain \(y = \frac{28}{16}x - \frac{45}{16} = \frac{7}{4}x - \frac{45}{16}\), giving a slope of \(\frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2(3x - y) + 5 = 4(x - 2y) - 7\).
qs.s: Expand both sides to get \(6x - 2y + 5 = 4x - 8y - 7\), then collect like terms to obtain \(6y = -2x - 12\). Dividing by \(6\) yields \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x - 2\), so the slope is \(-\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{3}{4}y = 1\).
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{2}{5}x\) from both sides to get \(\frac{3}{4}y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 1\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{4}{3}\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{8}{15}x + \frac{4}{3}\), so the slope is \(-\frac{8}{15}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2(x - 3) - 7(y - 1) = 5 - 3x\).
qs.s: Expand the equation to \(2x - 6 - 7y + 7 = 5 - 3x\), which simplifies to \(2x - 7y + 1 = 5 - 3x\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(-7y = -5x + 4\), or \(y = \frac{5}{7}x - \frac{4}{7}\), so the slope is \(\frac{5}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line \(5x + 2y = -9\).
qs.s: Solve for \(y\) to convert the equation to slope-intercept form: \(2y = -5x - 9\), which gives \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x - \frac{9}{2}\). The y-intercept is -\frac{9}{2}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(7x - 3y = 8\).
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) to put the equation in slope-intercept form: \(-3y = -7x + 8\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{7}{3}x - \frac{8}{3}\). Therefore, the slope is \frac{7}{3}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(3x - 4y = -10\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form by solving for \(y\): \(-4y = -3x - 10\), which gives \(y = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}\). The slope is the coefficient of \(x\), which is \frac{3}{4}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2x - 7y = -5\).
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to get \(-7y = -2x - 5\), then divide by \(-7\) to obtain \(y = \frac{2}{7}x + \frac{5}{7}\). The slope is \frac{2}{7}.

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line \(4x + 5y = 11\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation by solving for \(y\): \(5y = -4x + 11\), which yields \(y = -\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{11}{5}\). The y-intercept is \frac{11}{5}.

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line given by the equation \(8x - 7y + 9 = 2x + 4y - 15\).
qs.s: Group like terms on each side to get \(-11y = -6x - 24\). Dividing by \(-11\) gives \(y = \frac{6}{11}x + \frac{24}{11}\), so the y-intercept is \frac{24}{11}.

qs.q: Find the y-intercept of the line given by the equation \(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{5}y = \frac{7}{10}\).
qs.s: Multiply all terms by the common denominator 30 to clear fractions, obtaining \(20x - 18y = 21\). Solving for \(y\) yields \(y = \frac{10}{9}x - \frac{7}{6}\), so the y-intercept is -\frac{7}{6}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line given by the equation \(\frac{2x - 1}{3} - \frac{3y + 4}{5} = 2\).
qs.s: Multiply the entire equation by 15 to clear the denominators, giving \(5(2x - 1) - 3(3y + 4) = 30\). Expanding yields \(10x - 9y - 17 = 30\), or \(-9y = -10x + 47\), which results in a slope of \frac{10}{9}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line given by the equation \(4(2x - 3y) - 3(x - 5y) = 14\).
qs.s: Expand and combine like terms to get \(8x - 12y - 3x + 15y = 14\), which simplifies to \(5x + 3y = 14\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x + \frac{14}{3}\), so the slope is -\frac{5}{3}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line given by the equation \(65x - 91y = 150\).
qs.s: Rearrange to slope-intercept form: \(-91y = -65x + 150\), so \(y = \frac{65}{91}x - \frac{150}{91}\). Dividing both the numerator and denominator by their greatest common factor, 13, gives a slope of \frac{5}{7}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(2x - 5y = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to get \(-5y = -2x\), then divide both sides by \(-5\) to obtain \(y = \frac{2}{5}x\). The slope is \(\frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(7x + 2y = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7x\) from both sides to get \(2y = -7x\), then divide by \(2\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{7}{2}x\). The slope is \(-\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(5x - 3y = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(-3y = -5x\), then divide by \(-3\) to find \(y = \frac{5}{3}x\). The slope is \(\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(4x + 7y = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract \(4x\) from both sides to get \(7y = -4x\), then divide by \(7\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{4}{7}x\). The slope is \(-\frac{4}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(3x + 4y = 0\)
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) from both sides to get \(4y = -3x\), then divide by \(4\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x\). The slope is \(-\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(\frac{2}{3}x - 4y = 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{2}{3}x\) from both sides to get \(-4y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 5\), then divide each term by \(-4\) to obtain \(y = \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{5}{4}\). The slope is \(\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(3(x - 2) + 5y = 8 - x\)
qs.s: Distribute on the left to get \(3x - 6 + 5y = 8 - x\), then isolate \(y\) to obtain \(5y = -4x + 14\). Dividing by \(5\) gives \(y = -\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{14}{5}\), so the slope is \(-\frac{4}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(15x + 18y = 7\)
qs.s: Subtract \(15x\) from both sides to get \(18y = -15x + 7\), then divide by \(18\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{15}{18}x + \frac{7}{18}\). Simplifying \(-\frac{15}{18}\) gives a slope of \(-\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}y = -1\)
qs.s: Multiply the entire equation by the common denominator \(12\) to get \(9x + 8y = -12\). Solving for \(y\) yields \(8y = -9x - 12\), or \(y = -\frac{9}{8}x - \frac{3}{2}\), giving a slope of \(-\frac{9}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line: \(7x - 2y = 3x + 6y - 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) and \(6y\) across the equation to collect like terms, giving \(-8y = -4x - 5\). Dividing by \(-8\) yields \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{8}\), so the slope is \(\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(x - 5y = 15\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form by solving for \(y\): \(-5y = -x + 15\), which gives \(y = \frac{1}{5}x - 3\). The \(y\)-intercept is \(-3\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(x - 2y = -8\).
qs.s: Solve for \(y\) to obtain \(-2y = -x - 8\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 4\). The \(y\)-intercept is \(4\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(x - 3y = -6\).
qs.s: Subtract \(x\) from both sides to get \(-3y = -x - 6\), then divide by \(-3\) to get \(y = \frac{1}{3}x + 2\). The slope of the line is \(\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(x + 6y = -12\).
qs.s: Subtract \(x\) from both sides to get \(6y = -x - 12\), then divide by \(6\) to get \(y = -\frac{1}{6}x - 2\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{1}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(x + 2y = 8\).
qs.s: Subtract \(x\) from both sides to get \(2y = -x + 8\), then divide by \(2\) to get \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 4\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{4}y = 2\).
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{2}{3}x\) from both sides to get \(\frac{1}{4}y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 2\), then multiply by \(4\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{8}{3}x + 8\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{8}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(20x + 16y = -35\).
qs.s: Subtract \(20x\) from both sides to get \(16y = -20x - 35\), then divide by \(16\) to get \(y = -\frac{5}{4}x - \frac{35}{16}\). The slope of the line is \(-\frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(\frac{3}{5}x - \frac{2}{3}y = 4\).
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{3}{5}x\) from both sides to get \(-\frac{2}{3}y = -\frac{3}{5}x + 4\), then multiply by \(-\frac{3}{2}\) to obtain \(y = \frac{9}{10}x - 6\). The \(y\)-intercept is \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the \(y\)-intercept of the line \(8x - 12y = -28\).
qs.s: Isolate the \(y\)-term to get \(-12y = -8x - 28\), then divide by \(-12\) to obtain \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{7}{3}\). The \(y\)-intercept is \(\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(15x - 6y = 20\).
qs.s: Subtract \(15x\) from both sides to get \(-6y = -15x + 20\), then divide by \(-6\) to get \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - \frac{10}{3}\). The slope of the line is \(\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(3x + y = -5\).
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) from both sides to write the equation in slope-intercept form: \(y = -3x - 5\). The slope of the line is the coefficient of \(x\), so \(m = -3\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(4x - y = 7\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form by solving for \(y\): \(-y = -4x + 7\), which gives \(y = 4x - 7\). The slope of the line is the coefficient of \(x\), so \(m = 4\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(7x - y = -2\).
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) to write the equation in slope-intercept form: \(-y = -7x - 2\), which gives \(y = 7x + 2\). The slope of the line is \(7\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2x - y = -8\).
qs.s: Solve for \(y\) to express the equation in slope-intercept form: \(-y = -2x - 8\), which simplifies to \(y = 2x + 8\). The slope of the line is \(2\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(5x + y = 9\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form by subtracting \(5x\) from both sides to get \(y = -5x + 9\). The slope of the line is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(7x - 4y = 2x + 15\).
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to combine like terms, giving \(5x - 4y = 15\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(-4y = -5x + 15\), or \(y = \frac{5}{4}x - \frac{15}{4}\), which has a slope of \(\frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(14x + 4y = 9\).
qs.s: Solve for \(y\) to write the equation in slope-intercept form: \(4y = -14x + 9\), so \(y = -\frac{14}{4}x + \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{7}{2}x + \frac{9}{4}\). The slope is \(-\frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(10x - 15y = 22\).
qs.s: Isolate the \(y\)-term by subtracting \(10x\): \(-15y = -10x + 22\). Dividing each term by \(-15\) yields \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{22}{15}\), so the slope is \frac{2}{3}.

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(2(x - 3y) + 5x = 11\).
qs.s: Expand the parentheses to get \(2x - 6y + 5x = 11\), and combine like terms to reach \(7x - 6y = 11\). Solving for \(y\) gives \(-6y = -7x + 11\), or \(y = \frac{7}{6}x - \frac{11}{6}\), so the slope is \(\frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of the line \(9x - 2y = 3x + 6y - 7\).
qs.s: Collect all variable terms on the left side by subtracting \(3x\) and \(6y\) to obtain \(6x - 8y = -7\). Solving for \(y\) yields \(-8y = -6x - 7\), so \(y = \frac{6}{8}x + \frac{7}{8} = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{7}{8}\), which has a slope of \(\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to obtain \(y = -5x + 12\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(3x + y = 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) from both sides of the equation to isolate \(y\): \(y = -3x + 5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(7x + y = -3\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(9x - 6y = 8\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(6x + 8y = -20\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(15x - 12y = -20\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x - y = -2\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(2x - y = 5\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(6x - y = 8\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(x - y = 7\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(18x - 24y = 42\)
qs.s: Subtract \(18x\) from both sides to get \(-24y = -18x + 42\), then divide each term by \(-24\) and simplify the fractions to obtain \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(14x + 8y = -20\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(8x - 6y = 15\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(30x + 24y = 45\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(25x - 15y = -18\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x + 4y = 20\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(3x + 5y = 20\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x + 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(2y = -5x + 10\), then divide every term by \(2\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(15x - 9y = 42\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(7x - 4y = -12\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7x\) to get \(-4y = -7x - 12\), then divide every term by \(-4\) to find \(y = \frac{7}{4}x + 3\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(9x - 6y = 24\)

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x - 2y = 8\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(-2y = -5x + 8\), then divide each term by \(-2\) to get \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - 4\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(4x - 5y = -15\)

qs.s: Subtract \(20x\) from both sides to get \(-14y = -20x + 35\), then divide each term by \(-14\) and reduce the fractions to obtain \(y = \frac{10}{7}x - \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(2x + 9y = 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to get \(9y = -2x + 5\), then divide each term by \(9\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{2}{9}x + \frac{5}{9}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(3x + 5y = 8\)
qs.s: Subtract \(3x\) from both sides to get \(5y = -3x + 8\), then divide each term by \(5\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{3}{5}x + \frac{8}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(4x + 7y = 9\)
qs.s: Subtract \(4x\) from both sides to get \(7y = -4x + 9\), then divide each term by \(7\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{9}{7}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(7x + 2y = 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7x\) from both sides to get \(2y = -7x + 5\), then divide each term by \(2\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{7}{2}x + \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x + 3y = 4\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(3y = -5x + 4\), then divide each term by \(3\) to obtain \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x + \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(36x - 48y = 20\)
qs.s: Subtract \(36x\) to get \(-48y = -36x + 20\). Dividing by \(-48\) and simplifying \(\frac{-36}{-48}\) to \(\frac{3}{4}\) and \(\frac{20}{-48}\) to \(-\frac{5}{12}\) results in \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(\frac{2}{3}x + 4y = 6\)
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{2}{3}x\) from both sides to obtain \(4y = -\frac{2}{3}x + 6\), then divide every term by \(4\) and simplify to get \(y = -\frac{1}{6}x + \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(21x - 14y = -35\)
qs.s: Subtract \(21x\) to get \(-14y = -21x - 35\). Dividing by \(-14\) and simplifying by dividing each numerator and denominator by \(7\) gives \(y = \frac{3}{2}x + \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(8x - 12y = 20\)
qs.s: Subtract \(8x\) from both sides to get \(-12y = -8x + 20\). Dividing each term by \(-12\) and simplifying fractions yields \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(15x + 18y = -24\)
qs.s: Subtract \(15x\) from both sides to get \(18y = -15x - 24\). Dividing each term by \(18\) and simplifying both fractions gives \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(5x + 3y = 6\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to obtain \(3y = -5x + 6\). Divide each term by \(3\) to get \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x + 2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(8x - 4y = 3\)
qs.s: Subtract \(8x\) from both sides to obtain \(-4y = -8x + 3\). Divide each term by \(-4\) to get \(y = 2x - \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(4x - 2y = 7\)
qs.s: Subtract \(4x\) from both sides to obtain \(-2y = -4x + 7\). Divide each term by \(-2\) to get \(y = 2x - \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(7x + 2y = 9\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7x\) from both sides to obtain \(2y = -7x + 9\). Divide each term by \(2\) to get \(y = -\frac{7}{2}x + \frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{4}{5}y = -\frac{8}{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply the entire equation by the common denominator \(15\) to obtain \(10x + 12y = -8\). Subtract \(10x\), divide by \(12\), and reduce to get \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(42x - 28y = 35\)
qs.s: Subtract \(42x\) from both sides to obtain \(-28y = -42x + 35\). Divide each term by \(-28\) and simplify each fraction to get \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(60x - 84y = -49\)
qs.s: Subtract \(60x\) from both sides to obtain \(-84y = -60x - 49\). Divide each term by \(-84\) and reduce \(\frac{60}{84}\) by \(12\) and \(\frac{49}{84}\) by \(7\) to obtain \(y = \frac{5}{7}x + \frac{7}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y = \frac{5}{6}\)
qs.s: Subtract \(\frac{3}{4}x\) from both sides to obtain \(-\frac{1}{2}y = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{6}\). Multiply every term by \(-2\) and simplify to get \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the standard form equation in slope-intercept form: \(45x - 75y = -60\)
qs.s: Subtract \(45x\) from both sides to obtain \(-75y = -45x - 60\). Divide each term by \(-75\) and reduce both fractions by dividing by \(15\) to get \(y = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{4}{5}\).

exercises.name: Converting slope-intercept form to standard form

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -x + 4\)
qs.s: Add \(x\) to both sides of the equation to arrive at \(x + y = 4\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -3x + 7\)
qs.s: Add \(3x\) to both sides of the equation to obtain \(3x + y = 7\), which is in standard form with \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -6x - 1\)
qs.s: Add \(6x\) to both sides to express the equation in standard form as \(6x + y = -1\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{3}{5}x + 2\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by \(5\) to clear the fraction, giving \(5y = -3x + 10\), then add \(3x\) to both sides to obtain \(3x + 5y = 10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x - \frac{5}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiply all terms by the least common denominator \(12\) to get \(12y = -21x - 10\), then add \(21x\) to both sides to arrive at \(21x + 12y = -10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 7\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by \(3\) to get \(3y = 4x - 21\), then rearrange into standard form to obtain \(4x - 3y = 21\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{1}{6}x - \frac{2}{9}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the common denominator \(18\) to get \(18y = 3x - 4\), then rearrange into standard form to find \(3x - 18y = 4\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + \frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator \(4\) to obtain \(4y = -10x + 3\), then add \(10x\) to both sides to get \(10x + 4y = 3\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -x - 8\)
qs.s: Add \(x\) to both sides to get \(x + y = -8\), which is already in standard form with \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 2x + 5\)
qs.s: Subtract \(2x\) from both sides to obtain \(-2x + y = 5\), then multiply by \(-1\) so that the coefficient of \(x\) is positive, giving \(2x - y = -5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 7x + 2\)
qs.s: Subtract \(7x\) from both sides to get \(-7x + y = 2\), then multiply through by \(-1\) so that the \(x\)-coefficient is positive, yielding \(7x - y = -2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 5x - 4\)
qs.s: Subtract \(5x\) from both sides to get \(-5x + y = -4\), then multiply each term by \(-1\) to ensure \(A \ge 0\), resulting in \(5x - y = 4\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -4x + 7\)
qs.s: Add \(4x\) to both sides to write the equation in standard form as \(4x + y = 7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{7}{10}x - \frac{4}{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the least common denominator, 30, to obtain \(30y = 21x - 8\), then rearrange into standard form to get \(21x - 30y = 8\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{1}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 6 to clear the denominators, yielding \(6y = 5x + 1\), then rearrange into standard form to get \(5x - 6y = -1\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator, 12, to obtain \(12y = -9x + 8\), then add \(9x\) to both sides to get \(9x + 12y = 8\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 5\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 4 to clear the fraction, giving \(4y = 3x - 20\), then rearrange to obtain \(3x - 4y = 20\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 3\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 5 to clear the fraction, giving \(5y = -2x + 15\), then add \(2x\) to both sides to obtain \(2x + 5y = 15\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 6x\)
qs.s: Subtract \(y\) from both sides to obtain \(6x - y = 0\) in standard form.

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -2x\)
qs.s: Add \(2x\) to both sides of the equation to obtain \(2x + y = 0\), which is in standard form with \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -5x\)
qs.s: Add \(5x\) to both sides to write the equation as \(5x + y = 0\), satisfying \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 7x\)
qs.s: Subtract \(y\) from both sides to get \(7x - y = 0\), where \(A = 7\), \(B = -1\), and \(C = 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 4x\)
qs.s: Subtract \(y\) from both sides of the equation to get \(4x - y = 0\). Since \(A = 4\) is positive, the equation is in standard form.

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x + 4\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by \(3\) to eliminate the fraction, resulting in \(3y = -5x + 12\). Adding \(5x\) to both sides gives \(5x + 3y = 12\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -6x + 11\)
qs.s: Add \(6x\) to both sides of the equation to obtain \(6x + y = 11\). The coefficients are integers with \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 2\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by \(4\) to clear the fraction, giving \(4y = 3x - 8\). Rearranging into standard form yields \(3x - 4y = 8\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator \(12\) to clear fractions: \(12y = -10x + 9\). Adding \(10x\) to both sides yields \(10x + 12y = 9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{7}{10}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the common denominator \(10\) to obtain \(10y = 4x - 7\). Rearranging gives \(4x - 10y = 7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{4}{5}x - 3\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 5 to obtain \(5y = -4x - 15\). Add \(4x\) to both sides to obtain \(4x + 5y = -15\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 5\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 2 to get \(2y = x - 10\). Subtract \(2y\) and add 10 to both sides to write it in standard form with \(A \geq 0\), yielding \(x - 2y = 10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{3}{5}x + 4\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 5 to clear the fraction, giving \(5y = 3x + 20\). Rearrange to standard form with \(A \geq 0\) to get \(3x - 5y = -20\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 7\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 2 to get \(2y = -5x + 14\). Add \(5x\) to both sides to obtain \(5x + 2y = 14\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{8}{15}x + \frac{7}{20}\)
qs.s: The least common denominator of 15 and 20 is 60. Multiplying every term by 60 gives \(60y = -32x + 21\), which rearranges to \(32x + 60y = 21\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{7}{12}x - \frac{5}{18}\)
qs.s: The least common denominator of 12 and 18 is 36. Multiplying every term by 36 yields \(36y = -21x - 10\), which gives \(21x + 36y = -10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{9}{14}x + \frac{5}{21}\)
qs.s: The least common denominator of 14 and 21 is 42. Multiplying every term by 42 gives \(42y = 27x + 10\), which rearranges to \(27x - 42y = -10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - 6\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by 2 to clear the fraction, giving \(2y = 5x - 12\). Rearrange the equation into standard form with \(A \ge 0\) to get \(5x - 2y = 12\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 4\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by 3 to obtain \(3y = -x + 12\). Add \(x\) to both sides so that the \(x\)-coefficient is positive, resulting in \(x + 3y = 12\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{3}{7}x - 2\)
qs.s: Multiply the entire equation by 7 to clear the fraction, giving \(7y = -3x - 14\). Add \(3x\) to both sides to obtain \(3x + 7y = -14\) with \(A \ge 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{7}{8}x - \frac{5}{12}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator, 24, to get \(24y = -21x - 10\). Add \(21x\) to both sides to obtain \(21x + 24y = -10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{11}{14}x + \frac{5}{21}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the least common denominator, 42, yielding \(42y = 33x + 10\). Subtract \(42y\) and 10 from both sides to obtain \(33x - 42y = -10\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{13}{18}x + \frac{7}{12}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the least common denominator, 36, to get \(36y = -26x + 21\). Add \(26x\) to both sides to write the equation in standard form with \(A \ge 0\), resulting in \(26x + 36y = 21\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{9}{10}x - \frac{7}{15}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator, 30, to get \(30y = 27x - 14\). Rearrange terms into standard form with \(A \ge 0\) to get \(27x - 30y = 14\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{7}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiply every term by the least common denominator, 12, to obtain \(12y = -10x + 21\). Add \(10x\) to both sides to write the equation in standard form with \(A \ge 0\), resulting in \(10x + 12y = 21\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{4}{5}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the common denominator 10 to obtain \(10y = -15x + 8\). Adding \(15x\) to both sides yields \(15x + 10y = 8\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{3}{5}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the common denominator 15 to obtain \(15y = 5x - 9\). Rearranging to standard form with \(A \ge 0\) gives \(5x - 15y = 9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = \frac{4}{7}x + \frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the common denominator 14 to get \(14y = 8x + 7\). Subtracting \(14y\) and 7 from both sides gives \(8x - 14y = -7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{1}{6}x - \frac{3}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the least common denominator 12 to get \(12y = -2x - 9\). Adding \(2x\) to both sides yields \(2x + 12y = -9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -0.45x + 1.2\)
qs.s: Convert the decimals to simplified fractions to get \(y = -\frac{9}{20}x + \frac{6}{5}\), then multiply by the LCD 20 to obtain \(20y = -9x + 24\). Adding \(9x\) to both sides gives \(9x + 20y = 24\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = 1\frac{5}{9}x - 2\frac{1}{6}\)
qs.s: Convert to improper fractions to obtain \(y = \frac{14}{9}x - \frac{13}{6}\), and multiply by the LCD 18 to get \(18y = 28x - 39\). Rearranging with \(A \ge 0\) yields \(28x - 18y = 39\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -2\frac{1}{4}x - 1\frac{5}{6}\)
qs.s: Convert the mixed numbers to improper fractions, \(y = -\frac{9}{4}x - \frac{11}{6}\), then multiply through by the LCD 12 to get \(12y = -27x - 22\). Adding \(27x\) to both sides produces \(27x + 12y = -22\).

qs.q: Rewrite the slope-intercept equation in standard form: \(y = -\frac{11}{24}x + \frac{7}{16}\)
qs.s: Multiply each term by the least common denominator 48 to get \(48y = -22x + 21\). Adding \(22x\) to both sides gives the standard form \(22x + 48y = 21\).

exercises.name: Converting point-slope form to slope-intercept form

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 6 = -3(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute the \(-3\) to get \(y - 6 = -3x + 6\), then add 6 to both sides to obtain \(y = -3x + 12\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 5 = 4(x - 1)\)
qs.s: Distribute the 4 to get \(y + 5 = 4x - 4\), then subtract 5 from both sides to obtain \(y = 4x - 9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 4 = 2(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute the 2 to get \(y - 4 = 2x - 6\), then add 4 to both sides to obtain \(y = 2x - 2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 3 = 5(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute the 5 to get \(y + 3 = 5x + 10\), then subtract 3 from both sides to obtain \(y = 5x + 7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 1 = -2(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute the \(-2\) to get \(y - 1 = -2x - 8\), then add 1 to both sides to obtain \(y = -2x - 7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{1}{2}\) to get \(y - \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{1}{2}x + 2\), then add \(\frac{2}{3}\) (with \(2 = \frac{6}{3}\)) to both sides to obtain \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{8}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 6 = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y + 6 = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{15}{4}\), then subtract 6 (or \(\frac{24}{4}\)) from both sides to obtain \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{39}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{5}(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{5}\) to get \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{6}{5}\), then add 4 (or \(\frac{20}{5}\)) to both sides to obtain \(y = \frac{2}{5}x + \frac{14}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{5}{2} = -\frac{7}{3}(x - 6)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{7}{3}\) to get \(y + \frac{5}{2} = -\frac{7}{3}x + 14\), then subtract \(\frac{5}{2}\) to find \(14 - \frac{5}{2} = \frac{28}{2} - \frac{5}{2} = \frac{23}{2}\), resulting in \(y = -\frac{7}{3}x + \frac{23}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{6}(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{5}{3}\), then subtract \(\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(-\frac{5}{3} - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{20}{12} - \frac{9}{12} = -\frac{29}{12}\), resulting in \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{29}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 3 = 4(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute 4 to get \(y - 3 = 4x - 8\). Adding 3 to both sides results in \(y = 4x - 5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 5 = 3(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute 3 across \((x + 2)\) to get \(y - 5 = 3x + 6\). Then, add 5 to both sides to obtain \(y = 3x + 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 2 = -3(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-3\) to get \(y + 2 = -3x + 15\). Subtract 2 from both sides to obtain \(y = -3x + 13\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 7 = 2(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute 2 to obtain \(y + 7 = 2x - 8\). Then, subtract 7 from both sides to get \(y = 2x - 15\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 1 = -4(x + 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-4\) to get \(y + 1 = -4x - 12\). Subtracting 1 from both sides gives \(y = -4x - 13\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 5 = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 6)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y + 5 = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{9}{2}\). Subtracting 5 (which is \(\frac{10}{2}\)) from both sides gives \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{19}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{6}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y + \frac{3}{2} = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{10}{3}\). Subtracting \(\frac{3}{2}\) gives \(-\frac{10}{3} - \frac{3}{2} = -\frac{20}{6} - \frac{9}{6} = -\frac{29}{6}\), so \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{29}{6}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 18 = -7(x + 12)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-7\) to get \(y - 18 = -7x - 84\). Adding 18 to both sides results in \(y = -7x - 66\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{2}{3}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{2}{3}\) to get \(y - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{10}{3}\). Adding \(\frac{1}{3}\) to both sides gives \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{11}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{5}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{5}\) to get \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{8}{5}\). Adding 3 (which is \(\frac{15}{5}\)) to both sides yields \(y = \frac{2}{5}x + \frac{7}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{3}(x - 1)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{3}\) to obtain \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{2}{3}\). Adding \(4\) to both sides results in \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{10}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 2 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{2}\) to obtain \(y - 2 = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{3}{2}\). Adding \(2\) to both sides yields \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 1 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{1}{3}\) to get \(y + 1 = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{4}{3}\). Subtracting \(1\) from both sides gives \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 3 = \frac{1}{4}(x + 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{4}\) to get \(y + 3 = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{5}{4}\). Subtracting \(3\) from both sides gives \(y = \frac{1}{4}x - \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 3 = \frac{3}{5}(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{3}{5}\) to get \(y - 3 = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{6}{5}\). Adding \(3\) to both sides yields \(y = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{21}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 8 = -\frac{5}{7}(x - 6)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{7}\) across the parentheses to get \(y + 8 = -\frac{5}{7}x + \frac{30}{7}\). Subtracting \(8\) (or \(\frac{56}{7}\)) from both sides gives \(y = -\frac{5}{7}x - \frac{26}{7}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{2}{5} = -\frac{3}{4}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y - \frac{2}{5} = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{4}\). Adding \(\frac{2}{5}\) using the common denominator \(20\) gives \(-\frac{5}{20} + \frac{8}{20} = \frac{3}{20}\), so \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{3}{20}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 9 = -\frac{7}{4}(x + 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{7}{4}\) to obtain \(y - 9 = -\frac{7}{4}x - \frac{35}{4}\). Adding \(9\) (which equals \(\frac{36}{4}\)) to both sides yields \(y = -\frac{7}{4}x + \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{5}{6}\left(x - \frac{2}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{1}{3}\). Subtracting \(\frac{3}{4}\) with common denominator \(12\) gives \(\frac{4}{12} - \frac{9}{12} = -\frac{5}{12}\), resulting in \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{5}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 11 = -\frac{5}{8}(x + 14)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{8}\) to obtain \(y + 11 = -\frac{5}{8}x - \frac{35}{4}\). Subtracting \(11\) (or \(\frac{44}{4}\)) from both sides gives \(y = -\frac{5}{8}x - \frac{79}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 2 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y + 2 = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{15}{4}\), then subtract \(2\) (or \(\frac{8}{4}\)) from both sides to get \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 1 = \frac{3}{5}(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{3}{5}\) to get \(y + 1 = \frac{3}{5}x - \frac{6}{5}\), then subtract \(1\) (or \(\frac{5}{5}\)) from both sides to obtain \(y = \frac{3}{5}x - \frac{11}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 3 = \frac{1}{4}(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{4}\) to get \(y - 3 = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{1}{2}\), then add \(3\) to both sides to obtain \(y = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 5 = -\frac{2}{3}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{2}{3}\) to obtain \(y - 5 = -\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{8}{3}\), then add \(5\) (or \(\frac{15}{3}\)) to both sides to get \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - 12 = -\frac{7}{8}(x + 15)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{7}{8}\) to obtain \(y - 12 = -\frac{7}{8}x - \frac{105}{8}\), then add \(12 = \frac{96}{8}\) to both sides to get \(y = -\frac{7}{8}x - \frac{9}{8}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{2}{3}\left(x - \frac{5}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{3}\) to get \(y + \frac{3}{4} = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{5}{3}\), then subtract \(\frac{3}{4}\) using a common denominator of \(12\) (\(-\frac{20}{12} - \frac{9}{12}\)) to find \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{29}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{5}{6}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y - \frac{1}{3} = -\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{10}{3}\), then add \(\frac{1}{3}\) to both sides to get \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{9}{3}\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x - 3\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + 18 = \frac{5}{6}(x - 22)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y + 18 = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{55}{3}\), then subtract \(18 = \frac{54}{3}\) from both sides to obtain \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{109}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{3}(x - 9)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{3}\) to get \(y + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{3}x - 6\), then subtract \(\frac{1}{4}\) from both sides to find \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{25}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{1}{2}(x - 6)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{2}\) to get \(y - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\), then add \(\frac{3}{5}\) to both sides to find \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{12}{5}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{3}{4}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{3}{4}x + 3\), then subtract \(\frac{5}{6}\) from both sides to obtain \(y = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{13}{6}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{3}(x + 6)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{1}{3}\) to get \(y - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{3}x - 2\), then add \(\frac{1}{2}\) to both sides to obtain \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x - \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{4}{3} = -\frac{2}{5}(x - 10)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{2}{5}\) to get \(y - \frac{4}{3} = -\frac{2}{5}x + 4\), then add \(\frac{4}{3}\) to both sides to obtain \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{16}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{8} = -\frac{5}{6}\left(x - \frac{7}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{6}\) to get \(y + \frac{3}{8} = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{7}{6}\), then subtract \(\frac{3}{8}\) using a common denominator of 24 to get \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{19}{24}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{3}{8}\left(x + \frac{4}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{8}\) to get \(y - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{3}{8}x - \frac{3}{10}\), then add \(\frac{5}{6}\) to both sides using a common denominator of 30 to get \(y = -\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{8}{15}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{5}{12} = \frac{7}{8}\left(x - \frac{4}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{7}{8}\) to get \(y + \frac{5}{12} = \frac{7}{8}x - \frac{7}{6}\), then subtract \(\frac{5}{12}\) to yield \(y = \frac{7}{8}x - \frac{19}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{11}{15} = -\frac{2}{9}\left(x + \frac{6}{7}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{2}{9}\) to obtain \(y + \frac{11}{15} = -\frac{2}{9}x - \frac{4}{21}\), then subtract \(\frac{11}{15}\) using a common denominator of 105 to arrive at \(y = -\frac{2}{9}x - \frac{97}{105}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{7}{9} = -\frac{4}{7}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{4}{7}\) to obtain \(y - \frac{7}{9} = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{20}{7}\), then add \(\frac{7}{9}\) using a common denominator of 63 to get \(y = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{229}{63}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{3}\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{2}{3}\) to get \(y + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{2}\). Subtracting \(\frac{1}{2}\) from both sides gives \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 1\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{3}\) to get \(y - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{1}{6}\). Adding \(\frac{2}{5}\) to both sides gives \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{5}{30} + \frac{12}{30} = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{7}{30}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{4}\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{1}{4}\) to get \(y - \frac{1}{3} = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{1}{8}\). Adding \(\frac{1}{3}\) to both sides yields \(y = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{3}{24} + \frac{8}{24} = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{11}{24}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\left(x - \frac{2}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{3}{2}\) to get \(y - \frac{1}{6} = \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{3}{5}\). Adding \(\frac{1}{6}\) to both sides gives \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{18}{30} + \frac{5}{30} = \frac{3}{2}x - \frac{13}{30}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{1}{2}\) to obtain \(y + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{6}\). Subtracting \(\frac{3}{4}\) from both sides yields \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x - \frac{2}{12} - \frac{9}{12} = -\frac{1}{2}x - \frac{11}{12}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{4}{7}\left(x - \frac{21}{16}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{4}{7}\) to get \(y - \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{3}{4}\). Adding \(\frac{5}{8}\) to both sides yields \(y = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{6}{8} + \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{4}{7}x + \frac{11}{8}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y - \frac{7}{10} = -\frac{5}{8}\left(x + \frac{4}{15}\right)\)
Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{3}{4}\left(x - \frac{7}{9}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{3}{4}\) to get \(y + \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{7}{12}\). Subtracting \(\frac{5}{6} = \frac{10}{12}\) gives \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{3}{12} = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{11}{12} = \frac{7}{6}\left(x - \frac{9}{14}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(\frac{7}{6}\) to get \(y + \frac{11}{12} = \frac{7}{6}x - \frac{3}{4}\). Subtracting \(\frac{11}{12}\) gives \(y = \frac{7}{6}x - \frac{9}{12} - \frac{11}{12} = \frac{7}{6}x - \frac{20}{12} = \frac{7}{6}x - \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in slope-intercept form: \(y + \frac{7}{9} = -\frac{5}{12}\left(x + \frac{8}{15}\right)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-\frac{5}{12}\) to get \(y + \frac{7}{9} = -\frac{5}{12}x - \frac{2}{9}\). Subtracting \(\frac{7}{9}\) from both sides gives \(y = -\frac{5}{12}x - \frac{9}{9} = -\frac{5}{12}x - 1\).

exercises.name: Converting point-slope form to standard form

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 6 = -3(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-3\) to get \(y + 6 = -3x + 6\). Adding \(3x\) and subtracting 6 on both sides gives \(3x + y = 0\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 7 = 5(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Distribute 5 to get \(y - 7 = 5x + 10\). Subtracting \(y\) and subtracting 10 gives \(5x - y = -17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 5 = 2(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute the 2 to obtain \(y - 5 = 2x - 6\). Rearranging terms to standard form (\(Ax + By = C\) with \(A \ge 0\)) yields \(2x - y = 1\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 1 = -2(x + 3)\)
qs.s: Distribute \(-2\) to get \(y - 1 = -2x - 6\). Adding \(2x\) and adding 1 to both sides results in \(2x + y = -5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 4 = 4(x - 1)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y + 4 = 4x - 4\). Subtract \(y\) and add 4 to both sides to obtain \(4x - y = 8\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 1 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 4 to get \(4(y + 1) = -3(x - 5)\), which expands to \(4y + 4 = -3x + 15\). Rearranging gives \(3x + 4y = 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{3}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to clear the fraction, giving \(3(y - 3) = 2(x + 4)\), or \(3y - 9 = 2x + 8\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(2x - 3y = -17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 4 = -\frac{5}{2}(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 2 to obtain \(2(y - 4) = -5(x + 2)\), which expands to \(2y - 8 = -5x - 10\). Adding \(5x\) and 8 to both sides yields \(5x + 2y = -2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 6 = -\frac{4}{7}(x + 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 7 to get \(7(y + 6) = -4(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(7y + 42 = -4x - 12\). Rearranging to standard form gives \(4x + 7y = -54\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 5 = \frac{3}{5}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 5 to obtain \(5(y + 5) = 3(x - 4)\), or \(5y + 25 = 3x - 12\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(3x - 5y = 37\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 5 = -3(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y + 5 = -3x + 12\), then add \(3x\) and subtract \(5\) from both sides to obtain \(3x + y = 7\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 1 = 3(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y + 1 = 3x - 15\), then subtract \(y\) and add \(15\) to both sides to obtain \(3x - y = 16\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 1 = -5(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y - 1 = -5x + 10\), then add \(5x\) and \(1\) to both sides to obtain \(5x + y = 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 3 = 4(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y - 3 = 4x + 8\), then subtract \(y\) and \(8\) from both sides to obtain \(4x - y = -11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 6 = -4(x + 1)\)
qs.s: Expand the right side to get \(y - 6 = -4x - 4\), then add \(4x\) and \(6\) to both sides to obtain \(4x + y = 2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 3 = -\frac{3}{4}(x - 6)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 4 to get \(4(y + 3) = -3(x - 6)\), expand to \(4y + 12 = -3x + 18\), and add \(3x\) and subtract \(12\) to get \(3x + 4y = 6\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 11 = -\frac{7}{3}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to get \(3(y - 11) = -7(x - 5)\), expand to \(3y - 33 = -7x + 35\), and add \(7x\) and \(33\) to both sides to get \(7x + 3y = 68\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 5 = \frac{2}{3}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to clear the fraction, yielding \(3(y - 5) = 2(x + 4)\) or \(3y - 15 = 2x + 8\), which rearranges to \(2x - 3y = -23\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 8 = \frac{5}{6}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 6 to get \(6(y + 8) = 5(x - 4)\), expand to \(6y + 48 = 5x - 20\), and rearrange to get \(5x - 6y = 68\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 7 = -\frac{5}{2}(x + 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 2 to get \(2(y - 7) = -5(x + 3)\), expand to \(2y - 14 = -5x - 15\), and rearrange terms to obtain \(5x + 2y = -1\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 2 = -\frac{1}{3}(x + 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to obtain \(3(y - 2) = -(x + 4)\), which simplifies to \(3y - 6 = -x - 4\). Adding \(x\) and 6 to both sides results in \(x + 3y = 2\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 4 = \frac{1}{5}(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 5 to obtain \(5(y + 4) = x - 2\), which expands to \(5y + 20 = x - 2\). Subtracting \(5y\) and adding 2 yields \(x - 5y = 22\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 5 = \frac{1}{2}(x + 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 2 to get \(2(y - 5) = x + 3\), which expands to \(2y - 10 = x + 3\). Subtracting \(2y\) and 3 from both sides gives \(x - 2y = -13\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 2 = \frac{1}{4}(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 4 to get \(4(y + 2) = x - 3\), which simplifies to \(4y + 8 = x - 3\). Rearranging the terms into standard form gives \(x - 4y = 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{3}(x + 1)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to get \(3(y - 3) = 2(x + 1)\), which expands to \(3y - 9 = 2x + 2\). Subtracting \(3y\) and 2 from both sides results in \(2x - 3y = -11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{5}{6}(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 12 to clear the denominators, giving \(12y + 9 = -10(x - 2)\). Expanding to \(12y + 9 = -10x + 20\) and rearranging terms gives \(10x + 12y = 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 12 = -\frac{4}{7}(x + 9)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 7 to obtain \(7(y - 12) = -4(x + 9)\), which expands to \(7y - 84 = -4x - 36\). Adding \(4x\) and 84 to both sides gives \(4x + 7y = 48\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 16 = \frac{5}{8}(x - 24)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 8 to obtain \(8(y + 16) = 5(x - 24)\), which simplifies to \(8y + 128 = 5x - 120\). Subtracting \(8y\) and adding 120 yields \(5x - 8y = 248\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{2}{3}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by the least common denominator 6 to get \(6y - 3 = 4(x - 5)\), which expands to \(6y - 3 = 4x - 20\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(4x - 6y = 17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 18 = -\frac{11}{12}(x + 15)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 12 to get \(12(y - 18) = -11(x + 15)\), which expands to \(12y - 216 = -11x - 165\). Adding \(11x\) and 216 to both sides results in \(11x + 12y = 51\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 6 = -\frac{3}{7}(x + 2)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 7 to obtain \(7y + 42 = -3(x + 2)\), which expands to \(7y + 42 = -3x - 6\). Adding \(3x\) and subtracting 42 results in \(3x + 7y = -48\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 2 = \frac{3}{4}(x + 5)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 4 to get \(4y - 8 = 3(x + 5)\), which expands to \(4y - 8 = 3x + 15\). Subtracting \(4y\) and 15 gives the standard form \(3x - 4y = -23\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 5 = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 3 to get \(3y - 15 = -(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(3y - 15 = -x + 4\). Adding \(x\) and 15 yields the standard form \(x + 3y = 19\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 1 = \frac{5}{2}(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 2 to clear the fraction, giving \(2y + 2 = 5x - 15\). Rearranging terms so the \(x\)-coefficient is positive gives \(5x - 2y = 17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 14 = -\frac{9}{11}(x - 15)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 11 to obtain \(11y + 154 = -9x + 135\). Adding \(9x\) to both sides and subtracting 154 gives \(9x + 11y = -19\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 18 = \frac{11}{12}(x - 22)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 12 to clear the fraction: \(12y + 216 = 11(x - 22) = 11x - 242\). Subtracting \(12y\) and adding 242 gives \(11x - 12y = 458\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{5}{6}(x + 8)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by the least common denominator, 12, giving \(12y - 9 = -10(x + 8) = -10x - 80\). Adding \(10x\) and 9 produces \(10x + 12y = -71\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 5 = \frac{7}{4}\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 12 to clear denominators: \(12y + 60 = 21\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right) = 21x - 14\). Rearranging terms yields \(21x - 12y = 74\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{3}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply through by the common denominator 30 to get \(30y - 15 = -20\left(x + \frac{3}{5}\right) = -20x - 12\). Adding \(20x\) and 15 results in \(20x + 30y = 3\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{3}(x - 2)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 6 to clear the denominators, giving \(6y + 5 = 2(x - 2)\). Expanding gives \(6y + 5 = 2x - 4\), which rearranges to \(2x - 6y = 9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 6)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 4 to get \(4y - 2 = -3(x + 6)\). Distribute to obtain \(4y - 2 = -3x - 18\), and add \(3x\) and 2 to both sides to get \(3x + 4y = -16\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{2}{3}(x - 3)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 12 to clear the fractions to obtain \(12y + 3 = 8(x - 3)\). Distribute to get \(12y + 3 = 8x - 24\), then rearrange into standard form: \(8x - 12y = 27\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{3}{5} = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 10 to clear denominators, giving \(10y - 6 = 5(x - 4)\). Expanding and rearranging into \(Ax + By = C\) with \(A \ge 0\) yields \(5x - 10y = 14\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{4}{3} = -\frac{2}{5}(x - 5)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 15 to get \(15y - 20 = -6(x - 5) = -6x + 30\). Rearranging into \(Ax + By = C\) form gives \(6x + 15y = 50\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{7}{10} = -\frac{4}{15}\left(x + \frac{5}{6}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply through by 90 to obtain \(90y - 63 = -24\left(x + \frac{5}{6}\right) = -24x - 20\). Rearranging terms to standard form with \(A \ge 0\) gives \(24x + 90y = 43\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{5}{6}\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by the least common multiple of all denominators, 36, giving \(36y - 27 = 30\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right) = 30x + 20\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(30x - 36y = -47\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{7}{12} = -\frac{5}{18}\left(x - \frac{3}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply through by 36 to eliminate denominators: \(36y + 21 = -10\left(x - \frac{3}{5}\right) = -10x + 6\). Rearranging into \(Ax + By = C\) gives \(10x + 36y = -15\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{7}{12}\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 48 to clear all denominators, yielding \(48y + 30 = -28\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right) = -28x + 21\). Adding \(28x\) and subtracting 30 gives \(28x + 48y = -9\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{4}{9} = \frac{7}{6}\left(x - \frac{5}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Multiply both sides by 144 to clear fractions, yielding \(144y + 64 = 168\left(x - \frac{5}{8}\right) = 168x - 105\). Rearranging gives \(168x - 144y = 169\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distributing gives \(y - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{3}\). Multiplying by the LCD of 12 yields \(12y - 9 = 8x + 4\), which rearranges to \(8x - 12y = -13\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{1}{3}\right)\)
qs.s: Distributing gives \(y + \frac{1}{5} = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{1}{6}\). Multiplying both sides by the LCD of 30 gives \(30y + 6 = 15x - 5\), which rearranges to \(15x - 30y = 11\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{3}\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distributing gives \(y - \frac{2}{5} = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{6}\). Multiplying by the LCD of 30 yields \(30y - 12 = 10x + 5\), which rearranges to \(10x - 30y = -17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{4}\right)\)
qs.s: Distributing gives \(y + \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{12}\). Multiplying by the LCD of 12 gives \(12y + 6 = -4x + 1\), which simplifies to \(4x + 12y = -5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{4}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Distributing gives \(y + \frac{1}{3} = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{3}{8}\). Multiplying by the LCD of 24 yields \(24y + 8 = 18x - 9\), which rearranges to \(18x - 24y = 17\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - \frac{7}{15} = -\frac{4}{9}\left(x + \frac{3}{8}\right)\)
qs.s: Expanding gives \(y - \frac{7}{15} = -\frac{4}{9}x - \frac{1}{6}\). Multiplying by the LCD of 90 gives \(90y - 42 = -40x - 15\), which rearranges to \(40x + 90y = 27\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y - 1\frac{1}{4} = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x + 2\frac{1}{2}\right)\)
qs.s: Converting mixed numbers to improper fractions gives \(y - \frac{5}{4} = -\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{5}{3}\). Multiplying by 12 results in \(12y - 15 = -8x - 20\), which simplifies to \(8x + 12y = -5\).

qs.q: Rewrite the point-slope equation in standard form: \(y + 2\frac{1}{6} = \frac{5}{8}\left(x - 1\frac{3}{5}\right)\)
qs.s: Rewriting mixed numbers as improper fractions gives \(y + \frac{13}{6} = \frac{5}{8}x - 1\). Multiplying by 24 yields \(24y + 52 = 15x - 24\), which simplifies to \(15x - 24y = 76\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = 4, passing through \((-2, 5)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 4\), \(x_1 = -2\), and \(y_1 = 5\) into the point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) to get \(y - 5 = 4(x - (-2))\), which simplifies to \(y - 5 = 4(x + 2)\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = 3, passing through \((-6, -2)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 3\), \(x_1 = -6\), and \(y_1 = -2\) into \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) to get \(y - (-2) = 3(x - (-6))\), which simplifies to \(y + 2 = 3(x + 6)\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = -5, passing through \((-4, 1)\)?
qs.s: Using point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with \(m = -5\) and \((-4, 1)\) yields \(y - 1 = -5(x - (-4))\), simplifying to \(y - 1 = -5(x + 4)\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = -4, passing through \((-3, -8)\)?
qs.s: Using the point-slope form \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) with \(m = -4\) and \((-3, -8)\) gives \(y - (-8) = -4(x - (-3))\), or \(y + 8 = -4(x + 3)\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = -2, passing through \((3, -7)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(m = -2\), \(x_1 = 3\), and \(y_1 = -7\) into \(y - y_1 = m(x - x_1)\) to obtain \(y - (-7) = -2(x - 3)\), which gives \(y + 7 = -2(x - 3)\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = \(\frac{3}{5}\), passing through \((-4, 2)\)?
qs.s: Substitute into point-slope form to get \(y - 2 = \frac{3}{5}(x + 4)\), multiply both sides by 5 to obtain \(5y - 10 = 3x + 12\), and rearrange into standard form \(3x - 5y = -22\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = \(-\frac{3}{4}\), passing through \((-3, 2)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(m = -\frac{3}{4}\) and \((-3, 2)\) into \(y = mx + b\) to find \(2 = -\frac{3}{4}(-3) + b\), giving \(b = 2 - \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}\), so \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = \(\frac{4}{7}\), passing through \((-3, -5)\)?
qs.s: Write \(y + 5 = \frac{4}{7}(x + 3)\), clear the fraction to get \(7(y + 5) = 4(x + 3) \implies 7y + 35 = 4x + 12\), and rearrange into standard form \(4x - 7y = 23\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = \(-\frac{5}{2}\), passing through \((-4, -7)\)?
qs.s: Substitute into point-slope form to get \(y + 7 = -\frac{5}{2}(x + 4)\), multiply by 2 to get \(2y + 14 = -5x - 20\), and rearrange to get \(5x + 2y = -34\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: slope = \(-\frac{2}{3}\), passing through \((5, -1)\)?
qs.s: Substitute into point-slope form to get \(y + 1 = -\frac{2}{3}(x - 5)\), multiply by 3 to get \(3y + 3 = -2x + 10\), and rearrange to find \(2x + 3y = 7\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = 5, \(y\)-intercept \((0, 4)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the line is \(y = 5x + 4\). Subtracting \(y\) and 4 from both sides results in \(5x - y = -4\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = 2, \(y\)-intercept \((0, -5)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation of the line is \(y = 2x - 5\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(2x - y = 5\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = -1, \(y\)-intercept \((0, -8)\)?
qs.s: The slope-intercept form is \(y = -x - 8\). Adding \(x\) to both sides gives the standard form equation \(x + y = -8\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = -3, \(y\)-intercept \((0, 7)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = -3x + 7\). Adding \(3x\) to both sides gives the standard form equation \(3x + y = 7\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = -4, \(y\)-intercept \((0, -1)\)?
qs.s: The slope-intercept form is \(y = -4x - 1\). Adding \(4x\) to both sides yields the standard form equation \(4x + y = -1\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = \(-\frac{2}{3}\), \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, \frac{7}{6}\right)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{7}{6}\). Multiplying by 6 gives \(6y = -4x + 7\), which in standard form is \(4x + 6y = 7\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = \(\frac{3}{4}\), \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, -\frac{5}{2}\right)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{5}{2}\). Multiplying each term by the common denominator 4 gives \(4y = 3x - 10\), which rearranges to \(3x - 4y = 10\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = \(\frac{5}{6}\), \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, -\frac{7}{4}\right)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{7}{4}\). Multiplying each term by the least common denominator 12 gives \(12y = 10x - 21\), which rearranges to \(10x - 12y = 21\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = \(-\frac{5}{8}\), \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, -\frac{11}{4}\right)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = -\frac{5}{8}x - \frac{11}{4}\). Multiplying by 8 yields \(8y = -5x - 22\), which in standard form is \(5x + 8y = -22\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Slope = \(\frac{7}{9}\), \(y\)-intercept \(\left(0, \frac{4}{3}\right)\)?
qs.s: In slope-intercept form, the equation is \(y = \frac{7}{9}x + \frac{4}{3}\). Multiplying by 9 yields \(9y = 7x + 12\), which gives \(7x - 9y = -12\) in standard form.

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((-3, -7)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-7 - 0}{-3 - 0} = \frac{7}{3}\). Since the line crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, 0)\), the equation is \(y = \frac{7}{3}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through the origin and \((5, 2)\)?
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{2 - 0}{5 - 0} = \frac{2}{5}\). With a \(y\)-intercept of \(0\), the equation is \(y = \frac{2}{5}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((-2, 5)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{5 - 0}{-2 - 0} = -\frac{5}{2}\). Because the line passes through \((0, 0)\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), resulting in \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((4, -1)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 0}{4 - 0} = -\frac{1}{4}\). Since the line passes through the origin \((0, 0)\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), giving the equation \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through the origin and \((2, -6)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-6 - 0}{2 - 0} = -3\). Passing through \((0, 0)\) means the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), so the equation is \(y = -3x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((-1, 4)\) and \((3, -2)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - 4}{3 - (-1)} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Using point-slope form, \(y - 4 = -\frac{3}{2}(x + 1)\), which clears fractions to \(2(y - 4) = -3(x + 1)\) and rearranges to standard form as \(3x + 2y = 5\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((-6, 8)\) and \((9, -2)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - 8}{9 - (-6)} = -\frac{10}{15} = -\frac{2}{3}\). In point-slope form, \(y - (-2) = -\frac{2}{3}(x - 9)\), which simplifies to \(3(y + 2) = -2(x - 9)\) and rearranges to standard form as \(2x + 3y = 12\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((4, 9)\) and \((12, -7)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-7 - 9}{12 - 4} = \frac{-16}{8} = -2\). Substituting \((4, 9)\) into \(y = -2x + b\) gives \(9 = -2(4) + b\), so \(b = 17\), yielding the equation \(y = -2x + 17\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((-4, -5)\) and \((2, -2)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - (-5)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{3}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\). Substituting \((2, -2)\) into \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + b\) gives \(-2 = \frac{1}{2}(2) + b\), so \(b = -3\), resulting in \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: Passing through \((2, -3)\) and \((6, 5)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{5 - (-3)}{6 - 2} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\). Substituting \((6, 5)\) into \(y = 2x + b\) gives \(5 = 2(6) + b\), which yields \(b = -7\) and the equation \(y = 2x - 7\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((1, -4)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-4 - 0}{1 - 0} = -4\). Since the line passes through the origin \((0, 0)\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), so the equation is \(y = -4x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((5, -1)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 0}{5 - 0} = -\frac{1}{5}\). Since the line passes through the origin \((0, 0)\), the equation is \(y = -\frac{1}{5}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((3, 2)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{2 - 0}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\). Passing through \((0, 0)\) means the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), so the equation is \(y = \frac{2}{3}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((-2, -10)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-10 - 0}{-2 - 0} = 5\). Since the line passes through the origin, the \(y\)-intercept is \(0\), giving \(y = 5x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((0, 0)\) and \((-4, 3)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{3 - 0}{-4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{4}\). With a \(y\)-intercept of \(0\), the equation is \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x\).

qs.q: Which equation matches the description: passing through \((-2, 11)\) and \((4, -1)\)?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 11}{4 - (-2)} = -2\). In slope-intercept form, \(-1 = -2(4) + b\) gives \(b = 7\), so \(y = -2x + 7\), which in standard form is \(2x + y = 7\).
