exercises.name: Determine slope from equation or coordinate rule

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((x, -\frac{3}{5}x)\)?
qs.s: The coordinates follow the equation \(y = -\frac{3}{5}x\), so the slope is \(m = -\frac{3}{5}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((x, -x)\)?
qs.s: The relation between the coordinates is \(y = -1x\), which has a slope of \(m = -1\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((x, 4x + 9)\)?
qs.s: The relation is \(y = 4x + 9\), which is in slope-intercept form \(y = mx + b\) with slope \(m = 4\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((x, -2x - 3)\)?
qs.s: The equation of the line is \(y = -2x - 3\), so the slope is the coefficient of \(x\), which is \(m = -2\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((x, 7x)\)?
qs.s: The ordered pairs satisfy \(y = 7x\), which is in slope-intercept form \(y = mx\) with slope \(m = 7\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \(\left(x, \frac{5x - 1}{2} - \frac{2x + 3}{5}\right)\)?
qs.s: Combining over a common denominator gives \(y = \frac{5(5x - 1) - 2(2x + 3)}{10} = \frac{21x - 11}{10}\), so the slope is \(m = \frac{21}{10}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((3 - 2x, 4(2x - 1) - 3(x + 2))\)?
qs.s: Simplifying the \(y\)-coordinate gives \(8x - 4 - 3x - 6 = 5x - 10\). The slope is the ratio of the rates of change: \(m = \frac{5}{-2} = -\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((3x - 1, 5 - 12x)\)?
What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((4x - 3, 1 - 6x)\)?
What is the slope of all ordered pairs of the form \((2x + 3, 10x - 7)\)?

Given that a taxi ride of \(0\text{ km}\) has a base fee of \(\$5\) and a ride of \(20\text{ km}\) costs \(\$45\), determine the distance in kilometers of a trip that costs \(\$29\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The rate per kilometer is \(m = \frac{45 - 5}{20 - 0} = 2\text{ \$/km}\), giving the cost formula \(C = 2d + 5\). Setting \(C = 29\) gives \(29 = 2d + 5\), so \(2d = 24\) and \(d = 12\text{ km}\).

qs.q: Given that \(0^\circ\text{C}\) is equivalent to \(15^\circ\text{N}\) and \(100^\circ\text{C}\) is equivalent to \(215^\circ\text{N}\) on a newly designed temperature scale, determine the equivalent of \(95^\circ\text{N}\) in \(^\circ\text{C}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{215 - 15}{100 - 0} = 2\), giving the equation \(N = 2C + 15\). Setting \(N = 95\) gives \(95 = 2C + 15\), so \(2C = 80\) and \(C = 40^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: Given that a hanging spring has a length of \(14\text{ cm}\) when supporting \(0\text{ g}\) and stretches to \(38\text{ cm}\) when supporting \(60\text{ g}\), determine the mass in grams that stretches the spring to \(30\text{ cm}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The stretch rate is \(m = \frac{38 - 14}{60 - 0} = 0.4\text{ cm/g}\), giving the equation \(L = 0.4w + 14\). Setting \(L = 30\) gives \(0.4w + 14 = 30\), so \(0.4w = 16\) and \(w = 40\text{ g}\).

qs.q: Given that \(0^\circ\text{R}\) on the Réaumur scale is equivalent to \(32^\circ\text{F}\) and \(80^\circ\text{R}\) is equivalent to \(212^\circ\text{F}\), determine the equivalent of \(77^\circ\text{F}\) in \(^\circ\text{R}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{212 - 32}{80 - 0} = 2.25\), giving the equation \(F = 2.25R + 32\). Setting \(F = 77\) gives \(2.25R = 45\), so \(R = 20^\circ\text{R}\).

qs.q: Given that the pressure underwater is \(100\text{ kPa}\) at a depth of \(0\text{ m}\) and \(600\text{ kPa}\) at a depth of \(50\text{ m}\), determine the depth in meters where the pressure is \(340\text{ kPa}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The rate of pressure change is \(m = \frac{600 - 100}{50 - 0} = 10\text{ kPa/m}\), giving \(P = 10d + 100\). Setting \(P = 340\) yields \(10d + 100 = 340\), which gives \(10d = 240\) and \(d = 24\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Given that a temperature of \(15^\circ\text{P}\) corresponds to \(59^\circ\text{Q}\) and \(35^\circ\text{P}\) corresponds to \(107^\circ\text{Q}\) on two linearly related scales, determine the equivalent of \(155^\circ\text{Q}\) in \(^\circ\text{P}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{107 - 59}{35 - 15} = 2.4\), so the equation in point-slope form is \(Q - 59 = 2.4(P - 15)\), or \(Q = 2.4P + 23\). Setting \(Q = 155\) yields \(155 = 2.4P + 23\), which gives \(2.4P = 132\) and \(P = 55^\circ\text{P}\).

qs.q: Given that a temperature of \(10^\circ\text{X}\) corresponds to \(50^\circ\text{Y}\) and \(70^\circ\text{X}\) corresponds to \(140^\circ\text{Y}\) on two linearly related scales, determine the numerical temperature at which both scales give the same reading.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{140 - 50}{70 - 10} = 1.5\), giving the relationship \(Y - 50 = 1.5(X - 10)\), or \(Y = 1.5X + 35\). Setting \(Y = X\) gives \(X = 1.5X + 35\), which solves to \(-0.5X = 35\) and \(X = -70\).

qs.q: Given that producing \(250\) custom shirts costs \(\$3100\) and producing \(600\) shirts costs \(\$5900\), determine the number of shirts that can be produced for \(\$4780\), assuming a linear cost relationship.

Given that \(-10^\circ\text{C}\) corresponds to \(14^\circ\text{E}\) and \(30^\circ\text{C}\) corresponds to \(86^\circ\text{E}\) on an experimental temperature scale, determine the equivalent of \(-4^\circ\text{E}\) in \(^\circ\text{C}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{86 - 14}{30 - (-10)} = \frac{72}{40} = 1.8\), giving \(E - 14 = 1.8(C + 10)\), which simplifies to \(E = 1.8C + 32\). Setting \(E = -4\) gives \(-4 = 1.8C + 32\), so \(1.8C = -36\) and \(C = -20^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: Given that water boils at \(96^\circ\text{C}\) at an altitude of \(1200\text{ m}\) and at \(88^\circ\text{C}\) at an altitude of \(3600\text{ m}\), determine the altitude in meters where water boils at \(91^\circ\text{C}\), assuming a linear relationship.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{88 - 96}{3600 - 1200} = -\frac{1}{300}^\circ\text{C/m}\), giving \(T - 96 = -\frac{1}{300}(h - 1200)\). Substituting \(T = 91\) gives \(-5 = -\frac{1}{300}(h - 1200)\), leading to \(h - 1200 = 1500\) and \(h = 2700\text{ m}\).

exercises.name: Find unknown coefficients in a linear equation

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 4x - 2y - 20\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((5, -4)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a - 4)x + (b + 2)y = -20\). For a horizontal line, \(a - 4 = 0 \implies a = 4\), and substituting \(y = -4\) gives \((b + 2)(-4) = -20 \implies b = 3\), so \(a + b = 7\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = -4x + y + 15\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((3, -5)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a + 4)x + (b - 1)y = 15\). For a horizontal line, \(a + 4 = 0 \implies a = -4\), and substituting \(y = -5\) yields \((b - 1)(-5) = 15 \implies b = -2\), so \(a + b = -6\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 5x + 2y - 12\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((0, -4)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a - 5)x + (b - 2)y = -12\). Since the line is horizontal, \(a - 5 = 0 \implies a = 5\), and substituting \(y = -4\) gives \((b - 2)(-4) = -12 \implies b = 5\), so \(a + b = 10\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 3x - 4y + 8\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a vertical line passing through \((2, 5)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a - 3)x + (b + 4)y = 8\). For a vertical line, the \(y\)-coefficient must be zero, so \(b + 4 = 0 \implies b = -4\); substituting \(x = 2\) gives \((a - 3)(2) = 8 \implies a = 7\), so \(a + b = 3\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = -x + 5y + 12\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a vertical line passing through \((-3, 1)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a + 1)x + (b - 5)y = 12\). Since the line is vertical, \(b - 5 = 0 \implies b = 5\), and substituting \(x = -3\) yields \((a + 1)(-3) = 12 \implies a = -5\), so \(a + b = 0\).

qs.q: In the equation \(\frac{a}{2}x + \frac{b}{3}y = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y + 5\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \(\left(-2, \frac{5}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(\left(\frac{a}{2} - \frac{3}{4}\right)x + \left(\frac{b}{3} + \frac{1}{2}\right)y = 5\). For a horizontal line, \(\frac{a}{2} = \frac{3}{4} \implies a = \frac{3}{2}\), and substituting \(y = \frac{5}{2}\) gives \(\left(\frac{b}{3} + \frac{1}{2}\right)\left(\frac{5}{2}\right) = 5 \implies b = \frac{9}{2}\), so \(a + b = 6\).

qs.q: In the equation \((2a + b)x + (a - 2b)y = 7x - 4y + 20\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a vertical line passing through \((4, -1)\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \([(2a + b) - 7]x + [(a - 2b) + 4]y = 20\). For a vertical line, \(a - 2b + 4 = 0\), and substituting \(x = 4\) yields \(2a + b - 7 = 5\); solving this system gives \(a = 4\) and \(b = 4\), so \(a + b = 8\).

qs.q: In the equation \(a(x + 2) + b(y - 4) = 3x - 5y + 7\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((1, 3)\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \((a - 3)x + (b + 5)y = 7 - 2a + 4b\). A horizontal line requires \(a - 3 = 0 \implies a = 3\); substituting \(a = 3\) and \(y = 3\) into the equation yields \(3(b + 5) = 1 + 4b \implies b = 14\), so \(a + b = 17\).

qs.q: In the equation \(2(ax + 3) - 3(by - 1) = 8x - 6y + 27\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((1, -2)\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging terms gives \((2a - 8)x + (-3b + 6)y = 18\). A horizontal line requires \(2a - 8 = 0 \implies a = 4\), and substituting \(y = -2\) gives \((-3b + 6)(-2) = 18 \implies b = 5\), giving \(a + b = 9\).

qs.q: In the equation \((5a - 2)x + (b + 4)y = (3a + 4)x - (2b + 5)y + 36\), find the value of \(a + b\) if the graph is a vertical line passing through \((6, 8)\).
qs.s: Grouping like terms gives \((2a - 6)x + (3b + 9)y = 36\). A vertical line requires \(3b + 9 = 0 \implies b = -3\), and substituting \(x = 6\) gives \((2a - 6)(6) = 36 \implies a = 6\), so \(a + b = 3\).

exercises.name: Find unknown coefficients in a linear equation

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 4x - 5y + 12\), the graph is a vertical line passing through \((2, -1)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Rewriting the equation as \((a - 4)x + (b + 5)y = 12\), a vertical line requires the \(y\)-coefficient to be zero, so \(b + 5 = 0 \implies b = -5\). Since the line passes through \((2, -1)\), we have \((a - 4)(2) = 12\), which yields \(a = 10\), giving \(a + b = 10 + (-5) = 5\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax - 3y = x + by - 8\), the graph is a vertical line passing through \((4, 1)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Rearranging gives \((a - 1)x - (b + 3)y = -8\), where \(-(b + 3) = 0 \implies b = -3\) for a vertical line. Substituting \(x = 4\) yields \((a - 1)(4) = -8 \implies a = -1\), so \(a + b = -1 + (-3) = -4\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = -x + 4y + 15\), the graph is a vertical line passing through \((-3, 5)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Rearranging to \((a + 1)x + (b - 4)y = 15\), the \(y\)-coefficient must be zero for a vertical line, giving \(b - 4 = 0 \implies b = 4\). Substituting \(x = -3\) yields \((a + 1)(-3) = 15 \implies a = -6\), so \(a + b = -6 + 4 = -2\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 3x + 2y - 8\), the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((4, -2)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Rewriting the equation as \((a - 3)x + (b - 2)y = -8\), a horizontal line has an \(x\)-coefficient of zero, so \(a - 3 = 0 \implies a = 3\). Substituting \(y = -2\) gives \((b - 2)(-2) = -8 \implies b = 6\), so \(a + b = 3 + 6 = 9\).

qs.q: In the equation \(ax + by = 5x - y + 18\), the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((-2, 3)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Rewriting as \((a - 5)x + (b + 1)y = 18\), the line is horizontal so \(a - 5 = 0 \implies a = 5\). With \(y = 3\), \((b + 1)(3) = 18 \implies b = 5\), giving \(a + b = 5 + 5 = 10\).

qs.q: In the equation \(2(ax + 3y) - 5(x - by) = 7x + 4y - 45\), the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((6, -5)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting terms yields \((2a - 12)x + (5b + 2)y = -45\), so the \(x\)-coefficient must be zero for a horizontal line, giving \(a = 6\). Substituting \(y = -5\) into \((5b + 2)(-5) = -45\) gives \(b = \frac{7}{5}\), so \(a + b = 6 + \frac{7}{5} = \frac{37}{5}\).

qs.q: In the equation \(3(ax - 2y) + 4(x + by) = 2x - 5y + 24\), the graph is a vertical line passing through \((-4, 7)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Expanding and grouping like terms gives \((3a + 2)x + (4b - 1)y = 24\), so for a vertical line \(4b - 1 = 0 \implies b = \frac{1}{4}\). Since \(x = -4\), \((3a + 2)(-4) = 24 \implies a = -\frac{8}{3}\), giving \(a + b = -\frac{8}{3} + \frac{1}{4} = -\frac{29}{12}\).

qs.q: In the equation \(\frac{ax - 4}{3} + \frac{by + 2}{2} = x - y + 5\), the graph is a horizontal line passing through \((3, 4)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \(6\) to clear denominators and rearranging gives \((2a - 6)x + (3b + 6)y = 32\), so for a horizontal line \(2a - 6 = 0 \implies a = 3\). Substituting \(y = 4\) yields \((3b + 6)(4) = 32 \implies b = \frac{2}{3}\), so \(a + b = 3 + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{11}{3}\).

qs.q: In the equation \(4(ax - y) + 3(2x + by) = 10x - 7y + 36\), the graph passes through \((3, -4)\) and \((3, 8)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Since both points have an \(x\)-coordinate of \(3\), the line is vertical (\(x = 3\)), meaning the \(y\)-coefficient in \((4a - 4)x + (3b + 3)y = 36\) must be zero, so \(b = -1\). Substituting \(x = 3\) gives \((4a - 4)(3) = 36 \implies a = 4\), which results in \(a + b = 4 + (-1) = 3\).

qs.q: In the equation \(5(x - ay) - 2(bx + 3y) = -x + 6y + 40\), the graph passes through \((-5, -4)\) and \((7, -4)\). Find the value of \(a + b\).
qs.s: Because both points have \(y = -4\), the line is horizontal, requiring the \(x\)-coefficient of \((6 - 2b)x - (5a + 12)y = 40\) to be zero, giving \(b = 3\). Setting \(-(5a + 12)(-4) = 40\) gives \(a = -\frac{2}{5}\), so \(a + b = -\frac{2}{5} + 3 = \frac{13}{5}\).

exercises.name: Slopes of parallel and perpendicular lines

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(y = \frac{1}{7}x\).
qs.s: The line \(y = \frac{1}{7}x\) has a slope of \(\frac{1}{7}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, which is \(-7\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(y = -6x\).
qs.s: Parallel lines have identical slopes, so the slope of any line parallel to \(y = -6x\) is \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(y = -5x\).
qs.s: The line \(y = -5x\) has a slope of \(-5\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, which is \(\frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(y = 4x\).
qs.s: The line \(y = 4x\) has a slope of \(4\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, which is \(-\frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(y = \frac{2}{3}x\).
qs.s: Parallel lines have equal slopes, so the slope of a line parallel to \(y = \frac{2}{3}x\) is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(9x + 6y = 14\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(9x + 6y = 14\) into slope-intercept form gives \(y = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{7}{3}\), so the slope is \(-\frac{3}{2}\). A parallel line has the same slope, \(-\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(4x - 7y = 2(x - 3y) + 5\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging the equation gives \(y = 2x - 5\), which has a slope of \(2\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(2(3x - 2y) = 7 - (2x - y)\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides yields \(6x - 4y = 7 - 2x + y\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{8}{5}x - \frac{7}{5}\) with slope \(\frac{8}{5}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{5}{8}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(\frac{3}{5}x - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \(10\) gives \(6x - 5y = 30\), which rearranges to \(y = \frac{6}{5}x - 6\) with slope \(\frac{6}{5}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(3x - 5y = 15\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(3x - 5y = 15\) into slope-intercept form gives \(y = \frac{3}{5}x - 3\), so its slope is \(\frac{3}{5}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(y = \frac{2}{5}x\).
qs.s: The slope of the line \(y = \frac{2}{5}x\) is \(\frac{2}{5}\). The slope of a line perpendicular to it is the negative reciprocal, which is \(-\frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(y = \frac{3}{7}x\).
qs.s: The line \(y = \frac{3}{7}x\) has a slope of \(\frac{3}{7}\). Since parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope of a parallel line is \(\frac{3}{7}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x\).
qs.s: The slope of the line \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x\) is \(-\frac{1}{3}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, which is \(3\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(y = -5x\).
qs.s: The line \(y = -5x\) has a slope of \(-5\). Since parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope of a parallel line is \(-5\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{3}y = 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \(15\) to clear denominators gives \(6x - 5y = 60\), which rearranges to \(y = \frac{6}{5}x - 12\) with slope \(\frac{6}{5}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(14x - 21y = 9\).
qs.s: Rewriting the equation in slope-intercept form gives \(-21y = -14x + 9\), or \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{7}\). Since parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope of a parallel line is \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(6x + 8y = 21\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(6x + 8y = 21\) in slope-intercept form gives \(y = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{21}{8}\), so its slope is \(-\frac{3}{4}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the line \(5x - 2y = 3x + 10y - 8\).
qs.s: Rearranging terms gives \(12y = 2x + 8\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{2}{3}\), so the line's slope is \(\frac{1}{6}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the line \(15x + 9y - 7 = 0\).

qs.s: Solving for \(y\) yields \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{7}{6}\), which gives a slope of \(\frac{5}{6}\). Because parallel lines share the same slope, the required slope is \(\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(\frac{3}{2}x = \frac{2}{5}y - \frac{1}{4}\)?
qs.s: Rearranging the equation to solve for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{15}{4}x + \frac{5}{8}\), so the slope of the line is \(\frac{15}{4}\). Parallel lines have equal slopes, so the slope of the parallel line is \(\frac{15}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(\frac{3}{5}\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 2\right) = \frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{3}{4}y + 1\right) - \frac{7}{10}x\)?
qs.s: Expanding and multiplying by the common denominator 30 yields \(9x - 36 = 15y + 20 - 21x\), which simplifies to \(15y = 30x - 56\) or \(y = 2x - \frac{56}{15}\). The slope of the line is \(2\), so a perpendicular line has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(\frac{3}{8}x - \frac{2}{3}y + \frac{5}{12} = \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{1}{4}y - 1\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD of 24 yields \(9x - 16y + 10 = 4x + 6y - 24\), which simplifies to \(22y = 5x + 34\), or \(y = \frac{5}{22}x + \frac{17}{11}\). Because parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope is \(\frac{5}{22}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(\frac{2}{3}(x - 4) = \frac{5}{6}y + \frac{1}{2}(x + 2)\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by 6 to clear denominators gives \(4(x - 4) = 5y + 3(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(5y = x - 22\) or \(y = \frac{1}{5}x - \frac{22}{5}\). The slope of the line is \(\frac{1}{5}\), so a perpendicular line has slope \(-5\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(\frac{4x - 1}{3} - \frac{y + 2}{4} = \frac{2x + 3y}{6}\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by 12 yields \(4(4x - 1) - 3(y + 2) = 2(2x + 3y)\), which simplifies to \(9y = 12x - 10\) or \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{10}{9}\). The line has a slope of \(\frac{4}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: What is the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(\frac{5}{7}(2x - 1) - \frac{3}{14}x = \frac{2}{7}y - \frac{1}{2}(y - 4)\)?
qs.s: Multiplying by 14 gives \(10(2x - 1) - 3x = 4y - 7(y - 4)\), which simplifies to \(17x - 10 = -3y + 28\), or \(y = -\frac{17}{3}x + \frac{38}{3}\). Since parallel lines have identical slopes, the slope is \(-\frac{17}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(2.1x + 4.6 = 0.7y\).
qs.s: Divide both sides by \(0.7\) to obtain \(y = \frac{2.1}{0.7}x + \frac{4.6}{0.7} = 3x + \frac{46}{7}\), so the slope is \(3\). A parallel line has the identical slope, \(3\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(1.2x - 0.5 = -0.8y\).
qs.s: Dividing by \(-0.8\) yields \(y = -\frac{1.2}{0.8}x + \frac{0.5}{0.8} = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{5}{8}\), so the line's slope is \(-\frac{3}{2}\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, \(\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(0.6x - 1.7 = 0.8y\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form as \(y = \frac{0.6}{0.8}x - \frac{1.7}{0.8} = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{17}{8}\), so the slope of the line is \(\frac{3}{4}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{4}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(0.3x + 1.9 = 1.5y\).
qs.s: Rewrite the equation in slope-intercept form as \(y = \frac{0.3}{1.5}x + \frac{1.9}{1.5} = \frac{1}{5}x + \frac{19}{15}\), which gives a slope of \(\frac{1}{5}\). Since parallel lines have equal slopes, the slope of a parallel line is \(\frac{1}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(0.5x + 2.1 = 2.0y\).
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{0.5}{2.0}x + \frac{2.1}{2.0} = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{21}{20}\), so the slope of the given line is \(\frac{1}{4}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-4\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(\frac{2}{3}(x - 6) + \frac{1}{4}y = \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{1}{2}y + 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying the entire equation by \(12\) yields \(8(x - 6) + 3y = 10x - 6y + 12\), which simplifies to \(9y = 2x + 60\) or \(y = \frac{2}{9}x + \frac{20}{3}\). A line parallel to this has the same slope, \(\frac{2}{9}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line parallel to the equation \(0.75x - 1.25y + 2.5 = 0.45x + 0.35y - 1.8\).
qs.s: Group \(y\) terms and \(x\) terms to get \(1.60y = 0.30x + 4.30\), which gives \(y = \frac{0.3}{1.6}x + \frac{4.3}{1.6} = \frac{3}{16}x + \frac{43}{16}\). A line parallel to this has the same slope, \(\frac{3}{16}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(\frac{5x - 1}{3} - \frac{3y + 2}{4} = \frac{x - 2y}{6}\).
qs.s: Multiply through by \(12\) to clear denominators: \(4(5x - 1) - 3(3y + 2) = 2(x - 2y)\), which simplifies to \(5y = 18x - 10\) or \(y = \frac{18}{5}x - 2\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, \(-\frac{5}{18}\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(1.3x - 2.4y + 5.1 = 0.7x + 1.2y - 3.9\).
qs.s: Collecting like terms gives \(3.6y = 0.6x + 9\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{5}{2}\) with slope \(\frac{1}{6}\). The slope of a perpendicular line is the negative reciprocal, \(-6\).

qs.q: Find the slope of a line perpendicular to the equation \(0.4(3x - 5) - 1.1y = 0.2(x + 4) - 2.7y\).
qs.s: Expanding gives \(1.2x - 2.0 - 1.1y = 0.2x + 0.8 - 2.7y\), which rearranges to \(1.6y = -1.0x + 2.8\) or \(y = -\frac{5}{8}x + \frac{7}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal of \(-\frac{5}{8}\), which is \(\frac{8}{5}\).

exercises.name: Equation of parallel line through a point

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(1, 3); y = 4x - 7\).
qs.s: The parallel line has slope \(m = 4\). Using point-slope form with \((1, 3)\), \(y - 3 = 4(x - 1)\), which gives \(y - 3 = 4x - 4\), or \(4x - y = 1\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 0); y = -2x + 1\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = -2\), so using point-slope form with \((-3, 0)\) gives \(y - 0 = -2(x - (-3)) = -2x - 6\). In standard form, this is \(2x + y = -6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, -1); y = 3x + 8\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = 3\). Substituting \((2, -1)\) into point-slope form gives \(y - (-1) = 3(x - 2)\), leading to \(y + 1 = 3x - 6\), or \(3x - y = 7\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, -2); y = 5x + 3\).
qs.s: The parallel line has slope \(m = 5\) and passes through the \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), giving \(y = 5x - 2\). Rearranging into standard form yields \(5x - y = 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, 0); y = -3x + 4\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = -3\), so the parallel line also has slope \(-3\). Using \(P(0, 0)\), the equation is \(y - 0 = -3(x - 0)\), which simplifies to \(3x + y = 0\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(6, -2); y = -\frac{5}{3}x + 4\).
qs.s: The parallel slope is \(m = -\frac{5}{3}\). Using point-slope form, \(y - (-2) = -\frac{5}{3}(x - 6)\), which clears to \(3(y + 2) = -5(x - 6)\) and simplifies to \(5x + 3y = 24\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, -1); 3x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(3x - 2y = 8\) has the form \(3x - 2y = C\). Substituting \((4, -1)\) yields \(C = 3(4) - 2(-1) = 14\), giving \(3x - 2y = 14\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-5, 3); 2x + 9y - 11 = 0\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line as \(2x + 9y = 11\), a parallel line has the form \(2x + 9y = C\). Substituting \((-5, 3)\) gives \(C = 2(-5) + 9(3) = 17\), so the equation is \(2x + 9y = 17\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 5); 4x + 5y = 7\).
qs.s: A parallel line has the form \(4x + 5y = C\). Substituting \((-3, 5)\) gives \(C = 4(-3) + 5(5) = -12 + 25 = 13\), so the equation is \(4x + 5y = 13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, -7); 7x - 3y = 15\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(7x - 3y = 15\) has the form \(7x - 3y = C\). Substituting \((-2, -7)\) gives \(C = 7(-2) - 3(-7) = -14 + 21 = 7\), resulting in \(7x - 3y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(1, 3); x = 2y - 4\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line gives \(x - 2y = -4\), so a parallel line has the form \(x - 2y = C\). Substituting \(P(1, 3)\) gives \(1 - 2(3) = -5\), so the equation is \(x - 2y = -5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, -2); x = 3y + 1\).
qs.s: The given line has the form \(x - 3y = 1\), so a parallel line is \(x - 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(0, -2)\) gives \(0 - 3(-2) = 6\), resulting in \(x - 3y = 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, 0); 2x + 5y = 9\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(2x + 5y = 9\) has the form \(2x + 5y = C\). Substituting \(P(0, 0)\) gives \(2(0) + 5(0) = 0\), so the equation in standard form is \(2x + 5y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, 0); x = 3y - 7\).
qs.s: The line \(x = 3y - 7\) can be written as \(x - 3y = -7\), so any parallel line has the form \(x - 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(0, 0)\) gives \(0 - 3(0) = 0\), so the equation is \(x - 3y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, 0); y = 3x - 5\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(y = 3x - 5\) in standard form gives \(3x - y = 5\), so a parallel line has the form \(3x - y = C\). Substituting \(P(4, 0)\) gives \(3(4) - 0 = 12\), yielding \(3x - y = 12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-6, -5); \frac{x - 3}{4} + \frac{y + 1}{3} = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \(12\) gives \(3(x - 3) + 4(y + 1) = 12\), which simplifies to \(3x + 4y = 17\). A parallel line has the form \(3x + 4y = C\), and substituting \(P(-6, -5)\) gives \(3(-6) + 4(-5) = -38\), so the equation is \(3x + 4y = -38\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(7, -4); \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{2}y = \frac{5}{6}\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by \(6\) yields \(4x - 3y = 5\), so a parallel line has the form \(4x - 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(7, -4)\) gives \(4(7) - 3(-4) = 40\), resulting in \(4x - 3y = 40\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(9, -7); 2(2x - 5) - 3(y - 4) = x - 8y + 1\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms yields \(3x + 5y = -1\). A parallel line has the form \(3x + 5y = C\), and substituting \(P(9, -7)\) gives \(3(9) + 5(-7) = -8\), so the equation is \(3x + 5y = -8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-8, 11); 5x = 34 - 12y\).
qs.s: Rearranging the given equation into standard form yields \(5x + 12y = 34\). A parallel line has the form \(5x + 12y = C\), and substituting \(P(-8, 11)\) gives \(5(-8) + 12(11) = 92\), so the equation is \(5x + 12y = 92\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-5, 3); 3(x + 2) - 2(y - 1) = 5 - x + 5y\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging the given line gives \(4x - 7y = -3\). A parallel line has the form \(4x - 7y = C\), and substituting \(P(-5, 3)\) gives \(4(-5) - 7(3) = -41\), so the equation is \(4x - 7y = -41\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, 5); 2x - y = 3\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(2x - y = 3\) has the form \(2x - y = C\). Substituting \((2, 5)\) gives \(C = 2(2) - 5 = -1\), so the equation is \(2x - y = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -2); x - 2y = 5\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(x - 2y = 5\) has the form \(x - 2y = C\). Substituting \((3, -2)\) gives \(C = 3 - 2(-2) = 7\), so the equation is \(x - 2y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, 4); 4x + y = 2\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(4x + y = 2\) has the form \(4x + y = C\). Substituting \((-1, 4)\) gives \(C = 4(-1) + 4 = 0\), so the equation is \(4x + y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, -3); 5x - 3y = 1\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(5x - 3y = 1\) has the form \(5x - 3y = C\). Substituting \((-2, -3)\) gives \(C = 5(-2) - 3(-3) = -1\), so the equation is \(5x - 3y = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-7, 14); 9x - 5y = 23\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(9x - 5y = 23\) has the form \(9x - 5y = C\). Substituting \((-7, 14)\) gives \(C = 9(-7) - 5(14) = -63 - 70 = -133\), so the equation is \(9x - 5y = -133\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{2}{3}\right); 8x - 9y = 5\).
qs.s: A parallel line has the form \(8x - 9y = C\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) yields \(C = 8\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) - 9\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = 6 + 6 = 12\), so the equation is \(8x - 9y = 12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, -3); y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 7\).
qs.s: The slope of the line is \(-\frac{2}{5}\), so a parallel line in standard form has the form \(2x + 5y = C\). Substituting \((4, -3)\) yields \(C = 2(4) + 5(-3) = -7\), giving \(2x + 5y = -7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, 5); \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given line by \(4\) gives \(3x - 2y = 12\), so a parallel line has the form \(3x - 2y = C\). Substituting \((-2, 5)\) yields \(C = 3(-2) - 2(5) = -16\), resulting in \(3x - 2y = -16\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -4); 5(x + 2) - 2(y - 1) = 7\).
qs.s: Simplifying the given equation gives \(5x - 2y + 12 = 7\), or \(5x - 2y = -5\), so the parallel line has the form \(5x - 2y = C\). Substituting \((3, -4)\) gives \(C = 5(3) - 2(-4) = 23\), so the equation is \(5x - 2y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, 4); 5x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(5x - 2y = 8\) has the form \(5x - 2y = C\). Substituting \(P(-1, 4)\) gives \(5(-1) - 2(4) = -13\), so the equation in standard form is \(5x - 2y = -13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, -3); 4x + y = 5\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(4x + y = 5\) has the form \(4x + y = C\). Substituting \(P(0, -3)\) yields \(4(0) + (-3) = -3\), giving \(4x + y = -3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, -2); 2x - 7y = 1\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(2x - 7y = 1\) has the form \(2x - 7y = C\). Substituting \(P(-3, -2)\) gives \(2(-3) - 7(-2) = 8\), so the equation in standard form is \(2x - 7y = 8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, 1); 3x - 4y = 7\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(3x - 4y = 7\) has the form \(3x - 4y = C\). Substituting \(P(3, 1)\) gives \(3(3) - 4(1) = 5\), so the equation in standard form is \(3x - 4y = 5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, -5); x + 3y = -4\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(x + 3y = -4\) has the form \(x + 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(2, -5)\) gives \(1(2) + 3(-5) = -13\), so the equation in standard form is \(x + 3y = -13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(5, -2); y = -\frac{4}{7}x + 3\).
qs.s: The given line \(y = -\frac{4}{7}x + 3\) has slope \(-\frac{4}{7}\), so a parallel line has standard form \(4x + 7y = C\). Substituting \(P(5, -2)\) gives \(4(5) + 7(-2) = 6\), resulting in \(4x + 7y = 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-15, 12); 8x - 13y = 21\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(8x - 13y = 21\) has the form \(8x - 13y = C\). Substituting \(P(-15, 12)\) yields \(8(-15) - 13(12) = -120 - 156 = -276\), giving \(8x - 13y = -276\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 4); \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{4}y = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given line \(\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{1}{4}y = 1\) by \(12\) gives \(8x + 3y = 12\). A parallel line has the form \(8x + 3y = C\); substituting \(P(-3, 4)\) yields \(8(-3) + 3(4) = -12\), so the equation is \(8x + 3y = -12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(6, -5); 5x - 2y = 2(x - 3y) + 7\).
qs.s: Simplifying \(5x - 2y = 2(x - 3y) + 7\) yields \(3x + 4y = 7\). A parallel line has the form \(3x + 4y = C\); substituting \(P(6, -5)\) gives \(3(6) + 4(-5) = -2\), so the equation is \(3x + 4y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right); 5x - 4y = 9\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(5x - 4y = 9\) has the form \(5x - 4y = C\). Substituting \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) gives \(5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) - 4\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = -\frac{16}{3}\), and multiplying by \(3\) to clear denominators gives \(15x - 12y = -16\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, -4); x - 5y = 10\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(x - 5y = 10\) has the form \(x - 5y = C\). Substituting \(P(-2, -4)\) gives \((-2) - 5(-4) = 18\), so the equation in standard form is \(x - 5y = 18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, 6); 3y + x = 4\).
qs.s: The given line \(3y + x = 4\) can be written as \(x + 3y = 4\), so any parallel line has the form \(x + 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(-1, 6)\) gives \(-1 + 3(6) = 17\), which yields \(x + 3y = 17\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -2); y + 2x = -5\).
qs.s: The given line \(y + 2x = -5\) can be rewritten as \(2x + y = -5\), so any parallel line has the form \(2x + y = C\). Substituting \(P(3, -2)\) gives \(2(3) + (-2) = 4\), resulting in the equation \(2x + y = 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); y + 5x = -1\).
qs.s: The given line \(y + 5x = -1\) can be rewritten as \(5x + y = -1\), so any parallel line has the form \(5x + y = C\). Substituting \(P(-3, 2)\) gives \(5(-3) + 2 = -13\), resulting in \(5x + y = -13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, -5); y - 3x = 7\).
qs.s: The given line \(y - 3x = 7\) can be rewritten as \(3x - y = -7\), so any parallel line has the form \(3x - y = C\). Substituting \(P(2, -5)\) gives \(3(2) - (-5) = 11\), resulting in the equation \(3x - y = 11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-5, 7); 7x - 3y = 2x + 9y - 15\).
qs.s: Simplifying \(7x - 3y = 2x + 9y - 15\) gives \(5x - 12y = -15\), meaning a parallel line has the form \(5x - 12y = C\). Substituting \(P(-5, 7)\) gives \(5(-5) - 12(7) = -109\), so the equation is \(5x - 12y = -109\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-6, 5); y = -\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{5}{2}\).
qs.s: The line \(y = -\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{5}{2}\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{8}\), so any parallel line has standard form \(3x + 8y = C\). Substituting \(P(-6, 5)\) gives \(3(-6) + 8(5) = 22\), producing \(3x + 8y = 22\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-8, 9); \frac{x}{6} - \frac{y}{9} = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(\frac{x}{6} - \frac{y}{9} = 1\) by \(18\) gives \(3x - 2y = 18\), so any parallel line has the form \(3x - 2y = C\). Substituting \(P(-8, 9)\) gives \(3(-8) - 2(9) = -42\), which yields \(3x - 2y = -42\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-14, 9); 5y - 8x = 23\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line \(5y - 8x = 23\) in standard form gives \(8x - 5y = -23\), so a parallel line has the form \(8x - 5y = C\). Substituting \(P(-14, 9)\) yields \(8(-14) - 5(9) = -157\), so the equation is \(8x - 5y = -157\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(13, -4); 4(x - 2) + 3(y + 5) = 2\).
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying \(4(x - 2) + 3(y + 5) = 2\) gives \(4x + 3y = -5\), so any parallel line has the form \(4x + 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(13, -4)\) yields \(4(13) + 3(-4) = 40\), resulting in \(4x + 3y = 40\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, -1); 2y - 5 = -3x\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line in standard form gives \(3x + 2y = 5\), which has a slope of \(-\frac{3}{2}\). A parallel line through \((4, -1)\) satisfies \(3(4) + 2(-1) = 10\), giving \(3x + 2y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(6, 1); 5y - 2 = -3x\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(5y - 2 = -3x\) gives \(3x + 5y = 2\), which has a slope of \(-\frac{3}{5}\). Substituting \((6, 1)\) into \(3x + 5y = C\) gives \(3(6) + 5(1) = 23\), producing \(3x + 5y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, -4); 2x + 7 = 3y\).
qs.s: Rewriting the line as \(2x - 3y = -7\) gives a slope of \(\frac{2}{3}\). A line parallel to it passing through \((-1, -4)\) has the equation \(2(-1) - 3(-4) = 10\), yielding \(2x - 3y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); 5y - 4 = 2x\).
qs.s: Rearranging the equation yields \(2x - 5y = -4\), so the slope is \(\frac{2}{5}\). A parallel line has the form \(2x - 5y = C\); substituting \((-3, 2)\) gives \(2(-3) - 5(2) = -16\), which results in \(2x - 5y = -16\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, -5); 4y + 3 = -x\).
qs.s: The given line rearranges to \(x + 4y = -3\), with slope \(-\frac{1}{4}\). A parallel line through \((2, -5)\) satisfies \(1(2) + 4(-5) = -18\), so the equation is \(x + 4y = -18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(14, -9); 5(2x - 3) - 4(y + 2) = 3(x - 2y) + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(10x - 4y - 23 = 3x - 6y + 7\), which simplifies to \(7x + 2y = 30\). Substituting \((14, -9)\) into \(7x + 2y = C\) yields \(7(14) + 2(-9) = 80\), so the equation is \(7x + 2y = 80\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-4, 5); 3(x - 2y) + 4 = 5(2x + y) - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms in \(3(x - 2y) + 4 = 5(2x + y) - 7\) gives \(7x + 11y = 11\). Substituting \((-4, 5)\) into \(7x + 11y = C\) yields \(7(-4) + 11(5) = 27\), so the equation is \(7x + 11y = 27\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-10, 6); \frac{4x + 1}{5} - \frac{3y - 2}{2} = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying by \(10\) gives \(2(4x + 1) - 5(3y - 2) = 30\), which simplifies to \(8x - 15y = 18\). A parallel line through \((-10, 6)\) satisfies \(8(-10) - 15(6) = -170\), giving \(8x - 15y = -170\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{6}\right); 7x - 4y + 9 = 2(x - 5y)\).
qs.s: Simplifying the given equation yields \(5x + 6y = -9\). Substituting \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\) into \(5x + 6y = C\) gives \(5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) + 6\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{5}{3}\), and multiplying by \(3\) gives the standard form \(15x + 18y = 5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-7, 12); \frac{x - 3}{4} + \frac{y + 1}{6} = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by \(12\) gives \(3(x - 3) + 2(y + 1) = 12\), which simplifies to \(3x + 2y = 19\). Substituting \((-7, 12)\) into \(3x + 2y = C\) gives \(3(-7) + 2(12) = 3\), yielding \(3x + 2y = 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, 5); x = -\frac{3}{4}y + 2\).
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) gives \(y = -\frac{4}{3}x + \frac{8}{3}\), so the line has slope \(m = -\frac{4}{3}\). Substituting \(m = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(P(-2, 5)\) into point-slope form gives \(y - 5 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, 3); x = \frac{3}{2}y + 1\).
qs.s: The given line simplifies to \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{2}{3}\), giving slope \(m = \frac{2}{3}\). Using \(P(-1, 3)\) in point-slope form gives \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{3}(x + 1)\), which rearranges to \(2x - 3y = -11\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(1, -4); x = \frac{1}{3}y - 5\).
qs.s: The given equation rearranges to \(y = 3x + 15\), giving a slope of \(m = 3\). Using point-slope form with \(P(1, -4)\) yields \(y - (-4) = 3(x - 1)\), which converts to \(3x - y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -2); x = \frac{2}{5}y + 1\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line gives \(y = \frac{5}{2}x - \frac{5}{2}\), so the parallel line has slope \(m = \frac{5}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(3, -2)\) gives \(y - (-2) = \frac{5}{2}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to the standard form \(5x - 2y = 19\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, -1); x = -\frac{5}{2}y - 3\).
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) yields \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{6}{5}\), so the slope is \(m = -\frac{2}{5}\). Applying \(P(-3, -1)\) in point-slope form gives \(y + 1 = -\frac{2}{5}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(2x + 5y = -11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{5}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right); 2(3x - 4y + 1) - 5(x - 2y) = 3 - 4x\).
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms gives \(5x + 2y = 1\), so the slope is \(m = -\frac{5}{2}\). Substituting \(P\left(-\frac{5}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) into \(5x + 2y = C\) gives \(-\frac{29}{4}\), and multiplying by 4 produces the standard form \(20x + 8y = -29\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-12, 15); \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{3}{8} = \frac{7}{12}y - \frac{1}{4}x + 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 24 gives \(20x + 9 = 14y - 6x + 48\), which rearranges to \(26x - 14y = 39\) and slope \(m = \frac{13}{7}\). Substituting \(P(-12, 15)\) into \(13x - 7y = C\) gives \(13(-12) - 7(15) = -261\), so the equation is \(13x - 7y = -261\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(5, -7); \frac{2}{3}(x - 4) = \frac{3}{5}(y + 2) + 1\).
qs.s: Clearing denominators by multiplying by \(15\) yields \(10(x - 4) = 9(y + 2) + 15\), which simplifies to \(10x - 9y = 73\) with slope \(m = \frac{10}{9}\). A parallel line through \(P(5, -7)\) satisfies \(10(5) - 9(-7) = 113\), giving \(10x - 9y = 113\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-6, 8); \frac{3x - 1}{4} - \frac{2y + 5}{3} = \frac{1}{6}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD of 12 gives \(3(3x - 1) - 4(2y + 5) = 2\), which simplifies to \(9x - 8y = 25\) with slope \(m = \frac{9}{8}\). Substituting \(P(-6, 8)\) into \(9x - 8y = C\) yields \(9(-6) - 8(8) = -118\), giving \(9x - 8y = -118\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{3}\right); 5x - 4(y - 2) = 2(x + 3y) - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(3x - 10y = -15\), so the slope is \(m = \frac{3}{10}\). Substituting \(P\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\) into \(3x - 10y = C\) gives \(3\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 10\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{47}{6}\), and multiplying by 6 gives the standard form \(18x - 60y = 47\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, -1); x = -\frac{1}{2}y + 3\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(x = -\frac{1}{2}y + 3\) gives \(2x + y = 6\), which has a slope of \(-2\). A parallel line passing through \((2, -1)\) has equation \(2(2) + (-1) = 3\), which simplifies to \(2x + y = 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, 3); x = -\frac{1}{4}y + 2\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(x = -\frac{1}{4}y + 2\) in standard form gives \(4x + y = 8\), so the line has slope \(-4\). A parallel line through \((0, 3)\) has the form \(4x + y = C\), where \(C = 4(0) + 3 = 3\), giving \(4x + y = 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(0, 2); x = \frac{4}{3}y + 5\).
qs.s: Clearing fractions in \(x = \frac{4}{3}y + 5\) gives \(3x - 4y = 15\). A parallel line through \((0, 2)\) has the form \(3x - 4y = C\), where \(C = 3(0) - 4(2) = -8\), resulting in \(3x - 4y = -8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-4, 0); x = \frac{3}{5}y - 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(x = \frac{3}{5}y - 2\) by 5 and rearranging yields \(5x - 3y = -10\). A parallel line through \((-4, 0)\) satisfies \(5(-4) - 3(0) = -20\), so its equation is \(5x - 3y = -20\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 1); x = -\frac{3}{2}y - 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(x = -\frac{3}{2}y - 4\) by 2 gives \(2x + 3y = -8\). A parallel line through \((-3, 1)\) satisfies \(2(-3) + 3(1) = -3\), yielding \(2x + 3y = -3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-6, 7); \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{5}{6}y - 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 12 clears the fractions to give \(3x + 8 = -10y - 12\), or \(3x + 10y = -20\). A parallel line through \((-6, 7)\) satisfies \(3(-6) + 10(7) = 52\), giving \(3x + 10y = 52\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 14); 1 - (5x - 3y) = 2(3x + 4y) - 12\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging gives \(1 - 5x + 3y = 6x + 8y - 12\), which simplifies to \(11x + 5y = 13\). A parallel line through \((-3, 14)\) has the form \(11x + 5y = C\), where \(C = 11(-3) + 5(14) = 37\), so the equation is \(11x + 5y = 37\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(11, -13); y - 6 = -\frac{4}{7}(2x - 5)\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 7 gives \(7y - 42 = -8x + 20\), which rearranges to \(8x + 7y = 62\). A parallel line through \((11, -13)\) has the form \(8x + 7y = C\), where \(C = 8(11) + 7(-13) = -3\), yielding \(8x + 7y = -3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, -9); 3(x - 4) - 2(y + 5) = 5(2x - y) + 7\).
qs.s: Expanding both sides gives \(3x - 2y - 22 = 10x - 5y + 7\), which simplifies to \(7x - 3y = -29\). A parallel line through \((4, -9)\) has the form \(7x - 3y = C\), where \(C = 7(4) - 3(-9) = 55\), resulting in \(7x - 3y = 55\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-8, 3); \frac{2x + 1}{3} = -\frac{5y - 4}{2}\).
qs.s: Cross-multiplying gives \(2(2x + 1) = -3(5y - 4)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 15y = 10\). A parallel line through \((-8, 3)\) has the form \(4x + 15y = C\), where \(C = 4(-8) + 15(3) = 13\), giving \(4x + 15y = 13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, 8); x = -6\).
qs.s: A line parallel to the vertical line \(x = -6\) is also vertical and has the form \(x = c\). Since it passes through \(P(-1, 8)\), its equation in standard form is \(x = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-1, -4); y = \frac{2}{5}x - 3\).
qs.s: The parallel line has slope \(m = \frac{2}{5}\), so using point-slope form gives \(y - (-4) = \frac{2}{5}(x - (-1))\). Multiplying by \(5\) and rearranging terms yields the standard form \(2x - 5y = 18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-4, 1); 2x + 5y = 7\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(2x + 5y = 7\) has the form \(2x + 5y = C\). Substituting \(P(-4, 1)\) gives \(C = 2(-4) + 5(1) = -3\), yielding \(2x + 5y = -3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -2); 4x - 3y = 5\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(4x - 3y = 5\) has the form \(4x - 3y = C\). Substituting \(P(3, -2)\) gives \(C = 4(3) - 3(-2) = 18\), so the equation in standard form is \(4x - 3y = 18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(2, 5); y = 3x - 4\).
qs.s: The line \(y = 3x - 4\) has slope \(m = 3\), so the parallel line through \(P(2, 5)\) satisfies \(y - 5 = 3(x - 2)\). Rearranging into standard form gives \(3x - y = 1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, 4); y = -\frac{3}{4}x + 1\).
qs.s: The parallel line has slope \(m = -\frac{3}{4}\), giving \(y - 4 = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 2)\). Multiplying by \(4\) and rearranging into standard form yields \(3x + 4y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(5, 2); y = -9\).
qs.s: A line parallel to the horizontal line \(y = -9\) has the form \(y = c\). Passing through \(P(5, 2)\), its equation is \(y = 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-4, 7); y = -1\).
qs.s: A line parallel to the horizontal line \(y = -1\) is horizontal and has the form \(y = c\). Since it passes through \(P(-4, 7)\), its equation is \(y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-6, -3); y = 4\).
qs.s: A line parallel to the horizontal line \(y = 4\) has slope \(0\) and equation \(y = c\). Since it passes through \(P(-6, -3)\), its equation is \(y = -3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, 0); y = 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -8); y = 5\).
