qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, 5); 3x - 4y = 12\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(3x - 4y = 12\) has the form \(3x - 4y = C\). Substituting \(P(-2, 5)\) gives \(C = 3(-2) - 4(5) = -26\), resulting in \(3x - 4y = -26\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(4, -1); y = 3x - 7\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = 3\). Using point-slope form with \(P(4, -1)\) gives \(y - (-1) = 3(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(y + 1 = 3x - 12\), or \(3x - y = 13\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); y = -\frac{2}{5}x + 4\).
qs.s: The slope of the parallel line is \(m = -\frac{2}{5}\). In point-slope form, \(y - 2 = -\frac{2}{5}(x + 3)\), which cleared of fractions becomes \(5y - 10 = -2x - 6\), or \(2x + 5y = 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-4, 7); 5x + 6y = -13\).
qs.s: A line parallel to \(5x + 6y = -13\) has the form \(5x + 6y = C\). Substituting \(P(-4, 7)\) gives \(C = 5(-4) + 6(7) = -20 + 42 = 22\), yielding \(5x + 6y = 22\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(6, -1); 3x = 5y + 14\).
qs.s: Rearranging the given equation into standard form gives \(3x - 5y = 14\). A parallel line has the form \(3x - 5y = C\), and substituting \(P(6, -1)\) gives \(C = 3(6) - 5(-1) = 23\), giving \(3x - 5y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(5, 2); \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{2}y = 6\).
qs.s: Clearing denominators by multiplying by 4 gives \(3x - 2y = 24\), so a parallel line is \(3x - 2y = C\). Substituting \((5, 2)\) gives \(3(5) - 2(2) = 15 - 4 = 11\), which gives \(3x - 2y = 11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-2, -5); \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{1}{3}y = 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 15 yields \(9x + 5y = 60\), so a parallel line has the form \(9x + 5y = C\). Substituting \((-2, -5)\) gives \(9(-2) + 5(-5) = -18 - 25 = -43\), so the equation is \(9x + 5y = -43\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(3, -2); \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{2}{5}y = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD 10 gives \(5x - 4y = 30\), so any parallel line has the form \(5x - 4y = C\). Substituting \((3, -2)\) gives \(5(3) - 4(-2) = 15 + 8 = 23\), resulting in \(5x - 4y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(6, -1); \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{5}{6}y = 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 6 gives \(8x - 5y = 12\), so a parallel line is of the form \(8x - 5y = C\). Substituting \((6, -1)\) gives \(8(6) - 5(-1) = 48 + 5 = 53\), yielding \(8x - 5y = 53\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-3, 4); \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}y = 5\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 12 yields \(3x + 8y = 60\), meaning a parallel line has the form \(3x + 8y = C\). Substituting \((-3, 4)\) gives \(3(-3) + 8(4) = -9 + 32 = 23\), giving \(3x + 8y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-7, 6); \frac{3x - 2}{5} - \frac{y + 4}{2} = \frac{x - 2y}{10}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 10 gives \(2(3x - 2) - 5(y + 4) = x - 2y\), which simplifies to \(5x - 3y = 24\). Substituting \(P(-7, 6)\) into \(5x - 3y = C\) gives \(5(-7) - 3(6) = -53\), so the equation is \(5x - 3y = -53\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{4}{3}\right); \frac{5}{6}x + \frac{3}{8}y = \frac{7}{12}\).
qs.s: Multiplying by the LCD 24 gives \(20x + 9y = 14\), so a parallel line has form \(20x + 9y = C\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{4}{3}\right)\) yields \(20\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + 9\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = 10 - 12 = -2\), so \(20x + 9y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-5, 4); \frac{3}{4}(x + 2) - \frac{2}{3}(y - 1) = \frac{1}{6}x + 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 12 gives \(9(x + 2) - 8(y - 1) = 2x + 36\), which simplifies to \(7x - 8y = 10\). Substituting \(P(-5, 4)\) into \(7x - 8y = C\) yields \(7(-5) - 8(4) = -67\), producing \(7x - 8y = -67\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P(-8, -3); \frac{2}{3}(x - 4) + \frac{1}{2}(y + 6) = \frac{5}{6}(x - 2y) + 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 6 gives \(4(x - 4) + 3(y + 6) = 5(x - 2y) + 6\), which simplifies to \(x - 13y = -4\). Substituting \(P(-8, -3)\) into \(x - 13y = C\) yields \(-8 - 13(-3) = 31\), so the equation is \(x - 13y = 31\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{3}{7}\right); \frac{5}{8}x - \frac{7}{12}y = \frac{3}{4}\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 24 gives \(15x - 14y = 18\), so a parallel line is \(15x - 14y = C\). Substituting \(\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{3}{7}\right)\) gives \(15\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) - 14\left(\frac{3}{7}\right) = -6 - 6 = -12\), yielding \(15x - 14y = -12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{4}\right); \frac{1}{4}x + 0.6y = -1\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(\frac{1}{4}x + \frac{3}{5}y = -1\) by 20 gives \(5x + 12y = -20\). Substituting \(\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) into \(5x + 12y = C\) gives \(5\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) + 12\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}\), and multiplying by 3 yields \(15x + 36y = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{2}\right); 0.2x - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\).
qs.s: Clearing fractions in \(0.2x - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\) gives \(3x - 5y = 15\), which has slope \(\frac{3}{5}\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) into \(3x - 5y = C\) yields \(C = 3\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 5\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{9}{2}\), and multiplying by 2 gives \(6x - 10y = 9\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{1}{3}, -\frac{2}{5}\right); \frac{2}{5}x + 0.5y = -2\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{1}{2}y = -2\) by 10 yields \(4x + 5y = -20\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, -\frac{2}{5}\right)\) into \(4x + 5y = C\) gives \(4\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) + 5\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) = -\frac{2}{3}\), and multiplying by 3 produces \(12x + 15y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}\right); 0.75x - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(0.75x - \frac{1}{2}y = 3\) by 4 gives \(3x - 2y = 12\). Evaluating \(3x - 2y\) at \(\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{3}{4}\right)\) gives \(3\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) - 2\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{5}{2}\), and multiplying by 2 yields \(6x - 4y = -5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right); 0.5x - \frac{2}{3}y = 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying \(0.5x - \frac{2}{3}y = 4\) by 6 gives \(3x - 4y = 24\). Evaluating \(3x - 4y\) at \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) produces \(3\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) - 4\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{11}{4}\), so multiplying by 4 yields \(12x - 16y = 11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{8}\right); \frac{3}{5}x - 0.25y + 1 = \frac{1}{10}x + 0.5y\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 20 and rearranging yields \(10x - 15y = -20\), which simplifies to \(2x - 3y = -4\). Evaluating \(2x - 3y\) at \(\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{8}\right)\) gives \(2\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) - 3\left(\frac{5}{8}\right) = -\frac{27}{8}\), so multiplying by 8 results in \(16x - 24y = -27\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{4}{5}, \frac{2}{3}\right); 1.5x - \frac{5}{8}y = \frac{3}{4}(x - 2y) + 5\).
qs.s: Writing \(1.5\) as \(\frac{3}{2}\) and multiplying the entire equation by 8 yields \(12x - 5y = 6x - 12y + 40\), which rearranges to \(6x + 7y = 40\). Evaluating \(6x + 7y\) at \(\left(-\frac{4}{5}, \frac{2}{3}\right)\) yields \(6\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) + 7\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{2}{15}\), and multiplying by 15 gives \(90x + 105y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{7}{9}\right); \frac{2}{3}(x - 3) + 0.4y = \frac{1}{6}x - 1\).
qs.s: Expanding and multiplying by 30 gives \(20(x - 3) + 12y = 5x - 30\), which simplifies to \(15x + 12y = 30\) and reduces to \(5x + 4y = 10\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{7}{9}\right)\) into \(5x + 4y = C\) gives \(5\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) + 4\left(-\frac{7}{9}\right) = \frac{19}{18}\), and multiplying by 18 gives \(90x + 72y = 19\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{1}{3}\right); \frac{4}{9}x - 0.75y + \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{6}x - 0.2y\).
qs.s: Converting decimals to fractions and multiplying by 180 produces \(80x - 135y + 120 = 30x - 36y\), which simplifies to \(50x - 99y = -120\). Evaluating \(50x - 99y\) at \(\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{1}{3}\right)\) yields \(50\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) - 99\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = -20 - 33 = -53\), giving \(50x - 99y = -53\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is parallel to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{3}{8}, -\frac{5}{6}\right); \frac{1}{2}(3x - 1) - 0.6(y + 2) = \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{4}y\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 20 yields \(10(3x - 1) - 12(y + 2) = 8x - 5y\), which simplifies to \(22x - 7y = 34\). Evaluating \(22x - 7y\) at \(\left(\frac{3}{8}, -\frac{5}{6}\right)\) gives \(22\left(\frac{3}{8}\right) - 7\left(-\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{169}{12}\), and multiplying by 12 gives \(264x - 84y = 169\).

exercises.name: Equation of perpendicular line through a point

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(1, 2); y = -\frac{1}{3}x - 5\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = -\frac{1}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = 3\). Using point-slope form with \(P(1, 2)\), \(y - 2 = 3(x - 1)\), which simplifies to standard form \(3x - y = 1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, -2); y = 4x + 3\).
qs.s: The slope of the given line is \(4\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{4}\). With \(y\)-intercept \((0, -2)\), the equation is \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 2\), which in standard form is \(x + 4y = -8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, 0); y = -2x + 7\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = -2\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_\perp = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(4, 0)\), we get \(y - 0 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to standard form \(x - 2y = 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 1); y = 3x - 2\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = 3\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{3}\). Using the \(y\)-intercept \((0, 1)\), the equation is \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 1\), which rearranges to standard form \(x + 3y = 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, 2); y = 5x - 4\).
qs.s: The slope of the given line is \(5\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(-\frac{1}{5}\). Applying point-slope form with \(P(5, 2)\) gives \(y - 2 = -\frac{1}{5}(x - 5)\), which expands and rearranges to standard form \(x + 5y = 15\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-1, 4); 7x - 2y = 5\).
qs.s: The slope of \(7x - 2y = 5\) is \(m = \frac{7}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(-\frac{2}{7}\). Using \(P(-1, 4)\), we obtain \(y - 4 = -\frac{2}{7}(x + 1)\), which simplifies to \(7y - 28 = -2x - 2\), giving standard form \(2x + 7y = 26\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-4, 1); 3x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 2y = 8\) has slope \(m = \frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = -\frac{2}{3}\). Using \(P(-4, 1)\), we write \(y - 1 = -\frac{2}{3}(x + 4)\), which clears fractions to \(3y - 3 = -2x - 8\) and yields standard form \(2x + 3y = -5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, -5); 4x - 3y = 9\).
qs.s: The slope of \(4x - 3y = 9\) is \(m = \frac{4}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{3}{4}\). Substituting \(P(-2, -5)\) into \(y + 5 = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 2)\) gives \(4y + 20 = -3x - 6\), which rearranges to standard form \(3x + 4y = -26\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(6, -1); 5x + 3y = 12\).
qs.s: The slope of \(5x + 3y = 12\) is \(m = -\frac{5}{3}\), meaning the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{3}{5}\). Using \(P(6, -1)\), we have \(y + 1 = \frac{3}{5}(x - 6)\), leading to \(5y + 5 = 3x - 18\), which in standard form is \(3x - 5y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(3, -2); 2x + 5y = -10\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + 5y = -10\) has slope \(m = -\frac{2}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{5}{2}\). Using \(P(3, -2)\), we get \(y + 2 = \frac{5}{2}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to \(2y + 4 = 5x - 15\), or \(5x - 2y = 19\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 0); y = 3x - 4\).
qs.s: The line \(y = 3x - 4\) has slope \(3\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{3}\). Passing through \((0, 0)\), the line is \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x\), which in standard form is \(x + 3y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 3); x = 2y - 4\).
qs.s: The line \(x = 2y - 4\) has slope \(\frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-2\). Using \(P(0, 3)\), we have \(y - 3 = -2(x - 0)\), which simplifies to \(2x + y = 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 0); x = -3y + 6\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(x = -3y + 6\) gives \(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 2\), with slope \(-\frac{1}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(3\), giving \(y = 3x\), or \(3x - y = 0\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 0); x = 5y - 2\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(x = 5y - 2\) gives \(y = \frac{1}{5}x + \frac{2}{5}\), which has slope \(\frac{1}{5}\). The perpendicular slope is \(-5\), giving \(y = -5x\), or \(5x + y = 0\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, 0); x = -2y + 1\).
qs.s: The line \(x = -2y + 1\) has slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(2\). Using point \((4, 0)\), \(y - 0 = 2(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(2x - y = 8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, -3); 5x - 3(y - 2) = -2x + y + 10\).
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(7x - 4y = 4\) with slope \(\frac{7}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{7}\). Using \(P(5, -3)\), \(y - (-3) = -\frac{4}{7}(x - 5)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 7y = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, -6); 3(3x - 1) = 5y + 19\).
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(9x - 5y = 22\), with slope \(\frac{9}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{5}{9}\). Using \(P(4, -6)\), \(y - (-6) = -\frac{5}{9}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(5x + 9y = -34\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, -2); 4(x - 1) + 3y = 7x - 5y + 2\).
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(3x - 8y = -6\), so the slope is \(\frac{3}{8}\) and the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{8}{3}\). Using \(P(5, -2)\), \(y - (-2) = -\frac{8}{3}(x - 5)\), which simplifies to \(8x + 3y = 34\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); 2(x + 5y) + 3(x + y) = y + 8\).
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(5x + 12y = 8\), which has slope \(-\frac{5}{12}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(\frac{12}{5}\). Using \(P(-3, 2)\), \(y - 2 = \frac{12}{5}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(12x - 5y = -46\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 5); 3x - 5y = 2y - 7\).
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(3x - 7y = -7\), which has slope \(\frac{3}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{7}{3}\). Using \(P(-3, 5)\), \(y - 5 = -\frac{7}{3}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(7x + 3y = -6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, 1); x + 2y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(x + 2y = 8\) has slope \(m = -\frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = 2\). Using point-slope form with \(P(5, 1)\), \(y - 1 = 2(x - 5)\), which simplifies to standard form \(2x - y = 9\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(3, -1); x - 2y = 4\).
qs.s: The line \(x - 2y = 4\) has slope \(m = \frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -2\). Using point-slope form with \(P(3, -1)\), \(y + 1 = -2(x - 3)\), which simplifies to standard form \(2x + y = 5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(2, 4); 2x + y = 5\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + y = 5\) has slope \(m = -2\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_{\perp} = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(2, 4)\), \(y - 4 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to standard form \(x - 2y = -6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, 1); x + 3y = 9\).
qs.s: The line \(x + 3y = 9\) has slope \(m = -\frac{1}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = 3\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-2, 1)\), \(y - 1 = 3(x + 2)\), which simplifies to standard form \(3x - y = -7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-1, -2); 4x - y = 3\).
qs.s: The line \(4x - y = 3\) has slope \(m = 4\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{4}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-1, -2)\), \(y + 2 = -\frac{1}{4}(x + 1)\), which simplifies to standard form \(x + 4y = -9\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 4); 5x + 2y = 11\).
qs.s: The slope of \(5x + 2y = 11\) is \(m = -\frac{5}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_{\perp} = \frac{2}{5}\). Substituting \(P(-3, 4)\) into point-slope form gives \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{5}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to standard form \(2x - 5y = -26\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, -5); 7x - 4y = 18\).
qs.s: The slope of \(7x - 4y = 18\) is \(m = \frac{7}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{4}{7}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-2, -5)\) gives \(y + 5 = -\frac{4}{7}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to standard form \(4x + 7y = -43\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(3, -4); 6x + 9y = 14\).
qs.s: The slope of \(6x + 9y = 14\) is \(m = -\frac{6}{9} = -\frac{2}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{3}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(3, -4)\) gives \(y + 4 = \frac{3}{2}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to standard form \(3x - 2y = 17\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, -5); 3x = -8y + 7\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(3x = -8y + 7\) gives \(3x + 8y = 7\) with slope \(m = -\frac{3}{8}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{8}{3}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(4, -5)\) yields \(y + 5 = \frac{8}{3}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to standard form \(8x - 3y = 47\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, -1); 4x + 5y = 2\).
qs.s: The line \(4x + 5y = 2\) has slope \(-\frac{4}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{5}{4}\). Using \(P(-3, -1)\), the line is \(y + 1 = \frac{5}{4}(x + 3)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(5x - 4y = -11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-1, 2); x - 3y = 4\).
qs.s: The line \(x - 3y = 4\) has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-3\). Using \(P(-1, 2)\), the line is \(y - 2 = -3(x + 1)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(3x + y = -1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(2, -3); 5x - 2y = 1\).
qs.s: The line \(5x - 2y = 1\) has slope \(\frac{5}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{2}{5}\). Using \(P(2, -3)\), the line is \(y + 3 = -\frac{2}{5}(x - 2)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x + 5y = -11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, 0); 3x + 2y = 5\).
qs.s: The line \(3x + 2y = 5\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{2}{3}\). Using \(P(4, 0)\), the line is \(y - 0 = \frac{2}{3}(x - 4)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x - 3y = 8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(0, 3); 3x - 4y = 7\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 4y = 7\) has slope \(\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{3}\). Using \(P(0, 3)\), the line is \(y - 3 = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 0)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(4x + 3y = 9\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{2}\right); 6x - 4y = 7\).
qs.s: The line \(6x - 4y = 7\) has simplified slope \(\frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{2}{3}\). Using \(y - \frac{5}{2} = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)\) and simplifying leads to \(2x + 3y = 6\) in simplest standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{2}{3}\right); 3x - 5y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 5y = 8\) has slope \(\frac{3}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{5}{3}\). Substituting into \(y + \frac{2}{3} = -\frac{5}{3}\left(x - \frac{1}{2}\right)\) and multiplying through by 6 yields \(6y + 4 = -10x + 5\), which gives \(10x + 6y = 1\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, -1); \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{3}y = 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given line by 15 gives \(6x - 5y = 30\), which has slope \(\frac{6}{5}\). The perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{5}{6}\), so the line through \((4, -1)\) is \(y + 1 = -\frac{5}{6}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(5x + 6y = 14\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); 5(x - 1) + 2y = 3(x + 2y) - 7\).
qs.s: Expanding and rearranging the given line gives \(2x - 4y = -2\), which has slope \(\frac{1}{2}\). The perpendicular slope is \(-2\), so through \((-3, 2)\) the line is \(y - 2 = -2(x + 3)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x + y = -4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-8, 12); 7x - 11y = 4\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(\frac{7}{11}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{11}{7}\). Using \(P(-8, 12)\), we have \(y - 12 = -\frac{11}{7}(x + 8)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(11x + 7y = -4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, -2); y - 2x = 7\).
qs.s: The line \(y - 2x = 7\) has slope \(m = 2\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}\). Substituting \(P(-3, -2)\) into \(y + 2 = -\frac{1}{2}(x + 3)\) gives \(2y + 4 = -x - 3\), which simplifies to \(x + 2y = -7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, -1); y - 3x = 5\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, 2); x + 5y = -10\).
qs.s: The line \(x + 5y = -10\) has slope \(m = -\frac{1}{5}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = 5\). Using point-slope form with \(P(5, 2)\) gives \(y - 2 = 5(x - 5)\), which simplifies to \(5x - y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, 5); 2x + y = 3\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + y = 3\) has slope \(m = -2\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-2, 5)\) gives \(y - 5 = \frac{1}{2}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(x - 2y = -12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(1, -4); y + 3x = -2\).
qs.s: The line \(y + 3x = -2\) has slope \(m = -3\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{1}{3}\). Using \(P(1, -4)\) in \(y + 4 = \frac{1}{3}(x - 1)\) gives \(3(y + 4) = x - 1\), which simplifies to \(x - 3y = 13\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, -8); 6x + 9y = 14\).
qs.s: The line \(6x + 9y = 14\) has slope \(m = -\frac{6}{9} = -\frac{2}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{3}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-3, -8)\) gives \(y + 8 = \frac{3}{2}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(3x - 2y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(7, -5); 6y = -5x + 15\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(6y = -5x + 15\) gives \(y = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{5}{2}\) with slope \(m = -\frac{5}{6}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{6}{5}\). Using \(P(7, -5)\) gives \(y + 5 = \frac{6}{5}(x - 7)\), which clears to \(6x - 5y = 67\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-5, 4); 3x - 7y = 11\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 7y = 11\) has slope \(m = \frac{3}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{7}{3}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-5, 4)\) gives \(y - 4 = -\frac{7}{3}(x + 5)\), which expands and rearranges to \(7x + 3y = -23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(9, -3); 8x - 14y = 21\).
qs.s: The line \(8x - 14y = 21\) has slope \(m = \frac{8}{14} = \frac{4}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{7}{4}\). Substituting \(P(9, -3)\) into \(y + 3 = -\frac{7}{4}(x - 9)\) and clearing denominators results in \(7x + 4y = 51\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, 7); 9y - 4x = 18\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(9y - 4x = 18\) yields \(y = \frac{4}{9}x + 2\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{9}{4}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(-2, 7)\) gives \(y - 7 = -\frac{9}{4}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(9x + 4y = 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(-3, -2)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(2y + 7 = -3x\).
qs.s: The line \(3x + 2y = -7\) has slope \(m_1 = -\frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m = \frac{2}{3}\). Using \(P(-3, -2)\) gives \(y + 2 = \frac{2}{3}(x + 3)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x - 3y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(3, 4)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(2y - 3 = -5x\).
qs.s: The given line \(2y - 3 = -5x\) has slope \(m_1 = -\frac{5}{2}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m = \frac{2}{5}\). Using the point-slope form with \(P(3, 4)\) gives \(y - 4 = \frac{2}{5}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to standard form as \(2x - 5y = -14\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(4, -1)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(5y - 4 = 2x\).
qs.s: Rewriting the given line as \(2x - 5y = -4\) gives a slope of \(m_1 = \frac{2}{5}\), meaning the perpendicular slope is \(m = -\frac{5}{2}\). Substituting \(P(4, -1)\) into point-slope form gives \(y + 1 = -\frac{5}{2}(x - 4)\), which rearranges to \(5x + 2y = 18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(6, 1)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(y - 8 = -2x\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + y = 8\) has slope \(m_1 = -2\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m = \frac{1}{2}\). Applying point-slope form with \(P(6, 1)\) yields \(y - 1 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 6)\), which rearranges to \(x - 2y = 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(-2, 5)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(4y - 1 = 3x\).
qs.s: The line \(4y - 1 = 3x\) has slope \(m_1 = \frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using \(P(-2, 5)\), we write \(y - 5 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(\frac{2x + 1}{5} + \frac{3 - y}{2} = 1\).

Using \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\), the equation \(y - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{5}{4}\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)\) simplifies to \(5x + 4y = 0\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(-2, 3)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(3(x - 2y) + 8 = 2(4x + y) - 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P(15, -8)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(7x + 9y = 12x - 3y + 40\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the point \(P\left(\frac{5}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) and is perpendicular to the line \(4(2x - y) + 5 = 3(x + 2y) - 1\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-5, -2); x = 4\).
qs.s: The given line \(x = 4\) is vertical, so a line perpendicular to it is horizontal with the form \(y = k\). Passing through \(P(-5, -2)\), the equation is \(y = -2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 7); x = -2\).
qs.s: The given line \(x = -2\) is vertical, so any line perpendicular to it must be horizontal with the equation \(y = k\). Since it passes through \(P(-3, 7)\), the equation is \(y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(6, -8); y = -1\).
qs.s: The given line \(y = -1\) is horizontal, so any line perpendicular to it is vertical with the form \(x = k\). Passing through \(P(6, -8)\), the equation is \(x = 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 2); y = \frac{3}{5}x - 2\).
qs.s: The slope of the given line is \(\frac{3}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{5}{3}\). Using \(P(-3, 2)\), we have \(y - 2 = -\frac{5}{3}(x + 3)\), which rearranges to \(5x + 3y = -9\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, -7); 5x - 6y = 13\).
qs.s: The slope of \(5x - 6y = 13\) is \(m = \frac{5}{6}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(-\frac{6}{5}\). Using \(P(-2, -7)\), we have \(y + 7 = -\frac{6}{5}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(6x + 5y = -47\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-4, 3); 2x + 5y = -10\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = -\frac{2}{5}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = \frac{5}{2}\). Using \(P(-4, 3)\), we have \(y - 3 = \frac{5}{2}(x + 4)\), which converts to standard form \(5x - 2y = -26\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(1, -5); 3x - 4y = 8\).
qs.s: The slope of \(3x - 4y = 8\) is \(m = -\frac{3}{-4} = \frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{3}\). Using \(P(1, -5)\), we get \(y + 5 = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = -11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(4, 1); y = -2x + 7\).
qs.s: The given line has slope \(m = -2\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(4, 1)\) gives \(y - 1 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to the standard form \(x - 2y = 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(2, -3); \frac{4}{3}x - \frac{1}{2}y = 6\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given equation by 6 gives \(8x - 3y = 36\) with slope \(\frac{8}{3}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(-\frac{3}{8}\). Substituting \(P(2, -3)\) into \(3x + 8y = C\) gives \(3(2) + 8(-3) = -18\), resulting in \(3x + 8y = -18\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-2, 5); \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{1}{2}y = 3\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given equation by 10 gives \(6x + 5y = 30\) with slope \(-\frac{6}{5}\), which means the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{5}{6}\). Substituting \(P(-2, 5)\) into \(5x - 6y = C\) gives \(5(-2) - 6(5) = -40\), giving \(5x - 6y = -40\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(3, -2); \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{2}{3}y = 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given equation by 6 yields \(3x - 4y = 24\) with slope \(\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\). Substituting \(P(3, -2)\) into \(4x + 3y = C\) gives \(4(3) + 3(-2) = 6\), resulting in \(4x + 3y = 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, -1); \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{2}{5}y = 5\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given equation by 20 gives \(5x + 8y = 100\) with slope \(-\frac{5}{8}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{8}{5}\). Substituting \(P(-3, -1)\) into \(8x - 5y = C\) produces \(8(-3) - 5(-1) = -19\), so the equation is \(8x - 5y = -19\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(1, 4); \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{3}y = 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given equation by 12 gives \(9x - 4y = 24\) with slope \(\frac{9}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{9}\). Substituting \(P(1, 4)\) into \(4x + 9y = C\) yields \(4(1) + 9(4) = 40\), giving \(4x + 9y = 40\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-3, 8); \frac{5}{6}x - 2 = \frac{1}{4}x - \frac{2}{3}y + 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 12 and rearranging gives \(7x + 8y = 36\) with slope \(-\frac{7}{8}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{8}{7}\). Substituting \(P(-3, 8)\) into \(8x - 7y = C\) yields \(8(-3) - 7(8) = -80\), so the equation is \(8x - 7y = -80\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-1, -6); \frac{2}{3}(x - 4) - \frac{3}{5}(y + 1) = 2\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 15 and simplifying yields \(10x - 9y = 79\) with slope \(\frac{10}{9}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(-\frac{9}{10}\). Substituting \(P(-1, -6)\) into \(9x + 10y = C\) gives \(9(-1) + 10(-6) = -69\), so the equation is \(9x + 10y = -69\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(5, -2); \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{6}y = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{2}y - 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 12 and collecting like terms yields \(5x - 8y = -12\) with slope \(\frac{5}{8}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{8}{5}\). Substituting \(P(5, -2)\) into \(8x + 5y = C\) gives \(8(5) + 5(-2) = 30\), resulting in \(8x + 5y = 30\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{3}{4}\right); \frac{4}{9}x + \frac{5}{6}y = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 18 gives \(8x + 15y = 18\) with slope \(-\frac{8}{15}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{15}{8}\). Substituting \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{3}{4}\right)\) into \(15x - 8y = C\) gives \(15\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) - 8\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = 10 + 6 = 16\), giving \(15x - 8y = 16\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P(-6, 7); \frac{5}{8}x - \frac{7}{12}y = \frac{3}{4}\).
qs.s: Multiplying the equation by 24 gives \(15x - 14y = 18\) with slope \(\frac{15}{14}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{14}{15}\). Substituting \(P(-6, 7)\) into \(14x + 15y = C\) yields \(14(-6) + 15(7) = 21\), so the equation is \(14x + 15y = 21\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{4}\right); 0.8x + \frac{1}{3}y = -2\).
qs.s: The given line \(0.8x + \frac{1}{3}y = -2\) has slope \(m = -\frac{12}{5}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_{\perp} = \frac{5}{12}\). Using the point \(P\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\) gives \(y + \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{12}\left(x - \frac{2}{3}\right)\), which simplifies to standard form as \(15x - 36y = 19\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right); 0.5x + \frac{1}{4}y = 1\).
qs.s: The given line \(0.5x + \frac{1}{4}y = 1\) has slope \(m = -2\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_{\perp} = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P\left(-\frac{1}{3}, \frac{1}{2}\right)\) gives \(y - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{1}{2}\left(x + \frac{1}{3}\right)\), which simplifies to standard form as \(3x - 6y = -4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{1}{4}\right); 0.6x + \frac{1}{2}y = -1\).
qs.s: The line \(0.6x + \frac{1}{2}y = -1\) has slope \(m = -\frac{6}{5}\), which means the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{5}{6}\). Using point-slope form with \(P\left(-\frac{2}{5}, \frac{1}{4}\right)\) gives \(y - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{6}\left(x + \frac{2}{5}\right)\), simplifying to \(10x - 12y = -7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right); \frac{2}{3}x - 0.2y = 3\).
qs.s: The line \(\frac{2}{3}x - 0.2y = 3\) has slope \(m = \frac{10}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{3}{10}\). Substituting \(P\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) into \(y + \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{3}{10}\left(x - \frac{3}{4}\right)\) yields \(12x + 40y = -11\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{5}\right); \frac{3}{4}x - 0.5y = 1\).
qs.s: The line \(\frac{3}{4}x - 0.5y = 1\) has slope \(m = \frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{2}{3}\). Substituting \(P\left(-\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{3}{5}\right)\) into point-slope form yields \(y + \frac{3}{5} = -\frac{2}{3}\left(x + \frac{1}{2}\right)\), which simplifies to \(10x + 15y = -14\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{3}{5}\right); 0.8(2x - y) - \frac{1}{4}(x + 3) = \frac{1}{5}(y - 2x) + 0.5\).
qs.s: Clearing fractions by multiplying by 20 simplifies the line to \(7x - 4y = 5\) with slope \(m = \frac{7}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{4}{7}\). Substituting \(P\left(-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{3}{5}\right)\) into \(y - \frac{3}{5} = -\frac{4}{7}\left(x + \frac{2}{3}\right)\) and multiplying by 105 results in \(60x + 105y = 23\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{7}{4}\right); \frac{3}{5}(y + 4) - 0.75(x - 2) = \frac{1}{2}(x + y)\).
qs.s: Multiplying by 20 and grouping terms simplifies the line to \(25x - 2y = 78\) with slope \(m = \frac{25}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{2}{25}\). Using point-slope form with \(P\left(\frac{5}{6}, -\frac{7}{4}\right)\) yields \(y + \frac{7}{4} = -\frac{2}{25}\left(x - \frac{5}{6}\right)\), which rearranges to \(24x + 300y = -521\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{6}\right); \frac{2}{3}(x - 1) - 0.4(y + 2) = \frac{1}{6}x + 0.1\).
qs.s: Simplifying the given line equation yields \(5x - 4y = \frac{47}{3}\) with slope \(m = \frac{5}{4}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{4}{5}\). Using \(P\left(-\frac{3}{4}, \frac{5}{6}\right)\) in point-slope form gives \(y - \frac{5}{6} = -\frac{4}{5}\left(x + \frac{3}{4}\right)\), which simplifies to \(24x + 30y = 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(\frac{5}{3}, -\frac{3}{8}\right); 0.75(x + 2) - \frac{1}{3}y = \frac{1}{4}(y - 1) + 1.5x\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(9x + 7y = 21\) with slope \(m = -\frac{9}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{7}{9}\). Applying \(y + \frac{3}{8} = \frac{7}{9}\left(x - \frac{5}{3}\right)\) and multiplying through by 216 gives \(168x - 216y = 361\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in standard form, that passes through the given point and is perpendicular to the given line: \(P\left(-\frac{7}{5}, -\frac{4}{3}\right); \frac{1}{2}(x - 3y) + 0.2(2x + y) = 1.4\).
qs.s: Multiplying the given line by 10 and combining terms gives \(9x - 13y = 14\) with slope \(m = \frac{9}{13}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{13}{9}\). Substituting \(P\left(-\frac{7}{5}, -\frac{4}{3}\right)\) into point-slope form gives \(y + \frac{4}{3} = -\frac{13}{9}\left(x + \frac{7}{5}\right)\), which simplifies to \(65x + 45y = -151\).

exercises.name: Equation of parallel line from a graph

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((3, -2)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((2, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - 1}{2 - 0} = -\frac{1}{2}\). The parallel line through \((3, -2)\) is \(y - (-2) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(x + 2y = -1\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((1, 2)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((3, 1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{1 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\). A parallel line through \((1, 2)\) has equation \(y - 2 = \frac{2}{3}(x - 1)\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x - 3y = -4\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-1, 4)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((3, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{1}{3}\). Using point-slope form with \((-1, 4)\), we get \(y - 4 = \frac{1}{3}(x + 1)\), which converts to standard form as \(x - 3y = -13\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((4, -1)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((2, -2)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-2 - 1}{2 - 0} = -\frac{3}{2}\). A line with the same slope through \((4, -1)\) has equation \(y - (-1) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 2y = 10\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-2, 1)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((1, 2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-1)}{1 - 0} = 3\). The equation of a parallel line through \((-2, 1)\) is \(y - 1 = 3(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(3x - y = -7\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((7, -4)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: Reading grid points \((-3, 5)\) and \((-1, 0)\) from the graph, the slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 5}{-1 - (-3)} = -\frac{5}{2}\). Using the point \((7, -4)\), the parallel line equation is \(y - (-4) = -\frac{5}{2}(x - 7)\), which expands to \(5x + 2y = 27\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line and a point \(P\). Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through \(P\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((-2, 2)\) and \((2, -1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 2}{2 - (-2)} = -\frac{3}{4}\), and point \(P\) is located at \((-5, -3)\). The parallel line is \(y - (-3) = -\frac{3}{4}(x - (-5))\), which rearranges to \(3x + 4y = -27\).

qs.q: The graph shows a line. Determine the equation of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-8, 9)\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((-1, -1)\) and \((3, 2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-1)}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{3}{4}\). A line parallel to it passing through \((-8, 9)\) satisfies \(y - 9 = \frac{3}{4}(x + 8)\), which simplifies to standard form as \(3x - 4y = -60\).

qs.q: The graph shows triangle \(ABC\). Determine the equation of the line parallel to side \(AB\) that passes through vertex \(C\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: From the coordinates \(A(-4, -1)\) and \(B(2, 3)\), the slope of side \(AB\) is \(m = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{4}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\). Using vertex \(C(1, -3)\), the parallel line has equation \(y - (-3) = \frac{2}{3}(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(2x - 3y = 11\).

qs.q: The graph shows rectangle $ABCD$ and dashed diagonal \(AC\). Determine the equation of the line parallel to diagonal \(AC\) that passes through vertex \(D\), in standard form \(Ax + By = C\).
qs.s: From vertices \(A(-3, 3)\) and \(C(5, -1)\), the slope of diagonal \(AC\) is \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{5 - (-3)} = -\frac{1}{2}\). The parallel line passing through vertex \(D(-1, -3)\) is \(y - (-3) = -\frac{1}{2}(x - (-1))\), which in standard form is \(x + 2y = -7\).

qs.q: A line is shown on the coordinate plane below. Determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((3, -1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, 2)\) and \((1, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - 2}{1 - 0} = -2\). The parallel line through \((3, -1)\) has equation \(y - (-1) = -2(x - 3)\), which rearranges to standard form as \(2x + y = 5\).

qs.q: Determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line parallel to the line shown on the coordinate plane that passes through the point \((5, 2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((3, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{1}{3}\). The line parallel to it passing through \((5, 2)\) has equation \(y - 2 = \frac{1}{3}(x - 5)\), which simplifies to \(x - 3y = -1\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to find the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through \((2, -1)\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((4, 4)\), yielding slope \(m = \frac{4 - 1}{4 - 0} = \frac{3}{4}\). Using the point \((2, -1)\), the parallel line equation is \(y - (-1) = \frac{3}{4}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to \(3x - 4y = 10\).

qs.q: A line is graphed on the coordinate plane below. Find the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-2, -3)\).
qs.s: From the graph, the line passes through \((-1, 1)\) and \((1, -2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - 1}{1 - (-1)} = -\frac{3}{2}\). A parallel line through \((-2, -3)\) satisfies \(y - (-3) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - (-2))\), which in standard form is \(3x + 2y = -12\).

qs.q: A line is shown on the coordinate plane below. Find the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((-4, -1)\).
qs.s: From the graph, the line passes through \((0, -2)\) and \((3, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - (-2)}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\). A parallel line also has slope \(\frac{2}{3}\), and using the point \((-4, -1)\) gives \(y - (-1) = \frac{2}{3}(x - (-4))\), which simplifies in standard form to \(2x - 3y = -5\).

qs.q: A line is shown on the coordinate plane. Find the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the midpoint of the line segment connecting \(P(-5, 9)\) and \(Q(1, -3)\).
qs.s: The graphed line has slope \(m = \frac{1 - 4}{1 - (-3)} = -\frac{3}{4}\), and the midpoint of \(PQ\) is \(\left(\frac{-5 + 1}{2}, \frac{9 - 3}{2}\right) = (-2, 3)\). Writing the equation with slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\) through \((-2, 3)\) gives \(y - 3 = -\frac{3}{4}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 4y = 6\).

qs.q: A line is shown on the coordinate plane below. Determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line parallel to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-7, 4)\).
qs.s: From the graph, the line passes through \((-1, -2)\) and \((2, 3)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-2)}{2 - (-1)} = \frac{5}{3}\). The parallel line through \((-7, 4)\) is given by \(y - 4 = \frac{5}{3}(x + 7)\), which expands and rearranges to standard form as \(5x - 3y = -47\).

qs.q: Lines \(L_1\) and \(L_2\) are shown on the coordinate plane. Determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line that is parallel to line \(L_1\) and passes through the \(y\)-intercept of line \(L_2\).
qs.s: Line \(L_1\) passes through \((-4, -2)\) and \((2, 3)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{3 - (-2)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{5}{6}\), and line \(L_2\) crosses the \(y\)-axis at \((0, -3)\). The parallel line through \((0, -3)\) has equation \(y = \frac{5}{6}x - 3\), which in standard form is \(5x - 6y = 18\).

qs.q: Use the graph below to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the plotted point \(P\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, 2)\) and \((5, -1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 2}{5 - 0} = -\frac{3}{5}\). Reading point \(P(-4, -3)\) from the grid, the equation of the parallel line is \(y - (-3) = -\frac{3}{5}(x - (-4))\), which simplifies to \(3x + 5y = -27\).

qs.q: Triangle \(ABC\) is shown on the coordinate plane below. Determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)) of the line that is parallel to side \(AB\) and passes through vertex \(C\).
qs.s: Side \(AB\) connects \(A(-4, -1)\) and \(B(3, 4)\), with slope \(m = \frac{4 - (-1)}{3 - (-4)} = \frac{5}{7}\). The parallel line passing through vertex \(C(-2, 5)\) is \(y - 5 = \frac{5}{7}(x + 2)\), which rearranges to standard form as \(5x - 7y = -45\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(4, 1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = \frac{1}{2}\). The parallel line through \(P(4, 1)\) satisfies \(y - 1 = \frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(x - 2y = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(1, 4)\).
qs.s: The graphed line has a slope of \(m = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = 2\). Using point-slope form with \(P(1, 4)\), \(y - 4 = 2(x - 1)\), which rearranges to \(2x - y = -2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(-1, 2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line has a slope of \(m = \frac{1 - 3}{1 - 0} = -2\). Substituting \(P(-1, 2)\) into point-slope form gives \(y - 2 = -2(x + 1)\), which simplifies to \(2x + y = 0\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(2, -1)\).
qs.s: The slope of the graphed line is \(m = \frac{4 - 1}{1 - 0} = 3\). Using the point \(P(2, -1)\), the parallel line equation is \(y - (-1) = 3(x - 2)\), which simplifies to \(3x - y = 7\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(3, 2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, 2)\) and \((2, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 2}{2 - 0} = -1\). A parallel line through \(P(3, 2)\) has equation \(y - 2 = -(x - 3)\), which simplifies to \(x + y = 5\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(-2, 5)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-3, -2)\) and \((1, 1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{1 - (-2)}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{3}{4}\). The parallel line through \(P(-2, 5)\) is \(y - 5 = \frac{3}{4}(x + 2)\), which clears fractions to \(3x - 4y = -26\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(-5, -3)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-3, 3)\) and \((2, 1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{1 - 3}{2 - (-3)} = -\frac{2}{5}\). With \(P(-5, -3)\), the parallel line equation is \(y + 3 = -\frac{2}{5}(x + 5)\), which rearranges to \(2x + 5y = -25\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(-4, 3)\).
qs.s: The graphed line has slope \(m = \frac{1 - (-4)}{0 - (-2)} = \frac{5}{2}\). A parallel line passing through \(P(-4, 3)\) satisfies \(y - 3 = \frac{5}{2}(x + 4)\), yielding \(5x - 2y = -26\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(-3, -2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-2, 3)\) and \((1, -1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{1 - (-2)} = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using \(P(-3, -2)\), we get \(y + 2 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = -18\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \(P(3, -4)\).
qs.s: The slope of the graphed line is \(m = \frac{1 - 4}{0 - (-5)} = -\frac{3}{5}\). Using \(P(3, -4)\), the parallel line equation is \(y + 4 = -\frac{3}{5}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 5y = -11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((-3, 5)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((4, 1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{1 - (-1)}{4 - 0} = \frac{1}{2}\). The parallel line through \((-3, 5)\) satisfies \(y - 5 = \frac{1}{2}(x + 3)\), which rearranges to \(x - 2y = -13\) in standard form.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((2, -4)\).
qs.s: The graphed line has points \((-1, 3)\) and \((1, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - 3}{1 - (-1)} = -\frac{3}{2}\). A parallel line through \((2, -4)\) has equation \(y - (-4) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 2y = -2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((3, -2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line contains \((0, -1)\) and \((1, 2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-1)}{1 - 0} = 3\). The parallel line through \((3, -2)\) satisfies \(y - (-2) = 3(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(3x - y = 11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((4, 1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, 3)\) and \((2, -1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{2 - 0} = -2\). A parallel line through \((4, 1)\) has equation \(y - 1 = -2(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(2x + y = 9\) in standard form.

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((6, -1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-3, 3)\) and \((3, 1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{1 - 3}{3 - (-3)} = -\frac{1}{3}\). Using point-slope form with \((6, -1)\), we get \(y - (-1) = -\frac{1}{3}(x - 6)\), which simplifies to \(x + 3y = 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((5, 8)\).
qs.s: The graphed line contains \((-2, -4)\) and \((1, 3)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-4)}{1 - (-2)} = \frac{7}{3}\). Writing the equation of the parallel line through \((5, 8)\) gives \(y - 8 = \frac{7}{3}(x - 5) \implies 3y - 24 = 7x - 35\), which simplifies to \(7x - 3y = 11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((8, -3)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-4, 3)\) and \((2, -2)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-2 - 3}{2 - (-4)} = -\frac{5}{6}\). The parallel line through \((8, -3)\) has equation \(y - (-3) = -\frac{5}{6}(x - 8) \implies 6y + 18 = -5x + 40\), which gives \(5x + 6y = 22\).

qs.q: Line ℓ and point P are shown on the coordinate plane. Determine the standard form equation of the line passing through point P that is parallel to line ℓ.
qs.s: From the graph, line ℓ passes through \((-5, -2)\) and \((-1, 3)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-2)}{-1 - (-5)} = \frac{5}{4}\), and point P is located at \((3, -1)\). The parallel line has equation \(y - (-1) = \frac{5}{4}(x - 3) \implies 4(y + 1) = 5(x - 3)\), which gives \(5x - 4y = 19\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((-5, 7)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-4, 5)\) and \((2, -3)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-3 - 5}{2 - (-4)} = -\frac{4}{3}\). The line parallel to it through \((-5, 7)\) has equation \(y - 7 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 5) \implies 3y - 21 = -4x - 20\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line that is parallel to the graphed line and passes through the point \((-4, -7)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-1, -1)\) and \((1, 4)\), yielding a slope of \(m = \frac{4 - (-1)}{1 - (-1)} = \frac{5}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \((-4, -7)\), \(y - (-7) = \frac{5}{2}(x - (-4)) \implies 2y + 14 = 5x + 20\), which rearranges to \(5x - 2y = -6\).

exercises.name: Equation of perpendicular line from a graph

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(3, -3)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-4, -2)\) and \((0, 1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{1 - (-2)}{0 - (-4)} = \frac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{4}{3}\), and using point \(P(3, -3)\) yields \(y - (-3) = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to standard form \(4x + 3y = 3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-3, 2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-1, 4)\) and \((1, -2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - 4}{1 - (-1)} = -3\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{1}{3}\), and using point \(P(-3, 2)\) gives \(y - 2 = \frac{1}{3}(x - (-3))\), which simplifies to standard form \(x - 3y = -9\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(2, -1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-3, 3)\) and \((3, -1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{3 - (-3)} = -\frac{2}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{3}{2}\), and using \(P(2, -1)\) gives \(y - (-1) = \frac{3}{2}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to standard form \(3x - 2y = 8\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(3, 2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-2, -3)\) and \((2, -1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - (-3)}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{1}{2}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -2\), so using point \(P(3, 2)\) gives \(y - 2 = -2(x - 3)\), which simplifies to standard form \(2x + y = 8\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(4, 1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = 2\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{1}{2}\), and using point \(P(4, 1)\) gives \(y - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to standard form \(x + 2y = 6\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-2, -5)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-6, 3)\) and \((6, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 3}{6 - (-6)} = -\frac{1}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = 4\), so using point \(P(-2, -5)\) gives \(y - (-5) = 4(x - (-2))\), which simplifies to standard form \(4x - y = -3\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-3, -4)\).
qs.s: Using the marked points \((-6, 7)\) and \((4, -1)\), the graphed line has slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 7}{4 - (-6)} = -\frac{4}{5}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{5}{4}\), so \(y - (-4) = \frac{5}{4}(x - (-3))\), which in standard form is \(5x - 4y = 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-6, 1)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-2, -7)\) and \((4, 8)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{8 - (-7)}{4 - (-2)} = \frac{5}{2}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{2}{5}\), so \(y - 1 = -\frac{2}{5}(x - (-6))\), which simplifies to standard form \(2x + 5y = -7\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(5, -2)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-5, -6)\) and \((1, 4)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{4 - (-6)}{1 - (-5)} = \frac{5}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = -\frac{3}{5}\), so \(y - (-2) = -\frac{3}{5}(x - 5)\), which in standard form is \(3x + 5y = 5\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-4, 5)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-7, 2)\) and \((5, -7)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-7 - 2}{5 - (-7)} = -\frac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_{\perp} = \frac{4}{3}\), giving \(y - 5 = \frac{4}{3}(x - (-4))\), which simplifies to standard form \(4x - 3y = -31\).

qs.q: The graph shows line \(\ell\) and point \(P(-4, 1)\). Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((0, 3)\) and \((2, -1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{2 - 0} = -2\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{-2} = \frac{1}{2}\). Using \(P(-4, 1)\), the equation is \(y - 1 = \frac{1}{2}(x + 4)\), which simplifies to \(x - 2y = -6\).

qs.q: The graph shows line \(\ell\) and point \(P(-2, -3)\). Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-3, 4)\) and \((2, -1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 4}{2 - (-3)} = -1\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = 1\). Using \(P(-2, -3)\), we have \(y - (-3) = 1(x - (-2))\), which simplifies to \(x - y = 1\).

qs.q: The graph shows line \(\ell\) and point \(P(3, -2)\). Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-1, -3)\) and \((2, 3)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{3 - (-3)}{2 - (-1)} = 2\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}\). Substituting into point-slope form with \(P(3, -2)\) gives \(y + 2 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(x + 2y = -1\).

qs.q: The graph shows line \(\ell\) and point \(P(2, -3)\). Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-3, -1)\) and \((1, 2)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-1)}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, \(m_\perp = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(2, -3)\), \(y - (-3) = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to standard form as \(4x + 3y = -1\).

qs.q: The graph shows line \(\ell\) and point \(P(-1, 4)\). Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-4, -2)\) and \((1, 1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{1 - (-2)}{1 - (-4)} = \frac{3}{5}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{5}{3}\). Through \(P(-1, 4)\), the line is \(y - 4 = -\frac{5}{3}(x + 1)\), which yields \(5x + 3y = 7\) in standard form.

qs.q: Line \(\ell\) is graphed in the coordinate plane. Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to \(\ell\) that passes through the \(x\)-intercept of \(\ell\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: From the graph, line \(\ell\) passes through \((1, -2)\) and \((4, 0)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{0 - (-2)}{4 - 1} = \frac{2}{3}\) and an \(x\)-intercept at \((4, 0)\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{3}{2}\). Through \((4, 0)\), the equation is \(y - 0 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 2y = 12\).

qs.q: Use the graph showing line \(\ell\) and point \(P\) to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: From the graph, line \(\ell\) passes through \((-3, -3)\) and \((1, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - (-3)}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{3}{4}\), and point \(P\) is at \((-5, 7)\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using point-slope form, \(y - 7 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 5)\), which simplifies to \(4x + 3y = 1\).

qs.q: Line \(\ell\) and point \(P\) are shown on the graph. Determine the equation of the line perpendicular to line \(\ell\) that passes through \(P\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: Line \(\ell\) passes through \((-5, -6)\) and \((-1, 4)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{4 - (-6)}{-1 - (-5)} = \frac{5}{2}\), and point \(P\) is at \((3, 5)\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{2}{5}\). Through \(P(3, 5)\), \(y - 5 = -\frac{2}{5}(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(2x + 5y = 31\) in standard form.

qs.q: In the figure, triangle \(ABC\) is shown on a coordinate plane. Determine the equation of the line containing the altitude from vertex \(C\) to side \(AB\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: The altitude from \(C\) is perpendicular to side \(AB\). The slope of \(AB\) through \(A(-5, -3)\) and \(B(3, 1)\) is \(m = \frac{1 - (-3)}{3 - (-5)} = \frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -2\). Through \(C(-2, 6)\), the equation is \(y - 6 = -2(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(2x + y = 2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the perpendicular bisector of segment \(AB\), in standard form (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\) and \(\gcd(A, |B|, |C|) = 1\)).
qs.s: The midpoint of \(AB\) is \(M = \left(\frac{-6+2}{2}, \frac{2+(-4)}{2}\right) = (-2, -1)\). The slope of \(AB\) is \(m = \frac{-4 - 2}{2 - (-6)} = -\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{4}{3}\). Using \(M(-2, -1)\), we get \(y + 1 = \frac{4}{3}(x + 2)\), which simplifies to \(4x - 3y = -5\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \((1, 4)\).
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((3, 1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{1 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{2}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{3}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \((1, 4)\), \(y - 4 = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(3x + 2y = 11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \((-3, 1)\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((-1, -2)\) and \((1, 2)\) with slope \(m = \frac{2 - (-2)}{1 - (-1)} = 2\). The perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{2}\), giving \(y - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x + 3)\), which simplifies to \(x + 2y = -1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \((3, 2)\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((-2, 3)\) and \((2, -1)\), with slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 3}{2 - (-2)} = -1\). The perpendicular slope is \(1\), so the line through \((3, 2)\) is \(y - 2 = 1(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(x - y = 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \((1, -2)\).
qs.s: The line has points \((-3, 1)\) and \((0, 2)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{2 - 1}{0 - (-3)} = \frac{1}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(-3\), giving the equation \(y - (-2) = -3(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(3x + y = 1\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \((2, -1)\).
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, 2)\) and \((4, -1)\) with slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 2}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{4}{3}\). Using \((2, -1)\), we get \(y - (-1) = \frac{4}{3}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to \(4x - 3y = 11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to line \(L\) that passes through point \(P\).
qs.s: Line \(L\) passes through \((-4, -3)\) and \((3, 2)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{2 - (-3)}{3 - (-4)} = \frac{5}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{7}{5}\). Point \(P\) is \((-2, 5)\), so \(y - 5 = -\frac{7}{5}(x + 2)\), which yields \(7x + 5y = 11\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to line \(L\) that passes through the \(y\)-intercept of line \(L\).
qs.s: Line \(L\) has points \((-2, 5)\) and \((2, -1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-1 - 5}{2 - (-2)} = -\frac{3}{2}\) and a \(y\)-intercept at \((0, 2)\). The perpendicular line has slope \(\frac{2}{3}\) and passes through \((0, 2)\), yielding \(y - 2 = \frac{2}{3}x\), which simplifies to \(2x - 3y = -6\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation (\(Ax + By = C\), where \(A > 0\)) of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through point \(P\).
qs.s: The graphed line has slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 4}{1 - (-5)} = -\frac{5}{6}\), making the perpendicular slope \(\frac{6}{5}\). Point \(P\) is at \((3, 4)\), yielding \(y - 4 = \frac{6}{5}(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(6x - 5y = -2\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(3, 2)\), in standard form.
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((0, 1)\) and \((4, -2)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-2 - 1}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is the negative reciprocal, \(m_\perp = \frac{4}{3}\). Using \(P(3, 2)\), the equation is \(y - 2 = \frac{4}{3}(x - 3)\), which rearranges to \(4x - 3y = 6\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(2, 3)\), in standard form.
qs.s: The line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((5, 1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{1 - (-1)}{5 - 0} = \frac{2}{5}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{5}{2}\). Using point \(P(2, 3)\), we have \(y - 3 = -\frac{5}{2}(x - 2) \implies 2y - 6 = -5x + 10\), which simplifies to \(5x + 2y = 16\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(4, 1)\), in standard form.
qs.s: From the graph, the line passes through \((0, -1)\) and \((2, 3)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-1)}{2 - 0} = 2\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{1}{2}\). Using point-slope form with \(P(4, 1)\) gives \(y - 1 = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to standard form \(x + 2y = 6\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(3, -2)\), in standard form.
qs.s: The line passes through \((-2, 0)\) and \((0, -2)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-2 - 0}{0 - (-2)} = -1\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = 1\). Using \(P(3, -2)\), the equation is \(y - (-2) = 1(x - 3) \implies y + 2 = x - 3\), which in standard form is \(x - y = 5\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(-5, -2)\), in standard form.
qs.s: The graphed line passes through \((-3, 6)\) and \((0, 1)\), giving slope \(m = \frac{1 - 6}{0 - (-3)} = -\frac{5}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{3}{5}\). Using \(P(-5, -2)\), we have \(y + 2 = \frac{3}{5}(x + 5) \implies 5y + 10 = 3x + 15\), which yields \(3x - 5y = -5\).

qs.q: The graph shows two lines, \(L_1\) and \(L_2\). Determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to \(L_1\) that passes through the \(y\)-intercept of \(L_2\).
qs.s: \(L_1\) passes through \((-3, -1)\) and \((3, 3)\), so its slope is \(m_1 = \frac{3 - (-1)}{3 - (-3)} = \frac{2}{3}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_\perp = -\frac{3}{2}\). The \(y\)-intercept of \(L_2\) is \((0, -4)\). Using point-slope form gives \(y - (-4) = -\frac{3}{2}(x - 0) \implies 2y + 8 = -3x\), which in standard form is \(3x + 2y = -8\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through the point \(P(7, -4)\).
