qs.s: The line passes through \((-6, 5)\) and \((0, 1)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{1 - 5}{0 - (-6)} = -\frac{2}{3}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{3}{2}\). Through \(P(7, -4)\), the equation is \(y - (-4) = \frac{3}{2}(x - 7) \implies 2y + 8 = 3x - 21\), which rearranges to \(3x - 2y = 29\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed horizontal line that passes through the point \(P(-4, 5)\), in standard form.
qs.s: The graphed line is horizontal (\(y = -3\)) with a slope of \(0\). A perpendicular line is vertical and therefore has an undefined slope with equation \(x = h\). Since it passes through \(P(-4, 5)\), its equation is \(x = -4\).

qs.q: Use the graph to determine the standard form equation of the line perpendicular to the graphed line that passes through its \(x\)-intercept.
qs.s: From the graph, the line has intercepts \((0, 3)\) and \((4, 0)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 3}{4 - 0} = -\frac{3}{4}\). The perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{4}{3}\). Passing through the \(x\)-intercept \((4, 0)\), the equation is \(y - 0 = \frac{4}{3}(x - 4) \implies 3y = 4x - 16\), which in standard form is \(4x - 3y = 16\).

exercises.name: Equation of parallel line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(x - 4y = 7\) with the same y-intercept as \(6x + 5y = 11\).
qs.s: The line \(x - 4y = 7\) has slope \(m = \frac{1}{4}\), and setting \(x = 0\) in \(6x + 5y = 11\) gives \(y = \frac{11}{5}\). Thus, the parallel line is \(y = \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{11}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(4x - 3y = 6\) with the same y-intercept as \(2x + 5y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(4x - 3y = 6\) has slope \(m = \frac{4}{3}\), and setting \(x = 0\) in \(2x + 5y = 8\) gives \(y = \frac{8}{5}\). Thus, the parallel line is \(y = \frac{4}{3}x + \frac{8}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(5x + 2y = 10\) with the same y-intercept as \(3x - 4y = 6\).
qs.s: The line \(5x + 2y = 10\) has slope \(m = -\frac{5}{2}\), and setting \(x = 0\) in \(3x - 4y = 6\) gives \(y = -\frac{6}{4} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Thus, the parallel line is \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x - \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(2x + 5y = 12\) with the same y-intercept as \(4x - 3y = 7\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + 5y = 12\) has slope \(m = -\frac{2}{5}\), and setting \(x = 0\) in \(4x - 3y = 7\) gives \(y = -\frac{7}{3}\). Thus, the parallel line is \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(3x - 5y = 15\) with the same y-intercept as \(7x + 2y = 9\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 5y = 15\) has slope \(m = \frac{3}{5}\), and setting \(x = 0\) in \(7x + 2y = 9\) gives \(y = \frac{9}{2}\). Thus, the parallel line is \(y = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(7x - 4y = 21\) with the same x-intercept as \(3x + 8y = -18\).
qs.s: The line \(7x - 4y = 21\) has slope \(m = \frac{7}{4}\), and setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 8y = -18\) gives \(x = -6\). Using point-slope form with \((-6, 0)\), \(y - 0 = \frac{7}{4}(x + 6)\) simplifies to \(y = \frac{7}{4}x + \frac{21}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\) with the same x-intercept as \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}y = 6\).
qs.s: Solving \(\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{3}y = 1\) for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{6}{5}x - 3\), so \(m = \frac{6}{5}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{2}y = 6\) gives \(x = 8\), and substituting \((8, 0)\) into point-slope form gives \(y = \frac{6}{5}(x - 8) = \frac{6}{5}x - \frac{48}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(5(x - 1) + 2y = 3(x + 2) - 4\) with the same x-intercept as \(4(y + 2) - 3x = 2(x - 5) + 3\).
qs.s: Simplifying \(5(x - 1) + 2y = 3(x + 2) - 4\) gives \(2y = -2x + 7\), so \(m = -1\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(4(y + 2) - 3x = 2(x - 5) + 3\) yields \(8 - 3x = 2x - 7 \implies x = 3\), and point-slope form gives \(y - 0 = -1(x - 3)\), or \(y = -x + 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(4(x - 2y) + 3 = 5x - y + 7\) with the same y-intercept as \(2(3x - y) + 5 = x - 4(y - 1)\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(4(x - 2y) + 3 = 5x - y + 7\) yields \(7y = -x - 4\), so \(m = -\frac{1}{7}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(2(3x - y) + 5 = x - 4(y - 1)\) gives \(-2y + 5 = -4y + 4 \implies y = -\frac{1}{2}\), yielding \(y = -\frac{1}{7}x - \frac{1}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, parallel to \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}y = 5\) with the same y-intercept as \(\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{1}{2}y = \frac{7}{3}\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}y = 5\) gives \(y = -\frac{9}{8}x + \frac{15}{2}\), so \(m = -\frac{9}{8}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{1}{2}y = \frac{7}{3}\) gives \(y = -\frac{14}{3}\), resulting in \(y = -\frac{9}{8}x - \frac{14}{3}\).

exercises.name: Equation of parallel line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(3x - 4y = 7\) with the same y-intercept as \(2x + 5y = -15\).
qs.s: From \(3x - 4y = 7\), isolating \(y\) shows the slope is \(m = \frac{3}{4}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(2x + 5y = -15\) gives \(5y = -15\), so \(b = -3\), yielding \(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(x + 2y = 10\) with the same y-intercept as \(5x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: Rewriting \(x + 2y = 10\) gives \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5\), so the slope is \(m = -\frac{1}{2}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(5x - 2y = 8\) yields \(-2y = 8\), so \(b = -4\), giving \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x - 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(2x - y = 5\) with the same y-intercept as \(4x + 3y = 12\).
qs.s: The line \(2x - y = 5\) has slope \(m = 2\), so a parallel line also has slope \(2\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(4x + 3y = 12\) gives \(3y = 12\), or \(b = 4\), so the equation is \(y = 2x + 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(5x - y = 3\) with the same y-intercept as \(3x - 2y = -10\).
qs.s: The line \(5x - y = 3\) rearranges to \(y = 5x - 3\), giving a slope of \(m = 5\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(3x - 2y = -10\) gives \(-2y = -10\), so \(b = 5\), producing \(y = 5x + 5\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(2x + 3y = -9\) with the same y-intercept as \(x - 4y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(2x + 3y = -9\) has slope \(m = -\frac{2}{3}\), so any parallel line shares this slope. Setting \(x = 0\) in \(x - 4y = 8\) gives \(-4y = 8\), so the y-intercept is \(b = -2\), giving \(y = -\frac{2}{3}x - 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(5x - 2y = 3(x + y) - 8\) with the same y-intercept as \(4(x - 1) + 3y = 2\).
qs.s: Expanding the first equation gives \(5x - 2y = 3x + 3y - 8\), which simplifies to \(2x - 5y = -8\) with slope \(m = \frac{2}{5}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in the second equation gives \(4(-1) + 3y = 2\), so \(3y = 6\) and \(b = 2\), yielding \(y = \frac{2}{5}x + 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(4x - 3y = 11\) with the same x-intercept as \(5x + 2y = 15\).
qs.s: The line \(4x - 3y = 11\) has slope \(m = \frac{4}{3}\), and setting \(y = 0\) in \(5x + 2y = 15\) gives \(5x = 15\), so the x-intercept is \((3, 0)\). Substituting into point-slope form gives \(y - 0 = \frac{4}{3}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(8x + 5y = -1\) with the same x-intercept as \(3x - 4y = -18\).
qs.s: The slope of \(8x + 5y = -1\) is \(m = -\frac{8}{5}\), and setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x - 4y = -18\) gives the x-intercept \((-6, 0)\). Using point-slope form, \(y - 0 = -\frac{8}{5}(x + 6)\) simplifies to \(y = -\frac{8}{5}x - \frac{48}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(7x + 6y = 25\) with the same y-intercept as \(9x - 8y = 20\).
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) in \(7x + 6y = 25\) gives \(y = -\frac{7}{6}x + \frac{25}{6}\), so \(m = -\frac{7}{6}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(9x - 8y = 20\) yields \(-8y = 20\), which simplifies to \(b = -\frac{5}{2}\), giving \(y = -\frac{7}{6}x - \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line parallel to \(3x - 5y = 15\) with the same x-intercept as \(2x + 7y = -14\).
qs.s: The slope of \(3x - 5y = 15\) is \(m = \frac{3}{5}\), and setting \(y = 0\) in \(2x + 7y = -14\) gives the x-intercept \((-7, 0)\). Using point-slope form, \(y - 0 = \frac{3}{5}(x + 7)\) simplifies to \(y = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{21}{5}\).

exercises.name: Equation of parallel line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(4x - 3y = 9\) that has the same y-intercept as \(5x + 2y = 7\).
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) in \(5x + 2y = 7\) gives the y-intercept \(\left(0, \frac{7}{2}\right)\). A parallel line has the form \(4x - 3y = C\), and substituting \(\left(0, \frac{7}{2}\right)\) gives \(4(0) - 3\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) = -\frac{21}{2}\), which clears to \(8x - 6y = -21\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(3x + 5y = 8\) that has the same x-intercept as \(2x - 3y = 7\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) in \(2x - 3y = 7\) gives the x-intercept \(\left(\frac{7}{2}, 0\right)\). A line parallel to \(3x + 5y = 8\) has the form \(3x + 5y = C\), and substituting \(\left(\frac{7}{2}, 0\right)\) yields \(3\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) + 5(0) = \frac{21}{2}\), which simplifies to \(6x + 10y = 21\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(5x + 2y = 11\) that has the same x-intercept as \(4x + 3y = 9\).
qs.s: The x-intercept of \(4x + 3y = 9\) is \(\left(\frac{9}{4}, 0\right)\). Substituting this into the parallel family \(5x + 2y = C\) yields \(5\left(\frac{9}{4}\right) + 2(0) = \frac{45}{4}\), which gives \(20x + 8y = 45\) in standard form.

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(x - 4y = 6\) that has the same x-intercept as \(5x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: Setting \(y = 0\) in \(5x - 2y = 8\) gives the x-intercept \(\left(\frac{8}{5}, 0\right)\). The parallel line has form \(x - 4y = C\); substituting the intercept gives \(\frac{8}{5} - 4(0) = \frac{8}{5}\), so multiplying by \(5\) results in \(5x - 20y = 8\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(3x + 4y = 5\) that has the same y-intercept as \(2x - 5y = 6\).
qs.s: Setting \(x = 0\) in \(2x - 5y = 6\) gives \(y = -\frac{6}{5}\), so the intercept is \(\left(0, -\frac{6}{5}\right)\). Substituting into \(3x + 4y = C\) yields \(3(0) + 4\left(-\frac{6}{5}\right) = -\frac{24}{5}\), which multiplies by \(5\) to give \(15x + 20y = -24\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(5(2x - 1) - 3(y + 4) = 4x + 2\) that has the same x-intercept as \(4(x - 2) + 5(2y - 1) = 3y + 6\).
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation gives \(6x - 3y = 19\), which has slope \(2\) and reduced form \(2x - y = C\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(4(x - 2) - 5 = 6 \implies 4x = 19 \implies x = \frac{19}{4}\), and substituting \(\left(\frac{19}{4}, 0\right)\) into \(2x - y = C\) gives \(2\left(\frac{19}{4}\right) = \frac{19}{2}\), or \(4x - 2y = 19\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(8(x - 2y) - 3(3x - y) = 15\) that has the same y-intercept as \(5(2x + 3y) - 4(x - 2y) = 31\).
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(-x - 13y = 15 \implies x + 13y = -15\), so parallel lines satisfy \(x + 13y = C\). Setting \(x = 0\) in the second equation gives \(15y + 8y = 31 \implies y = \frac{31}{23}\), and substituting \(\left(0, \frac{31}{23}\right)\) gives \(13\left(\frac{31}{23}\right) = \frac{403}{23}\), which clears to \(23x + 299y = 403\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(\frac{x + 3}{4} - \frac{y - 1}{6} = 1\) that has the same x-intercept as \(\frac{2x - 5}{3} + \frac{y + 4}{2} = 4\).
qs.s: Multiplying the first line by \(12\) gives \(3(x + 3) - 2(y - 1) = 12 \implies 3x - 2y = 1\), giving the parallel family \(3x - 2y = C\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation yields \(\frac{2x - 5}{3} + 2 = 4 \implies x = \frac{11}{2}\), and substituting \(\left(\frac{11}{2}, 0\right)\) gives \(3\left(\frac{11}{2}\right) = \frac{33}{2}\), or \(6x - 4y = 33\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{5}y = \frac{7}{15}\) that has the same y-intercept as \(\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{6}y = \frac{11}{12}\).
qs.s: Multiplying the first line by \(15\) gives \(10x - 9y = 7\), so the parallel family is \(10x - 9y = C\). Setting \(x = 0\) in the second equation gives \(\frac{5}{6}y = \frac{11}{12} \implies y = \frac{11}{10}\), and substituting \(\left(0, \frac{11}{10}\right)\) gives \(10(0) - 9\left(\frac{11}{10}\right) = -\frac{99}{10}\), which clears to \(100x - 90y = -99\).

qs.q: Find the equation, in standard form, of the line parallel to \(7(2x - 3y) + 5(x + y) = 13\) that has the same x-intercept as \(3(4x - 5y) - 2(x - 7y) = 29\).
qs.s: Expanding the first equation yields \(19x - 16y = 13\), so parallel lines have the form \(19x - 16y = C\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(12x - 2x = 29 \implies x = \frac{29}{10}\), and substituting \(\left(\frac{29}{10}, 0\right)\) produces \(19\left(\frac{29}{10}\right) = \frac{551}{10}\), which clears to \(190x - 160y = 551\).

exercises.name: Equation of perpendicular line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(3x + 4y = 8\) and has the same y-intercept as \(2x - 5y = 15\).
qs.s: The line \(3x + 4y = 8\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(2x - 5y = 15\) gives \(y = -3\), so the equation is \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 3\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(4x + 3y = -6\) and has the same y-intercept as \(7x - 2y = -14\).
qs.s: The line \(4x + 3y = -6\) has slope \(-\frac{4}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{3}{4}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(7x - 2y = -14\) gives \(y = 7\), yielding \(y = \frac{3}{4}x + 7\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(5x - 2y = 4\) and has the same y-intercept as \(3x + 4y = -8\).
qs.s: The line \(5x - 2y = 4\) has slope \(\frac{5}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(-\frac{2}{5}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = -8\) gives \(y = -2\), so the equation is \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x - 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(3x - 5y = 10\) and has the same y-intercept as \(2x + 3y = -18\).
qs.s: The line \(3x - 5y = 10\) has slope \(\frac{3}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{5}{3}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(2x + 3y = -18\) yields \(y = -6\), so the equation is \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x - 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(x - 3y = 9\) and has the same y-intercept as \(4x + 3y = 12\).
qs.s: The line \(x - 3y = 9\) has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-3\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(4x + 3y = 12\) gives \(y = 4\), so the equation is \(y = -3x + 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(5(x - 2y) = 3(x + y) - 8\) and has the same y-intercept as \(4(y - 3) = 6x - 7\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(5(x - 2y) = 3(x + y) - 8\) yields \(2x - 13y = -8\) with slope \(\frac{2}{13}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{13}{2}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(4(y - 3) = 6x - 7\) gives \(4y - 12 = -7 \implies y = \frac{5}{4}\), resulting in \(y = -\frac{13}{2}x + \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(6x - 8y = 15\) and has the same x-intercept as \(5x + 3y = -45\).
qs.s: The slope of \(6x - 8y = 15\) is \(\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(5x + 3y = -45\) yields \(x = -9\), so \(y - 0 = -\frac{4}{3}(x + 9)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{4}{3}x - 12\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(3x + 5y = 11\) and has the same x-intercept as \(4x - 7y = 24\).
qs.s: The slope of \(3x + 5y = 11\) is \(-\frac{3}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{5}{3}\). The x-intercept of \(4x - 7y = 24\) is \((6, 0)\), so using point-slope form gives \(y - 0 = \frac{5}{3}(x - 6)\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{5}{3}x - 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(4(x - y) + 1 = 7x + 2y - 11\) and has the same x-intercept as \(3(x + 4) - 5y = x - 2\).
qs.s: Simplifying \(4(x - y) + 1 = 7x + 2y - 11\) gives \(-3x - 6y = -12\) with slope \(-\frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(2\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3(x + 4) - 5y = x - 2\) yields \(2x = -14 \implies x = -7\), giving \(y - 0 = 2(x + 7)\), which is \(y = 2x + 14\).

qs.q: Find the equation of a line in slope-intercept form that is perpendicular to \(8x - 3(y + 1) = 2x + 5y - 7\) and has the same y-intercept as \(4(x + 2) - 3y = 2x - 13\).
qs.s: Simplifying \(8x - 3(y + 1) = 2x + 5y - 7\) gives \(6x - 8y = -4\), which has slope \(\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{4}{3}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(4(x + 2) - 3y = 2x - 13\) gives \(8 - 3y = -13 \implies y = 7\), yielding \(y = -\frac{4}{3}x + 7\).

exercises.name: Equation of perpendicular line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(5x + 2y = 7\) and has the same y-intercept as \(3x - 4y = 8\).
qs.s: The line \(5x + 2y = 7\) has slope \(-\frac{5}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(\frac{2}{5}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in \(3x - 4y = 8\) gives the y-intercept \((0, -2)\), leading directly to \(y = \frac{2}{5}x - 2\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(x - 3y = 6\) and has the same x-intercept as \(4x + 7y = 0\).
qs.s: The line \(x - 3y = 6\) has slope \(\frac{1}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-3\). The line \(4x + 7y = 0\) has an x-intercept at \((0, 0)\), giving \(y = -3x\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(3x + 4y = 12\) and has the same x-intercept as \(5x + 6y = 0\).
qs.s: The line \(3x + 4y = 12\) has slope \(-\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{4}{3}\). Since \(5x + 6y = 0\) has its x-intercept at \((0, 0)\), the equation of the line is \(y = \frac{4}{3}x\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(2x - 5y = 10\) and has the same x-intercept as \(3x + 4y = 12\).
qs.s: The line \(2x - 5y = 10\) has slope \(\frac{2}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{5}{2}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = 12\) gives the x-intercept \((4, 0)\), so the equation is \(y - 0 = -\frac{5}{2}(x - 4)\), or \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + 10\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(2x - 4y = 5\) and has the same x-intercept as \(3x - 2y = 9\).
qs.s: The line \(2x - 4y = 5\) has slope \(\frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-2\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x - 2y = 9\) gives the x-intercept \((3, 0)\), so \(y = -2(x - 3)\) simplifies to \(y = -2x + 6\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(5(x + 2y) - 2(3x - y) = 18\) and has the same x-intercept as \(3(2x - 5) - 4(y - 1) = 2x + 1\).
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation gives \(-x + 12y = 18\) with slope \(\frac{1}{12}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-12\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(4x = 12\) or \(x = 3\), leading to \(y = -12(x - 3) = -12x + 36\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(7x - 9y = 42\) and has the same x-intercept as \(6x + 11y = 25\).
qs.s: The line \(7x - 9y = 42\) has slope \(\frac{7}{9}\), giving perpendicular slope \(-\frac{9}{7}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(6x + 11y = 25\) yields the x-intercept \(\left(\frac{25}{6}, 0\right)\), so \(y = -\frac{9}{7}\left(x - \frac{25}{6}\right) = -\frac{9}{7}x + \frac{75}{14}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(3(2x - y) + 4x = 5(y - 1) + 7\) and has the same x-intercept as \(4(x - 3) - 2(y + 5) = x - 7\).
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation gives \(10x - 8y = 2\), which has slope \(\frac{5}{4}\) and perpendicular slope \(-\frac{4}{5}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation simplifies to \(3x = 15\), giving the x-intercept \((5, 0)\), so \(y = -\frac{4}{5}(x - 5) = -\frac{4}{5}x + 4\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{2}{3}y = 1\) and has the same x-intercept as \(\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{6}y = -\frac{7}{3}\).
qs.s: The slope of \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{2}{3}y = 1\) is \(\frac{9}{8}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{8}{9}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives the x-intercept \(\left(-\frac{14}{3}, 0\right)\), yielding \(y = -\frac{8}{9}\left(x + \frac{14}{3}\right) = -\frac{8}{9}x - \frac{112}{27}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, that is perpendicular to \(8x - 14y = 21\) and has the same x-intercept as \(5(x - 2y) + 3 = 2(y + 6) - x\).
qs.s: The slope of \(8x - 14y = 21\) is \(\frac{4}{7}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{7}{4}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(6x = 9\), or \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), yielding \(y = -\frac{7}{4}\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{7}{4}x + \frac{21}{8}\).

exercises.name: Equation of perpendicular line with shared intercept

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{5}{2}x = \frac{1}{2}y - 3\) with the same x-intercept as \(3x + 4y = 10\).
qs.s: The line \(\frac{5}{2}x = \frac{1}{2}y - 3\) simplifies to \(y = 5x + 6\) with slope \(5\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{5}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(3x + 4y = 10\) yields \(x = \frac{10}{3}\), which gives \(y - 0 = -\frac{1}{5}\left(x - \frac{10}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{5}x + \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{2}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}y - 1\) with the same x-intercept as \(5x + 2y = 15\).
qs.s: The line \(\frac{2}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}y - 1\) has slope \(2\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{2}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(5x + 2y = 15\) gives \(x = 3\), leading to \(y = -\frac{1}{2}(x - 3) = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{3}{4}x = \frac{1}{4}y + 2\) with the same x-intercept as \(4x - 5y = 14\).
qs.s: The line simplifies to \(y = 3x - 8\) with slope \(3\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{3}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(4x - 5y = 14\) gives \(x = \frac{7}{2}\), which results in \(y = -\frac{1}{3}\left(x - \frac{7}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}x + \frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{4}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}y + 2\) with the same x-intercept as \(3x - 2y = 8\).
qs.s: Rearranging \(\frac{4}{3}x = \frac{1}{3}y + 2\) gives \(y = 4x - 6\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{4}\). The x-intercept of \(3x - 2y = 8\) is \(\left(\frac{8}{3}, 0\right)\), yielding \(y = -\frac{1}{4}\left(x - \frac{8}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{1}{2}x = \frac{3}{2}y + 2\) with the same x-intercept as \(4x + 3y = 6\).
qs.s: Solving for \(y\) gives \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - \frac{4}{3}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-3\). Setting \(y = 0\) in \(4x + 3y = 6\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}\), producing \(y = -3\left(x - \frac{3}{2}\right) = -3x + \frac{9}{2}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{5}{6}x - \frac{2}{3} = \frac{1}{4}y + \frac{1}{3}x\) with the same x-intercept as \(\frac{2x - 5}{7} + \frac{3y + 1}{4} = 1\).
qs.s: Multiplying the first line by 12 gives \(3y = 6x - 8\) with slope \(2\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-\frac{1}{2}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(\frac{2x - 5}{7} + \frac{1}{4} = 1\), which solves to \(x = \frac{41}{8}\), yielding \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\left(x - \frac{41}{8}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{41}{16}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(2(x - 3y) + 5 = 7x - 4(y - 1)\) with the same y-intercept as \(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{5}y = \frac{4}{5} - \frac{1}{2}y\).
qs.s: Rearranging the first equation gives \(y = -\frac{5}{2}x + \frac{1}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(\frac{2}{5}\). Setting \(x = 0\) in the second equation gives \(-\frac{1}{10}y = \frac{4}{5}\), so \(y = -8\), giving the line \(y = \frac{2}{5}x - 8\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{4x - 1}{3} - \frac{y + 2}{2} = 1\) with the same x-intercept as \(\frac{3}{4}(x + 2) - \frac{5}{6}y = 3\).
qs.s: Clearing denominators in the first equation yields \(8x - 3y = 14\), giving slope \(\frac{8}{3}\) and perpendicular slope \(-\frac{3}{8}\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(\frac{3}{4}(x + 2) = 3\), so \(x = 2\), producing \(y = -\frac{3}{8}(x - 2) = -\frac{3}{8}x + \frac{3}{4}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{3}y = \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{6}y - 2\) with the same x-intercept as \(5(x - 2) - 3(2y + 1) = 9\).
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 12 yields \(3x + 24 = 6y\), or \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 4\), so the perpendicular slope is \(-2\). Setting \(y = 0\) in the second equation gives \(5(x - 2) - 3 = 9\), which solves to \(x = \frac{22}{5}\), leading to \(y = -2\left(x - \frac{22}{5}\right) = -2x + \frac{44}{5}\).

qs.q: Find the equation of the line, in slope-intercept form, perpendicular to \(3(x - 2y) - 4 = 2(2x - y) + 1\) with the same y-intercept as \(\frac{5x + 3}{2} - \frac{4y - 7}{5} = 4\).
qs.s: Expanding the first equation gives \(4y = -x - 5\), so the slope is \(-\frac{1}{4}\) and the perpendicular slope is \(4\). Setting \(x = 0\) in the second equation gives \(\frac{3}{2} - \frac{4y - 7}{5} = 4\), which solves to \(y = -\frac{11}{8}\), giving \(y = 4x - \frac{11}{8}\).

exercises.name: Equation of a line perpendicular to a radius

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((-3, -1)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((-3, -1)\) has slope \(m = \frac{-1 - 0}{-3 - 0} = \frac{1}{3}\), meaning the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -3\). Through \((-3, -1)\), \(y - (-1) = -3(x - (-3))\), which simplifies to \(y = -3x - 10\).

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((-2, 3)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((-2, 3)\) has slope \(m = \frac{3 - 0}{-2 - 0} = -\frac{3}{2}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = \frac{2}{3}\). Using \((-2, 3)\), \(y - 3 = \frac{2}{3}(x - (-2))\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{13}{3}\).

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((-2, -5)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((-2, -5)\) has slope \(m = \frac{-5 - 0}{-2 - 0} = \frac{5}{2}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{2}{5}\). Through \((-2, -5)\), \(y - (-5) = -\frac{2}{5}(x - (-2))\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{29}{5}\).

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((1, -2)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((1, -2)\) has slope \(m = \frac{-2 - 0}{1 - 0} = -2\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_\perp = \frac{1}{2}\). Using point \((1, -2)\), \(y - (-2) = \frac{1}{2}(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((4, 3)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((4, 3)\) has slope \(m = \frac{3 - 0}{4 - 0} = \frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular line has slope \(m_\perp = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using point \((4, 3)\), the equation is \(y - 3 = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 4)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{4}{3}x + \frac{25}{3}\).

qs.q: A circle centred at \((2, 3)\) passes through the point \((6, 5)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at \((6, 5)\)?
qs.s: The radius connects \((2, 3)\) and \((6, 5)\), so its slope is \(m = \frac{5 - 3}{6 - 2} = \frac{1}{2}\), giving a perpendicular slope of \(m_\perp = -2\). The tangent line passes through \((6, 5)\), giving \(y - 5 = -2(x - 6)\), which simplifies to \(y = -2x + 17\).

qs.q: A circle centred at \((-1, 4)\) passes through the point \((3, 1)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at \((3, 1)\)?
qs.s: The radius from \((-1, 4)\) to \((3, 1)\) has slope \(m = \frac{1 - 4}{3 - (-1)} = -\frac{3}{4}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{4}{3}\). Using \((3, 1)\), \(y - 1 = \frac{4}{3}(x - 3)\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{4}{3}x - 3\).

qs.q: A circle centred at the origin passes through the point \((5, -12)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at this point?
qs.s: The radius from \((0, 0)\) to \((5, -12)\) has slope \(m = -\frac{12}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = \frac{5}{12}\). Using \((5, -12)\), \(y - (-12) = \frac{5}{12}(x - 5)\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{5}{12}x - \frac{169}{12}\).

qs.q: A circle centred at \((1, -4)\) passes through the point \((-5, -2)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at \((-5, -2)\)?
qs.s: The radius connecting \((1, -4)\) and \((-5, -2)\) has slope \(m = \frac{-2 - (-4)}{-5 - 1} = -\frac{1}{3}\), meaning the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = 3\). Through \((-5, -2)\), \(y - (-2) = 3(x - (-5))\), which simplifies to \(y = 3x + 13\).

qs.q: A circle centred at \((-3, -1)\) passes through the point \((2, 2)\). What is the equation, in slope-intercept form, of the line perpendicular to the radius at \((2, 2)\)?
qs.s: The radius has slope \(m = \frac{2 - (-1)}{2 - (-3)} = \frac{3}{5}\), so the perpendicular slope is \(m_\perp = -\frac{5}{3}\). Through the point on the circle \((2, 2)\), \(y - 2 = -\frac{5}{3}(x - 2)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x + \frac{16}{3}\).

exercises.name: Equations and properties of diagonals of a rhombus

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((1, 1)\), \((4, 5)\), \((9, 5)\), and \((6, 1)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((1, 1)\) to \((9, 5)\) and \((4, 5)\) to \((6, 1)\). The diagonal with negative slope passes through \((4, 5)\) and \((6, 1)\) with slope \(m = \frac{1 - 5}{6 - 4} = -2\), giving \(y - 1 = -2(x - 6)\), which simplifies to \(y = -2x + 13\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((0, 0)\), \((4, 3)\), \((9, 3)\), and \((5, 0)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with positive slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((0, 0)\) to \((9, 3)\) and \((5, 0)\) to \((4, 3)\). The diagonal with positive slope passes through \((0, 0)\) and \((9, 3)\) with slope \(m = \frac{3 - 0}{9 - 0} = \frac{1}{3}\), giving the equation \(y = \frac{1}{3}x\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((0, 0)\), \((4, 3)\), \((4, 8)\), and \((0, 5)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with positive slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((0, 0)\) to \((4, 8)\) and \((0, 5)\) to \((4, 3)\). The diagonal with positive slope connects \((0, 0)\) and \((4, 8)\) with slope \(m = \frac{8 - 0}{4 - 0} = 2\), yielding the equation \(y = 2x\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((-1, 2)\), \((1, 6)\), \((5, 4)\), and \((3, 0)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((-1, 2)\) to \((5, 4)\) and \((3, 0)\) to \((1, 6)\). The diagonal with negative slope connects \((3, 0)\) and \((1, 6)\) with slope \(m = \frac{6 - 0}{1 - 3} = -3\), giving the equation \(y - 0 = -3(x - 3)\), or \(y = -3x + 9\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((-2, -1)\), \((-1, 2)\), \((2, 1)\), and \((1, -2)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((-2, -1)\) to \((2, 1)\) and \((1, -2)\) to \((-1, 2)\). The diagonal with negative slope passes through \((1, -2)\) and \((-1, 2)\) with slope \(m = \frac{2 - (-2)}{-1 - 1} = -2\) and passes through the origin, so its equation is \(y = -2x\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((2, 2)\), \((-9, 9)\), \((-8, -4)\), and \((3, -11)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The opposite vertices are \((-8, -4)\) with \((2, 2)\) and \((3, -11)\) with \((-9, 9)\). The diagonal with negative slope passes through \((3, -11)\) and \((-9, 9)\) with slope \(m = \frac{9 - (-11)}{-9 - 3} = -\frac{5}{3}\), giving \(y - 9 = -\frac{5}{3}(x + 9)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{5}{3}x - 6\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((-7, 2)\), \((-6, 14)\), \((3, 6)\), and \((2, -6)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with positive slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The opposite vertices forming the diagonals are \((-7, 2)\) with \((3, 6)\) and \((2, -6)\) with \((-6, 14)\). The diagonal with positive slope passes through \((-7, 2)\) and \((3, 6)\) with slope \(m = \frac{6 - 2}{3 - (-7)} = \frac{2}{5}\), yielding \(y - 6 = \frac{2}{5}(x - 3)\), or \(y = \frac{2}{5}x + \frac{24}{5}\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((-1, -6)\), \((-1, 7)\), \((11, 2)\), and \((11, -11)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with positive slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The diagonals connect opposite vertices \((-1, -6)\) to \((11, 2)\) and \((11, -11)\) to \((-1, 7)\). The diagonal with positive slope passes through \((-1, -6)\) and \((11, 2)\) with slope \(m = \frac{2 - (-6)}{11 - (-1)} = \frac{2}{3}\), giving \(y - 2 = \frac{2}{3}(x - 11)\), or \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{16}{3}\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((8, 8)\), \((0, 2)\), \((7, 1)\), and \((1, 9)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: By checking side lengths, the opposite vertices forming the diagonals are \((0, 2)\) with \((8, 8)\) and \((7, 1)\) with \((1, 9)\). The diagonal connecting \((7, 1)\) and \((1, 9)\) has slope \(m = \frac{9 - 1}{1 - 7} = -\frac{4}{3}\), giving \(y - 1 = -\frac{4}{3}(x - 7)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{4}{3}x + \frac{31}{3}\).

qs.q: A rhombus has coordinates \((18, 4)\), \((1, 11)\), \((-6, -6)\), and \((11, -13)\). What is the equation of the diagonal with negative slope in slope-intercept form?
qs.s: The opposite vertices are \((-6, -6)\) with \((18, 4)\) and \((11, -13)\) with \((1, 11)\). The diagonal with negative slope connects \((11, -13)\) and \((1, 11)\) with slope \(m = \frac{11 - (-13)}{1 - 11} = -\frac{12}{5}\), giving \(y - 11 = -\frac{12}{5}(x - 1)\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{12}{5}x + \frac{67}{5}\).

exercises.name: Find initial value or fixed cost

qs.q: A law firm purchased office furniture that depreciates linearly. The value of the furniture after 3 years was $14,000, and after 7 years it was $6,000. Determine the original purchase price of the furniture.
qs.s: The annual depreciation is \(\frac{14\,000 - 6000}{7 - 3} = \$2000\) per year. The original purchase price is \(14\,000 + 3(2000) = \$20\,000\).

qs.q: A delivery van depreciates linearly over time. Its value was $27,000 after 3 years and $19,000 after 5 years. Determine the purchase price of the van.
qs.s: The annual depreciation is \(\frac{27\,000 - 19\,000}{5 - 3} = \$4000\) per year. The purchase price is \(27\,000 + 3(4000) = \$39\,000\).

qs.q: A catering service charges a fixed booking fee plus a constant amount per guest. An event with 40 guests costs $1,100, and an event with 70 guests costs $1,700. Determine the fixed booking fee.
qs.s: The rate per guest is \(\frac{1700 - 1100}{70 - 40} = \$20\). The fixed booking fee is \(1100 - 40(20) = \$300\).

qs.q: A construction company purchased an excavator. Under linear depreciation, its value was $115,000 after 2 years and $85,000 after 5 years. Determine the purchase price of the excavator.
qs.s: The annual depreciation is \(\frac{115\,000 - 85\,000}{5 - 2} = \$10\,000\) per year. The purchase price is \(115\,000 + 2(10\,000) = \$135\,000\).

qs.q: A printing shop charges a fixed setup cost plus a constant fee per booklet printed. An order of 200 booklets costs $550, and an order of 500 booklets costs $850. Determine the fixed setup cost.
qs.s: The variable rate is \(\frac{850 - 550}{500 - 200} = \$1\) per booklet. The fixed setup cost is \(550 - 200(1) = \$350\).

qs.q: A factory's monthly natural gas bill consists of a fixed administrative charge plus a constant fee per gigajoule (GJ) used. In March, using 420 GJ, the bill was $3,810. In April, using 650 GJ, the bill was $5,420. Determine the fixed administrative charge.
qs.s: The rate per gigajoule is \(\frac{5420 - 3810}{650 - 420} = \$7\) per GJ. The fixed administrative charge is \(3810 - 420(7) = \$870\).

qs.q: A medical laboratory bought specialized diagnostic equipment. After 15 months of operation, its value was assessed at $84,500. After 39 months of operation, its value dropped to $55,700. Assuming linear depreciation, determine the original purchase price of the equipment.
qs.s: The monthly depreciation is \(\frac{84\,500 - 55\,700}{39 - 15} = \$1200\) per month. The initial purchase price was \(84\,500 + 15(1200) = \$102\,500\).

qs.q: A courier service charges a flat pickup fee plus a constant rate per kilometre driven. A delivery of 35 km costs $44.75, while a delivery of 60 km costs $66.00. Determine the flat pickup fee.
qs.s: The cost per kilometre is \(\frac{66.00 - 44.75}{60 - 35} = \$0.85\). The flat pickup fee is \(44.75 - 35(0.85) = \$15.00\).

qs.q: A logistics company purchased a fleet of commercial vans in the year 2016. In 2019, the total value of the fleet was $186,000, and in 2023, its value was $114,000. Assuming linear depreciation, determine the purchase price of the fleet in 2016.
qs.s: The annual depreciation is \(\frac{186\,000 - 114\,000}{2023 - 2019} = \$18\,000\) per year. Since 2019 is 3 years after 2016, the original purchase price was \(186\,000 + 3(18\,000) = \$240\,000\).

qs.q: A banquet hall charges a fixed room fee plus a constant price per guest. When 40 guests attend, the average cost per guest is $55. When 70 guests attend, the average cost per guest is $40. Determine the fixed room fee.
qs.s: The total costs are \(40 \times \$55 = \$2200\) and \(70 \times \$40 = \$2800\), giving a rate of \(\frac{2800 - 2200}{70 - 40} = \$20\) per guest. Thus, the fixed room fee is \(2200 - 40(20) = \$1400\).

qs.q: A tech startup had 45 subscribers in its first month and 105 subscribers in its fourth month. If the number of subscribers continues to grow at this constant rate, how many subscribers will the startup have in its sixth month?
qs.s: The rate of increase is \((105 - 45) / (4 - 1) = 20\) subscribers per month. In the sixth month, the startup will have \(105 + 20(6 - 4) = 145\) subscribers.

qs.q: In the 2nd week of his training program, an athlete ran a total of 18 km. By the 6th week, he was running 34 km. If his weekly running distance increases linearly, how many kilometers will he run in the 8th week?
qs.s: The weekly increase is \((34 - 18) / (6 - 2) = 4\text{ km}\) per week. In the 8th week, he will run \(34 + 4(8 - 6) = 42\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A tutoring center had 52 students enrolled in its 2nd year of operation. By its 5th year, enrollment reached 118 students. If this linear trend continues, how many students will be enrolled in the 6th year?
qs.s: The rate of increase is \((118 - 52) / (5 - 2) = 22\) students per year. In the 6th year, enrollment will be \(118 + 22(6 - 5) = 140\) students.

qs.q: In its 2nd month of operation, a bakery sold 110 specialty cakes. In its 5th month, it sold 185 specialty cakes. If this linear trend continues, how many specialty cakes will the bakery sell in its 7th month?
qs.s: The rate of change is \((185 - 110) / (5 - 2) = 25\) cakes per month. In the 7th month, the bakery will sell \(185 + 25(7 - 5) = 235\) cakes.

qs.q: A community garden harvested 80 kg of vegetables in its 1st year. In its 4th year, the harvest increased to 155 kg. Assuming a linear relationship, how many kilograms of vegetables will the garden harvest in its 5th year?
qs.s: The rate of growth is \((155 - 80) / (4 - 1) = 25\text{ kg}\) per year. In the 5th year, the harvest will be \(155 + 25(5 - 4) = 180\text{ kg}\).

qs.q: The population of a town was 14,200 in the year 2010 and 18,700 in the year 2016. Assuming population growth follows a linear model, what will the town's population be in the year 2025?
qs.s: The annual population growth rate is \((18700 - 14200) / (2016 - 2010) = 750\) people per year. In 2025, the population will be \(18700 + 750(2025 - 2016) = 25{,}450\).

qs.q: A company purchased heavy machinery. After 3 years of use, its value was assessed at $43,500. After 7 years, its value had dropped to $27,900. Assuming the depreciation is linear, what will the machinery's value be after 11 years of use?
qs.s: The rate of depreciation is \((27900 - 43500) / (7 - 3) = -3900\) dollars per year. After 11 years, the value will be \(27900 - 3900(11 - 7) = \$12{,}300\).

qs.q: An environmental agency records the water level of a reservoir during a drought. On day 12, the reservoir level was 418 m. On day 36, the level was 370 m. If the water level continues to drop at this constant rate, what will the water level be on day 65?
qs.s: The rate of change is \((370 - 418) / (36 - 12) = -2\text{ m/day}\). On day 65, the water level will be \(370 - 2(65 - 36) = 312\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A printing service determines that the total cost to print 250 brochures is $185.00, while printing 650 brochures costs $365.00. Assuming a linear cost model, how much will it cost to print 1,200 brochures?

A catering company charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant rate per guest. The total cost for 40 guests is $1,180, and the total cost for 90 guests is $2,230. According to this linear model, what is the total cost for 145 guests?
qs.s: The variable cost per guest is \((2230 - 1180) / (90 - 40) = \$21\). For 145 guests, the total cost is \(2230 + 21(145 - 90) = \$3{,}385\).

qs.q: The high school graduation rate in a school district changed from 68.5% in 2002 to 74.9% in 2010. Assuming a linear relationship, predict the graduation rate in 2015.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{74.9 - 68.5}{2010 - 2002} = \frac{6.4}{8} = 0.8\%\) per year. In 2015 (\(5\) years after 2010), the predicted graduation rate is \(74.9 + 0.8(5) = 78.9\%\).

qs.q: The percentage of adults in a country who read a daily newspaper changed from 58.4% in 1995 to 44.4% in 2005. Assuming a linear trend, predict the percentage of adults who will read a daily newspaper in 2012.
qs.s: The rate of decrease is \(m = \frac{44.4 - 58.4}{2005 - 1995} = \frac{-14.0}{10} = -1.4\%\) per year. In 2012 (\(7\) years after 2005), the predicted percentage is \(44.4 - 1.4(7) = 34.6\%\).

qs.q: The percentage of electricity generated from renewable sources in a region changed from 14.5% in 2010 to 26.5% in 2018. Assuming a linear trend, predict the percentage of electricity generated from renewable sources in 2024.
qs.s: The rate of increase is \(m = \frac{26.5 - 14.5}{2018 - 2010} = \frac{12}{8} = 1.5\%\) per year. In 2024 (\(6\) years after 2018), the predicted percentage is \(26.5 + 1.5(6) = 35.5\%\).

qs.q: The percentage of households in a city with a landline phone decreased from 92% in 2004 to 68% in 2012. Assuming a linear relationship, predict the percentage of households that will have a landline phone in 2017.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{68 - 92}{2012 - 2004} = \frac{-24}{8} = -3\%\) per year. In 2017 (\(5\) years after 2012), the predicted percentage is \(68 + (-3)(5) = 53\%\).

qs.q: The percentage of employees working remotely at a company changed from 8.2% in 2005 to 15.2% in 2015. Assuming a linear relationship, predict the percentage of employees that will work remotely in 2021.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{15.2 - 8.2}{2015 - 2005} = \frac{7.0}{10} = 0.7\%\) per year. In 2021 (\(6\) years after 2015), the predicted percentage is \(15.2 + 0.7(6) = 19.4\%\).

qs.q: At an altitude of 1,500 meters above sea level, the outside air temperature is \(8.2^\circ\text{C}\). At an altitude of 3,500 meters, the temperature is \(-4.8^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming temperature decreases linearly with altitude, predict the temperature at an altitude of 5,200 meters.

A factory's monthly operating cost was $38,500 when producing 1,200 units, and $52,900 when producing 2,000 units. If the relationship between cost and the number of units produced is linear, predict the operating cost when producing 3,100 units.

A commercial printing press had an assessed value of $107,200 after 3.5 years of operation and $80,200 after 6 years of operation. Assuming the machine's value depreciates at a constant linear rate, predict its assessed value after 9.5 years of operation.
qs.s: The annual rate of depreciation is \(m = \frac{80200 - 107200}{6 - 3.5} = \frac{-27000}{2.5} = -10,800\) dollars per year. After \(9.5\) years (\(3.5\) years after year \(6\)), the predicted value is \(80200 - 10800(3.5) = 80200 - 37800 = \$42,400\).

qs.q: In 2010, 11,200 out of 40,000 residents in a city were enrolled in fitness programs. In 2015, the city had 50,000 residents and 20,000 were enrolled. Assuming the percentage of residents enrolled in fitness programs changes at a constant linear rate, predict the percentage of residents that will be enrolled in 2022.
qs.s: The percentage was \(\frac{11200}{40000} = 28\%\) in 2010 and \(\frac{20000}{50000} = 40\%\) in 2015, giving a rate of \(m = \frac{40 - 28}{2015 - 2010} = 2.4\%\) per year. In 2022 (\(7\) years after 2015), the predicted percentage is \(40 + 2.4(7) = 56.8\%\).

qs.q: During an extended dry period, a reservoir's water volume was measured at 184.6 million liters on Day 12 and 139.8 million liters on Day 28. If the water volume continues to decrease at a constant linear rate, predict the volume of water remaining in the reservoir on Day 45.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{139.8 - 184.6}{28 - 12} = \frac{-44.8}{16} = -2.8\text{ million L/day}\). On Day 45 (\(17\) days after Day 28), the remaining volume is \(139.8 - 2.8(17) = 139.8 - 47.6 = 92.2\text{ million liters}\).

qs.q: A printing press is purchased for $45,000. At the end of 10 years, it is sold for scrap for $5,000. If \(V\) represents the value in dollars and \(t\) represents the time in years, find the linear depreciation equation.
qs.s: The points are \((0, 45000)\) and \((10, 5000)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{5000 - 45000}{10 - 0} = -4000\), so the depreciation equation is \(V = -4000t + 45000\).

qs.q: A warehouse forklift is purchased for $28,000. At the end of 6 years, it is sold for scrap for $2,800. If \(V\) represents the value in dollars and \(t\) represents the time in years, find the linear depreciation equation.
qs.s: From \((0, 28000)\) and \((6, 2800)\), calculate the slope \(m = \frac{2800 - 28000}{6 - 0} = -4200\). Therefore, the linear equation is \(V = -4200t + 28000\).

qs.q: A delivery van is purchased for $32,000. At the end of 8 years, it is sold for scrap for $4,000. If \(V\) represents the value in dollars and \(t\) represents the time in years, find the linear depreciation equation.
qs.s: The initial value is \((0, 32000)\) and the scrap value is \((8, 4000)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{4000 - 32000}{8 - 0} = -3500\), giving the equation \(V = -3500t + 32000\).

qs.q: A farm tractor is purchased for $50,000. At the end of 8 years, it is sold for scrap for $6,000. If \(V\) represents the value in dollars and \(t\) represents the time in years, find the linear depreciation equation.
qs.s: Using the points \((0, 50000)\) and \((8, 6000)\), the slope is \(m = \frac{6000 - 50000}{8 - 0} = -5500\). Thus, the equation is \(V = -5500t + 50000\).

qs.q: An office computer server is purchased for $18,000. At the end of 5 years, it is sold for scrap for $1,500. If \(V\) represents the value in dollars and \(t\) represents the time in years, find the linear depreciation equation.
qs.s: Using the coordinates \((0, 18000)\) and \((5, 1500)\), the rate of depreciation is \(m = \frac{1500 - 18000}{5 - 0} = -3300\), yielding \(V = -3300t + 18000\).

qs.q: A construction crane is valued at $148,000 after 3 years of use and $88,000 after 7 years of use. If its value depreciates linearly, find the depreciation equation expressing value \(V\) in dollars in terms of age \(t\) in years.

A company fleet car is valued at $21,600 after 2.5 years of service and $14,400 after 6.5 years of service. If its value depreciates linearly, find the depreciation equation expressing value \(V\) in dollars in terms of age \(t\) in years.

A commercial aircraft engine is worth $620,000 after 4 years of operation and $380,000 after 12 years of operation. If its value depreciates linearly, find the depreciation equation expressing value \(V\) in dollars in terms of age \(t\) in years.

A commercial backup generator is purchased for $48,000. Its value depreciates linearly at a constant rate of $375 per month. Find the depreciation equation expressing its value \(V\) in dollars in terms of its age \(t\) in years.
qs.s: Convert the monthly depreciation rate to an annual rate: \(375 \times 12 = 4500\) dollars per year. With an initial value of $48,000, the equation is \(V = -4500t + 48000\).

qs.q: A factory purchases industrial equipment for $80,000. The company estimates that after 10 years, the equipment will be worth 15% of its original purchase price. Assuming linear depreciation, find the depreciation equation expressing value \(V\) in dollars in terms of time \(t\) in years.

A rare collectible coin was purchased for $3600. The buyer expects the coin to double in value in the next 9 years. Write a linear appreciation equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the coin after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The coin gains $3600 over 9 years, so its yearly rate of growth is \(m = \frac{3600}{9} = 400\). With an initial value of $3600, the equation is \(V = 400t + 3600\).

qs.q: A commercial warehouse was purchased for $750 000. The owners expect the warehouse to double in value in the next 15 years. Write a linear appreciation equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the warehouse after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The value increases by $750 000 over 15 years, which means the yearly appreciation is \(m = \frac{750\,000}{15} = 50\,000\). Hence, the equation is \(V = 50{,}000t + 750{,}000\).

qs.q: A plot of land was purchased for $150 000. The owner expects the land to double in value in the next 12 years. Write a linear appreciation equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the land after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The value increases by $150 000 over 12 years, so the annual rate of appreciation is \(m = \frac{150\,000}{12} = 12\,500\). With a starting value of $150 000, the equation is \(V = 12{,}500t + 150{,}000\).

qs.q: A condominium was purchased for $280 000. The owner expects the condominium to double in value in the next 14 years. Write a linear appreciation equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the condominium after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The condominium increases by $280 000 over 14 years, giving an appreciation rate of \(m = \frac{280\,000}{14} = 20\,000\) dollars per year. With an initial value of $280 000, the equation is \(V = 20{,}000t + 280{,}000\).

qs.q: A vintage car was purchased for $48 000. The collector expects the car to double in value in the next 8 years. Write a linear appreciation equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the car after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The car appreciates by $48 000 over 8 years, yielding an annual rate of \(m = \frac{48\,000}{8} = 6000\). Adding this rate to the purchase price gives \(V = 6000t + 48{,}000\).

qs.q: A cottage was purchased for $320 000. The owner expects its value to appreciate linearly by 75% over the next 12 years. Write a linear equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the cottage after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The total increase in value is \(0.75 \times 320\,000 = 240\,000\) dollars over 12 years, which gives a rate of \(m = \frac{240\,000}{12} = 20\,000\) per year. Thus, the equation is \(V = 20{,}000t + 320{,}000\).

qs.q: A corporate delivery van was valued at $42 000 after 2 years and $21 000 after 5 years. Assuming its value depreciates linearly, write a linear equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the van after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{21\,000 - 42\,000}{5 - 2} = -7000\). Finding the initial value gives \(b = 42\,000 - (-7000)(2) = 56\,000\), so the equation is \(V = -7000t + 56{,}000\).

qs.q: An investor bought a parcel of commercial real estate for $840 000. The investor anticipates that after 18 years, the property will be worth 2.5 times its purchase price. Assuming linear appreciation, write a linear equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the property after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The future value is \(2.5 \times 840\,000 = 2\,100\,000\), which is an increase of \(1\,260\,000\) over 18 years. The annual rate is \(m = \frac{1\,260\,000}{18} = 70\,000\), producing the equation \(V = 70{,}000t + 840{,}000\).

qs.q: An apartment building was valued at $640 000 after 3 years and $880 000 after 7 years. Assuming its value appreciates at a constant rate, write a linear equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the building after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{880\,000 - 640\,000}{7 - 3} = 60\,000\) dollars per year. Solving for the initial value gives \(b = 640\,000 - 60\,000(3) = 460\,000\), resulting in \(V = 60{,}000t + 460{,}000\).

qs.q: A manufacturing company purchased heavy equipment for $225 000. The company estimates that the equipment will linearly depreciate to a scrap value of $45 000 after 15 years. Write a linear equation for the value \(V\) (in dollars) of the equipment after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The total depreciation is \(45\,000 - 225\,000 = -180\,000\) dollars, giving a rate of \(m = \frac{-180\,000}{15} = -12\,000\) per year. With an initial value of $225 000, the equation is \(V = -12{,}000t + 225{,}000\).

qs.q: A commercial espresso machine costs $4,200 new and is expected to be worth $1,800 after 8 years. Assuming its value decreases linearly, what will it be worth after 3 years?
qs.s: The espresso machine loses \(\frac{4200 - 1800}{8} = 300\) dollars in value per year. After 3 years, it will be worth \(4200 - 3(300) = \$3{,}300\).

qs.q: A delivery van costs $32,000 new and is expected to be worth $8,000 after 8 years. Assuming a linear relationship, what will it be worth after 5 years?
qs.s: The van depreciates at a rate of \(\frac{32000 - 8000}{8} = 3000\) dollars per year. After 5 years, it will be worth \(32000 - 5(3000) = \$17{,}000\).

qs.q: A laptop costs $1,200 new and is expected to be worth $300 after 5 years. Assuming its value decreases linearly, what will it be worth after 3 years?
qs.s: The laptop depreciates by \(\frac{1200 - 300}{5} = 180\) dollars per year. After 3 years, its value is \(1200 - 3(180) = \$660\).

qs.q: An office desk costs $800 new and is expected to be worth $200 after 4 years. Assuming its value decreases linearly, what will it be worth after 1 year?
qs.s: The annual depreciation is \(\frac{800 - 200}{4} = 150\) dollars per year. After 1 year, the desk is worth \(800 - 150 = \$650\).

qs.q: A 3D printer costs $1,500 new and is expected to be worth $300 after 6 years. Under a linear depreciation model, what will it be worth after 2 years?
qs.s: The printer depreciates by \(\frac{1500 - 300}{6} = 200\) dollars per year. After 2 years, its value is \(1500 - 2(200) = \$1{,}100\).

qs.q: A catering company finds that the total cost to cater an event for 40 guests is $1,150, and the total cost for 90 guests is $2,150. Assuming a linear relationship between cost and the number of guests, what is the total cost to cater an event for 120 guests?
qs.s: The variable cost is \(\frac{2150 - 1150}{90 - 40} = 20\) dollars per guest, and the fixed cost is \(1150 - 40(20) = 350\). For 120 guests, the total cost is \(20(120) + 350 = \$2{,}750\).

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir is draining at a constant linear rate. After 4 hours of draining, the reservoir contains 42,000 gallons of water, and after 9 hours, it contains 27,000 gallons. How much water will remain in the reservoir after 14 hours of draining?
qs.s: The drainage rate is \(\frac{42000 - 27000}{9 - 4} = 3000\) gallons per hour. After 14 hours (5 hours past the 9-hour mark), the remaining water is \(27000 - 5(3000) = 12{,}000\text{ gallons}\).

qs.q: A fitness club uses a linear monthly fee structure based on the number of personal training sessions booked. A member taking 6 sessions pays $370, while a member taking 14 sessions pays $650. How much will a member pay in a month if they book 20 sessions?
qs.s: The cost per session is \(\frac{650 - 370}{14 - 6} = 35\), and the base monthly fee is \(370 - 6(35) = 160\). For 20 sessions, the total charge is \(35(20) + 160 = \$860\).

qs.q: A piece of industrial machinery is worth $18,500 after 2 years of operation and $11,300 after 6 years of operation. Assuming its value depreciates linearly, what will the machinery be worth after 9 years?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \(\frac{18500 - 11300}{6 - 2} = 1800\) dollars per year. Extrapolating 3 years past year 6, the value after 9 years is \(11300 - 3(1800) = \$5{,}900\).

qs.q: A company purchases a server for $14,400. After 18 months, its value has depreciated linearly to $10,800. If this trend continues, what will the server be worth 3.5 years after its purchase?
qs.s: Since 18 months is 1.5 years, the depreciation rate is \(\frac{14400 - 10800}{1.5} = 2400\) dollars per year. After 3.5 years, its value is \(14400 - 3.5(2400) = \$6{,}000\).

qs.q: A collectible vinyl record is expected to appreciate $25 each year. If the record will be worth $190 in 4 years, what will it be worth in 15 years?
qs.s: Over the 11 years between year 4 and year 15, the record appreciates by \(11 \times 25 = \$275\). Its value in 15 years will be \(190 + 275 = \$465\).

qs.q: A bamboo plant grows at a steady rate of 8 cm each month. If the plant is 94 cm tall after 5 months, how tall will it be after 18 months?
qs.s: Over the 13 months between month 5 and month 18, the plant grows \(13 \times 8 = 104\text{ cm}\). Adding this to its height at 5 months gives \(94 + 104 = 198\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rare comic book increases in value by $45 each year. If it is worth $380 in 3 years, what will it be worth in 11 years?
qs.s: In the 8 years between year 3 and year 11, the comic book gains \(8 \times 45 = \$360\). Adding this to its value in year 3 gives \(380 + 360 = \$740\).

qs.q: Water is pumped into a reservoir at a constant rate of 35 liters per minute. After 6 minutes, the reservoir contains 430 liters of water. How many liters of water will be in the reservoir after 16 minutes?
qs.s: In the 10 minutes from minute 6 to minute 16, an additional \(10 \times 35 = 350\text{ liters}\) are pumped in. The total volume after 16 minutes will be \(430 + 350 = 780\text{ liters}\).

qs.q: A vintage watch increases in value by $60 each year. If the watch will be worth $510 in 4 years, what will it be worth in 12 years?
qs.s: Over the 8 years from year 4 to year 12, the watch increases by \(8 \times 60 = \$480\). Its value in 12 years will be \(510 + 480 = \$990\).

qs.q: A delivery van depreciates by $3400 each year. If the van is worth $28,600 after 3 years, what will it be worth after 8 years?
qs.s: Over the 5 years from year 3 to year 8, the van loses \(5 \times 3400 = \$17,000\). Subtracting this loss from its value at year 3 gives \(28,600 - 17,000 = \$11,600\).

qs.q: A piece of factory equipment was valued at $42,000 after 2 years of operation and at $27,000 after 7 years of operation. Assuming it depreciates at a constant annual rate, what will its value be after 11 years of operation?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \((42,000 - 27,000) / (7 - 2) = \$3000\) per year. Over the 4 years from year 7 to year 11, the value drops by \(4 \times 3000 = \$12,000\), giving \(27,000 - 12,000 = \$15,000\).

qs.q: A cloud storage service charges a fixed monthly maintenance fee plus $0.15 for each gigabyte (GB) stored over the basic limit. A user who stored 240 GB over the limit was charged $58.00. What would be the total monthly charge for a user who stores 550 GB over the limit?
qs.s: The 310 additional gigabytes beyond 240 GB cost \(310 \times 0.15 = \$46.50\). Adding this to the 240 GB bill gives \(58.00 + 46.50 = \$104.50\).

qs.q: It costs a catering company $780 to prepare a dinner for 40 guests and $1260 to prepare a dinner for 70 guests. Assuming the cost is a linear function of the number of guests, what will it cost to prepare a dinner for 115 guests?
qs.s: The variable cost per guest is \((1260 - 780) / (70 - 40) = \$16\), which gives a fixed cost of \(780 - 16(40) = \$140\). For 115 guests, the total cost is \(16(115) + 140 = \$1980\).

qs.q: The outside air temperature decreases at a constant rate of 6.5 °C for every 1000 meters of increase in altitude. If the temperature is 18.2 °C at an altitude of 800 meters, what will the temperature be at an altitude of 3400 meters?
qs.s: The altitude increases by \(3400 - 800 = 2600\text{ m}\), producing a temperature drop of \((2600 / 1000) \times 6.5 = 16.9^\circ\text{C}\). Subtracting this drop from \(18.2^\circ\text{C}\) gives \(18.2 - 16.9 = 1.3^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: An antique painting is valued at $1800 after 2 years and $2400 after 5 years. Assuming its value increases at a constant linear rate, what will it be worth after 9 years?
qs.s: The rate of increase is \(\frac{2400 - 1800}{5 - 2} = \$200\) per year. In 9 years, the painting will be worth \(2400 + (9 - 5)(200) = \$3200\).

qs.q: A bamboo plant was measured to be 45 cm tall on day 4 and 75 cm tall on day 9. Assuming its growth is linear, how tall will the plant be on day 15?
qs.s: The plant grows at a rate of \(\frac{75 - 45}{9 - 4} = 6\text{ cm/day}\). On day 15, its height will be \(75 + (15 - 9)(6) = 111\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: A rare coin is projected to be worth $520 in 4 years and $700 in 7 years. If its value increases linearly, what will it be worth in 11 years?
qs.s: The coin's value increases by \(\frac{700 - 520}{7 - 4} = \$60\) per year. In 11 years, it will be worth \(700 + (11 - 7)(60) = \$940\).

qs.q: A print shop charges $460 to print 20 custom hoodies and $850 to print 50 custom hoodies. Assuming the relationship is linear, what will it cost to print 80 hoodies?
qs.s: The cost increases at a rate of \(\frac{850 - 460}{50 - 20} = \$13\) per hoodie. For 80 hoodies, the total cost is \(850 + (80 - 50)(13) = \$1240\).

qs.q: A chemist records the temperature of a cooling liquid. At 3 minutes, the temperature is 58°C, and at 8 minutes, it is 43°C. Assuming the temperature decreases linearly, what will the temperature be at 12 minutes?
qs.s: The cooling rate is \(\frac{43 - 58}{8 - 3} = -3^\circ\text{C/min}\). At 12 minutes, the temperature will be \(43 + (12 - 8)(-3) = 31^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A company purchased a delivery truck. After 3 years of service, the truck is valued at $28,400, and after 7 years, its value is $17,200. Assuming the truck depreciates at a constant linear rate, what will its value be after 11.5 years?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \(\frac{17200 - 28400}{7 - 3} = -\$2800\) per year. After 11.5 years, the truck's value will be \(17200 + (11.5 - 7)(-2800) = \$4600\).

qs.q: A manufacturing plant finds that producing 1200 units costs $18,600, while producing 2800 units costs $31,400. Assuming a linear relationship between cost and the number of units produced, how much will it cost to produce 4500 units?

A logistics company charges a base dispatch fee plus a constant rate per kilogram. Delivering a 35 kg package costs $89, while delivering an 80 kg package costs $179. If a customer sends two packages weighing 50 kg and 65 kg together in a single delivery, what will the total charge be?
qs.s: The per-kilogram rate is \(\frac{179 - 89}{80 - 35} = \$2\text{/kg}\). For the combined shipment of \(50 + 65 = 115\text{ kg}\), the cost is \(179 + (115 - 80)(2) = \$249\).

qs.q: An atmospheric research balloon records an air temperature of 13.4°C at an altitude of 1200 m, and -4.6°C at an altitude of 4200 m. Assuming the temperature decreases linearly with altitude, what will the temperature be at an altitude of 6500 m?
qs.s: The lapse rate is \(\frac{-4.6 - 13.4}{4200 - 1200} = -0.006^\circ\text{C/m}\). At 6500 m, the temperature will be \(-4.6 + (6500 - 4200)(-0.006) = -18.4^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: An environmental agency tracks the water level of a reservoir during a drought. Six months (0.5 years) after monitoring began, the water level was 142 metres. After 2 years of monitoring, the water level dropped to 115 metres. Assuming the water level decreases at a constant linear rate, what will the water level be 3.5 years after monitoring began?
qs.s: The rate of decrease is \(\frac{115 - 142}{2 - 0.5} = -18\text{ m/year}\). At 3.5 years, the water level will be \(115 + (3.5 - 2)(-18) = 88\text{ metres}\).

exercises.name: Find initial value or fixed cost

qs.q: A plot of land purchased 3 years ago is now worth $85,000. If the land has appreciated $6,500 per year, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Multiply the annual appreciation by 3 years: \(3 \times \$6,500 = \$19,500\). Subtract this amount from the current value: \(\$85,000 - \$19,500 = \$65,500\).

qs.q: A delivery van purchased 4 years ago is now worth $19,600. If the van has depreciated $3,200 per year, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Multiply the annual depreciation by the number of years: \(4 \times \$3,200 = \$12,800\). Add this to the current value to determine the original purchase price: \(\$19,600 + \$12,800 = \$32,400\).

qs.q: A piece of manufacturing equipment purchased 6 years ago is now worth $14,200. If it has depreciated $1,800 per year, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Multiply the annual depreciation by the number of years: \(6 \times \$1,800 = \$10,800\). Add this to the current value to find the original purchase price: \(\$14,200 + \$10,800 = \$25,000\).

qs.q: A collectible comic book purchased 8 years ago is now worth $4,100. If it has appreciated $350 per year, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Multiply the annual appreciation by the number of years: \(8 \times \$350 = \$2,800\). Subtract this total appreciation from the current value: \(\$4,100 - \$2,800 = \$1,300\).

qs.q: A vintage car purchased 5 years ago is now worth $24,500. If the car has appreciated $1,300 per year, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Multiply the annual appreciation by the number of years: \(5 \times \$1,300 = \$6,500\). Subtract this from the current value to find the original purchase price: \(\$24,500 - \$6,500 = \$18,000\).

qs.q: An office building was valued at $485,000 four years after it was purchased and $575,000 nine years after it was purchased. Assuming its value has grown at a constant rate, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: The annual appreciation rate is \(\frac{\$575,000 - \$485,000}{9 - 4} = \$18,000\) per year. Subtract 4 years of appreciation from the 4-year value: \(\$485,000 - 4(\$18,000) = \$413,000\).

qs.q: A print shop charges a fixed setup fee plus a constant cost per custom brochure printed. An order of 250 brochures costs $185, and an order of 600 brochures costs $395. What is the fixed setup fee?
qs.s: The cost per brochure is \(m = \frac{\$395 - \$185}{600 - 250} = \$0.60\). Subtract the variable cost for 250 brochures from the total cost: \(\$185 - 250(\$0.60) = \$35\).

qs.q: A company vehicle was appraised at $28,400 two years after it was bought and $17,600 six years after it was bought. Assuming linear depreciation, find its original purchase price.
qs.s: The rate of depreciation is \(\frac{\$28,400 - \$17,600}{6 - 2} = \$2,700\) per year. Add 2 years of depreciation to the 2-year value to find the original price: \(\$28,400 + 2(\$2,700) = \$33,800\).

qs.q: A piece of industrial equipment purchased 7 years ago is now worth $41,500. For the first 3 years, it depreciated at a rate of $6,200 per year, and for the last 4 years, it depreciated at $4,500 per year. Find its original purchase price.
qs.s: Calculate the total depreciation over both intervals: \(3(\$6,200) + 4(\$4,500) = \$18,600 + \$18,000 = \$36,600\). Add this total to the current value: \(\$41,500 + \$36,600 = \$78,100\).

qs.q: A catering company finds that the total cost to cater an event for 40 guests is $1,420, while the total cost for 90 guests is $2,720. Assuming the relationship is linear, find the fixed cost.
qs.s: Find the variable cost per guest: \(m = \frac{\$2,720 - \$1,420}{90 - 40} = \$26\). Subtract the variable cost for 40 guests from the total cost: \(\$1,420 - 40(\$26) = \$380\).

qs.q: An equipment rental company charges a fixed processing fee plus $8.50 per hour of tool use. If renting a tool for 6 hours costs $121.00, how much will it cost to rent the tool for 14 hours?
qs.s: The hourly charge for 6 hours is \(6 \times 8.50 = \$51.00\), giving a processing fee of \(121.00 - 51.00 = \$70.00\). For 14 hours, the total cost is \(70.00 + 14 \times 8.50 = \$189.00\).

qs.q: A banquet hall charges a flat cleaning fee plus $12.00 per guest. If an event with 50 guests costs $850.00, how much will an event with 90 guests cost?
qs.s: The guest cost for 50 guests is \(50 \times 12.00 = \$600.00\), making the cleaning fee \(850.00 - 600.00 = \$250.00\). For 90 guests, the total cost is \(250.00 + 90 \times 12.00 = \$1330.00\).

qs.q: A marketing agency charges a fixed account setup fee plus $7.00 for every 50 brochures printed. If an order of 300 brochures costs $67.00, how much will an order of 750 brochures cost?
qs.s: Printing 300 brochures requires 6 sets of 50, costing \(6 \times 7.00 = \$42.00\), so the setup fee is \(67.00 - 42.00 = \$25.00\). For 750 brochures (15 sets of 50), the total cost is \(25.00 + 15 \times 7.00 = \$130.00\).

qs.q: A taxi service charges a base pickup fare plus $2.20 for every kilometer driven. If a 15-kilometer ride costs $37.00, how much will a 26-kilometer ride cost?
qs.s: The mileage cost for 15 km is \(15 \times 2.20 = \$33.00\), which gives a base fare of \(37.00 - 33.00 = \$4.00\). For a 26-km ride, the cost is \(4.00 + 26 \times 2.20 = \$61.20\).

qs.q: A custom t-shirt shop charges a fixed design setup fee plus $4.50 for each shirt printed. If an order of 40 shirts costs $260.00, how much will an order of 75 shirts cost?
qs.s: The variable cost for 40 shirts is \(40 \times 4.50 = \$180.00\), which gives a fixed setup fee of \(260.00 - 180.00 = \$80.00\). For 75 shirts, the total cost is \(80.00 + 75 \times 4.50 = \$417.50\).

qs.q: A commercial bakery finds that it costs $310.00 to bake 80 loaves of artisan bread and $475.00 to bake 190 loaves. Assuming the relationship between the total cost and the number of loaves is linear, how much will it cost to bake 300 loaves?
qs.s: The variable cost is \(m = \frac{475 - 310}{190 - 80} = \$1.50\) per loaf, and the fixed cost is \(310 - 80(1.50) = \$190.00\). For 300 loaves, the cost is \(1.50(300) + 190.00 = \$640.00\).

qs.q: An equipment warranty plan reimburses a fixed percentage of repair costs, less a fixed $75.00 deductible. If a repair bill of $450.00 receives a reimbursement of $285.00, how much will be reimbursed for a repair bill of $1400.00?

A commercial printer charges a fixed file setup fee, plus $4.50 per book for paper and printing, and $1.75 per book for binding. If an order of 250 books costs $1662.50, how much will an order of 600 books cost?
qs.s: The combined variable cost is \(4.50 + 1.75 = \$6.25\) per book, so the setup fee is \(1662.50 - 250(6.25) = \$100.00\). For 600 books, the total cost is \(100.00 + 600(6.25) = \$3850.00\).

qs.q: A water utility charges a monthly infrastructure fee plus a constant rate per cubic meter of water used. In June, a household used 24 cubic meters and was billed $65.80. In July, the household used 40 cubic meters and was billed $97.80. How much will the bill be in August if the household uses 55 cubic meters of water?
qs.s: The rate per cubic meter is \(m = \frac{97.80 - 65.80}{40 - 24} = \$2.00\), so the monthly fee is \(65.80 - 24(2.00) = \$17.80\). For 55 cubic meters, the total bill is \(17.80 + 55(2.00) = \$127.80\).

qs.q: A bulk printing company charges a machine calibration fee, a fixed packaging fee of $15.00, and $8.25 for every 250 flyers printed. If an order of 3000 flyers costs $144.00 in total, how much will an order of 7500 flyers cost?
qs.s: Printing 3000 flyers is 12 batches of 250, costing \(12 \times 8.25 = \$99.00\), which leaves total fixed fees of \(144.00 - 99.00 = \$45.00\). For 7500 flyers (30 batches), the total cost is \(45.00 + 30(8.25) = \$292.50\).

qs.q: A bakery's monthly operating cost is $3200 when it produces 1200 loaves of bread. When it produces 1800 loaves of bread, its operating cost is $4100. Assuming a linear relationship between cost and the number of loaves produced, what will the operating cost be if the bakery produces 2600 loaves of bread?
qs.s: The cost increases at a rate of \(m = \frac{4100 - 3200}{1800 - 1200} = 1.50\) dollars per loaf, giving fixed costs of \(3200 - 1.50(1200) = \$1400\). For 2600 loaves, the operating cost is \(1.50(2600) + 1400 = \$5300\).

qs.q: A commuter rail system recorded 14 000 passenger trips per day when operating 45 trains. When the number of trains was increased to 65, the system recorded 20 000 passenger trips per day. If this linear trend continues, how many daily passenger trips will the system record when operating 90 trains?
qs.s: Each additional train yields \(\frac{20\,000 - 14\,000}{65 - 45} = 300\) daily passenger trips. For 90 trains, the daily passenger trips will be \(20\,000 + 300(90 - 65) = 27\,500\).

qs.q: A county with a population of 50 000 recorded 850 emergency room visits in a month. When the county's population grew to 70 000, the number of visits was 1150 in a month. If this linear trend continues, how many emergency room visits will be expected in a month when the population reaches 95 000?
qs.s: The rate of visits is \(m = \frac{1150 - 850}{70\,000 - 50\,000} = 0.015\) visits per resident. When the population reaches 95 000, the expected visits are \(1150 + 0.015(95\,000 - 70\,000) = 1525\).

qs.q: A town with a population of 40 000 generated 260 tonnes of recyclable waste per month. When the population grew to 55 000, the town generated 350 tonnes of recyclable waste per month. If this linear trend continues, how many tonnes of recyclable waste per month will the town generate when its population reaches 80 000?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{350 - 260}{55\,000 - 40\,000} = 0.006\) tonnes per person. When the population reaches 80 000, the waste generated is \(350 + 0.006(80\,000 - 55\,000) = 500\) tonnes.

qs.q: A small college campus used 35 000 litres of water daily when 500 students were enrolled. When enrollment increased to 800 students, daily water consumption rose to 47 000 litres. If this linear trend continues, what will the daily water consumption be, in litres, when enrollment reaches 1200 students?
qs.s: The rate of water usage is \(m = \frac{47\,000 - 35\,000}{800 - 500} = 40\) litres per student. For 1200 students, the consumption is \(47\,000 + 40(1200 - 800) = 63\,000\) litres.

qs.q: At an altitude of 1500 metres above sea level, the outside air temperature on a mountain is \(7.5^\circ\text{C}\). At an altitude of 3900 metres, the temperature drops to \(-8.1^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming temperature decreases linearly with altitude, what will the temperature be, in degrees Celsius, at an altitude of 6500 metres?
qs.s: The lapse rate is \(m = \frac{-8.1 - 7.5}{3900 - 1500} = -0.0065^\circ\text{C/m}\). At 6500 m, the temperature is \(-8.1 - 0.0065(6500 - 3900) = -25^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: In 2011, a regional solar power grid had an installed capacity of 145 megawatts (MW). By 2017, the installed capacity had grown to 367 MW. Assuming this growth follows a constant linear trend, what will the installed capacity of the grid be, in MW, in the year 2026?
qs.s: The annual growth rate is \(m = \frac{367 - 145}{2017 - 2011} = 37\) MW per year. In 2026, which is 9 years after 2017, the capacity will be \(367 + 37(9) = 700\) MW.

qs.q: A cargo plane at cruising altitude has 48 500 kg of fuel remaining after flying a distance of 1200 km. After flying 2800 km, its fuel remaining is 37 700 kg. If fuel consumption is a linear function of distance flown, how many kilograms of fuel will remain after the plane flies a total distance of 5500 km?
qs.s: The fuel burns at a rate of \(m = \frac{37\,700 - 48\,500}{2800 - 1200} = -6.75\) kg/km. After 5500 km, the remaining fuel is \(37\,700 - 6.75(5500 - 2800) = 19\,475\) kg.

qs.q: A manufacturing plant's cumulative energy consumption is 415 megawatt-hours (MWh) after running for 15 hours, and 655 MWh after running for 27 hours in a production cycle. Assuming a linear relationship, what will the cumulative energy consumption be, in MWh, if the plant operates continuously for 2.5 days?
qs.s: Operating for 2.5 days equals \(2.5 \times 24 = 60\) hours, and the power rate is \(m = \frac{655 - 415}{27 - 15} = 20\) MWh/h with a baseline of \(415 - 20(15) = 115\) MWh. At 60 hours, energy consumption is \(20(60) + 115 = 1315\) MWh.

qs.q: A commercial printing press draws ink from a large reservoir. After printing 18 500 posters, 462 litres of ink remain in the reservoir. After printing 42 500 posters, 318 litres remain. If ink consumption is linearly related to the number of posters printed, how many litres of ink will remain in the reservoir after printing 75 000 posters?
qs.s: The ink usage rate is \(m = \frac{318 - 462}{42\,500 - 18\,500} = -0.006\) litres per poster. After printing 75 000 posters, the remaining ink is \(318 - 0.006(75\,000 - 42\,500) = 123\) litres.

qs.q: A delivery truck is worth $48 000 when purchased new, but is worth nothing after its 8-year life cycle. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 48000}{8 - 0} = -6000\) and the initial value is the \(y\)-intercept \(b = 48000\). Thus, the depreciation equation is \(V = -6000t + 48000\).
