qs.q: A commercial lawnmower is worth $15 000 when bought new, but is worth nothing after its 6-year life cycle. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The rate of depreciation is \(m = \frac{0 - 15000}{6 - 0} = -2500\) per year, and the initial value is \(b = 15000\). Hence, the equation is \(V = -2500t + 15000\).

qs.q: An office copying system is worth $18 000 when installed new, but is worth nothing after its 5-year life cycle. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The rate of depreciation is \(m = \frac{0 - 18000}{5 - 0} = -3600\) per year, with an initial value of \(b = 18000\). Therefore, the linear depreciation equation is \(V = -3600t + 18000\).

qs.q: A data center server rack is worth $72 000 when installed new, but is worth nothing after its 12-year life cycle. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 72000}{12 - 0} = -6000\) and the starting value is \(b = 72000\). Writing this in slope-intercept form gives \(V = -6000t + 72000\).

qs.q: A manufacturing robot is worth $135 000 when installed new, but is worth nothing after its 9-year life cycle. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{0 - 135000}{9 - 0} = -15000\), and the initial value at \(t = 0\) is \(b = 135000\). Thus, the equation is \(V = -15000t + 135000\).

qs.q: A fleet of construction bulldozers is worth $840 000 when purchased new, but has a salvage value of $75 000 after its 15-year life cycle. Find the linear depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{75000 - 840000}{15 - 0} = \frac{-765000}{15} = -51000\), and the initial value is \(b = 840000\). Thus, the linear equation is \(V = -51000t + 840000\).

qs.q: A cargo vessel is worth $1 850 000 when purchased new, but has a scrap value of $125 000 after its 25-year life cycle. Find the linear depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.

An industrial turbine is worth $520 000 when installed new, but has a salvage value of $40 000 after its 20-year life cycle. Find the linear depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{40000 - 520000}{20 - 0} = \frac{-480000}{20} = -24000\), and the \(y\)-intercept is the initial value \(b = 520000\). The linear depreciation equation is \(V = -24000t + 520000\).

qs.q: A commercial airplane engine depreciates linearly. It is worth $450 000 after 4 years of operation and $270 000 after 10 years of operation. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.

A hospital's MRI machine depreciates linearly. It is worth $680 000 after 2 years of service and $360 000 after 6 years of service. Find the depreciation equation for its value \(V\) (in dollars) after \(t\) years.
The total cost, \(C\), of a bicycle is the sum of the selling price, \(p\), plus a sales tax of 8%, plus a $25 assembly fee. Express \(C\) as a linear function of \(p\).
qs.s: The total cost is the sum of the selling price, the 8% sales tax, and the assembly fee: \(C = p + 0.08p + 25\). Combining like terms gives \(C = 1.08p + 25\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(T\), of a refrigerator is the sum of the purchase price, \(r\), plus a sales tax of 5%, plus a $30 haul-away fee. Express \(T\) as a linear function of \(r\).
qs.s: Add the purchase price, the 5% sales tax, and the haul-away fee: \(T = r + 0.05r + 30 = 1.05r + 30\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(C\), of a smartphone is the sum of the selling price, \(s\), plus a sales tax of 13%, plus a $15 activation fee. Express \(C\) as a linear function of \(s\).
qs.s: Add the selling price, the 13% sales tax, and the activation fee: \(C = s + 0.13s + 15\). Combining like terms gives \(C = 1.13s + 15\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(T\), of a television is the sum of the retail price, \(x\), plus a sales tax of 6%, plus a $40 delivery charge. Express \(T\) as a linear function of \(x\).
qs.s: The total cost is the sum of the retail price, the 6% sales tax, and the delivery charge: \(T = x + 0.06x + 40\). Combining like terms yields \(T = 1.06x + 40\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(B\), of a concert ticket package is the sum of the face value, \(f\), plus a 15% service charge, plus a $5 processing fee. Express \(B\) as a linear function of \(f\).
qs.s: The total cost is the sum of the face value, the 15% service charge, and the processing fee: \(B = f + 0.15f + 5 = 1.15f + 5\).

qs.q: A clothing retailer offers a 20% discount on the regular price, \(r\), of a jacket. The total cost, \(C\), is the discounted price, plus a sales tax of 8% applied to the discounted price, plus a $6 flat shipping fee. Express \(C\) as a linear function of \(r\).
qs.s: The discounted price is \(0.80r\), and applying the 8% tax gives \(1.08(0.80r) = 0.864r\). Adding the $6 shipping fee yields \(C = 0.864r + 6\).

qs.q: A dealership sells a motorcycle at base price \(b\). The dealer applies a $500 promotional rebate directly to the base price before calculating sales tax. The buyer pays the discounted price, plus a 10% sales tax on that discounted price, plus a $180 documentation fee. Express the total cost, \(T\), as a linear function of \(b\).
qs.s: The discounted price with 10% tax is \(1.10(b - 500) = 1.10b - 550\). Adding the $180 documentation fee gives \(T = 1.10b - 550 + 180 = 1.10b - 370\).

qs.q: A customer buys a dishwasher with selling price \(p\). The retailer adds an 8% sales tax, a 5% extended warranty fee (both calculated on \(p\)), a $60 delivery fee, and deducts an instant manufacturer rebate of $100. Express the final amount paid, \(A\), as a linear function of \(p\).
qs.s: Combine the percentage terms: \(p + 0.08p + 0.05p = 1.13p\). Combine the constant amounts: \(60 - 100 = -40\), giving \(A = 1.13p - 40\).

qs.q: A boutique purchases a dining table at a wholesale price of \(w\) and marks it up by 40%. The customer pays the marked-up price, plus a sales tax of 5% on that marked-up price, plus a $75 home delivery fee. Express the total cost to the customer, \(C\), as a linear function of \(w\).
qs.s: The marked-up price is \(1.40w\). Applying 5% sales tax gives \(1.05(1.40w) = 1.47w\), and adding the delivery fee gives \(C = 1.47w + 75\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(C\), of a sound system is the sum of the retail price, \(p\), a state sales tax of 6.5%, a local sales tax of 1.5%, a $35 shipping fee, and a $15 recycling fee. Express \(C\) as a linear function of \(p\).
qs.s: Combine the tax rates, \(6.5\% + 1.5\% = 8\%\), so the taxed price is \(p + 0.08p = 1.08p\). Adding the combined fixed fees of \(35 + 15 = 50\) gives \(C = 1.08p + 50\).

qs.q: The total cost of a refrigerator is the sum of the purchase price, plus a sales tax of 6%, plus a $50 delivery fee. What is the total cost of a refrigerator with a purchase price of $1200?
qs.s: The sales tax is 0.06 * $1200 = $72. Adding the purchase price, tax, and delivery fee gives $1200 + $72 + $50 = $1322.

qs.q: The total cost of an electric bicycle is the sum of the list price, plus a sales tax of 5%, plus a $40 assembly fee. What is the total cost of an electric bicycle with a list price of $940?
qs.s: The sales tax is 0.05 * $940 = $47. Adding the list price, sales tax, and assembly fee gives $940 + $47 + $40 = $1027.

qs.q: The total cost of a smartphone is the sum of the retail price, plus a sales tax of 7%, plus a $25 activation fee. What is the total cost of a smartphone with a retail price of $600?
qs.s: The sales tax is 0.07 * $600 = $42. Adding the retail price, tax, and activation fee gives $600 + $42 + $25 = $667.

qs.q: The total cost of a television is the sum of the selling price, plus a sales tax of 8%, plus a $15 electronic recycling fee. What is the total cost of a television that sells for $850?
qs.s: The sales tax is 0.08 * $850 = $68. Adding the selling price, sales tax, and recycling fee gives $850 + $68 + $15 = $933.

qs.q: The total cost of a gas grill is the sum of the selling price, plus a sales tax of 9%, plus a $30 assembly fee. What is the total cost of a gas grill that sells for $450?
qs.s: The sales tax is 0.09 * $450 = $40.50. Adding the selling price, sales tax, and assembly fee gives $450 + $40.50 + $30 = $520.50.

qs.q: An insurance policy pays 80% of all medical expenses that exceed a $500 deductible, plus a fixed wellness allowance of $150. How much does the policy pay for a patient who has $4,250 in eligible medical expenses?
qs.s: Subtract the $500 deductible from $4,250 to get $3,750 in covered expenses. Then, find 80% of \(3,750 (\)3,000) and add the $150 allowance to get $3,150.

qs.q: A conference hall charges a base room rental of $1,500, a catering fee of $42 per attendee, a beverage fee of $13.50 per attendee, a 10% service charge applied only to the combined catering and beverage total, and a flat audiovisual fee of $350. What is the total cost to host an event for 180 attendees?
qs.s: The food and beverage cost is 180 * ($42 + $13.50) = $9,990, and adding the 10% service charge yields 1.10 * $9,990 = $10,989. Adding the flat room rental and audiovisual fees ($1,500 + $350) gives $10,989 + $1,850 = $12,839.

qs.q: The total cost of purchasing imported commercial fitness equipment is the sum of the wholesale price, an 8.5% import tariff, a 6% sales tax (both applied to the wholesale price), an environmental disposal fee of $120, and a flat freight shipping charge of $385. What is the total cost for an order with a wholesale price of $14,600?
qs.s: The tariff is 0.085 * $14,600 = $1,241 and the tax is 0.06 * $14,600 = $876. Adding the wholesale price, both percentage charges, and the fixed fees ($120 + $385) gives $14,600 + $1,241 + $876 + $505 = $17,222.

qs.q: A school club orders customized hooded sweatshirts. The total cost consists of a base price of $28 per sweatshirt, a shipping fee of $4.50 per sweatshirt, a one-time artwork setup fee of $75, and a flat handling fee of $30. What is the total cost to order 140 sweatshirts?
qs.s: The per-sweatshirt cost is $28 + $4.50 = $32.50, which totals $32.50 * 140 = $4,550. Adding the flat fees of $75 and $30 gives a total of $4,550 + $105 = $4,655.

qs.q: The total invoice price for a fleet vehicle purchase is calculated by taking the total list price, subtracting a 15% fleet discount, adding a 7% sales tax on the discounted amount, and adding a $250 administrative fee and an $1,150 destination charge. What is the total invoice price for an order with a list price of $64,000?
qs.s: The discounted price is 0.85 * $64,000 = $54,400. Adding 7% sales tax gives 1.07 * $54,400 = $58,208, and adding the two fees ($250 + $1,150 = $1,400) gives $59,608.

qs.q: The total cost of a television is the sum of the retail price, plus a sales tax of 5%, plus a $30 delivery fee. What is the retail price of a television whose total cost was $765.00?
qs.s: Subtract the $30 delivery fee from the total cost to get $735.00, then divide by 1.05 to find the retail price of $700.

qs.q: The total cost of a bicycle is the sum of the sticker price, plus a sales tax of 6%, plus a $25 assembly fee. What is the sticker price of a bicycle whose total cost was $449.00?
qs.s: Subtract the $25 assembly fee from the total cost to get $424.00, then divide by 1.06 to obtain the sticker price of $400.

qs.q: The total cost of a dishwasher is the sum of the list price, plus a sales tax of 7%, plus a $45 haul-away fee. What is the list price of a dishwasher whose total cost was $580.00?
qs.s: Subtract the $45 haul-away fee from the total to get $535.00, then divide by 1.07 to find the list price of $500.

qs.q: The total cost of a smartphone is the sum of the purchase price, plus a sales tax of 8%, plus a $15 activation fee. What is the purchase price of a smartphone whose total cost was $663.00?
qs.s: Subtract the $15 fee from the total to get $648.00, then divide by 1.08 to find the purchase price of $600.

qs.q: The total cost of a couch is the sum of the retail price, plus a sales tax of 9%, plus a $35 fabric-protection fee. What is the retail price of a couch whose total cost was $961.50?
qs.s: Subtract the $35 protection fee from the total to get $926.50, then divide by 1.09 to find the retail price of $850.

qs.q: The total amount paid for a car is the selling price minus a $1,200 trade-in credit, plus a 6% sales tax applied to the remaining balance, plus a $145 registration fee and a $75 documentation fee. What was the selling price of the car if the customer paid a total of $14,000?
qs.s: Subtract the fees ($145 + $75 = $220) from $14,000 to get $13,780, divide by 1.06 to find the post-trade-in amount of $13,000, and add the $1,200 credit to find the selling price of $14,200.

qs.q: An event hall charges a base rental fee of $500 plus $45 per guest for dinner. An 18% service charge is added to this subtotal, followed by a flat $220 cleaning fee. If the total bill for an event came to $3,996, how many guests attended?
qs.s: Subtract the $220 cleaning fee to get $3,776, divide by 1.18 to get a subtotal of $3,200, subtract the $500 base rental to get $2,700, and divide by $45 per guest to get 60 guests.

qs.q: An insurance policy reimburses 75% of eligible medical expenses after a $250 annual deductible is subtracted. A mandatory $35 processing fee is then deducted from this reimbursement payout. If the net payout received by the policyholder was $1,090, what was the total amount of eligible medical expenses?
qs.s: Add the $35 processing fee to $1,090 to get $1,125, divide by 0.75 to find the post-deductible expenses of $1,500, and add the $250 deductible to find total eligible expenses of $1,750.

qs.q: A customer bought a laptop using a $50 instant store coupon applied before taxes. The purchase was subject to a 5% GST and a 7% PST (both calculated on the discounted price), plus a $16 electronic recycling fee and an $8 shipping fee. What was the original sticker price of the laptop if the total amount paid was $864?
qs.s: Subtract the $24 in fees from $864 to get $840, divide by 1.12 (the combined 12% tax rate) to get the discounted price of $750, and add the $50 coupon to find the original sticker price of $800.

qs.q: A freelance graphic designer bills clients a base setup fee of $350 plus an hourly rate of $65. On rush projects, a 20% surcharge is added to the labor cost, along with a flat $45 digital asset archiving fee. If a client was billed a total of $1,565 for a rush project, how many hours of labor were billed?
qs.s: Subtract the fixed fees totaling \(395 (\)350 + $45) from $1,565 to get $1,170 in labor, then divide by the rush hourly rate of $65 \times 1.20 = $78 to find that 15 hours were billed.

qs.q: It costs $300 to purchase equipment to start making custom pinback buttons. Each button costs 20¢ in materials to produce. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n buttons.
qs.s: With a fixed startup cost of $300 and a variable cost of 20¢ = $0.20 per button, the cost equation is C = 0.20n + 300.

qs.q: It costs $1500 to purchase a cart and supplies to start a pretzel stand. Each pretzel costs 55¢ to produce. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n pretzels.
qs.s: The fixed initial cost is $1500 and the cost per pretzel is 55¢ = $0.55, so the equation modeling total cost is C = 0.55n + 1500.

qs.q: It costs $450 to start up a business selling lemonade at a park. Each cup of lemonade costs 35¢ to produce. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n cups of lemonade.
qs.s: The startup cost is the fixed cost ($450) and the production cost per cup is 35¢ = $0.35, giving the linear cost equation C = 0.35n + 450.

qs.q: It costs $520 to set up a craft business making scented candles. Each candle costs 80¢ in wax and wick to produce. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n candles.
qs.s: The constant startup expense is $520 and the rate per candle is 80¢ = $0.80, so the cost equation is C = 0.80n + 520.

qs.q: It costs $650 to start up a home baking business selling cupcakes. Each cupcake costs 75¢ to make. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n cupcakes.
qs.s: The initial startup cost represents the y-intercept ($650) and the cost per cupcake is the slope (75¢ = $0.75), yielding C = 0.75n + 650.

qs.q: An athletic apparel company pays a one-time equipment fee of $4800 and a monthly storage fee of $1200. Fabric costs $180 for every batch of 12 jerseys, and each jersey requires an additional $2.50 for custom numbering and 50¢ for packaging. Write the cost equation for the first month's total cost C (in dollars) to produce n jerseys.
qs.s: The total fixed cost is 4800 + 1200 = $6000. The cost per jersey is (180 / 12) + 2.50 + 0.50 = 15 + 2.50 + 0.50 = $18, yielding C = 18n + 6000.

qs.q: A print shop finds that it costs $490 to produce 150 customized photo books and $730 to produce 350 photo books. Assuming a linear relationship, write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) in terms of the number of photo books n.

A bicycle manufacturer has fixed monthly operating expenses of $8400. In addition, producing each bicycle requires $135 in frame components, $68 in gears and brakes, a hardware pack that costs $45 for every 3 bicycles, and $22 for assembly labor. Write the cost equation for the monthly total cost C (in dollars) to produce n bicycles.
qs.s: The fixed cost is $8400 and the unit cost is 135 + 68 + (45 / 3) + 22 = 135 + 68 + 15 + 22 = $240 per bicycle, giving C = 240n + 8400.

qs.q: A startup business manufactures handmade leather wallets. The initial startup expenses include $2300 for machinery, $450 for a business license, and $250 for website setup. In addition, each wallet requires $8.50 in leather, $1.75 in thread and hardware, and 75¢ in packaging. Write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) to produce n wallets.
qs.s: Sum the fixed costs: 2300 + 450 + 250 = $3000. Sum the costs per wallet: 8.50 + 1.75 + 0.75 = $11.00, resulting in C = 11n + 3000.

qs.q: A catering company determines that the total cost to cater an event for 40 guests is $760, and the total cost for 75 guests is $1180. Assuming the relationship is linear, write the cost equation for the total cost C (in dollars) in terms of the number of guests n.
qs.s: Find the slope m = (1180 - 760) / (75 - 40) = 420 / 35 = 12. Using point-slope form with (40, 760), C - 760 = 12(n - 40), which simplifies to C = 12n + 280.

qs.q: A vendor spends $600 on an espresso maker to start selling coffee. Each cup of coffee costs 50¢ in ingredients to produce. How many cups of coffee are produced if the total cost is $950?
qs.s: Subtract the $600 machine cost from the total cost ($950 - $600 = $350), then divide by the unit cost in dollars ($350 / $0.50 = 700 cups).

qs.q: A student starts a button-making hobby. The button press costs $60, and each button costs 20¢ in materials to produce. How many buttons are produced if the total cost is $150?
qs.s: Subtract the $60 equipment cost from the total cost ($150 - $60 = $90), then divide by the cost per button in dollars ($90 / $0.20 = 450 buttons).

qs.q: It costs $500 for equipment to start a scented candle business. Each candle costs $2.50 in materials to produce. How many candles are produced if the total cost is $1100?
qs.s: Subtract the $500 initial equipment cost from the total cost ($1100 - $500 = $600), then divide by the cost per candle ($600 / $2.50 = 240 candles).

qs.q: A baker spends $300 on specialty baking pans to start a cookie business. Each cookie costs 80¢ in ingredients to make. How many cookies are made if the total cost is $780?
qs.s: Subtract the $300 pan cost from the total cost ($780 - $300 = $480), then divide by the cost per cookie in dollars ($480 / $0.80 = 600 cookies).

qs.q: It costs $45 for supplies and equipment to start a lemonade stand. Each cup of lemonade costs 25¢ to make. How many cups of lemonade are made if the total cost is $95?
qs.s: Subtract the $45 startup cost from the total cost ($95 - $45 = $50), then divide by the cost per cup in dollars ($50 / $0.25 = 200 cups).

qs.q: A catering hall charges a flat room rental fee plus a fixed amount per guest. An event with 40 guests costs $1400, while an event with 80 guests costs $2400. How many guests attended an event if the total bill was $3400?
qs.s: The cost per guest is \(m = \frac{2400 - 1400}{80 - 40} = \$25\), giving a flat fee of \(1400 - 25(40) = \$400\). Solve \(25g + 400 = 3400\) to get \(25g = 3000\), so \(g = 120\) guests.

qs.q: A small company produces customized backpacks. The fixed costs include $2500 for equipment rental and $500 for a business permit. Each backpack costs $9.00 in fabric, $3.50 in hardware, and $2.50 in labor to produce. How many backpacks are produced if the total cost is $9000?
qs.s: The total fixed cost is $2500 + $500 = $3000, and the unit cost is $9.00 + $3.50 + $2.50 = $15.00. Solve $3000 + 15x = 9000 to find $15x = 6000, which gives \(x = 400\) backpacks.

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir initially holds 1800 megaliters of water and drains at a constant rate of 45 megaliters per day. After how many days will the reservoir contain 540 megaliters of water?
qs.s: Set up the linear relation \(1800 - 45d = 540\), where \(d\) is the number of days. Subtract 1800 to get \(-45d = -1260\), then divide by \(-45\) to get \(d = 28\) days.

qs.q: An extended health care plan reimburses 75% of prescription drug costs, less a $150 annual deductible, according to the formula \(R = 0.75C - 150\), where \(R\) is the reimbursement and \(C\) is the total prescription cost. If a patient received a reimbursement of $480, what was the total cost of the prescriptions?
qs.s: Substitute \(R = 480\) into \(480 = 0.75C - 150\). Add 150 to both sides to get \(630 = 0.75C\), then divide by 0.75 to obtain \(C = \$840\).

qs.q: A moving truck company charges a base rental fee of $80, an equipment fee of $30, and an insurance fee of $20, plus $0.50 per mile driven. If a customer's total bill before taxes is $310, how many miles was the truck driven?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $80 + $30 + $20 = $130. Set up the equation \(130 + 0.50m = 310\), which gives \(0.50m = 180\), so \(m = 360\) miles.

qs.q: It costs $840 to start up a business selling engraved wooden keychains. Each keychain costs 50¢ to make. How many keychains must be sold at two for $2.40 to break even?
qs.s: Each keychain sells for $2.40 / 2 = $1.20, giving a profit of $1.20 - $0.50 = $0.70 per keychain. Solving 0.70x = 840 yields x = 1200 keychains.

qs.q: It costs $600 to start up a business selling greeting cards. Each card costs 60¢ to produce. How many cards must be sold at three for $3.00 to break even?
qs.s: Each card sells for $3.00 / 3 = $1.00, resulting in a margin of $1.00 - $0.60 = $0.40 per card. Solving 0.40x = 600 gives x = 1500 cards.

qs.q: It costs $2400 to start up a business selling handmade soy candles. Each candle costs 80¢ to produce. How many candles must be sold at two for $4.00 to break even?
qs.s: Each candle sells for $4.00 / 2 = $2.00, providing a margin of $2.00 - $0.80 = $1.20 per candle. Solving 1.20x = 2400 gives x = 2000 candles.

qs.q: It costs $1800 to start up a business selling smoothies from a cart. Each smoothie costs 35¢ to make. How many smoothies must be sold at two for $1.50 to break even?
qs.s: Each smoothie sells for $1.50 / 2 = $0.75, yielding a margin of $0.75 - $0.35 = $0.40 per smoothie. Setting total revenue equal to total cost gives 0.40x = 1800, so x = 4500 smoothies.

qs.q: It costs $900 to start up a business selling fresh cookies at a weekend market. Each cookie costs 25¢ to make. How many cookies must be sold at two for $1.50 to break even?
qs.s: Each cookie sells for $1.50 / 2 = $0.75, giving a margin of $0.75 - $0.25 = $0.50 per cookie. Dividing the startup cost by the margin per cookie gives 900 / 0.50 = 1800 cookies.

qs.q: It costs $1950 for equipment and $450 for a vendor permit to start a food truck selling tacos. Each taco costs 50¢ for ingredients and 25¢ for packaging. How many tacos must be sold at two for $3.00 to break even?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $1950 + $450 = $2400, and variable cost per taco is $0.50 + $0.25 = $0.75. Each taco sells for $3.00 / 2 = $1.50, yielding a margin of $1.50 - $0.75 = $0.75, so 2400 / 0.75 = 3200 tacos must be sold.

qs.q: A student starts a custom screen-printing business with an initial equipment cost of $4500 and a studio deposit of $1500. Each T-shirt costs $3.25 for the blank shirt, 95¢ for ink, and 30¢ for a packaging sleeve. How many T-shirts must be sold at two for $15.00 to break even?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $4500 + $1500 = $6000, and the variable cost per shirt is $3.25 + $0.95 + $0.30 = $4.50. Each shirt sells for $15.00 / 2 = $7.50, yielding a margin of $7.50 - $4.50 = $3.00, so 6000 / 3.00 = 2000 shirts must be sold.

qs.q: To launch a gourmet popcorn stand, an entrepreneur spends $2700 on a commercial popper and $900 on an annual health permit. Each bag costs $1.20 for kernels and oil, 30¢ for the bag, and 10¢ in processing fees. How many bags must be sold at four for $10.00 to break even?
qs.s: The total fixed cost is $2700 + $900 = $3600, and the total variable cost per bag is $1.20 + $0.30 + $0.10 = $1.60. Selling at $10.00 / 4 = $2.50 per bag leaves a margin of $2.50 - $1.60 = $0.90, so 3600 / 0.90 = 4000 bags are needed to break even.

qs.q: To start a personalized phone case business, a creator buys a sublimation printer for $5400 and a heat press for $1800. Each phone case costs $1.75 for the blank case, 45¢ for ink and transfer paper, and 30¢ for a protective box. How many phone cases must be sold at two for $9.00 to break even?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $5400 + $1800 = $7200, and variable cost per case is $1.75 + $0.45 + $0.30 = $2.50. Selling at $9.00 / 2 = $4.50 gives a margin of $4.50 - $2.50 = $2.00 per case, so 7200 / 2.00 = 3600 cases are needed to break even.

qs.q: Starting an artisan jam business requires $2700 for commercial kitchen equipment and $900 for a licensing fee. Each jar of jam costs $1.00 for fruit and sugar plus 80¢ for the jar and label. How many jars must be sold at two for $6.00 to break even?
qs.s: Total fixed costs are $2700 + $900 = $3600, and production cost is $1.00 + $0.80 = $1.80 per jar. Each jar sells for $6.00 / 2 = $3.00, yielding a profit of $3.00 - $1.80 = $1.20 per jar, so 3600 / 1.20 = 3000 jars are needed to break even.

exercises.name: Find initial value or fixed cost

qs.q: It costs a factory $1320 to manufacture 300 bicycle helmets and $2720 to manufacture 800 bicycle helmets. What is the fixed cost for manufacturing the helmets?
qs.s: The variable cost per helmet is \(\frac{2720 - 1320}{800 - 300} = \frac{1400}{500} = \$2.80\). The fixed cost is \(1320 - 2.80(300) = \$480\).

qs.q: It costs a catering company $650 to cater an event for 30 guests and $1050 to cater an event for 70 guests. What is the fixed cost charged by the company?
qs.s: The variable cost per guest is \(\frac{1050 - 650}{70 - 30} = \frac{400}{40} = \$10\). The fixed cost is \(650 - 10(30) = \$350\).

qs.q: It costs a print shop $380 to print 40 custom hoodies and $620 to print 80 custom hoodies. What is the fixed setup cost for the order?
qs.s: The variable cost per hoodie is \(\frac{620 - 380}{80 - 40} = \frac{240}{40} = \$6\). The fixed setup cost is \(380 - 6(40) = \$140\).

qs.q: It costs a manufacturer $1450 to produce 200 ceramic mugs and $2350 to produce 500 ceramic mugs. What is the fixed cost for producing the mugs?
qs.s: The variable cost per mug is \(\frac{2350 - 1450}{500 - 200} = \frac{900}{300} = \$3\). The fixed cost is \(1450 - 3(200) = \$850\).

qs.q: It costs a publishing company $1850 to print 300 textbooks and $2750 to print 500 textbooks. What is the fixed cost for printing the textbooks?
qs.s: The variable cost per textbook is \(\frac{2750 - 1850}{500 - 300} = \frac{900}{200} = \$4.50\). The fixed cost is \(1850 - 4.50(300) = \$500\).

qs.q: A factory's production cost follows a linear relationship. The average cost per item is $24 when 250 items are produced, and the average cost per item drops to $18 when 500 items are produced. What is the fixed cost of production?
qs.s: Total cost is \(250 \times 24 = \$6000\) for 250 items and \(500 \times 18 = \$9000\) for 500 items. The variable cost is \(\frac{9000 - 6000}{500 - 250} = \$12\) per item, so the fixed cost is \(6000 - 12(250) = \$3000\).

qs.q: A manufacturer determines that the total cost to assemble 1200 circuit boards is $18,340, while the total cost to assemble 2500 circuit boards is $33,290. Assuming a linear relationship, what is the fixed cost for the assembly line?

An airplane descends at a constant rate toward an airport. At 6 minutes into its descent, its altitude is 21,400 feet, and at 14 minutes, its altitude is 11,800 feet. What was the airplane's initial cruising altitude before it began its descent?
qs.s: The rate of descent is \(\frac{11800 - 21400}{14 - 6} = -1200\) feet per minute. The initial cruising altitude was \(21400 - (-1200)(6) = 28,600\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A piece of industrial equipment depreciates in value at a constant linear rate. After 4 years, its value is $34,200, and after 9 years, its value is $19,700. What was the initial purchase price of the equipment?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \(\frac{19700 - 34200}{9 - 4} = -\$2900\) per year. The initial purchase price was \(34200 - (-2900)(4) = \$45,800\).

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir loses water at a constant rate during a drought. On day 8 of the drought, the reservoir holds 412,000 gallons, and on day 22, it holds 286,000 gallons. What was the initial volume of water in the reservoir on day 0?
qs.s: The rate of water loss is \(\frac{286000 - 412000}{22 - 8} = -9000\) gallons per day. The initial volume was \(412000 - (-9000)(8) = 484,000\) gallons.

qs.q: A company produces phone cases. It costs $1450 to produce 300 cases and $2200 to produce 600 cases. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of phone cases \(n\) produced.
A publisher finds that it costs $1800 to print 400 books and $2700 to print 700 books. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of books \(n\) printed.

A print shop finds that it costs $750 to print 200 custom calendars and $1350 to print 500 custom calendars. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of calendars \(n\) printed.
A catering service charges $850 to cater an event for 40 guests and $1450 for 80 guests. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of guests \(n\).

A bakery finds that it costs $320 to make 100 specialty cupcakes and $560 to make 300 specialty cupcakes. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of cupcakes \(n\) made.

A delivery vehicle depreciates linearly over time. After 3 years, the vehicle's value is $28,400, and after 7 years, its value is $17,600. Write a linear equation relating the vehicle's value \(V\) (in dollars) to its age \(t\) (in years).

A water reservoir is drained at a constant rate during maintenance. After 6 hours of draining, the reservoir holds 445,000 gallons of water, and after 14 hours, it holds 265,000 gallons. Write a linear equation relating the remaining volume \(V\) (in gallons) to the elapsed time \(t\) (in hours).

In a mountainous region, temperature decreases linearly as altitude increases. At an altitude of 1,200 meters, the temperature is \(18.4^\circ\text{C}\), and at 2,800 meters, the temperature is \(8.8^\circ\text{C}\). Write a linear equation relating the temperature \(T\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) to the altitude \(h\) (in meters).

A factory's monthly operating cost is linearly related to the number of units produced. It costs $54,600 to produce 8,000 units and $78,900 to produce 13,000 units. Write a linear equation relating the monthly operating cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of units \(n\) produced.

A manufacturer produces custom bicycle frames. The total cost to produce 350 frames is $43,750. When production is increased by 450 frames, the total cost increases to $86,500. Write a linear equation relating the total cost \(C\) (in dollars) to the number of frames \(n\) produced.
An equipment rental company charges $135 for a 3-day rental and $255 for a 7-day rental. If the cost varies linearly with the number of days, what is the total charge for a 10-day rental?
qs.s: The daily rate is m = (255 - 135)/(7 - 3) = $30, giving a base fee of 135 - 30(3) = $45. For a 10-day rental, the charge is 30(10) + 45 = $345.

qs.q: It costs a print shop $380 to print 400 brochures and $620 to print 800 brochures. Assuming a linear relationship, what is the total cost of printing 300 brochures?
qs.s: The variable cost is m = (620 - 380)/(800 - 400) = $0.60 per brochure, and the fixed cost is 380 - 0.60(400) = $140. Thus, printing 300 brochures costs 0.60(300) + 140 = $320.

qs.q: A courier service charges $42 to deliver a 10-pound package and $66 to deliver a 25-pound package. Assuming a linear relationship between the delivery charge and package weight, what is the total charge to deliver a 35-pound package?
qs.s: The rate per pound is m = (66 - 42)/(25 - 10) = $1.60, and the base fee is 42 - 1.60(10) = $26. For a 35-pound package, the total charge is 1.60(35) + 26 = $82.

qs.q: A catering service charges $540 to cater an event for 30 guests and $820 to cater an event for 50 guests. Assuming a linear relationship, what is the total cost to cater an event for 20 guests?
qs.s: The rate per guest is m = (820 - 540)/(50 - 30) = $14, giving a fixed fee of 540 - 14(30) = $120. Catering for 20 guests costs 14(20) + 120 = $400.

qs.q: A custom apparel company charges $750 to produce 50 shirts and $1350 to produce 100 shirts. Assuming the cost is linearly related to the number of shirts, what is the total cost to produce 80 shirts?
qs.s: The cost per shirt is m = (1350 - 750)/(100 - 50) = $12, and the setup cost is 750 - 12(50) = $150. Therefore, producing 80 shirts costs 12(80) + 150 = $1110.

qs.q: A manufacturing facility determines that the total production cost is linearly related to the number of components produced. It costs $24,875 to produce 1,250 components and $48,075 to produce 2,850 components. What is the total cost of producing 4,100 components?

A municipal water reservoir is drained for maintenance. After 6 hours of pumping, the reservoir holds 582,000 gallons of water, and after 14 hours, it holds 438,000 gallons. If water continues to be pumped out at the same constant rate, how many gallons of water will remain in the reservoir after 25 hours?
qs.s: The drainage rate is m = (438000 - 582000)/(14 - 6) = -18,000 gal/h, and the initial volume is 582000 - (-18000)(6) = 690,000 gallons. After 25 hours, the remaining water is 690000 - 18000(25) = 240,000 gallons.

qs.q: In the troposphere, air temperature decreases linearly as altitude increases. At an altitude of 1,200 meters, the temperature is 11.4°C, and at an altitude of 2,800 meters, the temperature is 1.8°C. What is the air temperature at an altitude of 4,500 meters?
qs.s: The lapse rate is m = (1.8 - 11.4)/(2800 - 1200) = -0.006°C/m, and the sea-level temperature is 11.4 - (-0.006)(1200) = 18.6°C. At 4,500 meters, the temperature is 18.6 - 0.006(4500) = -8.4°C.

qs.q: A scientific research probe descends into the ocean at a constant speed. At 18 minutes after tracking began, its depth is 514 meters, and at 42 minutes, its depth is 1,162 meters. Assuming depth increases linearly with time, what will the depth of the probe be at 1 hour and 15 minutes after tracking began?
qs.s: The descent rate is m = (1162 - 514)/(42 - 18) = 27 m/min, with an initial depth of 514 - 27(18) = 28 m. Since 1 hour 15 minutes is 75 minutes, the depth is 27(75) + 28 = 2,053 m.

qs.q: A catering company charges a flat setup fee plus a fixed rate per guest. An event for 75 guests costs $2,425, and an event for 140 guests costs $4,115. A client books two separate events on different dates: a workshop for 50 guests and a banquet for 80 guests. Since each event incurs the flat setup fee, what is the total cost for both events combined?
It costs a printing company $850 to produce 100 custom t-shirts and $1750 to produce 250 custom t-shirts. How many custom t-shirts can be produced for $3130?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{1750 - 850}{250 - 100} = 6\), giving the cost equation \(C = 6x + 250\). Solving \(6x + 250 = 3130\) gives \(6x = 2880\), so \(x = 480\) t-shirts.

qs.q: A publishing house finds that it costs $1950 to print 300 hardcover books and $3750 to print 700 hardcover books. How many hardcover books can be printed for $5550?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{3750 - 1950}{700 - 300} = 4.5\), yielding the cost model \(C = 4.5x + 600\). Solving \(4.5x + 600 = 5550\) gives \(4.5x = 4950\), so \(x = 1100\) books.

qs.q: A catering service charges $1140 to prepare 80 gourmet meal boxes and $2100 to prepare 200 gourmet meal boxes. How many gourmet meal boxes can be prepared for $3540?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{2100 - 1140}{200 - 80} = 8\), giving the linear relation \(C = 8x + 500\). Setting \(8x + 500 = 3540\) yields \(8x = 3040\), so \(x = 380\) meal boxes.

qs.q: A pottery studio finds that it costs $980 to craft 200 ceramic mugs and $2140 to craft 600 ceramic mugs. How many ceramic mugs can be crafted for $4344?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{2140 - 980}{600 - 200} = 2.9\), giving the cost equation \(C = 2.9x + 400\). Solving \(2.9x + 400 = 4344\) gives \(2.9x = 3944\), so \(x = 1360\) mugs.

qs.q: A manufacturer spends $1520 to produce 400 phone cases and $2645 to produce 850 phone cases. How many phone cases can be produced for $4270?
qs.s: The unit cost is \(m = \frac{2645 - 1520}{850 - 400} = 2.5\), giving the equation \(C = 2.5x + 520\). Setting \(2.5x + 520 = 4270\) gives \(2.5x = 3750\), so \(x = 1500\) phone cases.

qs.q: A freight logistics company determines that shipping 350 kg of cargo costs $1185, while shipping 800 kg costs $2400. During the peak holiday season, a 20% surcharge is applied to the total standard shipping fee. If a client is charged $4176 during the peak season, what was the weight of the cargo shipped, in kilograms?
qs.s: The standard rate is \(m = \frac{2400 - 1185}{800 - 350} = 2.7\), so standard cost is \(C = 2.7x + 240\). Removing the 20% surcharge gives a standard cost of \(4176 / 1.20 = 3480\), and solving \(2.7x + 240 = 3480\) yields \(x = 1200\) kg.

qs.q: A software firm uses a linear pricing model for its enterprise platform. A subscription for 450 user accounts costs $34,750 per year, and a subscription for 800 user accounts costs $57,500 per year. As part of a promotion, every client receives a flat rebate of $2500 deducted from their total bill. How many user accounts are included in an enterprise subscription if the final discounted bill is $95,300?
qs.s: The rate per user is \(m = \frac{57500 - 34750}{800 - 450} = 65\), giving a pre-discount equation of \(S = 65x + 5500\). Accounting for the $2500 rebate gives total bill \(D = 65x + 3000\), and solving \(65x + 3000 = 95300\) yields \(x = 1420\) user accounts.

qs.q: An extended dental plan reimburses expenses according to a linear model after a fixed annual deductible. A policyholder with $650 in dental expenses receives a reimbursement of $365, while a policyholder with $1400 in expenses receives a reimbursement of $890. What were the total dental expenses, in dollars, of a policyholder who received a reimbursement of $1520?
qs.s: The reimbursement rate is \(m = \frac{890 - 365}{1400 - 650} = 0.70\), giving the model \(R = 0.70x - 90\). Setting \(0.70x - 90 = 1520\) gives \(0.70x = 1610\), resulting in \(x = 2300\) dollars in expenses.

qs.q: A solar technology company determines that producing 2400 solar panels costs $186,000, and producing 5600 solar panels costs $378,000. In addition to the linear production cost, the company charges a flat delivery fee of $4500 per order. How many solar panels can be manufactured and delivered for a total cost of $537,000?
qs.s: The production rate is \(m = \frac{378000 - 186000}{5600 - 2400} = 60\), giving base cost \(C = 60x + 42000\). Adding the $4500 delivery fee gives \(T = 60x + 46500\); solving \(60x + 46500 = 537000\) yields \(x = 8175\) panels.

qs.q: An electronics plant finds that producing 1250 circuit boards costs $16,875, while producing 3750 circuit boards costs $43,125. A tech firm has an overall procurement budget of $80,000, but must reserve 10% of this budget for shipping and taxes, allocating the remaining funds entirely to production. How many circuit boards can be produced within this allocated budget?
qs.s: The unit cost is \(m = \frac{43125 - 16875}{3750 - 1250} = 10.5\), which gives \(C = 10.5x + 3750\). Allocating 90% of the $80,000 leaves $72,000 for production, and solving \(10.5x + 3750 = 72000\) gives \(x = 6500\) boards.

qs.q: A custom t-shirt shop charges $31.00 for an order of 2 shirts and $55.00 for an order of 5 shirts. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(n\) be the number of shirts. Find the cost equation.
qs.s: The rate per shirt is \(m = \frac{55 - 31}{5 - 2} = 8\). Using \((2, 31)\), the fixed setup fee is \(b = 31 - 8(2) = 15\), resulting in \(C = 8n + 15\).

qs.q: Shipping a crate by bus parcel express costs $45.60 for a 2-kilogram package and $67.20 for a 5-kilogram package. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(w\) be the weight in kilograms. Find the cost equation.
A local courier charges $14.50 to deliver a 2-pound parcel and $21.50 to deliver a 4-pound parcel. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(w\) be the weight in pounds. Find the cost equation.
Renting a utility trailer costs $38.50 for 1 day and $62.50 for 3 days. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(t\) be the rental time in days. Find the cost equation.
A taxi company charges $11.20 for a 3-mile ride and $16.60 for a 6-mile ride. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(d\) be the distance in miles. Find the cost equation.

An air freight carrier charges $73.40 to ship a 4.5-kilogram package and $118.60 to ship an 8.5-kilogram package. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(w\) be the weight in kilograms. Find the cost equation.

An electric utility company charges a customer $69.50 in a month when 450 kilowatt-hours (kWh) are used, and $111.50 in a month when 800 kWh are used. Let \(C\) be the monthly cost in dollars and \(k\) be the electricity used in kilowatt-hours. Find the cost equation.

A catering company charges $1525 to cater an event for 60 guests and $2845 to cater an event for 140 guests. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(n\) be the number of guests. Find the cost equation.

A publishing house determines that it costs $3420 to print and bind 400 books, and $5660 to print and bind 750 books. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(x\) be the number of books printed. Find the cost equation.
qs.s: The variable cost per book is \(m = \frac{5660 - 3420}{750 - 400} = \frac{2240}{350} = 6.40\). Using \((400, 3420)\), the fixed setup cost is \(b = 3420 - 6.40(400) = 860\), resulting in \(C = 6.40x + 860\).

qs.q: A trucking company charges $184.25 to haul 3.5 tonnes of gravel and $278.75 to haul 6.5 tonnes of gravel. Let \(C\) be the total cost in dollars and \(t\) be the weight in tonnes. Find the cost equation.
To rent a floor sander, an equipment rental shop charges $29.80 for 2 hours and $46.60 for 5 hours. Assuming the relationship is linear, find the cost to rent the sander for 7.5 hours.
A taxi service charges $14.20 for a 3-mile trip and $22.60 for a 7-mile trip. Assuming the cost is linearly related to the distance, find the cost of a 12.5-mile trip.

A dry cleaner charges $31.20 to clean 2 kilograms of garments and $37.60 to clean 6 kilograms. Assuming a linear relationship between cost and weight, find the cost to clean 8.5 kilograms of garments.

A plumbing service charges $65.00 for a 1.5-hour visit and $102.50 for a 4-hour visit. Assuming a linear relationship between the cost and the duration of the visit, find the cost of a 6.5-hour visit.
qs.s: The hourly rate is \(m = \frac{102.50 - 65.00}{4 - 1.5} = 15.00\) dollars per hour, and the base fee is \(b = 65.00 - 15(1.5) = 42.50\). For a 6.5-hour visit, the cost is \(15(6.5) + 42.50 = \$140.00\).

qs.q: A mobile phone provider charges $24.50 for 2 gigabytes of data and $39.50 for 5 gigabytes of data. Assuming a linear relationship, find the cost for 7.5 gigabytes of data.
qs.s: The rate per gigabyte is \(m = \frac{39.50 - 24.50}{5 - 2} = 5.00\), and the base fee is \(b = 24.50 - 5.00(2) = 14.50\). For 7.5 gigabytes, the cost is \(5.00(7.5) + 14.50 = \$52.00\).

qs.q: A publishing company determines that the cost to produce 150 copies of a book is $2,850, while the cost for 400 copies is $5,600. The company prices orders by adding an 8% markup to the total production cost. What will a customer be charged for an order of 650 copies?
qs.s: The variable cost per book is \(m = \frac{5600 - 2850}{400 - 150} = 11\) and the setup cost is \(b = 2850 - 11(150) = 1200\), so producing 650 copies costs \(11(650) + 1200 = \$8,350\). With the 8% markup, the customer is charged \(8350 \times 1.08 = \$9,018\).

qs.q: A commercial delivery van was purchased new and depreciates linearly over time. After 2.5 years of service, the van is valued at $28,900, and after 6.0 years, it is valued at $16,300. What will the value of the van be after 8.5 years of service?
qs.s: The annual depreciation rate is \(m = \frac{16300 - 28900}{6.0 - 2.5} = -3600\), and the initial purchase value is \(b = 28900 - (-3600)(2.5) = 37900\). After 8.5 years, the value is \(-3600(8.5) + 37900 = \$7,300\).

qs.q: At an elevation of 1,200 meters above sea level, the boiling point of water is \(96.0^\circ\text{C}\), and at 2,700 meters, it is \(91.5^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming a linear relationship between elevation and boiling point, find the boiling point of water at an elevation of 4,800 meters.
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{91.5 - 96.0}{2700 - 1200} = -0.003^\circ\text{C/m}\), and the sea-level boiling point is \(b = 96.0 - (-0.003)(1200) = 99.6^\circ\text{C}\). At 4,800 meters, the boiling point is \(-0.003(4800) + 99.6 = 85.2^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: An aircraft's fuel tank contains 14,200 liters of fuel after flying for 1.5 hours, and 9,700 liters after flying for 4.0 hours. Assuming fuel is consumed at a constant rate, how many liters of fuel remain in the tank after flying for 6.5 hours?
qs.s: The rate of fuel consumption is \(m = \frac{9700 - 14200}{4.0 - 1.5} = -1800\text{ L/h}\), and the initial fuel was \(b = 14200 - (-1800)(1.5) = 16900\text{ L}\). After 6.5 hours, the remaining fuel is \(-1800(6.5) + 16900 = 5,200\text{ L}\).

qs.q: An employer's health insurance plan reimburses prescription drug costs according to a linear model. For an annual prescription total of $500, the plan reimburses $260, and for a total of $1,200, the plan reimburses $820. How much will an employee have to pay out of pocket if their annual prescription total is $2,150?
qs.s: The reimbursement model is \(R = 0.80C - 140\), which for \(C = \$2,150\) yields a reimbursement of \(0.80(2150) - 140 = \$1,580\). The employee's out-of-pocket cost is therefore \(2150 - 1580 = \$570\).

qs.q: A taxi company charges $14.50 for a 3-mile trip and $26.50 for a 7-mile trip. Assuming the fare has a linear relationship with the distance, how many miles did a passenger travel if the fare was $38.50?

A custom printing shop charges $38.00 for an order of 4 custom mugs and $74.00 for an order of 10 custom mugs. If the cost is linearly related to the number of mugs, how many mugs were ordered if the total bill was $110.00?
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{74 - 38}{10 - 4} = 6\), giving the cost equation \(y = 6x + 14\). Solving \(6x + 14 = 110\) gives \(6x = 96\), so \(x = 16\text{ mugs}\).

qs.q: A catering service charges $155.00 for a dinner of 10 guests and $275.00 for 20 guests. Assuming the cost has a linear relationship with the number of guests, how many guests were served if the total charge was $335.00?
qs.s: The rate per guest is \(m = \frac{275 - 155}{20 - 10} = 12\), which gives the equation \(y = 12x + 35\). Setting \(12x + 35 = 335\) gives \(12x = 300\), so \(x = 25\text{ guests}\).

qs.q: A car rental agency charges $34.00 to rent a car and drive 20 km, and $46.00 to drive 50 km. Assuming a linear relationship between the cost and distance, how many kilometres was the car driven if the total cost was $58.00?
qs.s: The rate per kilometre is \(m = \frac{46.00 - 34.00}{50 - 20} = 0.40\), giving the cost equation \(y = 0.40x + 26.00\). Solving \(0.40x + 26.00 = 58.00\) yields \(0.40x = 32.00\), so \(x = 80\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A courier charges $11.00 to ship a 1-pound package and $21.50 to ship a 4-pound package. If the shipping cost is linearly related to the weight, how much does a package weigh if it costs $26.75 to ship?
qs.s: The rate per pound is \(m = \frac{21.50 - 11.00}{4 - 1} = 3.50\), so the cost equation is \(y = 3.50x + 7.50\). Setting \(3.50x + 7.50 = 26.75\) gives \(3.50x = 19.25\), so \(x = 5.5\text{ pounds}\).

qs.q: At an elevation of 500 metres, the air temperature is \(18.0^\circ\text{C}\). At an elevation of 2500 metres, the air temperature is \(6.0^\circ\text{C}\). Assuming a linear relationship between temperature and elevation, at what elevation is the air temperature \(-3.0^\circ\text{C}\)?
qs.s: The rate of change is \(m = \frac{6.0 - 18.0}{2500 - 500} = -0.006^\circ\text{C}/\text{m}\), yielding the formula \(T = -0.006x + 21\). Setting \(-0.006x + 21 = -3.0\) gives \(-0.006x = -24\), so \(x = 4000\text{ metres}\).

qs.q: A municipal water reservoir is being drained at a constant rate. After 4 hours of draining, the reservoir contains 198,000 litres of water. After 9 hours, it contains 153,000 litres. Assuming the water volume decreases linearly over time, after how many total hours will the reservoir contain 81,000 litres?

A publisher determines that printing 800 copies of a textbook costs $13,500, while printing 2400 copies costs $33,500. Assuming the production cost is linearly related to the number of copies printed, how many copies can be printed with a budget of $48,500?
qs.s: The marginal cost per copy is \(m = \frac{33,500 - 13,500}{2400 - 800} = 12.50\), so the cost function is \(C = 12.50x + 3500\). Solving \(12.50x + 3500 = 48,500\) gives \(12.50x = 45,000\), so \(x = 3600\text{ copies}\).

qs.q: A freight company charges $170.25 to transport a 40-kg crate and $332.75 to transport a 90-kg crate. If the shipping cost is linearly related to the mass, what is the mass of a crate that costs $449.75 to transport?

A sales representative earns a monthly base salary plus a commission that is a fixed percentage of sales. In March, her total earnings were $3,700 on $30,000 in sales, and in April, her earnings were $4,900 on $50,000 in sales. If her earnings are a linear function of her sales, what dollar amount of sales did she generate in May when her earnings reached $6,400?
qs.s: The commission rate is \(m = \frac{4900 - 3700}{50,000 - 30,000} = 0.06\), which gives the earnings equation \(E = 0.06S + 1900\). Setting \(0.06S + 1900 = 6400\) gives \(0.06S = 4500\), so \(S = \$75,000\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(f(x) = -2x + 1\):

| \(x\) | \(-2x + 1\) | \(f(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| | | \(-4m + 3\) | ? |

What is the ordered pair \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Set \(-2x + 1 = -4m + 3\), which gives \(-2x = -4m + 2\), so \(x = 2m - 1\). The corresponding ordered pair is \((2m - 1, -4m + 3)\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(g(x) = -4x + 7\):

| \(x\) | \(-4x + 7\) | \(g(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| \(3k\) | | ? | |

What is the simplified expression for \(g(3k)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3k\) into the function rule to obtain \(g(3k) = -4(3k) + 7 = -12k + 7\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(p(x) = 2x - 3\):

| \(x\) | \(2x - 3\) | \(p(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ? | | \(2c + 5\) | |

What is the input \(x\) in terms of \(c\)?
qs.s: Set \(2x - 3 = 2c + 5\). Add \(3\) to both sides to get \(2x = 2c + 8\), then divide by \(2\) to find \(x = c + 4\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(h(x) = 3x - 5\):

| \(x\) | \(3x - 5\) | \(h(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| \(a + 4\) | | ? | |

What is the simplified expression for \(h(a + 4)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = a + 4\) and distribute: \(h(a + 4) = 3(a + 4) - 5 = 3a + 12 - 5 = 3a + 7\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(f(x) = -3x + 4\):

| \(x\) | \(-3x + 4\) | \(f(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| \(-5\) | | | ? |

What is the ordered pair \((x, y)\) when \(x = -5\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -5\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(-5) = -3(-5) + 4 = 15 + 4 = 19\). Therefore, the ordered pair is \((-5, 19)\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(g(x) = -\frac{4}{3}x + 7\):

| \(x\) | \(-\frac{4}{3}x + 7\) | \(g(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| \(\frac{3}{2}c - 6\) | | | ? |

What is the ordered pair \((x, y)\) when \(x = \frac{3}{2}c - 6\)?
qs.s: Calculate \(g\left(\frac{3}{2}c - 6\right) = -\frac{4}{3}\left(\frac{3}{2}c - 6\right) + 7 = -2c + 8 + 7 = -2c + 15\), giving the ordered pair \(\left(\frac{3}{2}c - 6, -2c + 15\right)\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(f(x) = -5x + 18\):

| \(x\) | \(-5x + 18\) | \(f(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| | | \(-15c + 43\) | ? |

What is the ordered pair \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Solve \(-5x + 18 = -15c + 43\) by subtracting \(18\) to get \(-5x = -15c + 25\), then divide by \(-5\) to get \(x = 3c - 5\). The ordered pair is \((3c - 5, -15c + 43)\).

qs.q:
A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{5}x + 4\):

| \(x\) | \(-\frac{3}{5}x + 4\) | \(f(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| \(10a - 15\) | | ? | |

What is the simplified expression for \(f(10a - 15)\)?

A table of values is being completed for the linear function \(h(x) = \frac{3}{4}x - 6\):

| \(x\) | \(\frac{3}{4}x - 6\) | \(h(x)\) | \((x, y)\) |
| :---: | :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ? | | \(\frac{1}{2}k + 3\) | |

What is the input \(x\) in terms of \(k\)?
qs.s: Set \(\frac{3}{4}x - 6 = \frac{1}{2}k + 3\), which simplifies to \(\frac{3}{4}x = \frac{1}{2}k + 9\). Multiply both sides by \(\frac{4}{3}\) to obtain \(x = \frac{2}{3}k + 12\).
Substitute \(x = 6\) into the function: \(g(6) = 3(6) - 5 = 18 - 5 = 13\).
Substitute \(x = 4\) into the function: \(h(4) = 5(4) - 8 = 20 - 8 = 12\).
Substitute \(x = 2\) into the function: \(f(2) = 4(2) + 1 = 8 + 1 = 9\).
Substitute \(x = 5\) into the function: \(C(5) = 7(5) - 4 = 35 - 4 = 31\).
Substitute \(x = 3\) into the function: \(f(3) = 6(3) + 3 = 18 + 3 = 21\).
Substitute \(x = -8\) into the function: \(f(-8) = -14(-8) + 65 = 112 + 65 = 177\).

qs.q: For \(g(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{6}\), find \(g\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -\frac{2}{5}\) into the function: \(g\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) = -\frac{3}{4}\left(-\frac{2}{5}\right) + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{3}{10} + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{9}{30} + \frac{25}{30} = \frac{17}{15}\).
Simplify the expression to \(h(x) = 12 - 8x - 15x + 21 = -23x + 33\), then evaluate: \(h(-2) = -23(-2) + 33 = 46 + 33 = 79\).
Substitute \(x = -2\) into the function: \(h(-2) = 5(-2) - 8 = -10 - 8 = -18\).
Substitute \(x = -4\) into the function: \(p(-4) = 2(-4) - 11 = -8 - 11 = -19\).
Substitute \(x = -6\) into the function: \(g(-6) = -2(-6) - 9 = 12 - 9 = 3\).
Substitute \(x = -3\) into the function: \(f(-3) = 4(-3) + 7 = -12 + 7 = -5\).
Substitute \(x = -5\) into the function: \(r(-5) = -3(-5) + 4 = 15 + 4 = 19\).

qs.q: For \(h(x) = -\frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{6}\), find \(h\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\) into the function: \(h\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{3}{4}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{1}{2} + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{4}{3}\).
Substitute \(x = -7\) into the function: \(k(-7) = \frac{5(-7) - 13}{6} = \frac{-35 - 13}{6} = \frac{-48}{6} = -8\).
Replace the variable \(n\) with \(c\) in \(P(n) = 8n + 11\) to get \(P(c) = 8c + 11\).
Replace \(x\) with \(w\) in \(f(x) = -6x - 1\), yielding \(f(w) = -6w - 1\).

qs.q: For \(h(t) = 5t - 3\), find \(h(p)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(p\) in place of \(t\) in \(h(t) = 5t - 3\) to obtain \(h(p) = 5p - 3\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x + 7\), find \(f(a)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a\) in place of \(x\) in \(f(x) = 4x + 7\) to get \(f(a) = 4a + 7\).

qs.q: For \(h(x) = 8 - 3x\), find and simplify \(h(5 - 2m)\).
For \(f(x) = -5x + 6\), find and simplify \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \((x + h)\) for \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = -5(x + h) + 6 = -5x - 5h + 6\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5x - 8\), find and simplify \(f(3k + 4)\).
For \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x - 5\), find and simplify \(f(6w + 12)\).
For \(g(x) = -4x + 9\), find and simplify \(g(2a - 5)\).

qs.s: Substitute \(2x - 3\) into \(h(x)\) to get \(h(2x - 3) = 5(2x - 3) - 4\). Expanding and simplifying gives \(10x - 15 - 4 = 10x - 19\).
Substitute \(3x - 2\) for \(x\) to get \(f(3x - 2) = 4(3x - 2) + 1\). Distribute the 4 and combine like terms: \(12x - 8 + 1 = 12x - 7\).
Substitute \(5x - 2\) for \(x\) to get \(f(5x - 2) = 3(5x - 2) + 4\). Multiply through to get \(15x - 6 + 4 = 15x - 2\).
Substitute \(4x + 3\) into the function to obtain \(g(4x + 3) = 2(4x + 3) - 5\). Distributing the 2 gives \(8x + 6 - 5 = 8x + 1\).
Substitute \(3x + 4\) into \(p(x)\) to get \(p(3x + 4) = 2(3x + 4) - 7\). Distribute the 2 and simplify: \(6x + 8 - 7 = 6x + 1\).
Substitute \(4x - 9\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(4x - 9) = -7(4x - 9) + 15\). Distribute \(-7\) to get \(-28x + 63 + 15 = -28x + 78\).
Substitute \(8x - 16\) into \(h(x)\) to get \(h(8x - 16) = -\frac{3}{4}(8x - 16) + 5\). Distributing \(-\frac{3}{4}\) yields \(-6x + 12 + 5 = -6x + 17\).
Substitute the trinomial into \(f(x)\) to get \(4(2x^2 - 5x + 3) - 9\). Distribute 4 across the trinomial and combine constant terms: \(8x^2 - 20x + 12 - 9 = 8x^2 - 20x + 3\).
Substitute the expression into \(k(x)\) to get \(-3(3x^2 - 4x - 5) + 8\). Distribute \(-3\) to get \(-9x^2 + 12x + 15 + 8 = -9x^2 + 12x + 23\).
Substitute \(3 - 4x\) into \(g(x)\) to get \(g(3 - 4x) = 6 - 5(3 - 4x)\). Distribute \(-5\) to get \(6 - 15 + 20x = 20x - 9\).

qs.q: For \(g(x) = 2x - 7\), find \(g(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) into the function to obtain \(g(x + h) = 2(x + h) - 7\). Expanding gives \(2x + 2h - 7\).

qs.q: For \(P(x) = 5x - 1\), find \(P(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) for \(x\) to get \(P(x + h) = 5(x + h) - 1\). Expanding the brackets yields \(5x + 5h - 1\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x + 5\), find \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) for \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = 4(x + h) + 5\). Distributing the \(4\) gives \(4x + 4h + 5\).
Substitute \(x + h\) for \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = -3(x + h) + 8\). Distributing \(-3\) yields \(-3x - 3h + 8\).
Replace \(x\) with \(x + h\) to obtain \(f(x + h) = -6(x + h) - 4\). Distributing \(-6\) gives \(-6x - 6h - 4\).
Substitute \(8x - 4h + 12\) into \(g(x)\) to get \(-\frac{3}{4}(8x - 4h + 12) + 2\). Distributing \(-\frac{3}{4}\) gives \(-6x + 3h - 9 + 2\), which simplifies to \(-6x + 3h - 7\).
Substitute \(3x + 5h - 4\) for \(x\) to get \(15 - 2(3x + 5h - 4)\). Distributing \(-2\) gives \(15 - 6x - 10h + 8\), which simplifies to \(-6x - 10h + 23\).
Substitute \(9x + 6h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(9x + 6h) = \frac{2}{3}(9x + 6h) - 5\). Distributing \(\frac{2}{3}\) yields \(6x + 4h - 5\).
Substitute \(4x + 3\) into the function to get \(f(4x + 3) = 6(4x + 3) - 7\). Distribute the \(6\) to get \(24x + 18 - 7\), which simplifies to \(24x + 11\).
Substitute \(3x - 2h\) into \(g(x)\) to get \(g(3x - 2h) = -4(3x - 2h) + 9\). Distributing \(-4\) gives \(-12x + 8h + 9\).
Evaluate to find \(f(x) = -6x - 5\) and \(f(h) = -6h - 5\). Adding the two expressions gives \(f(x) + f(h) = (-6x - 5) + (-6h - 5) = -6x - 6h - 10\).
Evaluate at \(x\) and \(h\) to get \(f(x) = -2x + 9\) and \(f(h) = -2h + 9\). Adding them gives \(f(x) + f(h) = (-2x + 9) + (-2h + 9) = -2x - 2h + 18\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5x - 6\), find \(f(x) + f(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute to find \(f(x) = 5x - 6\) and \(f(h) = 5h - 6\). Adding them yields \(f(x) + f(h) = (5x - 6) + (5h - 6) = 5x + 5h - 12\).

qs.q: For \(g(x) = 7x - 3\), find \(g(x) + g(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x\) and \(h\) into \(g(x)\) to obtain \(g(x) = 7x - 3\) and \(g(h) = 7h - 3\). Adding these together yields \((7x - 3) + (7h - 3) = 7x + 7h - 6\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x + 7\), find \(f(x) + f(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x\) and \(h\) into the function to get \(f(x) = 4x + 7\) and \(f(h) = 4h + 7\). Adding these gives \(f(x) + f(h) = (4x + 7) + (4h + 7) = 4x + 4h + 14\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x - 7\), find \(f(x + h) + f(x - h)\).
qs.s: Evaluate \(f(x + h) = 4(x + h) - 7 = 4x + 4h - 7\) and \(f(x - h) = 4(x - h) - 7 = 4x - 4h - 7\). Summing them yields \((4x + 4h - 7) + (4x - 4h - 7) = 8x - 14\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -5x + 8\), find \(\frac{f(x + h) - f(x)}{h}\), where \(h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) to get \(f(x+h) = -5(x+h) + 8 = -5x - 5h + 8\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(-5x - 5h + 8) - (-5x + 8)}{h} = \frac{-5h}{h} = -5\).
Multiply \(f(x) = 5x - 4\) by 3 to get \(15x - 12\), and multiply \(f(h) = 5h - 4\) by 2 to get \(10h - 8\). Subtracting gives \((15x - 12) - (10h - 8) = 15x - 10h - 4\).
Substitute \(x = 5\) into the function: \(f(5) = 2(5) + 9 = 10 + 9 = 19\).
Substitute \(x = 3\) into the function: \(f(3) = 6(3) - 11 = 18 - 11 = 7\).
Substitute \(x = 2\) into the function: \(f(2) = 5(2) + 6 = 10 + 6 = 16\).
Substitute \(x = 4\) into the function: \(f(4) = 3(4) - 7 = 12 - 7 = 5\).
Substitute \(x = 4\) into the function: \(f(4) = 7(4) + 2 = 28 + 2 = 30\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{3}{5}x - \frac{7}{10}\), find \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -\frac{1}{2}\): \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{3}{5}\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) - \frac{7}{10} = -\frac{3}{10} - \frac{7}{10} = -\frac{10}{10} = -1\).
Substitute \(x = -12\) into the function: \(f(-12) = -8(-12) + 37 = 96 + 37 = 133\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 3x - 7\), find \(f(a)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(a\) for \(x\) in the function rule to obtain \(f(a) = 3a - 7\).

qs.q: For \(h(x) = 5 - 6x\), find \(h(t)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t\) into the function in place of \(x\) to get \(h(t) = 5 - 6t\).
Substitute \(w\) for \(x\) into \(p(x) = -x - 11\) to obtain \(p(w) = -w - 11\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 8x + 3\), find \(f(c)\).
qs.s: Evaluate the function at \(x = c\) to get \(f(c) = 8c + 3\).
Evaluate both expressions: \(f(4x - 1) = 3(4x - 1) + 2 = 12x - 1\) and \(f(2x + 5) = 3(2x + 5) + 2 = 6x + 17\). Subtracting yields \((12x - 1) - (6x + 17) = 6x - 18\).
Substitute \(6x - 9\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(\frac{2}{3}(6x - 9) - 5 = 4x - 6 - 5 = 4x - 11\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 3x + 7\), find \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) in place of \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = 3(x + h) + 7\). Distribute the 3 to obtain \(3x + 3h + 7\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5x - 2\), find \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) in place of \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = 5(x + h) - 2\). Distribute the 5 to obtain \(5x + 5h - 2\).

qs.q: For \(g(x) = 2x + 9\), find \(g(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) into the function to get \(g(x + h) = 2(x + h) + 9\). Distribute the 2 to obtain \(2x + 2h + 9\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 8x + 3\), find \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) in place of \(x\) to get \(f(x + h) = 8(x + h) + 3\). Distribute the 8 to obtain \(8x + 8h + 3\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 6x - 7\), find \(f(x + h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) into the function to get \(f(x + h) = 6(x + h) - 7\). Distribute the 6 to obtain \(6x + 6h - 7\).
Substitute \(4x - 5\) into the function to get \(f(4x - 5) = -3(4x - 5) + 4 = -12x + 15 + 4\). Combine constant terms to obtain \(-12x + 19\).
Substitute \(2x + 3\) into the function to get \(f(2x + 3) = 5(2x + 3) - 7 = 10x + 15 - 7\). Combine like terms to arrive at \(10x + 8\).
Substitute \(x - 2h\) into the function to get \(f(x - 2h) = -5(x - 2h) + 8\). Distribute the \(-5\) to obtain \(-5x + 10h + 8\).
Substitute \(2x - 3h + 5\) into the function to get \(f(2x - 3h + 5) = -4(2x - 3h + 5) + 11 = -8x + 12h - 20 + 11\). Combine constant terms to obtain \(-8x + 12h - 9\).
Substitute \(h\) into the function to obtain \(f(h) = -2h + 7\). Combining \(f(x)\) and \(f(h)\) gives \((-2x + 7) + (-2h + 7) = -2x - 2h + 14\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 3x + 8\), find \(f(x) + f(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(h\) into the function to obtain \(f(h) = 3h + 8\). Adding \(f(x)\) and \(f(h)\) gives \((3x + 8) + (3h + 8) = 3x + 3h + 16\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5x - 9\), find \(f(x) + f(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(h\) into the function to find \(f(h) = 5h - 9\). Then \(f(x) + f(h) = (5x - 9) + (5h - 9) = 5x + 5h - 18\).
Substitute \(h\) into the function to find \(f(h) = -4h - 3\). Adding \(f(x)\) and \(f(h)\) yields \((-4x - 3) + (-4h - 3) = -4x - 4h - 6\).
Evaluate \(2f(x + h) = 2[3(x + h) - 5] = 6x + 6h - 10\). Subtracting \(f(x)\) yields \((6x + 6h - 10) - (3x - 5) = 3x + 6h - 5\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{5}{8}\), find \(f(x) + f(h)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(h\) into the function to obtain \(f(h) = \frac{2}{3}h + \frac{5}{8}\). Adding \(f(x) + f(h)\) gives \(\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{2}{3}h + \frac{10}{8}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{2}{3}h + \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 7x + 4\), find \(f(x + h) + f(x)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x + h\) into the function to get \(f(x + h) = 7(x + h) + 4 = 7x + 7h + 4\). Adding \(f(x)\) gives \((7x + 7h + 4) + (7x + 4) = 14x + 7h + 8\).

qs.s: Set \(7x - 4 = -18\), add \(4\) to both sides to get \(7x = -14\), and divide by \(7\) to find \(x = -2\).

Set \(-2x - 9 = 3\), add \(9\) to both sides to get \(-2x = 12\), and divide by \(-2\) to obtain \(x = -6\).
Set \(6x + 11 = -1\), subtract \(11\) from both sides to get \(6x = -12\), and divide by \(6\) to find \(x = -2\).
Simplify the expression to \(f(x) = 2x - 15\). Setting \(2x - 15 = 9\) gives \(2x = 24\), which simplifies to \(x = 12\).
Distribute and simplify to get \(f(x) = 6x - 3\). Setting \(6x - 3 = -15\) gives \(6x = -12\), so \(x = -2\).

Set \(\frac{4 - 3x}{5} = -7\) and multiply by \(5\) to get \(4 - 3x = -35\). Subtract \(4\) to obtain \(-3x = -39\), then divide by \(-3\) to get \(x = 13\).
Set \(-15x + 340 = 85\) and subtract \(340\) to get \(-15x = -255\). Dividing both sides by \(-15\) yields \(x = 17\).
Substitute \(-1\) for \(g(x)\) to get \(-1 = -3x + 8\). Subtracting \(8\) from both sides gives \(-9 = -3x\), which yields \(x = 3\).
Set \(-2x - 9 = 5\) and add \(9\) to both sides to get \(-2x = 14\). Dividing both sides by \(-2\) yields \(x = -7\).
Set \(6x + 7 = -17\) and subtract \(7\) from both sides to obtain \(6x = -24\). Dividing both sides by \(6\) gives \(x = -4\).
Substitute \(11\) for \(f(x)\) to get \(11 = 4x - 5\). Adding \(5\) to both sides gives \(16 = 4x\), so \(x = 4\).

Set \(\frac{5x + 4}{3} = -12\) and multiply both sides by \(3\) to get \(5x + 4 = -36\). Subtracting \(4\) gives \(5x = -40\), so \(x = -8\).
Expand and simplify \(g(x) = 8x - 12 - 5x = 3x - 12\). Setting \(3x - 12 = 21\) gives \(3x = 33\), so \(x = 11\).
Set \(\frac{2}{3}x - 7 = 9\) and add \(7\) to both sides to get \(\frac{2}{3}x = 16\). Multiplying both sides by \(\frac{3}{2}\) yields \(x = 24\).
Distribute and simplify to get \(f(x) = 7 - 12 + 3x = 3x - 5\). Setting \(3x - 5 = 22\) gives \(3x = 27\), so \(x = 9\).
Set the function equal to \(23\): \(-4x + 3 = 23\). Subtract \(3\) to get \(-4x = 20\), then divide by \(-4\) to find \(x = -5\).
Set the function equal to \(5\): \(2x + 13 = 5\). Subtract \(13\) to get \(2x = -8\), then divide by \(2\) to find \(x = -4\).

Set \(-18x + 145 = -485\) and subtract \(145\) from both sides to get \(-18x = -630\). Divide by \(-18\) to obtain \(x = 35\).
Set \(\frac{2}{5}x - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{7}{4}\) and add \(\frac{3}{4}\) to both sides to get \(\frac{2}{5}x = \frac{10}{4} = \frac{5}{2}\). Multiply by \(\frac{5}{2}\) to find \(x = \frac{25}{4}\).
Distribute and simplify to get \(f(x) = 6x - 9 + 5 = 6x - 4\). Setting \(6x - 4 = -28\) gives \(6x = -24\), so \(x = -4\).
Expand and simplify to get \(f(x) = 6x - 15 - 4x + 1 = 2x - 14\). Setting \(2x - 14 = 16\) gives \(2x = 30\), so \(x = 15\).
Combine like terms to write \(f(x) = -4x + 7.8\). Setting \(-4x + 7.8 = -18.2\) gives \(-4x = -26\), so \(x = 6.5\).
Set \(-2x - 5 = 4\), add 5 to get \(-2x = 9\), then divide by \(-2\) to find \(x = -\frac{9}{2}\).
Set \(-3x + 7 = -2\), subtract 7 to get \(-3x = -9\), then divide by \(-3\) to get \(x = 3\).
Set \(5x - 8 = 7\), add 8 to get \(5x = 15\), then divide by 5 to find \(x = 3\).

Expand and simplify \(f(x)\) to \(5 - 6x + 8 - 4x = -10x + 13\), then solve \(-10x + 13 = -17\) to get \(-10x = -30\), so \(x = 3\).
