exercises.name: Determine linear function from two values

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(0) = -6\) and \(f(4) = 2\).
qs.s: Since \(f(0) = -6\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(b = -6\). The slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-6)}{4 - 0} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\), so the function is \(f(x) = 2x - 6\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(0) = 4\) and \(f(2) = -2\).
qs.s: Since \(f(0) = 4\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(b = 4\). The slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - 4}{2 - 0} = -3\), so the function is \(f(x) = -3x + 4\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(0) = 7\) and \(f(-2) = -1\).
qs.s: Since \(f(0) = 7\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(b = 7\). The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 7}{-2 - 0} = \frac{-8}{-2} = 4\), so the function is \(f(x) = 4x + 7\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(0) = -1\) and \(f(3) = 8\).
qs.s: Since \(f(0) = -1\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(b = -1\). The slope is \(m = \frac{8 - (-1)}{3 - 0} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\), so the function is \(f(x) = 3x - 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(0) = 1\) and \(f(-5) = 16\).
qs.s: Since \(f(0) = 1\), the \(y\)-intercept is \(b = 1\). The slope is \(m = \frac{16 - 1}{-5 - 0} = \frac{15}{-5} = -3\), so the function is \(f(x) = -3x + 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(2) = -7\) and \(f(-3) = 13\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{13 - (-7)}{-3 - 2} = \frac{20}{-5} = -4\). Substituting \((2, -7)\) into \(f(x) = -4x + b\) yields \(-7 = -4(2) + b\), which gives \(b = 1\), so \(f(x) = -4x + 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-5) = -38\) and \(f(7) = 46\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{46 - (-38)}{7 - (-5)} = \frac{84}{12} = 7\). Substituting \((7, 46)\) into \(f(x) = 7x + b\) yields \(46 = 49 + b\), so \(b = -3\), giving \(f(x) = 7x - 3\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-4) = 29\) and \(f(6) = -41\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(1) = 2\) and \(f(4) = 3\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{3 - 2}{4 - 1} = \frac{1}{3}\). Substituting \((1, 2)\) into \(f(x) = \frac{1}{3}x + b\) yields \(2 = \frac{1}{3}(1) + b\), so \(b = \frac{5}{3}\), giving \(f(x) = \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(4) = -1\) and \(f(-2) = 8\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{8 - (-1)}{-2 - 4} = \frac{9}{-6} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Substituting \((4, -1)\) into \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + b\) yields \(-1 = -6 + b\), so \(b = 5\), giving \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + 5\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = -7\) and \(f(3) = 8\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = 1\) and \(f(2) = 9\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{9 - 1}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\). Substituting \((2, 9)\) gives \(9 = 2(2) + b\), so \(b = 5\), giving \(f(x) = 2x + 5\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-3) = 10\) and \(f(1) = -2\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(1) = 2\) and \(f(5) = 5\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{5 - 2}{5 - 1} = \frac{3}{4}\). Substituting \((1, 2)\) into \(f(x) = \frac{3}{4}x + b\) gives \(2 = \frac{3}{4}(1) + b\), so \(b = \frac{5}{4}\), resulting in \(f(x) = \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(1) = 5\) and \(f(4) = -1\).
qs.s: The points are \((1, 5)\) and \((4, -1)\), giving a slope of \(m = \frac{-1 - 5}{4 - 1} = -2\). Substituting \((1, 5)\) into \(f(x) = -2x + b\) gives \(5 = -2(1) + b\), so \(b = 7\), yielding \(f(x) = -2x + 7\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 5\) and \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -1\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 5}{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)} = \frac{-6}{2} = -3\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -1\right)\) into \(f(x) = -3x + b\) yields \(-1 = -3\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + b\), so \(b = \frac{7}{2}\), giving \(f(x) = -3x + \frac{7}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -1\) and \(f\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = 7\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{7 - (-1)}{-\frac{4}{3} - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{8}{-2} = -4\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -1\right)\) gives \(-1 = -4\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + b\), so \(b = -1 + \frac{8}{3} = \frac{5}{3}\), which gives \(f(x) = -4x + \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-1) = \frac{5}{3}\) and \(f(3) = -\frac{1}{3}\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-14) = 108\) and \(f(26) = -52\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{2}}{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{-2}{\frac{1}{2}} = -4\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, \frac{3}{2}\right)\) gives \(\frac{3}{2} = -4\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) + b\), so \(b = \frac{3}{2} + 1 = \frac{5}{2}\), giving \(f(x) = -4x + \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(3) = 4\) and \(f(-2) = 1\).
qs.s: Find the slope \(m = \frac{1 - 4}{-2 - 3} = \frac{-3}{-5} = \frac{3}{5}\). Substitute \((3, 4)\) into \(f(x) = \frac{3}{5}x + b\) to find \(4 = \frac{3}{5}(3) + b\), giving \(b = 4 - \frac{9}{5} = \frac{11}{5}\), so \(f(x) = \frac{3}{5}x + \frac{11}{5}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(4) = 1\) and \(f(-2) = -3\).
qs.s: Find the slope \(m = \frac{-3 - 1}{-2 - 4} = \frac{-4}{-6} = \frac{2}{3}\). Substitute \((4, 1)\) into \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x + b\) to find \(1 = \frac{2}{3}(4) + b\), giving \(b = 1 - \frac{8}{3} = -\frac{5}{3}\), so \(f(x) = \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{5}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-1) = -4\) and \(f(2) = 5\).
qs.s: Find the slope \(m = \frac{5 - (-4)}{2 - (-1)} = \frac{9}{3} = 3\). Substitute \((2, 5)\) into \(f(x) = 3x + b\) to get \(5 = 3(2) + b\), which yields \(b = -1\), so \(f(x) = 3x - 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = 7\) and \(f(3) = -3\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(2.5) = -1.4\) and \(f(-1.5) = 8.6\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{3}{4}\right) = -\frac{7}{2}\) and \(f\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) = \frac{11}{3}\).
qs.s: Compute the slope \(m = \frac{\frac{11}{3} - \left(-\frac{7}{2}\right)}{\frac{5}{6} - \left(-\frac{3}{4}\right)} = \frac{\frac{43}{6}}{\frac{19}{12}} = \frac{86}{19}\). Substitute \(\left(\frac{5}{6}, \frac{11}{3}\right)\) into \(f(x) = \frac{86}{19}x + b\) to find \(\frac{11}{3} = \frac{86}{19}\left(\frac{5}{6}\right) + b\), which yields \(b = -\frac{2}{19}\), so \(f(x) = \frac{86}{19}x - \frac{2}{19}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{3}\).
qs.s: Find the slope \(m = \frac{-\frac{1}{3} - \frac{5}{2}}{\frac{3}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{17}{6}}{\frac{7}{4}} = -\frac{34}{21}\). Substitute \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{3}\right)\) into \(f(x) = -\frac{34}{21}x + b\) to find \(-\frac{1}{3} = -\frac{34}{21}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) + b\), yielding \(b = \frac{44}{21}\), so \(f(x) = -\frac{34}{21}x + \frac{44}{21}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(24) = -19\) and \(f(-16) = 41\).
qs.s: Calculate the slope \(m = \frac{41 - (-19)}{-16 - 24} = \frac{60}{-40} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Substitute \((24, -19)\) into \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + b\) to find \(-19 = -\frac{3}{2}(24) + b\), which yields \(b = 17\), so \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + 17\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{7}{2}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{\frac{7}{2} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{-\frac{1}{3} - \frac{2}{3}} = \frac{4}{-1} = -4\). Substitute \(\left(\frac{2}{3}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) into \(f(x) = -4x + b\) to find \(-\frac{1}{2} = -4\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) + b\), yielding \(b = \frac{13}{6}\), so \(f(x) = -4x + \frac{13}{6}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = 5\) and \(f(2) = -3\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-3 - 5}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\). Substitute \((2, -3)\) into \(-3 = -2(2) + b\) to find \(b = 1\), giving \(f(x) = -2x + 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-1) = -5\) and \(f(3) = 7\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{7 - (-5)}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{12}{4} = 3\). Substitute \((3, 7)\) into \(7 = 3(3) + b\) to find \(b = -2\), which gives \(f(x) = 3x - 2\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = -7\) and \(f(1) = 5\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{5 - (-7)}{1 - (-2)} = \frac{12}{3} = 4\). Substitute \((1, 5)\) into \(5 = 4(1) + b\) to find \(b = 1\), resulting in \(f(x) = 4x + 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-4) = -1\) and \(f(2) = 11\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{11 - (-1)}{2 - (-4)} = \frac{12}{6} = 2\). Substitute \((2, 11)\) into \(11 = 2(2) + b\) to solve for \(b = 7\), yielding \(f(x) = 2x + 7\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-5) = 8\) and \(f(1) = -4\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(12) = 45\) and \(f(36) = 105\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-6) = -7\) and \(f(1) = -2\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-2 - (-7)}{1 - (-6)} = \frac{5}{7}\). Substitute \((1, -2)\) into \(-2 = \frac{5}{7}(1) + b\) to find \(b = -2 - \frac{5}{7} = -\frac{19}{7}\), which gives \(f(x) = \frac{5}{7}x - \frac{19}{7}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-5) = -4\) and \(f(3) = 2\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{2 - (-4)}{3 - (-5)} = \frac{6}{8} = \frac{3}{4}\). Substitute \((3, 2)\) into \(2 = \frac{3}{4}(3) + b\) to find \(b = 2 - \frac{9}{4} = -\frac{1}{4}\), yielding \(f(x) = \frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-15) = 82\) and \(f(25) = -38\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = 5\) and \(f(4) = 1\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{1 - 5}{4 - (-2)} = -\frac{4}{6} = -\frac{2}{3}\). Substitute \((4, 1)\) into \(1 = -\frac{2}{3}(4) + b\) to solve for \(b = 1 + \frac{8}{3} = \frac{11}{3}\), giving \(f(x) = -\frac{2}{3}x + \frac{11}{3}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(2) = 5\) and \(f(4) = 11\).
qs.s: The points are \((2, 5)\) and \((4, 11)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{11 - 5}{4 - 2} = 3\), and substituting \((2, 5)\) into \(f(x) = 3x + b\) gives \(5 = 3(2) + b\), so \(b = -1\), yielding \(f(x) = 3x - 1\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-1) = -5\) and \(f(3) = 3\).
qs.s: The points are \((-1, -5)\) and \((3, 3)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{3 - (-5)}{3 - (-1)} = \frac{8}{4} = 2\), and using \((3, 3)\) gives \(3 = 2(3) + b\), so \(b = -3\), resulting in \(f(x) = 2x - 3\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-2) = 7\) and \(f(2) = -1\).
qs.s: The points are \((-2, 7)\) and \((2, -1)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 7}{2 - (-2)} = \frac{-8}{4} = -2\), and substituting \((2, -1)\) into \(f(x) = -2x + b\) gives \(-1 = -2(2) + b\), so \(b = 3\), giving \(f(x) = -2x + 3\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-3) = -4\) and \(f(1) = 8\).
qs.s: The points are \((-3, -4)\) and \((1, 8)\). The slope is \(m = \frac{8 - (-4)}{1 - (-3)} = \frac{12}{4} = 3\), and substituting \((1, 8)\) gives \(8 = 3(1) + b\), so \(b = 5\), giving \(f(x) = 3x + 5\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(1) = -3\) and \(f(5) = -7\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = -5\) and \(f(1) = 3\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-12) = -17\) and \(f(8) = 18\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{18 - (-17)}{8 - (-12)} = \frac{35}{20} = \frac{7}{4}\). Substituting \((8, 18)\) into the equation gives \(18 = \frac{7}{4}(8) + b = 14 + b\), so \(b = 4\), resulting in \(f(x) = \frac{7}{4}x + 4\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-5) = -4\) and \(f(3) = 1\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{1 - (-4)}{3 - (-5)} = \frac{5}{8}\). Substituting \((3, 1)\) gives \(1 = \frac{5}{8}(3) + b\), so \(b = 1 - \frac{15}{8} = -\frac{7}{8}\), which yields \(f(x) = \frac{5}{8}x - \frac{7}{8}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f(-14) = 53\) and \(f(18) = -43\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(f\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) = \frac{1}{3}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{\frac{1}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{2}\right)}{\frac{3}{4} - \frac{1}{4}} = \frac{\frac{5}{6}}{\frac{1}{2}} = \frac{5}{3}\). Solving for \(b\) using \(\left(\frac{1}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) gives \(b = -\frac{1}{2} - \frac{5}{3}\left(\frac{1}{4}\right) = -\frac{11}{12}\), so \(f(x) = \frac{5}{3}x - \frac{11}{12}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{5}{2}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{2}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{5}{2}}{-\frac{2}{3} - \frac{1}{3}} = \frac{-3}{-1} = 3\). Substituting \(\left(\frac{1}{3}, \frac{5}{2}\right)\), we find \(b = \frac{5}{2} - 3\left(\frac{1}{3}\right) = \frac{3}{2}\), giving \(f(x) = 3x + \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = 2\) and \(f\left(\frac{5}{3}\right) = -1\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-1 - 2}{\frac{5}{3} - \left(-\frac{1}{3}\right)} = \frac{-3}{2} = -\frac{3}{2}\). Solving for \(b\) gives \(b = 2 - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)\left(-\frac{1}{3}\right) = 2 - \frac{1}{2} = \frac{3}{2}\), so \(f(x) = -\frac{3}{2}x + \frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{1}{3}\) and \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{5}{3}\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{1}{4}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = \frac{7}{4}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{\frac{7}{4} - \left(-\frac{1}{4}\right)}{-\frac{1}{2} - \frac{3}{2}} = \frac{2}{-2} = -1\). Using the point \(\left(\frac{3}{2}, -\frac{1}{4}\right)\), \(b = -\frac{1}{4} - (-1)\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) = \frac{5}{4}\), so \(f(x) = -x + \frac{5}{4}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{4}{5}\right) = -\frac{61}{15}\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{12}\) and \(f\left(\frac{4}{5}\right) = -\frac{26}{15}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-\frac{26}{15} - \left(-\frac{1}{12}\right)}{\frac{4}{5} - \left(-\frac{2}{3}\right)} = \frac{-\frac{33}{20}}{\frac{22}{15}} = -\frac{9}{8}\). Then \(b = -\frac{1}{12} - \left(-\frac{9}{8}\right)\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = -\frac{1}{12} - \frac{3}{4} = -\frac{5}{6}\), which gives \(f(x) = -\frac{9}{8}x - \frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(f\left(\frac{9}{5}\right) = -\frac{1}{8}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{-\frac{1}{8} - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)}{\frac{9}{5} - \left(-\frac{3}{2}\right)} = \frac{\frac{11}{8}}{\frac{33}{10}} = \frac{5}{12}\). Finding the intercept gives \(b = -\frac{3}{2} - \frac{5}{12}\left(-\frac{3}{2}\right) = -\frac{3}{2} + \frac{5}{8} = -\frac{7}{8}\), so \(f(x) = \frac{5}{12}x - \frac{7}{8}\).

qs.q: Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{7}{2}\right) = \frac{13}{20}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) = \frac{71}{20}\).
Determine the linear function \(f(x) = mx + b\) if \(f\left(\frac{5}{8}\right) = \frac{5}{3}\) and \(f\left(-\frac{1}{4}\right) = \frac{17}{6}\).
qs.s: The slope is \(m = \frac{\frac{17}{6} - \frac{5}{3}}{-\frac{1}{4} - \frac{5}{8}} = \frac{\frac{7}{6}}{-\frac{7}{8}} = -\frac{4}{3}\). Using \(\left(\frac{5}{8}, \frac{5}{3}\right)\), \(b = \frac{5}{3} - \left(-\frac{4}{3}\right)\left(\frac{5}{8}\right) = \frac{5}{3} + \frac{5}{6} = \frac{5}{2}\), giving \(f(x) = -\frac{4}{3}x + \frac{5}{2}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 9x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{9(x+h) - 9x}{h} = \frac{9h}{h} = 9\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -5x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{-5(x+h) - (-5x)}{h} = \frac{-5h}{h} = -5\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{4(x+h) - 4x}{h} = \frac{4h}{h} = 4\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 6x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{6(x+h) - 6x}{h} = \frac{6h}{h} = 6\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -2x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{-2(x+h) - (-2x)}{h} = \frac{-2h}{h} = -2\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -6x + 19\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substituting \(f(x+h) = -6(x+h) + 19\) yields \(\frac{[-6x - 6h + 19] - [-6x + 19]}{h} = \frac{-6h}{h} = -6\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{2}{5}x + 3\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substituting \(f(x+h) = \frac{2}{5}(x+h) + 3\) gives \(\frac{[\frac{2}{5}x + \frac{2}{5}h + 3] - [\frac{2}{5}x + 3]}{h} = \frac{\frac{2}{5}h}{h} = \frac{2}{5}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 3(4 - 5x) + 2x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Simplify first to get \(f(x) = 12 - 13x\), which yields \(\frac{[12 - 13(x+h)] - [12 - 13x]}{h} = \frac{-13h}{h} = -13\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 15 - 4x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substituting \(f(x+h) = 15 - 4(x+h)\) gives \(\frac{[15 - 4x - 4h] - [15 - 4x]}{h} = \frac{-4h}{h} = -4\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{8 - 3x}{2}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Evaluating the difference quotient gives \(\frac{\frac{8 - 3(x+h)}{2} - \frac{8 - 3x}{2}}{h} = \frac{-\frac{3}{2}h}{h} = -\frac{3}{2}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -x - 6\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to get \(f(x+h) = -(x+h) - 6 = -x - h - 6\), so \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(-x - h - 6) - (-x - 6)}{h} = \frac{-h}{h} = -1\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5x + 2\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to get \(f(x+h) = 5(x+h) + 2 = 5x + 5h + 2\), so \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(5x + 5h + 2) - (5x + 2)}{h} = \frac{5h}{h} = 5\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -4x + 7\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to get \(f(x+h) = -4(x+h) + 7 = -4x - 4h + 7\), so \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(-4x - 4h + 7) - (-4x + 7)}{h} = \frac{-4h}{h} = -4\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 7x - 3\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to get \(f(x+h) = 7(x+h) - 3 = 7x + 7h - 3\), so \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(7x + 7h - 3) - (7x - 3)}{h} = \frac{7h}{h} = 7\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4 - 3x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to get \(f(x+h) = 4 - 3(x+h) = 4 - 3x - 3h\), so \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(4 - 3x - 3h) - (4 - 3x)}{h} = \frac{-3h}{h} = -3\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -\frac{5}{6}x + \frac{3}{8}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to find \(f(x+h) = -\frac{5}{6}(x+h) + \frac{3}{8}\), so \(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = \frac{-\frac{5}{6}h}{h} = -\frac{5}{6}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4(3 - 2x) - 5(x + 2)\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Simplifying the function first gives \(f(x) = 12 - 8x - 5x - 10 = -13x + 2\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = \frac{[-13(x+h)+2] - [-13x+2]}{h} = \frac{-13h}{h} = -13\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{11 - 9x}{4}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to find \(f(x+h) = \frac{11 - 9(x+h)}{4} = \frac{11 - 9x - 9h}{4}\), giving \(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = \frac{\frac{-9h}{4}}{h} = -\frac{9}{4}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 120 - 7(5x - 8) - 4(3 - 2x)\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(f(x) = 120 - 35x + 56 - 12 + 8x = -27x + 164\). Thus, the difference quotient is \(\frac{-27h}{h} = -27\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{7x - 4}{6}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute to find \(f(x+h) = \frac{7x+7h-4}{6}\), so \(\frac{f(x+h)-f(x)}{h} = \frac{\frac{7x+7h-4-(7x-4)}{6}}{h} = \frac{\frac{7h}{6}}{h} = \frac{7}{6}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 3x - 8\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(x+h) = 3(x+h) - 8 = 3x + 3h - 8\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(3x + 3h - 8) - (3x - 8)}{h} = \frac{3h}{h} = 3\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = -5x - 3\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(x+h) = -5(x+h) - 3 = -5x - 5h - 3\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(-5x - 5h - 3) - (-5x - 3)}{h} = \frac{-5h}{h} = -5\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 7 - 4x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(x+h) = 7 - 4(x+h) = 7 - 4x - 4h\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(7 - 4x - 4h) - (7 - 4x)}{h} = \frac{-4h}{h} = -4\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 6x + 11\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(x+h) = 6(x+h) + 11 = 6x + 6h + 11\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{(6x + 6h + 11) - (6x + 11)}{h} = \frac{6h}{h} = 6\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4250 - 138x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) into \(f(x)\) to get \(f(x+h) = 4250 - 138(x+h) = 4250 - 138x - 138h\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{-138h}{h} = -138\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{11 - 7x}{3}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) to obtain \(f(x+h) = \frac{11 - 7(x+h)}{3} = \frac{11 - 7x - 7h}{3}\). Subtracting \(f(x)\) gives \(\frac{-7h}{3}\), and dividing by \(h\) leaves \(-\frac{7}{3}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 5(3 - 4x) - 2(7 - 6x)\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Simplify the expression to \(f(x) = 15 - 20x - 14 + 12x = 1 - 8x\). Then \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h} = \frac{[1 - 8(x+h)] - [1 - 8x]}{h} = \frac{-8h}{h} = -8\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{3}{5} - \frac{4}{7}x\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x+h\) to get \(f(x+h) = \frac{3}{5} - \frac{4}{7}(x+h) = \frac{3}{5} - \frac{4}{7}x - \frac{4}{7}h\). Subtracting \(f(x)\) leaves \(-\frac{4}{7}h\), and dividing by \(h\) yields \(-\frac{4}{7}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = \frac{4x - 1}{3} - \frac{5x + 2}{4}\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: Combine terms with a common denominator of 12 to get \(f(x) = \frac{4(4x - 1) - 3(5x + 2)}{12} = \frac{x - 10}{12} = \frac{1}{12}x - \frac{5}{6}\). Then the difference quotient simplifies to \(\frac{\frac{1}{12}h}{h} = \frac{1}{12}\).

qs.q: For \(f(x) = 4x^2 - 1\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
For \(f(x) = 3x^2 + 2\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
For \(f(x) = -3x^2 - 4\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
For \(f(x) = 2x^2\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
For \(f(x) = -x^2 + 5\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
qs.s: \(f(x+h) - f(x) = [-(x+h)^2 + 5] - [-x^2 + 5] = -(x^2 + 2xh + h^2) + x^2 = -2xh - h^2\). Dividing each term by \(h\) gives \(-2x - h\).

For \(f(x) = 3x^2 - 4x + 5\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).
For \(f(x) = x^2 - 5x + 2\), determine \(\frac{f(x+h) - f(x)}{h}, h \neq 0\).

The function \(P(d) = \frac{2}{5}d + 15\) models the water pressure in pounds per square inch (psi) on a diver at a depth of \(d\) feet. Find the pressure at a depth of 65 feet.
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 65\) into the function: \(P(65) = \frac{2}{5}(65) + 15 = 26 + 15 = 41\text{ psi}\).

qs.q: The function \(v(T) = \frac{3}{5}T + 331\) models the speed of sound in dry air in meters per second, where \(T\) is the air temperature in degrees Celsius. Find the speed of sound when the temperature is \(25^\circ\text{C}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(T = 25\) into the function: \(v(25) = \frac{3}{5}(25) + 331 = 15 + 331 = 346\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(m) = 1.75m + 4.50\) models the fare in dollars for a taxi ride of \(m\) miles. Find the fare for an 8-mile taxi ride.
The function \(V(t) = 8500 - 650t\) models the value in dollars of office equipment \(t\) years after its purchase. Find the value of the equipment 6 years after its purchase.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 6\) into the function: $V(6) = 8500 - 650(6) = 8500 - 3900 = $4600.

qs.q: The function \(T(N) = \frac{1}{4}N + 40\) models the temperature in degrees Fahrenheit based on \(N\), the number of chirps a cricket makes in one minute. Find the temperature when a cricket chirps 112 times in one minute.
qs.s: Substitute \(N = 112\) into the function: \(T(112) = \frac{1}{4}(112) + 40 = 28 + 40 = 68^\circ\text{F}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(F) = \frac{5}{9}(F - 32)\) converts a temperature from degrees Fahrenheit to degrees Celsius. Find the Celsius equivalent of \(-13^\circ\text{F}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(F = -13\) into the function: \(C(-13) = \frac{5}{9}(-13 - 32) = \frac{5}{9}(-45) = 5(-5) = -25^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A catering company models its revenue in dollars by \(R(n) = 35n\) and its operating expenses by \(E(n) = 18n + 650\), where \(n\) is the number of guests. If profit is defined as \(P(n) = R(n) - E(n)\), find the profit earned from catering an event with 75 guests.

An industrial printing machine was purchased for $340,000 and depreciates according to the function \(V(t) = 340{,}000 - 23{,}500t\), where \(t\) is the number of years since purchase. Find the value of the machine 12 years after purchase.

A manufacturer models its daily operating cost in dollars with the function \(C(x) = 14.50x + 2800\), where \(x\) is the number of items produced. How much does the daily cost increase if production is increased from 120 items to 180 items?

A shipping company determines the cost in dollars to deliver an oversized parcel using the function \(C(w) = 24.50 + 3.75(w - 10)\), where \(w\) is the parcel's weight in pounds and \(w \ge 10\). Find the shipping cost for a parcel weighing 34 pounds.
The function \(F(m) = 1.50m + 4\) determines the fare, in dollars, for a taxi ride of \(m\) miles. Find the fare for a ride of \(6\text{ miles}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 6\) into the function: \(F(6) = 1.50(6) + 4 = 9 + 4 = 13\), so the fare is $13.

qs.q: The function \(H(t) = \frac{1}{2}t + 6\) determines the height of water in a storage tank, in feet, after filling for \(t\) hours. Find the height of the water after \(4\text{ hours}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 4\) into the function: \(H(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4) + 6 = 2 + 6 = 8\text{ feet}\).

qs.q: The function \(L(t) = 24 - 3t\) determines the length, in centimeters, of a burning candle after \(t\) hours. Find the length of the candle after \(5\text{ hours}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 5\) into the function: \(L(5) = 24 - 3(5) = 24 - 15 = 9\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The function \(S(T) = \frac{3}{5}T + 331\) determines the speed of sound in dry air, in meters per second, at a temperature of \(T\) degrees Celsius. Find the speed of sound in dry air at \(0^\circ\text{C}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(T = 0\) into the function: \(S(0) = \frac{3}{5}(0) + 331 = 0 + 331 = 331\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(n) = 0.05n + 12\) models the total cost, in dollars, to print \(n\) flyers at a local print shop. Find the total cost to print \(100\text{ flyers}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(n = 100\) into the function: \(C(100) = 0.05(100) + 12 = 5 + 12 = 17\), so the cost is $17.

qs.q: The total cost, in dollars, to purchase a television is given by the function \(C(p) = 1.07p + 25\), where \(p\) is the sticker price in dollars, \(1.07p\) includes a \(7\%\) sales tax, and $25 is a delivery fee. Find the total cost for a television with a sticker price of $650.
qs.s: Substitute \(p = 650\) into the function: \(C(650) = 1.07(650) + 25 = 695.50 + 25 = 720.50\), so the total cost is $720.50.

qs.q: An industrial fuel tank initially holds \(12\,500\text{ gallons}\) of fuel. A backup generator consumes fuel over time according to the function \(G(t) = 12\,500 - 42.5t\), where \(G(t)\) is the volume of fuel remaining, in gallons, after \(t\) hours. Find the volume of fuel remaining after \(140\text{ hours}\).

The water pressure, in kilopascals, at a depth of \(d\) meters in a lake is modeled by the function \(P(d) = 9.8d + 101.3\), where \(101.3\text{ kPa}\) is atmospheric pressure at the surface. Find the total pressure at a depth of \(35\text{ meters}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 35\) into the function: \(P(35) = 9.8(35) + 101.3 = 343 + 101.3 = 444.3\text{ kPa}\).

qs.q: In the troposphere, the temperature \(T\), in degrees Celsius, at an altitude of \(h\) kilometers above the ground is modeled by \(T(h) = 21 - 6.5h\). Find the temperature at an altitude of \(7.4\text{ kilometers}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 7.4\) into the function: \(T(7.4) = 21 - 6.5(7.4) = 21 - 48.1 = -27.1^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The total cost, in dollars, to produce \(x\) customized jerseys is modeled by the function \(C(x) = 16.75x + 450\). Find the total cost to produce \(120\text{ jerseys}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 120\) into the function: \(C(120) = 16.75(120) + 450 = 2010 + 450 = 2460\), so the total cost is $2460.

qs.q: Dolbear's Law estimates outdoor temperature in degrees Fahrenheit using the function \(T(N) = \frac{1}{4}N + 40\), where \(N\) is the number of chirps a snowy tree cricket makes per minute. Find the temperature when a cricket chirps \(68\) times in one minute.
qs.s: Substitute \(N = 68\) into the function: \(T(68) = \frac{1}{4}(68) + 40 = 17 + 40 = 57^\circ\text{F}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(F) = \frac{5}{9}(F - 32)\) converts a temperature from degrees Fahrenheit to degrees Celsius. Find the Celsius equivalent of \(-4^\circ\text{F}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(F = -4\) into the formula: \(C(-4) = \frac{5}{9}(-4 - 32) = \frac{5}{9}(-36) = -20^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The depth of water in a drainage canal is modeled by the function \(D(t) = \frac{3}{4}t + 18\), where \(t\) is the time in minutes after rain begins and \(D(t)\) is measured in inches. Find the water depth after \(28\) minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 28\) into the function: \(D(28) = \frac{3}{4}(28) + 18 = 21 + 18 = 39\text{ inches}\).

qs.q: A hot air balloon descends toward the ground according to the function \(h(t) = -\frac{5}{2}t + 450\), where \(h(t)\) is the height in meters and \(t\) is the time in minutes. Find the height of the balloon after \(30\) minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 30\) into the function: \(h(30) = -\frac{5}{2}(30) + 450 = -75 + 450 = 375\text{ meters}\).

qs.q: The speed of sound in dry air is modeled by the function \(v(T) = \frac{3}{5}T + 331\), where \(T\) is the temperature in degrees Celsius and \(v(T)\) is the speed in meters per second. Find the speed of sound when the temperature is \(20^\circ\text{C}\).
qs.s: Substitute \(T = 20\) into the function: \(v(20) = \frac{3}{5}(20) + 331 = 12 + 331 = 343\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The weekly profit \(P(x)\) (in dollars) of a bakery that bakes and sells \(x\) specialty cakes is modeled by \(P(x) = 38.50x - (13.50x + 1200) - 450\). Find the bakery's weekly profit if it sells \(140\) cakes.
A factory's total daily cost \(C(x)\) (in dollars) to manufacture \(x\) bicycles is given by \(C(x) = 1.08(125x + 4800) + 350\). Find the total cost to produce \(64\) bicycles in a day.

The atmospheric temperature \(T(h)\) (in \(^\circ\text{C}\)) at an altitude of \(h\) kilometers above the base of the lower stratosphere is modeled by \(T(h) = -56.5 + 1.8(h - 11)\). Find the temperature at an altitude of \(24.5\text{ km}\).

The total cost \(C(w)\) (in dollars) to ship an international package of weight \(w\) kilograms is given by \(C(w) = 1.35\left(\frac{16}{5}w + 45\right) + 18.25\). Find the total cost to ship a package weighing \(25\text{ kilograms}\).

A deep-sea research submarine's elevation \(E(t)\) (in meters relative to sea level) after \(t\) minutes of descent is modeled by the function \(E(t) = -180 - \frac{14}{3}(2t + 15)\). Find the submarine's elevation after \(45\) minutes.
A stone is dropped from a bridge into a river. The height of the stone in metres, \(t\) seconds after it is dropped, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 45\). Find \(h(0)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 0\) into the function: \(h(0) = -4.9(0)^2 + 45 = 0 + 45 = 45\).

qs.q: An acorn falls from a high tree branch. The height of the acorn in metres, \(t\) seconds after it falls, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 19.6\). Find \(h(0)\).

A garden barrel full of rainwater is being drained. The volume of water in litres remaining in the barrel, \(t\) minutes after the drain is opened, is given by the function \(V(t) = -6t^2 + 150\). Find \(V(1)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 1\) into the function: \(V(1) = -6(1)^2 + 150 = -6 + 150 = 144\).

qs.q: A bowl of hot soup is left to cool on a counter. The temperature of the soup in degrees Celsius, \(t\) minutes after it is served, is given by the function \(T(t) = -0.8t^2 + 82\). Find \(T(0)\).
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 0\) into the function: \(T(0) = -0.8(0)^2 + 82 = 0 + 82 = 82\).

qs.q: A tennis ball is dropped from the roof of a school building. The height of the ball in metres, \(t\) seconds after it is dropped, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 25\). Find \(h(1)\).
A small business models its daily profit in dollars from producing and selling \(x\) handmade chairs with the function \(P(x) = -5x^2 + 160x - 400\). Find \(P(8)\).
An arrow is shot vertically upward from an elevated platform. Its height in feet, \(t\) seconds after being released, is given by the function \(h(t) = -16t^2 + 96t + 10\). Find \(h(4)\).
An emergency flare is fired upward from the deck of a boat. Its height in metres above the water, \(t\) seconds after launch, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 39.2t + 4\). Find \(h(5)\).
An industrial oven is warming up. Its internal temperature in degrees Celsius, \(t\) minutes after being turned on, is given by the function \(T(t) = -0.5t^2 + 18t + 25\). Find \(T(6)\).
A model rocket is launched vertically upward. Its height in metres, \(t\) seconds after launch, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 30t + 2\). Find \(h(3)\).

A small probe is released downward from a drone. The height of the probe in metres, \(t\) seconds after release, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 250\). Find the height of the probe after \(6\) seconds.

A stone is dropped from a cliff into a canyon. The height of the stone in metres above the canyon floor, \(t\) seconds after being dropped, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 80\). Find the height of the stone after \(3\) seconds.

Water is draining from a storage tank. The volume of water remaining in litres, \(t\) minutes after the drain is opened, is modeled by the function \(V(t) = -1.2t^2 + 500\). Find the volume of water in the tank after \(10\) minutes.

A camera is accidentally dropped from a hot air balloon. Its height in metres, \(t\) seconds after slipping, is given by the function \(h(t) = -5t^2 + 200\). Find the height of the camera after \(5\) seconds.

The temperature of a cooling metal rod in degrees Celsius, \(t\) minutes after being removed from a furnace, is modeled by \(T(t) = -2.5t^2 + 150\). Find the temperature of the rod after \(4\) minutes.

Two drones fly vertically. Drone A's altitude in metres is given by \(A(t) = -3t^2 + 25t + 80\), and Drone B's altitude in metres is given by \(B(t) = 4t + 35\), where \(t\) is the time in seconds. Find the difference in altitude between Drone A and Drone B after \(5\) seconds.
qs.s: Evaluate both functions at \(t = 5\): \(A(5) = -3(5)^2 + 25(5) + 80 = 130\text{ m}\) and \(B(5) = 4(5) + 35 = 55\text{ m}\). The difference in altitude is \(130 - 55 = 75\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A company's daily profit in dollars from manufacturing \(x\) bicycles is given by the function \(P(x) = -0.5x^2 + 180x - 4200\). Find the daily profit when the company manufactures \(120\) bicycles.

A flare is launched vertically upward from an elevated platform. Its height in metres, \(t\) seconds after launch, is modeled by \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 39.2t + 15\). Find the height of the flare after \(4\) seconds.

The temperature of a chemical compound during an experiment, in degrees Celsius, is modeled by the function \(T(m) = -2m^2 + 14m + 18\), where \(m\) is the time in minutes since the reaction began. Find the temperature of the compound after \(3.5\) minutes.

A stunt diver jumps from a cliff. Her height above the water in metres, \(t\) seconds after jumping, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 - 2t + 60\). How many metres does she fall between \(t = 1\) second and \(t = 2\) seconds?
qs.s: Evaluate the height at both times: \(h(1) = -4.9(1)^2 - 2(1) + 60 = 53.1\text{ m}\) and \(h(2) = -4.9(2)^2 - 2(2) + 60 = 36.4\text{ m}\). The distance fallen is \(53.1 - 36.4 = 16.7\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A large storage tank is being drained of water. The volume of water remaining in the tank, in thousands of litres, \(t\) hours after drainage begins, is given by the function \(V(t) = -1.5t^2 + 96\). Find the time, in hours, it takes for the tank to be completely empty.
qs.s: Set \(V(t) = 0\) to get \(-1.5t^2 + 96 = 0\), leading to \(1.5t^2 = 96\) and \(t^2 = 64\). Taking the positive root gives \(t = 8\) hours.

qs.q: An astronaut on the Moon drops a small tool from the edge of a crater. The height of the tool in metres, \(t\) seconds after it is dropped, is modeled by the function \(h(t) = -0.8t^2 + 20\). Find the time, in seconds, it takes for the tool to hit the ground.

The electrical power \(P\), in watts, generated by a small wind turbine at a wind speed of \(w\) metres per second is given by the function \(P(w) = 2.5w^2\). If the turbine is generating \(250\text{ watts}\) of power, find the wind speed \(w\), in metres per second.
qs.s: Set \(P(w) = 250\) to get \(2.5w^2 = 250\), which yields \(w^2 = \frac{250}{2.5} = 100\). Taking the positive square root gives \(w = 10\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: The braking distance \(d\), in metres, of a car travelling at a speed of \(v\) metres per second on dry pavement is modeled by the function \(d(v) = 0.05v^2\). If the car takes \(45\text{ metres}\) to come to a complete stop, find its speed \(v\), in metres per second.
qs.s: Set \(d(v) = 45\) to get \(0.05v^2 = 45\), which simplifies to \(v^2 = \frac{45}{0.05} = 900\). Taking the positive square root gives \(v = 30\text{ m/s}\).

qs.q: A camera is accidentally dropped from an observation deck. The height of the camera in metres, \(t\) seconds after it is dropped, is given by the function \(h(t) = -4.9t^2 + 176.4\). Find the time, in seconds, it takes for the camera to hit the ground.
qs.s: Set \(h(t) = 0\) to get \(-4.9t^2 + 176.4 = 0\), which gives \(4.9t^2 = 176.4\) or \(t^2 = 36\). Since time must be positive, \(t = 6\) seconds.

qs.q: A skydiver jumps from an airplane at an altitude of \(2500\text{ metres}\). Before opening the parachute, the skydiver's altitude \(h(t)\), in metres above the ground, \(t\) seconds after jumping, is given by the function \(h(t) = 2500 - 4.9t^2\). Find the time, in seconds, it takes for the skydiver to descend to an altitude of \(540\text{ metres}\).
qs.s: Set \(h(t) = 540\) to get \(2500 - 4.9t^2 = 540\), so \(4.9t^2 = 1960\). Dividing yields \(t^2 = \frac{1960}{4.9} = 400\), which gives \(t = 20\) seconds.

qs.q: A manufacturing company finds that the total cost \(C(x)\), in dollars, to produce \(x\) custom engine components is given by the function \(C(x) = 0.08x^2 + 450\). If the total cost for a production run was $2498, how many components were produced?
qs.s: Set \(C(x) = 2498\) to get \(0.08x^2 + 450 = 2498\), so \(0.08x^2 = 2048\). Dividing by \(0.08\) gives \(x^2 = 25600\), and taking the square root gives \(x = 160\) components.

qs.q: A weather balloon is released and begins ascending. Its altitude \(A(t)\), in metres above the ground, \(t\) minutes after release, is modeled by the function \(A(t) = 120 + 2.5(t + 4)^2\). Find the time, in minutes after release, when the balloon reaches an altitude of \(480\text{ metres}\).
qs.s: Set \(A(t) = 480\) to get \(120 + 2.5(t + 4)^2 = 480\), so \(2.5(t + 4)^2 = 360\). Dividing by \(2.5\) gives \((t + 4)^2 = 144\), which means \(t + 4 = 12\), and therefore \(t = 8\) minutes.

qs.q: The signal intensity \(S\), in milliwatts, received from a transmitter at a distance of \(d\) kilometres is given by the function \(S(d) = \frac{4500}{d^2 + 11}\). At what distance \(d\), in kilometres, is the signal intensity equal to \(75\text{ milliwatts}\)?

A model rocket is launched from a raised platform. Its height \(h(t)\), in metres above the ground, \(t\) seconds after launch, is given by the function \(h(t) = -5(t - 4)^2 + 320\). Find the time, in seconds, it takes for the rocket to reach the ground.
qs.s: Set \(h(t) = 0\) to get \(-5(t - 4)^2 + 320 = 0\), so \((t - 4)^2 = 64\). Since the rocket hits the ground after reaching its peak, \(t - 4 = 8\), giving \(t = 12\) seconds.

qs.q: The function \(V(t) = 60 - \frac{t}{4}\) gives the volume of water in gallons remaining in a reservoir \(t\) minutes after a drain is opened. Find the volume of water remaining after 72 minutes.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 72\) into the function: \(V(72) = 60 - \frac{72}{4} = 60 - 18 = 42\). Therefore, 42 gallons remain.

qs.q: The function \(T(h) = 24 - \frac{h}{150}\) gives the temperature in degrees Celsius at an elevation of \(h\) meters above the base of a mountain. Find the temperature at an elevation of 900 meters.
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 900\) into the function: \(T(900) = 24 - \frac{900}{150} = 24 - 6 = 18\). The temperature is \(18^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The function \(H(w) = \frac{w}{6} + 5\) gives the height in inches of a young tree \(w\) weeks after being planted. Find the height of the tree after 42 weeks.
qs.s: Substitute \(w = 42\) into the function: \(H(42) = \frac{42}{6} + 5 = 7 + 5 = 12\). The height of the tree is 12 inches.

qs.q: The function \(C(m) = \frac{m}{5} + 12\) gives the total cost in dollars of renting a bicycle for \(m\) miles. Find the cost of renting a bicycle for 45 miles.
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 45\) into the function: \(C(45) = \frac{45}{5} + 12 = 9 + 12 = 21\). Thus, the total cost is $21.

qs.q: The function \(A(n) = \frac{n}{25} + 4\) gives the time in hours required to inspect \(n\) manufactured parts. Find the inspection time for 175 parts.
qs.s: Substitute \(n = 175\) into the function: \(A(175) = \frac{175}{25} + 4 = 7 + 4 = 11\). The inspection time is 11 hours.

qs.q: The function \(V(t) = 140\,000\left(1 - \frac{t}{25}\right)\) gives the value in dollars of heavy construction equipment \(t\) years after its purchase. Find the value of the equipment after 9 years.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 9\) into the function: \(V(9) = 140\,000\left(1 - \frac{9}{25}\right) = 140\,000\left(\frac{16}{25}\right) = 89\,600\). The value after 9 years is $89 600.

qs.q: The function \(T(a) = 21.5 - \frac{6.5(a - 400)}{1000}\) gives the temperature in degrees Celsius at an altitude of \(a\) meters above sea level. Find the temperature at an altitude of 3400 meters.
qs.s: Substitute \(a = 3400\) into the function: \(T(3400) = 21.5 - \frac{6.5(3000)}{1000} = 21.5 - 19.5 = 2\). The temperature is \(2^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(p) = 1.08p + 35\) gives the total cost in dollars of purchasing an appliance priced at \(p\) dollars, including an 8% sales tax and a $35 delivery fee. Find the total cost for an appliance priced at $650.
qs.s: Substitute \(p = 650\) into the function: \(C(650) = 1.08(650) + 35 = 702 + 35 = 737\). The total cost is $737.

qs.q: The function \(C(n) = \frac{1800 + 24n}{n}\) gives the average cost in dollars per jersey to produce an order of \(n\) custom jerseys. Find the average cost per jersey for an order of 120 jerseys.
qs.s: Substitute \(n = 120\) into the function: \(C(120) = \frac{1800 + 24(120)}{120} = \frac{4680}{120} = 39\). The average cost is $39 per jersey.

qs.q: The function \(d(s) = \frac{s^2}{20} + s\) gives the total stopping distance in feet of a car traveling at a speed of \(s\) miles per hour. Find the stopping distance for a car traveling at 60 miles per hour.
qs.s: Substitute \(s = 60\) into the function: \(d(60) = \frac{60^2}{20} + 60 = \frac{3600}{20} + 60 = 180 + 60 = 240\). The stopping distance is 240 feet.

qs.q: The function \(H(t) = 28 - \frac{t}{15}\) gives the height in centimeters of a burning candle after \(t\) minutes. After how many minutes is the candle's height 17.6 centimeters?
qs.s: Set \(17.6 = 28 - \frac{t}{15}\), which rearranges to \(\frac{t}{15} = 28 - 17.6 = 10.4\). Multiplying both sides by 15 gives \(t = 156\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: The function \(C(m) = \frac{m}{25} + 12\) gives the monthly cost in dollars of a water utility service when \(m\) cubic meters of water are used. At what water usage is the monthly cost $18.40?
qs.s: Set \(C(m) = 18.40\) to get \(18.40 = \frac{m}{25} + 12\). Subtract 12 to obtain \(6.40 = \frac{m}{25}\), then multiply both sides by 25 to find \(m = 160\text{ m}^3\).

qs.q: The function \(F(d) = \frac{d}{40} + 3.5\) gives the taxi fare in dollars for a trip of \(d\) city blocks. For what distance, in blocks, is the fare $11.50?
qs.s: Set \(11.50 = \frac{d}{40} + 3.5\), subtract \(3.5\) to get \(8 = \frac{d}{40}\), and multiply by 40 to get \(d = 320\text{ blocks}\).

qs.q: The function \(L(w) = \frac{w}{16} + 5\) gives the length in inches of a hanging spring supporting a weight of \(w\) ounces. At what weight is the spring length 8.25 inches?
qs.s: Substitute 8.25 into the function to obtain \(8.25 = \frac{w}{16} + 5\). Subtract 5 to get \(3.25 = \frac{w}{16}\), then multiply by 16 to find \(w = 52\text{ ounces}\).

qs.q: The function \(T(n) = \frac{n}{4} + 40\) gives the estimated temperature in degrees Fahrenheit when a snowy tree cricket chirps \(n\) times per minute. How many chirps per minute correspond to a temperature of 74.5 °F?
qs.s: Set \(74.5 = \frac{n}{4} + 40\). Subtract 40 to get \(34.5 = \frac{n}{4}\), then multiply by 4 to find \(n = 138\text{ chirps per minute}\).

qs.q: A shipping company calculates the delivery cost in dollars for an oversized package using the function \(C(w) = \frac{3(w - 40)}{8} + 65\), where \(w\) is the package's weight in pounds (\(w \ge 40\)). What is the weight of a package that costs $107 to ship?
qs.s: Subtract 65 from 107 to get \(42 = \frac{3(w - 40)}{8}\). Multiply by 8 and divide by 3 to find \(w - 40 = 112\), which yields \(w = 152\text{ pounds}\).

qs.q: A publishing company determines that the total production cost in dollars for printing \(n\) textbooks is given by the function \(C(n) = 0.85n + \frac{n}{20} + 4500\). How many textbooks can be produced for a total cost of $11,250?
qs.s: Combine like terms using \(\frac{n}{20} = 0.05n\), giving \(C(n) = 0.90n + 4500\). Set \(0.90n + 4500 = 11\,250\), subtract 4500 to get \(0.90n = 6750\), and divide by 0.90 to find \(n = 7500\).

qs.q: The altitude in feet of a descending glider after \(t\) minutes is given by the function \(A(t) = \frac{18\,000 - 450t}{4} + 1200\). At what time \(t\), in minutes, will the glider reach an altitude of 3450 feet?
qs.s: Subtract 1200 from 3450 to get \(2250 = \frac{18\,000 - 450t}{4}\). Multiply both sides by 4 to obtain \(9000 = 18\,000 - 450t\), which simplifies to \(450t = 9000\), giving \(t = 20\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: A sales representative earns a monthly income in dollars modeled by the function \(S(x) = \frac{3}{50}x + 0.04(x - 5000) + 2800\) for total sales \(x > 5000\), where \(x\) is measured in dollars. What was the representative's total monthly sales if their income was $4900?

The resale value in dollars of a commercial excavator after \(t\) years of operation is given by the function \(V(t) = 184\,000 - \frac{46\,000}{3}t\). After how many years will the excavator have a resale value of $69,000?
qs.s: Set \(69\,000 = 184\,000 - \frac{46\,000}{3}t\), which gives \(\frac{46\,000}{3}t = 115\,000\). Multiplying by 3 and dividing by 46,000 yields \(t = \frac{345\,000}{46\,000} = 7.5\text{ years}\).

qs.q: The water level in a reservoir, \(H(t)\) in centimetres, during a rainstorm is given by \(H(t) = 4t + 85\), where \(t\) is the time in hours. Find the water level after 6 hours.
qs.s: Substitute \(t = 6\) into the function: \(H(6) = 4(6) + 85 = 24 + 85 = 109\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The cost, \(C(n)\) in dollars, to order \(n\) custom T-shirts is given by \(C(n) = 8n + 25\). Find the cost to order 15 T-shirts.
qs.s: Substitute \(n = 15\) into the function: \(C(15) = 8(15) + 25 = 120 + 25 = 145\) dollars.

qs.q: The height of a bamboo plant, \(h(d)\) in centimetres, after \(d\) days of growth is given by \(h(d) = 15d + 30\). Find the height of the plant after 9 days.
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 9\) into the function: \(h(9) = 15(9) + 30 = 135 + 30 = 165\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(C(d)\) in dollars, of renting a truck for a day and driving it \(d\) kilometres is given by \(C(d) = 0.50d + 40\). Find the total cost if the truck is driven 70 km.
qs.s: Substitute \(d = 70\) into the function: \(C(70) = 0.50(70) + 40 = 35 + 40 = 75\) dollars.

qs.q: The total number of calories burned during a workout, \(C(m)\), is given by \(C(m) = 12m + 50\), where \(m\) is the duration of the workout in minutes. Find the total calories burned in a 45-minute workout.
qs.s: Substitute \(m = 45\) into the function: \(C(45) = 12(45) + 50 = 540 + 50 = 590\) calories.

qs.q: The air temperature, \(T(h)\) in degrees Celsius, at an altitude of \(h\) kilometres above sea level is given by \(T(h) = 21.4 - 6.5h\). Find the air temperature at an altitude of 5.8 km.
qs.s: Substitute \(h = 5.8\) into the function: \(T(5.8) = 21.4 - 6.5(5.8) = 21.4 - 37.7 = -16.3^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: A catering company models its fee, \(C(g)\) in dollars, for an event with \(g\) guests (where \(g \ge 30\)) using the function \(C(g) = 450 + 28(g - 30)\). Find the total cost for an event with 75 guests.
A commercial electricity bill, \(B(k)\) in dollars, for using \(k\) kilowatt-hours (kWh) of electricity is given by \(B(k) = 0.145k + 42.80\). Find the total bill for using 1600 kWh.
The value of a construction vehicle, \(V(t)\) in dollars, after \(t\) years of operation is modeled by the function \(V(t) = 145\,000 - 13\,500t\). Find the value of the vehicle after 7 years.
The net profit of a small business, \(P(x)\) in dollars, from selling \(x\) items is given by \(P(x) = 85x - (32x + 1650)\). Find the net profit when 140 items are sold.
The height of a burning candle, in centimetres, after \(t\) hours is given by \(h(t) = 28 - 2.5t\). After how many hours will the candle have a height of \(10.5\text{ cm}\)?
qs.s: Set \(h(t) = 10.5\) to get \(28 - 2.5t = 10.5\). Subtract 28 to get \(-2.5t = -17.5\), then divide by \(-2.5\) to find \(t = 7\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: A hiker's elevation, \(E\), in metres after hiking for \(t\) hours is given by \(E(t) = 180t + 350\). After how many hours is the hiker at an elevation of \(1250\text{ metres}\)?
qs.s: Set \(E(t) = 1250\) to get \(180t + 350 = 1250\). Subtract 350 to get \(180t = 900\), then divide by 180 to find \(t = 5\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: The monthly cost, in dollars, of a cell phone plan is given by \(C(m) = 0.15m + 35\), where \(m\) is the number of text messages sent. How many text messages were sent in a month when the bill was $56?
qs.s: Set \(C(m) = 56\) to get \(0.15m + 35 = 56\). Subtract 35 to get \(0.15m = 21\), then divide by 0.15 to find \(m = 140\).

qs.q: The cost, in dollars, to rent a canoe for \(h\) hours is given by \(C(h) = 12h + 25\). For how many hours was the canoe rented if the total cost was $109?
qs.s: Set \(C(h) = 109\) to get \(12h + 25 = 109\). Subtract 25 to obtain \(12h = 84\), then divide by 12 to find \(h = 7\text{ hours}\).

qs.q: The volume of water, \(V\), in litres remaining in a tank after draining for \(t\) minutes is given by \(V(t) = 450 - 15t\). After how many minutes will there be \(120\text{ litres}\) of water left in the tank?
qs.s: Set \(V(t) = 120\) to get \(450 - 15t = 120\). Subtract 450 to get \(-15t = -330\), then divide by \(-15\) to find \(t = 22\text{ minutes}\).

qs.q: The temperature in degrees Fahrenheit, \(F\), is given as a function of the temperature in degrees Celsius, \(C\), by \(F(C) = \frac{9}{5}C + 32\). What is the temperature in degrees Celsius when the temperature is \(-13^\circ\text{F}\)?
qs.s: Set \(F(C) = -13\) to get \(\frac{9}{5}C + 32 = -13\). Subtract 32 to get \(\frac{9}{5}C = -45\), then multiply by \(\frac{5}{9}\) to find \(C = -25^\circ\text{C}\).

qs.q: The total cost, \(C(p)\), in dollars of purchasing and delivering a refrigerator is given by the function \(C(p) = 1.08p + 65\), which includes an \(8\%\) sales tax on the purchase price \(p\) and a $65 delivery fee. What was the purchase price of the refrigerator if the total cost was $983?
qs.s: Set \(C(p) = 983\) to get \(1.08p + 65 = 983\). Subtract 65 to get \(1.08p = 918\), then divide by 1.08 to find \(p = \$850\).

qs.q: A manufacturing company models its daily production cost, in dollars, using the function \(C(x) = 3.75(x - 40) + 1650\), where \(x\) represents the number of units produced (\(x \ge 40\)). How many units were produced on a day when the total cost was $3450?

The outside air temperature, \(T(a)\), in degrees Celsius at an altitude of \(a\) metres above sea level is given by \(T(a) = 15 - \frac{3}{400}a\). At what altitude is the outside temperature \(-9^\circ\text{C}\)?
qs.s: Set \(T(a) = -9\) to get \(15 - \frac{3}{400}a = -9\). Subtract 15 to get \(-\frac{3}{400}a = -24\), then multiply by \(-\frac{400}{3}\) to find \(a = 3200\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A catering service calculates the total charge, in dollars, for an event using the function \(C(n) = 35n + 0.20(35n) + 450\), which includes the meal cost for \(n\) guests, a \(20\%\) gratuity on meals, and a flat $450 setup fee. For how many guests was an event catered if the total charge was $3180?
qs.s: Combine like terms to write \(C(n) = 42n + 450\). Set \(42n + 450 = 3180\), subtract 450 to get \(42n = 2730\), and divide by 42 to find \(n = 65\).

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((3, -2)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(2x + y = 4\)
\(x - 2y = 7\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 3\) and \(y = -2\) into \(2x + y = 4\) yields \(2(3) + (-2) = 4\), and into \(x - 2y = 7\) yields \(3 - 2(-2) = 7\). Since both statements are true, \((3, -2)\) is a solution to the linear system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((-1, 3)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(3x + 2y = 5\)
\(4x - y = -6\)
qs.s: Substituting \((-1, 3)\) into \(3x + 2y = 5\) gives \(3(-1) + 2(3) = 3 \neq 5\), and into \(4x - y = -6\) gives \(4(-1) - 3 = -7 \neq -6\). Since it satisfies neither equation, it is not a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((1, 4)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(2x + y = 8\)
\(5x - y = 1\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, 4)\) into \(2x + y = 8\) gives \(2(1) + 4 = 6 \neq 8\) (false), while substituting into \(5x - y = 1\) gives \(5(1) - 4 = 1\) (true). Thus, it satisfies only the second equation and is not a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((3, 2)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(4x - y = 10\)
\(2x + 3y = 16\)
qs.s: Substituting \((3, 2)\) into \(4x - y = 10\) yields \(4(3) - 2 = 10\) (true), but substituting into \(2x + 3y = 16\) yields \(2(3) + 3(2) = 12 \neq 16\) (false). Because it only satisfies the first equation, it is not a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((4, 1)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(2x + y = 9\)
\(x + 3y = 7\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 4\) and \(y = 1\) into \(2x + y = 9\) gives \(2(4) + 1 = 9\), and into \(x + 3y = 7\) gives \(4 + 3(1) = 7\). Since both equations are true, \((4, 1)\) is a solution to the linear system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -3\right)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(4x - 3y = 11\)
\(6x + 2y = -3\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(y = -3\) into \(4x - 3y = 11\) gives \(2 - (-9) = 11\), and into \(6x + 2y = -3\) gives \(3 + (-6) = -3\). Since both equations hold true, \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -3\right)\) is a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((1, -2)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(3(x + 4) - 2y = x - 5y + 7\)
\(4x - 3y + 2 = 2y + 16\)
qs.s: Substituting \((1, -2)\) into the first equation yields \(19 = 18\) (false), while substituting into the second equation yields \(12 = 12\) (true). Therefore, the ordered pair satisfies only the second equation.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((4, -3)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{2}{3}y = -5\)
\(\frac{1}{2}x + \frac{5}{6}y = 7\)
qs.s: Substituting \((4, -3)\) into the first equation yields \(3 - (-2) = 5 \neq -5\), and into the second equation yields \(2 - 2.5 = -0.5 \neq 7\). Since neither equation is satisfied, \((4, -3)\) is not a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((1.5, -2)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(0.4x - 0.3y = 1.2\)
\(1.2x + 0.5y = 0.8\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 1.5\) and \(y = -2\) gives \(0.4(1.5) - 0.3(-2) = 0.6 + 0.6 = 1.2\) for the first equation and \(1.2(1.5) + 0.5(-2) = 1.8 - 1.0 = 0.8\) for the second. Since both equations are true, \((1.5, -2)\) is a solution.

qs.q:

\(2(x - 1) + 3(y + 2) = 13\)
\(4(x + y) - (2x - y) = 5\)
d: No, it satisfies only \(4(x + y) - (2x - y) = 5\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = 3\) and \(y = 1\) into the first equation gives \(2(2) + 3(3) = 13\) (true). Substituting into the second equation gives \(4(4) - (6 - 1) = 16 - 5 = 11 \neq 5\) (false), so it only satisfies the first equation.

qs.q:

qs.q:

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \(\left(\frac{3}{4}, -\frac{1}{2}\right)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(\frac{2}{3}x - 4y = \frac{5}{2}\)
\(2x + \frac{5}{2}y = \frac{1}{4}\)

d: No, it satisfies only the first equation
No, it satisfies only the second equation

Both equations are satisfied, so it is a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((2.5, -1.5)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(1.2x - 0.8y = 3.6\)
\(0.6x + 1.4y = -0.6\)
qs.a: No, it satisfies only the second equation
d: Yes, it is a solution to the system
No, it satisfies only the first equation

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((5, -4)\) is a solution to the linear system:

\(5(x + y) - 2(2x - y) = -15\)

No, it satisfies only the second equation

qs.q:

\(3(x + 2y) - 5 = 2x + 3y + 4\)
\(4(2x - y) + 7 = 3(x - 3y) - 2\)

d: Yes, it is a solution to the system
No, it satisfies only the second equation

qs.q:

qs.a: Yes, it is a solution to the system
d: No, it satisfies only the first equation

qs.q:

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((2, -3)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(2x + y = 1\)
\(4x - y = 5\)
qs.a: No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the first equation.
d: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the second equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies neither equation.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((4, -2)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(2x + 3y = 5\)
\(5x - y = 18\)
qs.a: No, it is not a solution because it satisfies neither equation.
d: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the first equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the second equation.
qs.s: Substituting \((4, -2)\) into \(2x + 3y = 5\) gives \(2(4) + 3(-2) = 2 \neq 5\), and into \(5x - y = 18\) gives \(5(4) - (-2) = 22 \neq 18\). Since neither equation is satisfied, the ordered pair is not a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((3, -1)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(3x - 2y = 11\)
\(x + 4y = -1\)
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.
d: No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the first equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the second equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies neither equation.
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3\) and \(y = -1\) into both equations: \(3(3) - 2(-1) = 9 + 2 = 11\) and \(3 + 4(-1) = 3 - 4 = -1\). Since both equations are true, \((3, -1)\) is a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((-2, -3)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(4x - y = -5\)
\(3x - 2y = 0\)
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.

qs.q:

\(2(x - 3y) - 5 = 3(x + y) + 10\)
\(4(2x + y) - 3x = 2(y - 1) + 17\)

d: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.

qs.q:

\(15x + 8y = -2\)
\(12x - 11y = -125\)

qs.q:

qs.q:

\(3(2x + y) - 2(x - 2y) = 27\)
\(5(x + y) + 4(2x - y) = -21\)
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.
d: No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the first equation.

No, it is not a solution because it satisfies neither equation.
qs.s: Substituting \((-2, 5)\) into the first equation yields \(3(1) - 2(-12) = 27\), and into the second equation yields \(5(3) + 4(-9) = -21\). Since both equations are satisfied, \((-2, 5)\) is a solution to the linear system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) is a solution to the linear system:
\(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{4}y = \frac{5}{6}\)
\(\frac{4}{5}x + \frac{9}{10}y = -\frac{1}{5}\)
qs.a: Yes, it is a solution because it satisfies both equations.
d: No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the first equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies only the second equation.
No, it is not a solution because it satisfies neither equation.
qs.s: Substituting \(\left(\frac{1}{2}, -\frac{2}{3}\right)\) into the first equation gives \(\frac{2}{3}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) - \frac{3}{4}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{1}{3} + \frac{1}{2} = \frac{5}{6}\), and into the second equation gives \(\frac{4}{5}\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + \frac{9}{10}\left(-\frac{2}{3}\right) = \frac{2}{5} - \frac{3}{5} = -\frac{1}{5}\). Since both equations are true, the ordered pair is a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((-2, 5)\) is a solution to the linear system:
(1) \(5x = 3y - 23\)
(2) \(4x = -2y + 2\)
qs.s: Substituting \((-2, 5)\) into equation (1) gives \(5(-2) = 3(5) - 23\), or \(-10 = -8\) (false), while substituting into equation (2) gives \(4(-2) = -2(5) + 2\), or \(-8 = -8\) (true). Therefore, the ordered pair satisfies only equation (2).

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((-3, -4)\) is a solution to the linear system:
(1) \(2x = y - 2\)
(2) \(5x = 3y - 3\)
qs.s: Substituting \((-3, -4)\) into equation (1) gives \(2(-3) = -4 - 2\), which is \(-6 = -6\) (true), and into equation (2) gives \(5(-3) = 3(-4) - 3\), which is \(-15 = -15\) (true). Because both equations are satisfied, it is a solution to the system.

qs.q:
Determine whether the ordered pair \((4, -1)\) is a solution to the linear system:
(1) \(3x = 10 - 2y\)
