\(x - 3y = y + 11\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations in standard form as \(3x + 2y = 5\) and \(x - 4y = 11\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and adding gives \(7x = 21\), so \(x = 3\); substituting into \(3 - 4y = 11\) gives \(y = -2\), giving the solution \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 4\)
\(\frac{x}{6} - \frac{y}{4} = -1\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(2\) to get \(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = -2\), then add it to the first equation to obtain \(\frac{2x}{3} = 2\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 4\) gives \(1 + \frac{y}{2} = 4\), so \(y = 6\), giving the solution \((3, 6)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(3x + 2y = 6\)
\(x - 4y = 16\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to get \(6x + 4y = 12\), then add it to the second equation to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(7x = 28\), so \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(x - 4y = 16\) gives \(4 - 4y = 16\), which yields \(y = -3\), giving the solution \((4, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(2x + y = 8\)
\(x + y = 5\)
qs.s: Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(x + y = 5\) gives \(3 + y = 5\), so \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(2x - y = 7\)
\(x + y = 2\)
qs.s: Adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(3x = 9\), which means \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(x + y = 2\) gives \(3 + y = 2\), so \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(x - 3y = -1\)
\(x + y = 7\)
qs.s: Subtracting the first equation from the second eliminates \(x\) and yields \(4y = 8\), so \(y = 2\). Substituting \(y = 2\) into \(x + y = 7\) yields \(x = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(x + 2y = 8\)
\(3x - 2y = 0\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) and gives \(4x = 8\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(x + 2y = 8\) gives \(2 + 2y = 8\), so \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(3x + 4y = 10\)
\(2x - 3y = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4, then add them to get \(17x = 34\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(2x - 3y = 1\) gives \(4 - 3y = 1\), so \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(4x = 7 - 3y\)
\(5y = 17 - 6x\)
qs.s: Rearrange to \(4x + 3y = 7\) and \(6x + 5y = 17\), then multiply the first by 3 and the second by -2; adding gives \(-y = -13\), so \(y = 13\). Substituting \(y = 13\) into \(4x + 3(13) = 7\) gives \(4x = -32\), so \(x = -8\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(4x - 5y = 26\)
\(3x + 2y = 8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second equation by 5, then add to eliminate \(y\), giving \(23x = 92\), so \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(3x + 2y = 8\) gives \(12 + 2y = 8\), so \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{3} = 4\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{6} = 3\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 2 to get \(x - \frac{y}{3} = 6\), then add it to the first equation to get \(\frac{5}{4}x = 10\), giving \(x = 8\). Substituting \(x = 8\) into the first equation yields \(2 + \frac{y}{3} = 4\), so \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(5x = 3y + 19\)
\(2x + 5y = 20\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first equation as \(5x - 3y = 19\), then multiply it by 5 and the second equation by 3; adding them yields \(31x = 155\), so \(x = 5\). Substituting \(x = 5\) into \(2x + 5y = 20\) gives \(10 + 5y = 20\), so \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x - 3y = 18\)
\(4x + y = 10\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(-1\) and add to the first equation to get \(-4y = 8\), so \(y = -2\). Substituting \(y = -2\) into \(4x + y = 10\) yields \(4x = 12\), so \(x = 3\), giving the solution \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x - 3y = 5\)
\(-x - 3y = -7\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(-1\) and add to the first equation to get \(3x = 12\), so \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(2x - 3y = 5\) yields \(-3y = -3\), so \(y = 1\), giving the solution \((4, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(-5x + 2y = 20\)
\(5x + 3y = 5\)
qs.s: Add the equations directly to eliminate \(x\), yielding \(5y = 25\), which gives \(y = 5\). Substituting \(y = 5\) into \(5x + 3y = 5\) yields \(5x = -10\), so \(x = -2\), giving the solution \((-2, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 2y = 5\)
\(5x + 2y = 3\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(-1\) and add it to the second equation to get \(2x = -2\), so \(x = -1\). Substituting \(x = -1\) into \(3x + 2y = 5\) gives \(2y = 8\), so \(y = 4\), giving the solution \((-1, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x + 3y = -5\)
\(2x - y = 7\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(-1\) and add to the first to get \(4y = -12\), which gives \(y = -3\). Substituting \(y = -3\) into \(2x - y = 7\) yields \(2x = 4\), so \(x = 2\), giving the solution \((2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x - 3y = 23\)
\(3x + 4y = 8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(4\) and the second by \(3\), then add to get \(29x = 116\), which gives \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(3x + 4y = 8\) gives \(4y = -4\), so \(y = -1\), giving the solution \((4, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3(x + 2y) - y = -1\)
\(2(2x - y) + 3x = 25\)
qs.s: Simplify both equations to standard form: \(3x + 5y = -1\) and \(7x - 2y = 25\). Multiply the first by \(2\) and the second by \(5\), then add to get \(41x = 123\), so \(x = 3\); substituting into \(3x + 5y = -1\) gives \(y = -2\), giving \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x = 7 - 2y\)
\(5x - 4(y - 1) = -21\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations in standard form as \(3x + 2y = 7\) and \(5x - 4y = -25\). Multiplying the first by \(2\) and adding to the second gives \(11x = -11\), so \(x = -1\), and substituting into \(3x + 2y = 7\) yields \(y = 5\), giving \((-1, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 0\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{4} = 4\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the first equation by \(6\) and the second by \(4\) to obtain \(2x + 3y = 0\) and \(2x - y = 16\). Subtracting the equations gives \(4y = -16\), so \(y = -4\), and substituting into \(2x - y = 16\) gives \(x = 6\), giving \((6, -4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(7x - 4y = -1\)
\(5x - 6y = 15\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) and the second by \(-2\) to eliminate \(y\), which results in \(11x = -33\), so \(x = -3\). Substituting \(x = -3\) into \(7x - 4y = -1\) gives \(-4y = 20\), so \(y = -5\), giving \((-3, -5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle x = 4y\)
\(\displaystyle y = 2x - 7\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations as \(x - 4y = 0\) and \(-2x + y = -7\). Multiplying the second equation by \(4\) and adding gives \(-7x = -28\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = 1\), yielding \((4, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle y = 3x\)
\(\displaystyle x = -2y + 21\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations as \(-3x + y = 0\) and \(x + 2y = 21\). Multiplying the second equation by \(3\) and adding gives \(7y = 63\), so \(y = 9\) and \(x = 3\), resulting in \((3, 9)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle y = 2x\)
\(\displaystyle x = 4y - 21\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations as \(-2x + y = 0\) and \(x - 4y = -21\). Multiplying the second equation by \(2\) and adding gives \(-7y = -42\), so \(y = 6\) and \(x = 3\), giving \((3, 6)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle y = -4x\)
\(\displaystyle x = 2y + 18\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations as \(4x + y = 0\) and \(x - 2y = 18\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and adding gives \(9x = 18\), so \(x = 2\) and \(y = -8\), giving \((2, -8)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle x = -2y\)
\(\displaystyle y = 3x + 14\)
qs.s: Rewrite the system in standard form as \(x + 2y = 0\) and \(-3x + y = 14\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding gives \(7x = -28\), so \(x = -4\) and \(y = 2\), yielding \((-4, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 2(x - 3y) + x = 12\)
\(\displaystyle 3(2x + y) - 4y = 13\)
qs.s: Expand and simplify into \(3x - 6y = 12\) and \(6x - y = 13\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-2\) and adding to the second gives \(11y = -11\), so \(y = -1\) and \(x = 2\), giving \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 5x + 3y = y + 19\)
\(\displaystyle 4x - 2y = 3y + 2\)
qs.s: Combine like terms to get \(5x + 2y = 19\) and \(4x - 5y = 2\). Multiplying the first equation by \(5\) and the second by \(2\) and adding gives \(33x = 99\), so \(x = 3\) and \(y = 2\), yielding \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{4} = -\frac{y}{3}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(3x + 4y = 0\) and \(3x + y = 9\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-1\) and adding gives \(3y = -9\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = 4\), resulting in \((4, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 2(x - y) = x + 2y + 9\)
\(\displaystyle 3(x + y) = x + 7\)
qs.s: Expand and collect like terms to obtain \(x - 4y = 9\) and \(2x + 3y = 7\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-2\) and adding to the second yields \(11y = -11\), giving \(y = -1\) and \(x = 5\), or \((5, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 4x = 5y + 22\)
\(\displaystyle 2y = 5 - 3x\)
qs.s: Rearrange into standard form as \(4x - 5y = 22\) and \(3x + 2y = 5\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and the second by \(5\), then adding gives \(23x = 69\), which yields \(x = 3\) and \(y = -2\), or \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x - 10 = 4y\)
\(x - 3y + 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Rewrite the system as \(3x - 4y = 10\) and \(x - 3y = -5\). Multiply the second equation by \(-3\) and add it to the first to get \(5y = 25\), giving \(y = 5\) and \(x = -5 + 3(5) = 10\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x - 9 = 5y\)
\(x + 2y - 12 = 0\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations in standard form as \(4x - 5y = 9\) and \(x + 2y = 12\). Multiply the second equation by \(-4\) and add it to the first to get \(-13y = -39\), giving \(y = 3\), and substituting into \(x = 12 - 2y\) yields \(x = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x - 14 = 2y\)
\(2x - y - 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Rewrite the system as \(5x - 2y = 14\) and \(2x - y = 5\). Multiply the second equation by \(-2\) and add it to the first to find \(x = 4\), then substitute to get \(y = 2(4) - 5 = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x - 7 = 3y\)
\(3x + y - 5 = 0\)
qs.s: Rewrite the system as \(2x - 3y = 7\) and \(3x + y = 5\). Multiply the second equation by \(3\) and add it to the first to obtain \(11x = 22\), which gives \(x = 2\) and \(y = 5 - 3(2) = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x - 13 = 6y\)
\(x + 4y - 3 = 0\)
qs.s: Rewrite the system as \(2x - 6y = 13\) and \(x + 4y = 3\). Multiply the second equation by \(-2\) and add it to the first equation to obtain \(-14y = 7\), yielding \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3 - 4\left(-\frac{1}{2}\right) = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{2} - 4 = \frac{y}{3}\)
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{6} - 1 = 0\)
qs.s: Clear denominators to write the equations as \(3x - 2y = 24\) and \(3x + 2y = 12\). Adding the two equations directly gives \(6x = 36\), so \(x = 6\), and substituting into the second equation gives \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.4x - 1.1 = 0.3y\)
\(0.3x + 0.5y - 3 = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by \(10\) to clear decimals, resulting in \(4x - 3y = 11\) and \(3x + 5y = 30\). Multiply the first by \(5\) and the second by \(3\), then add to obtain \(29x = 145\), which gives \(x = 5\) and \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(6x - 12 = 5(3 - y)\)
\(8x + 3(2y - 5) + y = 20\)
qs.s: Simplify both equations to standard form to get \(6x + 5y = 27\) and \(8x + 7y = 35\). Multiply the first equation by \(4\) and the second by \(-3\), then add to get \(-y = 3\), giving \(y = -3\) and \(x = 7\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3(x - 1) + 5y = 4\)
\(5x - 4 = 2(y + 9)\)
qs.s: Expand and simplify into standard form as \(3x + 5y = 7\) and \(5x - 2y = 22\). Multiply the first equation by \(2\) and the second by \(5\), then add them to get \(31x = 124\), yielding \(x = 4\) and \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5(x - 1) - 3(y + 2) = -28\)
\(4(x + 2) + 7(y - 1) = 25\)
qs.s: Simplify each equation to standard form: \(5x - 3y = -17\) and \(4x + 7y = 24\). Multiply the first by \(4\) and the second by \(-5\), then add to get \(-47y = -188\), which gives \(y = 4\) and \(x = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(2x + 3y = 7\)
\(x - 2y = -7\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by -2 to get \(-2x + 4y = 14\), then add to the first equation to find \(7y = 21\), or \(y = 3\). Substituting \(y = 3\) into \(x - 2y = -7\) gives \(x = -1\), so the solution is \((-1, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(5x + 2y = -1\)
\(3x + y = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by -2 to get \(-6x - 2y = -2\), then add to the first equation to find \(-x = -3\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(3x + y = 1\) yields \(y = -8\), so the solution is \((3, -8)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(4x + y = 5\)
\(3x - 2y = 12\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 to get \(8x + 2y = 10\), then add to the second equation to obtain \(11x = 22\), which gives \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(4x + y = 5\) yields \(y = -3\), so the solution is \((2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(x + 4y = 14\)
\(3x - 2y = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 2 to get \(6x - 4y = 0\), then add to the first equation to find \(7x = 14\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(x + 4y = 14\) gives \(y = 3\), so the solution is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x + y = -1\)
\(2x + 3y = 11\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by -3 to get \(-9x - 3y = 3\), then add to the second equation to obtain \(-7x = 14\), which gives \(x = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) into \(3x + y = -1\) yields \(y = 5\), so the solution is \((-2, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{6} = \frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the equations by 6 and 12 to get \(3x + 2y = 6\) and \(3x - 2y = 18\), then add them to obtain \(6x = 24\), so \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(3x + 2y = 6\) gives \(y = -3\), so the solution is \((4, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(8x - 5y + 14 = 0\)
\(6x = 7y - 4\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations as \(8x - 5y = -14\) and \(6x - 7y = -4\), then multiply by 3 and -4 respectively to eliminate \(x\), giving \(13y = -26\) and \(y = -2\). Substituting \(y = -2\) into \(8x - 5y = -14\) yields \(x = -3\), so the solution is \((-3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(6x + 5y = 11\)
\(9x + 4y = -8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by -2 to get \(18x + 15y = 33\) and \(-18x - 8y = 16\), then add to find \(7y = 49\), so \(y = 7\). Substituting \(y = 7\) into \(6x + 5y = 11\) gives \(x = -4\), so the solution is \((-4, 7)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(7x = 3y + 29\)
\(4y = -5x - 10\)
qs.s: Rewrite both equations in standard form as \(7x - 3y = 29\) and \(5x + 4y = -10\), then multiply by 4 and 3 respectively to eliminate \(y\), giving \(43x = 86\) and \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) gives \(y = -5\), so the solution is \((2, -5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(4x - 7y = 31\)
\(5x + 3y = 27\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 7 to get \(12x - 21y = 93\) and \(35x + 21y = 189\), then add to find \(47x = 282\), so \(x = 6\). Substituting \(x = 6\) into \(5x + 3y = 27\) yields \(y = -1\), giving the solution \((6, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(2x + 5y = 0\)
\(3x + 4y = 7\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by -2 to eliminate \(x\), resulting in \(7y = -14\), so \(y = -2\). Substituting \(y = -2\) into \(2x + 5y = 0\) gives \(2x = 10\), so \(x = 5\), giving \((5, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x + 4y = 1\)
\(2x + 3y = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by -4 to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(2x + 3y = 0\) gives \(3y = -6\), so \(y = -2\), giving the solution \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(4x - 3y = -9\)
\(3x - 5y = -4\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by -4 to eliminate \(x\), giving \(11y = -11\), so \(y = -1\). Substituting \(y = -1\) into \(4x - 3y = -9\) gives \(4x = -12\), so \(x = -3\), yielding \((-3, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x + 5y = 21\)
\(4x + 3y = 17\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by -5 to eliminate \(y\), giving \(-11x = -22\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(3x + 5y = 21\) gives \(5y = 15\), so \(y = 3\), giving \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(5x + 3y = 7\)
\(2x + 5y = 18\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by -3 to eliminate \(y\), resulting in \(19x = -19\), so \(x = -1\). Substituting \(x = -1\) into \(2x + 5y = 18\) gives \(5y = 20\), so \(y = 4\), yielding \((-1, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(0.4x + 0.3y = 0\)
\(0.5x - 0.2y = 2.3\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 10 to clear decimals, giving \(4x + 3y = 0\) and \(5x - 2y = 23\). Multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3 to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(23x = 69\) (\(x = 3\)), and substituting gives \(y = -4\), so the solution is \((3, -4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(4x - 7 = 5y + 12\)
\(3x = 2y + 16\)
qs.s: Rearrange into standard form as \(4x - 5y = 19\) and \(3x - 2y = 16\). Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by -5 to eliminate \(y\), giving \(-7x = -42\) (\(x = 6\)), and substituting \(x = 6\) gives \(y = 1\), giving \((6, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(7x + 9y = 22\)
\(8x + 5y = 41\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by -5 and the second by 9 to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(37x = 259\), which gives \(x = 7\). Substituting \(x = 7\) into \(7x + 9y = 22\) yields \(9y = -27\), so \(y = -3\), giving the solution \((7, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = \frac{17}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 6 to clear denominators, giving \(3x + 2y = 6\) and \(2x - 3y = 17\). Multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2 to eliminate \(y\), giving \(13x = 52\) (\(x = 4\)), which yields \(y = -3\) upon substitution, so the solution is \((4, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(2(x + 3y) - y = 21\)
\(3(2x - y) + 4x = -35\)
qs.s: Simplify both equations to \(2x + 5y = 21\) and \(10x - 3y = -35\). Multiply the first equation by -5 and add to the second equation to get \(-28y = -140\) (\(y = 5\)), then substitute \(y = 5\) to find \(x = -2\), yielding \((-2, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(5x - 4y = -11\)
\(2x + 7y = -13\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 7 and the second equation by 4 to get \(35x - 28y = -77\) and \(8x + 28y = -52\). Adding yields \(43x = -129\), which gives \(x = -3\), and substituting into \(2x + 7y = -13\) yields \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x + 4y = 4\)
\(7x - 3y = 34\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second equation by 4 to get \(9x + 12y = 12\) and \(28x - 12y = 136\). Adding gives \(37x = 148\), so \(x = 4\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x - 4y = -6\)
\(5x + 3y = 19\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second equation by 4 to get \(9x - 12y = -18\) and \(20x + 12y = 76\). Adding gives \(29x = 58\), so \(x = 2\), and substituting into \(5x + 3y = 19\) results in \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(4x + 3y = 8\)
\(5x - 2y = -13\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second equation by 3 to get \(8x + 6y = 16\) and \(15x - 6y = -39\). Adding gives \(23x = -23\), so \(x = -1\), and substituting into \(4x + 3y = 8\) yields \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(2x - 5y = 16\)
\(3x + 2y = 5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second equation by 5 to obtain \(4x - 10y = 32\) and \(15x + 10y = 25\). Adding the equations yields \(19x = 57\), giving \(x = 3\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(3x - 2(y + 1) = 16\)
\(4(x - 1) + 3y = 3\)
qs.s: Simplify to general form to get \(3x - 2y = 18\) and \(4x + 3y = 7\). Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2, then add to get \(17x = 68\), giving \(x = 4\) and \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(11x - 7y = 41\)
\(8x + 5y = 50\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by 7 to get \(55x - 35y = 205\) and \(56x + 35y = 350\). Adding gives \(111x = 555\), so \(x = 5\), and substituting into the second equation gives \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{3} = \frac{1}{6}\)
\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = \frac{7}{6}\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the equations by 12 and 6 respectively to get \(3x + 4y = 2\) and \(2x - 3y = 7\). Multiplying these by 3 and 4 and adding gives \(17x = 34\), so \(x = 2\) and \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(5x + y = 3x - 2y + 6\)
\(7x + 2(y - 1) = 2x - 2y - 1\)
qs.s: Rearrange into standard form as \(2x + 3y = 6\) and \(5x + 4y = 1\). Multiply the first equation by 4 and the second by \(-3\) to get \(8x + 12y = 24\) and \(-15x - 12y = -3\), which add to \(-7x = 21\), yielding \(x = -3\) and \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:

\(6x + 5y = -7\)
\(4x - 3y = 8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 to obtain \(18x + 15y = -21\) and \(20x - 15y = 40\). Adding results in \(38x = 19\), giving \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), and substituting into \(4x - 3y = 8\) yields \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 4y = 6\)
\(4x + 3y = 1\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by -4 gives \(9x + 12y = 18\) and \(-16x - 12y = -4\), which add to \(-7x = 14\), yielding \(x = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) into \(3x + 4y = 6\) gives \(-6 + 4y = 6\), so \(y = 3\), giving the solution \((-2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x + 3y = 3\)
\(5x + 4y = 11\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 4 and the second by -3 gives \(8x + 12y = 12\) and \(-15x - 12y = -33\), which add to \(-7x = -21\), yielding \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(2x + 3y = 3\) gives \(6 + 3y = 3\), so \(y = -1\), giving the solution \((3, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x - 5y = 7\)
\(2x + 3y = 11\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 gives \(9x - 15y = 21\) and \(10x + 15y = 55\), which add to \(19x = 76\), yielding \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(2x + 3y = 11\) gives \(8 + 3y = 11\), so \(y = 1\), giving the solution \((4, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 2y = 16\)
\(5x - 3y = -5\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by 2 gives \(9x + 6y = 48\) and \(10x - 6y = -10\), which add to \(19x = 38\), yielding \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(3x + 2y = 16\) gives \(6 + 2y = 16\), so \(y = 5\), giving the solution \((2, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x - 3y = 2\)
\(5x - 2y = -1\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by -2 and the second by 3 gives \(-8x + 6y = -4\) and \(15x - 6y = -3\), which add to \(7x = -7\), yielding \(x = -1\). Substituting \(x = -1\) into \(4x - 3y = 2\) gives \(-4 - 3y = 2\), so \(y = -2\), giving the solution \((-1, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{4} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{3} = \frac{13}{3}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the equations by 12 and 6 clears the denominators to give \(4x + 3y = 12\) and \(3x - 2y = 26\). Multiplying these by 2 and 3 gives \(8x + 6y = 24\) and \(9x - 6y = 78\), which add to \(17x = 102\), so \(x = 6\) and \(y = -4\), giving \((6, -4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3(x - 1) + 4y = -2\)
\(5x - 3(y + 2) = 15\)
qs.s: Expanding both equations gives \(3x + 4y = 1\) and \(5x - 3y = 21\); multiplying them by 3 and 4 gives \(9x + 12y = 3\) and \(20x - 12y = 84\), which add to \(29x = 87\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(3x + 4y = 1\) gives \(9 + 4y = 1\), so \(y = -2\), yielding \((3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(7x + 9y = 21\)
\(8x + 5y = 61\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 5 and the second by -9 gives \(35x + 45y = 105\) and \(-72x - 45y = -549\), which add to \(-37x = -444\), yielding \(x = 12\). Substituting \(x = 12\) into \(7x + 9y = 21\) gives \(84 + 9y = 21\), so \(y = -7\), giving \((12, -7)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x + 12 = 3y - 18\)
\(4x = 13 - 5y\)
qs.s: Rewriting in standard form gives \(5x - 3y = -30\) and \(4x + 5y = 13\). Multiplying by 5 and 3 yields \(25x - 15y = -150\) and \(12x + 15y = 39\), which add to \(37x = -111\), giving \(x = -3\) and \(y = 5\), or \((-3, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.4x + 0.3y = 1.8\)
\(0.3x + 0.5y = 1.9\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 10 gives \(4x + 3y = 18\) and \(3x + 5y = 19\), and multiplying these by 5 and -3 gives \(20x + 15y = 90\) and \(-9x - 15y = -57\). Adding yields \(11x = 33\), so \(x = 3\), and substituting into \(4x + 3y = 18\) gives \(y = 2\), resulting in \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 4y = 13.5\)
\(4x - 3y = -7\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(9x + 12y = 40.5\) and \(16x - 12y = -28\). Adding them gives \(25x = 12.5\), so \(x = 0.5\), and substituting into \(4(0.5) - 3y = -7\) gives \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x + 3y = 3.5\)
\(3x - 2y = -8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3 to get \(8x + 6y = 7\) and \(9x - 6y = -24\). Adding gives \(17x = -17\), so \(x = -1\), and substituting into \(4(-1) + 3y = 3.5\) gives \(y = 2.5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 5y = 5.5\)
\(4x - 3y = -12\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 to get \(9x + 15y = 16.5\) and \(20x - 15y = -60\). Adding gives \(29x = -43.5\), so \(x = -1.5\), and substituting into \(3(-1.5) + 5y = 5.5\) gives \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x - 4y = 3.5\)
\(2x + 3y = 8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(9x - 12y = 10.5\) and \(8x + 12y = 32\). Adding gives \(17x = 42.5\), so \(x = 2.5\), and substituting into \(2(2.5) + 3y = 8\) gives \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x + 2y = 4\)
\(3x - 5y = 5.5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by 2 to get \(25x + 10y = 20\) and \(6x - 10y = 11\). Adding gives \(31x = 31\), so \(x = 1\), and substituting into \(5(1) + 2y = 4\) gives \(y = -0.5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{2x}{3} - \frac{3y}{4} = \frac{59}{12}\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(3x + 2y = 6\) and \(8x - 9y = 59\). Multiplying the first by 9 and the second by 2 then adding results in \(43x = 172\), giving \(x = 4\) and \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3(x - 1) - 2(y + 2) = 1\)
\(2(2x + y) + x + y = 26\)
qs.s: Simplifying both equations gives \(3x - 2y = 8\) and \(5x + 3y = 26\). Multiplying the first by 3 and the second by 2 then adding yields \(19x = 76\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(6x - 5 = 2x + 3y + 14\)
\(5x + 2y = 2x - 3y + 7\)
qs.s: Rearranging terms into general form gives \(4x - 3y = 19\) and \(3x + 5y = 7\). Multiplying the first by 5 and the second by 3 then adding yields \(29x = 116\), which gives \(x = 4\) and \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(8x - 5y = 71\)
\(6x + 7y = 21\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 7 and the second by 5 to obtain \(56x - 35y = 497\) and \(30x + 35y = 105\). Adding gives \(86x = 602\), so \(x = 7\), and substituting into \(6(7) + 7y = 21\) gives \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.3(x - y) + 0.2x = 0.9\)
\(0.2(2x + y) + 0.3y = 2.2\)
qs.s: Expanding and clearing decimals produces \(5x - 3y = 9\) and \(4x + 5y = 22\). Multiplying the first by 5 and the second by 3 then adding gives \(37x = 111\), yielding \(x = 3\) and \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x - 5y = 4\)
\(-4x + 10y = -4\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to get \(4x - 10y = 8\). Adding this to \(-4x + 10y = -4\) gives \(0 = 4\), which is a false statement, so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x + 2y = 6\)
\(-15x - 6y = -6\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to get \(15x + 6y = 18\). Adding this to \(-15x - 6y = -6\) gives \(0 = 12\), a contradiction, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x - 2y = 3\)
\(-8x + 4y = -3\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to obtain \(8x - 4y = 6\). Adding this to \(-8x + 4y = -3\) gives \(0 = 3\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(-6x + 8y = 7\)
\(3x - 4y = -7\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(2\) to get \(6x - 8y = -14\). Adding this to \(-6x + 8y = 7\) results in \(0 = -7\), an impossible statement, meaning there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(x + 3y = 5\)
\(-3x - 9y = -5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to obtain \(3x + 9y = 15\). Adding this to \(-3x - 9y = -5\) yields \(0 = 10\), which is false, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x = 6y + 7\)
\(9y - 6x = -7\)
qs.s: Rewrite the equations in standard form as \(4x - 6y = 7\) and \(-6x + 9y = -7\). Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) and the second by \(2\) gives \(12x - 18y = 21\) and \(-12x + 18y = -14\), which add to \(0 = 7\), meaning there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(6x - 4y = 5\)
\(-9x + 6y = -5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to get \(18x - 12y = 15\) and the second by \(2\) to get \(-18x + 12y = -10\). Adding the two equations results in \(0 = 5\), so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{4} = 3\)
\(-\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{8} = 1\)
qs.s: Clear fractions by multiplying the first equation by \(4\) to get \(2x - y = 12\) and the second by \(8\) to get \(-2x + y = 8\). Adding the equations yields \(0 = 20\), which is false, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(12x - 15y = 14\)
\(-16x + 20y = -15\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(4\) to get \(48x - 60y = 56\) and the second by \(3\) to get \(-48x + 60y = -45\). Adding the equations gives \(0 = 11\), a false statement, so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2(3x - 2y) + 2y = 8\)
\(3(y - 2x) - y = -5\)
qs.s: Simplifying each equation gives \(6x - 2y = 8\) and \(-6x + 2y = -5\). Adding these eliminates both variables and leaves \(0 = 3\), so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(-x + 4y = 7\)
\(3x - 12y = -21\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to get \(-3x + 12y = 21\). Adding this to \(3x - 12y = -21\) yields \(0 = 0\), so the system has infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(2x - 5y = 10\)
\(-4x + 10y = -20\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to obtain \(4x - 10y = 20\). Adding this to \(-4x + 10y = -20\) results in \(0 = 0\), which indicates the system has infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(5x - 2y = 8\)
\(-10x + 4y = -16\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to get \(10x - 4y = 16\). Adding this to \(-10x + 4y = -16\) results in \(0 = 0\), so there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3x + 5y = 15\)
\(-6x - 10y = -30\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to get $6x + 10y = 30. Adding this to \(-6x - 10y = -30\) yields \(0 = 0\), which means there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(4x + 3y = -12\)
\(-8x - 6y = 24\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to obtain \(8x + 6y = -24\). Adding this to \(-8x - 6y = 24\) gives \(0 = 0\), meaning the lines coincide and there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(12x - 15y = 33\)
\(-20x + 25y = -55\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(5\) to obtain \(60x - 75y = 165\) and the second equation by \(3\) to obtain \(-60x + 75y = -165\). Adding the resulting equations gives \(0 = 0\), so there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(7x = 4y + 14\)
\(8y - 14x = -28\)
qs.s: Rearrange both equations into standard form to get \(7x - 4y = 14\) and \(-14x + 8y = -28\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and adding gives \(0 = 0\), indicating infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(6x - 8y = 20\)
\(-9x + 12y = -30\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(3\) to get \(18x - 24y = 60\) and the second equation by \(2\) to get \(-18x + 24y = -60\). Adding the two equations produces \(0 = 0\), so there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{6} = \frac{1}{2}\)
\(-\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = -1\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the first equation by \(12\) to get \(3x - 2y = 6\) and the second by \(6\) to get \(-3x + 2y = -6\). Adding the equations yields \(0 = 0\), so the system has infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(3(x + y) + x - 2y = 9\)
\(-2(3x + y) - 2x = -18\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms yields \(4x + y = 9\) and \(-8x - 2y = -18\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) and adding it to the second yields \(0 = 0\), so there are infinite solutions.

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{4} = \frac{7}{2}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 to get \(x + \frac{y}{2} = 7\), then add it to the second equation to get \(\frac{4x}{3} = 8\), so \(x = 6\). Substituting \(x = 6\) into the second equation gives \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{6} + \frac{y}{8} = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(-2\) to get \(-\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{4} = 0\), then add it to the first equation to find \(\frac{y}{4} = 1\), giving \(y = 4\). Substituting \(y = 4\) into the second equation yields \(x = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{8} - \frac{y}{4} = \frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 2 to get \(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{2} = 3\), then add it to the first equation to obtain \(\frac{x}{2} = 4\), so \(x = 8\). Substituting \(x = 8\) into the first equation results in \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = \frac{4}{3}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{2} = 2\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 6 gives \(3x + 2y = 8\), and multiplying the second equation by 4 gives \(x - 2y = 8\). Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(4x = 16\), which yields \(x = 4\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x}{5} + \frac{2y}{3} = \frac{8}{5}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{5x}{6} - \frac{y}{4} = -\frac{29}{6}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions gives \(9x + 10y = 24\) and \(10x - 3y = -58\). Multiplying these equations by 3 and 10 and adding produces \(127x = -508\), so \(x = -4\), and substituting yields \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 2}{3} - \frac{y - 1}{2} = 2\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x - 3}{4} + \frac{y + 1}{2} = 3\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions and simplifying gives \(2x - 3y = 5\) and \(x + 2y = 13\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding eliminates \(x\) to yield \(-7y = -21\), so \(y = 3\), which gives \(x = 7\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x}{4} + \frac{3y}{8} = \frac{1}{8}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} - \frac{9y}{4} = \frac{7}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the equations by 8 and 4 gives \(6x + 3y = 1\) and \(2x - 9y = 7\). Multiplying the first equation by 3 and adding it to the second gives \(20x = 10\), so \(x = \frac{1}{2}\), and substituting gives \(y = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x}{3} - \frac{3y}{4} = \frac{11}{2}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x}{2} + \frac{5y}{6} = \frac{22}{3}\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(8x - 9y = 66\) and \(9x + 5y = 44\). Multiplying these equations by 5 and 9 respectively and adding yields \(121x = 726\), which gives \(x = 6\) and subsequently \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x - 1}{3} - \frac{y + 2}{4} = 2\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 3}{2} + \frac{2y - 1}{3} = 5\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators and combining like terms yields \(8x - 3y = 34\) and \(3x + 4y = 23\). Multiplying these by 4 and 3 respectively and adding gives \(41x = 205\), so \(x = 5\), which leads to \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{5}{x} - \frac{2}{y} = \frac{11}{6}\)
\(\frac{3}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = \frac{17}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 2 and adding it to the second eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{13}{x} = \frac{13}{2}\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the second equation gives \(\frac{3}{2} + \frac{4}{y} = \frac{17}{6}\), which yields \(y = 3\), so the solution is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{4}{x} - \frac{3}{y} = \frac{7}{12}\)
\(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = \frac{23}{12}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding it to the first eliminates \(x\) to give \(-\frac{13}{y} = -\frac{13}{4}\), so \(y = 4\). Substituting \(y = 4\) into the first equation gives \(\frac{4}{x} - \frac{3}{4} = \frac{7}{12}\), which yields \(x = 3\), so the solution is \((3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{3}{x} + \frac{6}{y} = \frac{1}{2}\)
\(\frac{5}{x} - \frac{4}{y} = -\frac{23}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 2 and the second by 3, then adding them eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{21}{x} = -\frac{21}{2}\), so \(x = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) into the first equation gives \(-\frac{3}{2} + \frac{6}{y} = \frac{1}{2}\), which yields \(y = 3\), so the solution is \((-2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = 1\)
\(\frac{3}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = \frac{7}{4}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by \(-2\), then adding eliminates \(x\) to give \(-\frac{1}{y} = -\frac{1}{2}\), so \(y = 2\). Substituting \(y = 2\) into the first equation yields \(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{2} = 1\), giving \(x = -4\), so the solution is \((-4, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{4}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = -1\)
\(\frac{3}{x} - \frac{2}{y} = \frac{7}{2}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 2 and the second by 3, then adding them eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{17}{x} = \frac{17}{2}\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(\frac{4}{2} + \frac{3}{y} = -1\), which gives \(y = -1\), so the solution is \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{6}{x} + \frac{1}{y} = \frac{2}{x} - \frac{2}{y} + 1\)
\(\frac{5}{x} - \frac{5}{y} = \frac{3}{x} - \frac{2}{y} + 2\)
qs.s: Collecting like terms gives \(\frac{4}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = 1\) and \(\frac{2}{x} - \frac{3}{y} = 2\); adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{6}{x} = 3\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the second simplified equation gives \(1 - \frac{3}{y} = 2\), which yields \(y = -3\), so the solution is \((2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{7}{x} + \frac{6}{y} = \frac{4}{5}\)
\(\frac{5}{x} - \frac{9}{y} = 5\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by 2, then adding eliminates \(y\) to yield \(\frac{31}{x} = \frac{62}{5}\), so \(\frac{1}{x} = \frac{2}{5}\) and \(x = \frac{5}{2}\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(5\left(\frac{2}{5}\right) - \frac{9}{y} = 5\), which gives \(-\frac{9}{y} = 3\), so \(y = -3\), resulting in the solution \((5/2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{2}{x} = 1 - \frac{4}{y}\)
\(\frac{4}{x} - 9 = \frac{6}{y}\)
qs.s: Rewriting in general form gives \(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 1\) and \(\frac{4}{x} - \frac{6}{y} = 9\); multiplying the first by \(-2\) and adding eliminates \(x\) to yield \(-\frac{14}{y} = 7\), so \(y = -2\). Substituting \(y = -2\) into the first equation gives \(\frac{2}{x} - 2 = 1\), which leads to \(\frac{2}{x} = 3\) and \(x = \frac{2}{3}\), so the solution is \((2/3, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{5}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = -\frac{14}{3}\)
\(\frac{2}{x} - \frac{9}{y} = -\frac{26}{3}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 3 and adding it to the second eliminates \(y\) to give \(\frac{17}{x} = -\frac{68}{3}\), so \(\frac{1}{x} = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(x = -\frac{3}{4}\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(5\left(-\frac{4}{3}\right) + \frac{3}{y} = -\frac{14}{3}\), yielding \(\frac{3}{y} = 2\), so \(y = \frac{3}{2}\), giving the solution \((-3/4, 3/2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system by the addition method:
\(\frac{6}{x} + \frac{8}{y} - 1 = 0\)
\(\frac{4}{x} = \frac{12}{y} - 21\)
qs.s: Rearranging gives \(\frac{6}{x} + \frac{8}{y} = 1\) and \(\frac{4}{x} - \frac{12}{y} = -21\); multiplying the first by 2 and the second by \(-3\) and adding eliminates \(x\) to give \(\frac{52}{y} = 65\), so \(y = \frac{4}{5}\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(\frac{6}{x} + 10 = 1\), so \(\frac{6}{x} = -9\), which yields \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\), giving the solution \((-2/3, 4/5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = 3\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{6}{x} - \frac{9}{y} = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 to get \(\frac{12}{x} + \frac{9}{y} = 9\), then add the second equation to get \(\frac{18}{x} = 9\), which gives \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(\frac{4}{2} + \frac{3}{y} = 3\), which simplifies to \(y = 3\), so the solution is \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{x} + \frac{2}{y} = -1\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{6}{x} - \frac{5}{y} = 7\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(-2\) to get \(-\frac{6}{x} - \frac{4}{y} = 2\), then add the second equation to obtain \(-\frac{9}{y} = 9\), so \(y = -1\). Substituting \(y = -1\) into the first equation gives \(\frac{3}{x} - 2 = -1\), which solves to \(x = 3\), giving \((3, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 2\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{x} - \frac{2}{y} = 2\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 2 to get \(\frac{10}{x} - \frac{4}{y} = 4\), then add the first equation to find \(\frac{12}{x} = 6\), giving \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation yields \(1 + \frac{4}{y} = 2\), giving \(y = 4\), so the solution is \((2, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 1\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{6}{x} - \frac{2}{y} = -3\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 2 to get \(\frac{12}{x} - \frac{4}{y} = -6\), then add the first equation to find \(\frac{15}{x} = -5\), which gives \(x = -3\). Substituting \(x = -3\) into the first equation gives \(-1 + \frac{4}{y} = 1\), which solves to \(y = 2\), giving \((-3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = 3\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{x} - \frac{6}{y} = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 to obtain \(\frac{4}{x} + \frac{6}{y} = 6\), then add the second equation to get \(\frac{7}{x} = 7\), so \(x = 1\). Substituting \(x = 1\) into the first equation gives \(2 + \frac{3}{y} = 3\), which results in \(y = 3\), giving \((1, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = 7\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = -1\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by \(-4\) to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(\frac{13}{x} = 39\), so \(\frac{1}{x} = 3\) and \(x = \frac{1}{3}\). Substituting \(\frac{1}{x} = 3\) into the second equation yields \(9 + \frac{5}{y} = -1\), which gives \(\frac{1}{y} = -2\) and \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\), so the solution is \((\frac{1}{3}, -\frac{1}{2})\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{x} - \frac{3}{y} = 1 - \frac{3}{x}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{x} + \frac{2}{y} = 3 - \frac{4}{y}\)
qs.s: Combine like terms to rewrite the equations in standard form as \(\frac{8}{x} - \frac{3}{y} = 1\) and \(\frac{4}{x} + \frac{6}{y} = 3\). Multiply the first equation by 2 and add to the second to get \(\frac{20}{x} = 5\), giving \(x = 4\); substituting \(x = 4\) into the second equation gives \(1 + \frac{6}{y} = 3\), so \(y = 3\), yielding \((4, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{y} - 1 = 0\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{x} - \frac{6}{y} = -14\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first equation as \(\frac{2}{x} + \frac{3}{y} = 1\), multiply it by 2, and add it to the second equation to get \(\frac{8}{x} = -12\), giving \(\frac{1}{x} = -\frac{3}{2}\) and \(x = -\frac{2}{3}\). Substituting \(\frac{1}{x} = -\frac{3}{2}\) into the first equation gives \(-3 + \frac{3}{y} = 1\), so \(\frac{1}{y} = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(y = \frac{3}{4}\), yielding \((-\frac{2}{3}, \frac{3}{4})\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{x} + \frac{4}{y} = \frac{1}{6}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{x} + \frac{6}{y} = \frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by \(-2\) to eliminate \(y\), giving \(-\frac{1}{x} = -\frac{1}{2}\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into the first equation gives \(\frac{3}{2} + \frac{4}{y} = \frac{1}{6}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{4}{y} = -\frac{4}{3}\) and \(y = -3\), yielding \((2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{7}{x} = \frac{3}{y} + 11\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{4}{x} + \frac{5}{y} = 13\)
qs.s: Rewrite the first equation as \(\frac{7}{x} - \frac{3}{y} = 11\), then multiply it by 5 and the second equation by 3 to add and obtain \(\frac{47}{x} = 94\), giving \(x = \frac{1}{2}\). Substituting \(\frac{1}{x} = 2\) into the second equation gives \(8 + \frac{5}{y} = 13\), which yields \(y = 1\), giving \((\frac{1}{2}, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.3x + 0.02y = 1.26\)
\(0.2x + 0.07y = 1.01\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 100 yields \(30x + 2y = 126\) and \(20x + 7y = 101\). Multiplying the first equation by 2 and the second by \(-3\), then adding, gives \(-17y = -51\), so \(y = 3\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.5x + 0.04y = 0.74\)
\(0.2x + 0.03y = 0.38\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 100 gives \(50x + 4y = 74\) and \(20x + 3y = 38\). Multiplying the first by 3 and the second by \(-4\), then adding, gives \(70x = 70\), which gives \(x = 1\) and \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.1x - 0.03y = 0.74\)
\(0.3x + 0.04y = 2.48\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 100 gives \(10x - 3y = 74\) and \(30x + 4y = 248\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) and adding gives \(13y = 26\), so \(y = 2\) and substituting gives \(x = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.2x + 0.03y = 1.06\)
\(0.1x - 0.04y = 0.42\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 100 gives \(20x + 3y = 106\) and \(10x - 4y = 42\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding gives \(11y = 22\), which yields \(y = 2\) and \(x = 5\) upon substitution.

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.04x + 0.1y = 0.78\)
\(0.03x + 0.2y = 1.46\)
qs.s: Multiplying both equations by 100 gives \(4x + 10y = 78\) and \(3x + 20y = 146\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-2\) and adding gives \(-5x = -10\), which results in \(x = 2\) and \(y = 7\).

Expanding and clearing decimals gives \(7x + 4y = 64\) and \(5x + 6y = 8\). Multiplying the first equation by 3 and the second by \(-2\), then adding, gives \(11x = 176\), so \(x = 16\) and substituting gives \(y = -12\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.006x + 0.015y = 0.21\)
\(0.008x - 0.025y = -0.08\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 1000 to clear decimals, producing \(6x + 15y = 210\) and \(8x - 25y = -80\). Dividing the first equation by 3 gives \(2x + 5y = 70\); multiplying this by 5 and adding to the second gives \(18x = 270\), so \(x = 15\) and \(y = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.2(x + y) + 0.05x = 1.15\)
\(0.1(x - y) - 0.04y = 1.12\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms gives \(0.25x + 0.2y = 1.15\) and \(0.1x - 0.14y = 1.12\), which simplify to \(5x + 4y = 23\) and \(5x - 7y = 56\) after clearing decimals and dividing. Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(11y = -33\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = 7\).

Expanding and rearranging gives \(0.04x - 0.03y = 0.33\) and \(0.02x + 0.05y = 0.49\), or \(4x - 3y = 33\) and \(2x + 5y = 49\) after multiplying by 100. Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding yields \(-13y = -65\), so \(y = 5\) and \(x = 12\).

qs.q:
Solve by the addition method:
\(0.08x = 0.58 - 0.06y\)
\(0.15x + 0.9 = 0.02y\)
qs.s: Rearranging to standard form and multiplying by 100 gives \(8x + 6y = 58\) and \(15x - 2y = -90\). Multiplying the second equation by 3 and adding eliminates \(y\) to yield \(53x = -212\), so \(x = -4\) and \(y = 15\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 0.2x + \frac{y}{5} = 0.4\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{3} - 0.4y = -3\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(x + y = 2\) and \(5x - 6y = -45\); multiplying the first by 6 and adding to the second gives \(11x = -33\), so \(x = -3\) and \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{4} + 0.3y = 0.4\)
\(\displaystyle 0.05x - \frac{y}{5} = 0.6\)
qs.s: Multiplying the equations by 20 gives \(5x + 6y = 8\) and \(x - 4y = 12\); multiplying the second equation by \(-5\) and adding to the first gives \(26y = -52\), so \(y = -2\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 0.04x + \frac{y}{4} = -0.6\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} - 0.3y = 6.2\)
qs.s: Clearing decimals and fractions gives \(4x + 25y = -60\) and \(5x - 3y = 62\); multiplying by 5 and \(-4\) respectively and adding yields \(137y = -548\), giving \(y = -4\) and \(x = 10\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{2} + 0.1y = 1.6\)
\(\displaystyle 0.05x - \frac{y}{3} = -1.9\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 10 yields \(5x + y = 16\) and the second by 60 yields \(3x - 20y = -114\); multiplying the first by 20 and adding eliminates \(y\) to give \(103x = 206\), yielding \(x = 2\) and \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 0.3x - \frac{y}{2} = -0.5\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x}{5} + 0.08y = -1.16\)
qs.s: Clearing decimals and fractions gives \(3x - 5y = -5\) and \(5x + 2y = -29\); multiplying by 2 and 5 respectively and adding yields \(31x = -155\), so \(x = -5\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x + y}{5} - 0.3(x - 2y) = -2\)
\(\displaystyle 0.25(3x + y) + \frac{x - y}{7} = 0.5x + 1.25\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators and combining like terms yields \(x + 8y = -20\) and \(11x + 3y = 35\); multiplying the first by \(-11\) and adding gives \(-85y = 255\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x - y + 1}{5} + 0.4(x + y) = 0.2x - 0.8\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 2y - 1}{2} - 0.25(3x - y) = 0.5y + 5.5\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators and rearranging into standard form produces \(4x + y = -5\) and \(-x + 3y = 24\); multiplying the second equation by 4 and adding gives \(13y = 91\), which yields \(y = 7\) and \(x = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 3y}{7} - 0.2(2x - y) = 2.4\)
\(\displaystyle 0.5(x + y) + \frac{3x + 2y}{4} = 0.25x + 1\)
qs.s: Simplifying each equation yields \(-9x + 22y = 84\) and \(x + y = 1\); multiplying the second equation by 9 and adding yields \(31y = 93\), which gives \(y = 3\) and \(x = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 2y}{3} - 0.25(x + 8) = 1.5y - 9\)
\(\displaystyle 0.2(2x - y) + \frac{3x + y}{2} = 0.1(x - y) - 4\)
qs.s: Simplifying each equation into standard form gives \(x - 10y = -84\) and \(9x + 2y = -20\); multiplying the second equation by 5 and adding to the first gives \(46x = -184\), so \(x = -4\) and \(y = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations by the addition method:
\(\displaystyle 0.3(x - 2) + \frac{y + 6}{4} = 0.1x + 1.6\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x - y}{7} - 0.5(y + 4) = 0.2x - 0.2\)
qs.s: Expanding and clearing denominators simplifies the equations to \(4x + 5y = 14\) and \(2x - 15y = 42\); multiplying the first by 3 and adding eliminates \(y\) to give \(14x = 84\), so \(x = 6\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{4} = \frac{5}{4}\)
\(\frac{x}{6} - \frac{y}{3} = \frac{1}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 12 gives \(4x + 3y = 15\), and multiplying the second by 6 gives \(x - 2y = 1\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-4\) and adding to the first gives \(11y = 11\), so \(y = 1\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{6} = -\frac{1}{6}\)
\(\frac{x}{5} - \frac{y}{2} = \frac{17}{10}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions by multiplying the equations by 6 and 10 gives \(2x + y = -1\) and \(2x - 5y = 17\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-1\) and adding to the second gives \(-6y = 18\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{6} = \frac{11}{6}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 6 and the second by 12 gives \(2x + 3y = 6\) and \(3x - 2y = 22\). Multiplying the first by 2 and the second by 3, then adding them gives \(13x = 78\), so \(x = 6\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{2} = 0\)
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{5} = -\frac{14}{15}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions gives \(x + 2y = 0\) and \(5x + 3y = -14\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-5\) and adding to the second gives \(-7y = -14\), yielding \(y = 2\) and \(x = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{4} = \frac{7}{4}\)
\(\frac{x}{5} + \frac{y}{2} = \frac{13}{10}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions gives \(2x - y = 7\) and \(2x + 5y = 13\). Multiplying the first equation by \(-1\) and adding to the second yields \(6y = 6\), so \(y = 1\) and \(x = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x - 1}{4} + \frac{y + 4}{2} = 2\)
\(\frac{x + 3}{2} - \frac{y - 1}{3} = 5\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions and simplifying gives \(x + 2y = 1\) and \(3x - 2y = 19\). Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(4x = 20\), so \(x = 5\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{4} = 0\)
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{2} = \frac{11}{24}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by 12 and the second by 24 gives \(4x + 3y = 0\) and \(6x - 12y = 11\). Multiplying the first equation by 4 and adding to the second gives \(22x = 11\), yielding \(x = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(y = -\frac{2}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{x + y}{3} - \frac{x}{2} = \frac{11}{6}\)
\(\frac{2x - y}{5} + \frac{y}{2} = 0\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions and combining like terms gives \(-x + 2y = 11\) and \(4x + 3y = 0\). Multiplying the first equation by 4 and adding to the second gives \(11y = 44\), so \(y = 4\) and \(x = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{2x + 5}{3} - \frac{y - 1}{2} = 0\)
\(\frac{x + 7}{6} + \frac{2y + 4}{5} = 3\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions and simplifying leads to \(4x - 3y = -13\) and \(5x + 12y = 31\). Multiplying the first equation by 4 and adding to the second gives \(21x = -21\), so \(x = -1\) and \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the addition method:
\(\frac{2x}{7} - \frac{y}{3} = \frac{30}{7}\)
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{5y}{12} = -\frac{1}{2}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions by multiplying by 21 and 12 yields \(6x - 7y = 90\) and \(3x + 5y = -6\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-2\) and adding gives \(-17y = 102\), so \(y = -6\) and \(x = 8\).

Adding the equations eliminates \(y\), resulting in \(\frac{3x}{4} = \frac{5}{12}\), so \(x = \frac{5}{9}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{5}{9}\) into the second equation yields \(\frac{y}{6} = \frac{5}{36}\), which gives \(y = \frac{5}{6}\).

Adding the equations eliminates \(x\), giving \(\frac{y}{4} = \frac{1}{4}\), so \(y = 1\). Substituting \(y = 1\) into \(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{4} = 0\) gives \(\frac{x}{3} = \frac{1}{4}\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{3}{4}\).

Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\), giving \(\frac{x}{2} = \frac{3}{10}\), so \(x = \frac{3}{5}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{3}{5}\) into \(\frac{x}{6} - \frac{y}{5} = 0\) gives \(\frac{y}{5} = \frac{1}{10}\), so \(y = \frac{1}{2}\).

Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\), giving \(\frac{7x}{10} = \frac{7}{15}\), which solves to \(x = \frac{2}{3}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{2}{3}\) into \(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = 0\) yields \(\frac{y}{3} = -\frac{1}{3}\), so \(y = -1\).

Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\), giving \(\frac{x}{2} = \frac{5}{12}\), so \(x = \frac{5}{6}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{5}{6}\) into the second equation gives \(\frac{y}{4} = \frac{5}{36}\), which simplifies to \(y = \frac{5}{9}\).
Clearing denominators gives \(4x - 9y = 30\) and \(4x + 5y = 2\). Multiplying the second equation by \(-1\) and adding gives \(-14y = 28\), so \(y = -2\), which gives \(x = 3\) upon substitution.

Clearing denominators gives \(3x - 2y = 5\) and \(8x + 9y = -1\). Multiplying the first equation by \(9\) and the second by \(2\), then adding eliminates \(y\) to give \(43x = 43\), which leads to \(x = 1\) and \(y = -1\).

Clearing denominators yields \(15x - 8y = 6\) and \(2x + 3y = 13\). Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) and the second by \(8\), then adding them eliminates \(y\) to give \(61x = 122\), yielding \(x = 2\) and \(y = 3\).

Multiplying the second equation by \(2\) gives \(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = \frac{4}{3}\), and adding this to the first equation eliminates \(y\) to give \(x = \frac{3}{2}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{3}{2}\) into the first equation yields \(\frac{3}{4} - \frac{y}{3} = \frac{1}{6}\), which solves to \(y = \frac{7}{4}\).

Rewriting the first equation in general form and clearing fractions gives \(4x + 3y = 13\), while the second equation clears to \(3x - y = 13\). Multiplying the second equation by \(3\) and adding eliminates \(y\) to yield \(13x = 52\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -x - 1\)
\(3x + 2y = 1\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -x - 1\) into \(3x + 2y = 1\) to get \(3x + 2(-x - 1) = 1\), which simplifies to \(x - 2 = 1\), so \(x = 3\). Then \(y = -(3) - 1 = -4\), giving the solution \((3, -4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 2x - 1\)
\(3x + y = 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 1\) into \(3x + y = 9\) to get \(3x + (2x - 1) = 9\), which simplifies to \(5x = 10\), so \(x = 2\). Then \(y = 2(2) - 1 = 3\), giving the solution \((2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = 3y - 2\)
\(3x - 4y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3y - 2\) into \(3x - 4y = 4\) to get \(3(3y - 2) - 4y = 4\), which simplifies to \(5y - 6 = 4\), so \(y = 2\). Then \(x = 3(2) - 2 = 4\), giving the solution \((4, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = -2y + 7\)
\(2x + 3y = 12\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -2y + 7\) into \(2x + 3y = 12\) to get \(2(-2y + 7) + 3y = 12\), giving \(-y + 14 = 12\), so \(y = 2\). Then \(x = -2(2) + 7 = 3\), giving the solution \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -3x + 5\)
\(x - 2y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -3x + 5\) into \(x - 2y = 4\) to get \(x - 2(-3x + 5) = 4\), which simplifies to \(7x - 10 = 4\), so \(x = 2\). Then \(y = -3(2) + 5 = -1\), giving the solution \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2x + y = 11\)
\(3x + 4y = 14\)
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) in the first equation to get \(y = -2x + 11\), and substitute into the second: \(3x + 4(-2x + 11) = 14\), which simplifies to \(-5x = -30\), so \(x = 6\). Then \(y = -2(6) + 11 = -1\), giving \((6, -1)\).

qs.q:

qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 5y - 22\), and substitute into the second: \(3(5y - 22) - 2y = 12\), which gives \(13y = 78\), so \(y = 6\). Then \(x = 5(6) - 22 = 8\), giving \((8, 6)\).

qs.q:

\(x - 4y = -1\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 4y - 1\), then substitute into the first equation: \(2(4y - 1) - 3y - 13 = 0\), giving \(5y = 15\), so \(y = 3\). Then \(x = 4(3) - 1 = 11\), giving \((11, 3)\).

qs.q:

\(4x + 6y = 7\)
qs.s: Isolate \(x\) from the first equation to get \(x = 3y + 4\), then substitute into the second: \(4(3y + 4) + 6y = 7\), giving \(18y = -9\), so \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\). Then \(x = 3(-\frac{1}{2}) + 4 = \frac{5}{2}\), giving \((\frac{5}{2}, -\frac{1}{2})\).

qs.q:

\(7x - y = 44\)
\(4x + 3y = 43\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = 7x - 44\), then substitute into the second: \(4x + 3(7x - 44) = 43\), giving \(25x = 175\), so \(x = 7\). Then \(y = 7(7) - 44 = 5\), giving \((7, 5)\).

qs.q:

\(x = 4y + 1\)
\(x - 2y = 7\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4y + 1\) into the second equation to get \((4y + 1) - 2y = 7\), which simplifies to \(2y = 6\), so \(y = 3\). Then \(x = 4(3) + 1 = 13\), giving the solution \((13, 3)\).

qs.q:

\(x = 2y + 1\)
\(x - 3y = -2\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2y + 1\) into the second equation to get \((2y + 1) - 3y = -2\), which gives \(-y = -3\), so \(y = 3\). Substituting \(y = 3\) back gives \(x = 2(3) + 1 = 7\), so the solution is \((7, 3)\).

qs.q:

\(3x - y = -1\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 3\) into the second equation to get \(3x - (2x + 3) = -1\), which simplifies to \(x - 3 = -1\), so \(x = 2\). Then \(y = 2(2) + 3 = 7\), yielding \((2, 7)\).

qs.q:

\(x + 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5y - 4\) into the second equation to get \((5y - 4) + 2y = 10\), which gives \(7y = 14\), so \(y = 2\). Then \(x = 5(2) - 4 = 6\), giving the solution \((6, 2)\).

qs.q:

\(x + y = 7\)

qs.q:

qs.q:

\(4x - 3y = 6\)

qs.q:

qs.q:

\(2x - 3y + 19 = 0\)
\(x + 4y - 7 = 0\)
qs.s: Rearrange the second equation to \(x = 7 - 4y\), then substitute into the first: \(2(7 - 4y) - 3y + 19 = 0\), giving \(-11y + 33 = 0\), so \(y = 3\). Then \(x = 7 - 4(3) = -5\), giving \((-5, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x - 4y = 1\)
\(3x + 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 4y + 1\), and substitute into the second equation: \(3(4y + 1) + 2y = 10\), giving \(14y = 7\), so \(y = \frac{1}{2}\). Then \(x = 4(\frac{1}{2}) + 1 = 3\), giving \((3, \frac{1}{2})\).

qs.q:

\(3x - 2y = 7\)
\(y = x - 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = x - 3\) into the first equation to get \(3x - 2(x - 3) = 7\), which simplifies to \(x = 1\). Substituting \(x = 1\) into \(y = x - 3\) gives \(y = -2\), so the solution is \((1, -2)\).

qs.q:

\(2x - 5y = 9\)
\(y = 3x - 7\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 7\) into the first equation to get \(2x - 5(3x - 7) = 9\), which simplifies to \(-13x = -26\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(y = 3x - 7\) gives \(y = -1\), yielding \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:

\(3x + 4y = -2\)
\(y = 2x + 5\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 5\) into the first equation to get \(3x + 4(2x + 5) = -2\), which simplifies to \(11x = -22\), so \(x = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) into \(y = 2x + 5\) yields \(y = 1\), so the solution is \((-2, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(5x - 2y = 9\)
\(y = 3x - 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x - 4\) into the first equation to obtain \(5x - 2(3x - 4) = 9\), which solves to \(x = -1\). Then, substitute \(x = -1\) into \(y = 3x - 4\) to find \(y = -7\), giving \((-1, -7)\).

qs.q:

\(2x + 3y = 1\)
\(x = 4 - 2y\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4 - 2y\) into the first equation to get \(2(4 - 2y) + 3y = 1\), which gives \(y = 7\). Substituting \(y = 7\) into \(x = 4 - 2y\) yields \(x = -10\), giving the solution \((-10, 7)\).

qs.q:

\(4x - y = 19\)
\(3x + 5y = -3\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y = 4x - 19\) and substitute into the second equation: \(3x + 5(4x - 19) = -3\), which simplifies to \(23x = 92\) or \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(y = 4x - 19\) gives \(y = -3\), yielding the solution \((4, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(3x - 2y = 8\)
\(x + 4y = 5\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x = 5 - 4y\) and substitute into the first equation: \(3(5 - 4y) - 2y = 8\), which simplifies to \(-14y = -7\) or \(y = 1/2\). Substituting \(y = 1/2\) into \(x = 5 - 4y\) gives \(x = 3\), so the solution is \((3, 1/2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(3x + 2y = 13\)
\(x - 4y = -5\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 4y - 5\), then substitute into the first equation: \(3(4y - 5) + 2y = 13\), which gives \(y = 2\). Substituting \(y = 2\) into \(x = 4y - 5\) yields \(x = 3\), giving \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(2(x - 1) + 3y = 15\)
\(x + 2y = 11\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x = 11 - 2y\) and substitute into the first equation to get \(2(10 - 2y) + 3y = 15\), which gives \(y = 5\). Substituting \(y = 5\) into \(x = 11 - 2y\) gives \(x = 1\), so the solution is \((1, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(5x - y = 14\)
\(2x + 3y = 9\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = 5x - 14\), and substitute into the second equation: \(2x + 3(5x - 14) = 9\), yielding \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(y = 5x - 14\) gives \(y = 1\), so the solution is \((3, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(5x - 2y = -1\)
\(3x - y = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = 3x\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(5x - 2(3x) = -1\), so \(-x = -1\), which yields \(x = 1\) and \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2x - 3y = 22\)
\(3x + y = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = -3x\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(2x - 3(-3x) = 22\), so \(11x = 22\), which yields \(x = 2\) and \(y = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x + 2y = 21\)
\(2x - y = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = 2x\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3x + 2(2x) = 21\), so \(7x = 21\), which yields \(x = 3\) and \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2x + 3y = 18\)
\(x - 3y = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = 3y\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(2(3y) + 3y = 18\), so \(9y = 18\), which yields \(y = 2\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 2y = -16\)
\(x + 2y = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = -2y\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(-2y) - 2y = -16\), so \(-8y = -16\), which yields \(y = 2\) and \(x = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4x - 3(y + 2) = 5\)
\(x - 2y = -1\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 2y - 1\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(4(2y - 1) - 3(y + 2) = 5\), which simplifies to \(5y - 10 = 5\), yielding \(y = 3\) and \(x = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 2y = 16\)
\(x + 4y = 3\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 3 - 4y\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(3 - 4y) - 2y = 16\), which simplifies to \(-14y = 7\), yielding \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x + 5y = -7\)
\(2x - 4y = 10\)
qs.s: Divide the second equation by 2 to get \(x - 2y = 5\), or \(x = 2y + 5\). Substituting into the first equation yields \(3(2y + 5) + 5y = -7\), which simplifies to \(11y = -22\), giving \(y = -2\) and \(x = 1\).

qs.q:

\(5x + 3y = 81\)
\(x - 4y = -16\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 4y - 16\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(5(4y - 16) + 3y = 81\), which simplifies to \(23y = 161\), so \(y = 7\) and \(x = 12\).

qs.q:

\(2x + 5y = 23\)
\(\frac{x}{3} - y = 2\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 3y + 6\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(2(3y + 6) + 5y = 23\), which simplifies to \(11y = 11\), giving \(y = 1\) and \(x = 9\).

qs.q:

\(4x - y = -2\)
\(-8x + 2y = 4\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y = 4x + 2\), and substituting into the second equation yields \(-8x + 2(4x + 2) = 4\), which simplifies to \(4 = 4\), confirming infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(3x - y = 4\)
\(-6x + 2y = -8\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y = 3x - 4\), and substituting into the second equation yields \(-6x + 2(3x - 4) = -8\), which simplifies to the identity \(-8 = -8\), indicating infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(-x + 3y = 5\)
\(-2x + 6y = 10\)
qs.s: Expressing \(x\) in terms of \(y\) from the first equation gives \(x = 3y - 5\), and substituting into the second equation yields \(-2(3y - 5) + 6y = 10\), which reduces to \(10 = 10\), showing the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x - 2y = 3\)
\(3x - 6y = 9\)
qs.s: Isolating \(x\) in the first equation gives \(x = 2y + 3\), and substituting this into the second equation results in \(3(2y + 3) - 6y = 9\), which simplifies to \(9 = 9\), meaning there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(2x + y = -3\)
\(-6x - 3y = 9\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) yields \(y = -2x - 3\), and substituting into the second equation gives \(-6x - 3(-2x - 3) = 9\), which simplifies to the true statement \(9 = 9\), so there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(3(x - 2) - y = 2x - 1\)
\(-4x + 4y = -20\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(x - y = 5\), or \(y = x - 5\). Substituting this into the second equation gives \(-4x + 4(x - 5) = -20\), which simplifies to the identity \(-20 = -20\), meaning the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(\frac{2x - y}{4} = 3\)
\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{6} = 2\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(4\) gives \(2x - y = 12\), so \(y = 2x - 12\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{2x - 12}{6} = 2\), which simplifies to \(\frac{12}{6} = 2\), or \(2 = 2\), showing there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(-1.5x + 3y = -7.5\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y = 0.5x - 2.5\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(-1.5x + 3(0.5x - 2.5) = -7.5\), which simplifies to \(-7.5 = -7.5\), indicating infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(2x - 3y = 6\)
qs.s: From the first equation, isolate \(x\) to get \(x = \frac{3}{2}y + 3\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(2\left(\frac{3}{2}y + 3\right) - 3y = 6\), which simplifies to \(6 = 6\), showing there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(4(x - 1) + 2y = x + y + 5\)
\(6x + 2(y - 3) = 12\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(3x + y = 9\), or \(y = -3x + 9\). Substituting this into the second equation gives \(6x + 2((-3x + 9) - 3) = 12\), which simplifies to \(12 = 12\), confirming infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:

\(x + 2y = 6\)
\(-x - 2y = 4\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(x\) gives \(x = -2y + 6\). Substituting this into the second equation yields \(-(-2y + 6) - 2y = 4\), which simplifies to \(-6 = 4\); since this statement is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:

qs.q:

\(x - 3y = 4\)
\(-x + 3y = 2\)

qs.q:

\(2x - y = 3\)
\(-2x + y = 4\)

qs.q:

\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(-x + 2y = 6\)
qs.s: Solving the second equation for \(x\) gives \(x = 2y - 6\). Substituting this into the first equation yields \(\frac{2y - 6}{4} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\), which simplifies to \(-\frac{3}{2} = 1\); since this statement is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method.
\(8x - 3y = 2x + y + 11\)
\(3x - 2y = 7\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(6x - 4y = 11\), and solving the second for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{2}{3}y + \frac{7}{3}\). Substituting this into the first equation gives \(6\left(\frac{2}{3}y + \frac{7}{3}\right) - 4y = 11\), which simplifies to \(14 = 11\); since this is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:

\(0.4x - 0.8y = 1.2\)
\(-0.2x + 0.4y = 0.5\)
qs.s: Solving the second equation for \(x\) gives \(x = 2y - 2.5\). Substituting this into the first equation gives \(0.4(2y - 2.5) - 0.8y = 1.2\), which simplifies to \(-1 = 1.2\); since this statement is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:

\(2(3x + y) - y = 5\)
qs.s: Simplifying the equations gives \(6x + y = 11\) and \(6x + y = 5\). Solving the first for \(y\) gives \(y = -6x + 11\), and substituting into the second yields \(6x + (-6x + 11) = 5\), or \(11 = 5\); since this is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:

\(4x - 6y = 7\)
\(-2x + 3y = 5\)
qs.s: Solving the second equation for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}y - \frac{5}{2}\). Substituting this into the first equation gives \(4\left(\frac{3}{2}y - \frac{5}{2}\right) - 6y = 7\), which simplifies to \(-10 = 7\); since this is false, there is no solution.

qs.q:
