\(5x - 3y = 0\)
\(x - y = -4\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = y - 4\). Substituting into the first equation yields \(5(y - 4) - 3y = 0\), which gives \(2y = 20\), so \(y = 10\) and \(x = 10 - 4 = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x + 2y = 0\)
\(x - y = 5\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = y + 5\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(y + 5) + 2y = 0\), which simplifies to \(5y = -15\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = -3 + 5 = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4x - 3y = 0\)
\(x + y = 7\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = 7 - x\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(4x - 3(7 - x) = 0\), which simplifies to \(7x - 21 = 0\), yielding \(x = 3\) and \(y = 7 - 3 = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 2y = 0\)
\(x - y = -1\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = y - 1\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(y - 1) - 2y = 0\), so \(y = 3\) and \(x = 3 - 1 = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 4y = 0\)
\(x - y = 2\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = y + 2\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(y + 2) - 4y = 0\), which simplifies to \(-y + 6 = 0\), so \(y = 6\) and \(x = 6 + 2 = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4(x - y) - x = 2\)
\(x - 2y = -2\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(3x - 4y = 2\), and from the second equation, \(x = 2y - 2\). Substituting gives \(3(2y - 2) - 4y = 2\), which results in \(2y = 8\), so \(y = 4\) and \(x = 2(4) - 2 = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 11 = 8y\)
\(x + 6y - 8 = 0\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = 8 - 6y\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(3(8 - 6y) - 11 = 8y\), which simplifies to \(13 = 26y\), so \(y = \frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 8 - 6\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2(x + 1) + 3y = 25\)
\(x - 2(y - 1) = 3\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(2x + 3y = 23\) and \(x - 2y = 1\). Expressing \(x = 2y + 1\) and substituting into the first equation yields \(2(2y + 1) + 3y = 23\), giving \(7y = 21\), so \(y = 3\) and \(x = 2(3) + 1 = 7\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(5x + 8y = 1\)
\(x - 4y = -4\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = 4y - 4\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(5(4y - 4) + 8y = 1\), which simplifies to \(28y = 21\), so \(y = \frac{3}{4}\) and \(x = 4\left(\frac{3}{4}\right) - 4 = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4x - 3y = 18\)
\(2x + y = -1\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = -2x - 1\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(4x - 3(-2x - 1) = 18\), simplifying to \(10x + 3 = 18\), so \(x = \frac{15}{10} = \frac{3}{2}\) and \(y = -2\left(\frac{3}{2}\right) - 1 = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 3x - 10\)
\(y = -x + 6\)
qs.s: Equating both expressions gives \(3x - 10 = -x + 6\), so \(4x = 16\) and \(x = 4\). Substituting \(x = 4\) into \(y = -4 + 6\) gives \(y = 2\), resulting in the solution \((4, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -2x - 9\)
\(y = -5x + 12\)
qs.s: Setting \(-2x - 9 = -5x + 12\) gives \(3x = 21\), so \(x = 7\). Substituting \(x = 7\) into \(y = -2(7) - 9\) yields \(y = -23\), giving the solution \((7, -23)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 5x + 13\)
\(y = 1 - x\)
qs.s: Substitute to get \(5x + 13 = 1 - x\), which leads to \(6x = -12\), so \(x = -2\). Substitute \(x = -2\) into \(y = 1 - (-2)\) to find \(y = 3\), giving the solution \((-2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -4x + 6\)
\(y = 11 - 5x\)
qs.s: Set the expressions for \(y\) equal: \(-4x + 6 = 11 - 5x\), which gives \(x = 5\). Substitute \(x = 5\) into \(y = -4(5) + 6\) to get \(y = -14\), so the solution is \((5, -14)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 2x - 7\)
\(y = -3x + 8\)
qs.s: Substitute \(2x - 7\) for \(y\) in the second equation to get \(2x - 7 = -3x + 8\), which simplifies to \(5x = 15\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(y = 2(3) - 7\) gives \(y = -1\), yielding the solution \((3, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 5\)
\(y = -\frac{1}{4}x + 6\)
qs.s: Equating gives \(\frac{2}{3}x - 5 = -\frac{1}{4}x + 6\); multiplying through by 12 gives \(8x - 60 = -3x + 72\), so \(11x = 132\) and \(x = 12\). Substituting \(x = 12\) yields \(y = \frac{2}{3}(12) - 5 = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 0.8x - 5.4\)
\(y = -1.2x + 6.6\)

Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 5x - 8\)
\(y = 2 - 3x\)
qs.s: Equating \(5x - 8 = 2 - 3x\) gives \(8x = 10\), so \(x = \frac{5}{4}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{5}{4}\) into \(y = 2 - 3(\frac{5}{4})\) gives \(y = \frac{8}{4} - \frac{15}{4} = -\frac{7}{4}\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 2(3x - 4) - 7\)
\(y = 4(x + 1) + 1\)
qs.s: Expanding both equations gives \(y = 6x - 15\) and \(y = 4x + 5\). Setting them equal gives \(6x - 15 = 4x + 5\), so \(2x = 20\) and \(x = 10\), which gives \(y = 4(11) + 1 = 45\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -8x + 137\)
\(y = 7x - 148\)
qs.s: Setting \(-8x + 137 = 7x - 148\) yields \(-15x = -285\), which simplifies to \(x = 19\). Substituting \(x = 19\) into \(y = 7(19) - 148\) gives \(y = 133 - 148 = -15\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 2x - 5\)
\(3x + 2y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 5\) into \(3x + 2y = 4\) to get \(3x + 2(2x - 5) = 4\), which simplifies to \(7x - 10 = 4\), giving \(x = 2\). Then \(y = 2(2) - 5 = -1\), so the solution is \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = 3y + 1\)
\(2x - 5y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3y + 1\) into \(2x - 5y = 4\) to get \(2(3y + 1) - 5y = 4\), which simplifies to \(y + 2 = 4\), giving \(y = 2\). Then \(x = 3(2) + 1 = 7\), so the solution is \((7, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = 4 - 2y\)
\(3x + 5y = 11\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 4 - 2y\) into \(3x + 5y = 11\) to get \(3(4 - 2y) + 5y = 11\), which simplifies to \(12 - y = 11\), giving \(y = 1\). Then \(x = 4 - 2(1) = 2\), so the solution is \((2, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -2x + 7\)
\(4x - 3y = 9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -2x + 7\) into \(4x - 3y = 9\) to get \(4x - 3(-2x + 7) = 9\), which simplifies to \(10x - 21 = 9\), giving \(x = 3\). Then \(y = -2(3) + 7 = 1\), so the solution is \((3, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 4x - 3\)
\(5x - 2y = -3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 4x - 3\) into \(5x - 2y = -3\) to get \(5x - 2(4x - 3) = -3\), which simplifies to \(-3x + 6 = -3\), giving \(x = 3\). Then \(y = 4(3) - 3 = 9\), so the solution is \((3, 9)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = 5y - 18\)
\(7x - 4y = 29\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 5y - 18\) into \(7x - 4y = 29\) to obtain \(7(5y - 18) - 4y = 29\), which simplifies to \(31y - 126 = 29\), giving \(31y = 155\), so \(y = 5\). Then \(x = 5(5) - 18 = 7\), so the solution is \((7, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x - 6y = 8\)
\(4x + 9y = 21\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 6y + 8\), and substitute into the second equation: \(4(6y + 8) + 9y = 21\), which yields \(33y = -11\), so \(y = -1/3\). Then \(x = 6(-1/3) + 8 = 6\), so the solution is \((6, -1/3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(5x - 3y + 27 = 0\)
\(2x + y + 2 = 0\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(y\) to get \(y = -2x - 2\), and substitute into the first equation: \(5x - 3(-2x - 2) + 27 = 0\), which gives \(11x + 33 = 0\), so \(x = -3\). Then \(y = -2(-3) - 2 = 4\), so the solution is \((-3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x + y = 13\)
\(2x - 3y = 5\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = 13 - 3x\), and substitute into the second equation: \(2x - 3(13 - 3x) = 5\), giving \(11x - 39 = 5\), so \(x = 4\). Then \(y = 13 - 3(4) = 1\), so the solution is \((4, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2(x + 4) - y = 10\)
\(5x - 2y = 7\)
qs.s: Simplify the first equation to \(2x + 8 - y = 10\), which gives \(y = 2x - 2\). Substitute this into the second equation: \(5x - 2(2x - 2) = 7\), which simplifies to \(x + 4 = 7\), giving \(x = 3\) and \(y = 2(3) - 2 = 4\), so the solution is \((3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 5x\)
\(2x - y = -9\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 5x\) into the second equation to get \(2x - 5x = -9\), which gives \(-3x = -9\), so \(x = 3\). Then, \(y = 5(3) = 15\), giving the solution \((3, 15)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -4x\)
\(3x - 2y = 22\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -4x\) into the second equation to get \(3x - 2(-4x) = 22\), which simplifies to \(11x = 22\), so \(x = 2\). Then, \(y = -4(2) = -8\), giving the solution \((2, -8)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = 2y\)
\(3x - 5y = 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 2y\) into the second equation to get \(3(2y) - 5y = 4\), which simplifies to \(y = 4\). Then, \(x = 2(4) = 8\), giving the solution \((8, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = 3x\)
\(2x + 3y = 22\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 3x\) into the second equation to get \(2x + 3(3x) = 22\), which simplifies to \(11x = 22\), so \(x = 2\). Then, \(y = 3(2) = 6\), giving the solution \((2, 6)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = -3y\)
\(4x - 5y = -34\)
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3y\) into the second equation to get \(4(-3y) - 5y = -34\), which gives \(-17y = -34\), so \(y = 2\). Then, \(x = -3(2) = -6\), giving the solution \((-6, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x + 4y = 14\)
\(x - 2y = 3\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 2y + 3\), and substitute into the first equation: \(3(2y + 3) + 4y = 14\), giving \(10y = 5\), so \(y = \frac{1}{2}\). Then, \(x = 2\left(\frac{1}{2}\right) + 3 = 4\), giving the solution \(\left(4, \frac{1}{2}\right)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2x - 5y = -19\)
\(3x + y = 14\)
qs.s: Solve the second equation for \(y\) to get \(y = -3x + 14\), and substitute into the first equation: \(2x - 5(-3x + 14) = -19\), which simplifies to \(17x = 51\), so \(x = 3\). Then, \(y = -3(3) + 14 = 5\), so the solution is \((3, 5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 1\)
\(3x - 6y = 12\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 1\) into the second equation to get \(3x - 6\left(\frac{2}{3}x - 1\right) = 12\), which simplifies to \(-x + 6 = 12\), so \(x = -6\). Then, \(y = \frac{2}{3}(-6) - 1 = -5\), giving the solution \((-6, -5)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x - 3y = -11\)
\(4x + 5y = 7\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = 3y - 11\), and substitute into the second equation: \(4(3y - 11) + 5y = 7\), which simplifies to \(17y = 51\), so \(y = 3\). Substituting \(y = 3\) gives \(x = 3(3) - 11 = -2\), so the solution is \((-2, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x + 5y = -22\)
\(5x - 2y = 25\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = -5y - 22\), and substitute into the second equation: \(5(-5y - 22) - 2y = 25\), which simplifies to \(-27y = 135\), so \(y = -5\). Then, \(x = -5(-5) - 22 = 3\), giving the solution \((3, -5)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(7x - y = 0\)
\(9x - 2y = -15\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(y = 7x\). Substituting into the second yields \(9x - 2(7x) = -15\), so \(-5x = -15\), which gives \(x = 3\) and \(y = 7(3) = 21\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(x + 5y = 0\)
\(3x + 8y = 14\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(x = -5y\). Substituting into the second gives \(3(-5y) + 8y = 14\), so \(-7y = 14\), yielding \(y = -2\) and \(x = -5(-2) = 10\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(x - 3y = 0\)
\(2x - 5y = -4\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(x = 3y\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(2(3y) - 5y = -4\), so \(y = -4\) and \(x = 3(-4) = -12\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(4x - y = 0\)
\(5x - 2y = 9\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(y = 4x\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(5x - 2(4x) = 9\), which simplifies to \(-3x = 9\), so \(x = -3\) and \(y = 4(-3) = -12\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(4x - y = 0\)
\(6x - 5y = 21\)
qs.s: From the first equation, \(y = 4x\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(6x - 5(4x) = 21\), so \(-14x = 21\), which gives \(x = -3/2\) and \(y = 4(-3/2) = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(4x - 3y = -35\)
\(x + 5y + 26 = 0\)
qs.s: Rearrange the second equation to \(x = -5y - 26\) and substitute into the first: \(4(-5y - 26) - 3y = -35\), which simplifies to \(-23y = 69\), so \(y = -3\) and \(x = -5(-3) - 26 = -11\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(2x - 3y = -14\)
\(3x + 2y = 5\)
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x = \frac{3y - 14}{2}\) and substitute into the second: \(3(\frac{3y - 14}{2}) + 2y = 5\). Clearing fractions gives \(3(3y - 14) + 4y = 10\), so \(13y = 52\), yielding \(y = 4\) and \(x = \frac{3(4) - 14}{2} = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(7x - y = 38\)
\(4x + 3y = 11\)
qs.s: Rearrange the first equation to \(y = 7x - 38\) and substitute into the second: \(4x + 3(7x - 38) = 11\), leading to \(25x = 125\), so \(x = 5\) and \(y = 7(5) - 38 = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + y = 2\)
\(5x - 6y = 37\)
qs.s: Isolate \(y\) in the first equation to get \(y = 2 - \frac{x}{3}\), then substitute into the second: \(5x - 6(2 - \frac{x}{3}) = 37\), so \(7x = 49\), giving \(x = 7\) and \(y = 2 - \frac{7}{3} = -\frac{1}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\(x - 0.4y = 3\)
\(0.5x + 1.2y = 7.1\)
qs.s: Isolate \(x = 0.4y + 3\) from the first equation and substitute into the second: \(0.5(0.4y + 3) + 1.2y = 7.1\), which simplifies to \(1.4y = 5.6\), so \(y = 4\) and \(x = 0.4(4) + 3 = 4.6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(3m + n = 1\)
\(4m + 3n = 8\)

What is the solution \((m, n)\)?
qs.s: From the first equation, \(n = 1 - 3m\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(4m + 3(1 - 3m) = 8\), giving \(m = -1\) and \(n = 1 - 3(-1) = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(2a - b = 6\)
\(5a + 3b = 26\)

What is the solution \((a, b)\)?
qs.s: From the first equation, \(b = 2a - 6\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(5a + 3(2a - 6) = 26\), which simplifies to \(11a = 44\), so \(a = 4\) and \(b = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(p + 4q = -14\)
\(3p - 2q = 0\)

What is the solution \((p, q)\)?
qs.s: Isolating \(p\) from the first equation gives \(p = -14 - 4q\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(3(-14 - 4q) - 2q = 0\), giving \(q = -3\) and \(p = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(3x - y = 7\)
\(2x + 3y = -10\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y = 3x - 7\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(2x + 3(3x - 7) = -10\), which simplifies to \(11x = 11\), so \(x = 1\) and \(y = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(x + 3y = 0\)
\(2x + 5y = 1\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Isolating \(x\) from the first equation gives \(x = -3y\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(2(-3y) + 5y = 1\), which solves to \(y = -1\), and then \(x = -3(-1) = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(2x + 3y = 7\)
\(3x - 4y = 19\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{7 - 3y}{2}\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(3\left(\frac{7 - 3y}{2}\right) - 4y = 19\), which simplifies to \(-17y = 17\), yielding \(y = -1\) and \(x = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - y = 7\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) in the second equation gives \(y = \frac{x}{2} - 7\). Substituting into the first equation and multiplying by \(12\) gives \(3x + 4\left(\frac{x}{2} - 7\right) = 12\), which solves to \(x = 8\) and \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(2(x + 1) + 3y = 2\)
\(x - 2(y + 3) = 1\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Simplifying both equations gives \(2x + 3y = 0\) and \(x = 2y + 7\). Substituting \(x\) into the first equation yields \(2(2y + 7) + 3y = 0\), which solves to \(y = -2\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(0.5x - y = -1.5\)
\(0.3x + 0.4y = 4.1\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Isolating \(y\) from the first equation gives \(y = 0.5x + 1.5\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(0.3x + 0.4(0.5x + 1.5) = 4.1\), which simplifies to \(0.5x = 3.5\), giving \(x = 7\) and \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by substitution:
\(11x + y = 47\)
\(5x - 3y = 11\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) gives \(y = 47 - 11x\). Substituting into the second equation yields \(5x - 3(47 - 11x) = 11\), which simplifies to \(38x = 152\), giving \(x = 4\) and \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = \frac{1}{3}y + 4\)
\(3x - y = 12\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = \frac{1}{3}y + 4\) into \(3x - y = 12\) gives \(3\left(\frac{1}{3}y + 4\right) - y = 12\), which simplifies to \(12 = 12\). Since this equation is always true, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 1\)
\(2x - 3y = 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{2}{3}x - 1\) into \(2x - 3y = 3\) to get \(2x - 3\left(\frac{2}{3}x - 1\right) = 3\), which simplifies to \(3 = 3\). Because the variable is eliminated and the resulting equation is true, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5\)
\(x + 2y = 10\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 5\) into the second equation yields \(x + 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}x + 5\right) = 10\), which reduces to \(10 = 10\). This true statement indicates that the lines coincide and there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\)
\(x - 2y = 6\)
qs.s: Substituting \(y = \frac{1}{2}x - 3\) into the second equation gives \(x - 2\left(\frac{1}{2}x - 3\right) = 6\), which simplifies to the true statement \(6 = 6\). Because this is an identity, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(x = -\frac{3}{2}y + 6\)
\(2x + 3y = 12\)
qs.s: Substituting \(x = -\frac{3}{2}y + 6\) into \(2x + 3y = 12\) gives \(2\left(-\frac{3}{2}y + 6\right) + 3y = 12\), which simplifies to \(-3y + 12 + 3y = 12\) or \(12 = 12\). Since this is always true, there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{4} = 1\)
\(\frac{2x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 2\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(x\) gives \(x = 3 - \frac{3}{4}y\). Substituting this into the second equation yields \(\frac{2}{3}\left(3 - \frac{3}{4}y\right) + \frac{y}{2} = 2\), which simplifies to \(2 = 2\), showing the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x - 2y = 8\)
\(-6x + 4y = -16\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) yields \(y = \frac{3}{2}x - 4\). Substituting this into the second equation produces \(-6x + 4\left(\frac{3}{2}x - 4\right) = -16\), which simplifies to \(-16 = -16\), meaning the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2(x + 3y) - 5y = 3y + 4\)
\(5x - 2(x + y) = y + 6\)
qs.s: Simplifying the equations gives \(2x - 2y = 4\) (so \(x = y + 2\)) and \(3x - 3y = 6\). Substituting \(x = y + 2\) into \(3x - 3y = 6\) yields \(3(y + 2) - 3y = 6\), which simplifies to the identity \(6 = 6\), resulting in infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(0.4x - 0.2y = 1.2\)
\(-1.2x + 0.6y = -3.6\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(y\) yields \(y = 2x - 6\). Substituting this into the second equation gives \(-1.2x + 0.6(2x - 6) = -3.6\), which simplifies to \(-3.6 = -3.6\), so the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4x - 6y = 14\)
\(-6x + 9y = -21\)
qs.s: Solving the first equation for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}y + \frac{7}{2}\). Substituting this into the second equation gives \(-6\left(\frac{3}{2}y + \frac{7}{2}\right) + 9y = -21\), which reduces to \(-21 = -21\), indicating infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(5x = 2y + 3\)
\(15x = 6y + 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(15x = 3(5x) = 3(2y + 3) = 6y + 9\) into the second equation to obtain \(6y + 9 = 6y + 4\). Subtracting \(6y\) yields \(9 = 4\), a contradiction, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(4x = 6y - 2\)
\(8x = 12y - 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(8x = 2(4x) = 2(6y - 2) = 12y - 4\) into the second equation to get \(12y - 4 = 12y - 4\). This simplifies to \(0 = 0\), which is always true, so there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2x = 5y + 1\)
\(6x = 15y + 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(6x = 3(2x) = 3(5y + 1) = 15y + 3\) into the second equation to obtain \(15y + 3 = 15y + 3\). This simplifies to \(0 = 0\), so the two equations coincide and there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x = 4y - 2\)
\(6x = 8y + 5\)
qs.s: Substitute \(6x = 2(3x) = 2(4y - 2) = 8y - 4\) into the second equation to get \(8y - 4 = 8y + 5\). This simplifies to \(-4 = 5\), which is impossible, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3x = 2y + 5\)
\(9x = 6y + 11\)
qs.s: Substitute \(9x = 3(3x) = 3(2y + 5) = 6y + 15\) into the second equation to get \(6y + 15 = 6y + 11\). This simplifies to the false statement \(15 = 11\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(3(x - 2) = 2y + 1\)
\(6x - 4y = 19\)
qs.s: Expand the first equation to obtain \(3x - 6 = 2y + 1\), or \(3x = 2y + 7\). Substituting \(6x = 2(3x) = 4y + 14\) into the second equation gives \(4y + 14 - 4y = 19\), which simplifies to \(14 = 19\), so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(5x - 3y + 4 = 2x + y - 1\)
\(6x - 8y = 7\)
qs.s: Rearranging the first equation gives \(3x = 4y - 5\). Substituting \(6x = 2(3x) = 8y - 10\) into the second equation yields \(8y - 10 - 8y = 7\), which reduces to \(-10 = 7\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{2} = \frac{2y}{3} + 2\)
\(\frac{3x}{4} - y = 5\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(3x = 4y + 12\) and \(3x - 4y = 20\). Substituting \(3x = 4y + 12\) into the second equation yields \(4y + 12 - 4y = 20\), or \(12 = 20\), which is false, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(2(2x + 1) = 3(y - 2) + 14\)
\(8x - 6y = 12\)
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying the first equation gives \(4x = 3y + 6\). Substituting \(8x = 2(4x) = 6y + 12\) into the second equation produces \(6y + 12 - 6y = 12\), or \(0 = 0\), meaning there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{3} = \frac{y}{2} + 1\)
\(4x - 6y = 12\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 6 to get \(2x = 3y + 6\). Substituting \(4x = 2(2x) = 6y + 12\) into the second equation yields \(6y + 12 - 6y = 12\), or \(12 = 12\), so there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\frac{1}{5}x - y = -1
2x + \frac{1}{2}y = 11
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to obtain \(y = \frac{1}{5}x + 1\), then substitute into the second equation to get \(2x + \frac{1}{2}(\frac{1}{5}x + 1) = 11\), which simplifies to \(\frac{21}{10}x = \frac{21}{2}\), yielding \(x = 5\) and \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
x - \frac{1}{2}y = 5
\frac{1}{3}x + 2y = 6
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(x\) to get \(x = \frac{1}{2}y + 5\), then substitute into the second equation to obtain \(\frac{1}{3}(\frac{1}{2}y + 5) + 2y = 6\), which yields \(y = 2\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\frac{1}{2}x + y = 4
3x - \frac{1}{3}y = 5
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = 4 - \frac{1}{2}x\), then substitute into the second equation: \(3x - \frac{1}{3}(4 - \frac{1}{2}x) = 5\), which simplifies to \(\frac{19}{6}x = \frac{19}{3}\), giving \(x = 2\) and \(y = 3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
x + \frac{1}{3}y = 0
\frac{1}{2}x + 2y = 11
qs.s: Isolate \(x\) in the first equation as \(x = -\frac{1}{3}y\), then substitute into the second equation: \(\frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{3}y) + 2y = 11\), which gives \(\frac{11}{6}y = 11\), so \(y = 6\) and \(x = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
\frac{1}{4}x + y = -1
3x - \frac{1}{2}y = 13
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = -\frac{1}{4}x - 1\), then substitute into the second equation: \(3x - \frac{1}{2}(-\frac{1}{4}x - 1) = 13\), which gives \(\frac{25}{8}x = \frac{25}{2}\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
3x + \frac{1}{2}y = 1
6x - \frac{3}{4}y = -5
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y\) to get \(y = 2 - 6x\), then substitute into the second equation: \(6x - \frac{3}{4}(2 - 6x) = -5\), which yields \(\frac{21}{2}x = -\frac{7}{2}\), giving \(x = -\frac{1}{3}\) and \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
2(x - y) + 3y = x + 5
3(x - 2) - 4(y + 1) = -2
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(x + y = 5\), so \(y = 5 - x\). Simplifying the second equation yields \(3x - 4y = 8\); substituting \(y = 5 - x\) gives \(3x - 4(5 - x) = 8\), which solves to \(x = 4\) and \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by the substitution method:
3(x - 2) + 4y = -1
2x - 3(y + 1) = 6
qs.s: Simplifying both equations gives \(3x + 4y = 5\) and \(2x - 3y = 9\); solving the second for \(x\) gives \(x = \frac{3}{2}y + \frac{9}{2}\), and substituting into the first yields \(17y = -17\), so \(y = -1\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q:

0.5x - 0.3y = 0.3
qs.s: Solve the first equation for \(y = 4.6 - 0.2x\) and substitute into the second equation to get \(0.5x - 0.3(4.6 - 0.2x) = 0.3\), which simplifies to \(0.56x = 1.68\), giving \(x = 3\) and \(y = 4\).

From the first equation, isolate \(y\) to get \(y = 2 - \frac{4}{3}x\). Substituting this into the second equation gives \(\frac{3}{4}x - \frac{1}{3}(2 - \frac{4}{3}x) = -\frac{17}{4}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{43}{36}x = -\frac{43}{12}\), yielding \(x = -3\) and \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{4} + \frac{y}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - 3y = -11\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: From the second equation, solve for \(x\) to get \(x = 6y - 22\). Substitute into the first equation: \(\frac{6y - 22}{4} + \frac{y}{6} = -\frac{1}{2}\), which simplifies to \(20y = 60\), giving \(y = 3\) and \(x = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{2y}{3} = 3\)
\(x + \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: From the second equation, solve for \(x\) to get \(x = 1 - \frac{y}{2}\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(\frac{1 - y/2}{2} + \frac{2y}{3} = 3\), which simplifies to \(\frac{5y}{12} = \frac{5}{2}\), yielding \(y = 6\) and \(x = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{4} - y = 4\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: From the second equation, solve for \(y\) to get \(y = \frac{x}{4} - 4\). Substituting this into the first equation gives \(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{\frac{x}{4} - 4}{3} = 1\), which simplifies to \(\frac{7x}{12} = \frac{7}{3}\), yielding \(x = 4\) and \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\)
\(\frac{x}{2} + 2y = 7\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: From the second equation, isolate \(x\) to get \(x = 14 - 4y\). Substitute this into the first equation: \(\frac{14 - 4y}{3} - \frac{y}{2} = 1\), which clears to \(28 - 11y = 6\), giving \(y = 2\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q:

\(\frac{x}{3} + 4y = -1\)
\(\frac{x}{6} - \frac{2y}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: From the first equation, solve for \(x\) to get \(x = -3 - 12y\). Substitute into the second equation: \(\frac{-3 - 12y}{6} - \frac{2y}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\), which simplifies to \(-16y = 8\), giving \(y = -\frac{1}{2}\) and \(x = 3\).

qs.q:

\(\frac{x}{3} - \frac{y}{4} = \frac{x - 2y}{6} + 1\)
\(\frac{x + 1}{2} + \frac{y - 3}{3} = 3\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(12\) yields \(4x - 3y = 2x - 4y + 12\), which simplifies to \(y = 12 - 2x\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(\frac{x + 1}{2} + \frac{9 - 2x}{3} = 3\), which simplifies to \(-x = -3\), yielding \(x = 3\) and \(y = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x + 2y}{3} - \frac{x - y}{2} = -1\)
\(\frac{2x - y}{3} + \frac{x + 3y}{6} = 11\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: Clearing fractions in the first equation gives \(-x + 7y = -6\), so \(x = 7y + 6\). Substituting this into the simplified second equation, \(5x + y = 66\), gives \(5(7y + 6) + y = 66\), which simplifies to \(36y = 36\), so \(y = 1\) and \(x = 13\).

qs.q:
Solve by the substitution method:
\(\frac{x + 3}{4} - \frac{y - 1}{3} = 1\)
\(\frac{2x - 1}{3} + \frac{y + 2}{2} = 6\)
Find the solution \((x, y)\).
qs.s: Clearing denominators gives \(3x - 4y = -1\) and \(4x + 3y = 32\). Isolating \(x = \frac{4y - 1}{3}\) and substituting into the second equation gives \(4\left(\frac{4y - 1}{3}\right) + 3y = 32\), which simplifies to \(25y = 100\), so \(y = 4\) and \(x = 5\).

qs.q:

\(\frac{2x}{3} - \frac{3y}{4} = 7\)
\(\frac{5x}{6} + \frac{y}{2} = 3\)

qs.s: From the second equation, \(y = 6 - \frac{5x}{3}\). Substituting into the first equation gives \(\frac{2x}{3} - \frac{3}{4}\left(6 - \frac{5x}{3}\right) = 7\), which simplifies to \(\frac{23x}{12} = \frac{23}{2}\), giving \(x = 6\) and \(y = -4\).

qs.q:

qs.s: From the first equation, \(x = \frac{44}{3} + \frac{10y}{9}\). Substituting into the second equation gives \(\frac{5}{8}\left(\frac{44}{3} + \frac{10y}{9}\right) + \frac{7y}{12} = \frac{3}{2}\), which simplifies to \(\frac{46y}{36} = -\frac{276}{36}\), giving \(y = -6\) and \(x = 8\).

Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(2x + 5y = -6\)
\(-6x - 15y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) gives \(-6x - 15y = 18\). For the system to have an infinite number of solutions, the equations must be equivalent, so \(k = 18\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(5x - 3(x - 2y) = 18\)
\(kx - 9y = -27\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation gives \(2x + 6y = 18\). Multiplying this equation by \(-\frac{3}{2}\) yields \(-3x - 9y = -27\), so \(k = -3\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(0.4x - 0.3y = 1.2\)
\(-1.2x + 0.9y = 2k + 1\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) gives \(-1.2x + 0.9y = -3.6\). Setting \(2k + 1 = -3.6\) gives \(2k = -4.6\), so \(k = -2.3\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(4(x - y) + 3x = 2y + 9\)
\(-14x + 12y = 3k - 6\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms in the first equation gives \(7x - 6y = 9\). Multiplying by \(-2\) yields \(-14x + 12y = -18\), so \(3k - 6 = -18\), which gives \(k = -4\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(\frac{2}{3}x - \frac{3}{4}y = \frac{5}{6}\)
\(-24x + 27y = 5k + 5\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(12\) gives \(8x - 9y = 10\), and multiplying by \(-3\) yields \(-24x + 27y = -30\). Setting \(5k + 5 = -30\) gives \(5k = -35\), so \(k = -7\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(\frac{x + 1}{3} - \frac{y - 2}{4} = 1\)
\(-12x + 9y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(12\) and simplifying yields \(4x - 3y = 2\). Multiplying this result by \(-3\) gives \(-12x + 9y = -6\), so \(k = -6\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(2x + 3y = 7\)
\(4x + 6y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) gives \(4x + 6y = 14\). For the system to have an infinite number of solutions, the equations must be equivalent, so \(k = 14\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(3x - 2y = -6\)
\(-9x + 6y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) gives \(-9x + 6y = 18\). For the system to have infinitely many solutions, the equations must be equivalent, so \(k = 18\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(x - 4y = 3\)
\(-3x + 12y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-3\) gives \(-3x + 12y = -9\). For the system to have infinitely many solutions, the two equations must be identical, so \(k = -9\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(-5x + 2y = -4\)
\(10x - 4y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-2\) yields \(10x - 4y = 8\). For the system to have an infinite number of solutions, the equations must coincide, so \(k = 8\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(4x + y = 5\)
\(12x + 3y = k\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives \(12x + 3y = 15\). For the system to have an infinite number of solutions, the equations must coincide, so \(k = 15\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(\frac{3}{5}x - \frac{1}{2}y = 2\)
\(-6x + 5y = 2k - 4\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(-10\) yields \(-6x + 5y = -20\). For the system to have infinitely many solutions, the constant terms must match, so \(2k - 4 = -20\), which gives \(k = -8\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(0.4x - 0.6y = 1.2\)
\(3y - 2x = k - 4\)
qs.s: Rearranging the second equation gives \(-2x + 3y = k - 4\). Since multiplying the first equation by \(-5\) yields \(-2x + 3y = -6\), we have \(k - 4 = -6\), which gives \(k = -2\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(3(x - 2y) + y = 4\)
\(-6x + 10y = 2k - 2\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation gives \(3x - 5y = 4\). Multiplying by \(-2\) yields \(-6x + 10y = -8\), so \(2k - 2 = -8\), which solves to \(k = -3\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(6x = 4y - 10\)
\(-15x + 10y = k\)
qs.s: Rewriting the first equation gives \(6x - 4y = -10\). Multiplying by \(-\frac{5}{2}\) yields \(-15x + 10y = 25\), so for infinitely many solutions, \(k = 25\).

qs.q:
Choose the value of \(k\) such that the system of linear equations has an infinite number of solutions.
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{6} = \frac{2}{3}\)
\(-3x + 2y = 2k + 4\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(12\) gives \(3x - 2y = 8\), and multiplying by \(-1\) gives \(-3x + 2y = -8\). Setting \(2k + 4 = -8\) yields \(k = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(x + 2ay = b\)
\(x - 2ay = 3b\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations gives \(2x = 4b\), so \(x = 2b\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(4ay = -2b\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{b}{2a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(x + by = a\)
\(x - by = 3a\)
qs.s: Adding the equations gives \(2x = 4a\), so \(x = 2a\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2by = -2a\), so \(y = -\frac{a}{b}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2x + ay = 4b\)
\(2x - ay = 2b\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations yields \(4x = 6b\), so \(x = \frac{3b}{2}\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(2ay = 2b\), giving \(y = \frac{b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(ax + y = 3b\)
\(ax - y = b\)
qs.s: Adding the two equations produces \(2ax = 4b\), so \(x = \frac{2b}{a}\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(2y = 2b\), so \(y = b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3x + ay = b\)
\(3x - ay = 5b\)
qs.s: Adding the equations yields \(6x = 6b\), so \(x = b\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(2ay = -4b\), which simplifies to \(y = -\frac{2b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\frac{x}{a} + \frac{y}{2b} = 5\)
\(\frac{x}{2a} - \frac{y}{b} = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(\frac{1}{2}\) to get \(\frac{x}{4a} - \frac{y}{2b} = 0\), and add it to the first equation to obtain \(\frac{5x}{4a} = 5\), giving \(x = 4a\). Substituting \(x = 4a\) into the second equation yields \(2 - \frac{y}{b} = 0\), so \(y = 2b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2(x + ay) - x = 7b\)
\(3(x - ay) + 2ay = 0\)
qs.s: Expanding gives the standard system \(x + 2ay = 7b\) and \(3x - ay = 0\). Multiplying the second equation by 2 and adding it to the first yields \(7x = 7b\), so \(x = b\), which then gives \(3b - ay = 0\), or \(y = \frac{3b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3x + 2ay = 13b\)
\(2x - 3ay = 0\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 2 to obtain \(9x + 6ay = 39b\) and \(4x - 6ay = 0\), then add them to get \(13x = 39b\), or \(x = 3b\). Substitute \(x = 3b\) into \(2x - 3ay = 0\) to get \(6b = 3ay\), which gives \(y = \frac{2b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + 3by = 12\)
\(ax - by = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 3 to get \(3ax - 3by = 3\), and add this to the first equation to find \(5ax = 15\), so \(x = \frac{3}{a}\). Substituting \(x = \frac{3}{a}\) into \(ax - by = 1\) gives \(3 - by = 1\), so \(y = \frac{2}{b}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2x + 3ay = 7b\)
\(3x - ay = 5b\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 3 to get \(9x - 3ay = 15b\), and add it to the first equation to obtain \(11x = 22b\), so \(x = 2b\). Substitute \(x = 2b\) into \(3x - ay = 5b\) to find \(6b - ay = 5b\), giving \(y = \frac{b}{a}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(ax + 2y = -b\)
\(3ax - 2y = 13b\)
qs.s: Add both equations to eliminate \(y\), which gives \(4ax = 12b\), so \(x = \frac{3b}{a}\). Substitute \(x\) into \(ax + 2y = -b\) to get \(3b + 2y = -b\), so \(2y = -4b\) and \(y = -2b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(4ax + y = 7b\)
\(ax - y = 3b\)
qs.s: Add the two equations to eliminate \(y\), giving \(5ax = 10b\), so \(x = \frac{2b}{a}\). Substitute \(x = \frac{2b}{a}\) into \(ax - y = 3b\) to get \(2b - y = 3b\), which simplifies to \(y = -b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3ax - y = 2b\)
\(ax + y = 6b\)
qs.s: Add the two equations to eliminate \(y\), giving \(4ax = 8b\), so \(x = \frac{2b}{a}\). Substitute into the second equation: \(a\left(\frac{2b}{a}\right) + y = 6b \implies 2b + y = 6b\), so \(y = 4b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(5ax + 3y = 2b\)
\(2ax - 3y = 5b\)
qs.s: Add the equations to eliminate \(y\), obtaining \(7ax = 7b\), which gives \(x = \frac{b}{a}\). Substitute into the first equation: \(5b + 3y = 2b \implies 3y = -3b\), so \(y = -b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + y = 5b\)
\(3ax - y = 0\)
qs.s: Add the equations to eliminate \(y\), yielding \(5ax = 5b\), so \(x = \frac{b}{a}\). Substitute \(x\) into the second equation: \(3a\left(\frac{b}{a}\right) - y = 0 \implies 3b - y = 0\), giving \(y = 3b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + 3y = 12b\)
\(3ax - 2y = 5b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) and the second by \(3\) to get \(4ax + 6y = 24b\) and \(9ax - 6y = 15b\). Adding them gives \(13ax = 39b\), so \(x = \frac{3b}{a}\), and substituting back gives \(2(3b) + 3y = 12b\), so \(y = 2b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + 3y = 7b\)
\(ax - y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(3\) to get \(3ax - 3y = 3b\), and add it to the first equation to obtain \(5ax = 10b\), so \(x = \frac{2b}{a}\). Substitute \(x\) into \(ax - y = b\) to get \(2b - y = b\), so \(y = b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + by = 2a^2 + b^2\)
\(ax - by = a^2 - b^2\)
qs.s: Add the equations to eliminate \(by\), giving \(3ax = 3a^2\), which yields \(x = a\). Substitute \(x = a\) into the second equation: \(a^2 - by = a^2 - b^2 \implies -by = -b^2\), so \(y = b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\frac{ax}{2} + y = 4b\)
\(\frac{ax}{3} - y = b\)
qs.s: Add the equations to eliminate \(y\), giving \(\left(\frac{1}{2} + \frac{1}{3}\right)ax = 5b \implies \frac{5ax}{6} = 5b\), so \(x = \frac{6b}{a}\). Substitute \(x\) into the second equation: \(\frac{a(6b/a)}{3} - y = b \implies 2b - y = b\), so \(y = b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \((x, y)\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2ax + by = 5ab\)
\(ax - 2by = -5ab\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by \(2\) to get \(2ax - 4by = -10ab\). Subtract this from the first equation to obtain \(5by = 15ab\), so \(y = 3a\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(2ax + 3ab = 5ab \implies x = b\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(4x - y = a\)
\(2x + 3y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 to get \(12x - 3y = 3a\). Adding this to the second equation gives \(14x = 3a + b\), so \(x = \frac{3a + b}{14}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2x + 5y = a\)
\(x + y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 5 to obtain \(5x + 5y = 5b\). Subtracting the first equation from this gives \(3x = 5b - a\), which yields \(x = \frac{5b - a}{3}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(4x + 3y = a\)
\(x - y = b\)
qs.s: From the second equation, \(x = y + b\). Substituting this into the first equation gives \(4(y + b) + 3y = a\), which simplifies to \(7y + 4b = a\), so \(y = \frac{a - 4b}{7}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3x + y = a\)
\(x - 2y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 to get \(6x + 2y = 2a\), then add the second equation to obtain \(7x = 2a + b\). Dividing by 7 yields \(x = \frac{2a + b}{7}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3x - 2y = a\)
\(x + y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the second equation by 3 to get \(3x + 3y = 3b\). Subtracting the first equation gives \((3x + 3y) - (3x - 2y) = 3b - a\), which simplifies to \(5y = 3b - a\), so \(y = \frac{3b - a}{5}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(2(x + 2y) - x = a\)
\(3(x - y) + 4y = b\)
qs.s: Simplify both equations to \(x + 4y = a\) and \(3x + y = b\). Substitute \(x = a - 4y\) into the second equation to get \(3(a - 4y) + y = b\), which simplifies to \(3a - 11y = b\), so \(y = \frac{3a - b}{11}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(5x - 4y = a\)
\(3x - 7y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 7 and the second by 4 to get \(35x - 28y = 7a\) and \(12x - 28y = 4b\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \(23x = 7a - 4b\), so \(x = \frac{7a - 4b}{23}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(3x + 5y = a\)
\(2x - 3y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 to obtain \(9x + 15y = 3a\) and \(10x - 15y = 5b\). Adding them eliminates \(y\) to give \(19x = 3a + 5b\), so \(x = \frac{3a + 5b}{19}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(4x - 3y = a\)
\(3x + 2y = b\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(12x - 9y = 3a\) and \(12x + 8y = 4b\). Subtracting the first from the second gives \(17y = 4b - 3a\), so \(y = \frac{4b - 3a}{17}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = a\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{y}{3} = b\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 6 to clear fractions, obtaining \(2x + 3y = 6a\) and \(3x - 2y = 6b\). Then multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3 to get \(4x + 6y = 12a\) and \(9x - 6y = 18b\); adding them yields \(13x = 12a + 18b\), so \(x = \frac{12a + 18b}{13}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax - by &= 9 \\ bx + ay &= 2 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(a\) to get \(a^2x - aby = 9a\) and the second equation by \(b\) to get \(b^2x + aby = 2b\). Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\), giving \((a^2 + b^2)x = 9a + 2b\), so \(x = \frac{9a + 2b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax + by &= -15 \\ bx - ay &= 8 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(b\) to get \(abx + b^2y = -15b\) and the second by \(a\) to get \(abx - a^2y = 8a\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \((a^2 + b^2)y = -15b - 8a\), so \(y = \frac{-8a - 15b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax + by &= 5 \\ bx - ay &= 12 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(a\) to get \(a^2x + aby = 5a\) and the second equation by \(b\) to get \(b^2x - aby = 12b\). Adding the two equations eliminates \(y\) and yields \((a^2 + b^2)x = 5a + 12b\), so \(x = \frac{5a + 12b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax + by &= 3 \\ bx - ay &= -4 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(b\) to get \(abx + b^2y = 3b\) and the second equation by \(a\) to get \(abx - a^2y = -4a\). Subtracting the second equation from the first gives \((a^2 + b^2)y = 3b - (-4a) = 4a + 3b\), so \(y = \frac{4a + 3b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax + by &= -11 \\ bx - ay &= 6 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(a\) to get \(a^2x + aby = -11a\) and the second by \(b\) to get \(b^2x - aby = 6b\). Adding the equations produces \((a^2 + b^2)x = -11a + 6b\), so \(x = \frac{-11a + 6b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} 2ax + 3by &= -5 \\ 3bx - 2ay &= 12 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2a\) to get \(4a^2x + 6aby = -10a\) and the second by \(3b\) to get \(9b^2x - 6aby = 36b\). Adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to give \((4a^2 + 9b^2)x = -10a + 36b\), so \(x = \frac{-10a + 36b}{4a^2 + 9b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} \frac{a}{3}x + \frac{b}{2}y &= 5 \\ \frac{b}{3}x - \frac{a}{2}y &= 1 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying both equations by 6 to obtain \(2ax + 3by = 30\) and \(2bx - 3ay = 6\). Multiply the first by \(a\) and the second by \(b\), then add them to get \(2(a^2 + b^2)x = 30a + 6b\), which simplifies to \(x = \frac{15a + 3b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(x\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} ax + by &= 24 \\ bx + ay &= -18 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(a\) to get \(a^2x + aby = 24a\) and the second by \(b\) to get \(b^2x + aby = -18b\). Subtracting the second equation from the first eliminates \(y\) and yields \((a^2 - b^2)x = 24a - (-18b) = 24a + 18b\), so \(x = \frac{24a + 18b}{a^2 - b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} 3ax - 4by &= 7 \\ 4bx + 3ay &= -2 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(4b\) to get \(12abx - 16b^2y = 28b\) and the second by \(3a\) to get \(12abx + 9a^2y = -6a\). Subtracting the first from the second eliminates \(x\), giving \((9a^2 + 16b^2)y = -6a - 28b\), which yields \(y = \frac{-6a - 28b}{9a^2 + 16b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system for \(y\) in terms of \(a\) and \(b\):
\(\displaystyle \begin{aligned} \frac{a}{2}x - \frac{b}{5}y &= 3 \\ \frac{b}{2}x + \frac{a}{5}y &= -2 \end{aligned}\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 10 to clear fractions, giving \(5ax - 2by = 30\) and \(5bx + 2ay = -20\). Multiply the first by \(b\) and the second by \(a\), then subtract the first from the second to get \(2(a^2 + b^2)y = -20a - 30b\), so \(y = \frac{-10a - 15b}{a^2 + b^2}\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(2x + 5y = -9\)
\(x = -3y - 7\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = -3y - 7\) into the first equation to get \(2(-3y - 7) + 5y = -9\), which simplifies to \(-y - 14 = -9\), giving \(y = -5\). Then substitute \(y = -5\) into \(x = -3(-5) - 7\) to get \(x = 8\), so the solution is \((8, -5)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(4x - 3y = -10\)
\(y = 2x + 4\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x + 4\) into the first equation to obtain \(4x - 3(2x + 4) = -10\), which simplifies to \(-2x - 12 = -10\), giving \(x = -1\). Substituting \(x = -1\) into the second equation yields \(y = 2(-1) + 4 = 2\), so the solution is \((-1, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(5x - 2y = 12\)
\(y = -4x + 7\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -4x + 7\) into the first equation to get \(5x - 2(-4x + 7) = 12\), which simplifies to \(13x - 14 = 12\), giving \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(y = -4(2) + 7\) yields \(y = -1\), so the solution is \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(2x + 3y = 7\)
\(x = 3y - 1\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(x = 3y - 1\) into the first equation to get \(2(3y - 1) + 3y = 7\), which simplifies to \(9y - 2 = 7\), giving \(y = 1\). Substituting \(y = 1\) into \(x = 3(1) - 1\) gives \(x = 2\), so the solution is \((2, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(3x - 4y = 1\)
\(y = 2x - 4\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Substitute \(y = 2x - 4\) into the first equation to get \(3x - 4(2x - 4) = 1\), which simplifies to \(-5x + 16 = 1\), giving \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into the second equation gives \(y = 2(3) - 4 = 2\), so the solution is \((3, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(4x - 3y = 2(x - y) + 7\)
\(5(x + 1) - 2y = 3x + 15\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Simplify both equations by distributing and combining like terms to obtain \(2x - y = 7\) and \(x - y = 5\). Subtracting the second equation from the first yields \(x = 2\), and substituting \(x = 2\) into \(x - y = 5\) gives \(y = -3\), so the solution is \((2, -3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(\frac{x}{3} + \frac{y}{2} = 4\)
\(\frac{2x}{3} - \frac{y}{4} = 3\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the first equation by 6 to get \(2x + 3y = 24\) and the second by 12 to get \(8x - 3y = 36\). Adding these equations yields \(10x = 60\), so \(x = 6\), and substituting into \(2(6) + 3y = 24\) gives \(y = 4\), so the solution is \((6, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(7x - 4y = 57\)
\(3x + 5y = 11\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 5 and the second by 4 to obtain \(35x - 20y = 285\) and \(12x + 20y = 44\). Adding the two equations results in \(47x = 329\), which gives \(x = 7\), and substituting into \(3(7) + 5y = 11\) gives \(y = -2\), so the solution is \((7, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(3(x - 2) - 2(y + 3) = 2\)
\(4(x + 1) + 5(y - 2) = 5\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Expand and simplify the equations to standard form to obtain \(3x - 2y = 14\) and \(4x + 5y = 11\). Multiplying the first equation by 5 and the second by 2 and adding them gives \(23x = 92\), so \(x = 4\), which leads to \(y = -1\), giving the solution \((4, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of linear equations:
\(\frac{x + 1}{3} + \frac{y + 4}{2} = 5\)
\(\frac{2x - 1}{3} - \frac{3y - 2}{4} = 2\)

What is the solution \((x, y)\)?
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 6 to obtain \(2x + 3y = 16\) and the second equation by 12 to obtain \(8x - 9y = 22\). Multiplying the first equation by 3 and adding it to the second gives \(14x = 70\), so \(x = 5\), which then gives \(y = 2\), yielding the solution \((5, 2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(3x + 5y = 1\)
\(4x + 3y = 5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 to obtain \(9x + 15y = 3\) and \(20x + 15y = 25\). Subtracting the first from the second gives \(11x = 22\), so \(x = 2\), and substituting into the first equation yields \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(4x + 3y = 7\)
\(5x + 2y = 14\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 2 and the second by 3 to get \(8x + 6y = 14\) and \(15x + 6y = 42\). Subtracting gives \(7x = 28\), so \(x = 4\), and substituting into \(4(4) + 3y = 7\) gives \(y = -3\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(3x - 4y = -2\)
\(5x - 3y = -7\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(9x - 12y = -6\) and \(20x - 12y = -28\). Subtracting gives \(-11x = 22\), so \(x = -2\), and substituting gives \(y = -1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(4x + 3y = 13\)
\(3x + 5y = 18\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(12x + 9y = 39\) and \(12x + 20y = 72\). Subtracting yields \(11y = 33\), so \(y = 3\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(x = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(2x + 5y = 4\)
\(5x + 3y = -9\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 5 to get \(6x + 15y = 12\) and \(25x + 15y = -45\). Subtracting the equations yields \(-19x = 57\), so \(x = -3\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(y = 2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(\frac{x}{2} + \frac{y}{5} = 2\)
\(\frac{2x}{3} - \frac{3y}{5} = 7\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the first equation by 10 and the second by 15, giving \(5x + 2y = 20\) and \(10x - 9y = 105\). Multiplying the first by 2 and subtracting from the second yields \(-13y = 65\), so \(y = -5\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(5x + 2y - 1 = 2(x - y) + 6\)
\(3(2x + y) - 4 = x - 3y + 5\)
qs.s: Simplify both equations by distributing and moving all variable terms to one side, yielding \(3x + 4y = 7\) and \(5x + 6y = 9\). Multiplying the first by 3 and the second by 2 and then subtracting gives \(x = -3\), which yields \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(8x + 5y = 171\)
\(6x + 7y = 177\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 3 and the second by 4 to get \(24x + 15y = 513\) and \(24x + 28y = 708\). Subtracting gives \(13y = 195\), so \(y = 15\), and substituting into the first equation gives \(x = 12\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(0.4x + 0.3y = 4.7\)
\(0.7x - 0.2y = 4.6\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 10 to clear decimals, resulting in \(4x + 3y = 47\) and \(7x - 2y = 46\). Multiply the first by 2 and the second by 3, then add to get \(29x = 232\), which gives \(x = 8\) and \(y = 5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(4(x - 1) + 3(y + 2) = 10\)
\(3(x + 2y) - 5(y - 1) = 1\)
qs.s: Expand and combine like terms to write the system in standard form as \(4x + 3y = 8\) and \(3x + y = -4\). From the second equation, \(y = -4 - 3x\); substituting into the first yields \(x = -4\), which gives \(y = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = 3x - 5\)
\(y = -x + 7\)
qs.s: Equating the two expressions for \(y\) gives \(3x - 5 = -x + 7\), which simplifies to \(4x = 12\) and yields \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(y = 3x - 5\) gives \(y = 3(3) - 5 = 4\), so the solution is \((3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = 4x - 7\)
\(y = -2x + 5\)
qs.s: Setting the equations equal gives \(4x - 7 = -2x + 5\), which simplifies to \(6x = 12\), so \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(y = 4x - 7\) gives \(y = 4(2) - 7 = 1\), giving the solution \((2, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = -4x + 2\)
\(y = -x - 4\)
qs.s: Setting the two expressions for \(y\) equal gives \(-4x + 2 = -x - 4\), which simplifies to \(3x = 6\) or \(x = 2\). Substituting \(x = 2\) into \(y = -x - 4\) yields \(y = -2 - 4 = -6\), giving the solution \((2, -6)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = -3x - 2\)
\(y = x + 6\)
qs.s: Setting \(-3x - 2 = x + 6\) gives \(-4x = 8\), so \(x = -2\). Substituting \(x = -2\) into \(y = x + 6\) yields \(y = -2 + 6 = 4\), giving the solution \((-2, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = 2x + 5\)
\(y = 5x - 4\)
qs.s: Equating the expressions gives \(2x + 5 = 5x - 4\), which rearranges to \(3x = 9\), so \(x = 3\). Substituting \(x = 3\) into \(y = 2x + 5\) produces \(y = 2(3) + 5 = 11\), resulting in the solution \((3, 11)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\frac{1}{4}x + \frac{1}{3}y = 3\)
\(\frac{1}{2}x - \frac{5}{6}y = \frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(12\) gives \(3x + 4y = 36\) and the second by \(6\) gives \(3x - 5y = 9\). Subtracting the two equations yields \(9y = 27\), so \(y = 3\), and substituting back into \(3x + 4(3) = 36\) gives \(x = 8\), so the solution is \((8, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(3(x - 1) + 2(y + 3) = 14\)
\(4(x + 2) - 3(y - 1) = 37\)
qs.s: Simplifying the equations gives \(3x + 2y = 11\) and \(4x - 3y = 26\). Multiplying the first by \(3\) and the second by \(2\), then adding, yields \(17x = 85\), so \(x = 5\), and substituting into \(3(5) + 2y = 11\) gives \(y = -2\), for a solution of \((5, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(0.5x + 0.2y = 2.8\)
\(0.3x - 0.4y = 2.2\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by \(10\) to obtain \(5x + 2y = 28\) and \(3x - 4y = 22\). Multiplying the first by \(2\) and adding to the second gives \(13x = 78\), so \(x = 6\), and substituting into \(5(6) + 2y = 28\) gives \(y = -1\), yielding \((6, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(y = \frac{3}{4}x - 5\)
\(y = -\frac{1}{3}x + 8\)
qs.s: Setting \(\frac{3}{4}x - 5 = -\frac{1}{3}x + 8\) and multiplying through by \(12\) yields \(9x - 60 = -4x + 96\), which gives \(13x = 156\) or \(x = 12\). Substituting into \(y = \frac{3}{4}(12) - 5\) yields \(y = 4\), resulting in \((12, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(4x + 3y = 61\)
\(5x - 2y = 13\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by \(2\) to get \(8x + 6y = 122\) and the second by \(3\) to get \(15x - 6y = 39\). Adding these equations yields \(23x = 161\), so \(x = 7\), and substituting into \(4(7) + 3y = 61\) yields \(y = 11\), giving \((7, 11)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(x + 2y = -2x - y + 6\)
\(3x - y = x + y + 12\)
qs.s: Simplifying gives \(x + y = 2\) and \(x - y = 6\). Adding the equations yields \(2x = 8\), so \(x = 4\) and \(y = -2\), resulting in \((4, -2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(3x - y = x - 4y - 7\)
\(-2x + y = x + 3y + 8\)
qs.s: Rearranging terms gives \(2x + 3y = -7\) and \(-3x - 2y = 8\). Solving by elimination gives \(y = -1\) and \(x = -2\), so the solution is \((-2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(4x - 2y = x + y - 6\)
\(2x + 3y = -x + y + 9\)
qs.s: Simplifying both equations yields \(x - y = -2\) and \(3x + 2y = 9\). Substituting \(x = y - 2\) into the second equation gives \(y = 3\) and \(x = 1\), which gives \((1, 3)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(-3x + 2y = -x - y + 18\)
\(2x + 5y = x + y + 13\)
qs.s: Combining like terms simplifies the equations to \(-2x + 3y = 18\) and \(x + 4y = 13\). Solving this system gives \(x = -3\) and \(y = 4\), so the solution is \((-3, 4)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(5x - y = 2x - 3y + 4\)
\(4x + y = 3x + 4y + 5\)
qs.s: Rearranging the equations into standard form gives \(3x + 2y = 4\) and \(x - 3y = 5\). Solving by substitution or elimination gives \(x = 2\) and \(y = -1\), so the solution is \((2, -1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(\frac{2x - y}{3} + 1 = \frac{x + 3y}{4} + 2\)
\(\frac{x + y}{2} - \frac{2x - y}{3} = y - 1\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions by multiplying the equations by 12 and 6, respectively, simplifies them to \(5x - 13y = 12\) and \(x + y = 6\). Solving this system yields \(x = 5\) and \(y = 1\), giving \((5, 1)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(8x - y + 5 = 2x + 3y + 14\)
\(7x + 2y - 3 = 3x - 4y - 10\)
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form gives \(6x - 4y = 9\) and \(4x + 6y = -7\). Multiplying the equations by 3 and 2 respectively and adding eliminates \(y\), giving \(26x = 13\), so \(x = 1/2\) and \(y = -3/2\), which is \((1/2, -3/2)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(5(2x + y) - 3(x - 2y) = 4x - y + 72\)
\(4(x + y) + 2(3x - y) = -(3x - 5y) - 73\)
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms leads to \(x + 4y = 24\) and \(13x - 3y = -73\). Substituting \(x = 24 - 4y\) into the second equation yields \(y = 7\) and \(x = -4\), so the solution is \((-4, 7)\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations for \((x, y)\):
\(3(x - 2y) - 4 = 2(2x + y) + 9\)
\(2(x - 3y) + 3x = -(x + 2y) + 26\)
qs.s: Expanding and collecting like terms produces \(x + 8y = -13\) and \(3x - 2y = 13\). Solving by substitution or elimination gives \(x = 3\) and \(y = -2\), resulting in \((3, -2)\).

Multiplying both equations by 10 and collecting like terms results in \(3x - 5y = -15\) and \(4x + 5y = 155\). Adding the equations eliminates \(y\) to give \(7x = 140\), so \(x = 20\) and \(y = 15\), giving \((20, 15)\).

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(3x + 6y = 18\)
\(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 3\) into the first equation to get \(3x + 6\left(-\frac{1}{2}x + 3\right) = 18\), which simplifies to \(3x - 3x + 18 = 18\), or \(18 = 18\). Because this is an identity, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(x - 4y = -12\)
\(y = \frac{1}{4}x + 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1}{4}x + 3\) into the first equation to obtain \(x - 4\left(\frac{1}{4}x + 3\right) = -12\), which simplifies to \(-12 = -12\). Since the resulting statement is always true, there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(x + 2y = 8\)
\(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 4\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = -\frac{1}{2}x + 4\) into the first equation to get \(x + 2\left(-\frac{1}{2}x + 4\right) = 8\), which simplifies to \(x - x + 8 = 8\), or \(8 = 8\). Since this equation is always true, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(2x - 4y = -8\)
\(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1}{2}x + 2\) into the first equation to yield \(2x - 4\left(\frac{1}{2}x + 2\right) = -8\), which simplifies to \(2x - 2x - 8 = -8\), or \(-8 = -8\). Because this equality is an identity, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(x - 3y = 9\)
\(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 3\)
qs.s: Substitute \(y = \frac{1}{3}x - 3\) into the first equation to obtain \(x - 3\left(\frac{1}{3}x - 3\right) = 9\), which simplifies to \(x - x + 9 = 9\), or \(9 = 9\). Because this statement is an identity true for all real values, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(2(3x - y) - 2(y + 6) = 3x + 12\)
\(\frac{x}{4} - \frac{y}{3} = 2\)
qs.s: Simplifying the first equation yields \(3x - 4y = 24\), and multiplying the second equation by the LCD of \(12\) produces \(3x - 4y = 24\). Since both equations represent the exact same line, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(\frac{x + 1}{2} - \frac{y - 2}{3} = 2\)
\(\frac{x - 1}{4} - \frac{y + 1}{6} = 0\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(6\) yields \(3(x + 1) - 2(y - 2) = 12\), which simplifies to \(3x - 2y = 5\), and multiplying the second equation by \(12\) gives \(3(x - 1) - 2(y + 1) = 0\), which also simplifies to \(3x - 2y = 5\). Since both equations are equivalent, the system has infinitely many solutions.

Simplifying the first equation gives \(4x - 5y + 11 = 2x - 2y + 20\), which reduces to \(2x - 3y = 9\), while multiplying the second equation by \(7\) gives \(4x - 6y = 18\), or \(2x - 3y = 9\). Because the equations are identical, the system has infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(4(x - y) - 3 = 2(x + y) + 9\)
\(\frac{2x - 3}{6} - y = \frac{3}{2}\)
qs.s: Expanding and combining like terms in the first equation gives \(2x - 6y = 12\), and multiplying the second equation by \(6\) also gives \(2x - 6y = 12\). Subtracting the two identical equations yields \(0 = 0\), meaning the system has infinitely many solutions.

Simplifying the first equation gives \(0.7x + 0.1y = 2.1\), or \(7x + y = 21\) after multiplying by \(10\), while multiplying the second equation by \(7\) yields \(7x + y = 21\). Because the two equations are identical, there are infinitely many solutions.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(2x - 8y = 3\)
\(3x - 12y = 4\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) yields \(6x - 24y = 9\), and multiplying the second equation by \(2\) yields \(6x - 24y = 8\). Subtracting the equations gives the false statement \(0 = 1\), meaning there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(15x - 10y = 4\)
\(6x - 4y = 3\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) gives \(30x - 20y = 8\), while multiplying the second equation by \(5\) gives \(30x - 20y = 15\). Subtracting these equations produces \(0 = -7\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(10x + 15y = 8\)
\(6x + 9y = 5\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives \(30x + 45y = 24\), and multiplying the second by \(5\) gives \(30x + 45y = 25\). Subtracting the two equations results in \(0 = -1\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(6x - 4y = 5\)
\(9x - 6y = 7\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives \(18x - 12y = 15\), and multiplying the second equation by \(2\) gives \(18x - 12y = 14\). Subtracting the equations yields \(0 = 1\), which is a contradiction, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(8x + 6y = 9\)
\(12x + 9y = 11\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(3\) gives \(24x + 18y = 27\), and multiplying the second by \(2\) gives \(24x + 18y = 22\). Subtracting eliminates both variables and leaves \(0 = 5\), which is impossible, so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(\frac{2x}{3} - y = \frac{1}{2}\)
\(\frac{x}{2} - \frac{3y}{4} = \frac{2}{5}\)
qs.s: Clearing fractions by multiplying the first equation by \(6\) and the second by \(20\) yields \(4x - 6y = 3\) and \(10x - 15y = 8\). Multiplying these by \(5\) and \(2\) respectively gives \(20x - 30y = 15\) and \(20x - 30y = 16\), which subtract to \(0 = -1\), meaning there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(2(3x - y) = 6y + 5\)
\(3(3x - 2y) - 6y = 7\)
qs.s: Simplifying both equations gives \(6x - 8y = 5\) and \(9x - 12y = 7\). Multiplying the first by \(3\) and the second by \(2\) results in \(18x - 24y = 15\) and \(18x - 24y = 14\), which subtract to give \(0 = 1\), so there is no solution.

Expanding and combining like terms simplifies the equations to \(6x - 5y = 7\) and \(12x - 10y = 11\). Multiplying the first equation by \(2\) gives \(12x - 10y = 14\), which contradicts \(12x - 10y = 11\), showing that there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(\frac{x + 1}{2} - \frac{2y + 1}{3} = \frac{5}{6}\)
\(\frac{3x - 1}{4} - y = \frac{3}{8}\)
qs.s: Multiplying the first equation by \(6\) and simplifying yields \(3x - 4y = 4\), while multiplying the second by \(8\) yields \(6x - 8y = 5\). Multiplying the first simplified equation by \(2\) gives \(6x - 8y = 8\), which contradicts \(6x - 8y = 5\), so the system has no solution.

qs.q:
Solve by any method:
\(12x - 15 = 20y + 4\)
\(15y - 9x + 8 = 0\)
qs.s: Rearranging both equations into standard form gives \(12x - 20y = 19\) and \(9x - 15y = 8\). Multiplying the first by \(3\) and the second by \(4\) produces \(36x - 60y = 57\) and \(36x - 60y = 32\), which subtract to \(0 = 25\), so there is no solution.

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{3}x + \frac{1}{2}y = -\frac{7}{6}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{4}x + \frac{2}{5}y = 1\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 6 and the second by 20 to clear denominators, giving \(2x + 3y = -7\) and \(15x + 8y = 20\). Solving this system yields \(x = 4\) and \(y = -5\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{6}x - \frac{1}{4}y = \frac{11}{2}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{3}x + \frac{4}{5}y = \frac{12}{5}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 12 to get \(10x - 3y = 66\), and the second by 15 to get \(10x + 12y = 36\). Subtracting the equations gives \(15y = -30\), so \(y = -2\) and \(x = 6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{5}x - \frac{1}{3}y = \frac{6}{5}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{7}{10}x + \frac{1}{4}y = -\frac{29}{10}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 15 to get \(6x - 5y = 18\) and the second by 20 to get \(14x + 5y = -58\). Adding the two equations gives \(20x = -40\), which leads to \(x = -2\) and \(y = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{2}{5}y = \frac{1}{10}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}x + \frac{2}{3}y = \frac{23}{12}\)
qs.s: Clearing denominators by multiplying the first equation by 10 and the second by 12 yields \(5x + 4y = 1\) and \(3x + 8y = 23\). Eliminating \(y\) results in \(7x = -21\), so \(x = -3\) and \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3}{8}x + \frac{1}{6}y = \frac{8}{3}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{4}x - \frac{3}{10}y = \frac{13}{5}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 24 and the second by 20 to obtain \(9x + 4y = 64\) and \(5x - 6y = 52\). Using elimination gives \(37x = 296\), so \(x = 8\) and \(y = -2\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{3x - 2y}{5} - \frac{x - 4y}{3} = 2\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 2y}{3} + \frac{2x - y}{7} = 3\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 15 and simplify to \(2x + 7y = 15\), then multiply the second by 21 to get \(13x + 11y = 63\). Solving the resulting system gives \(x = 4\) and \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{5}{12}x - \frac{3}{8}y = 4\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{7}{18}x + \frac{5}{12}y = \frac{2}{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 24 to get \(10x - 9y = 96\) and the second by 36 to get \(14x + 15y = 24\). Eliminating \(y\) gives \(92x = 552\), so \(x = 6\) and \(y = -4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}(x - 2y) + \frac{1}{3}(2x + y) = \frac{17}{6}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{5}(x + y) - \frac{1}{4}(x - y) = \frac{11}{10}\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 6 to simplify to \(7x - 4y = 17\), and the second by 20 to get \(3x + 13y = 22\). Solving this system yields \(x = 3\) and \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{2}{3}x - \frac{1}{4}y = \frac{1}{6}x + \frac{1}{2}y + 1\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{1}{2}x + \frac{1}{6}y = -\frac{1}{4}x + \frac{1}{2}y + \frac{14}{3}\)
qs.s: Multiply both equations by 12 and collect like terms to obtain \(2x - 3y = 4\) and \(9x - 4y = 56\). Solving by elimination yields \(x = 8\) and \(y = 4\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations:
\(\displaystyle \frac{x + 3}{4} - \frac{y - 2}{3} = \frac{7}{3}\)
\(\displaystyle \frac{2x - 1}{3} + \frac{y + 3}{2} = 5\)
qs.s: Clear denominators by multiplying the first equation by 12 to get \(3x - 4y = 11\), and the second by 6 to get \(4x + 3y = 23\). Solving this linear system gives \(x = 5\) and \(y = 1\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.08x - 0.15y = -0.24\)
\(0.7x - 0.4y = 5.2\)
qs.s: Clear decimals to get \(8x - 15y = -24\) and \(7x - 4y = 52\). Multiplying the first equation by 4 and the second by 15, then subtracting gives \(73x = 876\), so \(x = 12\) and \(y = 8\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.09x + 0.16y = -0.68\)
\(0.3x + 1.4y = 3.8\)
qs.s: Clear decimals to obtain \(9x + 16y = -68\) and \(3x + 14y = 38\). Multiplying the second equation by 3 and subtracting the first gives \(26y = 182\), so \(y = 7\) and \(x = -20\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.06x + 0.11y = 0.46\)
\(0.9x + 0.5y = 11.5\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 100 to get \(6x + 11y = 46\) and the second by 10 to get \(9x + 5y = 115\). Multiplying by 3 and 2 respectively and subtracting gives \(23y = -92\), so \(y = -4\) and \(x = 15\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.15x - 0.04y = 1.44\)
\(0.7x + 0.3y = 3.8\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 100 to get \(15x - 4y = 144\) and the second by 10 to get \(7x + 3y = 38\). Multiplying the first by 3 and the second by 4, then adding gives \(73x = 584\), which yields \(x = 8\) and \(y = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.07x + 0.04y = 0.18\)
\(0.6x + 1.1y = 12.9\)
qs.s: Clear decimals to obtain \(7x + 4y = 18\) and \(6x + 11y = 129\). Multiplying the equations by 6 and 7 respectively and subtracting yields \(53y = 795\), so \(y = 15\) and \(x = -6\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.16x + 0.24 = -0.09y\)
\(0.25x + 0.14y = -0.39\)
qs.s: Rearranging into standard form with cleared decimals gives \(16x + 9y = -24\) and \(25x + 14y = -39\). Multiplying the equations by 14 and 9 respectively and subtracting yields \(x = -15\), which gives \(y = 24\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.025x + 0.015y = 0.625\)
\(0.08x - 0.06y = 0.38\)
qs.s: Multiply the first equation by 1000 and divide by 5 to get \(5x + 3y = 125\), and multiply the second by 100 and divide by 2 to get \(4x - 3y = 19\). Adding the two simplified equations yields \(9x = 144\), which gives \(x = 16\) and \(y = 15\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.12x - 0.05y + 0.64 = 0.04x + 0.03y + 2\)
\(0.7x + 0.2y - 1.6 = 0.3x - 0.6y + 2.8\)
qs.s: Collecting terms and clearing decimals gives \(x - y = 17\) and \(x + 2y = 11\). Subtracting the first equation from the second yields \(3y = -6\), so \(y = -2\) and \(x = 15\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.2(x + 2y) + 0.15(x - y) = 4.15\)
\(0.04(3x - y) - 0.06(x - 2y) = 1.12\)
qs.s: Expanding and simplifying the equations gives \(7x + 5y = 83\) and \(3x + 4y = 56\). Multiplying by 4 and 5 respectively and subtracting gives \(13x = 52\), which yields \(x = 4\) and \(y = 11\).

qs.q:
Solve the system of equations by any method:
\(0.05(2x + y) - 0.03(x - y) = 0.73\)
\(0.4x - 0.3(x - 2y) = 2.5\)
qs.s: Distributing and combining like terms simplifies the equations to \(7x + 8y = 73\) and \(x + 6y = 25\). Substituting \(x = 25 - 6y\) into the first equation gives \(34y = 102\), so \(y = 3\) and \(x = 7\).

exercises.name: Number, Geometry, and Age Word Problems

qs.q: One number is 5 more than another number, and their sum is 19. Find the larger number.
qs.s: Writing the system as \(x - y = 5\) and \(x + y = 19\), adding the two equations yields \(2x = 24\), which gives the larger number \(x = 12\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 8, and their difference is 12. Find the smaller number.
qs.s: Adding the equations \(x + y = 8\) and \(x - y = 12\) gives \(2x = 20\) so \(x = 10\), and substituting into the first equation yields the smaller number \(y = 8 - 10 = -2\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is -4, and their difference is 16. Find the larger number.
qs.s: Adding the equations \(x + y = -4\) and \(x - y = 16\) gives \(2x = 12\), which gives the larger number \(x = 6\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 25, and their difference is 7. Find the smaller number.
qs.s: Subtracting the equation \(x - y = 7\) from \(x + y = 25\) yields \(2y = 18\), so the smaller number is \(y = 9\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 14, and their difference is 4. Find the larger number.
qs.s: Adding the equations \(x + y = 14\) and \(x - y = 4\) yields \(2x = 18\), so the larger number is \(x = 9\).

qs.q: A father is currently four times as old as his son. In 14 years, the father will be twice as old as his son will be then. Find the father's current age.
qs.s: Let \(F\) and \(S\) be their current ages; substituting \(F = 4S\) into \(F + 14 = 2(S + 14)\) gives \(4S + 14 = 2S + 28\), leading to \(S = 7\) and \(F = 28\).

qs.q: The sum of two numbers is 43. Twice the smaller number added to three times the larger number is 114. Find the smaller number.
qs.s: Let \(x\) be the larger number and \(y\) be the smaller; solving the system \(x + y = 43\) and \(3x + 2y = 114\) by multiplying the first equation by 2 gives \(x = 28\), so \(y = 43 - 28 = 15\).

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangle is 64 cm. The length of the rectangle is 4 cm less than three times its width. Find the length of the rectangle in centimeters.
qs.s: From the perimeter, \(2l + 2w = 64\) gives \(l + w = 32\); substituting \(l = 3w - 4\) yields \(4w - 4 = 32\), which gives \(w = 9\) cm and length \(l = 3(9) - 4 = 23\) cm.

qs.q: The difference between two numbers is 24. The larger number is 2 more than three times the smaller number. Find the larger number.
qs.s: Setting up \(x - y = 24\) and \(x = 3y + 2\), substituting gives \((3y + 2) - y = 24\), which yields \(2y = 22\), so \(y = 11\) and the larger number is \(x = 11 + 24 = 35\).

qs.q: In an isosceles triangle, each of the two equal sides is 5 cm longer than half the base. If the perimeter of the triangle is 50 cm, find the length of the base in centimeters.
qs.s: Let \(b\) be the base and each equal side be \(s = \frac{1}{2}b + 5\); substituting into the perimeter equation \(2s + b = 50\) gives \(2(\frac{1}{2}b + 5) + b = 50\), so \(2b + 10 = 50\), giving \(b = 20\) cm.

exercises.name: Number, Geometry, and Age Word Problems

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular field is 110 m. The length of the field is 15 m greater than the width. Find the length of the field.
qs.s: Let \(l\) and \(w\) be the length and width; the system is \(l + w = 55\) and \(l = w + 15\). Substituting yields \(2w + 15 = 55\), so \(w = 20\text{ m}\) and \(l = 20 + 15 = 35\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular banner is 130 cm. The length of the banner is 25 cm more than its width. Find the length of the banner.
qs.s: Let \(l\) and \(w\) be the length and width; then \(l + w = 65\) and \(l = w + 25\). Substituting gives \(2w + 25 = 65\), so \(w = 20\text{ cm}\) and \(l = 20 + 25 = 45\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular picture frame is 72 cm. The width of the frame is 8 cm less than the length. Find the width of the frame.
qs.s: Let \(l\) and \(w\) be the length and width; then \(l + w = 36\) and \(l = w + 8\). Substituting gives \((w + 8) + w = 36\), so \(2w = 28\), yielding \(w = 14\text{ cm}\).

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular swimming pool is 64 m. The length of the pool is 12 m longer than the width. Find the width of the pool.
qs.s: Let \(l\) and \(w\) be the length and width; then \(l + w = 32\) and \(l = w + 12\). Substituting gives \(2w + 12 = 32\), so \(2w = 20\), which gives \(w = 10\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The perimeter of a rectangular garden is 84 m. The length of the garden is 6 m more than the width. Find the length of the garden.
