qs.s: Draw altitude \(h = 15\sin 65^\circ \approx 13.595\text{ cm}\) from \(Q\) to \(PR\). Then \(PS = 15\cos 65^\circ \approx 6.339\text{ cm}\) and \(SR = \sqrt{22^2 - 13.595^2} \approx 17.297\text{ cm}\), making the area \(\frac{1}{2}(6.339 + 17.297)(13.595) \approx 160.7\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: In \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\), \(\mathrm{AB} = 14\text{ cm}\), \(\mathrm{BC} = 25\text{ cm}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 30^\circ\). Determine the area of \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\). (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: Draw altitude \(h\) from \(B\) to \(AC\): \(h = 14\sin 30^\circ = 7\text{ cm}\), \(AD = 14\cos 30^\circ \approx 12.124\text{ cm}\), and \(CD = \sqrt{25^2 - 7^2} = 24\text{ cm}\). The base is \(AC = 12.124 + 24 = 36.124\text{ cm}\), giving an area of \(\frac{1}{2}(36.124)(7) \approx 126.4\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: In \(\Delta\mathrm{XYZ}\), \(\mathrm{XY} = 6\text{ m}\), \(\mathrm{YZ} = 10\text{ m}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{X} = 40^\circ\). Determine the area of \(\Delta\mathrm{XYZ}\). (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: The altitude from \(Y\) to \(XZ\) is \(h = 6\sin 40^\circ \approx 3.857\text{ m}\). With \(XW = 6\cos 40^\circ \approx 4.596\text{ m}\) and \(WZ = \sqrt{10^2 - 3.857^2} \approx 9.226\text{ m}\), the area is \(\frac{1}{2}(4.596 + 9.226)(3.857) \approx 26.7\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A surveyor maps a triangular plot of land \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\) with \(\mathrm{AB} = 125\text{ m}\), \(\mathrm{BC} = 210\text{ m}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 52^\circ\). Determine the area of the plot. (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: The altitude from \(B\) to \(AC\) is \(h = 125\sin 52^\circ \approx 98.501\text{ m}\). The base segments are \(AD = 125\cos 52^\circ \approx 76.958\text{ m}\) and \(CD = \sqrt{210^2 - 98.501^2} \approx 185.466\text{ m}\), yielding an area of \(\frac{1}{2}(76.958 + 185.466)(98.501) \approx 12924.5\text{ m}^2\).

qs.q: A triangular shade sail \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\) has \(\mathrm{AB} = 5.2\text{ m}\), \(\mathrm{BC} = 8.5\text{ m}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 48^\circ\). If the shade fabric costs \(\$35\) per square meter, determine the total cost of fabric for the sail. (Round to the nearest dollar.)
qs.s: The altitude is \(h = 5.2\sin 48^\circ \approx 3.864\text{ m}\) and base \(AC = 5.2\cos 48^\circ + \sqrt{8.5^2 - 3.864^2} \approx 3.479 + 7.571 = 11.050\text{ m}\), giving an area of \(\frac{1}{2}(11.050)(3.864) \approx 21.352\text{ m}^2\). Multiplying by \(\$35/\text{m}^2\) gives a total cost of \(21.352 \times 35 \approx \$747\).

qs.q: A rectangular sheet of metal measures \(20\text{ cm}\) by \(30\text{ cm}\). A triangular piece \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\) with \(\mathrm{AB} = 15\text{ cm}\), \(\mathrm{BC} = 22\text{ cm}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 70^\circ\) is cut out from it. Determine the remaining area of the sheet metal. (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: In \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\), \(h = 15\sin 70^\circ \approx 14.095\text{ cm}\) and base \(AC = 15\cos 70^\circ + \sqrt{22^2 - 14.095^2} \approx 5.130 + 16.891 = 22.022\text{ cm}\), giving a triangle area of \(\frac{1}{2}(22.022)(14.095) \approx 155.2\text{ cm}^2\). Subtracting this from the rectangle's area (\(20 \times 30 = 600\)) leaves \(600 - 155.2 = 444.8\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: In parallelogram \(\mathrm{ABCD}\), side \(\mathrm{AB} = 16\text{ cm}\), diagonal \(\mathrm{BD} = 26\text{ cm}\), and \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 60^\circ\). Determine the total area of parallelogram \(\mathrm{ABCD}\). (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: In \(\Delta\mathrm{ABD}\), altitude \(h = 16\sin 60^\circ = 8\sqrt{3}\text{ cm}\), segment \(AE = 16\cos 60^\circ = 8\text{ cm}\), and \(ED = \sqrt{26^2 - (8\sqrt{3})^2} = 22\text{ cm}\), giving base \(AD = 30\text{ cm}\). The area of \(\Delta\mathrm{ABD}\) is \(\frac{1}{2}(30)(8\sqrt{3}) = 120\sqrt{3}\), so the parallelogram area is \(2 \times 120\sqrt{3} = 240\sqrt{3} \approx 415.7\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: In obtuse triangle \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\), \(\angle\mathrm{A} = 115^\circ\), \(\mathrm{AB} = 12\text{ cm}\), and \(\mathrm{BC} = 28\text{ cm}\). Determine the area of \(\Delta\mathrm{ABC}\). (Round to the nearest tenth.)
qs.s: The exterior altitude from \(B\) to the line of \(AC\) is \(h = 12\sin(180^\circ - 115^\circ) = 12\sin 65^\circ \approx 10.876\text{ cm}\), with extension \(AD = 12\cos 65^\circ \approx 5.071\text{ cm}\). Then \(CD = \sqrt{28^2 - 10.876^2} \approx 25.802\text{ cm}\), so base \(AC = CD - AD = 20.730\text{ cm}\) and \(\text{Area} = \frac{1}{2}(20.730)(10.876) \approx 112.7\text{ cm}^2\).

qs.q: From the observation deck of a tower 150 m above the ground, a surveyor spots two landmarks on level ground directly south. The angles of depression to the two landmarks are \(15^\circ\) and \(38^\circ\). How far apart are the two landmarks, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
qs.s: The distances to the landmarks are \(150 / \tan 38^\circ \approx 192.00\text{ m}\) and \(150 / \tan 15^\circ \approx 559.82\text{ m}\). The distance between them is \(559.82 - 192.00 = 367.8\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A drone hovering at an altitude of 250 m spots two cars on a straight road directly ahead. The angles of depression to the cars are \(24^\circ\) and \(48^\circ\). How far apart are the two cars? Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: The horizontal distance to the closer car is \(250 / \tan 48^\circ \approx 225.10\text{ m}\) and to the farther car is \(250 / \tan 24^\circ \approx 561.51\text{ m}\). The distance between the cars is \(561.51 - 225.10 = 336.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A helicopter is flying at an altitude of 800 ft. The pilot observes two rescue boats directly in front. The angles of depression to the boats are \(22^\circ\) and \(41^\circ\). What is the distance between the boats, to the nearest tenth of a foot?
qs.s: The horizontal distance to the near boat is \(800 / \tan 41^\circ \approx 920.30\text{ ft}\) and to the far boat is \(800 / \tan 22^\circ \approx 1980.07\text{ ft}\). The distance between them is \(1980.07 - 920.30 = 1059.8\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A hot air balloon is hovering at a height of 500 m. The pilot looks down at two tents located directly in line with each other on the ground. The angles of depression to the tents are \(26^\circ\) and \(52^\circ\). What is the distance between the two tents, to the nearest tenth of a metre?
qs.s: The horizontal distance to the nearer tent is \(500 / \tan 52^\circ \approx 390.64\text{ m}\) and to the farther tent is \(500 / \tan 26^\circ \approx 1025.15\text{ m}\). The distance between the tents is \(1025.15 - 390.64 = 634.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A person standing at the top of a cliff 120 m high spots two boats in the ocean directly in line with their view. The angles of depression to the boats are \(18^\circ\) and \(35^\circ\). Find the distance between the two boats, to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: The horizontal distances to the boats are \(120 / \tan 35^\circ \approx 171.38\text{ m}\) and \(120 / \tan 18^\circ \approx 369.32\text{ m}\). Subtracting gives \(369.32 - 171.38 = 197.9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A communication antenna sits on top of a 150 m tall building. From a point on level ground, the angle of elevation to the base of the antenna is \(42^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the antenna is \(51^\circ\). How tall is the antenna? Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: The distance to the building is \(d = 150 / \tan 42^\circ \approx 166.59\text{ m}\). The total height to the top of the antenna is \(H = 166.59 \cdot \tan 51^\circ \approx 205.72\text{ m}\), so the antenna height is \(205.72 - 150 = 55.7\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An airplane is flying at a constant altitude of 8500 m in a straight line directly over a tracking station. At one moment, the angle of elevation from the station to the plane is \(25^\circ\). A few minutes later, the plane has passed directly overhead to the opposite side of the station and the angle of elevation is \(38^\circ\). How far did the plane travel between the two observations? Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.
qs.s: Because the observations are on opposite sides of the station, add the horizontal distances: \(d = 8500 / \tan 25^\circ + 8500 / \tan 38^\circ \approx 18228.3\text{ m} + 10879.5\text{ m} = 29107.8\text{ m} \approx 29.1\text{ km}\).

qs.q: From the roof of a 45 m tall building, the angle of depression to the base of a nearby skyscraper is \(22^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the skyscraper is \(48^\circ\). How tall is the skyscraper? Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: The horizontal distance between the buildings is \(w = 45 / \tan 22^\circ \approx 111.38\text{ m}\). The height of the skyscraper above the roof is \(111.38 \cdot \tan 48^\circ \approx 123.70\text{ m}\), so the total height is \(123.70 + 45 = 168.7\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An observer whose eye level is 1.8 m above the ground stands on top of a 125 m vertical cliff. Looking out at the ocean, the observer spots two buoys that are directly in line with the observer. The angle of depression to the nearer buoy is \(44^\circ\) and to the farther buoy is \(19^\circ\). How far apart are the two buoys? Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: The total height of the observer is \(125 + 1.8 = 126.8\text{ m}\). The distances are \(126.8 / \tan 44^\circ \approx 131.31\text{ m}\) and \(126.8 / \tan 19^\circ \approx 368.25\text{ m}\), giving a separation of \(368.25 - 131.31 = 236.9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A surveyor measures the angle of elevation to the peak of a mountain to be \(28^\circ\). After walking 500 m closer to the mountain on level ground, the angle of elevation is \(39^\circ\). How high is the mountain? Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.
qs.s: Setting up the relation between the distances gives \(h / \tan 28^\circ - h / \tan 39^\circ = 500\). Factoring out \(h\) gives \(h(1.8807 - 1.2349) = 500\), so \(h = 500 / 0.6458 \approx 774.2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: From a distance of 150 yds across a field, an observer measures the angle of elevation to the bottom of a water tank's antenna as \(25.2^\circ\) and to the top of the antenna as \(28.6^\circ\). What is the height of the antenna? (Round to the nearest tenth of a yard.)
qs.s: The height to the antenna's top is \(150 \tan(28.6^\circ) \approx 81.79\text{ yds}\) and to the base is \(150 \tan(25.2^\circ) \approx 70.58\text{ yds}\). Subtracting gives \(81.79 - 70.58 = 11.21 \approx 11.2\text{ yds}\).

qs.q: From a point 110 ft in front of a parking garage, the angle of elevation to the bottom of a billboard on the roof is \(22.4^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the billboard is \(29.8^\circ\). What is the height of the billboard? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: The total height to the billboard's top is \(110 \tan(29.8^\circ) \approx 63.00\text{ ft}\) and the garage height is \(110 \tan(22.4^\circ) \approx 45.34\text{ ft}\). The height of the billboard is \(63.00 - 45.34 = 17.66 \approx 17.7\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: From a point 85 m in front of a building, the angle of elevation to the base of a communications tower mounted on the roof is \(42^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the tower is \(48^\circ\). How high is the tower? (Round to the nearest tenth of a meter.)
qs.s: The height to the top is \(85 \tan(48^\circ) \approx 94.40\text{ m}\) and the height to the base is \(85 \tan(42^\circ) \approx 76.53\text{ m}\). Subtracting gives the tower's height: \(94.40 - 76.53 = 17.87 \approx 17.9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Standing 75 m from the base of a barn, the angle of elevation to the base of a weather vane on the roof peak is \(18.5^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the weather vane is \(21.0^\circ\). How tall is the weather vane? (Round to the nearest tenth of a meter.)
qs.s: The height to the top of the weather vane is \(75 \tan(21.0^\circ) \approx 28.79\text{ m}\) and to its base is \(75 \tan(18.5^\circ) \approx 25.09\text{ m}\). The difference gives the height of the vane: \(28.79 - 25.09 = 3.70 \approx 3.7\text{ m}\).

qs.q: From a point 50 ft from the base of a monument's pedestal, the angle of elevation to the bottom of the statue on top of the pedestal is \(28^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the statue is \(35^\circ\). How tall is the statue? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: The height to the top of the statue is \(50 \tan(35^\circ) \approx 35.01\text{ ft}\) and to the bottom is \(50 \tan(28^\circ) \approx 26.59\text{ ft}\). The statue's height is \(35.01 - 26.59 = 8.42 \approx 8.4\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A 24-foot antenna is mounted on the roof of a building. From a point on level ground, the angle of elevation to the bottom of the antenna is \(38^\circ\) and the angle of elevation to the top of the antenna is \(44^\circ\). Find the height of the building, to the nearest tenth of a foot.
qs.s: Setting \(d(\tan 44^\circ - \tan 38^\circ) = 24\) gives a ground distance of \(d = 24 / (0.9657 - 0.7813) \approx 130.15\text{ ft}\). The height of the building is then \(H = 130.15 \tan(38^\circ) \approx 101.7\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: From the roof of a 40-meter-tall building, the angle of depression to the base of a taller building across the street is \(34^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the taller building is \(48^\circ\). How tall is the taller building? (Round to the nearest tenth of a meter.)
qs.s: The street width is \(w = 40 / \tan(34^\circ) \approx 59.30\text{ m}\), and the portion of the taller building above the roof is \(h_2 = 59.30 \tan(48^\circ) \approx 65.86\text{ m}\). Adding the building heights gives \(40 + 65.86 = 105.86 \approx 105.9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A 25-meter-tall lighthouse sits at the edge of a cliff that is 175 m above sea level. From the top of the lighthouse, an observer spots two buoys directly in line with each other offshore. The angles of depression to the two buoys are \(8.5^\circ\) and \(12.0^\circ\). How far apart are the two buoys? (Round to the nearest tenth of a meter.)
qs.s: The total elevation is \(175 + 25 = 200\text{ m}\). The distances to the buoys are \(200 / \tan(8.5^\circ) \approx 1338.23\text{ m}\) and \(200 / \tan(12.0^\circ) \approx 940.93\text{ m}\), so the distance between them is \(1338.23 - 940.93 = 397.30 \approx 397.3\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An observation deck is located 50 ft below the top of a skyscraper. From the top of the skyscraper, the angle of depression to a car on the street is \(42^\circ\). From the observation deck, the angle of depression to the same car is \(35^\circ\). What is the total height of the skyscraper? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: Setting up the distance equations gives \(H / \tan(42^\circ) = (H - 50) / \tan(35^\circ)\). Solving for \(H\) yields \(H = (50 \tan 42^\circ) / (\tan 42^\circ - \tan 35^\circ) \approx 45.020 / 0.2002 \approx 224.9\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: A surveyor at point \(A\) on level ground measures the angle of elevation to the top of a communications tower to be \(28^\circ\). Walking 120 m directly toward the tower to point \(B\), the angle of elevation increases to \(43^\circ\). What is the height of the tower? (Round to the nearest tenth of a meter.)
qs.s: Using the two overlapping right triangles, \(h(1/\tan 28^\circ - 1/\tan 43^\circ) = 120\), which simplifies to \(h(1.8807 - 1.0724) = 120\). Solving for height yields \(h = 120 / 0.8084 \approx 148.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: An airplane leaves an airport at 10:00 am and flies due north at 240 km/h. At 11:30 am, the pilot changes course to \(\mathrm{N}\,50^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) at the same speed. Find the distance of the airplane from the airport at 12:30 pm, to the nearest kilometer.
qs.s: The airplane flies 360 km north, then 240 km along \(\mathrm{N}\,50^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\). Total north displacement is \(360 + 240\cos(50^\circ) \approx 514.27\) km and east displacement is \(240\sin(50^\circ) \approx 183.85\) km, yielding \(\sqrt{514.27^2 + 183.85^2} \approx 546\) km.

qs.q: A ship leaves port at 7:00 am, heading due west at 16 knots. At 9:00 am, it alters course to \(\mathrm{N}\,30^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\) at the same speed. Find the distance of the ship from the port at 11:00 am, to the nearest tenth of a nautical mile.
qs.s: The ship sails 32 nm west, then 32 nm on \(\mathrm{N}\,30^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\), giving west displacement \(32 + 32\sin(30^\circ) = 48\) nm and north displacement \(32\cos(30^\circ) \approx 27.71\) nm. The distance is \(\sqrt{48^2 + 27.71^2} = \sqrt{3072} \approx 55.4\) nautical miles.

qs.q: A ship leaves port at 1:00 pm, heading due south at 12 knots. At 4:00 pm, it changes course to \(\mathrm{S}\,40^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\) at the same speed. Find the bearing of the ship from the port at 6:00 pm, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
qs.s: The south displacement is \(3(12) + 2(12)\cos(40^\circ) \approx 54.39\) nm and the west displacement is \(24\sin(40^\circ) \approx 15.43\) nm. The bearing angle west of south is \(\tan^{-1}(15.43 / 54.39) \approx 15.8^\circ\), giving \(\mathrm{S}\,15.8^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\).

qs.q: A ship leaves port at 8:00 am, heading due east at 15 knots. At 10:00 am, it changes course to \(\mathrm{N}\,35^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) at the same speed. Find the distance of the ship from the port at 1:00 pm, to the nearest tenth of a nautical mile.
qs.s: The ship travels 30 nm east on the first leg, and \(3 \times 15 = 45\) nm on \(\mathrm{N}\,35^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) on the second leg. The total east displacement is \(30 + 45\sin(35^\circ) \approx 55.81\) nm and north displacement is \(45\cos(35^\circ) \approx 36.86\) nm, giving a distance of \(\sqrt{55.81^2 + 36.86^2} \approx 66.9\) nautical miles.

qs.q: A fishing boat leaves a harbour at 6:00 am, sailing due east at 10 knots. At 8:00 am, the boat changes course to \(\mathrm{S}\,20^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) at the same speed. Find the bearing of the boat from the harbour at 11:00 am, to the nearest tenth of a degree.
qs.s: The boat travels 20 nm east, then 30 nm on \(\mathrm{S}\,20^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\), giving total east displacement \(20 + 30\sin(20^\circ) \approx 30.26\) nm and south displacement \(30\cos(20^\circ) \approx 28.19\) nm. The angle east of south is \(\tan^{-1}(30.26 / 28.19) \approx 47.0^\circ\), so the bearing is \(\mathrm{S}\,47.0^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\).

qs.q: A rescue cutter leaves its station at 6:00 am, heading due north at 20 knots. At 8:00 am, it turns due west and travels at 15 knots until 10:00 am. At 10:00 am, it changes course to \(\mathrm{S}\,35^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\) at 25 knots. Find the cutter's distance from the station at 12:00 pm, to the nearest tenth of a nautical mile.
qs.s: Displacements are 40 nm north, 30 nm west, and 50 nm along \(\mathrm{S}\,35^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\). Net north-south position is \(40 - 50\cos(35^\circ) \approx -0.96\) nm (south) and net east-west position is \(-30 - 50\sin(35^\circ) \approx -58.68\) nm (west), so distance is \(\sqrt{(-0.96)^2 + (-58.68)^2} \approx 58.7\) nautical miles.

qs.q: A patrol aircraft leaves base at 1:00 pm, flying due south at 320 km/h. At 2:30 pm, it turns to a heading of \(\mathrm{S}\,60^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) and reduces speed to 280 km/h. At 4:00 pm, the pilot must fly directly back to base. What compass bearing should the pilot steer to return directly to the base, to the nearest tenth of a degree?
qs.s: The aircraft's displacement from base is \(480 + 420\cos(60^\circ) = 690\) km south and \(420\sin(60^\circ) \approx 363.73\) km east. To return to base, the aircraft must travel 690 km north and 363.73 km west, giving a bearing of \(\tan^{-1}(363.73 / 690) \approx 27.8^\circ\) west of north, or \(\mathrm{N}\,27.8^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\).

qs.q: A sailboat departs a marina at 9:00 am, traveling on a course of \(\mathrm{N}\,40^\circ\,\mathrm{W}\) at 12 knots. At 11:30 am, the sailboat changes course to due north and increases speed to 16 knots. If the sailboat heads directly back to the marina at 1:30 pm at a speed of 15 knots, how long will the return trip take, to the nearest tenth of an hour?
qs.s: Leg 1 gives \(30\cos(40^\circ) \approx 22.98\) nm north and \(30\sin(40^\circ) \approx 19.28\) nm west. Adding leg 2 (32 nm north) gives total north \(54.98\) nm and west \(19.28\) nm; straight-line distance back is \(\sqrt{54.98^2 + 19.28^2} \approx 58.26\) nm, taking \(58.26 / 15 \approx 3.9\) hours.

qs.q: A cruise ship and a cargo ship leave the same port at 1:00 pm. The cruise ship travels due east at a constant speed of 22 knots. The cargo ship travels on a bearing of \(\mathrm{N}\,55^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) at a constant speed of 16 knots. To the nearest tenth of a nautical mile, how far apart are the two ships at 4:00 pm?
qs.s: After 3 hours, the cruise ship is at \((66, 0)\) and the cargo ship is at \((48\sin 55^\circ, 48\cos 55^\circ) \approx (39.32, 27.53)\). The distance between them is \(\sqrt{(66 - 39.32)^2 + (0 - 27.53)^2} = \sqrt{26.68^2 + (-27.53)^2} \approx 38.3\) nautical miles.

qs.q: Two hikers leave the same campsite at the same time. Hiker A walks due north at 4.5 km/h. Hiker B walks on a bearing of \(\mathrm{S}\,70^\circ\,\mathrm{E}\) at 3.5 km/h. To the nearest tenth of a kilometer, how far apart are the two hikers after 4 hours?
qs.s: After 4 hours, Hiker A is 18 km north. Hiker B is \(14\cos(70^\circ) \approx 4.79\) km south and \(14\sin(70^\circ) \approx 13.16\) km east. Total north-south separation is \(18 + 4.79 = 22.79\) km, so their distance apart is \(\sqrt{22.79^2 + 13.16^2} \approx 26.3\) km.

qs.q: An oil pipeline is being constructed due west from facility A. At point B, dense forest requires a detour on a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 36^\circ \mathrm{W}\) for \(1600\text{ m}\) to point C. The pipeline then turns \(\mathrm{N} 44^\circ \mathrm{W}\) to rejoin the original east-west line at point D. How far must the pipeline extend from C to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular displacement south of the baseline is \(h = 1600\cos(36^\circ) \approx 1294.427\text{ m}\). Setting \(CD\cos(44^\circ) = h\) yields \(CD = \frac{1294.427}{\cos(44^\circ)} \approx 1799.5\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A pipeline being laid due east from point A encounters a swamp at point B. The crew diverts along a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 28^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(1800\text{ m}\) to point C, then turns to a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 48^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to return to the original east-west line at point D. How far must they lay the pipe from C to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The northward displacement from B to C is \(h = 1800\cos(28^\circ) \approx 1589.306\text{ m}\). To return to the east-west line, the southward displacement is \(CD\cos(48^\circ) = h\), giving \(CD = \frac{1589.306}{\cos(48^\circ)} \approx 2375.2\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A hiker walking due east along a trail meets a rockfall at point B. She takes a detour on a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 25^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(850\text{ m}\) to point C, and then turns \(\mathrm{N} 35^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to return to the trail at point D. How far must she hike from C to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The southward displacement from the trail is \(h = 850\cos(25^\circ) \approx 770.362\text{ m}\). Hiking northward to rejoin the trail gives \(CD = \frac{770.362}{\cos(35^\circ)} \approx 940.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A ship sailing due west encounters a restricted area at point P. The navigator changes course to \(\mathrm{N} 38^\circ \mathrm{W}\) and sails for \(15.0\text{ nautical miles}\) to point Q, then alters course to \(\mathrm{S} 52^\circ \mathrm{W}\) to return to the original west-bound track at point R. How far must the ship travel from Q to reach point R? (Round to the nearest tenth of a nautical mile.)
qs.s: The northward distance is \(h = 15.0\cos(38^\circ) \approx 11.820\text{ nmi}\). Then \(QR = \frac{h}{\cos(52^\circ)} = \frac{11.820}{\cos(52^\circ)} \approx 19.2\text{ nautical miles}\).

qs.q: A power company is running a transmission line due east from substation A. At point B, a protected wetland is reached. The line is routed along a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 41^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(2100\text{ m}\) to point C, and then turns \(\mathrm{S} 32^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to meet point D on the east-west line through A. How long is the section of the line from C to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The northward displacement from the east line is \(h = 2100\cos(41^\circ) \approx 1584.890\text{ m}\). The required length is \(CD = \frac{1584.890}{\cos(32^\circ)} \approx 1868.9\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A drone surveys a straight boundary line running due north from base station P. At point Q, severe turbulence requires the drone to divert along a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 26^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(1500\text{ m}\) to point R. The drone then turns to a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 44^\circ \mathrm{W}\) to return to the boundary line at point S. What is the straight-line distance from Q to S along the original north-south boundary line? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular eastward displacement is \(d_E = 1500\sin(26^\circ) \approx 657.557\text{ m}\), which gives \(RS = \frac{d_E}{\sin(44^\circ)} \approx 946.590\text{ m}\). The total northward distance along the boundary line is \(QS = 1500\cos(26^\circ) + 946.590\cos(44^\circ) \approx 1348.191 + 680.919 = 2029.1\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A cross-country runner heading due south along a desert trail reaches an impassable canyon at point B. He takes a detour on a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 34^\circ \mathrm{W}\) for \(4.2\text{ km}\) to point C, and then turns to a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 48^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to rejoin the original north-south trail at point D. How many extra kilometres did the runner travel by taking the detour rather than the straight trail from B to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The westward displacement is \(d_W = 4.2\sin(34^\circ) \approx 2.349\text{ km}\), giving \(CD = \frac{d_W}{\sin(48^\circ)} \approx 3.160\text{ km}\) and a detour distance of \(4.2 + 3.160 = 7.360\text{ km}\). The direct distance is \(BD = 4.2\cos(34^\circ) + 3.160\cos(48^\circ) \approx 3.482 + 2.114 = 5.596\text{ km}\), so the extra distance is \(7.360 - 5.596 = 1.8\text{ km}\).

qs.q: A ship is cruising due east toward port. At point B, the captain alters course to \(\mathrm{N} 32^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(28.0\text{ nautical miles}\) to point C to navigate around an oil spill, and then turns to \(\mathrm{S} 50^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to return to the original eastward path at point D. How many extra nautical miles did the ship travel by taking the detour instead of a direct path from B to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a nautical mile.)
qs.s: The northward displacement is \(h = 28.0\cos(32^\circ) \approx 23.745\text{ nmi}\), so \(CD = \frac{h}{\cos(50^\circ)} \approx 36.941\text{ nmi}\), giving detour distance \(28.0 + 36.941 = 64.941\text{ nmi}\). The direct distance is \(BD = 28.0\sin(32^\circ) + 36.941\sin(50^\circ) \approx 43.136\text{ nmi}\), and the extra distance is \(64.941 - 43.136 = 21.8\text{ nautical miles}\).

qs.q: A highway is being constructed due east from point A. At point B, a protected wildlife habitat is encountered. The survey team detours along a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 35^\circ \mathrm{E}\) for \(3600\text{ m}\) to point C, and then turns to \(\mathrm{S} 46^\circ \mathrm{E}\) to rejoin the planned east-west highway line at point D. What is the straight-line distance along the east-west highway from B to D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The northward displacement is \(h = 3600\cos(35^\circ) \approx 2948.947\text{ m}\), and \(CD = \frac{h}{\cos(46^\circ)} \approx 4245.176\text{ m}\). The distance along the east-west line is \(BD = 3600\sin(35^\circ) + CD\sin(46^\circ) \approx 2064.875 + 3053.725 = 5118.6\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A team is laying a fiber-optic cable due west from central hub A. The cable extends straight for \(4500\text{ m}\) to point B, where a granite formation blocks the way. The crew routes the cable along a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 37^\circ \mathrm{W}\) for \(2500\text{ m}\) to point C, and then turns to a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 53^\circ \mathrm{W}\) to meet point D on the original east-west line through A. What is the total straight-line distance from hub A to point D? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The northward offset is \(h = 2500\cos(37^\circ) \approx 1996.589\text{ m}\), so \(CD = \frac{h}{\cos(53^\circ)} \approx 3317.612\text{ m}\). The west displacement bypassed is \(BD = 2500\sin(37^\circ) + CD\sin(53^\circ) \approx 1504.538 + 2649.563 = 4154.101\text{ m}\), so \(AD = 4500 + 4154.101 = 8654.1\text{ m}\).

qs.q: From the top balcony of a hotel, the angle of depression to a fountain in the courtyard is \(52^\circ\). From a lower balcony located 36 m directly beneath the top balcony, the angle of depression to the fountain is \(37^\circ\). What is the horizontal distance from the balconies to the fountain? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: Using the two right triangles, \(d\tan(52^\circ) - d\tan(37^\circ) = 36\), which gives \(d = \frac{36}{\tan(52^\circ) - \tan(37^\circ)} \approx 68.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: From the top of a suspension bridge tower, the angle of depression to a toll plaza is \(24^\circ\). From an inspection platform located 45 m directly below the top of the tower, the angle of depression to the toll plaza is \(18^\circ\). How far is the toll plaza from the base of the tower? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The vertical separation between the top of the tower and the platform is \(d(\tan(24^\circ) - \tan(18^\circ)) = 45\), giving \(d = \frac{45}{\tan(24^\circ) - \tan(18^\circ)} \approx 374.0\text{ m}\).

qs.q: The angle of depression to the roof of a warehouse from the upper observation deck of a communication tower is \(41^\circ\). From a lower observation deck, located 65 ft directly below the upper deck, the angle of depression to the same roof is \(31^\circ\). How far apart are the communication tower and the warehouse? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: Let \(d\) be the horizontal distance between the tower and the warehouse. The vertical separation gives \(d(\tan(41^\circ) - \tan(31^\circ)) = 65\), so \(d = \frac{65}{\tan(41^\circ) - \tan(31^\circ)} \approx 242.2\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: The angle of depression to the top of a monument from the roof of an office building is \(48^\circ\). From a window 80 ft directly below the roof, the angle of depression to the top of the same monument is \(35^\circ\). What is the horizontal distance between the office building and the monument? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: The vertical separation between the two observation points gives \(d(\tan(48^\circ) - \tan(35^\circ)) = 80\), so \(d = \frac{80}{\tan(48^\circ) - \tan(35^\circ)} \approx 194.9\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: From the lantern room at the top of a lighthouse, the angle of depression to an ocean buoy is \(38^\circ\). From a maintenance platform located 28 m directly below the lantern room, the angle of depression to the buoy is \(29^\circ\). What is the horizontal distance from the lighthouse to the buoy? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: Setting up the difference between the two vertical drops gives \(d(\tan(38^\circ) - \tan(29^\circ)) = 28\), which yields \(d = \frac{28}{\tan(38^\circ) - \tan(29^\circ)} \approx 123.4\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A surveyor on level ground measures the angle of elevation to the top of a transmission tower as \(25^\circ\). After walking 120 m directly toward the tower, the angle of elevation to the top becomes \(42^\circ\). What is the height of the transmission tower? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: Letting \(h\) be the height, the distance moved satisfies \(h\left(\frac{1}{\tan(25^\circ)} - \frac{1}{\tan(42^\circ)}\right) = 120\text{ m}\). Solving yields \(h = \frac{120}{\frac{1}{\tan(25^\circ)} - \frac{1}{\tan(42^\circ)}} \approx 116.1\text{ m}\).

qs.q: A person stands on level ground directly between two vertical towers of equal height that are 200 m apart. The angle of elevation to the top of the first tower is \(55^\circ\), and the angle of elevation to the top of the second tower is \(38^\circ\). What is the height of the towers? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The sum of the distances from the person to each tower is \(\frac{h}{\tan(55^\circ)} + \frac{h}{\tan(38^\circ)} = 200\text{ m}\). Factoring out \(h\) gives \(h = \frac{200}{\frac{1}{\tan(55^\circ)} + \frac{1}{\tan(38^\circ)}} \approx 101.0\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Building B is 250 ft tall. The angle of depression from the top of Building B to the top of Building A is \(32^\circ\). The angle of depression from a window 75 ft below the top of Building B to the top of Building A is \(21^\circ\). What is the height of Building A? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: First, find the horizontal distance \(d = \frac{75}{\tan(32^\circ) - \tan(21^\circ)} \approx 311.2\text{ ft}\). The vertical drop from the top of Building B to Building A is \(311.2\tan(32^\circ) \approx 194.5\text{ ft}\), so the height of Building A is \(250 - 194.5 = 55.5\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: From the top of a 180 ft vertical cliff, the angle of depression to the top of a tower standing on level ground below is \(28^\circ\), and the angle of depression to the base of the tower is \(46^\circ\). What is the height of the tower? (Round to the nearest tenth of a foot.)
qs.s: The horizontal distance to the tower is \(d = \frac{180}{\tan(46^\circ)} \approx 173.8\text{ ft}\). The vertical drop from the cliff top to the top of the tower is \(173.8\tan(28^\circ) \approx 92.4\text{ ft}\), giving a tower height of \(180 - 92.4 = 87.6\text{ ft}\).

qs.q: From a window 60 m above the ground in building X, the angle of elevation to the top of building Y across the street is \(38^\circ\), and the angle of depression to the base of building Y is \(27^\circ\). What is the total height of building Y? (Round to the nearest tenth of a metre.)
qs.s: The horizontal distance between the buildings is \(d = \frac{60}{\tan(27^\circ)} \approx 117.8\text{ m}\). The height above the window is \(117.8\tan(38^\circ) \approx 92.0\text{ m}\), so the total height of building Y is \(60 + 92.0 = 152.0\text{ m}\).

qs.q: Two conveyor belts at a processing plant discharge grain into the same bin at the same vertical height. The longer conveyor belt is \(3\) times as long as the shorter conveyor belt. If the shorter conveyor belt has an incline angle of \(60^\circ\) with the floor, what is the incline angle of the longer conveyor belt? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The bin height is \(h = L \sin(60^\circ)\), which gives \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{\sin(60^\circ)}{3} \approx 0.2887\) for the longer belt. Then \(\theta = \arcsin(0.2887) \approx 16.8^\circ\).

qs.q: Two zip lines start from the same elevated treetop platform and end on level ground. The longer line is \(1.8\) times the length of the shorter line. If the shorter zip line makes an angle of \(54^\circ\) with the ground, what angle does the longer zip line make with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: With a common vertical drop \(h\), the angle of the longer line satisfies \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{\sin(54^\circ)}{1.8} \approx 0.4495\). Thus, \(\theta = \arcsin(0.4495) \approx 26.7^\circ\).

qs.q: Two support cables are anchored to the ground and attached to the same point on a vertical cell tower. One cable is twice as long as the other. If the shorter cable forms an angle of \(70^\circ\) with the ground, what angle does the longer cable form with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The shared vertical height is \(h = L \sin(70^\circ)\), so for the longer cable, \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{\sin(70^\circ)}{2} \approx 0.4698\). Thus, \(\theta = \arcsin(0.4698) \approx 28.0^\circ\).

qs.q: A firefighter has two ladders placed against a wall so that their tops reach the exact same vertical height. The longer ladder is \(1.5\) times the length of the shorter ladder. If the shorter ladder makes an angle of \(65^\circ\) with the ground, what angle does the longer ladder make with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: Since both ladders reach the same vertical height \(h\), \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{h}{1.5L} = \frac{\sin(65^\circ)}{1.5} \approx 0.6042\). Taking the inverse sine yields \(\theta = \arcsin(0.6042) \approx 37.2^\circ\).

qs.q: Two skateboard ramps lead to the same elevated platform. The longer ramp is \(2.4\) times as long as the shorter ramp. If the longer ramp makes an angle of \(22^\circ\) with the ground, what angle does the shorter ramp make with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The platform height is \(h = (2.4L) \sin(22^\circ)\), so for the shorter ramp, \(\sin(\theta) = 2.4 \sin(22^\circ) \approx 0.8991\). Therefore, \(\theta = \arcsin(0.8991) \approx 64.0^\circ\).

qs.q: A vertical wall has two ladders leaning against it such that both reach the exact same height. Ladder A is \(15\text{ ft}\) long and its base is \(9\text{ ft}\) from the wall. Ladder B is \(20\text{ ft}\) long. What angle does Ladder B make with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: By the Pythagorean theorem, the shared wall height is \(h = \sqrt{15^2 - 9^2} = 12\text{ ft}\). For Ladder B, \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{12}{20} = 0.6\), so \(\theta = \arcsin(0.6) \approx 36.9^\circ\).

qs.q: A radio mast is supported by two guy wires attached to the mast at the same vertical height and anchored to level ground. Wire B is \(60\%\) longer than Wire A. If Wire A makes an angle of \(68^\circ\) with the ground, by how many degrees does the angle formed by Wire A exceed the angle formed by Wire B? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: Since \(L_B = 1.6L_A\), Wire B's angle satisfies \(\sin(\theta_B) = \frac{\sin(68^\circ)}{1.6} \approx 0.5795\), so \(\theta_B \approx 35.4^\circ\). The difference in angles is \(68^\circ - 35.4^\circ = 32.6^\circ\).

qs.q: Two guy wires are anchored to level ground on opposite sides of a vertical antenna and attached to the same point at the top of the antenna. The first wire is anchored \(15\text{ m}\) from the base of the antenna and makes an angle of \(52^\circ\) with the ground. The second wire has a length of \(24\text{ m}\). What angle does the second wire make with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The antenna height is \(h = 15 \tan(52^\circ) \approx 19.20\text{ m}\). For the second wire, \(\sin(\theta) = \frac{19.20}{24} = 0.80\), which yields \(\theta = \arcsin(0.80) \approx 53.1^\circ\).

qs.q: Two extension ladders are placed against a building such that their tops reach the exact same window. Ladder A is \(16\text{ ft}\) long and makes an angle of \(72^\circ\) with the ground, while Ladder B is \(26\text{ ft}\) long. What is the difference between the angles of inclination of the two ladders with the ground? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The window height is \(h = 16 \sin(72^\circ) \approx 15.217\text{ ft}\), so Ladder B makes an angle of \(\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{15.217}{26}\right) \approx 35.8^\circ\). The difference between the angles is \(72^\circ - 35.8^\circ = 36.2^\circ\).

qs.q: A rescue ladder on a fire truck is initially extended to a length of \(18\text{ m}\), reaching a window at an angle of \(74^\circ\) with the horizontal. To increase stability, the ladder is extended by an additional \(6\text{ m}\) while keeping the top at the exact same window. By how many degrees does the ladder's angle of inclination decrease? (Round to the nearest tenth of a degree.)
qs.s: The window height is \(h = 18 \sin(74^\circ) \approx 17.303\text{ m}\), and the extended length is \(24\text{ m}\), giving a new angle of \(\theta = \arcsin\left(\frac{17.303}{24}\right) \approx 46.1^\circ\). The angle decreases by \(74^\circ - 46.1^\circ = 27.9^\circ\).

qs.q: Two observation posts, M and N, are 36 km apart, with post M directly north of post N. A cargo vessel is spotted from post M at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 22^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and from post N at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 38^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far is the cargo vessel from post M? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular distance \(h\) to line MN satisfies \(h/\tan 22^\circ + h/\tan 38^\circ = 36\), giving \(h \approx 9.59\) km. The distance from post M is \(h/\sin 22^\circ \approx 25.6\) km.

qs.q: Two tracking stations, A and B, are 50 km apart on a north-south line, with Station A directly north of Station B. A weather balloon is spotted from Station A at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 42^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and from Station B at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 28^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far is the balloon from Station A? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular distance \(h\) to line AB satisfies \(h/\tan 42^\circ + h/\tan 28^\circ = 50\), yielding \(h \approx 16.71\) km. The distance from Station A is \(h/\sin 42^\circ \approx 25.0\) km.

qs.q: Two observation towers are 40 km apart, with Tower A directly north of Tower B. Smoke from a forest fire is spotted from Tower A at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 35^\circ \mathrm{W}\) and from Tower B at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 40^\circ \mathrm{W}\). How far is the fire from Tower A? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: Let \(h\) be the perpendicular distance from the fire to the north-south line; then \(h/\tan 35^\circ + h/\tan 40^\circ = 40\), giving \(h \approx 15.27\) km. The distance from Tower A is \(h/\sin 35^\circ \approx 26.6\) km.

qs.q: Two radar stations, X and Y, are 18 km apart, with Station X directly north of Station Y. A boat is detected at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 50^\circ \mathrm{W}\) from Station X and at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 20^\circ \mathrm{W}\) from Station Y. How far is the boat from Station Y? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular distance \(h\) from the boat to line XY satisfies \(h/\tan 50^\circ + h/\tan 20^\circ = 18\), giving \(h \approx 5.02\) km. The distance from Station Y is \(h/\sin 20^\circ \approx 14.7\) km.

qs.q: Two coast guard stations, P and Q, are 25 km apart, with Station P directly north of Station Q. A distressed sailboat is spotted from Station P at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 30^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and from Station Q at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 45^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far is the sailboat from Station Q? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The perpendicular distance \(h\) from the sailboat to line PQ satisfies \(h/\tan 30^\circ + h/\tan 45^\circ = 25\), so \(h \approx 9.15\) km. The distance from Station Q is \(h/\sin 45^\circ \approx 12.9\) km.

qs.q: Lighthouse A is 20 km directly north of Lighthouse B. A ship located north of both lighthouses is spotted from Lighthouse A at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 35^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and from Lighthouse B at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 20^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far is the ship from Lighthouse A? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: Because the ship is north of both stations, the perpendicular distance \(h\) satisfies \(h/\tan 20^\circ - h/\tan 35^\circ = 20\), giving \(h \approx 15.16\) km. Thus, the distance from Lighthouse A is \(h/\sin 35^\circ \approx 26.4\) km.

qs.q: An airplane leaves an airport and flies due north for 150 km. It then changes heading to a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 40^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and flies for another 200 km. How far is the airplane from the airport? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The total eastward displacement is \(200\sin 40^\circ \approx 128.56\) km, and the total northward displacement is \(150 + 200\cos 40^\circ \approx 303.21\) km. The distance from the airport is \(\sqrt{128.56^2 + 303.21^2} \approx 329.3\) km.

qs.q: A ship leaves a harbor and sails due south for 35 miles. It then changes course to a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 40^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and travels for another 25 miles. How far is the ship from the harbor? (Round to the nearest tenth of a mile.)
qs.s: Resolving the second leg into components gives an eastward distance of \(25\sin 40^\circ \approx 16.07\) miles and a southward distance of \(35 + 25\cos 40^\circ \approx 54.15\) miles. By the Pythagorean theorem, the total distance is \(\sqrt{16.07^2 + 54.15^2} \approx 56.5\) miles.

qs.q: A ship is sailing due north at a constant speed of 18 km/h. At 8:00 AM, the navigator spots a lighthouse at a bearing of \(\mathrm{N} 28^\circ \mathrm{E}\). At 10:30 AM, the same lighthouse is spotted at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 42^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far is the ship from the lighthouse at 10:30 AM? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: In 2.5 hours the ship travels \(18 \times 2.5 = 45\) km between observations A and B. Dropping a perpendicular \(h\) to line AB gives \(h/\tan 28^\circ + h/\tan 42^\circ = 45\), so \(h \approx 15.04\) km, making the distance at 10:30 AM equal to \(h/\sin 42^\circ \approx 22.5\) km.

qs.q: Two coast guard stations, A and B, are 60 km apart, with Station A directly north of Station B. Station A spots a cargo ship at a bearing of \(\mathrm{S} 35^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and a fishing boat along the same line of sight at \(\mathrm{S} 35^\circ \mathrm{E}\). Station B spots the cargo ship at \(\mathrm{N} 45^\circ \mathrm{E}\) and the fishing boat at \(\mathrm{N} 25^\circ \mathrm{E}\). How far apart are the cargo ship and the fishing boat? (Round to the nearest tenth of a kilometre.)
qs.s: The distance from A to the cargo ship is \(60\sin 45^\circ / \sin 100^\circ \approx 43.1\) km, and the distance from A to the fishing boat is \(60\sin 25^\circ / \sin 120^\circ \approx 29.3\) km. Since both vessels lie on the same bearing line from A, the distance between them is \(43.1 - 29.3 = 13.8\) km.
